If you're already in the Samsung ecosystem, these earbuds are an outstanding upgrade and are well worth the investment.

review_title: I couldn't imagine paying this much was that much better than ones I used for 1/10th the price
body_en: Situation: I couldn't imagine paying this much was that much better than ones for 1/10th the price. This begs the question, Then why did I try them? - I am learning Spanish to be with orphan kids in Colombia. I go to a church to be around them. I have an S24 Ultra that can translate to text or voice. I was wondering if it would be worth getting the S26 Ultra before going to Colombia again. Battery life was the same and the processor was a lot faster. - I expected go for it, but that's not the advice I received. Instead I received your S24 Ultra already has the Galaxy AI Interpreter for face-to-face conversations, Live Translate for phone calls, excellent microphones, and plenty of AI processing power. Samsung's newer hardware improves AI performance, but translation quality is mostly limited by speech recognition (understanding the speaker), translation model quality, context understanding, accents, slang, and background noise, not raw phone speed. Going S24 Ultra to the S26 Ultra might get slightly faster response, smoother offline AI, maybe less delay, but it will not suddenly make Spanish conversation feel like a Star Trek universal translator. Your S24 Ultra is already a monster. For translation, the bottleneck is not your Snapdragon processor, it is capturing clean speech and the AI model doing the interpretation. A better microphone path can help more than a faster phone. The Samsung earbuds Buds4 Pro is what I would recommend. The reason they matter is not that they magically translate by themselves, they improve the whole workflow. The microphones are closer to your mouth, they reduce background noise, you can hear translations privately, and you are not always holding a phone between two people. For example, with Galaxy AI Interpreter, you wear earbuds, the other person talks toward the phone, you hear English translation in your ear, your phone can output your voice translated Spanish. Moreover, if you have a Samsung phone, Galaxy Buds can do some translation tricks too. - It took me some time to overcome feeling stupid for spending 10x as much for something I had that works well, it was unimaginable that they could be that much better, and something I had to guard with my life now. I ordered, then struggled with cancelling, and then let it go on the basis that I also wouldn't know unless I "rolled the dice" to know, and the importance of the mission. The struggle was not the money. It was feeling stupid after I already had some that worked fine. Experience: - Setup surprise: Like all earbuds, they come with various sizes to fit your ears. Unlike the others I have, it has a setup that tests and determines the size that fits your ear. You do not do the determine which size, it does. You get a green check when you get a size that passes. There was only one of the sizes that passed, and they were not the same size for each ear. When I had someone look at my ears and size of the opening, they said they are exactly the same. I tried to trick it by changing its position to have it use the same size for each ear, but it wasn't buying it. I'm guessing it detects how much escapes from the ear to the microphone. Next it wants to do a hearing test like the flight surgeons used to do. This takes a while. Flight surgeons check to see if your hearing is still good. This uses the results of the tests to profile your hearing sensitivity across frequencies to adjust the volumes to make it perfect for each ear. That's more than my ~$1600 flight helmet does. - Comparison: My cheap ones worked just fine, I don't listen to music, and adjusting a mixer to the way I want to hear music just isn't a "duck in my pond". I just want to hear the unaltered sound, clearly, and be understood clearly, that's all I care about. You will not be able to imagine there could be a difference beyond that UNTIL you experience them side-by-side. Then they are very different. According to the scientific tests, the battle is between these and the ones from Apple, which are about the same price. However, if you have a Samsung Phone, it's no contest, which I do, because the iPhone doesn't have the smarts , flexibility, ability to document and record my phone calls automatically, enable you to write scripts to automate things without external approval, or have both eSIM and nanoSIM, as often nanoSIM plans are much cheaper abroad for some reason unknown to me. E.G. The iPhone is a great phone too, but it simply "cannot get there from here". - Features: It has different modes available to control the cancelling of background noise, one of which is to turn off the cancelling when you start talking so you can hear the response of the person next to you without removing the ear buds. There is a mode for driving to hear alert noises. It is much nicer for translation as mentioned in the advice I was given. Like the AirPods, these are also water resistant. You can also track and find them over the Internet from last place used, in Bluetooth range, and you can also find them in the case and turned off locally. There is no tendency for them to fall out of my ears while running. Summary: These are a different ball game than the inexpensive ones. If you have a use case like mine it is, and might also be worthwhile for someone whose hearing isn't the best. What I've written should help you determine if the extra initial cost and cost if you lose them, is worth the advantages they bring for your use case.

review_title: Superior quality, well worth the money.
body_en: Impeccable quality! Nice bass, clear sound, amazing noise canceling! Well worth the money. My samsung phone connected to them like they have known each other forever. review_title: Comfortable but some problems with features
body_en: Better fit for me than the Buds 2 and great sound cancelling. Here's are my pros and cons: Pro: Comfortable for me and stays in my ear better than the Buds 2 and Buds 3. It doesn't feel like it's always on the verge of falling out, or that is plugging up my ear causing pressure in my ear. Pro: The case has a pairing button to make it easier to pair with your laptop and other non-phone devices. Con: When I had 2 devices paired with the Buds 4, it kept losing the connection to my laptop in the middle of use. I suspect there's a software bug. Con: As with all recent Samsung earbuds, the controls are somewhat hidden in the volume setting of the phone now, so non-Android phones and non-phone devices won't have access to many of the settings. There used to be a wearables app that let you access this settings, but that is not the case now so long term usability may also be a problem, as long as Google doesn't change the audio/sound interface in Android. This integrated setting can also be confusing to get to since no other devices integrate this way (that I've seen). I would prefer an app for those controls, personally. Overall, the battery life and sound quality are good. At least as good as other ear buds that I've used over the past 15 years, and the stems do give you some pinch (pause or assistant) and swipe (volume or tracks) controls, like recent Apple'earpods. But here's the one really big negative that earned these 4 stars instead of 5. Live translate. It sucks. I would much prefer to link to Google translate or something else. The Samsung version just doesn't work consistently. I tried it with a fluent Spanish speaker in a quiet room and it missed words, stopped listening mid sentence and was completely unreliable. Do not buy these if you need that feature. These are not a Babble Fish. I would also prefer that the digital assistant was user selectible. I don't want to use Bixby, ever! Otherwise, for listening to music and audio books, having a phone call or Zoom meeting, these are great and comfortable for long periods of time.

review_title: Samsung's Best Earbuds Yet – Incredible Sound, ANC, and Comfort
body_en: Samsung's Best Earbuds Yet – Incredible Sound, ANC, and Comfort I've owned several generations of wireless earbuds over the years, and the Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro are easily the most impressive pair I've used. Paired with my Samsung phone, they deliver exceptional audio quality, excellent noise cancellation, and a comfortable fit that I can wear for hours. Samsung equipped the Buds 4 Pro with upgraded dual-driver speakers, Hi-Res Audio support, and improved Active Noise Cancellation, and the difference is immediately noticeable. The sound quality is outstanding. Music feels more detailed and spacious, with strong bass that doesn't overpower the mids or highs. Vocals are crisp, instruments are well separated, and everything sounds richer than previous Galaxy Buds models. Whether I'm listening to music, watching movies, or streaming videos, the audio is consistently impressive. The Active Noise Cancellation is another major highlight. It does an excellent job reducing background noise in busy environments while still allowing useful features like adaptive ambient awareness when needed. Calls are also remarkably clear, with microphones that do a great job isolating my voice from surrounding noise. Comfort has been excellent as well. The earbuds stay secure during long listening sessions, and the charging case feels premium while remaining compact enough to carry easily. Battery life has been more than enough for my daily use, and wireless charging support is a nice bonus. Pros: • Outstanding sound quality with excellent clarity and bass • Effective Active Noise Cancellation • Crystal-clear call quality • Comfortable fit for extended use • Great integration with Samsung devices • Premium charging case with wireless charging support Cons: • Some advanced features work best within the Samsung ecosystem • Premium price compared to budget earbuds Overall, the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro have exceeded my expectations. They combine premium sound, strong ANC, excellent call quality, and a comfortable design into one package. If you're a Samsung user looking for high-end wireless earbuds, these are an easy 5-star recommendation and one of the best audio upgrades you can make.

review_title: Wireless - Waterproof - Great Sound - Phone App - Mind Blowingly low price point for this quality!
body_en: I had been searching for a decent pair of wireless waterproof earbuds where the battery would play music for at least 4 hours on a full charge. I wasn't going to even consider any pair fitting my needs priced below $40, until my daughter told me about these, saying she really loved them and used them until she lost one of them after only a few weeks of use. So I bought them, and have all positive things to say about them, except for one thing. Here goes: PRO's: - They come with 4 pair of different sized rubber fitting tips - Using the pre-installled earbud tips, I was shocked in surprise that all it took was one quick finger press and they fit snugly and better than any other pair I have ever worn. As opposed to having to fiddle with them, twist and turn with a bit of force to make them stay in position. Not these - perfect instant snug fit that stays in place! - near continuous run time playing music or listening to audio books is at least 4 hours! Are you kidding me? For under $15, having 4-5+ hours battery time? Awesome! - When you need to keep using them but a battery dies - This is awesome - One side will always run out of battery before the other. When it does, or better, when it gives the 1st of 3 warning beeps that it is getting low, immediately take it out of your ear and put it in the charge case. OMG. It will charge to 80-90% in 20 mins or so! This means, when one starts to die, put it in the charge case, still listening to the other one. When that dies, even if it's 10 or 20 minutes later, put that one in the charge case, and start listening to the other one that you just put in the charge case a few minutes ago. You will find that it will run long enough for the one you just put in the case to charge to get to a full charge! Doing this, you will always be listening to at least one, but after a couple of times swapping them in/out of the charge case, they charge so fast that you will be back listening to BOTH again for another 1-2 hours, as the charge case if fully charged overnight will charge both earbuds at least 2-3 times. This is amazing - I've had to do this trick of using one while charging the other, but never do they charge fast enough to soon be using both again the same day because of such fast charge times compared to long run times. $15!!! This is an exceptional product and rare to have so many great features for pretty much a cost that makes them disposable but they are anything but!! - Sound quality! OMG! Really nice deep base response, and nothing missing throughout the mids and highs either! - The phone app makes it easy to pick from a huge repository of EQ settings. The phone EQ app isn't just a cheap attempt so they can advertise it as having a 10 band EQ - it is a bonafide 10 band EQ with a 10 DB range (+5 to -5 per each frequency band). You can create as many EQ templates as you like, give them a custom name, save them, even share them. At least 100 or more you can access from other users whose templates show up in the app. -Waterproof! I use them working in the yard (sweating profusely) at the gym, and in the shower blasting hot water from the shower head right on them. CON's: - Just one. As stated, they fit perfectly... until. At some point wearing them for an hour or so, you can feel one starting to get loose - DAMN! There it is on the ground - I hope it didn't break. Whew, it's still fine. It might just be me, but every single day, after wearing them both for at least an hour of a perfect fit - the moment I feel either one starting to loosen up - is when it is falling out. I took Karate, and I;m known for my fast reflexes, but not once so far have I ever been able to stop either one from falling out. Like I said, they fit perfectly, so I don't adjust them. They seem like they never move at all, maybe my ears build up with a thin layer of humidity/sweat, but without notice either one will just pop out faster than I can try to catch it free-falling 6 feet from my head to the ground. So it's been several weeks, so each one has jumped without a parachute to a crash landing on the ground every day, so each one roughly 20 6 foot drops, most of which to cement or asphalt. They both still work 100%, so I am just more surprised than upset at this phenomenon. Perhaps I'll attach a string to them, so when one falls out, I will have time to cup the opposite ear, and it will only fall the length of the string and not hit the ground. Instead of a string, I'll just buy at least one more pair, probably two, so that whenever one breaks, is lost, no longer lasts long after charging, it will become disposable (unless first try to take it apart and see if I can buy a super small rechargable battery and replace it myself, who knows, just a fun "maybe" thing. I completely 100% endorse these earbuds though. Even in the comments, there doesn't appear to be any issue that keeps coming up over and over, a sign of a well-designed product with a rare lifecycle!

review_title: Two for the price of one!!!!!True value

review_title: Small ear canal fit, all day charged
body_en: I love these earbuds! I’m buying my third pair simply due to use and misplacement. Fit: I have small ear canals and jlab and sony earbuds didn’t fit. These come with so many silicon options for your ear. The smallest fit me perfectly! Another bonus is under my snowboard helmet. It truly takes a fingerprint to pause. It has a low profile and when I turn my head, it doesn’t pause from the pressure of the helmet. Charge: I love to listen to audiobooks while hiking. My hikes can range up to 15 hours + multi day. I use one earbud at a time so I can tune into nature as well and can listen all day or multiple days when I’m super into the book. And recharge a bud as needed. They are water resistant, listening through rain, and the case has also been dropped in water and still works. Online calls: I use these paired with my laptop to record videos for my online courses, make phone calls, or zoom. The earpiece focuses well on my voice and dampens out external noise. Noise Cancellation: I also had 2 kids under 2. I relied on the noise cancellation feature during double tantrums to self regulate and be calm for them. I can’t recommend these enough for their price point, fit adjustability, charge life, and water resistance!

Update 1 year later: I still love these!! They still work great and connect with no problems. They stay connected even when I go to the other side of my house without my phone. The battery has gone down some to where I now get only about 4-5 hrs before having to charge them. I decided a month ago to get another pair of TOZO earbuds with a longer battery life. I got the A-6s. Those worked great but were too big for my ears and wouldn’t stay in place. I apparently have child sized ears! These earbuds fit great and I can wear them all day. There was a sale for a couple days where you could get them cheaper (forget how much), so I now own 4 pairs of these - 2 green, a blue and a black pair! Lastly, my initial pair that I bought a year ago was accidentally washed through a whole wash cycle when I forgot them in my pocket. I was so sad cause I thought they would be totally dead. Opened up the case and popped the buds in my ears; and not a hint of anything gone wrong!! They still work perfectly!! Original: I got these after returning another brand - this other brand I ended up returning 2 different pairs because they would not turn off and on when you put them into/ took out of their case and they wouldn’t charge! The second set had those problems and wouldn’t sync with my Bluetooth without going through several elaborate steps! I was done! I’m used to over the ear headphones and after the other brands issues, I was skeptical on Bluetooth earbuds. I decided to try these mostly because they were cute and the price wasn’t crazy high for something I might not like. I actually love these! Pros They charge well and pretty quickly. They are cute/aesthetic (I got the mint ones). The buds came with a ton of different ear hole covers including several small ones- I have smaller ear holes and these fit well in my ears. The sound is good, and with the app you can choose your EQ. Originally I thought the sound was just ok, but after getting the app and changing my settings, the sound was so much better. The earbuds work like they’re supposed to and turn on and off when you take them out/put them in the case! I’m able to listen with one ear and not worry that the other is wasting battery. On a long trip I was able to do one ear and change ears when that battery got low. I got through the super long trip on one charge! The earbuds fit well and stay in my ears well. Cons I did have to buy another charging cord; the one it comes with is crazy short and doesn’t reach anywhere near where I can charge things! You can’t really lay down with them in (I could do this with my over the ear ones). I’m not sure that audiophiles would find the sound up to their standards. This one is only a con if you’re like me (autistic) and have days where you like to go out in public but don’t want to interact with anyone! With my over the ear headphones most people wouldn’t bother me when they were on. These earbuds are not that visible to others unless you have your hair up and the person is close and to the side of you! Even then, some people don’t notice! Not a con - just something to get used to… I had to get used to was the controls on the sides. Mostly because I would pull one earbud out and hold it in my fingers to hear instructions/announcements/etc and I would accidentally change something with the tap controls on the earbud I was holding! Also, when adjusting them you want to make sure you just grab the sides of them and not hit the controls. I haven’t tested the range of these or had them in when I’ve been super sweaty yet. I can’t run, so have no idea how they perform when you’re doing that! If I bend over to one side I do have to make sure they don’t fall out of my ear, but I also don’t like putting them in far enough that it feels like it seals the air. I highly recommend getting the TOZO app. If just for being able to choose your EQ!

review_title: Just as Good as the Galaxy Buds FE
body_en: Just as Good as the Galaxy Buds FE I previously owned the Galaxy Buds FE and was unsure whether the Galaxy Buds Core would be as good or feel like a downgrade. After using them, I can confidently say that I have found zero noticeable difference between the two when it comes to noise cancelling, overall sound quality, or the experience within the Galaxy Wearable app. The sound is clear and balanced, with good bass and crisp vocals. The active noise cancelling works extremely well and performs just as well as it did on my Galaxy Buds FE. Ambient Sound is also available when you need to hear what is happening around you, and the touch controls make it easy to control your music and switch listening modes. The silicone wingtips help keep the earbuds secure, and each earbud is small and lightweight. They also have an IP54 rating for protection against dust and water splashes, which is a nice feature for workouts and everyday use. Battery life is rated for up to 35 hours with noise cancelling turned off or up to 20 hours with it turned on when using the charging case. The connection has been reliable, and the app provides the same familiar controls and settings that I was used to with the Galaxy Buds FE. Nothing about the Core feels like a major compromise or a step backward. These are fantastic earbuds. For anyone who previously owned the Galaxy Buds FE and cannot decide whether the Galaxy Buds Core are as good, I can confidently say that there is no noticeable difference between the two in the areas that matter most. I am extremely happy with them and would absolutely recommend them.

I bought these to replace my original galaxy buds that began to die. I liked the shape of my previous galaxy buds, so I was looking for earbuds that would be similar in shape and quality as my old earbuds and work with my Samsung phone. I was shocked to find these for less then I spent on my old galaxy buds originally, and even more shocked by how well they work. They are comfortable, easy to use, and the sound quality is great. The microphone works well for calls and the range is good/ appropriate for my use. I like how discrete they appear in my ears. They do a great job blocking out sound! If I could change anything, I would make them come in fun colors and work with wireless charging. However these are completely worth the price and superseded my expectations!

review_title: Best buds for buds+ buddies - but storage case is lacking
body_en: I've had the Galaxy Buds Plus for several years. Loved them, but all good things come to an end. I accidentally washed them and now the left one won't work. Can't figure out if it's the bud or the case or both. I wanted something similar - I did NOT want something with a stem. My son has the Buds FE so I tried them. I liked them but they've have been discontinued. What's a girl to do when she likes what she knows and struggles with change? These seem to be the only Samsung buds similar to the old Buds+ and readily available. I dont understand the "latin american stock" part. Reviews seem to indicate the buds will work just fine in the US so I ordered... Mine came with a sticker that says "united arab emirates." Not sure it matters. I'm under the impression that no matter what, buying for a different market than I live in would mean no warranty. I'm hoping since the buds+ never let me down until I washed them, lack of a warranty is ok. Physically they are very similar to the buds+. Almost identical, not quite. The rubbery portion of the core is more front and center and the rubbery portion of the plus is more slanted and to the side. The buds+ might be ever so slightly bigger. The buds+ are also kind of open in the soundhole portion of the rubbery thing whereas with the core, the rubbery thing covers the soundhole and has tiny perforations. The bud+, under the rubbery cover, is kind of metal with small holes, like a colander, whereas with the core it's more like a mesh. If you prefer the open hole rubber cover, it might not be a good idea with these. I'm assuming earwax will get mashed into the mesh but not so much into the colander. Core vs. plus - they feel basically the same in my ears. The left one started to hurt a little after an hour the first time I wore them but they were fine the second time - I think the slight difference in how the tip points requires a slight adjustment in putting them in. It's very minor. The sound is basically what I've been used to with the buds+. I wear these while doing chores or walking. I'm not a music critic or a great judge of amazing sound - I can't tell you if these are up to the task for more demanding things. These seem to block out outside sounds more than my buds+ but if this is something you don't want it's probably something you can change in the settings - I haven't really tried to play around with these yet in the the wearable ap. They're doing what I need them to do right out of the box. Tapping the right core bud pauses and unpauses whatever I am listening to very easily - sometimes I had to fight with the buds+ and in fact sometimes it refused to work at all. Maybe my buds+ got a little finicky with age or maybe these are just better in that regard. I do not like to make calls with earbuds in but I got a phone call while wearing them and the person on the other end was able to hear me just fine. The actual buds are basically perfect - exactly what I want - but I am docking a star for the case. They clearly took some cost-cutting measures with the case. 1. It does not have a light on the inside indicating if the buds are charged, although as soon as I open the case my phone pops up with how much life they have so I can still figure it out. 2. It's very shiny and slippery which makes it easy to drop. The lack of shaping inside the lid for the buds, which most other cases have, bothers me aesthetically but the magnets that hold the buds in to the case are so strong it's not a problem - they're not going anywhere UNLESS you drop the case and it pops open, which I have done. Twice. Everything still works but my buds+ case never popped open like that - in fact the case was still closed tight that horrible day I found it in the washing machine. My son's FEs have gone through the wash twice now and the case has stayed closed (and the buds and case survived). The lid for the buds core lacks a nice tight magnetic closure. If you wanted to go fancier the Buds FE case seems to work and you should be able to buy replacements for those - it has the inner charging light and a stronger closing lid. Of course then you are paying more money. Cheap solution is to get a round zippered earbud case at the dollar store which won't help with the charging light but will at least protect them if they drop. I'm hoping never to find out whether or not these can hold up to washing. Overall I am happy and reccommend these for someone in the market for a buds+ replacement.

review_title: Great for difficult to fit ears
body_en: Great. no complaints -fit so much better than my last Samsung pair. Would recommend for anyone that has trouble getting ear buds to fit properly. Battery has been fine so far. review_title: Redragon Gaming Mouse beats all the other gaming mice
body_en: Redragon Gaming Mouse Beats Other Gaming Mice To start off with, I think that the Redragon gaming mouse is one of the best mice as of right now. I have owned this mouse for about 3 years and it is just as good as brand new. When looking at the price of this mouse compared to other gaming mice, this is cheaper, durable, longer-lasting, and has most of the features as the other expensive mice have. I would most certainly recommend any interested buyers looking for a gaming mouse to buy this product. First and foremost, I think that the Redragon gaming mouse is one of the best mice as of right now because it’s cheap and affordable. When looking for a desktop gaming mouse, you should always research and look for other products that might be similar, less expensive, and easier to use especially when it comes to gaming mice. One of the popular gaming mice that is competing against the redragon mice in the market as of right now would be the glorious model o. This mouse comes around $100 in the market and functions similarly to the redragon mouse. The redragon mouse comes in around $20 as of now due to inflation as well. There isn’t much of a difference between the two mice besides the shape, size, and price. Paying $80 more isn’t worth it if most of the controls, and key features function the same way. Some of the key features that the glorious model o can do as well as the redragon gaming mouse are drag click, butterfly click, has the same amount of sensitivity, and DPI. The main difference between these two desktop gaming mice is that the glorious model “o” feels much lighter and sturdier. The redragon mouse feels a little bit heavier however, it is a decent size for any beginners or experienced gamers. It also has side palm grips for you to keep your thumb, ring finger, and pinky finger on support giving you the most comfortable experience as well. Some of the features that both mice can do that interested buyers would look forward to is having the mouse double click, drag click, and butterfly click. Furthermore, this mouse is very comfortable and durable for a long period of time. The gaming mouse's texture is matte which makes the gaming experience even better. There are also side buttons to change the RGB color or lighting to whichever settings you’d prefer with 7-8 different color options. All of these features are adjustable just by downloading the app or software if needed. After owning this product for 3 years, I have not felt the need to buy another mouse yet at all because of how well-made it is. However, despite all of the pros mentioned, there are always a few flaws or cons since nothing is perfect. One of the cons I experienced by owning this product would be that when gaming, some of the clicks on the redragon gaming mouse don’t register due to how big it is. Even though it is recommended to have lighter-weight desktop mice when gaming, it makes it harder to click while having some clicks not register. Over the past 3 years of owning this product, I have noticed that there is also a solution to fixing this problem. I have improved my gaming skills and it has made clicking faster and much easier for me. I would most definitely recommend this product to gamers who are at least experienced a little bit and have fast clicking hands to enjoy the full experience.

review_title: Title: Fantastic Value & Durability – Still Going Strong After Constant Use!
body_en: I’ve been using the Redragon M602 Wired Gaming Mouse for quite a while now, and I am honestly impressed by how well it has held up. If you are looking for a high-performance mouse that doesn't break the bank, this is a top-tier choice. Design and Ergonomics: The first thing you notice is the ergonomic shape. It fits naturally in the hand, which is a lifesaver during long gaming sessions or even long workdays. The textured side grips provide great control, and the weight feels substantial without being too heavy. It feels much more premium than its price tag suggests. Performance & RGB: The sensor is very responsive and accurate. I haven't experienced any lag or jittering, which is crucial for FPS and fast-paced games. The RGB lighting is another highlight—it’s vibrant and looks great on my desk. The different lighting modes and DPI adjustments (which you can change on the fly) make it very versatile for different types of games. Durability: What impresses me most is that I’m still using it today and it works as well as the day I unboxed it. The buttons still have a crisp click, the scroll wheel is smooth, and the braided cable is very durable and hasn't frayed at all. It’s built like a tank. Pros: Super Comfortable: Great for palm or claw grips. Customizable: Easy DPI switching and beautiful RGB effects. Reliable: No double-clicking issues or sensor failures after extended use. Braided Cable: Adds a layer of protection and premium feel. Final Verdict: The Redragon M602 is proof that you don't need to spend $80+ to get a great gaming mouse. It’s reliable, looks awesome, and is built to last. I’m still very happy with my purchase!

review_title: The best gaming mouse I’ve ever used
body_en: I’ve owned and tested many gaming mice over the years, and the Logitech G Superstrike X2 is, without question, the best one I’ve ever used. I don’t play competitively—I mostly enjoy adventure games, action titles, and other immersive experiences—but this mouse has made every gaming session more enjoyable. It combines incredible comfort, premium build quality, and features that genuinely stand out. The biggest highlight for me is the haptic switches. They feel amazing, providing a tactile, satisfying click that makes every input feel deliberate and precise. The feedback is unlike anything I’ve experienced on another mouse, adding a level of immersion that you don’t realize you’re missing until you try it. Combined with the outstanding responsiveness, every click feels fast, consistent, and incredibly satisfying. Another thing I absolutely love is how lightweight it is. It glides effortlessly across the mousepad and never feels fatiguing, even after hours of gaming. The shape is comfortable, the weight is perfectly balanced, and it almost feels like an extension of your hand. The wireless connectivity has also been flawless. It’s fast, stable, and completely reliable, with no noticeable latency or dropouts. It truly delivers the freedom of wireless without any of the compromises that used to come with it. Logitech has once again delivered a premium product. From the build quality to the innovative haptic switches, lightweight design, and rock-solid wireless performance, everything about the Superstrike X2 feels refined and thoughtfully engineered. It’s a mouse that makes you appreciate the little details every time you use it. Overall, this is easily the best mouse I’ve ever owned, and I couldn’t recommend it more. Whether you’re a competitive player or, like me, simply want the best possible experience while enjoying your favorite games, the Logitech Superstrike X2 is absolutely worth it.

I’ve had this mouse for almost a week now, and I can confidently say it’s hands down the best mouse I’ve ever used. It’s incredibly lightweight, the wireless performance has been flawless, and it just feels high quality overall. I am 35 years old and don't have the best reaction time but this mouse dropped my Human Benchmark reaction time average from 190 ms to around 160 ms. I wasn’t even planning on testing this, but one of my friends told me to try it and see if there was actually a difference. I tested on my old mouse, a Model O, and then back to the Superstrike X2 just to make sure it wasn’t in my head. The difference was still there. Everything just feels quicker and more in control, and the speed and click feel really make a difference. The feeling when you click it is incredibly responsive and smooth. The only thing I can compare it to is clicking an iPhone sleep button. Battery life has been very good also. After about six hours of gameplay, the battery only went from 82% down to 75%, which is impressive for a wireless gaming mouse. Can't recommend this mouse enough to everyone

I’ve been using it daily for about a month and a half now. First thing you notice is how insanely light it is, my hand doesn’t get tired even after long sessions. The buttons feel really nice to press. The magnetic analog switches are smooth and the fact that there are basically no loud clicks is actually pretty cool and satisfying. You can adjust the haptic feedback and trigger stops which is a nice touch. It’s comfortable tracks perfectly and the wireless connection has been rock solid. Battery life is good too. No major complaints so far

review_title: huge difference during long gaming sessions
body_en: The Logitech PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE is easily one of the best gaming mice I’ve used. The first thing you notice is how incredibly lightweight it is—it glides effortlessly, which makes a huge difference during long gaming sessions. The responsiveness is top-tier, and the Lightspeed wireless connection feels just as fast and reliable as a wired mouse. The build quality is excellent, with a clean, minimalist design that looks great on any setup. The clicks feel crisp and precise, and the customizable haptics add a nice touch for those who want to fine-tune their experience. Battery life is also impressive, and the USB-C charging is a welcome upgrade.

review_title: Haptic is the future for mice.
body_en: I gave this mouse 5 stars simply because of the haptic triggers. Ive only ever used the razer viper pro mouse and for my large hands its the only one that fits comfortably. The superstrike is a bit smaller in my hand but nothing that would make me stop using it. Its heavier than the razer and to my surprise I actually like and prefer that. The battery life on the mouse is great. The settings you choose for the haptic triggers does affect battery life but its nothing major. Now the main reason I bought this mouse was for the haptic system it uses and ill be blunt and say its the best thing ever and I hope more companies adapt this. Being able to adjust the actuation points is fantastic. It will take a few days to get used to the sensitivity if you go all the way to one but once youre used to it you'll never want a regular mouse again. Overall I think its a fantastic mouse its a bit spendy but in my opinion the haptic system by itself is worth the price. The only issue i have with this mouse is the side buttons they are extremely squishy they barely click its very unsatisfying I would give the side buttons a half a star.

review_title: Lightweight, super fast and great for gaming
body_en: I’ve been using this mouse for a while now and honestly I’m really impressed. It’s super lightweight and feels very comfortable in hand, even during long gaming sessions. The response time is excellent — everything feels smooth and precise, especially in FPS games. Battery life is also really good, I don’t have to charge it often which is a big plus. The wireless connection is stable with no lag at all. The only small thing is that it might feel a bit too light if you prefer heavier mice, but for me it’s perfect. Overall, definitely worth it if you’re looking for a high-performance wireless gaming mouse.

review_title: Really great mouse, but terrible skates.
body_en: I absolutely loves this mouse. I usually have stuck to only using razer mice in the past. However I made the switch to this one and its honestly so great. I only really have one complaint and the rest is amazing. Pros: Battery life is honestly amazing. Its really quiet because it no longer clicks, its just haptic feedback like the ps5 controller. You can adjust when it actually clicks which is super cool just like a Hall effect keyboard, because it's the same tech. Mouse just feels great and the included grips are nice, but they do take some getting used to as they aren't what I was expecting. However I have come to like them. Cons: It's vey expensive for a mouse, there's a lot of competition and a variety of mice esp way cheaper. The stock skates are absolutely terrible, that's why I changed them jade's and now its perfect. No complaints after that. However for a mouse this expensive, I was hoping for better skates. I also don't really like the scroll wheel, to be fair I do come from razer mice so that might be why I hate it. It also takes some getting used to as the mouse is front heavy because of the switches on the mouse, but I bet you can fix that if you have a powerplay to balance it out. However I have this mouse for 2 months now and I absolutely love it and I wouldn't switch for another. The only thing I would change if you were buying this mouse today is to also order skates so you can replace them. Would be a 5/5 if it weren't for the terrible skates. TL;DR: Great mouse if purchasing, buy skates as well.

After just a week of using this mouse, I can confidently say this is the best peripheral purchase I have ever made. I initially wasn't in the market for a new mouse, until my scroll wheel broke on my razer mouse. I decided to just pull the trigger on the X2 Superstrike instead of purchasing another razer mouse. The mouse material feel is excellent, and the wheel is great as well. I've also seen some reviews disliking the skates on the X2 Superstrike, however I personally found them to be great. The haptic feedback mouse click seemed a bit gimmicky before I actually used it. Right off the bat, the mouse click feels incredibly responsive and similar to that of any high quality mouse. You get enough feedback and it doesn't feel that much different from a regular mouse click. But, you also have optionality to adjust a ton of settings, like accuation, feedback strength, etc. For gaming, with the right settings, this genuinely feels amazing, and that's before the performance upgrade. As many other reviewers have noted, it noticeably decreases latency on top of all of this. Another huge perk with this mouse I found, was that it's almost dead silent as well. No more loud clicking! My only critique with the mouse are the side buttons and the size. The side buttons are the only part of the mouse that feel "cheap". Because I use the side buttons often in competitive games, I notice it a lot more than probably most people would. I also have large hands, and this is the smallest mouse I have used. I got used to it pretty quick, but the mouse is on the smaller side. Nonetheless, if you are looking to upgrade your mouse and have the money, I would 100% recommend. This feels as impactful as going from a 60hz monitor to a 144hz+.

review_title: Yes! Beats the G502 Hero (which I liked) and the G502 X (by a lot)
body_en: Good god, what a mouse. I mean, it's not perfect; nothing is. But it's so good. I came from years of the G502 Hero; the grips on it were wearing out. I first decided to try a G502 X, as it was supposed to be an improved version of the Hero, essentially. For $25 more than the Basilisk, it pretty much sucked in my opinion. The only thing I could imagine picking it over the Basilisk for is weight. But if you care that much about weight, there are much lighter mice on the market. --- I'll review it as compared to the Hero (and a bit to the X), as that's what I know. They're pretty common, so maybe this will help people out if they're thinking about converting: Initially I wasn't so sure about the grip and the main mouse buttons. The mouse buttons have a rough texture, and I found with my Hero that when my fingers were slightly tacky/damp, they would stick slightly to the surface of the buttons in the same way a clean basketball shoe does to a court (i.e., not "sticky", but grippy). I liked that. But after using it for a while, I think it's totally fine and maybe even better. The feet seem the same to me as the G502 X, which is good. They're white PTFE. Very smooth. The scroll wheel is *fantastic*. Like, it's perfect. It seems to control the mode with an electromagnet, so it makes a cool click sound when the computer is restarted and such. And it even has a setting in the software where you can have it tactile by default, but with a quick flick, it switches to free-spin temporarily. Awesome. And when I move the mouse quickly side to side, there is absolutely no play in the wheel. Nothing. That was one of my annoyances with the Hero. The scroll wheel would wobble audibly and tactilely when in free spin mode with even moderately fast mouse movements. The click noise isn't as nice as I expected, but it's totally fine and better than the X (which was super loud and piercing). I'd put it somewhere between the X and the Hero. It's kind of like if someone built the X and then was like, oh, that sucks, and then made adjustments like a sane human. I believe the Basilisk switches are optical (the Hero is mechanical and the X is hybrid mech/optical), and so maybe that's approximately what happened. In short, I think the Hero is a pretty quiet click, and I think the Basilisk is a very standard click. Sounds like what I'd use as a mouse click if I were a foley artist. The Basilisk's weight is listed at 101g, and it feels quite nice. Not hard to control. I'm sure I'll get even better as we go, though. The palm section is actually quite high! Like, even more than the Hero. It feels pretty good so far. The Basilisk's cable is an absolute work of art. I mean, it's perfect. It's got a soft woven sleeve and is not stiff at all. I had the same kind of reaction to it as I did when I got my current massage shower head and found that no, the tube connecting the head to the spigot doesn't actually have to be stiff at all to do its job. The software is slightly annoying because there's a separate program for the lighting and the mouse (though they're styled identically and could ostensibly be packaged in one app). But its functionality is nice. There are 9 RGB zones around the bottom edge of the mouse, plus one on the scroll wheel and the logo under the palm. They seem rather infinitely adjustable. Neat! --- Hope this helps somebody!

I used the Razer Mamba Elite for many years and absolutely loved it, so I was hesitant to switch. This mouse was recommended to me as a replacement, and I have been pleasantly surprised. It feels comfortable in the hand, responds quickly, and the customizable buttons and RGB lighting are excellent. The scroll wheel is especially smooth and versatile. Overall, it has been a great change and I am very happy with it.

review_title: This Mouse Ruined Cheap Mice for Me
body_en: I’ve genuinely liked using the Razer Basilisk V3. The first thing I noticed was how comfortable it felt. Some mice are fine for about 20 minutes and then they start feeling like a weirdly shaped brick. This mouse has been much better for longer use, whether I’m gaming or just clicking around online doing whatever nonsense I got distracted by. What I like most is that it feels like someone actually thought about how a hand works. The buttons are responsive, the movement is smooth, and the scroll wheel feels so nice that it almost made reading comment sections worth it. Almost. While this mouse has not been life changing in a dramatic movie soundtrack kind of way, it has changed my expectations enough that going back to a cheaper mouse would feel like using a shopping cart with one bad wheel. Oh, and the customization. I am not out here trying to launch a space mission from my desk, but it is nice being able to set things up in a way that actually fits how I use it. Once everything is dialed in, it just feels easy. Overall, it has been a genuinely solid mouse and one of those upgrades you stop thinking about because it just quietly does its job well. Which, for a mouse, is honestly the dream. It just sits there, minds its business, and makes me slightly more powerful than I probably deserve.

review_title: One of my favorite mice and you will love it too
body_en: This mouse is just incredibly smooth. Even with its high weight the skates make it super easy to move around and the weight gives it control, resulting in superb aim. The material can make your hands a bit sweaty when death gripping it, but it’s very solid matte surface. You can grip test and throw this mouse across a room without it breaking. The shape this mouse has just fits right in your hand, and the rubber side grips make it super comfortable and easy to use, it’s basically great with any grip type. The skates are super glidey and quiet even when under the weight of this chunker of a mouse. It’s better for bigger hands of course, it’s harder to use with smaller hands but it’s doable. The scroll wheel is the best of any mouse, even the Logitech g502. It has a setting in the software where it can be a tactile scroll wheel when scrolling slowly, but becomes a freely spinning wheel when flicked fast. You can even switch between spinny wheel mode and tactile mode with the click of a button. I loved this mouse so much I upgraded to the wireless version, and I wasn’t sacrificing much leaving wired because the battery life was great on that one. 10/10 mouse.

Best mouse I've ever used. Every surface is comfortable to touch & adds to its controllability. The RMB & LMB are soft & responsive, and have a quick reset. Easy to hold & thumb rest allows for greater control during long use.

review_title: Good gaming mouse and does what it needs. Just wish it would last longer.
body_en: To be honest they don't make mice like they used to. I remember a time where you would buy gaming mice and they would last 5 years minimum. Now a days they last a year if you are lucky. So far this mouse has worked pretty good and seems like it is holding up quite fine. I also want to point out I haven't had this for a very long time and I suspect the build quality of the mouse should last a year if this was anything like my old razor mouse. The scroll wheel is pretty solid. I like how responsive it is. I have never seen a mouse scroll wheel quite like this. Scrolling speed is pretty good. Was able to do a lot of jagged movements and noticed the mouse handled it very well in minecraft. Ergonomic of the mouse are probably the best part. I haven't used a non trackball mouse that felt this great in maybe ever. The programmable buttons I haven't used for anything since I literally have nothing to remotely use them for whatsoever. RGB is decent. Not a selling point for me that is a selling point for some people I guess. With that said I am not sure if I can recommend this just because it seems pretty good but the way gaming mice have been going I don't see this lasting more than a year. I remember a time where mice would last like a decade now they break if you look at them the wrong way. I will say the big pro to a gaming mouse is the fact it is meant for gaming. Yes you are paying a lot of money for something that will break within a year but you pretty much have no choice just because these mice have a sensor in them that is significantly way better than most mice.

The Razer Basilisk V3 is hands down one of the best gaming mice I've ever used. It's super comfy even during long gaming sessions thanks to its ergonomic design, and the customizable buttons are perfect for both gaming and getting stuff done. The RGB lighting looks awesome, and the HyperScroll wheel is surprisingly handy for switching between precise and fast scrolling. The sensor is super accurate and responsive, and the mouse just glides across my mousepad. I also love how easy it is to customize everything through Razer Synapse. Whether I'm playing FPS games, MMOs, or just browsing, this mouse works perfectly. If you want a top-notch gaming mouse with tons of customization and excellent comfort, the Basilisk V3 is totally worth it. Highly recommended!

This mouse is basically the “I’m him” of gaming mice. It’s super comfortable, the buttons feel crisp, and the 26K DPI sensor tracks like it’s reading your mind. The RGB lighting goes full rave mode (in a good way), and the HyperScroll wheel is clutch whether you’re swapping weapons or doom‑scrolling. The 11 programmable buttons give you all the customization you could want, and the whole thing just feels premium. It’s fast, smooth, and honestly makes every other mouse feel a little mid.

review_title: Fantastic mouse for those who like it heavy.
body_en: I'm an avid PC user and rarely replace my accessories. My mouse especially was hard to replace, as every top end mouse seems to get lighter and lighter. However, after using the Basilisk V3, I can safely say this mouse has been a perfect upgrade from my 2013 Deathadder. It weighs roughly the same, being on the heavier side for a mouse, and that's perfect for me. It's built great, has a fantastic braided cable which is smooth to the touch, it doesn't catch on corners like the older Razer cables, and the RGB is stellar. I really like the ring of RGB that goes around the base, and it's incredibly easy to edit in Razer Synapse. The mouse is also extremely comfortable. I didn't expect a thumb rest to do much, but I'll honestly miss it if I ever have to upgrade. For the price, you really can't go wrong. This mouse is incredible for its price point and well worth investing in if you like to 'feel' your mouse movements.

review_title: オススメ出来ると思います。
body_en: Deathadder v2 pro broke down so I bought a new one. I generally don't play games, but I often switch DPI on a 4K monitor, so a gaming mouse is ideal if you can switch it at hand and have enough buttons to assign a certain amount of macros. Since it was originally a wireless mouse, I was reluctant to switch to a wired mouse, but the thick-looking cable is lighter and softer than I expected, so I don't feel any discomfort when operating the mouse. It has a suitable weight and is easy to grip, so personally, I made the right decision to buy a new one. Since there is one more button, I assigned Alt+F4 (close window) to the innermost button, which I personally find very convenient and use frequently. One negative thing I noticed right after purchasing it (which has already been resolved) is that the scroll wheel feels too light. Even when I turned the deathadder v2 pro, it felt like it was turning one step at a time, but this product spins so lightly that I thought it was almost free, so I thought it was a little weird.However, I was a little impressed when I found out that you can change the feel of the wheel mechanically by setting it on the SYNAPSE side. I felt the evolution of the mouse.

This mouse works smoothly and feels very comfortable to use. The buttons are responsive, the scroll wheel is precise, and the design fits nicely in the hand. Great for both work and gaming. Easy to set up and excellent value for the price. Highly recommended

review_title: Overall, a great mouse. Has become my go to.
body_en: I got my first basilisk mouse on a Black Friday sale, and I got hooked. These are great, quality mouses that still use AA batteries. As someone who loves the MX series, and is sad that they’ve moved to Lipo, these mouses are much more affordable, functional, and still can be portable quite well. I love it.

My previous mice include the Razer Deathadder V2, Razer Basilisk V2 X Hyperspeed, and the Logitech Pro X Superlight. This is easily the most comfortable mouse I've used, the contours feel perfect and the extra button the side is well placed and feels like a natural addition. I've personally not found the weight an issue, though it is much heavier that most other mice, even ones that use a AA battery. I do prefer the external battery as I disliked having to plug in my mouse every so often to charge it, something that became much more frequent as the internal battery lost capacity. The new switches feel excellent, a noticeable improvement from the V2. Performance is good in all areas with the exception of the scroll wheel, which feels like it eats inputs for breakfast lunch and dinner. Basically when scrolling fast the Basilisk V3 seems to skip inputs. My V2 had similar issues and eventually I had to replace it when the scroll wheel started acting haywire and scrolling on its own or backwards. Something to keep an eye on. Appearance is unremarkable. The new RGB scroll wheel is appreciated, but fairly simple in customization. I have it set to static color but you can have it be reactive to clicking, color cycle, breathing, or a few other options with Razer Synapse. One small quirk is that if you have auto sleep on, it takes a bit to actually turn back on when using it again. Whereas the Razer Deathadder V2 was near instant in my experience, the Basilisk V3 takes a few seconds to get going, which sounds like nothing but does make a difference when it happens so often. TL;DR - It's a really good mouse at this price point, good performance and great comfort. Only negative is the scroll wheel and the weight if that matters to you.

review_title: Not as good as a 3S, but less expensive. Hopefully better quality switches than the 3S.
body_en: I like this mouse, but it could be better. I purchased it to replace a Logitech MX-Master 3S, which is a great mouse except the microswitch for the left button stopped being reliable after less than three years. While that's a reasonable life for some users, perhaps, it seemed inadequate to me. My use case is general pc use for searching the web, writing emails, and managing finances. The Logitech wasn't used every day. The 3S has a higher palm hump, which the Basilisk lacks and I really prefer. The Basilisk is similar in overall size to the 3S, so for the most part it fits my hand sufficiently well. Hump size is the main downside to the Basilisk. That, plus the battery is not rechargeable. What, in 2026?! But I've adapted to it, and battery life so far has been very good. It has the combo BT + 2.4 gHz connectivity with a dongle. Both choices work very well and reliably. I like the center wheel size and action a lot. I like the slip pads on the bottom of the mouse. It has a very handy and perfectly responsive third thumb button that I don't currently use but gamers may find it useful. Only time will tell if Razer's microswitch quality is more durable, reliable, and longer lived than the crap switches Logitech put into the otherwise very good 3S. I have used the Basilisk about two months at the time of this review.

The low latency with Hyperspeed technology is fantastic, and the sensor precision is seriously impressive. I’m also a designer, so I need accuracy for detailed work in Illustrator, and this mouse has performed perfectly for both gaming and professional use. Definitely one of the best wireless mice I’ve used.

The scroll wheel and buttons have excellent performance. However, the movement isn't as smooth as the Logitech and fine control is a bit lacking. This is problematic when working on very small things in Photoshop. This problem exists no matter how I tried to tune it in software. Also, the continual red flashing when the battery is getting low is super annoying. All in all it is a good enough mouse that I'll continue to use it for the foreseeable future.

review_title: Price is low, Performance & Quality is High!

I never use it, but it's a nice option and doesn't get in the way. Grip is nice and so is the texture. The two side buttons higher up curve, unlike my Asus RoG mouse. Wanted wireless but didn't feel like having another USB-C thing to charge, plus to stay wireless, plus save a bit on price, I went with the battery one. Cover is magnetic and very stealth, easy to use and doesn't fall off, even in my backpack on my motorcycle. Battery lasts me for about 2 months at a time, with daily, steady use. Takes one single AA. Lots of RGB settings via brightness & patterns. Way more quick DPI settings than I've seen on a mouse which is nice. I like heavy mice and am getting used to light ones, this one is the perfect weight and very flickable. Perfect match with my Razer Goliathus Speed Mousepad. Has BT and wireless. I don't ever feel any lag with either and I play a lot of FPS. More and bigger skates than I'm used to but it works well and don't seem to wear down and the pattern makes a smiley face lol. Stealth logo. Thing still looks brand new. Got it at a great price, shipped fast. Amazon didn't package it well and Razer usually packages a lot thicker but it was basic inside, but I wasn't paying top tier, which makes sense. Recommended! review_title: Good stock of beater mice for troubleshooting PCs! Also great for deployment to offices, schools!
body_en: I like to fix up and troubleshoot computers in my office, but I always have to use my good mouse to access the system. The Amazon Vine Program pointed me to this 6-pack of bulk wired computer mice, and I thought it would be a perfect addition to my office workshop. This is the 6-pack of wired USB silent computer mice, under the aptly branded "WYQQXZYKJ". It all comes tightly packed together in a small cardboard box. You get exactly what is shown, 6 black computer mice, with about a 4.5ft (or 1.5m) USB wire attached to it. It's an extremely basic computer mouse. You get the essential mouse functions: left click, right click, and scroll wheel. It uses an optical red laser, and 1000 DPI is adequate for basic desktop navigation. It's symmetrically shaped for both the left and right-handed. The most interesting part of the mouse is the silent clicking action, which makes this mouse one step up from an otherwise totally no-frills deal. I'm not going to totally knock the mouse for how basic it is, as it's actually useful for troubleshooting PCs. Sometimes you don't need all the extra buttons, bells, and whistles. I'm tired of using my good computer mice with random computers. I had one incident where I accidentally left the wireless dongle in a PC I sold, rendering a good $100 computer mouse totally useless. When you tinker, work on, and refurbish PCs, it helps to have a good stock of beater mice on hand when you need to get the OS installed and updated, or to work into what's gumming up the system. This bulk pack makes it all ideal for this purpose. The listing advertises itself for home, office, school lab, and PC gaming use in the title (at the time of review), but I find the PC gaming part to be a huge stretch. I wouldn't recommend this mouse for any serious gaming. Beyond troubleshooting PCs, I'd imagine another ideal use for a bulk pack of mice is to deploy them with a fleet of computers, like in an office, library, or school lab setting. Silent clicking makes it incredibly ideal, as you probably wouldn't prefer to listen to loud mouse clicks from dozens of people all day. $14 for a six-pack, along with additional options for 12, 30, 80, or even a 120 pack, is all an excellent deal if you need a bulk supply of basic computer mice. Overall, I recommend!

review_title: Great Troubleshooting Spares—Excellent Backup Value for the Workshop
body_en: Great Troubleshooting Spares—Excellent Backup Value for the Workshop Sometimes you just absolutely have to use a wired mouse. Whether you are actively troubleshooting a finicky system, working with a legacy machine, configuring a bare-metal OS before Bluetooth drivers are installed, or simply requiring a tactile interface over an integrated trackpad, keeping a basic wired mouse on hand is incredibly convenient. I maintain an office closet with multiple servers running continuously, and even premium wireless hardware—whether running over standard Bluetooth or proprietary wireless dongles—can occasionally suffer from dropped signals or jittery tracking. A basic wired connection, by contrast, connects smoothly and works instantly with almost any architecture. I originally only required two fresh mice for my setup, but this package arrives as a bulk six-pack. While six is more than I strictly needed, the low unit cost makes it incredibly convenient to scatter them around as utility tools—stashing one directly inside a portable system repair toolbox, leaving a couple hooked up to the local server rack, and keeping a spare tucked away inside the main desk drawer. I tested the compatibility across both macOS and Windows environments using a direct native USB-A link as well as a standard USB-A to USB-C adapter, and every unit initialized immediately without any manual configuration. The only minor caveat to note is the overall physical feel: these mice are lightweight and inexpensive and you can tell when you hold it. To provide an exact point of comparison, these units weigh roughly 44 grams, whereas a standard daily driver like the Logi Pebble 2 sits closer to 77 grams. The physical disparity is immediately noticeable in the hand, and the main click buttons feel decidedly hollow and basic. That said, the microswitches registers cleanly and activated successfully every time they were pressed. If you are looking for a premium, ergonomic daily driver for an eight-hour workday, this isn't the right fit. However, if you need a reliable, cost-effective bundle of utility mice to distribute throughout a workshop, tech bag, or server rack, this multi-pack handles the job perfectly. -- How my star ratings work: 5 Stars: Very positive. High quality/design. Fully accomplishes goals. I’d likely buy again. 4 Stars: Positive. Good quality. Accomplishes goals, but there might be better alternatives. 3 Stars: Neutral. Medium quality or design quirks limit its utility. Caution advised. 2 Stars: Low quality. Design flaws make it hard to recommend. 1 Star: Negative experience. Serious flaws or poor quality. Not recommended.

review_title: Quiet clicks and smooth tracking, handy to have a six pack of spares
body_en: Bought these to have on hand because between the shop computer, the kids machines, and a couple boxes out in the server rack there is always one that needs a mouse, and a six pack for cheap beats buying them one at a time. For basic corded mice they are honestly better than I expected. They are plug and play, hook the USB in and you are moving the cursor, no drivers or software to mess with. The clicks are genuinely quiet, that soft muffled click instead of the loud tack tack, which is nice late at night. Tracking at 1000 dpi is smooth and accurate on a regular desk and even on a bare workbench, no jumping around. The cord is a good length so I am not stretching to reach the tower. They do not feel like throwaways either, decent weight and the buttons do not wobble. For knocking around the shop and having spares in the drawer these are exactly what I wanted, no complaints for what they are.

For around $14 for a pack of six, I really can't complain too much. These mice definitely feel cheaply made, but considering the price, that's kind of what I expected. They work fine for basic tasks like browsing the internet, schoolwork, or simple office applications. The buttons respond well enough, and they're easy to plug in and start using without any setup. That said, I wouldn't recommend these for gaming or as your primary mouse for everyday office work. They just don't have the solid feel or precision that I'd want if I were using one for hours every day. The lightweight plastic construction makes them feel more like disposable or backup mice than something built for long-term use. Where I think these really shine is in places like schools, computer labs, libraries, or offices that need multiple inexpensive replacement mice. If one breaks, it's not a huge deal because you still have several more in the box. Overall, I wouldn't call them high quality, but I also don't think they're a bad purchase. If you're looking for an affordable bulk pack of basic wired mice, they do exactly what they're meant to do. Just keep your expectations realistic for the price.

To begin- I should state that I've been in the mouse community for a few years now and I've purchased mice from many different brands, big or relatively little. I've used Razer, Logitech, SteelSeries, Zowie, Corsair, Glorious, Pulsar, etc. I always seem to find myself coming back to either Razer or Logitech for specific needs that other brands don't necessarily offer. I have a lengthy history with Razer products, and that includes their Viper line of mice. I've owned the original, the mini, the ultimate edition, the 8khz wired release, as well as the Viper V2 Pro. There was one thing that kept my away from these mice for so long- shape. The original Viper mice, while excellent, weren't good for me comfort wise. The hump wasn't pronounced enough, and the curvature on the sides would cramp my hand every single time. I know, I know- why keep buying a mouse with a shape that makes you uncomfortable? Best answer: I like symmetrical mice, and other than shape, the Viper was/is amazing. Enter the V3 Hyperspeed! I was leaning towards 4.5 stars, but since I can't post a half star I'm comfortable rounding up. The V3 boasts a few changes that, in my personal opinion, are upgrades. The sides of the mouse are less aggressive with their curvature and I found them to be much more comfortable for my hands which are roughly 20x11. They've also done away with any worry of your ring finger clipping the side of your secondary click. They gave this mouse the same treatment the Deathadder V3 pro received. Weight isn't bad at all. It's around 82-83 grams with the included alkaline aa battery. I was able to get it down to a comfortable 70ish by using a lithium aaa and a separate aaa to aa conversion kit. This can be reduced even further by placing a small piece of aluminum foil between the battery(+) and the mouse's contact point. And another point to add- batteries. This mouse is NOT rechargeable, and it does NOT come with any included cables. For some this may be a deal breaker, but for me it's perfect. I don't mind rechargeable mice, but with 4K polling becoming the new " standard " I imagine constant charging could be a nuisance. However, there's a kit on here from PowerOwl that contains 8 aaa batteries and a charging system. I paid around $30 for the rechargeable lithiums and the aaa to aa converters in total. The converters came in a 10 pack so that was nice. This mouse is paired with my Hyperpolling dongle which can be purchased separately, or bundled together with this mouse when purchased from Razer. This. Thing. Is. Insane. When it comes to tracking accuracy I have absolutely nothing bad to say. The Focus Pro 30K in this mouse is the same sensor found in their flagships. Kudos to Razer for implementing that into their Hyperspeed line, which is widely recognized as their budget tier lineup. A few grievances of mine are that M2 ( right mouse click ) is considerably light. It might just be a case of heavy finger, but I found myself accidentally actuating the click at times. The side buttons are different in the fact that they are separated and have a bit of space between them. This is a good change, but I utilize M5 ( front side button ) as a Hypershift key, and it makes it a bit more difficult to hit M4 due to that split in distance. If you don't use Hypershift, then this should be of no concern. My copy has no creaking on the shell, no severe rattle, and the clicks are very crisp. I attribute that to the Gen 2 mechanical switches Razer are using in this mouse. For $70 you can't beat this, in my opinion! You're getting an insane amount of performance for a reasonable price. Pair this with a 4K polling dongle, grab some lithium rechargeable batteries, a few converters and you'll be fragging without the worry of cable drag in no time! Final score: 4.5/5 Amazing job, Razer!

review_title: The Ultimate Ambidextrous Endgame! 45 Days of Heavy Gaming and Pure Perfection
body_en: I am coming back to write this review after putting this mouse through its paces for a solid 45 days. After upgrading my desktop with a premium 8K magnetic keyboard, I knew my mouse setup had to match that elite level of performance. That is why I pulled the trigger on the latest Razer Viper V4 Pro, and after a month and a half of intense daily use, it has completely redefined my gaming experience. If you are looking for the absolute pinnacle of symmetrical gaming mice, this is the endgame. First, let us talk about the design because there is a lot of confusion out there. This Viper V4 Pro is a flawless, perfectly symmetrical shape. It is a completely different beast compared to the older, bulky, asymmetrical right-handed design of the DeathAdder V4 Pro. As someone who prefers a claw/fingertip grip for high-precision micro-adjustments, this symmetrical shell melts into my hand perfectly, giving my thumb and fingers ultimate control. At a mind-blowing 49 grams, the weight distribution is pure wizardry. Combined with the native 8000Hz polling rate and the 50K DPI sensor, the tracking feels like an extension of my own nervous system. In high-APM gaming sessions and chaotic shooters like World War Z or CS2, swapping targets is instantaneous with zero initial drag. Furthermore, it is an absolute dream for massive open-world action games like Where Winds Meet. During high-stakes martial arts combat, dodging, executing flawless parries, and rapidly controlling the 3D camera feels incredibly smooth and responsive. There is absolutely no pixel-skipping or camera stutter, giving me perfect situational awareness. Out of the box and after 45 days of absolute abuse, the build quality feels incredibly solid despite being so incredibly light—no creaking, no flexing, and the Gen-4 optical switches offer a crisp, satisfyingly tactical click that hasn't degraded a bit. If I have to nitpick, running this monster at a full, unrestricted native 8K polling rate does drain the battery significantly faster than standard mice. It is a trade-off for infinite performance. However, the real sweet spot here is the 4K polling rate mode. With about 3 to 4 hours of gaming per day on the 4K setting, the mouse can easily coast for 8 to 10 days straight without even completely draining the battery to zero. This exceptional power efficiency completely eliminates any battery anxiety. Also, the premium price tag might make your wallet sweat, but for a top-tier esports weapon, you absolutely get what you pay for. To sum it all up, the Viper V4 Pro is the undisputed king of symmetrical lightweight mice. It delivers unrivaled performance, unparalleled speed, and an incredibly locked-in grip. It has officially earned a permanent spot as the perfect crown jewel for my high-end setup. Highly recommended! Money well spent!

review_title: This is just one of my favorite mice now
body_en: TLDR: This is the mouse I keep coming back to. Long story short, I want nothing more when using this mouse. I'm one of those that just collects mice. I have my favorites, and I have some that I have just used once and put away. This is one that I keep bringing out. Simply put, the latest Viper and Deathadder are just some of my favorite mice period. They are built very solid, light weight, and flawless sensors. They have an instant wake up, fantastic battery life, satisfying clicks, great scroll wheel, and great side buttons. They are pricey, but quality-wise, it really doesn't get better than Razer now. Obviously, the shape is subjective, so if you've used the Viper V3 and didn't like the shape, you're not gonna like this. But I love the size shape, and weight.
