I've tested the USB-A ports with my keyboard and mouse, which work flawlessly. For my main use, I connect a data cable from the USB Hub (connected to any of my devices) to my KVM switch, so if you want to use it for a KVM setup, I highly recommend it. The USB-C ports also worked really well with my external drives. I do some light video editing, but even 4K video on my editing timeline worked amazingly. Build Quality: The shell itself is nothing spectacular; it's good and gets the job done, absolutely no complaints. The cable actually feels way better than the other USB Hubs I've had. It appears to have a braided cable, but all I know is that it isn't rubber, which is what I prefer. Because of that, I feel confident putting it in a bag without worrying about the cable getting squished, bent, or damaged (though I don't plan to). It's also very light and thin, adding to the portability. Nitpicks: The HDMI port is kind of in an awkward spot (at the end of the Hub rather than next to the USB ports) compared to other USB Hubs I've used; however, it's not a problem at all. Like all USB Hubs, it gets hot; however, it's not been a problem for me, even with all my devices plugged into it. Finally, the power draw issue. I've only had this happen to me twice, usually after changing the USB-C PD plug (right now a 67W charger, but I will upgrade to a 100W), but every time it would fix after unplugging and replugging everything back in, which is mildly annoying. If anything changes, I'll update my review.

I’ve been very impressed with this USB-C hub. The build quality feels premium, the 10Gbps data transfer is fast and reliable, and the 4K 60Hz HDMI output delivers a crisp, smooth display. The 100W Power Delivery keeps my laptop charged while using multiple accessories, making it perfect for a clean, productive setup. UGREEN did an excellent job balancing portability, performance, and value. Highly recommended!

review_title: UGREEN Revodok Pro 6-in-1 USB-C Hub - Perfect for Kids' Rooms and Multi-Device Use
body_en: Purchased 4 of these and put them in each of my kids' rooms (yes I have 4 kids). Pros: - Supports Chromebook charging and connecting to monitors/TVs - 10Gbps data transfer and 4K 60Hz HDMI - 100W Power Delivery for charging devices - Works with Nintendo Switch as well - Multiple ports for keyboards, mouse, Ethernet, and more Cons: - None noted Great little docks that make it easy for the kids to connect everything they need. Highly recommend for family setups or anyone needing versatile USB-C expansion. Would I recommend? Yes, 5 stars.

review_title: Perfect Port Expander for M1 MacBook Air & M4 Mac Mini – Frees Up Ports Without the Hassle
body_en: I own a 2020 MacBook Air M1 (16GB RAM, 256GB storage) for mobile work and a 2024 Mac mini M4 (16GB RAM, 256GB storage) for my home office, and port limitations were driving me nuts, especially on the Air with just two USB-C ports. The UGREEN Revodok 105 5-in-1 hub, snagged for around $25, has been a lifesaver for expanding connectivity while keeping things simple and affordable. It’s plug-and-play on macOS Sequoia for both machines, and it perfectly hits my needs: charging, external displays, and legacy USB-A devices without dongle chaos. Here’s my experience after a week of heavy use. Pros: On the MacBook Air, this hub is a port-freeing champ. It uses one USB-C port and lets me charge via its 100W power delivery port with my 30W Apple adapter, leaving the second USB-C free for a Thunderbolt drive. I connected a 4K Dell monitor via HDMI (3840x2160 at 30Hz, sharp and stable), a USB-A keyboard, and an external HDD to the USB-A 3.0 port, which transferred a 50GB video project in under 5 minutes. No lag or disconnects. On the Mac mini, with its three USB-C and two USB-A ports, the hub adds flexibility. I plugged it into a front USB-C for a second 4K monitor via HDMI, using the native HDMI for my main display, and it handles dual displays like a dream. The USB-A ports ran my old USB stick and printer without issues. The aluminum build feels sturdy, stays cool even with all ports active, and is compact enough to toss in my bag with the Air. Battery life on the Air stays strong at 15+ hours. For the price, it’s a steal compared to Apple’s pricey adapters. Cons: The HDMI is 4K at 30Hz, great for work or editing but not ideal for gaming needing 60Hz—look at Thunderbolt hubs if that’s you. The two USB-A 2.0 ports are slow (480Mbps), so use the 3.0 port for fast drives. No SD card or Ethernet, but I didn’t need those. It warms up slightly under heavy load (charging, HDMI, data), but never hot. Tip: For the Air, connect hub, PD charger, then HDMI for a clean setup; pair a Bluetooth mouse to avoid USB-A clutter. On the Mini, use System Settings to extend displays for dual-monitor productivity. This hub is a must for Apple Silicon users needing more ports on a budget. It’s reliable, sleek, and does exactly what I need. Highly recommend!

review_title: Great USB C hub, can also serve as a dock
body_en: I bought this to use with a Minisforum mini PC I have to expand one of the rear type C USB 4 ports, not only for more connectivity, but to prevent regular plugging and unplugging from the computer itself. It's a great little hub with all of the IO I need, including an HDMI port which, honestly, I don't really need since the PC itself has both an HDMI and a DisplayPort connection. It provides 2 USB type A ports, two 10 Gbps type C ports and a third type C port that is capable of 100 watt power delivery. That combined with the HDMI output means this hub could also feasibly be used as a dock for something like a Steam Deck, ROG Ally, a laptop PC, etc. I tested it with my Steam Deck OLED and it worked just fine and was able to output an HDR signal to my LG television while charging the Deck at full speed since the Deck's charger puts out way less than 100 watts. It feels reasonably sturdy, has a braided cable and even a faint little LED to let you know when it's actually plugged in. The cable could have been a little longer, though it's serviceable since it spends its time just sitting on a desk right beside the PC. When I tested it with my Steam Deck though, to test whether it could serve as a dock for that, it was short enough that the hub couldn't lay flat on the desk behind the Deck and was sort of suspended in the air by the tension in the cable, which would probably damage it over time, so if you want to use this as a dock for another device I would consider mounting it to the back of the device's stand or to the wall or something to keep it from just hanging from its own cable. I also think more companies should consider opting for the more open Displayport instead of the more proprietary HDMI. Not having to pay licensing fees to use HDMI could have brought the cost down a little bit. Overall though it's easy to use, turns my otherwise hard to reach rear facing USB 4 port into something more accessible and can even charge attached devices at up to 100 watts. I'm pretty happy with the purchase and will definitely consider UGreen for my needs in the future.

I originally bought this usb ports hub because i needed to plug in additional ssds into my laptop, but the side of my laptop was getting too crammed, so i had to opt in for a ports hub, and after about a month of using this thing, I can say that its really good, although I wish the ports were a bit spaced out a bit. For 13USD, the pricing on this is not bad, although the 10Gbps transfer speed really shows when multiple flash drives and external SSDs are connected and running at the same time. The PD port is also reliable, as I have not experienced any charging problems with this ports hub. The light on the top of the dock is a little less visible in daylight, but nonetheless, it still helps to see an indicator showing that the ports hub is on. The hub works on my Windows laptop, my MacBook Pro, my iPad, and even my phone without any problems. It's safe to say that I have not run into any compatibility issues while using the ports hub. The cord length is a bit short for my liking, although the cord itself seems extremely high quality and durable, although it does get a bit hot after long periods of use, but nothing too out of the ordinary. Another problem is that while using the HDMI port connected to an external display, the transfer speeds dip really low, although it's not that big of a surprise, seeing that the max speed of this thing is only 10Gbps anyways, but it would have been even better if it used all 40Gbps of my thunderbolt 4 speeds. Overall, if you really need a new ports hub, I would go for this one, because it's extremely compatible, and it seems to be able to go for years without a replacement.

review_title: UGREEN Revodok Pro USB-C Hub 6 in 1
body_en: Well made and solid build. Works great for my needs. I use it as a USB hub for my project Pis. I can read and write digital media drives. There is an HDMI connection I have yet to try. The cable is a little short but not really an issue. It's plug and play so no issues with drivers. I recommend it.

review_title: Good hub, but BEWARE: Your laptop MUST support "DP Alt Mode" for HDMI to work!
body_en: I build computers and I'm pretty tech-savvy, but even I missed a critical detail before buying this: Not all USB-C ports carry video. This UGreen hub is a "passive" device, meaning its HDMI port will only work if your laptop natively supports DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt. My laptop - bought last year - has a single "Data-Only" USB-C port. The hub handles USB data perfectly, but the HDMI port is completely dead because my laptop physically cannot send video data through that port. So, how do you know if your laptop will support HDMI through this thing? Before you buy it, check the symbol next to your laptop's USB-C port. If it has a lightning bolt or a stylized "D" logo, it *should* work. If it has a battery icon or no symbol it's probably data-only and this hub's HDMI port won't work for you. You need an active "DisplayLink" adapter instead (and those have other limitations and can be laggy). Long story short, check your hardware first to make sure this is supported if you want HDMI. It's three stars for me, because this should've been a huge flashing neon sign when I bought it instead of a complicated footnote buried in an image.

review_title: Six ports done right — everything works at full spec simultaneously
body_en: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Six ports done right — everything works at full spec simultaneously Been through enough USB-C hubs to know that the spec sheet and the real world performance are two different conversations. Hubs that claim 4K HDMI but throttle to 1080p under load, or PD charging that slows to a trickle the moment you plug in a display — these are the failure modes that make hub shopping frustrating. The UGREEN Revodok delivers on every spec simultaneously without compromise. 4K HDMI output is clean and stable — no signal dropout, no resolution negotiation on reconnect, just a solid 4K signal from the moment the hub is plugged in. Color accuracy and refresh rate are correct without any manual display configuration needed. Drives a 4K monitor without any of the flickering or handshake issues that plague cheaper hubs. 100W PD charging passthrough is the other critical spec and it holds up under real load. Laptop charges at full speed while simultaneously driving the HDMI output and pushing data through the USB ports — no thermal throttling, no charge speed reduction from splitting duties. The hub handles the power budget correctly which is not a given at this price point. Gigabit Ethernet is a legitimate gigabit connection — ran a speed test to confirm throughput matches a direct connection without the bottleneck that USB-C Ethernet adapters sometimes introduce. Stable link with no dropped packets under sustained transfer load. Build quality is classic UGREEN — aluminum housing, tight port tolerances, USB-C connection to the host that seats firmly without wobble. Compact enough for travel without sacrificing the port selection that makes it useful at the desk. Six ports, full spec, no compromises. Highly recommended.

review_title: Great 10gbps USB-C Hub, worked with Anker support through compat issues with PD4 iteration 1
body_en: Original Review (updates below): ----- The moment I noticed this thing on Amazon, I bought it and it literally just arrived. Finally, 4K60 over just USB-C with other ports (including making up to 10Gbps available to them) for a reasonable price. Unfortunately, the first two things I've done with it were both disappointing. I'll cut to the chase, the power delivery pass through isn't working with one of their own chargers. The first device I tried connecting this with is my Anker PD4 with one USB-C cable as the only thing plugged into it so I can test the truly up to 100W (-15 for its own power) claims. I've tried connecting it with Apple's 2m USB-C charge cable (100w capable) and an equivalent CableMatters cable that also supports 100W. When plugged directly into my laptop, both of these cables immediately start charging it and show up as 100W power sources. When this Anker hub is plugged in and either of them is connected to the power delivery port on the side of it, the laptop does not charge (laptop is a 16" Macbook Pro, I've tried multiple ports just for the heck of it). My second complaint is that when absolutely nothing is plugged into it, it becomes fairly warm to the touch. Why, when it's doing nothing, is it hot? I'm clearly not running data or even power through it so I have low hopes for it under load. The fact that it doesn't work in exactly the scenario they want it to most (a MacBook Pro with one of their own chargers) seems like a pretty big fail. I've got lots of USB-C things though so I thought I'd grab a couple and try those. Using an Apple 96W USB-C charger, the device does pass through power delivery properly. It shows up as providing 79W to the laptop (siphoning off 17W in this instance). I also have a 56W Aukey charger that splits power between a USB-A port and a USB-C port that can provide 45W of power delivery. When plugged into that charger it does appear to work as well and appears in macOS as a 30W power source. Maybe the problem is the Anker PD4? But it works fine providing power to the laptop directly. Would love to hear from Anker about these two products working together and what I should actually expect. Having it be unreliable for power delivery isn't great, but power and heat aside (it is getting a little bit warmer now that it's providing power from the Apple power adapter, but still definitely holdable), the hardware looks and feels good and the cable feels durable. Worth also noting that there's a white LED ring on the side of it that appears to be always on when it's plugged in. Don't know why it needs an LED. ----- Update, June 22, 2020: I've done some more testing and Anker has reached out to me to investigate what might be the issue. I can say that the hub works as I would expect from a quick test with my iPad Pro 11" with the above functioning chargers. It was able to pass through power with the 96W Apple Charger on the other end to both the iPad port as well as a Magic Keyboard port. The ethernet adapter showed up in iOS settings and an external drive was functional. When connected via the Magic Keyboard, which is a power only connection, as expected it provided only power. Still no power passthrough of any kind when connected to the PD4. ----- Update July 1, 2020: I've written back and forth with Anker and they've sent me a replacement hub. It also doesn't work with the PD4. I've tried multiple USB-C cables but they have also shipped a cable to test with it. For now I'm increasing the review from 2 to 3 stars because I am more and more suspicious about the PD4 and less about this hub. They claim that they have tested the setup I have separately without issue, and I've sent video showing the problems I've encountered, so the troubleshooting is ongoing. Have had a chance to use Ethernet on it without issue. Still need to try to test out its throughput when trying to use a 10Gbps USB-C enclosure and a 4K60 monitor at the same time (+ ethernet). More updates to come. ----- Update July 10, 2020: I've continued to talk with Anker support and they shipped me a replacement PD4. The one I had was labeled as "Iteration 1" on its barcode, the one I got back was labeled "Iteration 2". I tested it out and it works perfectly with this hub, passing through the correct amount of power to multiple Macbook Pros and fast charging an iPad Pro. Clearly the fault doesn't lie with this hub and is instead an issue with the first iteration PD4, so I'm updating my review accordingly. Working with Anker support was great. I've also been able to test USB-C throughput (without driving a display as well so far) and it properly utilizes 10Gbps. I've attached some extra images showing various devices connected to it (keyboard dongle, SD card, USB-C 10Gbps external SSD enclosure, USB sound card, ethernet).
This port extender has the ports your MacBook Air needs, but it's bigger than you think. The cord is 6" which is 2" linger than you'd like. But it works well.

review_title: Like It, but it required additional equipment to charge iPad Air 4
body_en: I am exploring ways to make my iPad behave like a laptop, and with this little device, I am on my way. One of my primary concerns is that sometimes I have to troubleshoot routers at other people's homes. So I tried it out on my home. I found that I had to install an app from the manufacturer to make it work, then I had to reboot the router. Then, I got an amazing interface that was not the same as the interface on my laptop. It told me that I need a firmware update, but at this point, I am more comfortable doing the update on my laptop. One quirk I don't understand is that I plugged the PD port into my power cube, and the iPad told me it wasn't charging. That isn't good. I might have to return it and shop for a different brand. The newer Apple devices are awfully picky as to where they get their power from. Update: I found the email for Anker customer support, sent an email, and they got right back to me. Here is what they said: "Please first know: Due to the power input limitations of mobile devices, this hub can not provide pass-through charging to tablets (including iPad Pro/Air) or phones when using the original wall charger that came with your mobile device. To support full-speed charging for iPad Pro/Air, use an adapter that supports at least 15V (45W)." I found that the 3 foot power cord that Apple sent me is nowhere near long enough for charging while using the dock, so I sent away for a 45W charger and a 10 foot USB-C to USB-C charging cable that was compatible with iPad. Please be aware that Apple has circuitry embedded in the cord and you cannot use just any cord. The equipment I got was this: Charger https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B083BRKMJQ/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 Cord https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B07LF1FNRV/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 Cords are not rated in either volts or watts, so I sent another email to Anker asking if a 3 amp cable would work, and they told me that it should. Pay attention to the amperage when purchasing a cable to go with a high wattage charger. The cord that I purchased also comes in a 15 foot length. If this rig works, I will also purchase the 15 foot cord. The reason being that sometimes I need to do stuff in other people's houses, and I cannot count on a nearby outlet. I will update when the new equipment comes. Update: I installed a 45W charger with a USB-C TO USB-C cable that was advertised for iPads, and now my iPad is charging through the PD port, so that problem is taken care of. I sold the iPad and bought a 2019 MacBook Pro. The MacBook Pro has four Type C USB ports only, no others. I use one of the ports on the Mac for charging and another for the hub. I use the Type 3 USB ports on the hub for my mouse and graphic tablet. I like wired mice, because they use a wire for power, are more reliable, and do not generate dead batteries to pollute the environment. I wish the hub had an additional Type 2 or 3 USB port. Maybe I will buy an additional adapter, because I can't find a hub that sports the extra ports. I looked for a mouse that would plug into a USB C port, but did not find one to my taste. I like wired keyboards for the same reason I like wired mice. At any rate, all these wires that will not plug directly into my computer makes kind of a clutter, as depicted in my photo. Not much I can do about it at this stage of the game, however.

Pros Allows multiple devices (ext drives, keyboard) and Ethernet and HMDI cables to be plugged into one USB computer port (also has two card slots, SD and microSD) All devices can be disconnected from the laptop by pulling out one cable Can be powered either from the laptop, or from an external supply (not included) When powered from an external supply can provide power to the laptop Cons Gets very hot! This hub occupies one USB-C port on my new laptop, yet allows me to plug in two external hard drives and a keyboard. Most importantly, I can also plug in an Ethernet cable, to avoid the hassles (and security issues) of WiFi and take full advantage of my high-speed Internet connection. (I don't use the other features) In addition, I can route the power to the laptop through the same USB connection, potentially saving yet another USB port (while my MacBook has a separate power port, I can still use the USB for power). When I want to take my laptop somewhere (which is, after all, the whole point of a laptop!), I only need to unplug one thing. (Although I do have to remember to eject the external drives or I get a nagging reminder from the OS). The device gets very hot: I've measured 42C/108F with an IR thermometer. There is a warning label on the bottom saying that it may reach 122F (50C).This is disappointing: I got this unit as a replacement for another, similar unit from a different manufacturer that burned out on a hot summer day. (No, no flames and smoke, it just stopped working!) I got a small fan to cool the other unit on hot days (my room gets to 27C/81F). Now I'm concerned the same may happen to the Anker. I'll keep the fan on in the summer, I guess. The unit works as expected; I have gotten downloads from the Internet at speeds exceeding 600MB/s (probably limited by my ISP).

review_title: Excellent Quality and Reliable Performance from Anker’s 8-in-1 USB-C Hub
body_en: I’m really impressed with this Anker USB-C Hub with Ethernet (8-in-1). The build quality feels premium, setup was completely plug-and-play, and all ports work flawlessly with my laptop. The Ethernet connection is stable and fast, which has been perfect for work calls and large file transfers. I also love how compact and portable it is while still offering plenty of connectivity options. HDMI output looks great, USB ports transfer quickly, and the SD card reader is very convenient for photo and video work. Anker continues to deliver reliable products, and this hub is no exception. Highly recommended if you need a dependable all-in-one USB-C hub for productivity or travel.

review_title: Almost perfect, could use one more USB-C Gen 2 port and a metal case instead of plastic.
body_en: Never really had any problems with Anker gear, I've come to trust the brand name. This little hub is almost perfect for use with my 2019 MacBook Pro, but where Anker really dropped the ball is by not adding one more USB-C port. I mean, there's two, but if one is dedicated to power devices only that doesn't really leave much room for expansion by only giving you one extra, I mean they were thoughtful enough to give you two USB-A ports. I do like that the USB-C and two USB-A ports are version 3.2 Gen 2 rated for up to 10Gbps transfer speeds versus Gen 1 at 5Gbps. The plastic casing does get hot, not sure if aluminum metal would be any better, but it would feel nicer, plastic just feels cheap. Also, a dark case with dark letter printing doesn't work because you can't see the writing, should have used lighter letter coloring. Otherwise, solid performer. I'll keep it along with my other one because having two hubs with a laptop is convenient so I don't have to always haul a hub around from place to place. PROS: • 1 USB-C port version 3.2 Gen 2 rated up to 10Gbps. • 2 USB-A ports version 3.2 Gen 2 rated up to 10Gbps. • Also includes, HDMI, Ethernet, SD and micro SD card ports. CONS: • Plastic casing, gets hot. • Should have one more USB-C port. • Port description lettering is too dark, gets lost against dark case color, should have used white or silver lettering instead. • No audio port.

review_title: Read this if you are having issues
body_en: I bought this a while back and while shopping for a second dock for my wife, I came across a lot of reviews where people are complaining about this thing. I relate to those experiences, but the problem is not the dock itself. Mine worked at first and then it started to work intermittently. Sometimes, my external monitor would come on and sometimes it wouldn't. I tried it with different Anker cables (I had been using the one that came with it) and I even tried it with different Macbooks. At one point, I actually thought the problem was probably with Apple. It was really frustrating and annoying. But then I decided to try a new Thunderbolt 4 cable I had purchased from Cable Matters. I didn't really expect that to make a difference, but it solved everything. It has worked perfectly for over a year now. I connect my laptop and I can instantly use my monitor and get to work without a hassle. I've since realized that while Anker makes good power bricks and even hubs, they make really crappy cables. I have a LOT of them, unfortunately. They short out very quickly and I've noticed they often separate near the connectors. For stuff like lightning cables, you know right away when it stops working. I hate to say it, but this hub (at least the one I received) is garbage. I will give the manufacturer points for build quality, the hub seems to built well and using quality materials. Unfortunately, that's about where the positive news ends and as far as usability goes I cannot recommend this device. I've listed below the problems I experienced within the first 24 hours of usage: 1) The switches outright just do not work for many devices. I tried several devices which seem to somehow just "ignore" the switch being turned off. I put ignore in quotes, because the device should not be built in a way that would allow any attached device to communicate with the host while it's off. For some devices, the switch does work correctly. However, for other devices, I can plug a USB cable into the hub and have it persistently connected to the host no matter how many times I toggle the switch on and off. This is a key indicator that the device was not designed in a secure way. When the toggle switch is off, power and connectivity should be completely disconnected to the port. The fact that I am able to bypass the toggle switch is an indicator that some sort of firmware workaround is being used. Bad news here. 2) Power delivery does not seem to work correctly on the hub. I'm using the power adapter that was delivered with the device which is plugged into a stable power source. Some devices which require power delivery (USB-PD) get stuck in an initializing state when drawing power from the hub. They get enough power to appear powered on, but the device never initializes and the host system can detect something was plugged in but cannot interface with the device. When I switch these devices to a different hub (or directly to the host), the issue is not present and the device works as expected. 3) Even devices that do connect, seem to have issues with performance and/or connectivity. When some devices are attached to the hub, the host operating system seems to hang while the device is connecting. I experience this on about 1/3 of my attempts with any mass storage device, and some devices fairly consistently. When I do get a device to connect to the host, my transfer speeds are considerably lower than if I had used a different hub or connected directly to the host. All in all, I absolutely do not recommend this device. There are several clear indicators of poor and unsafe design when it comes to this hub, and I would not trust that it delivers power cleanly or that there's any consistent integrity on file transfers. Again, all of these issues were experienced within the first 24 hours of usage. I tested over a dozen different devices with this hub, of varying types and manufacturer. If I had this many issues straight away, I can guarantee it's not an isolated incident. Even if my hub was "defective", there's no way it would have been defective in a way that would selectively allow some devices to connect while toggled off. Let this be a warning to you!

review_title: The Travel Dock in My Laptop Bag
body_en: What I like Plug-and-play. One USB-C cable in, several ports out. No drivers, no setup, no configuration. HDMI output for plugging into a hotel-room TV or conference projector without an adapter. SD card reader for moving photos off a camera. The microSD reader is a bonus. Two USB-A ports are enough for a mouse, a USB stick, or a card reader I already own. 85 W pass-through charging means I can keep my laptop charged through the hub when I have a USB-C charger handy. Lives in the laptop bag and is ready when I travel. It is the kind of accessory that pays for itself the first time you really need it. Compact and light. I forget it is in the bag until I need it. What annoys me Not a daily driver on my home desk. My home computers already have the ports I need, so the hub sits in the bag most of the time. Bus-powered. No battery, no separate power input. I am not trying to power a hungry external device through it, so this is fine, but it is not a “real docking station” with its own power supply. One HDMI output. If I wanted to drive two external monitors, I would need a different hub or a dock with display-multiplication support. The transcript says “second HDMI port,” and this hub gives me one, not two. No Ethernet port. Wireless works almost everywhere I travel, but a wired Ethernet jack would be a real bonus on hotel networks that block Wi-Fi or charge for it. I do not actually use it on my Mac mini. It would work, but I have not built the habit of plugging the mini through the hub. That is a me problem, not an Anker problem. Who it is for, and who should skip it If you travel with a laptop and need HDMI, an SD card reader, extra USB-A, and the option to charge the laptop through a single cable, this is the right tool. It is small enough to leave in the bag and useful enough to justify its weight. Skip it if you want a full desktop dock with its own power supply, multiple display outputs, Ethernet, and the ability to drive a multi-monitor workstation. That is a different product class, and a single USB-C hub with bus power will not do that job. Skip it if your laptop already has every port you need. The hub is solving a missing-port problem, and if you do not have one, it will just sit in your bag. Verdict The Anker USB-C 7-in-1 hub is a small, useful travel accessory that lives in my laptop bag and earns its place every time I take a trip. It is not exciting. It is not a daily driver. It is the kind of thing that disappears into your workflow and then you are grateful for it when you need it. Grade: A—if you want a single-cable travel dock for a laptop or Mac mini. Buy the linked listing if your use case matches mine.

Here's why I'm giving it a five-star salute: Connectivity Powerhouse: This compact hub packs a punch with 7 ports: 4K HDMI, 100W Power Delivery, USB-C, 2 USB-A, microSD, and SD card reader. It's like having a mini docking station that fits in the palm of my hand. Crystal-Clear Display: The 4K HDMI port allows me to connect my laptop to an external monitor for a crisp, high-resolution display. It's perfect for presentations, streaming movies, or just expanding my workspace. Blazing-Fast Data Transfer: The USB-C and USB-A ports offer impressive data transfer speeds, making it quick and easy to move files between my devices. No more waiting around for those large files to transfer! Pass-Through Charging: The 100W Power Delivery pass-through charging ensures that my laptop stays powered up while I'm using the hub. This is a lifesaver when I'm working remotely or traveling. Sleek and Portable: The hub's compact and lightweight design makes it incredibly portable. It easily slips into my laptop bag, so I can take it with me wherever I go. A Few Minor Considerations: While I'm extremely happy with the Anker USB-C Hub, there are a couple of minor drawbacks that I've seen mentioned in other reviews: Limited Ethernet: Some users have expressed a desire for an Ethernet port on the hub. While it's not a dealbreaker for me, it's something to consider if you require a wired internet connection. Can Get Warm: A few reviewers have mentioned that the hub can get a bit warm during use, especially when transferring large files or using the HDMI port. I've noticed this as well, but it hasn't caused any performance issues. Overall: Despite these minor points, the Anker USB-C Hub is an excellent addition to any tech enthusiast's arsenal. It's a versatile, reliable, and portable solution that expands the capabilities of your laptop and simplifies your workflow.

Anker is always a little bit more premium but this does exactly what i needed it to, it has all the connections i need to be able to connect my external mic, keep my ipad charged through the power delivery through an external power supply. its handy to have the sd and micro sd card slots as i transfer a lot of files between my ipad and mac and now i can do this quickly through one device, its an upgrade on my previous and the aluminium casing keeps it premium feeling while also keep the internals cool. it does everything i needed it to and looks great

Works very well with Android. Using Android mobile A21S, downloaded 375GB Insta360 Video to A Hard Drive. A bit slower than using the Computer, but no longer a need to take computer on Motorbike. 4 Stars as charging while working as above requires a larger capacity (Watts) charger.

I have a bunch of thumb drives that I use to move data from my pc to my portable devices. While I have a port extender, it is tough to reach and the Samsung and Sandisk Fit style drives are difficult to remove since they are aligned parallel on the wide sides. This hub is just over 4" wide and allows easy access to even the small thumb drives. The cable is 24" long and is just the right length for my applicatioin. As noted in the instructions, this device does get warm when fully loaded so it would be a good idea to put it in a location that allows it to "breath". There is a blue led power led, but it is exceedingly small and not very bright. There is a usb-c power port on the end which may be needed when external hard drive or other power hungry devices are plugged in, Great price for a solid product.

review_title: Good quality and value for the price
body_en: Small, compact multi port. Has worked well with my Mac desktop. Good quality for the price.
Amazing quality. Works as described. Easy to install. Slim design makes ot easy to use in any space.

I bought an external keyboard and a headset to use on my laptop, but I didn’t have enough USB ports. This attachment is perfect. It gives me plenty of USB ports for an external keyboard and a headset to my laptop. This attachment is perfect. It gives me plenty of USB ports for what I need.

I’ve been using this Acer USB hub for a few weeks now, and overall I’m really happy with it. I bought it mainly because my laptop doesn’t have enough USB ports for all my schoolwork gear and gaming accessories, and this hub has made things so much easier. Setup and use Right out of the box, it was completely plug-and-play — no software, no setup. I just plugged it into my laptop and started connecting my devices. The size is perfect for portability; I toss it in my backpack when I go between school and home, and it doesn’t take up much space on my desk either. Performance For most of my devices, the hub works flawlessly. My mouse, keyboard, flash drives, and external hard drive all connect instantly and run smoothly. File transfers are quick, and I didn’t notice any lag or drop in performance. The USB 3.0 speeds feel solid, which is great when I’m moving large files for class projects or videos. Build quality It feels well-made for the price — not cheap or flimsy. The cord is thick enough that I’m not worried about it bending or breaking easily, and the ports hold connections snugly. It’s clearly built to handle everyday use. The one issue The only thing keeping this from being a 5-star review is my headset. For some reason, when I plug my USB headset into the hub, it either doesn’t get recognized or the microphone cuts in and out. When I plug it directly into my laptop, it works perfectly fine. It’s not a huge deal since everything else works great, but it’s a bit annoying since I use the headset for both online classes and gaming. From what I can tell, the hub might not deliver enough power or stability for certain audio devices, which isn’t uncommon for smaller, bus-powered hubs like this one. Final thoughts Aside from that minor issue, I’m really happy with this hub. It does exactly what I need — adds a few extra ports, keeps everything connected, and is simple to use. For everyday accessories and school use, it’s a great buy. Just be aware that some more sensitive or high-power devices (like headsets or external hard drives) might work better plugged directly into your computer. Overall rating: 4 out of 5 stars Would I recommend it? Definitely — especially if you just need more USB ports for regular devices and don’t plan on using it for audio or power-hungry gear
Works good and very reasonable pricing. Enabled me to add (4) more USB ports to my computer. Currently my USB ports are in the back of the monitor. This makes my job much easier.

Works well, and by a name brand company. I bought this to replace or supplement two other very old hubs I have. It is faster than the old ones (although, to be honest, my computers are old enough that it probably makes little difference). It plugs in firmly, and this is important to me as one of the old ones sometimes requires plugging in more than once before it makes good contact. All in all, this hub is quite adequate.
Connected most of my things, works well.
Very good, practical and works very well
All my USBs are connected in the same box and to a single laptop input.
Best usb hub u will fine just buy it
Purchased for a mini PC with only one USB port. It's thin so you can insert it into a gap on your tabletop.

review_title: Great product, solid build, and fast performance
body_en: I’m very happy with this Acer USB Hub. The build quality feels premium and sturdy despite being ultra-slim and lightweight. Data transfer speed is fast, and all four USB ports work smoothly without any lag or disconnections. The 2ft cable length is very convenient and gives enough flexibility for desk setup. I also like that it supports both USB-A and Type-C power (5V 3A), which makes it reliable even when multiple devices are connected at the same time. I’ve used it with my laptop for mouse, keyboard, and external devices, and it performs consistently well. Plug-and-play setup with no drivers required, and it works perfectly with Windows and Linux. Overall, it’s a good-quality, reliable USB hub from Acer, and definitely worth the price. Highly recommended for anyone needing extra USB ports.

review_title: I would buy this again without a doubt!
body_en: Works great! Charges everything I need it too without skipping a beat, even my DJI charging hub gets plenty of power. The best thing I have noticed is even with multiple items plugged in, it still puts out the rated wattage of that socket so long as you don't exceed total output. I would buy it again!

review_title: Powers multiple devices without any problems
body_en: I keep this device on my desk to charge other things as necessary, cell phone, tablet, etc. Charging multiple devices is no problem. The device has no LEDs so using it in a bedroom to charge devices overnight would be good, too. The power cord does not have a "brick" so it can easily be hidden behind a desk or dresser. The power cord is 2 prong so there is no ground and it will work with an extension cord that is not grounded.

This power station stands out with its ample USB-C ports, smartly designed to minimize device resets common in multi-port chargers. It cleverly groups ports to manage devices sharing a power control chip, accommodating sensitive devices by allowing you to isolate them from those unaffected by power interruptions. Additionally, it tackles power-hungry gadgets with an ultra-high-power port, alongside a versatile range of power outputs. The inclusion of a single USB-A port has proven unexpectedly handy, ensuring compatibility with a broad array of devices. This thoughtful design mirrors the strategy of separating squabbling siblings on a long drive, ensuring peace and functionality for all connected devices.
I was looking for something small with multiple charging ports to put on my nightstand. This fit my needs. Wish it had a few more options for ports but I recommend this product.
Works great! It definitely cleared some of my desk clutter.
WORTH WAITING FOR. Works great love the stand.
Works great served on purpose

Detachable cord, nice vertical stand, multiport versatility. Used for charging my 15 inch MacBook Air during the day and my iPhone 15 Pro and Apple Watch Ultra 2 at night. I have a 3 in 1 charger for the phone and watch, where I use the 45W port to charge, no issues. Must buy, I returned a brand named that was lower wattage with 3 normal plug on it. I like this product more for my charging needs, the detachable cord helps out. (Always use charging cables that work with the highest wattage port)

This keyboard offers a truly premium feel at an excellent price. The build quality is solid, the keys are responsive and comfortable, and typing on it is a pleasure. Everything feels well made and reliable, making it great for both work and everyday use.

The keyboard feels solid and sounds much better than I expected for the price. The keys are smooth, the compact 75% layout saves desk space, and it still keeps the function row and arrow keys. The wireless connection was easy to set up, and switching between devices has been convenient. The RGB lighting looks good without being too bright, and the battery has lasted well with the lights turned down. The software could be a little easier to use, but I did not need it for basic settings. Overall, it is a comfortable and good-looking keyboard for gaming, work, and everyday use.

review_title: Great for both work and gaming
body_en: I bought this keyboard after spending some time looking for a wireless mechanical keyboard that I could use for both work and gaming, and I’m really happy with my purchase. What I like most is the feel of the keys when typing and the sound. It has that characteristic mechanical keyboard sound that is very satisfying without becoming annoying when I’m working for several hours. I also think the 75% size is perfect: it takes up much less space on my desk without sacrificing the keys I actually use. I also really like the way it looks. It feels stylish, solid, and much more polished than I expected. The wireless connection has worked very well, and being able to switch between devices is really convenient. I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations. When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly. The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway. I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

review_title: 10/10 would buy another one, perfect gift
body_en: The AULA F75 Pro isn’t just a keyboard — it’s a life upgrade. From the moment I unboxed it, I knew this thing was built different. The build quality feels premium in a way that makes everything else on my desk feel insecure. The weight, the finish, the layout — chef’s kiss. But the sound? Oh man… pure mechanical ASMR. Every keystroke is a buttery, creamy “thock” that makes typing feel less like a task and more like a treat. It’s so smooth and satisfying I found myself typing things I didn’t even need to type — emails, notes, grocery lists, lorem ipsum paragraphs — just to hear it sing. Key layout & switch orientation: One thing I absolutely love is how the keys are south-facing, sitting slightly inward instead of pointing outward toward you. It gives the whole board a cleaner, sleeker look and makes the RGB shine through in a softer, more premium way. Wireless performance: flawless. Zero lag, zero hiccups, zero drama. It connects instantly and stays rock-solid whether I’m gaming, working, or just vibing on YouTube comments. Battery life: absurdly good. I swear this thing runs on wizard energy because I keep checking the percentage and it keeps refusing to go down. RGB: The lighting is vibrant without being over-the-top, and the multi-function knob makes switching effects, brightness, and colors stupidly satisfying. One smooth twist and you can go from a calm ambient glow to full-on gamer neon. It’s intuitive, responsive, and makes controlling the RGB feel extra premium without the need of a software which is a plus. Overall? This keyboard is elite. Legendary. A masterpiece of clicky, thocky engineering. If you want something that feels incredible, sounds incredible, and looks incredible, the AULA F75 Pro is the one. I absolutely, genuinely loved this product.

Just, WOW! This thing is HEAVY but feels like it was made out of butter. The exterior casing is made out of what feels like dense '90s style plastic which doesn't show fingerprints. If I didn't know better I thought it was metal covered in some kind of coating. The keys on this thing are the smoothest I have ever felt in my life. Just pure buttery smoothness, but a really nice clickety clack when you start typing. There isn't a spring sound like a lot of old keyboards from the '80s up to the mid '90s, but the clacking sound is still very satisfying and retro in its own way. The lighting patterns are just out of this world. I expected it to just light up, but it has quite a few different patterns like rippling, pulsing, and my favorite is some kind of mode that makes the colors jump around. The fact that the lettering is on the front of the key instead of the top is really cool. So far the Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz connections have both been really good, I haven't tried it plugged in but I'm sure it would be good. Seriously, the quality on this thing is unreal and exceeds my expectations by several miles. I thought I was just getting a fairly decent plastic keyboard that would weigh about the same as most others and have springy sounding keys. This thing reminds me of some kind of professional music gear. If you aren't sure, just get one, this is seriously one of the highest quality items I have ever received from Amazon from a non-top-tier brand.

I'm impressed. Coming from a 4 year old Corsair mechanical keyboard with cherry mx switches, I had high hopes that this keyboard would get the job done. It lacks dedicated media keys, but you still have media keys by using the function key. The battery is excellent to start; I hope it lasts just as long as my Corsair did. The weight is a little beefy despite it being mostly plastic and thicc. The size is perfect if you intend to use it on your lap or TV tray. There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them. While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row. Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands. The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying. Overall, I'm Impressed. (update as of 3-15-26) Nearly a year later, the battery's lifespan has decreased to about 50% of its original capacity.

I’m honestly really impressed with the AULA F75 Pro Wireless Mechanical Keyboard. Right out of the box, it feels like a premium product. The build quality is solid and has a nice weight to it, so it stays firmly in place and doesn’t slide around during use. One of my favorite things about this keyboard is the sound. The clicking is super satisfying without being overly loud—it just has that perfect mechanical feel that makes typing enjoyable. The RGB lighting is another standout feature. At first, I didn’t realize there was software available, but once I found the link at the bottom of the product page and installed it, the level of customization blew me away. You can really dial in the exact colors and effects you want. Overall, this keyboard exceeded my expectations. Great feel, great sound, and excellent customization options. Definitely a solid buy.

I bought this keyboard for my husband and switched the keycaps to fit his aesthetic as well as so he can read a bit better. (He’s new to the computer club used to be console and he’s got bad eyesight from the military.) so in the picture the keycaps are changed but not the switches! The original keycaps it comes with is a grey with the letters, symbols, and words on the side. Even though I swapped them out I want to state they are absolutely excellent quality, super soft matte feel, and low profile. I kept the keycaps for future use instead of tossing them or offering them up to my family. Which is what I usually do with manufactured keycaps. So, that’s how good they are! That and they honestly are an absolutely gorgeous color in person despite just being greytones. Now onto more of the benefits this keyboards the forth of fifth I’ve customized (I just customize as a hobby for friends and family) This one though is the first of this brand and oh my gosh do I regret not buying this brand sooner! Mainly for myself because of all the bonuses with this keyboard. Haha. Firstly, the keyboard came in awesome packaging and when I realized it can be used wirelessly too! Absolutely fantastic! I didn’t check for that before purchasing so it was a super awesome surprise! And the quality too my husband has absolutely loved getting to use his new keyboard and he got so giddy with the RGB too. I feel like building wise too this is a great keyboard for beginners. If you want a nice keyboard that has easy hot-swappable capabilities this is definitely where to start! And the volume button is such a bonus too. It makes accessibility count with this keyboard. That along with how compact it is too it takes such little space. To put into retrospect his desk is only I think 38 inches width and he still has plenty of room on each side of his desk for his snacks and drinks because of how little space the keyboard is. Literally no issues have come from the keyboard, it even with his wonky usb ports (a custom built computer composed of old/used parts.) it works well and doesn’t have any connectivity issues. So, to put all the perks together: -compact and comfortable -easy to swap keycaps around and switches —switches it came with are the perfect click for those who don’t like it to be an overbearing sound. —perfect for beginners of customizing keyboards. -Volume nob to control volume with easy access rather than fighting around your desk to get to the speaker control. -has wired, Bluetooth, and dongle capabilities which cleans up wire management. — Battery life is great so charging doesn’t happen as often and it lasts even longer with rgb turned off. - I almost forgot: also, has amazing presets of rgb colors that are fun and is perfect for zoning out to when you are having writers or artist block. Now, for the jealousy caption. I need to save up to get me one too! Because, this keyboard is everythingggg and I am definitely in need of an upgrade from my wired keyboard as well as all the perks of this keyboard. Definitely, looking forward to customizing one for myself down the line! This company is for sure my go too for keyboards. I highly recommend! For now I’ll just enjoy seeing the smile on my husband’s face every time he looks at his keyboard while we game together! The best Christmas purchase I’ve ever made!
