review_title: Excelente calidad por el precio, el mejor teclado que he tenido
body_en: First of all, if you don't have much knowledge of mechanical keyboards and want to start with this keyboard, it is a very good option. The quality is felt from the moment you take it out of the box, it is a heavy keyboard and that does not mean it is bad, it feels very good to type on it, plus the sound is quite different from a keyboard that normally comes with a new computer or that you simply bought a cheap one at a Walmart or on the internet, it sounds firm and good when typing. Compared to cheaper keyboards, these mechanical switches are very sensitive, I am not referring to their duration, but to the force necessary to press them since the force needed is minimal, which makes them less burdensome for long days at the computer. It has several RGB lighting modes, for my part I only have it in white and at a moderate brightness, because yes, the brightness of the backlight is quite a bit. Another thing that I liked is that you can check the keyboard battery with the key combination: FN + B. Which is very useful since it does not have another battery indicator. Just to conclude, it is an excellent keyboard that is very worth it, and if you find it at a discount, do not hesitate to purchase it.
As a developer, it is very important to have a good keyboard. It just arrived and so far the weight, feel, connectivity are excellent. I hope it lasts long enough.

review_title: Great keyboard, definitely happy with the purchase - great price too.
body_en: Easily the best keyboard I've ever bought, and I've bought some high-tier brands in the past for over a hundred dollars. It comes with a keyswitch tool, extra switches, and does not feel cheap in quality. It also sounds nice when typing. It's that kind-of "muted clack" sound. Hard to describe such things but that's my best shot at it. The size is standard array and my fingers feel good on it. I was able to switch out my keycaps for WASD (I prefer circular key caps for those) and the caps do not clash with the other caps what-so-ever. The wireless bluetooth and plugged in modes both work well; I was able to use it wirelessly for about 3 days of near-constant use before having to plug it in. Honestly, I just left it plugged in since then so not sure how well the battery is on a recharge. The lights are appealing, the keys look nice; the color scheme is kinda abstract but I'm not mad about it. Overall, great keyboard, and it's held up for a couple months now with no degradation. Thanks Redragon. Appreciate a good product.

I would highly recommend this keyboard and company. It worked great for some time and then within the 2 year warranty period, my num1 key started acting up. I use my num pad just enough for it to be bothersome. I reached out to the company with the issue and supporting documentation and they were kind enough to get me a new one sent out, same model and everything. I love the sound of the keyboard, the ergonomics are fantastic, the size is comfortable, it responds that way you think it would/should and is compatible with every program I use. Great product! And YES, you should buy it!

review_title: Bought both keyboards so I could compare
body_en: (TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting. If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more! - - - - - I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more. One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both! So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences: RBG LED (White Logo) On Box: Sindri Red Dragon Price: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option) Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol) Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable though Lighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work use RGB QWERTY (Red Logo) On Box: Rudra Red Dragon Price: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh) Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud either Base: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier. Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use - - - - - My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!

review_title: Cheap price for a great Keyboard
body_en: This Redragon keyboard is a cheap and very well-rounded keyboard. Keys are smooth with a very satisfying mechanical sound. A lot quieter than pervious mechanical keyboards I've had int the past. The RGB lights are vibrant and have a couple different options for customization. I just bought it recently and the keyboard program to customize the lights is not the best. Those are the reason I'm leaving a four-star review. Other than that, I think this is a great keyboard for the price!

review_title: Works Fine. Not too big. Great value
body_en: Works fine so far. Love me some red switches. A nice, satisfying "thock". It is not too big even though it has the ten key pad. Illumination options are fine. Good quality and value if it holds up. Got it on sale for $25. That is the price of a decent membrane keyboard. This is mechanical switches so better value.

Sounds great, feels great. Nothing fancy. I did notice the the keys are quite responsive and don’t need to be pressed down all the way to activate. Very comfortable to type and game on. The material isn’t anything fancy but it gets the job done. Just a simple usb port and I can even connect to my Xbox. Great compatibility and very happy with the product

Very nice bit of kit, I've used this keyboard for over a year and the only issue is one of the number keys stopped providing a backlight. It still functions as a number key but no light. At first, I thought I needed to replace the key connection. But after doing that. It still is not providing a backlight.

review_title: Decent for a deal, but could be more durable.
body_en: I wouldn't buy this keyboard for more than thirty dollars, but it goes on sale enough that I believe it's worth buying for the twenty or so dollars the bring the price down to. I've had this keyboard for over a year, and it's worked flawlessly for most of that time. There's not much to say about it, functionally. It's a standard full-sized mechanical keyboard. It's not quiet, but I like how clicky it is, personally. Now, for the reason I don't recommend you buy this for full price. About nine or ten months into owning this item, the keys started to behave finicky. The 'R' key no longer lights up and the 'A' key has a problem with double inputs. I'll give the keyboard this, I use it a lot. I'm a writer and a gamer, so I've really put it through its paces. I'm also not as anal about maintenance as I probably should be. If you regularly dust and clean under the keycaps, it would probably last you a good deal longer. If your like me, someone who puts your keyboard through heavy use, I would go with something more durable. If you only intend to game with it, it should be fine for about a year, which for twenty dollars is a fine deal.
My favourite brand of inexpensive mechanical keyboards. I have three, one very old, and all work just fine.
Keys are in English only

My 12yo son LOVES it for the multi-coloured light effect and my 17yo son nabs it at every opportunity! I've marked it down a star as I find the keyboard 'clacky' to type on but for gaming that's not a requirement.

review_title: Works great, lasts forever, LEDs not very bright
body_en: The keyboard and mouse work well. The keys are good quality. They both have been working for years with no problem. They LEDs are a little dim though; they’re not the brightest I’ve seen.

The cable is different than advertised. The RGB is a single ugly static mode. The only customisation is to turn off or on specific keys RGB. For example the Q key is always an ugly yellow static backlight that can be turned off but not changed colours. The keyboard is hot swappable but good luck getting any of the switches out with how tightly they are fitted. This means that the board is effectively NOT hot swappable.

review_title: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
body_en: It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so. This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to. It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever. As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience. The only complaint from my daughter is that it doesn't have colored backlight. It's just plain white.

If you need a keyboard that fits in a crowded desktop or you just like a clean and neat desk looks, and if you work with applications that require precision on what you type, coding, CAD, the feel and precision of a mechanical keyboard is what you need. Love it. I've heard it's great for games too, but I don't play games at all, so I can't tell, but I bet durability required for games is similar to software coding, tons of strokes per minute. Games are certainly more rough, due to adrenaline, that can be hard on a keyboard. Not my thing, I need precision, and compact format.

So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below. -The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch. -Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment. -Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.) One minor negative is the backlight. The first problem was even getting the keyboard to light up at all. The keys for the keyboard backlight simply did not seem to function at all, no matter if I had the FN key held or not. Puzzled, I installed logitech's software and looked for options there. No luck. A bit annoyed at this point. Luckily, their software offered me access to an upcoming beta version of their software, "Logitech Options", so I downloaded that to poke around and see if there were more settings there. As it turns out there were. Oddly, they didn't work though. The keyboard refused to light up, the keys meant to dim or brighten it doing nothing at all. As I began a search to see if this was a common issue, the backlight finally came on. No idea what changed. Pretty standard white LED backlights. Lots of pissed off customers on forums about it though. Apparently, Logitech has been pretty silent about the issue. I'd be pissed too, if my $200 keyboard didn't have a functioning backlight due to software issues. With that rambling anecdote, the backlight itself is just fine, about what I expected for a professional keyboard like this. Just clean white LEDs. In summary, a very nice looking, nice feeling premium keyboard. Pretty unassuming in a professional environment. Easy setup. Quite happy with it. Edit: The backlight does not seem to remember brightness settings between use sessions, so if you will get super annoyed or angry about having to hit brightness up each time you use, that's something to consider. Most annoyingly, if the room is deemed "too bright" by the sensor, the backlight will not turn on at all. Understandable, but I'd still like the option.

I replaced a Logitech 860 with the MX, the quality and feel of the MX is very good. I love the feel of the keys. The key setup is more tighter than the 860, but after a couple days I’ve became accustomed to it and I like it. The difference in the feel and quality is significantly better than the 860.

I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard. First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off. I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is... And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck. At first I thought I just had to adjust the timeout settings on the Logi Options+ app. Nope! No options! Just a couple of annoying, distracting backlight animations (like, random keys illuminating, why would anyone want that?!). I'm not sure who signed-off on the design for this thing or what they were thinking. Furthermore, the caps lock key has a distracting blinking whenever it is on, especially annoying if you are gaming and caps lock is set to something like toggle run/walk. The keyboard is Bluetooth only, which seems to work fine. But I would have liked to have the option to plug it in like a normal USB keyboard. As far as I know the USB plug is only for charging, but also leaves an always illuminated and fairly bright "charging" LED, very obnoxious if your computer is in your bedroom. In short: Don't waste your money on this. I will be returning mine.

I just finished my first long work session with this keyboard. I'm glad I bought it. It's very easy to type on. It's my first mechanical keyboard of any kind. I went with the quieter version. You still get the clicking sounds, just not super loud. I finally understand what people mean when they say typing on a mechanical keyboard feels more satisfying compared to non-mechanical ones. Highly recommend this keyboard if you're looking to get into mechanical keyboards. Definitely won't be my last.

Original review: It's a keyboard an it works After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing). I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had. Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that. For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software. Honestly, at this price, I am not sure I would recommend this keyboard. Ok, so why 4 stars? It does have some positive points. First, it looks pretty sharp. Second, aside from not sitting flat, it feels solid / well-built / quality. It is small, yet it is heavier than most keyboards. I am used to keyboards lasting "forever", so I will update here if/when I run into issues. Third, switching between different machines works flawlessly. Fourth, it allows me to bring my settings to all computers (e.g. remapping the screen capture key). Fifth, it has a rechargeable battery and it lasts long enough that I never have to worry. I do have a charging cable right on my desk, so every once in a while I just leave it plugged in, so I have never seen it go below 85%. What else can I say, it is a keyboard and it works. ----- Updated review: beware the USB dongles. Logitech mouses and keyboards (e.g. "MX Mechanical", "MX Master 3s", "MX Anywhere 3") connect either via Bluetooth, or via a USB dongle. However, the USB dongles are not all the same. For example, the "MX mechanical" keyboard only connects to a "bolt" dongle; and the "MX Anywhere 3" mouse only connects to a "unifying" dongle. Unfortunately, there is no clear guide / summary for which devices go together. You just have to check each device before buying to see what dongle it uses. Devices in the same generation are *not* guaranteed to use the same type of dongle. Here is my experience: I setup for myself a MX mechanical keyboard + MX Master 3s mouse and everything works fine. Both devices connect to a "bolt" dongle, so I have a "bolt" dongle on my laptop, and another "bolt" dongle on a desktop computer. I can switch between laptop and desktop with a press of a button. The keyboard/mouse itself is fine, the review can be seen above. My wife saw my setup and wanted the same, but she didn't want the MX Master 3s mouse ("it is too big"), so I got her a this same "MX Mechanical" keyboard and a pink "MX Anywhere 3". As it turns out, the mouse does not come with a "bolt" dongle, it comes with a "unifying" dongle. So now I have one "bolt" dongle which connects only to the keyboard, and one "unifying" dongle which connects only to the mouse. Thus, to "fix" this situation, I either need to use Bluetooth for everything (which I was trying to avoid to begin with), or I need to purchase 1 extra bolt dongle and 1 extra unifying dongle, so that each computer has both a "unifying" and a "bolt" dongle. Let's hope I have enough USB ports, or I will also need a USB hub. Even if you are aware that different dongles exist, you still need to be careful. If you buy a "MX Anywhere 3", you get a "unifying" dongle, but if you buy a "MX Anywhere 3 for business", then it has a "bolt" dongle. This is, by the way, how I ended up with a "unifying" dongle - while browsing the products, I opened up two tabs, one with a black MX Anywhere 3, and one with a pink MX Anywhere 3, except one of them was "for business" and the other was not. You might think this mess would warrant giant disclaimers ("DOES NOT HAVE A BOLT CONNECTOR"), or some kind of guide for which devices go together, but nope. For extra hilarity, Amazon bundles a "MX mechanical mini" (bolt) with a "MX Anywhere 3" (unifying). The whole thing is confusing, misleading, and just terrible user/customer experience. If I could start over, I would just get something else.

review_title: Lovely Product - but US layout not clear in product description
body_en: Product is excellent, but be aware this is a US layout keyboard. If you want a UK layout (or European) you need to look for this specifically on Amazon.

This keyboard is pretty amazing. I own a HHKB, and a Pok3r. I build and customize my own keyboards. I bought this mainly because of the Logitech Flow feature. But first, I wanted to talk about the keyboard itself and why I think this is the best office keyboard to date. The build quality is amazing. It's sturdy, and the internals are very tight, which means, no rattling, no added noise or reverbiation. As a result, this is a very quiet mechanical keyboard (I can only speak for the brown switch version). The keycaps are made out of recycled plastic, but they don't feel cheap. They are quite smooth and easy to type with. The typing experience is very consistent and smooth (see type test photo). My typing speed is consistent with my other keyboards, but for me, it's definitely feels much better to type with tactile silent switches compared to my other keyboards. Even though this keyboard is a low profile keyboard, there are flip up feet at the bottom of the keyboard to lift it up a little more to get a better angle if that's what you prefer. The lights are nice, but what makes this keyboard really stand out is when it doesn't use the lights at all. Without the backlights on, this keyboard can do 10 months on 1 charge, which is completely unheard of for a mechanical full size wireless keyboard. I've had this keyboard for a couple of days on the whole time, and by now, my other wireless 60% would have died and required a recharge. There is only one issue with this keyboard which is customization. For Macros, only some of the keys (F Keys and Cursor Targeting Group) can be customized vs what I am used to, which is being able to customize every single key. For customizing the physical look itself such as changing the switches or the keycaps, this keyboard cannot be customized like that. The spacebar doesn't use standard stabilizer stem widths. You can replace every key cap except for the spacebar. You also cannot change the switches unless you know some soldering which is not recommended. As for the reason why I bough the keyboard. I absolutely love it! The logitech flow option allows me to move from my multiple computer setups with only one keyboard and mouse. I often multitask, I have a computer running 24/7 as my "smart tv" as well as my personal laptop, and my work computer. Considering how I can flow through all those computers from one set of mouse and keyboard without having to physically switch the mouse to use that specific computer is absolutely game changing. I feel like I am using one computer, even though they are all completely seperated. Whenever a product can make someone's life easier, is when you know you have something truly revolutionary. For work and every day use, this is absolutely the best office keyboard to date.

review_title: An Excellent Successor to the Venerable K800 Wired/Wireless Keyboard - Different but AWESOME!!
body_en: I really like this keyboard!!! In fact, I would say that this is a good/reasonable successor to the magical, venerable K800 Wireless and Wired I (like most) have an old wired K800 (attached to my work laptop), and was sooooo sad to see that I couldn't get another one. I took the leap and purchased the K800 wireless as a backup (what I writing this on..) for my personal laptop, and it truly is such a wonderful easy feeling keyboard. Again, logitech has discontinued the wireless one - enter to MX Keys (full size) I think that this one has that old school IBM-style feel, yet waay more robust, heavy (surprisingly), and modular (regarding key caps and triggers) I think, if past is prologue (as it invulnerably i..) this product to will either disappear, or get worse - I will by a 1 or 2 for safe keeping

review_title: Does not state that this is a US keyboard layout (on sale in the UK)
body_en: This is a US layout keyboard on sale in the UK... but no mention of that on the description.

review_title: Excellent keyboard with a few minor issues
body_en: This keyboard is a solid little keyboard. It’s very well built and has a satisfying feel and noise while typing. I really like how easy it is to switch between different computers. I have it set to use both my desktop PC and my MacBook Air when I dock it on my desk. It knows which is which and changes the keyboard layout accordingly. Everything just works. The battery life is excellent and it charges up really quickly over usb c. The Logitech Options app is really easy to use with everything laid out in such a way to just make sense. Also; the back lighting is simple but still nice. Ok onto my complaints. First I wish the key caps were a better material. They get glossy really quick from the slightly dirtiest fingers. I dunno if that’s due to the dark grey colour or the material itself. But for the price it should have better key caps. Second; I wish this thing had full rgb backlighting. The white is nice; but full colour would be better. Ok that’s it. So overall this is a great desktop keyboard that you could also take with you if you wanted to use your laptop or iPad on the go with it. It’s great for multi device use and the typing experience is really nice!! If you’re coming from the keyboard that came with your Mac or PC… or want something small and portable; this is definitely for you!

review_title: Light, bright, responsive, and with a wonderful profile layout
body_en: Best keyboard I've ever owned. Sturdy case, sleek profile, the layout makes this keyboard incredibly easy to clean without the need to dismantle the keys in the process. The White LEDs are bright and easy to see in the dark, unlike many backlit keyboards that can make it harder to read the keys. The responsiveness both in typing and in the tactile feel of every key clacking on release is a delight. I was skeptical when the sale brought the price below $35, but I could not be more impressed with the quality upon arrival. As a friend has been using a slightly different G4 model for 5 years, I have every expectation that I will be using this keyboard for years to come. Very happy customer.

review_title: Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.
body_en: I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated. After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games. As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium. Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

review_title: Great Mechanical Keyboard for gaming or surfing the web.
body_en: Satisfying but quiet clicks, decent lighting, solid construction, and amazing responsiveness give this keyboard a 5 ⭐ from me. I game pretty much everyday and Logitech is the only keyboard/mouse company I find worthwhile AND affordable. As a major plus, it's also very ergonomic and easy to use for long periods of time.

review_title: Perfect for me. Really like it.
body_en: Just got it so not a complete review. But so far, I really like it. I'm not a gamer, but just needed a keyboard upgrade and this is perfect. So far :) Note: True, there are no painted letters/numbers on the keys. Once usb plugged in, everything is seen with the backlight on the keys. I figured out the reason: painted letters and numbers wear off after a while. This see-through letters/numbers (presumably) will always remain. You don't use the keys unless plugged in anyhoo! So, I see no problem! It's very nicely weighted and has a nice feel on the keys. Great for the $35 price I paid!

review_title: Not the best choice for Mac; satisfying click but not for quiet environments
body_en: I can't tell you how well this works for gaming, but if you're looking to buy this as a Mac keyboard for standard daily use, definitely read on. This keyboard is far better for a PC. It doesn't have matching keys for a Mac keyboard, so you'll have reduced functionality with key commands. These are differences I've come across so far: - Instead of a CMD key on both sides of the space bar, this keyboard has only one on the left of the spacebar that functions that way, and it's not in the position of the usual Mac CMD key. (see my pic) - There's no volume control on this keyboard, so you'll have to have your Mac keyboard available to change volume unless you keep volume control visible on your menu bar. - Screen dimming requires holding this keyboard's fn key and then using F1 or F2. - Some special function keys on this keyboard don't do anything on a Mac. Here's what I do like about the keyboard: - Satisfying click. The keys are like old school keyboards with large keys that actually had feel to them. The volume of the click is kind of loud though, so if you need to maintain a quieter environment this keyboard won't do. - The attached 10 key is nice to have. - It's corded so no batteries required. - The keyboard is sturdy feeling with just-right weight to it - The key backlighting is adjustable - No quick trigger keys means no accidental double lettering - Because the keyboard rises high off your desktop compared to modern keyboards, make sure you have a seating position that lets you keep your hands lower than normal. Overall this keyboard is probably great for gaming or for PC users who don't have to keep it down while using it. If you're a Mac user, especially one who needs a quiet environment, you should look at different models.

review_title: Great keyboard with backlight with mechanical keys.
body_en: This is a mechanical keyboard. That means it is noisy where it has the traditional keyboard sound. I personally love it! The key are far more responsive than the soft-touch keyboards that are mostly used today. The clicking of the keys could be distracting to someone sharing an office, however, if you work in a private office, this keyboard is great. Also, the keyboard is backlit which makes it that much more useful when working late nights in a darker environment. It is constructed of metal and has a slip resistant base that stays put on my keyboard slide.

I've been very happy with this keyboard for everyday work use. The mechanical keys have a great feel and make typing much more enjoyable, especially during long periods of writing and data entry. The build quality feels solid, and the keyboard has a clean, professional look that fits well in an office setup.

I am not impressed, compared to an old and cheap Steelseries Apex 100 (Fuhlen rubber dome) I've had since the late 2010s. This keyboard has taught me that I really dislike backlit keyboards. Even on its lowest backlight setting, it is distracting, and the keycaps are not visible with it off. I haven't used a good mechanical keyboard in quite some time but I did not enjoy the typing feel of this one. The keys are subjectively spongy and stiff. Sadly, it is boxed up for return and was not meant to be. I will still give it three stars as the build quality seems solid and I think it would work well for someone who is not bothered by bright backlighting and enjoys the distinctive feel of these keys.
Very good

I am using this keyboard right now to type this review. I got one of these for work, and I like it so much I bought another one for home. The brown switches have tactile feedback, but no audible click. The feel and sound of these keys while typing is very satisfying. This keyboard is a bit noisy, but I haven't heard any complaints about that so far. I much prefer this mechanical keyboard to my old membrane keyboards. I am still getting used to it, so I make a few typos, but the frequency of them is diminishing. Build quality is excellent, the chassis is aluminum. There is no pointless, annoying RGB backlighting. Only the keys light up, which makes it easy to use in the dark. I would recommend this keyboard. It's more expensive than membrane keyboards, but I think it's worth the extra money.
Excellent, smooth when pressing the keys. Some noise, but I like the sound. It does not have programmable keys. It feels durable.

review_title: I liked it so much I used it to write this review!
body_en: I wanted to wait a couple months before writing this review, give myself time to decide my opinion. Well, I would say it is excellent, one can usually rely on Logitech to provide a good product and this is a prime example. The noise level is not the loudest I have heard from mechanical keyboards. Besides, if you want the responsiveness of a mechanical keyboard, you have to expect and accept a certain level of click-clack. I use it mostly to play games and secondly to write stories, as such it works well. While I do not play professionally, or online, nor care to, during my usage I have not noticed any lag or ghosting. In particular, I like the while lighting, it is not strong, but not weak either, allowing me to see the keys in any lighting situation. Which I appreciate, as the popular RGB keyboards are a bit too "loud" for me. It is also very tight and small for a mechanical, and fits comfortably on a small desk. I highly recommend this keyboard!
The person who gave it to him loves the Logitech brand and was very happy so I think it's very good

Bought this for my wife’s WFH setup. She fell in love with the Creamy Switch craze on TikTok and this was a reasonably priced keyboard that fit the bill. I found a cute sakura themed keycap set to replace these, but she said she’d have been happy with the blues and purples that came preinstalled. It looks great, feels and sounds fantastic, and does everything you’d want from a keyboard. She loves the size, specifically that it includes the number pad. Not enough decent keyboards do these days. People want minimalism in everything, but the functionality of a dedicated number pad is hard to beat. Connecting is super easy. We’re using the hardwired USB-C option, but I was able to use Bluetooth on my laptop at work while I was testing and installing the other keycaps prior to giving this as a birthday gift. She loves that it’s such a lightweight feel of typing, even noticeably so to someone without the heavy handed typing of myself, having grown up on IBM and Alps switches which allow for some decent banging. I’m not a keyboard snob or really a deep enthusiast, but some of my friends and coworkers that care more than I do really loved it as well. It’s a crowd pleaser, and that wonderful little subdued THOK on each tap is soothing as foretold.

review_title: Perfect for work and the sound is ohh so goood!!!
body_en: I LOVE this keyboard!! After spending two weeks researching I decided on the Aula F99 and I am so happy with my decision. I’m not a gamer but wanted a full keyboard for work and this checked all the boxes. The sound is so creamy and reminds me of marbles or smooth stones. It’s so fun to type on and the RGB is kinda fun too. Bluetooth connected with ease, so did wired. Haven’t tried the dongle yet but so far it’s been plug and play play with no issues. Feels sturdy not cheap. Sounds great out of the box. Ordered the Gatreon Milky Yellow switches but I may not even need them cuz I’m kinda digging this sound already. It’s soooo satisfying. Great value!!

review_title: First mechanical keyboard ever - love it!
body_en: Perfect right out of the box. Set up was effortless. I love the simple and minimalist look and layout of it. I decided to swap my old HP wireless keyboard that I use for work out for this one and while it's a tad bit louder than I expected for snall office settings, I still love the sound and feel of it. It is definitely "stockier" than expected for plastic. Bit on the heavyside in comparison to a standard HP keyboard. Feels good and solid though. I've been using it all day and have no complaints so far. Small side note: if you're a dingus like me, the ÷ key on the number pad is the same as /. Took me a minute to figure that out because I'm so used to / + - * 🤣

review_title: Bought it for my husband and now it's mine
body_en: First I want to say that I initially bought this for my husband as he had bought a walmart clicky brand keyboard and was finally growing tired of the clicky sound lol. Well as the keyboard enthusiast I suggested this one as it was simple and a few of the review videos had sounded promising. When it arrived the first thing I noticed was the heft, this was made with durable material and not light weight at all, which put some ease to my mind that it wasn't just made of cheap plastic. The size was just perfect, I couldn't be happier, and when I typed for the first time the creamy and thocky sound just itched the right place in my brain. I could not get enough of it. I love that there are 3 types of way that you can connect, BT; Dongle or wired. I always prefer wired. The keycaps are nice, although I prefer rounded keycaps to the sharp square ones, I did replace the factory keycaps and I just fell in love with this more. The switches sound nice and deep and honestly, this is almost perfect for me, I'll be playing around with this keyboard especially since it's hot swappable and I might try other switches. For those just starting out with interest in the keyboard area, this is a great first start with a not too expensive price point! I did end up having to buy another keyboard for my husband since I stole this one, it was definitely worth it though! Can't wait to mod this one a little more!

Coming up on almost a year of owning this keyboard. It was just what I needed. I love the feel of the keys, the sound, the 3 different options to connect, the weight and the number pad. The battery life wireless is okay. I wish there was a power button. Sometimes you accidentally touch a key after turning off the computer and the keyboard feels like it stays on forever lol. I use it for my WFH job and light gaming. I bought it last April and now it’s February and I’m starting to notice connection issues (non responsive) and sticky keys. It’s been acting a bit possessed lately. I work with a lot of VDIs so that could also play apart in the weirdness but it’s been more and more frequent lately. I use the Bluetooth option, I will try to hardwire to see if there is a difference. Will update my review if it poops out 🤔🤔

I’ve had this keyboard for almost 2 months now and wanted to wait to write a review until I had used it for a while. I’ve got to say this keyboard is awesome. recently got a WFH after only ever working in an office so I knew I wanted to invest in a nice keyboard. I spent at least a week researching and reading reviews on keyboards and didn’t realize how hard it would be to find nice keyboard with a num pad but I kept coming back to this one because of the amazing reviews and of course I love the way it sounds! For the average person yes this is a little bit on the pricier side but to me it was totally worth it, I like that it has 3 forms of connection (Wired, Bluetooth, and USB), there are a million different RGB options and it sounds amazing and it comes with super easy instructions and you can change the key caps if you want nicer keys. I will say, as you can see in the video I have two keys where the lighting under them doesn’t work/ change color, but I still have it 5 stars because it doesn’t affect the function of the key board. Another slight inconvenience is that you do have to charge it with the wire after a few days if you’re using Bluetooth or USB and it doesn’t give a low power warning but besides that it’s perfect. I also want to note that I have seen that this key board had gone a little viral on TikTok and I did purchase before it was trending so I would say if you are coming here from TikTok no, it’s not a scam it’s actually a great keyboard!

The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests. It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one. The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that. I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

review_title: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
body_en: AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.

review_title: Best board for the price, BY FAR !!
body_en: Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time. I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect. It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate. My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable. For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.

Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard. It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set. But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me. All of that at this price point makes this a really, really, really good option and one that I can absolutely recommend.

review_title: Amazing, and truly worth the price.
body_en: It's a truly amazing keyboard, it feels great, looks great, and sounds great. I have only one issue with it, it's loud, but that's only an issue at night. The ergonomics feel pretty good, and the switches are very nice and responsive. Everything feels high quality, especially for this price. Very worth it and affordable. The backlight is a nice touch, it can be disabled and enabled, along with changing the color and speed. Note: "Mom if you're seeing this, I wrote this review" -your son.

review_title: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
body_en: This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable. My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

This keyboard sounds even better than the reviews claim. Before buying, I came across a few comments suggesting that some of the internal padding had been removed or that the overall quality had declined as the keyboard became more popular. After using it myself, I can confidently say that those concerns were unfounded. The build quality is excellent, the typing experience is incredibly satisfying, and the switches feel fantastic. Every keypress sounds and feels premium, making it a joy to use for both work and gaming. So far, I’ve only tested the 2.4GHz wireless mode, so I can’t comment on the wired or Bluetooth performance. However, based on my experience, I have no hesitation recommending it. For the price, this keyboard offers outstanding value. It was absolutely worth the wait, especially considering I ordered it from the US and had it shipped to South Africa.

review_title: Comfortable, creamy sound, easy set up.
body_en: Set up was a breeze, simply plug in. It charges in a few hours. This keyboard is really nice. I like the “creamy” sound other viewers have described. A VERY light touch is all you need to type. I won’t say it’s sensitive, it just requires a light touch of each key. That is something I need to get used to. I have a laptop set up on a riser, and needed a keyboard that will fit in the small space beneath it. This was my choice after reviewing MANY keyboards. I also wanted a laptop with raised keys, a mechanical keyboard. I like the “old school” feel of it. Weight: it’s heavy. I won’t be traveling with it, so that doesn’t matter to me. But I love the heaviness of it. Feels secure in its spot. Ergonomics: there are two levels if you want to change the angle. Three is you count not using the little feet at the back. I also have a padded hand/wrist rest for extra comfort (NOT INCLUDED) but the keyboard itself is comfortable to use. Color: I would have preferred black to match my desk accessories and laptop, or blue my favorite color. I went for the least expensive option as the color doesn’t change the effectiveness of the device. Lights: it’s advertised as a gaming keyboard. I’m not a gamer, nor will I ever be. You CAN turn off the lights. Simply read the paperwork that comes in the package to know how.

review_title: Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables
body_en: The keyboard exceeded my expectations in the essentials: very pleasant “thock” sound, firm keystrokes and three connection modes that work without problem. The construction feels solid; The plastic is thick and clean to the touch, better quality than other models in its range. Pros: Excellent feel and linear response. Bass-creamy sound from the factory, without the need for mods. Very good value for the price: it is close to “custom” features of higher ranges. Points for improvement: The management software was useless on two PCs. The page is confusing, and although the keyboard was recognized, it offered no real configuration options. The back uses a simpler plastic, and the non-slip rubbers are glued with double-sided tape that began to peel off from the first day. I'm worried they will get lost or need to be replaced soon. Does not include numpad: ideal for gaming and writing, but can be limiting for those who use numerical input a lot. Conclusion: An excellent gateway to the “custom” world for its sound, touch and connectivity, as long as you do not depend on the software or need a full keyboard. Side note (does not influence product rating): tracking took four days to update; The package arrived without damage, but the logistics process, communication and professionalism on the part of the seller can improve.
Excellent Product

review_title: BEST KEYBOARD I HAVE EVER USED. WORTH EVERY PENNY.
body_en: Honestly, I am absolutely blown away with the quality of this kisnt KN85, it's hands down the best keyboard I have ever owned. First of all, the sound quality of the key click is insane, this thing is so thocky with the bsun switches, PBT double shot key caps, gasket mounts and multiple layers of dampening foam/silicone, genuinely such a pleasure to type with. It is even hot-swappable if you want to change or upgrade your switches. The battery life is amazing, first use never charged out of the box lasted over a full week of heavy daily use. I find it very hard to find any fault with this keyboard whatsoever. One note is that the LED's are south-facing, so shine-through backlit keycaps won't work, I like double-shot caps for the thock, so this doesn't bother me one bit. But seriously, I have never been so happy to be typing at my desk. It has changed my whole experience. I watch reviews of £200-£500 keyboards, and I still think this is better. All I will say is get it fast, as prices are constantly rising due to demand.

looks and feels amazing, setup was easy and battery is lasting along time which is great. but the sound of the keyboard is so creamy, it really does sound like a premium keyboard. I also love the beige color scheme its very clean yet retro and the letters are bolded and of course its not a lousy 60% so you can enjoy all the key functions without having to press FN all the time

Awesome keyboard that punches above its weight. Stock switches are louder than I'd like, but hey it's a custom keyboard, so just swap them out easily for anything you like. For the price it's great keyboard. ONLY major issue is I like separate numpad controllers (I put these on the right of my mouse so it's quicker) but Kisnt only make these seperate numpads for the two other colour schemes that exist. The beige and green scheme is missing.

I’ve been using the RK Royal Kludge R98 Pro for a little over a week, and I’m honestly impressed with how much value this keyboard delivers. The moment you take it out of the box, it feels solid and well-built definitely not your typical budget keyboard. Typing Experience (5/5) The gasket mount design combined with the pre‑lubed linear switches makes typing incredibly smooth and quiet. It has that “creamy” feel everyone talks about. No pinging, no rattling just clean, soft keystrokes. The MDA profile PBT keycaps are thick, durable, and comfortable to type on. Design & Layout (5/5) I love the 96% layout. It saves desk space but still includes a full number pad, which I use constantly for work. The addition of the volume knob is a nice touch and works great for quick adjustments. RGB & Customization (4.5/5) The RGB is bright, vibrant, and offers a ton of effects. Customizing it is easy once you get familiar with the shortcuts. I only wish the software was a bit more intuitive, but it’s definitely not a deal‑breaker. Performance (5/5) For gaming, it’s responsive and stable with zero noticeable latency. Hot‑swappable sockets are a big win if you ever want to switch to different switches later. Overall If you’re looking for a keyboard that feels like a premium custom build for a fraction of the price, the RK R98 Pro is a fantastic choice. Great for both work and gaming, excellent build quality, and a super satisfying typing experience. Highly recommended!

So, i dont usually write reviews, but i felt i had to for this keyboards. the creamy clicks are AMAZING (its my first time having it so im super impressed.) the tiny screen is actually pretty simple and easy to use, you can customize the backlight color and style, speed, etc. the knob works perfect. feels great. it came with extra keys, a usb-c to plug in if you prefer wired, and a key remover. everything feels amazing, very high quality. its obviously not 10 pounds, but carries some heft that feels super secure. its got little folded stands to prop your keyboard up if desired, which i think is super nice. i love the color variety (i got the brown, for reference.), it can be hard finding a nice keyboard that is still stylish and pretty. im extremely satisfied, especially with the price being only 70 usd for this nice of a keyboard. i still have yet to use it, but im pretty confident it will be nice. ill update if anything happens!

review_title: I am surprised how much I actually like this keyboard
body_en: I recently purchased this item a couple of weeks ago and so I think it was a good purchase. First of all, they keyboard is super smooth and because of the switches, you do hear some clicks but they're not that loud, just enough to be satisfying. The product feels well-crafted with quality in mind. The keyboard stands; are the perfect size, not freakish large so typing for long periods of time is comfortable. I also like how they send you the "end" key in the box so if you don't like the volume knob, you can put the "end" key back in. I type 80 words a minute, especially when I am writing programs, I pleased on how well the keys on this board respond and the entire feeling of when a key is pressed. When I type superfast on things that are super important, I don't want my keyboard to fail me. Now, there are a few things I don't really like about it but overall, like I said, this is a great keyboard. - The volume knob: Hey, it works but personally, I feel that it is too close to the "pgdn" key so you really can't grip it like a knob. I kind of wished it had groves or something on the dial making it easier to turn. Right now, I just got to try and turn it little by little by spinning the know from the top down to the "-" key. That's about all the room you got. - Key position: This one is more of my fault. I am more used to full sized keyboards and not the space saving ones with less keys. The part that messes me up is where the arrows, shift, and enter is all smushed together. If this might also, be you, check out the S98 model instead. - Drivers and App: I can't really download this because the website is blocked at work for gaming lol. I don't know if the site is listed as gaming or if it is just because of their name. I know, this is totally not their fault haha.

I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing. Strengths: Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds. Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality. Build quality: PBT double-shot keycaps with an MDA profile feel sturdy and resist wear; they’re grippy and comfortable for long sessions. The detachable aluminum volume knob is a treat for instant control. Layout: The 98-key layout keeps the numpad and arrow keys but eliminates wasted space—a space-saving solution perfect for both gaming and work. Universal compatibility: Works perfectly with Windows and Mac out of the box, and includes both a 2-in-1 keycap/switch puller and extra switches for future customization. Bottom Line: This is an exceptional value for anyone who wants a customizable, quiet, and responsive keyboard for gaming, work, and creative projects. The smooth switches, full-featured software, and premium build make it a standout in its price range. Highly recommended for enthusiasts and everyday users alike.

So I upgraded my desk setup to include this keyboard. I did minimal research but I knew I liked the color and the number pad. After having it for several months: 1. The keyboard is indeed "creamy" and smooth 2. The lighting is fun and the quality of the board is very nice. 3. It has a good weight and the volume knob is very helpful. 4. I am glad I didn't go smaller 5. The key swap capability is nice but I don't use it a whole lot. Overall a good keyboard to replace my Bluetooth work one. I definitely think this a worthy upgrade if you're in need of one.

I was looking for a keyboard that had a nice compact profile, looked nice, has a volume control knob, AND sounds great when typing. THIS keyboard literally hits everything I was looking for. It's just the right size and weight - it looks and feels premium. The keys have that creamy/clacky sound I was looking for. The colors of the keys are great - but that being said - the backlights don't seem as bright as other keyboards I've owned, but that's not really a big deal to me - but it might be to some people. Overall - I love this keyboard - now I just hope it lasts. I've read some reviews that make it seem like it might not, but I'm hoping it's durable. As of this review, I've only had it for about an hour, so I'll update this review if anything changes with time.

review_title: Where sound, price, and comfort meet.
body_en: Absolutely worth the money, and even got it on sale! As I was looking for a replacement for my Logitech G512 that had finally started to show its age, after nearly 5 years of daily wear and tear from both games and general typing, I stumbled upon this board after seeing the shop it was inside of. I've been using it now for close to a week, and it has sealed the deal for my desire to build a keyboard once I have the means to do such. Each keycap having a small variance in its elevation by just a few millimeters may not sound like much, but it allows for a much smoother flow in typing and touch feel as you move through the keys. Additionally the sound the keyboard makes with the lubed switches below each key, effectively a quiet thunk-click is just beautiful. Its also much quieter than the G512 was, and is less noticed by people when I am speaking with them over the phone for work. So major win there! Solid 5/5 stars, if you need a keyboard for a good price and solid function - fully recommend.

review_title: Loved it so much I bought 2 of them
body_en: This keyboard is great, little heavy and only connects via USB, but as far as everything else you'll be pressed to find a better keyboard at this price range that is as satisfying to type on, cause the "creamy" switches sound like something that punches WELL above its weight. Nothing necessarily ergonomic about it but it does have a satisfying color to it and the lights aren't exactly offensive in terms of "too bright" If you're looking for wireless don't get this one, look at RK's other offerings but if you're okay only hooking up wired for work or other reasons this is going to be the one you want.
Very good & my son loves his new keyboard

"+" - Qualitative injection of key plastics, - Flattering appearance and robust chassis, - Not aggressive branding, - Super responsive, - The definition of the RGB backlighting is excellent and the LeD scenarios are good, - 98% really cool format. - Little parasitic vibration, - Excellent quality/price ratio, - Replacement set of a few switches and wheel replacement button if necessary. The RK ROYAL KLUDGE R98 Pro convinced me from the first moment. The workmanship is high quality, the keyboard appears stable and the compact 96% layout offers all the important keys including the number pad without taking up unnecessary space on the desk. I am particularly impressed by the pleasant typing feeling. The already lubricated switches run smoothly and sound pleasantly rich. I used to type 60wpm, now its 90wpm in only 1 week of having this keyboard. Its amazing for work!

Let's get straight the points. Advantages: - PBT keycaps. I don't know how to describe it but it feels great. Oh, the colors are nice too. - Support both Windows and Mac - The sound is nice - The Space button feels nice, very stable - Have PrintScreen (PRTSC) button (because I use this button a lot so this is a pro for me) - Have Numpad keys. As an accountant, this numpad never fails me lol. Disadvantages: - Requires a great force to press, but you can enhance this by replacing to other keycap layouts. I'm a typist, therefore I really care about this. - The brightness is okay, but I expect to have brighter LEDs. Oh well, that's all. This is a decent product. I recommend people buying this product. Please make sure that you choose the right product for your use. Thanks for reading.

This keyboard is probably the best one I've ever had. It is built so well. It is made mostly of some sort of aluminum. It does not bend at all and it just feels very nice. I have had a keyboard that was so cheap that it bent even when I was typing normally (I don't type very hard), so this was a nice change. The metal volume dial is very high quality, and yet again, just feels well-built. There is also a little button that controls 4 things. It will pause and play your music, skip to the next song, go to the previous song, and open up menus in the OLED display. The OLED screen is very nice. It could be a little brighter, and the larger pixels make it harder to display certain things. But, what makes up for that is that with the program you can install, you can download apps that will change what the screen says. My 2 favorites are Discord and System Monitor. They RGB lighting is really nice. Each light can be its own color and with the program, you can make your own lighting configurations. The keys sound very nice. They are clicky, but too clicky. They are also easy to press, but not so easy that I could see myself accidentally pressing one. It also comes with a wrist rest. It magnetically attaches and feels very smooth and high quality. Overall this keyboard just feels very premium and super high quality. I would recommend it to someone who wants a good keyboard with some very nice features from a good brand and does not mind spending the premium cost.

Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns. This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. This uses cherry stems and switches, and the keys are naturally a cherry profile, so finding aftermarket replacements/decorative keycaps is easy as well. The keys feel responsive and clicky, delightfully so, when gaming or typing for general purpose. But there's a catch; it's a hybrid, so not truly mechanical. It does feel very good, but I have concerns that the membrane will wear down in time as opposed to a true blue mechanical keyboard, which will stay responsive and snappy for a lesser eternity where membranes begin to show wear after a year of heavy use. Time will tell. The lighting is phenomenal - the LEDs are bright, responsive, and have great color depth and range compared to a lot of RGB hardware out there. You can use Steelseries' own software to customize and program this keyboard outside of the 5 existing presets saved onto the board's memory, but you can also use other third-party RGB control software like SignalRGB. All in, it's a quality keyboard for a great price; one wire connects everything, you have a stop/start button, a wheel for volume, and a built in profile-swap button, which is entirely unnecessary but quite nice.

review_title: SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)
body_en: The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. It’s a well-built keyboard with some excellent features and clever design choices. The cable is thick, long, and even has a nice touch — the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug. The RGB effects are top-notch, with smooth transitions both on keypress and when idle. I was genuinely excited about all of this... until I noticed what was missing. And for me, that’s a big deal. Let’s break it down.😁 ### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃 - Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient. - Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting. - Smart OLED Display: It shows the status of Num Lock, Caps Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Windows key is disabled. Very handy (though there’s a small catch — more on that below). - Customization & Visual Feedback: Besides full per-key RGB customization and reactive effects, pressing the “Fn” key (the SteelSeries logo key) lights up related function keys in red for quick reference. It’s super helpful… but again, not perfect (you can’t change the color — more on that too). - Profile Memory Built-In: You can save up to 5 profiles directly on the keyboard and toggle them on/off without cycling through all of them. I personally use just two: one for gaming and one for productivity. ### The Not-So-Good – My Gripes😒: - No Dedicated Context Menu Key: This is my biggest issue. A full-size keyboard should include the dedicated menu key (the "right-click menu" key). SteelSeries replaced it with their custom “Fn” key, which really disrupted my usual workflow. I ended up switching to Shift + F10 to keep things consistent across devices. - Fn Key Can’t Be Reassigned: The SteelSeries logo key, which replaces the context menu key, is fixed — it can’t be remapped. Personally, I’d have preferred having the Windows key only on the left, and using the right one for Fn, keeping the menu key in its usual place. - OLED Button Always Lit: The brightness of the button next to the OLED screen cannot be dimmed or turned off. If you’re working in a dark room or watching movies, this little light will keep shining at you — kind of annoying. - OLED Icons Overlap Custom Logos: If you upload a custom image to the OLED screen, the status icons for Num Lock, Caps, etc. may overlap your logo.
