Not a dealbreaker, but it limits how creative you can get with personalization. - No Visual Feedback When Windows Key Is Locked: Unlike other lock states (like Caps Lock), there’s no lighting change or visual indicator on the keyboard itself when the Windows key is disabled — just a small icon on the OLED. Feels inconsistent. - Function Key Highlight Color Can’t Be Changed: When pressing “Fn,” the related keys light up red — but that red is not customizable. If your RGB theme is red, this effect becomes basically invisible. - Slight Input Delay: There’s a small delay in key activation. I don’t notice it while typing or working, but for competitive gaming, it might matter. Rtings.com confirmed this in their testing too. - Non-Replaceable Hybrid Switches This is the most serious issue. The switches aren’t standard and can’t be replaced by the user. If a key fails, you’re stuck with relying on warranty, support… or scavenging another board. Not great. ### Neutral Points – Might Be Good or Bad Depending on You🤷🏻‍♂️: - Actuation Distance: I switched from a keyboard with ultra-light 0.8 mm actuation, and I kept typing extra characters. The Apex 5 feels much more precise and helped reduce typos — a big plus for me. - Key Feel & Keycaps: The keycaps aren’t made from premium material, but they feel decent. Coming from linear switches, the tactile feel took a bit of getting used to — but I adjusted quickly. - Magnetic Wrist Rest: I don’t use it much, but the magnets are strong and hold it firmly in place. - Macro Labeling (M1, M2, etc.): Some keys are labeled as macro keys (M1, M2...), which can be confusing at first — but you’ll get used to it. - Customization Without Software: You can change basic RGB effects and profiles directly from the keyboard. The software adds more depth, but it’s nice that you’re not forced to use it. - USB Plug with Logo: A small but smart touch: the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug helps you spot which device you’re plugging in. - No Physical Lock LEDs: The lock indicators (Num Lock, Caps, Scroll) have been moved to the OLED screen, and you can set those keys to change color when active. Some might miss the old-school LED lights, but I’m fine with it. ### Final Verdict 💸😇 The SteelSeries Apex 5 is a well-built, visually polished keyboard with great RGB, useful media controls, and a solid set of features for gamers and professionals alike. Still, a few oversights — especially the missing context menu key and the non-replaceable switches — keep it from being a perfect 5-star device in my eyes. If those flaws don’t bother you, then this keyboard is an easy recommendation. Just know what you're getting — and what you're not

review_title: Great entry mechanical keyboard with solid feel and comfort
body_en: I bought this for my 14-year-old, and it’s been a great keyboard for both gaming and schoolwork. The hybrid switches feel clicky and responsive without being overly loud, and the RGB is bright and customizable enough for their setup. The included wrist rest adds real comfort and doesn’t slide around. No issues with software or macros so far. It’s a well-rounded keyboard that feels more premium than its price suggests.

Excellent individual RGB keys. Cool but small LCD screen (But it displays my CPU temp, so I'm happy). Volume control is super handy, and it's compatible with SignalRGB. Not to mention this keyboards clicks sound amazing! If you're into the old school keyboard sound.

review_title: Nice keyboard - Amazon Refurbished just sucks
body_en: I have only had this keyboard for a few days at the time of this review, but from what I can tell it is a solidly built keyboard with a nice feel and decently responsive keys. I did have to knock off a star though as the keyboard I received was in poor condition with two of the keys having keypress detection issues. This however was NOT the fault of SteelSeries as I bought this one from Amazon Refurbished. Do NOT buy this keyboard from Amazon Refurbished. They do only the bare minimum to make the keyboard presentable, and do not open it to check the internals before shipping it. Or else they would have seen the gunk inside that was causing the key press detection issue. Thankfully, user maintenance was easy. Simple matter of taking off the key caps, taking out the cover screws, and the mainboard screws. Then I was able to clean it with a little alcohol and reassemble it. Works like it was new. Just didn't expect that I would have to be the one doing the refurbishing on day one. But that's why I gave it 4 stars, pretty easy to perform user maintenance on it to ensure that it continues to function. Which boggles me why Amazon didn't do that.

Got this to replace a $250 Razor keyboard that went out after four years with largely only work-related use. I have keyboards from the '90s that still work. Razor customer service didn't even respond to me. That being said, I'm happy with this one. Less than half the price and works just as well. So much, I bough one for my son as well!
Amazing! It has many cool features and sounds amazing. It’s full sized too so you don’t miss out on any extra keys.

review_title: Mi primer teclado mecánico. Totalmente satisfecho
body_en: Excellent build materials, extensive options to configure virtually anything on the keyboard, and great comfort. I went from a Logitech G213 "gamer" membrane keyboard to this SteelSeries Apex 5 and the difference can be noticed. From the widely configurable RGB effects through the SteelSeries GG software to the feel on the keys and wrist rest (which is made of a soft-touch plastic material), everything is super comfortable and high quality. Something that I really like about this keyboard is its small OLED screen in the upper right corner, which can be configured with a drawing, a GIF or with some of the integrations it has with some games or programs. I particularly use it to monitor my system and see the temperature of my CPU and GPU quickly and easily without having to run MSI Afterburner or RivaTuner SS. However, as I saw on the product page itself and in some reviews on YouTube, you could view the song you were listening to at the time, but from what I was able to investigate this is only possible if you use TIDAL and well, I use Spotify, so I didn't like this as much. The sound of the keyboard is noticeable and can be annoying if you are not used to it or if you live with someone else and usually use it at night not far from other people. The video I attached is very faithful (in my opinion) to the sound you get once the keyboard is in your hands. Something I would like to mention is that, even though the keyboard came well packaged along with other products, the keyboard box itself came with some extra tape on several sides, which made me a little doubt whether the product was new or used, but when I opened it I realized that it was new or in practically perfect condition, so I was calmer, but that extra tape detail on the box did not please me too much.

The keyboard is amazing. It has per key illumination which the software is very cool with. It gets recognised by signal rgb software so it syncs everything together. The feel is good it has mechanical clicks with membrane so doesn't feel like your bottoming out the keys.

I wanted a kind of middle road price RGB keyboard and I am in love with this one. The keys feel very satisfying and loud and clicky. The RGB support is great, I use signalRGB so that was a major selling point that it worked for that. I do wish it had better side controls for audio and even though you can pause spotify or whatever with the top right button it only pauses your last application which can be anything so that can be a bit annoying. The scroll wheel does work well for volume control though. Overall I do like it a lot, good colour and feel. Recommend for those who want something nice but dont want to drop 200
nice switches, almost cant feel the rubber dome, the hand rest feels great
Never knew what I was missing out on before I got this. So. Worth. It.

Just received my RisoPhy RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard and I'm already impressed! Unboxing was smooth — everything was well packaged and arrived in perfect condition. Right out of the gate, the mechanical switches feel fantastic — satisfying and responsive with great tactile feedback. Typing this review on it now and it already feels way better than my old membrane keyboard. The RGB lighting looks amazing — all 104 keys are individually backlit with tons of color and lighting mode options. Instantly upgraded the look of my desk setup. Build quality feels solid and premium — no flex, no creaking, and the keycaps have a nice, smooth texture. It's a standard full-size layout with number pad, so it was easy to jump right in with no learning curve. Can't speak to long-term durability yet, but based on first impressions, this keyboard seems like an excellent value. Will update if anything changes, but so far I'm very happy

Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age. The value of this keyboard is excellent. Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism. The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters. Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much. I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me). I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke. So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate. But for actually getting work done, the hair-trigger of the Razer keyboard makes it really hard not to make typos, and this keyboard is a lot better in that regard. One minor nitpick is that the font used to label the keys is a little odd, and the "6" really, really looks like a "G", which can be a little off-putting at first. But that's just a minor quibble. Final verdict: Definitely worth buying, unless you're an absolutely elite hardcore gamer.

review_title: Great for those with long nails.
body_en: I got this keyboard for a couple of reasons. I type at night, and when I wake up early, I'll do schoolwork. It's backlit and I can see the keys in the dark. There are a few settings to have the keys act or light up differently. And, because I have medium-long nails - the keys are large enough, and there is enough space between them, to accommodate my medium-length gel nails. I got raised keycaps to stick on the keys of this keyboard but they are not necessary for the length of my nails. Its appearance is as depicted, not too big, not too small. The keyboard connected easily to my laptop and is just as easy to set on top when not in use. It unplugs from the USB outlet easily, making removability a cinch when I decide enough is enough (not often) and pack everything up and put it away. It's very responsive, typing exactly as I type or game. None of the keys have stopped working or gotten stuck, even with my long nails. I love the sound of the keys clicking, again not too loud nor too soft. It gives me a 90s vibe while typing, and I can hear if I've hit the keys. Overall, I'm very glad I decided to buy this keyboard. It's perfect for my needs.

review_title: Nice, blue switch. led mechanical keyboard that doesn't break the bank.
body_en: If you're looking for a slim, low profile, led mechanical keyboard with blue switches, then you will be happy with this. The keyboad is exactly as described in the listing. The keyboard housing is made of plastic which makes the keyboard lightweight. The keys have a nice tactile feel with a nice "clicky" sound. The build quality is good, but doesn't compare to the solid feel of my Motospeed or Red Dragon keyboards. Included with the keyboard is a little plastic keycap puller. The led's are nice and bright and can be turned off. The CON is that each key is a set color, so if you're looking for a keyboard whose keys can change to various colors, you might want to skp this one. I personally did not care for any of the available 9 light modes. The 9 modes were definitely not exciting in my opinion and with keys being a preset color, I found some of the modes quite distracting. You can increase, decrease the brightness or turn off the leds. If you're looking for a keyboard where each key can display a multitude of different colors, this is keyboard is not for you. As for the the sole purpose of using this as a mechanical keyboard, then you won't be disappointed. I purchased this for use at work because I love the tactile feedback of mechanical keyboards. I didn't not test the liquid resistance of the kayboard but there are cutouts on the bottom for liquid drainage. No key ghosting was detected during its use. Again, if LED keyboards is what you fancy, I don't think you will be pleased with this because the keys are a preset color and can't be changed. As for the function of being a mechnical keyboard, this works well for the price point.

review_title: Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Over a Year of Flawless Performance!
body_en: After using this mechanical gaming keyboard for well over a year now, I can confidently say it's one of the best purchases I've ever made — not a single issue has come up the entire time. It's seen heavy daily use for both gaming and typing, and it's held up beautifully, including one memorable incident where I accidentally spilled soda right onto it; I was able to quickly disassemble it, clean it thoroughly with water and some rubbing alcohol, and it came back working like nothing ever happened, which speaks volumes about its build quality and durability. The RGB lighting is absolutely vibrant and stunning, with multiple settings and effects that let me customize the look to match my setup, whether I'm going for a subtle glow or a full-blown rainbow light show. The mechanical blue switches are honestly the sweet spot — they offer that satisfying, tactile clicky feel that's so satisfying for typing, while still being incredibly responsive and snappy for gaming, and thanks to the full anti-ghosting on the 104 keys, every single keypress registers perfectly even during the most intense, fast-paced gaming moments. With its rugged build, gorgeous RGB, fantastic switches, and full-sized layout, this keyboard has completely exceeded my expectations — I couldn't recommend it more to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performing mechanical keyboard!
Really clicky and bright, and works really good for typing or especially gaming.

review_title: Just buy the keyboard! You won’t regret it!!
body_en: I have started wearing long press on nails and was struggling with typing at work. I tried some of those stick on things but I wasn’t crazy about them. Decided to give this keyboard a try. It’s awesome! So much easier to type with my long nails. The colors are so pretty. I love that you can change them to do different things. The best part is the clicky keys. The sound is so relaxing. I would 100% recommend this keyboard. The colors are bright ant vibrant, the clicks are calming. It’s definitely one of the best purchases I have made off Amazon.

review_title: Feels like the legendary Model M, sporting it strong points and its quirks.
body_en: If you missed the old,clicky Model M from IBM, this keyboard emulates it pretty well. One must consider though, that it may emulate it too well. If you have fat fingers, you will find yourself making the same typos that you mad in high school when you learned to type on one. However, this is no deal breaker in my opinion. The speed at which I can type has vastly improved with the solid tactile feedback that tells you without a doubt that you press was registered. Setup couldn't be easier, just plug it into any USB port and away you go. Recognizes immediately as a 104 key with perks. Having the media controls and other immediate functions right there is nice too. As far as the design goes, it is very rugged and ready for the millions of keystrokes you will put on it as a writer. You will find a kind of typing joy you haven't experienced in quite a long time. No soft-touch or sickle keyboard will match the feel from what you get here. The only thing I find really off is the shallow height of the back stands. I think that they should be redesigned to be a bit taller. I cut a little piece of flat trim to set them on and that made the angle perfect. All-in-all, this keyboard is a joy to type on. I don't use it for gaming, because I see this as a waste of a premium feeling keyboard, wearing out the ASWD area and ruining it. I haven't had such a good keyboard in years and I'm not destroying that way. The one caveat I would warn you about is that if you use it on a KVM switch that is USB powered, this keyboard draws quite a bit of power to run the back light. be aware that you may get video background issues. Mine works just fine if I turn the backlight down low.
Beautiful keyboard! The tactile keys are so satisfying to press!

review_title: RisoPhy Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Excellent product.
body_en: Absolute game changer. I type everyday as an admin worker and now rarely make a typo. Blew my mind how this has improved my typing. Would recommend.

review_title: High Quality, Gorgeous LED Backlighting, Perfect Price
body_en: This mechanical keyboard is amazing for gamers looking to pick up a high-quality blue-switch mechanical keyboard. When I consider and review this product, I keep the following factors in mind: Functionality and Use - 5/5 The overall functionality of this keyboard is perfect, leaving me with minimal complains as a high-frequency and intensity user. As a proficient typist, I frequently type over 120 WPM and use combinations of hotkeys to complete tasks efficiently. This keyboard has supported this level of use during work/office settings, and feels highly responsive and crisp during high-intensity gaming moments, due to the blue key-switches creating a noticeable "click" with each keypress. If you have roommates or family, you may want to consider the clicking sounds of this keyboard while typing. The fact that they will likely hear your typing due to the pure "clicky-ness" of the key switches may present itself as an issue to some. Personally, this is not a factor that applies to my circumstances. Build Quality and Durability - 5/5 After 1 Month of intensive use, I have not noticed any issues so far in terms of key-press responsiveness, structural integrity, or wiring/USB issues. The keys hold in place well and the LED's have stayed consistently bright. Product Design - 5/5 The design of this keyboard is minimal, but effective. Exactly what I was looking for when shopping for a keyboard within this general price range. The all-black style allows the LED backlights to really *pop*, even in bright light/daylight. The inclusion of a "Fn" key allows for the same hotkeys and macros most would be used to with other keyboards, such as volume control and media playback, amongst other things. QoL Features - 4.5/5 This keyboard comes with 9 different LED-backlighting effects, such as lighting per keypress, "breathing" effects, WASD + Arrow Key backlighting, and more to complement a variety of use-cases. It would be nice to have the option to customize the LED backlighting colours themselves, as the backlighting options are pre-set; however, the crisp glow and colour choice are visually appealing and I am happy with the options provided. Value for Money - 5/5 Overall, I am highly satisfied with the purchase of this Keyboard and would recommend it to any gamer, office-worker, or avid tech geek like myself. For such a low price-point, you are getting a physical product that is equal in quality to that of a name brand like Razer or Corsair, without paying for the related bloatware and branding. Anybody looking to pick up their first mechanical keyboard, you cannot go wrong with this!

review_title: Good quality, affordable mechanical keyboard. Surprised by its quality given its price range.
body_en: Very satisfied with this purchase. Head and shoulders above my membrane Logitech K120 Wired Business Keyboard, and without breaking the bank too! To be honest, I feel lucky to have gotten this keyboard at such a low price. At this price point, I could not find a single mechanical keyboard that met all of my requirements but this one. In fact, even some of the more expensive mechanical keyboards didn't meet all of my requirements. For starters, the keyboard uses the UK layout with the pound sign and hash symbol key in the right place—very important for me. Second, this is a full-size keyboard with a numeric keypad at the right. This was important for me as I wanted a keyboard that did all of the same things as my previous keyboard, the only difference being that it is mechanical—a requirement that this RisoPhy mechanical keyboard fulfils precisely. (I should note, too, that most of the mechanical keyboards at this price range and even some more expensive ones, being shorter in width, lacked a numeric keypad.) Then there is the feel of the keyboard. The product description says that it uses "BLUE switches", seemingly modelling its switches on the classic tactile and clicky Cherry MX Blue switches. (It is unlikely that the keyboard uses actual Cherry MX Blue switches, given the price range, but rather its own knock-off versions of the switches.) While this may not be what some gamers are looking for (looking for something smoother and offering the same resistance all the way down without a slight bump as you press each key), this is perfect for me, as I was looking for a keyboard that produced nice responsive, tactile feedback, mirroring a classic typewriter effect. Some people may be put off by this, thinking that it makes the keyboard too noisy, and while, yes, there is a clicking noise with each key press, it honestly isn't that loud (though because there is still an audible clicking noise, I can understand criticisms saying that this keyboard is inappropriate for an office environment, for example, where such a constant clicking noise can cause distractions.) The keyboard is nice to type on, which is my primary use for it rather than gaming. A feature I don't care as much for is the rainbow backlighting. From my tests, the "9 different backlights" settings mentioned in the product description work exactly as expected. Also working as intended (at least from my tests on Windows 11) are the "12 multimedia combinations", effectively function keys that perform operations, such as, open a calculator and open Windows search. The major downside to this keyboard that I can think of is that the keyboard switches are not hot-swappable (though at this price point, this isn't a disappointment but just something to be expected.) In all, if you are looking for a keyboard that meets some of the same requirements as I was, at this price, I am unaware of a better keyboard on this website than this one.

As said in another comment, it's perfect when that's what you want. I write a lot and I type very quickly. When you type quickly, the best is a mechanical keyboard of this type, and it's very rare to find one for less than €100! [TYPING] I have a preference for those with sound feedback (like the switch keyboards/blue switch) and good anti-ghosting: you can strike quickly, accurately and if necessary correct immediately. Whether for gaming or very fast typing, this is an excellent keyboard. On the other hand, clearly, I don't see people who occasionally type supporting this keyboard, which is noisy... like a keyboard with a blue switch! When I'm on the phone, I sometimes try to type something discreetly: I always get grilled and told not to smash my keyboard... people are used to silent keyboards. [SOLIDITY] The keyboard is really excellent: I have been using it intensively for 1 year. The space key is a little worn (glossy but you can still see the horizontal bar) but all the keys are still perfectly readable, which is exceptional for ABS and my intensive use! Hours of typing per day, at least one cleaning per week (not delicate, with a product, and brushes to remove masses of cat hair... and crumbs ^^). [ERGONOMICS] The elevation is a little too marked for me: it creates a break in the wrist which is tiring, but the tactile feedback is enormous. As said, the backlighting is at a perfect dosage: neither too little (helps with quick identification when needed), nor too much (eye fatigue). The rear legs tend to fold up, but I'm a big brute and that bothers me less than on many keyboards. [CONCLUSION] Keyboard suitable for a person who is looking for solid, efficient, good quality equipment at a low price and above all a mechanical keyboard with strong sound feedback. For me we are not far from the perfect keyboard!

This is certainly a bargain priced mechanical keyboard but that doesn't mean it's bad; in fact, it's excellent. I got the model with silent red switches. I already own a Cherry silent red without the number pad but I wanted a full size. This one is ever so slightly less silent, likely due to an aluminum frame (a plus) rather than plastic. But it is still quiet enough to use in the bedroom at any hour. It is wired only. I actually prefer a wired connection rather than fooling with Bluetooth or dongles. To save space there is no plastic "frame" around the keys but this is just a matter of looks and you may prefer it, as the aluminum base is very attractive. It did take a little positioning to reach a stable state but that may have been my desk as much as the keyboard. There are tabs to raise the back but I don't use them. The keys are clearly marked and have a good feel to them. Let's see if with use they take on a shine; it's too soon to tell. This is a keyboard I will use a lot as I do most of my work on my home desktop setup. So far the typing experience has been exactly what I expect from this type of switch; there is enough of a tactile feel to be reliable but of course it's limited by the damped switches. (I do love the positive solid feedback of the very loud, clicky blue switches but my home office is in the bedroom and that doesn't work out.) The only thing I can't speak to is the software for remapping the keys. This can be downloaded from the Cherry site. But it doesn't run on my Linux system so I can't make use of it. However I really see no need to remap any of the keys, and if I really need to do that, there are other ways. I definitely rate this keyboard at 5 stars. It is great value for the money and gets you into the wonderful world of mechanical keyboards without breaking the bank. I have had great luck with Cherry products and this one is another winner.

review_title: I can't believe the improvement over other switches. It's crazy!
body_en: If you thought other companies made good key switches, then you are in for a surprise with this keyboard. Cherry absolutely nailed it with these new MX2A switches. I purchased the version with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. Now, I basically hate linear switches. Really, I usually can't stand them, but these new silents reds are the smoothest, and most buttery feeling switches I have ever felt. I have been using mechanical keyboards my entire life. Since before the patent ran out on the Cherry MX switches and the only mechanical keyboards you could buy had Cherry switches. Now, everyone makes their own switches, with all kinds of "features" like hall effect, rapid trigger, analog, adjustable actuation, magnets, etc.. Here's the issue with all of those though, they feel like crap to type on and are super loud. I have spent thousands on keyboards over the years. I still have over 15 mechanical keyboards sitting in storage that I stopped using. I am not exaggerating either. To give you an idea of where I'm coming from, my favorite switches used to be Cherry MX Brown. Now they are Cherry MX2A Silent Reds. I haven't even mentioned how quiet they are too. Unbelievably quiet for a mechanical keyboard. It's definitely the quietest mech keyboard I have ever used, which is saying a lot. Some people may think the keyboard is fairly basic, and in all reality, it is. It doesn't require software, doesn't have RGB or any lights (besides the led for caps lock and such), it doesn't have a removeable cable, or a super high polling rate over 1000Hz. Visually and functionally speaking, the keyboard is simple. But that a huge positive in my book. It does have full N-key rollover, so if you do use it for gaming, there won't be any issues there. I don't need to install any bloat to use the keyboard. I don't need to configure anything. It's just plug and play. It's fairly compact for a full-sized keyboard too, so be aware of the slightly more compact layout. My only real complaint is that it does not have 4 rubber feet on the bottom to keep it from sliding around. There are 2 rubber feet on the bottom front, but on the bottom rear, the feet are hard plastic, so it doesn't stay in place super well. There are rubber pads on the bottom rear feet that fold out, but I don't use a keyboard angled, so they are useless for me. Other than that, one thing, this keyboard is perfect for me. Am I going to use it for my hardcore gaming sessions? No. I actually purchased it for office work, and it's going to be perfect for that. However, will I be purchasing another keyboard with these same exact switches for my gaming pc? 100% YES! Look, you may not like the design of this keyboard, or its simplicity, but do not sleep on these new Cherry switches. Cherry is back with a vengeance, and if you're looking for a new keyboard, get one with these new Cherry switches. Whether it be this keyboard or not. The switch is king, and Cherry is back on top. Update: I now own 3 of these keyboards, lol, all with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. One for the gaming pc, one for the work office, and one for the home office. They can't be beaten when it comes to typing quality. No regrets.

I got this keyboard 3 weeks ago and I am very impressed. I used this at work and it suits my needs perfectly. It is extremely elegant and the keys are so satisfying to press. It feels very solid and hopefully should last a very long time. I share an office with one other person and the silent red switches are perfect for my environment. I would definitely recommend this keyboard to anyone who wants a simple but effective office keyboard.

Great productivity keyboard. Satisfying “thunk” on usage with fast throw. The switches being reds are easy so it doesn’t take much effort and it’s a good mechanical keyboard if you are coming from a cheaper style membrane or scissor style keyboard but want to venture into the world of mechanical keyboards. Not perfect but pretty good especially for the money.

I have always had mechanical keyboards but they are loud and are not appreciated by coworkers in nearby offices. This keyboard solves the problem and sacrifices nothing to do so. It turned out to be quieter than I thought it would be and feels great for all day typing!

Has held up extremely well! My typing speed has held up through a fairly intensive use for this while using Discord fairly heavily, while writing 3+ hours per day and while gaming on fairly heavily (Helldivers 2, Deadlock, Counter-Strike). The keys are a little heavy but in a way that seems well-built rather than is exhausting to type with. It's very nice to type with and gives good feedback. The keys spring back in a very responsive manner and provide a very good typing experience. The layout and feeling of typing with it overall has been really nice, no complaints of things like function keys. The dedicated calculator function key is unexpectedly more helpful than I had given it credit for and all function keys work with Linux.

Almost perfect, but the function key row is terribly integrated. It's too close to the number row. Same issue for the arrow keys and number pad. They're all too close together and I hit adjacent keys. Since every other keyboard in the world has separation, due to muscle memory I find myself hitting the function keys when reaching for the number row. I have giant hands though, so may be less of a nuisance for normal-handed folks. They should have made the keyboard a quarter inch taller and half inch wider and fixed this.

When I started looking for a keyboard all I wanted was easy push keys and this one fits the bill. I love the raised keys and the buttons are very smooth and easy to press. I work at a computer all day and love this keyboard. It has significantly eased my finger fatigue. Would recommend 👌 Also the keys are very quiet. I have had this keyboard for several months now and its still like new.

review_title: Swapped from a Razer Ornata v3, no regrets
body_en: I was using an Ornata v3 before this, which is pretty close in price. I wanted something I could use for both work and gaming. Here's a comparison that might help if you're looking for where this excels against the Ornata and similar competitors: No lighting: I'm tired of everything having freaking lights on them! I could just disable it in the settings I guess, but then I'm just paying for a feature I'm never using. Only keys with a light are Capslock and Numlock to let you know they're on. Keys: Good tactile feel and not too loud. Just enough of each to make you feel like you're typing. I use it for both gaming and work and it handles both jobs well. Very responsive for gaming. Some might consider it a little loud if you're in a cubicle with someone and you have to type a lot, but that's what headphones are for I guess! You won't find a more quiet mechanical keyboard that stll has that tactile typing feel, so you'll have to choose which you value more. (feel > sound for me) Size: A big more compact that some keyboards, but that's a plus. No lost real estate around the edges, just well-spaced keys and easy typing. You don't feel cramped at all if you're a touch typer. It has some heft to it. I often sit with it on my lap and it's fine. Not bouncing around like leaf, but doesn't cut off circulation to your legs. Durability: Again, it has some heft to it. When I pick it up I have a habit of snagging a key and pulling the cap off. I actually broke a key or two on my Ornata because the cap connectors are flimsy plastic posts and trying to find replacements was a nightmare. These keys are well-made and durable; haven't lost one yet. Only negative to me was the Calculator(???) button in the top-right. When I have it on my lap I was accidentally pressing it against the edge of my desk a lot and opening calculator app(s) mid-game; very frustrating. It was a simple job to go into windows settings and remove the mapping to the key (google for instructions) and now it's not an issue for a recliner like me. Anyone having it sit on their desk will likely never have this issue. I was a little leery of the price point when purchasing, but I'm seeing the value in the design, layout and build quality. I don't regret my purchase at all. In the last couple years I've gone through Razer, Steel Series and Logitech keyboards all around the $100 price point and this is by far my favourite. Highly recommend it.
perfect for silent work environments, very nice to the touch
Extremely happy with product

Excellent keyboard, works very well for gaming. The problem is the price: when I bought mine for $101 CAN, they were decent value for the money. Now a year later they want $216 CAN for them, and...that's a little absurd.

My first mechanical keyboard and sounds exactly how I imagined! It’s nice solid , creamy click noise! So satisfying!!! I loved the key color combo! The RGB lights are customizable, down to each key! Super cool. I am overall impressed with my purchase, as I was hesitant to buy something I wouldn’t like the sound of. I was also hesitant because there are so many options but I am glad I picked this! Good value for your money. The keyboard is heavy and feel super sturdy, doesn’t feel cheap. The keys were very responsive to touch and the Bluetooth was easy to setup with my windows laptop. The only thing I don’t like is the look of the keys, they do have a sheen/texture to them I don’t like but honestly, overall, I don’t mind it at all! Great buy!

review_title: Excellent Keyboard With Minor Software Issues
body_en: This is my first mechanical keyboard, and I finally understand what all the hype is about. The sound is incredibly satisfying. It has that nice mechanical sound without being overly loud or obnoxious, but it also isn't so quiet that you lose the satisfying typing experience. The typing feel is probably my favorite part—the keys feel incredibly smooth and satisfying, and so far everything has felt flawless. The build quality is also really impressive for the price. It has some nice weight to it and doesn't feel cheap or flimsy at all. The smart display is a fun addition. Is it necessary? Absolutely not. 😂 But it's definitely nice to have. You can use it for things like Bluetooth connection and volume settings, and you can also customize it with your own photo or GIF. The one area that could definitely be improved is the software. It's not particularly user-friendly, and finding the correct software to customize the keyboard took me longer than it should have. Once I actually found it, though, it wasn't too difficult to figure out with a little patience. The software itself also feels a little chunky and dated. That said, this has zero effect on the actual performance of the keyboard, so it's a very minor complaint. I've had absolutely no issues with wireless connectivity. I've used both Bluetooth and the included cable and haven't experienced any disconnections, lag, or other problems. One thing to note is that you'll need to use the included cable when connecting the keyboard to the software for customization. The battery life has also been surprisingly good so far. I haven't actually had to charge it yet, so I can't speak to the full battery life, but I work from home about 9 hours a day and also casually game in the evenings. After two days of that, the battery has only dropped about 5%. Overall, I have very little negative to say about this keyboard. The software could definitely use some improvement, and there could be better information provided about where to find and how to use it. But that's a very small complaint compared to everything else this keyboard does well. For my first mechanical keyboard, I'm extremely happy with it. Everything about it has exceeded my expectations. 5/5 and definitely recommend!

review_title: Great design. Great functionality. 100% Recommend if it fits your general specifications.
body_en: tl;dr: I am EXTREMELY happy with this keyboard. Build? Beautiful. Sound? Amazing. Functionality? PERFECT. Price? FANTASTIC. If this keyboard fits your specifications for your desk and you happen to work with two different computers at the same time, get it ASAP. More details: Previously I had a significantly smaller RK 68 which was great for me. It was perfect for what I wanted, a small profile and clacky keyboard. Unfortunately, I spilled soda all over it and it died so I had to get a new one. Fortunately, it was this keyboard. In my search for a new keyboard I had a couple things I was looking for: - A green color way to match my set up - A nice clack to it. - A numpad attached. Clearly it's not something very specific. But during my search I came across other features that I had no idea I wanted. But this one hit pretty much what I was looking for so I decided to give it a try and boy did it blow my expectations out of the water. == Design == Pros: This keyboard looks sleek. Before, to build something like this I had considered paying my friend to build it from scratch but the colorway and the key placements are just so clean. With multifunctional keycaps, they've added the second function on the side of the keycap so you can easily see the primary and the secondary without it feeling too cluttered. The back lighting options really make it fun to customize. They give you default options you can run with and each of those options you can tweak to your liking in terms of color. The digital display seems more like a part of the design the way it links to the volume knob, rather than an after thought like some other keyboards. This provides another option for you to make the keyboard your own by letting you upload a gif to just loop by default. Cons: No complaints really, except the digital display occasionally pops off slightly, requiring you to press it back in but it hasn't become too much of an issue for me yet. Also, uploading the gif to the keyboard takes a good amount of time (something like 5 minutes) , so if they could fix that speed that would be amazing. Oh one more complaint is that it's too tall. I had to get a wrist mount just to feel comfortable typing on it. == Functionality == Pros: MAN, this keyboard is PACKED with features I never thought I would need. Aside from the aforementioned backlight customization, something that has made my life so much better is hidden behind the digital display. It's base functionality of controlling the volume of your computer works like a charm but it's when you get into the submenus that you can really see where it shines. You see, I am someone who bounces between a macbook pro for work and a windows PC for play and so I'm constantly bouncing between the two. Before, I had a mac specific keyboard and a windows specific keyboard, both occupying space on my desk. This keyboard has eliminated that need in a sleek and elegant way by allowing me to hardwire into my desktop and bluetooth to my macbook. From there, I can easily use the digital display + volume knob to switch my connection between the two. Heck, if I needed to add another couple I could. It seems like I can have up to 5 different devices connected (3 bluetooth, 1 wired, 1 wireless dongle). So if for some reason I had another device, I could easily switch between the two. You might ask yourself, but what about the difference in layout between macs and windows machines? Oh my friend, you see... THEY THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING. Through the same digital display, you can swap the layouts between the two types. I was totally fine with that until I read the manual a bit more and found you could even use a hotkey JUST for that. Remember the secondary functions of the various keys? If you look on the side of the 'A' and 'S' keys, you can see that they read 'WIN' and 'MAC' respectively. So to switch formats, all you have to do is hit 'Fn' + 'A' or 'S' to switch between the two. This really pushed my like for this keyboard to love. Cons: The only thing I can really think of is a nitpick and is possibly even already a function, I'd just have to read through the manual a bit more. It would be nice to be able to use a shortcut to bounce between the different keyboard connections like you can switch formats. == Sound and Feel == Pros: I am having a BLAST typing this review. Every keypress feels so satisfying as the switches engage and disengage making you really feel connected to the keyboard. The sound is more thocky than clacky which is extremely pleasing to my ears, especially after coming from a clackier keyboard. Cons: While this keyboard is probably 50 percent quieter than my last keyboard, it's still definitely louder than a membrane keyboard, so if you're looking for silent, this isn't what you want. But if you're looking at mechanical keyboards, then this most likely isn't you. == Price == I feel like this keyboard is well worth the 89 dollar price tag for what you get. I feel like even a couple years ago, you'd have to pay 300 bucks to someone to custom make something like this with the design options. Sure, it's not as bespoke as the true customs, but I feel like it holds up just as well. Overall, I'd give this keyboard a 'have no fear, buy away' if your needs are similar to what I've mentioned above!

I recently got into keyboard building and I chose this keyboard for my first build. I love that it’s basically full size but has a compact feel. I choose the sky blue option that came with the pale green tactile switches. I enjoy the feel of a tactile switch, but the switches that came stock were a little too high pitch for me. I swapped out the switches for some hand lubed Leobog Greywood v3s (sound test in video). The keyboard has a surprising amount of weight to it, and the knob and screen are very useful. Pros: South facing RGB Sounds amazing (imo) after I swapped the switches and put new keycaps on The LED screen and the knob are extremely handy and a really cool feature Battery works REALLY well - when the RGB is off Tri-mode feature - I personally have some issues with the Bluetooth with one specific computer of mine (they won’t connect unless the keyboard is on and in the right mode before I turn my computer on) but I don’t have this issue with any of my other devices and believe it’s likely due to an old Bluetooth adapter. Cons: Battery - I did a full test of this and the battery with RGB on is honestly terrible in my opinion. I started my workday with a fully charged battery, and it had drained to 28 percent after 10 hours Software - Can’t seem to be able to change the clock from 24hr format to 12hr format Software for the keyboard itself is definitely lacking, and there were little resources I could find on how to use it All that being said I don’t regret buying this keyboard at all. It’s a major upgrade from what I had before, and I’m extremely proud of my first build.

review_title: All the mechanical keyboard I need
body_en: First mechanical keyboard I’ve owned, can’t imagine I’d need anything different. Bought two of these, one for my workspace and one for my wife. We both needed accurate and responsive keys for frequent data and password entry, the lights and display are just bonus points. I change out my display for random gifs and RGB weekly using the web portal, easy enough once you get the hang of it, takes 5-10 minutes to upload a gif. Can confirm battery lasts about a week with moderate workday use. Keys are on the quieter end of clacky, not as obnoxious as some mechanical keyboards I’ve used in the past. Key travel registers about 75% from fully depressed which took me a tiny bit of time to adapt to. More often now, I’ll think I missed a letter because I didn’t press quite hard enough, but look back to find it registered after all. Comes with a few replacement switches, key puller, and usb-c cable which is nice. I’m sure there is better quality for more money out there but I’m not the demographic for it, this is all the keyboard I think I’ll ever need.

review_title: A must have for anyone looking for an amazing sounding keyboard!
body_en: When I first got a gaming PC, I figured I didn't really need a super expensive keyboard and that a cheap one that sounded "clicky" and had lights was fine enough. I also didn't want to bother with charging a wireless keyboard. However, I started to hear from YouTube videos and TikToks about "creamy" and "thocky" keyboards. I immediately started to do research, because I was obsessed with the sound. This is one of those rare purchases that I cannot stop thinking about how happy it makes me. I have absolutely no qualms with it. Here's what I love: The sound is excellent. Videos that I watched were a good indicator, but as other reviews have said, they really do not do the keyboard justice for how it actually sounds. The letters themselves are very creamy, while the function buttons (spacebar, shift, enter, backspace, etc.) have a much deeper "thocky" sound to them. If you're on the fence, at least try it and return if it's not for you. The functionality is incredible. There are a ton of lighting options that you can play with. You can mess around with them in the software on your PC. But because this keyboard has a small LCD screen, you can also change them directly on the keyboard itself. I have mine set to light up the entire keyboard cyan from whichever key I press, expanding out. Speaking of the LCD screen, you're able to upload GIFS or images to the screen, which is a really cool feature. As far as connectivity, you have every imaginable option available to you. I have my gaming rig connected via the 2.4USB wireless adapter. You can also connect up to three devices via bluetooth. And of course you can opt to hardware in. I love the the keyboard has both a USB-A and USB-C port. I am a huge advocate for technology having USB-C as an option, as it is much more convenient, provide faster transfer times, and faster charging times. Speaking of charging, the battery life on this keyboard is excellent. I seem to get about a week's worth of charge with extreme use daily. I know that the keyboard is hot swappable, meaning you can swap out the switches, which ultimately determine the sound of the keyboard, but personally, I haven't messed with that, as I love the way it sounds now. Overall, this is an excellent keyboard. If you're in the market for a wireless keyboard that sounds great, this is the best option out there! I typically don't like spending a ton of money on stuff unless I am absolutely sure of its value, and let me put your mind at ease that this keyboard is worth so much more than what the price tag shows.

review_title: To many firmware glitches - basically unusable for any serious work
body_en: Today, I initially wrote a negative review of this keyboard due to issues with missed or repeated keystrokes, or keys continuing to fire until another key was pressed. However, after extensive investigation (because I really wanted to keep this keyboard for its mechanical build), I finally discovered that the issues were caused by an obscure, lingering USB driver from a device no longer connected to my PC. That driver was behind all the trouble. I hope this revised review is published before the original one, which is no longer valid. After 15+ years of using Cherry MX Blue switches on a single keyboard that eventually got damaged, I was in search of a replacement. This keyboard seemed like a good option - more compact than my full-size board and featuring “tactile” pale green switches. I hoped they would resemble MX Blues in feel, just without the audible click. Unfortunately, these switches aren’t really that much (or at all) tactile. I don’t understand the claim. There is a point somewhere along the key travel where pressure slightly decreases, but you’d need to press very slowly and have an extremely sensitive touch to notice it. In actual typing, it feels - at least to me - indistinguishable from a regular linear switch. That said, I’ve gotten used to them and didn’t have much trouble adapting after so many years with MX Blues. And the 'thocky' sound still sounds nice. The build quality is solid. The board is sturdy, heavy, and a definite improvement over my old keyboard. I’m not particularly interested in the display or LED lighting. I don’t see the point - especially since the keycaps aren’t translucent, so the lights don’t help in the dark. Omitting those toddler-toy-like features and lowering the price - or populating that space with more keys - would be more useful, in my opinion. I used the included keycap puller to swap the positions of the 'Home' and 'Del' keys, then made the change in the RK software. It took just a few seconds. These settings are retained even if you unplug the keyboard or uninstall the RK software entirely from your PC. All things considered, in terms of mechanical construction, this is a very good keyboard. I do wish the switches were more tactile, but that’s just a matter of personal preference. These switches are still decent, and I’ll probably swap them out in the future for some Kailh clicky switches.

review_title: Good keyboard but little support for Mac
body_en: The keyboard part is awesome and the keys feel good with a satisfying clack that isn't sharp or too loud. I use this on a Mac and it does have a Mac mode. However, I find it hard to use with the wireless dongle (doesn't work on my Mac) and just have to use it wired. Fortunately, it does have a supplemental USB-A port for my wireless mouse transmitter. The screen is OK and the volume knob is useful. I think this is a Windows keyboard and Mac compatibility was added afterwards as the F keys don't work even in Mac mode to adjust volume or activate programs like a native Mac keyboard. Still, the keyboard is worth keeping even if the program needed to control the LED lights and other functions is Windows only.

review_title: Tastiera ottima, peccato mi sia arrivata palesemente usata
body_en: Premise. The keyboard arrived new but clearly used. The package was sealed by a second sticker applied on the previous one, the keyboard had fingerprints, the booklet was as in the photo, the power cable was even pinched, all the bags were ruined. In short, if I buy a new product it must be new, otherwise I would have bought a guaranteed used one for less. I can understand a possible return during the withdrawal period but at least the cable needed to be replaced. Going to the top of the line keyboard from Royal Kludge. The type of switches fitted are not declared, they arrived with the tactiles and they are still excellent, I hadn't had the opportunity to try them. Very pleasant and which cause a minimum of resistance and then lower decisively. I don't mind them at all. The surface of the keys is slightly reduced on the flat part, which helps to avoid accidentally pressing unwanted keys. The sound is quite pleasant, a little dry but not annoying, probably influenced by the rigid structure of the keyboard. Writing is facilitated by the reduced width of the surface of the keys although they do not have the ergonomic inclination that other keyboards of the same range offer, but the tone on tone on some keys makes them not immediately identifiable. The backlight is missing. An absence that I find inexplicable in keyboards that cost over €100 but I see that, excluding the classic gaming brands, there is little to be found. The keyboard has two height levels with rubberized feet, but it is quite tall. Personally I use it without a riser. Full RGB, totally modulatable via software but with the possibility of managing everything via the integrated screen. Good brightness and intense colors. Possibility of connection via cable, included in the package, via Bluetooth and with dongle. The latter with a lateral magnetic seat. It also features two physical buttons. On one corner we find the connection selection between cable or key and a little further on the on and off button. The control of the small monitor is comfortable and easy to read, as are the LEDs for Num Lock and Caps Lock, also present as LEDs near the Esc key. The signs on F, J and 5 are also easily identifiable by touch. The small monitor has a menu function for various settings that can be navigated via a practical wheel. Battery level, date, connection type, caps lock and num block, if it is in Win or IOS mode. In short, it shows what is needed and is easily readable. You can also upload GIFs limited to 60 images. A little bit and goes to remove the other info. Nice option but I remain of the opinion that, having a small additional monitor available, you should be able to make better use of it. For example with the operating temperatures of the components, the percentage of use, etc. The software is complete. It offers to save 3 different command mappings and fully manage the lighting. Not very intuitive, I must admit. There is a menu whose use I am not clear about and no information is provided either in the paper manual or in the one available on the site (both in English). Excellent keyboard, overall the one I'm happy with is better than the others I've tried (and I've tried several in the €50/150 range). It's really a shame about the lack of backlighting as well as, seeing that it is present on other products, the lack of being able to combine it with the magnetic wrist rest.

review_title: Great mechanical keyboard and seller delivery support
body_en: The keyboard works flawlessly and has a really great mechanical feel and sound. The keyboard delivery was very prompt and thank you to the team for providing a hassle free online purchasing equipment
This is a great and reasonably priced keyboard. The key sound/feel is super pleasing, and the quick switch between devices/volume/effects with the dial and screen is awesome.

review_title: Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type!
body_en: Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type! The build is sturdy and the keyboard is heavy. I am expecting it to last long. I liked the small screen for configuration. There is a time display on the keyboard, which I don't find useful. Once charge last about two weeks with bluetooth connectivity.

review_title: The sound and typing experience is amazing.
body_en: This is my 2nd Royal Kludge keyboard and I am very impressed. I've had mechanical keyboards from Logitech, Keychron, Corsair, Drevo and Redragon and I like my RK ones more. This one in particular is just super satisfying to type on. I love the creamy sound from the keys, it's unlike anything else I've owned so far. The green and clay-red color scheme also looks awesome. Keycaps are soft touch but not shine-through which is a bit of a disappointment but not a deal breaker. The little screen and knob is easy to use and actually useful. It's nice to change settings in a menu vs using function keys, and being able to check the time when enjoying full screen entertainment is also handy to me. My audio setup is also able to use the knob as a volume control which is an added bonus. All three connectivity modes work well for me - Bluetooth is reliable, 2.4Ghz is fast and reliable, and wired mode is also fast and reliable. Range on BT/2.4Ghz is average, but since this isnt really an HTPC keyboard I don't think it matters much. My only complaint is the battery life. RK claims they have a gigantic battery in this keyboard but I only get 2-3 days of use between charges, and it takes a loooooong time to charge so it ends up being plugged in a little more than I'd like. If I keep the RGB lighting on the 2nd lowest setting, I can get another day or two of usage but I wish I didn't have to charge this keyboard once a week. I really like this keyboard overall and I'd definitely recommend it! It's a good keyboard for full price but RK has sales all the time so I'd wait for a 20-25% discount, where it becomes a killer deal in my opinion. Edit: 3 months in and still very fun to type on and 100% reliable. I just keep the backlighting off most of the time now to conserve battery and it lasts a while without the backlight on 2.4Ghz link (2-3 weeks light use). Only thing I don't like after a few months of use is having to press fn + PgDn for the End key.

Zero complaints, satisfying sound, a lot of cool features. Very satisying feeling when typing, not loud or clunky at all. You can tell the quality of the build by the weigh it feels and it's weight. I love also the volume wheel, so cool!

Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you- A couple of things I wasn't really aware of- 1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys 2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

review_title: Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.
body_en: I have the green switch version. Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference. Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now. After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal. 2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily. 18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.

Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.
Awesome keyboard!
absolutely love it great keyboard. really good for the price lighting on the rgb is amazing. so far it feels really durable.

Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck. Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter. I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often. Eventually I decided that since I paid $100+ I was going to get a working product. My RMA process started on April 20, 2024, and after many days of back and forth emails with razer trying to convince them it was a hardware, not software, issue they gave me a shipping label to send out on April 26, 2024. I received the replacement about 3 weeks later on May 17, 2024. Today on May 18, 2024 I noticed the same unresponsive key issue with the "2" key above the "W" key. This IS a big deal for gaming since it is used very often. I dont want to go through the RMA process again, and im pretty sure I cant get a refund from amazon after 4 months so this keyboard will likely just be tossed in the garbage where it belongs. A lot of time and money wasted on a sub-par product. Been using Razer keyboards and mice since about 2012 but its probably time to try a different brand to try since their quality seems to have gone down. Shame.

Fun RGB lighting, fully customizable colors within the Razer lighting program. Lighting program is easy to use with plenty of tutorials on installation. Can customize individual keys for different lighting when pressed. Extra macro buttons on the left will take some getting used to, but just imagine what all you can assign them as. Solid keyboard in terms of weight, back wings to lift up to have it at a slight angle. Keycaps nice and solid quality. These are soft and bubbly sounding in my opinion, not sharp and clicky. In prior experience with Razer, the price is a bit up there, but I would wager its worth it. Received on September 28th, 2025; will check back after a while to update review if needed.
Fantastic keyboard as per my choice and also this works well. The package was all good at the time I recieved it. All items were there and the experience is amazing.

I've had my fair share of gaming keyboards but this one in particular feels great and was way better quality than expected. It is relatively quiet for a gaming keyboard and has excellent tactile feedback. The backlight is clean and vibrant as well. My only complaint would be the macro buttons on the left of the keyboard, but only because I am personally not used to it from previous keyboards.
It's the first keyboard I've bought. It is the contemporary style. I'm happy with my friend, it doesn't feel cheap until the very recent USB cord. The lights are very pretty.

review_title: Don't prefer Razer, but it's ZZZ so I made an exception
body_en: It's super clicky which I hate and it's not swappable which is absurd. The RGB is very inaccurate when setting up but when you do, it looks nice enough. I still prefer my KDA Logitech G Pro keyboard but I got this because it's miyabi <3 the keys are very nice to the touch, although I hate that the macro buttons are on the left, they're messing up with my muscle memory but I can get used to them. The keyboard is metal, cool to the touch, and heavy.
The switches are a little noisy but I still really liked the design and quality of the keyboard.

If you are interested in transitioning from an old school to mechanical keyboard, want something with an absolutely sick looking design, is simple to use, and doesn't have insanely loud key press noises, this is definitely a top option! I have had this unboxed for barely 30 minutes and am already in love with it. It was super easy to plug-n-play and use the built in functions immediately. I have used old style, full-length keyboards for decades and was extremely hesitant to try out a mechanical keyboard, especially because of the noise I had heard from seeing video reviews and how unsure I was if I could deal with the loss of full buttonology. One major reason I looked into one of this type/size was that I realized one of the main reasons I have issues with soreness and pain in my left shoulder, neck, and upper arm is due to how I would position my left hand and tilt the keyboard in order to use the traditional movement keys WASX on a full sized keyboard for gaming. With this one, my arm is now in a natural resting position at 90 degrees against my side, negating the angular stress on all those muscle groups, and when I want to do some typing while gaming, I don't have to stretch across the board to my left as much with my right hand to get to home keys. Additionally, one big assumption killer was that, even though the size is cut down by a ton from a full-sized keyboard, the muscle memory transition to the slightly more compacted keys took hardly any time at all when typing with home keys. I type about 100 WPM, so I assumed I'd have a super difficult time with this aspect of the transition, but the spacing of keys doesn't have a huge difference of feel. The other big plus is that the noise level isn't huge on key press when gaming, and is not bothersome when typing; it's not that high pitched clickity clack you might get from many other types, rather a dull, thud-like sound. Now add in the amazing painted design (especially if you like Japanese wood block print/art), and the colored light functions, which mind you are accessible by using the keyboard and the built in mini screen aka not requiring you to download software, as well as the pre-programmed FN + <key> functions that replace the buttons you lost from a full sized keyboard, and this thing is just a dream. HIGHLY RECOMMEND to one and all, especially old folks like me that are afraid to make that leap into transitioning to a mechanical style board. P.S.: If you're looking for actual dimensions of the keyboard itself, which are not on this Amazon page nor on the company's item page, they are approximately as follows: 12.75"x5.75"x1.375"-0.875" (the last number is the height, without the height extenders being used, at the top of the keyboard vs. at the bottom. it slopes upward towards the back)

This is a fantastic mechanical keyboard on a budget. This is my first keyboard I’ve purchased for my gaming PC after using the one it comes with, and I’ve really enjoyed it. The keyboard has drivers, but they aren’t necessary, it’s a good plug and play. The colors are cute and the lighting doesn’t detract from the design. I really love the sound - when I’m just typing and listening to music, it’s pretty easy on the ears, a good creamy click. The size is just perfect as my last keyboard was 100% and took up way too much space on my desk. Not too bulky or heavy. I’ve been using this to play games that require WASD pretty heavily and the keys have been holding up!

I love it! It's my first keyboard other than an old 2015 work keyboard. It's super smooth and the sound is very nice. It's totally asmr worthy. It was smaller than I expected but just because it doesn't have a number pad like my old keyboard did. It glows rainbow but I lowkey lost my manual so I don't know how to change the lighting, but I remember there being a bunch of combinations you can do to change them on either windows or mac. And it is so cute my fav color is green and it is adorable with the frogs. 10/10 would buy again if mine breaks (knock on wood).

I really liked the color and the frogs, and wanted to try a 75%. It was only $49 when I got it, and it has screen controls, really good RBG, and is hot swappable. The only thing that is holding this back is the fact that it is only a wired connection, which for just $10-$15 more you can get tri-connect. But that was my mistake. And if that doesn't bother you then there really is no reason not to get this fully customizable board over more higher priced options The stock switches are very good if you like linear, but I switched them with some Kaihl Box Pink, and it was very easy. Keycaps shine through and print are both quality and very comfortable to type on. The board itself is solid with a good build, proper gasket mounts and sound dampening.

review_title: Great quality - Not the best instructions
body_en: I have only had this keyboard for a few days, but I will say that it is of very nice quality and works well with my Lenovo Yoga Laptop. The feel and size are great, the keyboard is a bit on the heavier side, which I don't mind. and it seamlessly connects while also super cute! The only reason I did not give the keyboard 5 stars is that the setup instructions were a bit vague and did not include how to download the software needed to set up and customize (I was able to figure it out, and the colors work great, and I can upload GIFs to the screen). I had to visit the brand's website to download and install the software (steps not included in the manual). I think if you have a general understanding of how to set up these types of keyboards and download software, it's fine, but adding these steps would make everything much more streamlined. Besides that, everything else works great so far, and I really like using the keyboard!

Love this keyboard! It’s compact (75%) and has a creamy sound when typing. It’s more of a dull and thumpy sound if that helps! I preferred this since I’m in an office and didn’t want to have a loud mechanical keyboard clacking away. But aside from sound it’s also extremely cute with all of the pictures on it! It was easy to setup and the website to download the drivers is mainly in another language (possibly Chinese?) but again easy to find the correct keyboard. Now I have to setup the RGB that I prefer and what gif I’d like in the upper screen. The connection was easy and simple to setup and I love that there’s a reinforced port underneath the keyboard and not off to the side where it can get caught or snagged on stuff. Overall I highly recommend this keyboard!!!

review_title: I’m soooo happy with my purchase!!
body_en: LOVE!!!! What more could you ask for $43 (sale)??? Thocky, beautiful customizable RGB, AND a gif display??? I’m very happy with my purchase. Would spend the extra 20 bucks every time for this masterpiece over a cheap basic keyboard. No reason to buy an expensive one either when it looks, sounds, and has features this good. PLEASE DOWNLOAD THE RIGHT APP FOR THE KEYBOARD OR ELSE ITLL MESS UP AND BRICK IT. I did that and my gif was all wonky. I just reset it and used the correct one and it worked perfectly. The kitty keycaps are called TYRIXKI 26 Keys Crystal Jelly and they’re also on Amazon. The Juno (from OW) keycap I just got off aliexpress!!

I so far love this keyboard! It sounds so creamy compared to my previous keyboard, downloading the software for the lighting was also very easy! I also enjoy the fact it has 3 different levels of height due to the stands in the back and it can be used for anything that you use a keyboard for (writing documents, video games, etc.). I got the green one with the frogs and it fits the green aesthetic I am going for in my room and I could not be happier! I definitely recommend getting it if you are looking for a stylish and creamy sounding keyboard. (Sorry for a bad video, I was sending it to a friend originally)
It's cute, it works very well. I would like the sound to be creamier. But the quality is perfect.

My so loves this keyboard. I heard him encouraging friends to purchase because it takes the gaming experience to another level! He loves playing xbox games using the features on this keyboard aswell as doing other work! Definitely worth the wait...looks cool also with the different patterns and effects!
Absolutely love the keyboard it sounds really nice and I love the little screen on it and its performance it very good and shipping was fast thank you!!

review_title: Deeper Insights Than Apple Watch – WHOOP 5.0 Delivers Serious Data with Minimal Hassle
body_en: After a ton of research into wearables that go beyond basic step counting and heart rate, I chose the WHOOP 5.0 (with the 12-month membership) specifically because I wanted way more detailed, actionable data than what my Apple Watch provides. And it's delivered big time. The band itself is incredibly lightweight and comfortable—I barely notice it's on my wrist all day and night. I only take it off for showers, which is a huge win for continuous tracking. The real game-changer is the charger: it snaps right on top while you're still wearing it, so there's zero downtime or lost data. That's a thoughtful design that makes staying consistent effortless. The metrics are fantastic—sleep stages, recovery scores, strain, HRV, respiratory rate, and all the deep physiological insights feel accurate and meaningful. What surprised me most was uploading my recent physical lab results directly into the app; WHOOP factored those biomarkers right into my overall data and trends, giving even more context to how my habits affect my health long-term. The GenAI-powered WHOOP Coach is another standout—you can chat with it to ask specific questions about your results, get personalized explanations, or dive deeper into why your recovery dipped or how to optimize training. It's like having a smart coach in your pocket. The app is clean, intuitive, and clearly well-thought-out—everything from daily summaries to long-term trends is easy to navigate and feels intentional, not overwhelming. My one complaint is the clasp. It might just be my unit, but it feels a bit finicky and harder to close securely than it should—sometimes takes a couple tries to get it to click properly. Not a dealbreaker, especially since the rest of the experience is so seamless, but it's worth noting for anyone picky about quick on/off. If you're serious about health optimization, recovery, and getting beyond surface-level tracking, the WHOOP 5.0 is worth it. The subscription unlocks all this depth, and after a few weeks, I can't imagine going back to less insightful devices. Highly recommend for data-driven folks!

review_title: Whoop has some good stats, and some fake hype too
body_en: WHOOP will be at you day and night; the device is very frisky when it comes to telling you your basic health stats and behaviors. However, I would like to add a few caveats: 1) The AI or algorithm that they use SOUNDS like it's personalized to you, but the conclusions and statements the device makes are based on collected, aggregated, and thoroughly-predigested data. That's not to say its inaccurate, but it's not "personal" in a real sense--the sense that a series of physiological and blood tests would deliver. that would be specific to you. You are more likely to get recos based on standardized data. 2) The app is really busy. There are so many charts and data points and subcategories that it becomes difficult (for me, anyway) to find precisely what I'm looking for. I have to ASK (query) to get to see my running stats, for instance; I can't seem to find them otherwise. 3) The loads of data and so-called personal recos are designed to keep you interested and committed, andf that's basically a good thing, but it's also to hook you into paying an annual fee FOREVER. Compared to a high-end sports watch (Garmin, Suunto, or even Apple) you will be paying ad infinitum for something others offer for free. That said, I've only had my WHOOP for about a month, so I'm expecting a fresh batch of data when I hit the 30-day point, and perhaps I'll find more of it useful when I get there. Right now it's a pleased enough with the info provided, though I do wish it "agreed". more with my watch. Not quite sure whose stats to believe! ***UPDATE*** A few days short of two full months. I DO like their AI; when I correct it ("No that wasn't a run I was digging in the garden / walking the dog") it accepts and adjust response accordingly. Nice. Though I still find the data provided kind of scattered around the site, with no simple menu to help locate something. And WHOOP is OBSESSED with "Strain;" even after reading their explanations I still can't compute their approach. Accuracy still a big ? mark, as it only occasionally matches what my Garmin watch reports. Who to believe??
