review_title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
body_en: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

review_title: The best fitness tracker I've used
body_en: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. Overall I think this watch is a great fit for a more casual user who isn't running marathons but wants to track fitness and sleep and get some extras like smartphone notifications and see the weather at a glance. If you want something with more smart features and better build quality (i.e. more metal and less plastic), then the Venu might be a better fit. Or they have the Forerunner if you do run marathons. Or a bunch of other models for more specific use cases. But I would highly recommend giving this watch a try if you're looking for the same things that I am.

review_title: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
body_en: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

review_title: This watch is an Amazing buy!
body_en: I am beyond happy with my new watch! You get the luxury without the cost. It has so many amazing features using the "Glory Fit App," which is very user-friendly. I'm able to take calls, make calls, and text from the watch. Listen to music by connecting via bluetooth. It allows you to customize countless features like temperature units, weight, and metrics. You can choose between multiple digital face diplays in your watch settings. You can also set the length of time display stays lit before it disappears. It features: training plans, goal setting and allows you to connect with friends. The watch straps are interchangeable so that you can attach different colors or styles. You can monitor your heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep, step count, weight, and more! It has a voice assistant and alarm clock as well. You can also sync most of your Apps on your paired device (I did my my phone), so that you can receive notifications and even use the same functions on your watch simultaneously. For example, I paired my youtube account so that whenever I receive a notification in the Youtube App of a new video, it shows that notification on my phone as well. I can even listen to YouTube using the play, pause, and stop buttons from my phone. I also synced our security camera device so that I can receive those notifications as well while away from home. I am able to select any number of applications I want to individually sync or not. This is great so that I can be selective and not have my watch going off every second of the day. It helps me to stay motivated as far as my fitness goes because I'm able to set goals - it sends you an achievement reward notification, which sounds once a goal has been reached. It has so many features that I haven't even begun to tap into. There is a slight learning curve, as with sny smart device, but it's very user-friendly after you patiently program and customize each feature to fit your needs and get the hang of it. I love the color selection options. I chose the black and light pink/rose gold color (for him & her), I also ordered (from another seller) face covers for protection. The covers were very easy to slip on (see in photos & video). It comes with a convenient USB, and the watch is packed in its own individual box. Note: THE BOX HAS (2) WATCHES PICTURED BUT ONLY COMES WITH ONE WATCH. It didn’t track my sleep well, which was one of the reasons I bought it, but it does have to be in constant contact with your wrist and I don’t like my watches that tight. It did do a decent job on vitals and had charts to show weekly levels. The negatives were you had to change your settings to a certain exercise to get a more accurate result. Especially on steps. Since I’m up doing a lot of walking, lifting, bending and sometimes crawling when cleaning the house I found you get a better representation of steps if you changed the setting to indoor walking. 😁 The drawback on any of the exercise settings I would forget to switch back to normal. Which is a negative on me. The next one is a very personal preference. I really wanted to be able to change the bands. I like sparkles and my daughter likes blues. I couldn’t find any that would fit the watch. We ended up making a few cuts here and adjustments there to get them to fit but I don’t think most people would want to do that. My husband bought me an apple watch for my birthday and my daughter didn’t like having anything on her wrist so I gave them to the grandsons 10 & 9. They are obviously not gentle with them but they are still going. I would place that into the sturdy column.

review_title: Everyone thinks it’s an Apple Watch lol
body_en: I’m super happy with this purchase. I honestly wasn’t expecting to like this smartwatch as much as I do, but it surprised me in a good way. The screen is big, bright, and very clear, which makes it easy to read messages, check notifications, and track my workouts throughout the day. The fitness tracking also seems pretty accurate from what I’ve used so far. One thing I really like is being able to answer calls from the watch. The call quality sounds decent, and it’s convenient when my phone isn’t right next to me. It’s also very comfortable to wear all day and doesn’t feel heavy on my wrist. The battery life has been solid too. I usually get around two days before needing to recharge it. The funniest part is that almost everyone who sees me wearing it thinks I’m wearing an Apple Watch lol. It definitely has a premium look to it without the expensive Apple price tag. Overall, I’m really glad I bought it.

I really like this smartwatch. The screen is clear, it’s easy to use, and the call feature works great. It has plenty of fitness options and is comfortable to wear. Great value for the price and definitely recommend it!

I loved this watch for the price. But I purchased 2 watches on May 8th and received them on May 12th. The first watch literally died completely after 2 weeks of using it. Tried charging it, tried holding the button...nothing. I am deaf, and I rely on the vibrations on the watch when someone texts me. I never used the call function, so I can't tell you how well it works. Compatibility, it's great! Connectivity, it stays connected for the MOST part, but at times, it won't stay connected. I wish the battery lasted longer. It lasted less than 7 days! Not the kind of watch I wanted. There are other watches I've had in the past that lasted close to a month! This one sucked on battery life. The sleep monitoring sucked. It doesn't record it well at all—the heart rate and oxygen work just as they're supposed to do. I cannot contact seller to tell them their product sucks. So, on to a watch search that would last longer than what I have now.

Im at little on the fence about this watch. For the price it is great and when I first got it I was in love. Now that I've had it for a few weeks and have been able to use it I'm not sure how I feel about it all the time. It adds steps randomly, like even when I'm sleeping (I don't move in my sleep) I wake up and it'll say i took like 400 steps. The heart rate monitor and blood oxygen monitor seem to work just as intended. I got this watch to help track my sleep and this is where I keep having issues. Sometimes it won't register that I slept, or doesn't record it properly (and i have even started wearing the watch backwards so that the sensor is on my wrist so it can get a better read). Today it said I slept for 3 hours while I was out running errands. I also accidentallyet the watch die the other day (it lasted a few days without charging), but it seems like since then I've been having a lot of issues with the Bluetooth, the call features, tracking and notifications. The app is also pretty basic. Sometimes it's hard to find the settings your looking for and they don't give you many options to begin with. When I go in to look at my sleep it shows a graph which is nice, but if you want to try to see the times you have to press on this tiny sliver and most of the time it highlights the wrong thing and doesn't really break anything down for you. I know I got this watch at a great price, but I will be honest I have been looking for a different one similarly priced, considering sending this back. I guess if my opinion changes I'll update my review.
Wifey loves hers. We submit recorded data to insurance company for extra incentives.

review_title: Smartwatch con multiples funcionalidades y de calidad mas que aceptable.
body_en: I was pleasantly surprised by this smart watch. The quality, in general, is good, as is the software and the application to pair it via Bluetooth. Even those who are not very familiar with technology will find it easy to navigate between the various functions. The instructions are clear and pairing with the phone was quick and smooth. Very nice watch, very easy to connect to the phone. The brightness is great. It comes with the cable to charge it. It is ideal for reading messages, receiving phone calls, calculating heart rate, etc. I am delighted with my purchase.
Quality, price, excellent, long battery life, large dial, easy to use

review_title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
body_en: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

I've been using Garmin for running for years now. They've improved a lot! This one does everything I need and more. I like the body battery, sleep info. The 5 syncs up to GPS much faster than my 4 to run or walk. I love the music, however, my headphones sometimes disconnect to the watch while running. Not sure if it's the headphones or the watch. It's pretty easy to use if you've had one before. It has changed on the strength where you hit the bottom button vs tapping the watch to enter weight/reps (don't have to do that anymore, not that it was a problem). Overall I'm super satisfied. Can see it better as well with the new display.

review_title: The best fitness tracker I've used
body_en: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. Overall I think this watch is a great fit for a more casual user who isn't running marathons but wants to track fitness and sleep and get some extras like smartphone notifications and see the weather at a glance. If you want something with more smart features and better build quality (i.e. more metal and less plastic), then the Venu might be a better fit. Or they have the Forerunner if you do run marathons. Or a bunch of other models for more specific use cases. But I would highly recommend giving this watch a try if you're looking for the same things that I am.

review_title: Great choice for my sensitive skin.
body_en: Great so far. I tried another brand the caused a rash from the heart rate monitor (not the band because I swap them for cloth or leather). Garmin Vivoactive 5 has not caused any skin irritation! I am pleased with the metrics it gives. The app takes some getting used to, but it isn't complicated to navigate...just different from fitbit. So far the battery charge lasts for at least 7 days. It charges quickly. I like the screen size, metrics and words are easy to read. The screen reacts well to touch even with a screen protector on. It is easy to access the watches features. I like the wake up summary. It gives me prompts to move and stretch. It gives sleep advice and measures body battery throughout the day. The watch is comfortable to wear and looks great with everything. I swap between a nylon band and leather band. I would highly recommend.

review_title: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
body_en: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

I was concerned the watch face would be too big but I got used to it right away. The size makes the display easy to read so I can keep track of my steps with just a glance. I also use the bike riding function (GPS) to track miles. I wish it would convert miles biked to steps taken but not sure any watch does that. I used the golf app the other day for distance and scoring. With any new electronics it takes a while and patience to figure it out but once I did I really like it. I'm still learning. I also like the sleep tracking function. Long battery life.

review_title: Garmin vívoactive® 5 Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch
body_en: The Garmin vívoactive® 5 has been a great watch to help monitor my daily activities, sleep, heart rate, and so much more. I wasn't so interested in the idea of connecting to my phone but rather the health benefits. It was a great purchase. The screen size is not too large for my small 5 inch wrist, but also large enough that I can clearly see the screen. The watch was easy to set up, make adjustments to as I learn about the various functions, and was easy to connect to my phone and work benefits. I like that I am able to select which features I would like to use. Garmin is very compatible with many fitness programs. I don't have good success wearing a silicone strap so I did purchase other bands which were simple to remove and connect to the watch head. I believe Garmin was a very good choice for a first health and fitness watch for me.

Just received the watch today, it’s nice but I have some concerns. For starters the band is completely silicone and plastic- the buckle piece is plastic, even the case around the watch is plastic. For $200 you’d think it would at-least be metal. The setup was easy- but came with very little instruction for other things like changing watch faces, setting up apps, etc. Learning how to use the watch and what the buttons all do is pure guessing. The charger is USB-C- if it wasn’t for my laptop I would have no way to charge the watch. Should have come with a compatible block. UPDATE: After using the watch for several days I do like it. While the overall construction (plastic casing) could be better, the overall operation works great. Steps and heart rate seem accurate. The display looks nice, customizable, and the watch is comfortable. The stress levels don’t seem to be accurate. I get “high stress” alerts when all I’ve been doing is laying in bed all day. Just add a titanium casing to the surrounding of the watch and provide more thorough instructions on overall use + updates for accuracy on certain apps and it would be perfect!

I'm writing this review about 3 weeks after purchase, so I've already gotten to know the watch well. The product is amazing and meets all my expectations and even more. Great workmanship, the watch is light and the strap is very soft, so you practically don't feel it on your hand. A fantastic display that shows everything perfectly, even in direct sunlight. With continuous heart rate measurement, smartphone notifications turned on, recording several activities and making several payments a day, the watch lasts 7 full days on a single charge and usually has about 20-30% of the battery left. For me, it's a fantastic result. Great customizable dials that can be downloaded for free from the Connect IQ store. The watch will be perfect for a person who wants a small and light watch with contactless payments, continuous health monitoring and activity recording. Of course, for professional athletes, Garmin has better devices, but for amateurs it is a very good choice.
I’ve been using the watch for a while now. It’s amazing and well worth the price. Highly recommend

Excellent product like all others from the brand. It took me a while to choose, as there are so many options. Just very happy with it. Besides being too cute.

For somebody who doesn’t wanna spend $100+ on a smart watch I do really like this one, affordable, it works pretty, easy to use, well now am I expecting the step counting and calories to be exact? I love that I can receive my calls and text through it, I do wish I could respond to texts but that’s okay it keeps me off my phone some. My watch works very well. Make sure the download the VeryFit app set up some features and monitor your workouts. Also, when attaching the power connector to the watch and One direction it will magnetically clamp to the back of the watch if you flip it around it will not, so make sure it holds on tight. You can set it to respond to incoming phone calls via a sound or a vibration or silent and it will also show you snippets of text messages and emails. I really like this watch. There's only a small section in English that will help you get it connected the rest of it is pretty straightforward on the watch and the VeryFit app. You may also select from a large variety of watch faces through the app.

review_title: Great smartwatch for an Android (Google pixel)
body_en: I had gotten a different smart watch originally just so I could see who was texting or calling so I didn't have to have my phone out all the time. It was junk! I stumbled across this watch and am sad I didn't replace the other one sooner! This is a big enough screen to be able to see the start of a text or email, but not so big that restricts mobility! Decent range between phone and watch to keep the Bluetooth connection, and accurate steps count! Also love that I can customize the picture it uses for the home screen

I am really liking this watch! I was horribly sad when I broke my Apple watch. I refused to pay to fix it or to pay for a new more expensive one. This watch made my month. Rarely it does something annoying like warn me about high heart rate that is not high, not switch time zones, or light up too much bursting forth light while I try to sleep, but the price made it well worth it. review_title: Great Value Smartwatch with Useful Features
body_en: For the price, this watch has been a nice surprise. It looks good on my wrist, feels comfortable even after wearing it for hours, and I really like the color. Pairing was easy, the connection stays stable, and calls come through clearly without much delay.

I’ve been using this Cillso smartwatch。and it’s been fantastic. The screen is clear touch response is smooth and tracking my daily steps and workout activity is super easy. Battery life is solid as well. Definitely a great buy for the price。

It’s honestly a decent smart watch/exercise/step tracker, and connectivity on land is pretty good (I can go a fair distance in open space away from my phone before the watch disconnects). Battery life is pretty good, and it does receive texts and allows you to control your music. I am writing this review as someone who works in aquatics-specifically spending a lot of time in the water. While the watch does have good water resistance, the connectivity under water is non existent and it also tends to react as though I’m manipulating the screen (I am aware that all these complaints are normal with water). All in all, it’s not what I was looking for. One other MINOR complaint. The app that comes with the watch gives you the ability to personalize your home screen (which is genuinely fun/a great feature). A lot of them come with a “current outside temp” reading, but I can never get this part of the home screen to connect properly regardless of the home screen in question. A petty complaint but a complaint nonetheless XD All in all, it’s probably great for on land day to day/exercise, but definitely not for water related activities.

review_title: Great for the price! Can't complain.
body_en: I've worn the watch for a few days now. I love how you can change the watch images and layout. There are some free options which is amazing. Love how you can switch out the band as well. Silicone tends to irriate my skin and its too big for my wrist, so I ordered smaller nylon bands. Helps you exercise if thats something you partake in. I don't. 😅 I do wish the band had a few extra holes for us smaller wrist people. But overall, great watch.

Not a true smart watch which can operate without a phone, but the features it does have work extremely well. You can sign up for a fitness tracker, or just use it to check vitals on the go. Only annoyance is the magnetic charging piece, nowhere near as easy as Qi charging, but it is a lot more affordable than others. We used it to monitor blood oxygen when suffering from influenza A - the missus has asthma, but no need to go to hospital if O2 remains above 90%

This smart watch with Alexa and a 1.83″ screen has surprised me for the better, especially because of how complete it is for its price. From the size of the screen you can see that you can read notifications and see information without straining your eyes, and with Alexa integrated it feels more “intelligent” than other basic watches. When we open the box we find: The watch itself, a magnetic charging cable and a leaflet as an instruction manual. The first thing is to charge it and then scan the QR code with your phone to obtain the Veryfit application. What I liked most: The integration with calls and notifications works fluidly and means you don't always have to take out your phone. The sports modes (more than 110) are very abundant for the price, and allow you to record everything from walks to more specific activities that I am missing... The heart rate monitor, pedometer and sleep monitor functions are there and do a good job for daily use (although they are not medical level, they give you a good general idea). The fact that it's IP68 waterproof is a plus for everyday use — you forget to take it off even in the shower or when it's raining. The DIY sphere is fun: you can personalize it, which adds a more personal touch. The overall feel: It feels solid, well integrated with Android/iOS, and has features you'd normally expect on more expensive watches. For someone who wants a complete smartwatch without investing a fortune, this model has many pleasant surprises. If you want a versatile smartwatch without breaking the bank, this one is worth it.

Among the many smartwatches I have tried, I admit that this is certainly among the best! It even has 100 different sports modes!! Whatever type of training you choose to do, find the right function!! I wore it overnight and the sleep tracking is very accurate and helps you improve your sleep quality. It is water resistant with IP68 rating, in fact I tried it in the shower. You can forward calls directly from the display. I highly recommend it!
Bought in 2024 it is an excellent product!

review_title: Une montre intelligente complète et étonnamment convaincante pour le prix
body_en: 1) Getting started and connection The initial configuration is done without major difficulty. Pairing with the phone is quick and stable, provided you install the required companion app. This passage is mandatory to fully exploit the functions, but everything remains accessible even for a user unaccustomed to connected objects. review_title: Smart sports watch for women. Grateful gift 🎁 💛 💓 💖
body_en: This smartwatch is an excellent choice for anyone who wants to stay active and keep track of their health. It features sports and fitness tracking, heart rate monitoring, sleep monitoring, and daily activity tracking to help users achieve their wellness goals. The easy-to-read display shows the date and time, while multiple sports modes make it suitable for walking, running, cycling, and other activities. The watch is also designed to withstand rainy conditions, thanks to its water-resistant construction. With a comfortable design, long battery life, and useful health-monitoring features, this smartwatch earns a 5-star rating for its performance, convenience, and value. ❤️ the pink callor and the An extra watch band.

I loved this women's smartwatch from the very first moment. It features an elegant, modern design that pairs perfectly with any style, whether casual or dressy. The screen is clear and user-friendly, and the functions are highly practical for daily life. I especially appreciate being able to receive notifications, track my daily activity, and stay organized without constantly having to take out my phone. Plus, it is comfortable to wear all day long, and the battery life is impressive. Overall, it is a beautiful, functional, and practical watch. I think it’s an excellent choice for any woman looking for a stylish smartwatch that doesn't compromise on the features needed for everyday use.

I’ve been using this smartwatch and really like it so far. The rose gold color is cute and the extra band is a nice bonus. The screen is clear, it’s comfortable to wear, and having features like step tracking, sleep monitoring, heart rate, and call notifications is really convenient. *** I've been using this watch for 3-years (& 1-month) now. It still works great and I still have zero regrets! I even got one of my sons to buy the same model. *** ------------------------------- Original 11-month review: Thanks to this watch, I was able to drop the 20+ pounds I put on during my post-covid depression. It got me moving again and whereas the original daunting number of 10k steps in a day made me nervous, I now walk around 23k steps daily without even thinking about it. The challenges on the app have helped me move from my former weight loss goals to my present toning ones and suffice it to say, all of this has helped tremendously with my mental health as well. As for the watch features, I was looking at all sorts of brands and all kinds of models and settled on this one and never looked back. I needed a time teller, a pedometer and a heart rate monitor, in no specific order. I received all of those and more with this wrist decor. Not only does the watch look nice and feel weightless on my skin when adjusted correctly, but it works so well at everything it was made to. The heart rate monitor is very accurate when compared with other heart rate monitoring devices. The watch is simple to clean although I was afraid of damaging something whilst attempting to clear out the 'gunk' around the plug-in site. I didn't purchase the watch for the sleep related feature but it is an interesting bonus. After roughly 9-10 months of continuous 24-hour use, I finally started noticing it act up during my treadmill workouts. My heart rate would drop to 0 and at one point I saw it jump to 248. Since I wasn't dead or dying during any of these times, I thought I'd start turning it off at night and I haven't noticed the issue since. It could have just been an error that required an update but like I said, I didn't buy for the sleep feature anyhow. The battery life is pretty good I'd say. When I told my husband one day that I should 'charge my watch tonight because it's been a couple weeks' he was really surprised. I keep track on my exercise calendar whenever I feel the need to plug in, which I do during the night so it doesn't interrupt my steps during the day. I normally charge once it hits somewhere in the 10-19 percentile. This takes (me specifically) about two weeks to accomplish, with roughly an hour and a half, minimum, of recorded activities at least five days a week and the watch otherwise just being turned on consistently. Of course, there are extra outings that warrant using the start button once in a while and yet I still find my charge schedule to remain the same. You can choose from a variety of watch faces that come standard but I definitely have enjoyed looking through the Garmin store at other options. The background I've used for quite some time now shows the moon in its current phase and as a lifetime star gazer, this is a face I was more than happy to throw money at. I spent just a few dollars and received something around 10 different looks, several animated such as plants or flowers that grow or open as you complete your steps for the day- amazing, if you like that sort of thing, turns out I do. Overall, I love my watch and I hope it lasts me a good, long time but if and when it finally dies from time cancer, I'll be sure to replace it with another Garmin!

review_title: Excellent watch functionality but some tweaks recommended
body_en: I had a sports watch and polar chest strap monitor 25 years ago for Concept 2 rower training. Technology has improved enormously since then. I chose the Garmin Forerunner 55 because I wanted simplicity as well as multi-functionality. It fulfils both needs. Above all the Garmin sports watch is accurate. I am now 71 and have just started training prep for another C25K with my daughter - hence the need for an accurate heart rate monitor. The things I like about the watch and app follow plus some suggested tweaks. On the positive side customisable heart rate zones are useful, and it is easy to develop warm up, walk, run, repeat x8 workouts, which can then be modified in subsequent weeks. However, I had to use AI to pose a dozen or so technical questions about how to set up specific procedures and to analyse and interpret some of the performance data that the Garmin produces. The written Garmin instructions in multiple languages don’t touch the sides of what the app can do hence using Google Gemini to pose detailed questions. Another user tip - the Garmin app can be integrated with the Chronometer app which monitors food and exercise expenditure. This combination of apps is a really sophisticated tool to record data, if you are of a scientific disposition. For example, if your Adjusted Baseline Activity hits zero, it indicates that your Garmin has accounted for every metabolic "tick" above your resting BMR. The wider screen of an Apple Mac is much more accessible to see all the post exercise Garmin data. The IPAD version of the Garmin app is actually a scaled mobile app and it is difficult to escape from a page as the menus are obscured. A workaround is to reset your IPad display to ‘more space’, but I would recommend using a laptop and the Garmin website which have no technical issues.

Edit (06/10/25): Now about 8 days into the Bip 6. After a week of use, the watch was sitting at 50% charge. I charged it up to 96%+ in about an hour. I'm using a USBC charger which I think provides about 2A. Can't say for sure as it's a charger built into a lamp in my bedroom that has both USBC and USBA; the "C" charger shows my Pixel phone charges "rapidly" whereas the "A" plug charges normally (slower but fast enough for the phone to hit 100% sometime during the night). I did try the "A" port (with an A-to-C cable) but it is slower. Still totally happy with the Bip 6. More feedback in a few months. Early days but I thought it might be helpful for those trying to decide between a Fitbit and this Amazfit Bip 6 (a truly unfortunate name). I had been using a Fitbit Charge 5 for a couple of years. The first week I wore it, the Charge 5 detected Afib and that probably saved my life. So I wanted to really like the Charge 5 and continue using it. However, I discovered it was terribly inconsistent in providing a sleep score and HRV; perhaps 40% of the time it just failed. A month or so ago (after 2+ years of use), it would just go "black screen" if I did anything with the Charge 5 other than simply looking at the screen. The battery also didn't last very long and the charger "connection" (magnetic) was hit-or-miss so it was time for a new watch. After deciding against another Fitbit (reviews have gotten worse over the years and Google has already said Fitbit will soon no longer be supported properly), the choice was either an expensive Garmin (and they're all expensive), a Samsung Galaxy watch (also $$$), or one of these "cheap" Chinese brands. (Can't use an Apple watch as my phone is of the Android variety). This Amazfit seemed to have the best reviews of the cheap smartwatches so I bought it with the 3-yr warranty for under $100 total. Amazon delivered it the next morning. Followed the prompts and set it up in a few minutes so it syncs with my Pixel 6a with the Amazfit Zepp app. I charged it using the provided charger "puck" (you must provide your own USB-C cable, remember this!) and, once it reached 100% (a couple of hours maybe), I strapped it on and configured the watch both with the watch's preferences and the Zepp app. I have most of the integration with the phone switched off; why did I need to answer my phone with the watch when I have my phone on my hip all day? I just wanted the watch to keep track of my steps, heart health, and sleep (the latter the most important point). So here we are after three nights and the watch seems to be 100% accurate in sleep tracking and heart health reporting (and it keeps perfect time, of course). As I indicated above, these are still early days but I'm thrilled with this Bip 6. I even am dabbling in the watchface creation app on the web and even that works! Why would I want to use that? I hate tiny type on a large screen so why not make a watchface that really shows off how large all the information can be presented? Great stuff. I am not going to test how waterproof the watch might be; I remove it before showering or swimming and am careful otherwise. BTW: There's a function on the watch where you can "eject" any water that might have found its way into the speaker. (Yes; the watch can play music and you can speak through it to your phone but I'm not going down that patch.) The only downside I can see (and it's not for me) is the length of the band; I have a small wrist but the fourth hole in the strap makes the watch fit properly; I would have expected a longer strap for larger wrists. However, using that fourth hole leaves about 1.75" beyond the buckle (.75" of which tucks back inside the band and that's fine). I would recommend to Amazfit that they provide a longer strap for larger wrists (much like how Fitbit does it). Oh, yeah; one more thing. One of the included apps on the phone is a compass! I set it up so one of the buttons on the side of the watch launches it. You know when your GPS starts off by saying "head east"? Who knows where that is without a compass? Now I know. I'll report back in a few months with more info.

review_title: Here’s an honest review for ya!
body_en: I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide. For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL. After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise. I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature! The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus! I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing. Cons: The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol. It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps. I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning. Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks. Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you. I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money. Hope this helps!! EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.

review_title: This Review is the only one you need to read! This watch DOES IT ALL!!!!!
body_en: This will be the only review needed to know this is the Smart Watch to purchase!! I have at this point probably purchased and returned more than 50 smart watches because I wanted notifications to have an audible tone and not just vibrate. With Bluetooth 5.2 it was an automatic with most of the accompanying apps you had to partner the watch with but when 5.3 came out, it became vibrate only on all apps with the exception of ONE…VeryFit. Additionally, VeryFit is the ONLY one which will register notifications from LITERALLY EVERY SINGLE APP you have which sends banner notifications to your phone, not just the 10-15 options typically seen in the other apps like Gloryfit, DaFit, FitCloudPro, HBand, etc. In order to receive these Push Notifications on an iPhone, which is what I have, you need to go into Settings, Bluetooth, touch the “i” in the circle and check off “Show Message Notifications” and “Share System Notifications”. You must then go to the App List, find VeryFit, make sure Background App Refresh is checked and Notifications are mirroring the ones I’ve captured in my images. The other important piece of info is the watch volume is set low when it first arrives. Make a phone call from the watch and touch the speaker icon key to allow for raising the volume. In the VeryFit app itself, go to Device, click Notifications, be patient and wait a few seconds and the screen will expand - check off “Sync Phone Notifications” and this is where all the excitement is! As notifications come to your phone, they will also become listed here on this page (and your watch will get the alert for them at the same time) and this is where you can Allow or Turn Off the specific notification. I have also captured this in my images for reference. As you can see, I get notifications for everything I receive on my phone. If you need more assistance, do as it says and tap the “i” in the circle on that page and you will get the detailed instructions just as I have given you now. I have also captured those in my images for you to reference as well. This tracks sleep, stress, energy, blood oxygen level, heart rate, gives you weekly averages on all. It can track your cycle for females and ones weight. It has suggested programs to help with better sleep habits, managing weight, stress, breathing exercises etc. It has every possible physical exercise activity one could imagine. It’s waterproof, has excellent options for watch faces - many are free or you can opt to pay for some if you choose not to become a Community member and if you do, those become free then as well. You can share your progress within the community to help stay motivated if needed. You can contact customer service if you have additional questions at anytime by tapping the little blue operator floating on the page within the app as well. There are screen protectors available, watch cases are shown available but they are too big, so don’t bother, you can change out the bands - there’s nothing you can’t do with this watch and the battery life is also fantastic, lasting me a week so far, even with all the many notifications I receive!! Obviously, I highly recommend it!! You won’t regret the purchase! The only thing I am now in need of is finding its twin in rectangular form because I like to switch between that and round; should I find it, I will update this review with the information! I hope this review has helped!

Plus the battery life is way longer than the 10 days claimed on the Active 2 and while it's not a huge deal to charge, it's still much more convenient to have extra battery life. One thing I was a little unsure of was the thickness. The photos kind of make it look like a beast. While it is thicker than the Active 2 it's not obnoxious and it's given me no pause whatsoever in terms of look and feel. Brightness is excellent, though I haven't had it long enough to test it on a sunny day outdoors. **Edit** Have been out in full sun with it and no problems seeing the screen The strap is very comfortable and is the same type of quick release strap with the pins that other smart watches have. Doing some googling it's a 22mm strap which shouldn't be a problem to find. One thing worth mentioning is some peoples skin is sensitive to silicone straps. My skin is not, but I've also had nylon with velcro and can recommend that if you want to use a different strap. Also there's no more tucking the tail of the strap down between your skin and under the strap, it's now routed the way most other straps are, on the outside. I'll update this review if I have any issues, but if you're up in the air between this and the Active 2 and you don't have tiny wrists I'd definitely go with this. Edit 1/22/26: Zero issues to report. One thing worth mentioning is that the face is not completely flat. The edges at the bezel curve down slightly. This means a flat 1.5 inch screen protector won't work; the edges would come off or there would be bubbles that you can't remove. I'm currently using the same screen protector I had for my Active 2. It doesn't cover everything but it does cover the flat part and vast majority of the screen completely and without any raised edges or bubbles. You can view my profile to see which I used. There seem to be some tempered glass screen protectors here on Amazon that curve down at the edges (with the bezel markings to match), but since this is so new I haven't bought one yet.
