review_title: Affordable price, the watch does a million things. Great customer service, too!
body_en: Was pretty easy to set up with the app, it came with pretty clear instructions. If you read some of the other reviews it's helpful as well to get it set up. It does a lot more than I thought it would! I just wanted something that would count my steps and my heart rate and this does a million more things than just that. Blood oxygen levels and stress monitoring? Excellent! I can even listen to music and make phone calls on this watch! It works on my Android just fine and even lets me connect my Bluetooth headphones at the same time the watch is also connected with Bluetooth.

review_title: Recommended, lots of pluses, a few caveats
body_en: I've come to really like this rose gold smartwatch that I bought as a replacement for a Fitbit Charge 4. I have narrow wrists so it's big in comparison but as said, I'm getting used to it. I love being able to read it at a glance without squinting. The screen is sharp, crisp, gorgeous color and easy to read. Set up was initially easy but when I started using the watch, customizing screens, layout of icons and grant it the permissions it needs, I had to turn to googling "IDW28" and found most of the answers i needed. I am fairly tech savvy and after a lot of frustration, I could only solve my issues this way. (The companion app was no help.) The biggest problem was the watch would compete with my ear buds, phone or bedside speaker to take over Bluetooth control, and attempt to direct the audio to the watch. Audio would cut in and out as it repeatedly tried to take control. I finally figured out what was wrong when I realized a phone call I received was switched to my watch. I had a Dick Tracy watch! 😂 Lol and the audio is not nearly loud enough to make calls on our listen to music. Overall the watch with its phone app is exceptional to monitor steps, heart rate, sleep patterns, exercise sessions, stress level, water intake, weather and control your phone's music app, camera and much more. It also alerts you to notifications of messages and emails. Essentially it's the same notification that your phone displays (not the whole email or text) and you cannot respond. It does not measure blood pressure as some reviews suggest. It will connect to your AI asst but I don't need that. I do wish for a way to enter water intake in the watch but for now that has to be done on the phone app. It charges fast and is easy to hook up. The battery lasts about a week but you're mileage may vary depending on your settings. I would definitely recommend buying if you are looking for an easy to read screen that is a giant step up from something like a Fitbit. If you want to send messages or emails, respond to them, see images attached in same then look to spend 5-10 times the price. Me? I'm happy with the purchase. I don't need to make calls on a watch or compose replies to texts and emails on my wrist. I really hope they solve the problem competing for Bluetooth as I'd like to turn on some of the features I had to give up to solve the problem.

Hello there, future watch owners. If you're like me, you've spent wayyy too much time agonizing over which knockoff smart watch to buy, and have probably read every review ever written. So, here is a list of every observed helpful and unfortunate aspect of this quality timepiece. I've been using it about a month. Pros: It looks nice. The screen is large enough to read and navigate easily, without feeling like you have a tablet on your wrist. The responsiveness is decent and the picture is clear. The swipe-right shortcut saves your most recent selections. There are lots of options for what it can do. Workouts, music, phone, calculator, stress, sleep, O2, heart rate, water intake, and something I found especially helpful as someone who leaves their phone lying around, Find My Phone. I've used most of these but have barely scratched the surface on the sports/workouts. Notifications show up with a red dot rather than a large icon, which I like and are easy to read and clear. I really like being able to adjust the brightness on the screen, and having a shortcut for the wake gesture; it's easy to turn off at night - because it's bright enough to burn your retnas - and back on during the day. The flashlight function is very helpful and almost absurdly bright. The alarm works well. The battery has been fantastic. I probably have less notifications set up for social media and email than some, but it easily lasts me a week+, which is way more than my poor, retired 4 year old Versa Lite ever did. Cons: The app sucks. It's like they tracked daily notifications with "app unpaired from device" and forgot to fix it. I am re-pairing every couple of days. It links up quickly but I wish it would stay linked. There are no screen protectors available that I've found and as a result, there is already a scratch on the face. There is also a chip off the wrist sensor already, which makes me wonder about the longevity, and my skins safety. I wish that when you pressed the side button from a selection, it would take you back to the menu, rather than back to the home screen, but that's minor. I also haven't found replacement bands. I don't care for the cloth band but I like the silicone. Eventually it will wear out and I would like to be able to replace it. I haven't braved the water with it yet because I'm afraid of drowning it, so I can't speak to that. I think that for the price-point, it is worth it. I threw the extended warranty on it, so I'm basically covered for three years if something messes up and then I just get a new one. Rant over, enjoy your day 🙂 hope it helps!

review_title: Great value smart watch with tons of features
body_en: This is a great budget smart watch for someone who is maybe interested in trying one and doesn't want to spend hundreds of pounds on a top branded one. This watch offers you a wide variety of apps and facilities that you would find on a top branded watch It has lots of health apps such as heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen levels and stress levels. It also has a wide variety of fitness apps included which can help you begin your fitness journey with things like walking plans and running plans, or to continue in a journey with more advanced features. The display is large and clear, colours of vibrant and it's a very sensitive screen allowing you to easily navigate your way through the various menus and settings. You will download an app indicated in the instructions, this will allow you to fully personalise your watch as well as store your data - obviously your watch has a limited memory and you will need to store data externally. It charges using a special magnetic USB cord which attaches to the back of the watch. Charging is fast. It's incredible how much you get in this watch for such a low price, it's fantastic for people on a budget or someone just wanting to test the water to see if a smart watch is for them.

review_title: Packed with Features and Surprisingly Polished
body_en: This smartwatch delivers far more than I expected at its price. It’s stylish and comfortable to wear, and the pink gold version looks particularly refined without feeling too flashy. The screen is clear and responsive, and basic navigation feels smooth. Bluetooth calling has worked well, and the battery life has easily lasted a full week with moderate use. I like the health features, especially the heart rate and sleep tracking, which seem reasonably accurate for general wellness. Notifications come through reliably, and I’ve found the hydration reminders and camera shutter function more useful than expected. The included extra strap is a nice touch, and the ability to swap bands with standard 22mm ones adds even more versatility. While I didn’t dive deep into the fitness modes, the range of options is impressive for anyone with an active routine. The app has room for improvement, especially in reducing clutter and simplifying customization, but it does what’s needed once set up. Overall, this is a very capable smartwatch that gets a lot right, especially for everyday tracking and light communication needs.
Watch is exactly what I wanted/needed. Smart, comfortable and easy to use. Great value for money too! Screen quality is great and battery life fantastic.

This feature-packed watch goes beyond just telling time, diligently tracking your steps and much more. Setting it up is a breeze, and personalizing the watch face to match your style is a real treat. With its stunning design and the comfortable Velcro band option, it not only looks fantastic but performs exceptionally well, rivaling watches at three times the price – making it an incredible value.

review_title: Ottimo prodotto ricco di funzioni ed adatto ad ogni occasione!
body_en: Questo smartwatch della AEAC si è dimostrato un prodotto davvero valido e qualitativamente ben fatto. Arriva a casa in una scatolina carina bianca con l’immagine di un orologio e la scritta smartwatch. Aprendo il packing troviamo lo smartwatch con cassa quadrata di colore dorato con un cinturino in silicone di colore rosa già montato. In dotazione abbiamo poi il cavo di ricarica usb con attacco magnetico e il libretto di istruzioni con la lingua italiana. L’orologio, che è un articolo da donna, si presenta molto elegante e adatto ad ogni tipo di occasione. Presenta 1 pulsante al lato che serve per accenderlo/spegnerlo e per navigare nei vari menù e sottomenù, in alternativa al touch screen che risulta comunque preciso e sensibile. Una volta acceso compare la schermata iniziale ed effettuando swipe si scelgono le varie funzioni. Le cose che questo smartwatch può fare sono davvero tante: per le sportive ci sono tutte quelle funzioni relative al benessere del corpo dovute a più di 100 attività tra le quali nuoto, trekking, corsa etc.etc. Ci sono anche molte funzioni più o meno utili come contapassi, cardiofrequenzimetro, monitoraggio ossigeno, monitoraggio del sonno e misuratore di pressione. Poi ci sono le funzioni di un orologio classico come la sveglia e il datario e le funzioni smart che attraverso un collegamento bluetooth ad uno smartphone ci permettono di leggere messaggi da app social come instagram e facebook o da applicazioni come messanger o whatsapp. La connessione ci permette anche di utilizzare le varie play list presenti sul device o di utilizzare la fotocamera dello stesso senza bisogno di prenderlo. L’orologio ha un quadrante rettangolare LCD da 1,8 pollici con una ottima risoluzione di 240x280p in full HD e luminosità, che può essere ulteriormente modificata attraverso le impostazioni. La chiusura del cinturino risulta molto forte e resiste anche a strattoni abbastanza violenti. La connessione con il cellulare è immediata ed è stabile fino a 10 mt circa dal dispositivo (in presenza di ostacoli come porte o muri ovviamente è minore). L’orologio comparirà nella sezione del bluetooth del dispositivo con il nome IDW19 BT. Se tutto questo non bastasse Il costruttore ci mette a disposizione un app gratuita di nome “Very fit” anche in lingua italiana che completa ulteriormente questo smartwatch. Quest'app è davvero utile in quanto una volta scaricata e abbinato l’orologio ci permette di rispondere e chiamare senza prendere il cellulare con una qualità audio sufficientemente buona per conversare anche all’aperto in mezzo ai rumori del traffico. L’app fornisce ulteriori possibilità di settare lo smartwatch nelle sue funzioni e scaricare tanti quadranti diversi o utilizzare una foto personale come sfondo ed ovviamente scaricare eventuali aggiornamenti. Sempre con l’aiuto dell'app possiamo avere un data base dei nostri progressi nelle varie attività sportive e nel monitoraggio delle funzioni corporali ed è possibile anche importare vari contatti telefonici, quelli che magari si chiamano più frequentemente, cosi da non prendere affatto il cellulare. Il costruttore asserisce che questo orologio è impermeabile infatti ha la certificazione IP68 però io il bagno o la doccia con l’orologio eviterei di farlo in quanto il vapore potrebbe danneggiare la batteria. Può essere collegato a dispositivi che hanno android 6.0 o superiore o iOS 9.0 o superiore. Le mie impressioni su questo prodotto sono davvero ottime. Menu e sottomenu sono cosi facili ed intuitivi che non c’è alcun bisogno di vedere il libretto di istruzioni. La batteria al litio è di buona qualità con una durata superiore ai 6/7 giorni utilizzandolo in maniera normale con una ricarica che non dura più di 2 ore. Il cinturino in silicone sembra di buona qualità morbido e flessibile risulta molto comodo e anche dopo averlo indossato una intera giornata non porta prurito o rossore. Vedremo con il tempo anche la durabilità. La lunghezza totale di questo smartwatch è di 25 cm circa il che significa che può essere indossato da persone con una circonferenza del polso che va da 15 cm fino a 20 cm e oltre. Questo tipo di smartwatch non permette di installare applicazioni aggiuntive, non è fornito di GPS integrato per un eventuale navigatore e non da la possibilità di scrivere messaggi o vedere foto. Io l’ho regalato a mia moglie e devo dire che le è subito piaciuto. Lei non è particolarmente affine con la tecnologia ma ha subito imparato ad usarlo, almeno nelle sue funzioni principali. Lo indossa tutto il giorno anche quando lavora e mi ha detto che è cosi leggero che a volte dimentica di indossarlo. Il prezzo di questo al momento della recensione non è disponibile quindi non posso fare una comparazione ed una eventuale valutazione in merito. In conclusione questo è un prodotto di cui sicuramente ne consiglio l’acquisto anche per un eventuale idea regalo appena ritornerà disponibile alla vendita. Spero di essere stato utile nell'esporre tutte le caratteristiche di questo prodotto che mi è stato proposto tramite il programma Vine di Amazon, in cui cerco di dare sempre valutazioni oggettive ed obiettive dei prodotti offerti e testati. Resto comunque a disposizione per chiarire ulteriori dubbi sul prodotto.

review_title: Durable Case with a Great Built In Kickstand
body_en: This case has been excellent for my iPhone 15 Pro Max. The fit is perfect and feels very secure without adding too much bulk. One of the standout features is the MagSafe magnet strength, which is incredibly strong and holds accessories firmly in place without slipping. I also appreciate that the clear material has stayed clear and has not yellowed from regular handling or oils from my hands, which has been an issue with other clear cases I have used. It was easy to install on the phone and has held up very well with daily use. The built-in kickstand is also a really nice addition and works well for watching videos or using the phone hands-free without feeling flimsy. Overall, it feels durable and well-made, offers great protection, and still shows off the phone’s design.

review_title: Premium quality without the premium price tag.
body_en: Design & Fit: It fits my iPhone perfectly. It has a slim, sleek profile that doesn't add unnecessary bulk to the phone while still providing excellent drop protection.Feel & Grip: The material feels premium in the hand and is so much easier to grip than the bare glass of the phone. I haven't had any issues with it slipping out of my hands or pockets.Functionality: All of the buttons remain perfectly clicky and responsive. Plus, the wireless charging and [MagSafe] magnet strength are incredibly strong—my accessories snap on and hold securely.If you're looking for a reliable, stylish case that will actually keep your device safe from everyday accidents, I highly recommend this one!

I've been using ESR for years, and I have been very happy with everything they make. This case is no exception. It's well built, all the buttons line up perfectly and can be pressed easily. The magnet on the back is super powerful. It attaches really well to any mounts or stands or other attachments. The built-in stand around the upper camera part is really nice. I got my phone in blue and wasn't thrilled at the idea of covering it with a case, so I really like that this case is clear (mine is ringed in black and looks really nice with the blue phone). I've also dropped my phone about 100 times since I started using this case and it's still in perfect condition. Highly recommend! I also want to mention I've had to contact ESR for a couple issues I've had over the years and they always respond and fix the issue.

I like it. It was worth it. The magnet was great for holding the snap on wallet. The stand was an amazing feature. I truly love the stand on the camera. So basically bought the same case again to a replace the original worn down one. I have had the first case for 2 years.

Works great, nice grip. Looks so nice and clear and I can see my phone color without distortion. I love the camera frame/stand. I like the white side button. Easy to take on and off but always feels secure.

Couldn't find a better case. We are obsessed with the flex stand. It holds in place at any angle. Perfect for watching shows/movies. Protects the phone and the stand helps protect the cameras. This is perfect for all ages and so easy to use.

review_title: It's from ESR, so you know it's GOOD!
body_en: Since I posted this review, and used the case on my new iPhone, I realized that while I love the case, I don't honestly love clear cases. So I have now purchased the case in Frosted Orange, which for me is just a more pleasing color combination. The buttons are still clicky, the case just as protective and I LOVE LOVE the Stash Stand. If there was one thing, I'd change, I would like the buttons to be separate, not built into the case itself. Building the buttons into the case, leaves an opening above and below the button, which could let dust get in between the case and your iPhone, but this isn't unusual and isn't really an issue. Otherwise, I just LOVE this case, even more so in Frosted Orange. Here is the original review I wrote: OK, so Apple hasn't even formally announced the new iPhone's coming, but I know I'll be getting the Pro Max version and I like to be prepared for a new iPhone well in advance of it's arrival. I was very pleased to see ESR already offering them for the 2025 models (likely to be called iPhone 17), so I went ahead and ordered a Pro and Pro Max in clear as we'll get both when we can preorder them. The case appears very well made as you'd expect from ESR as they are one of the really good case makers for iPhone. It's your typical Polycarbonate back, with TPU sides, which are grippy. ESR buttons are usually very clicky, but I won't know how they work on the new phone till it's in hand. I currently own iPhone 16 Pro Max and when they first came out, I bought a couple cases, none of which had a dedicated Camera Capture button built into the case. But when I got a case with a dedicated Camera Capture button, I realized that for me, it's mandatory on ALL future cases. And this case from ESR indeed has a Camera Capture button built in. ESR says this case is scratch resistant and that's really good as scratches do annoy me. But its certainly NOT scratch proof, so keep that in mind if buy this case. They also suggest the TPU sides of the case are anti-yellow, which is an added benefit. Only time will tell on that as eventually, TPU will yellow. Also built into this ESR case is what they call a Stash Stand. It actually surrounds the camera surround and is made of Zinc Alloy. It hides seamlessly, but when you pull it out, it turns into a stand you can use to prop your phone in either landscape or portrait orientation. The only question I have overall with the case is the camera surround is completely made of Polycarbonate, with precise sized openings for the cameras themselves. Not that this is a problem, but if dust get inside the area, it might be annoying as I'd need to remove my phone from the case to blow any dust out. Again, time will tell on this. Otherwise, while there are surely going to be lots of case options for the new phones this year, I can say without question that buying one from ESR is always a great choice in a case which is better made than lesser priced cases and it will provide excellent protection for an expensive iPhone with 3X Military Grade Protection.

review_title: Protective case that isn't very heavy, with handy stand.
body_en: I recently upgraded to the iPhone 17 Pro Max which is the nicest iPhone I've had to date, and I've had them all. I knew I wanted to get strong protection but was worried because even on its own, this is a large, heavy phone. I have the iPhone a little over a week, and have tried at least 10 cases, all different price ranges. And I already had to replace the screen protector because I dropped it without a case on 😡. My last iPhone had an ESR case I liked and used throughout its life so I wanted to try this brand again for the 17 Pro Max. I got both the Classic and Cyber to compare them. While these aren't high end cases, you get good protection from this brand. Here's the curious thing; the Cyber is the stronger case but yet it was cheaper on Amazon than the Classic for some reason. Cyber has 2 parts, a soft and hard and is tricky to get on. Definitely good protection but heavy and, the parts didn't line up perfectly which annoyed me. No fingerprint material however which is a big plus since that annoys me as well. The Classic is lighter (does show prints but is easily wiped off), goes on nicely and firmly and the protection is decent. It has the same handy stand which I trust won't break off before its time. Alas, I'm probably going to return both in my quest to find the perfect case but the Classic is a good basic, day to day workhorse, and looks quite nice on my new investment. Tip: Do NOT use this phone without a case! Your welcome.

I got this for my partner's iPhone 16e. He needed a new case & just wanted a plain black 1. review_title: Great MagSafe Hold & Premium Look without the Premium Price Tag
body_en: Finding a solid case for an iPhone SE that actually includes strong, reliable MagSafe compatibility can be a bit of a hunt. I picked this up looking for an everyday protective cover that wouldn't break the bank, and straight out of the box, it delivered exactly what was advertised. It offers an incredible value compared to high-end name-brand cases that cost three to four times as much. Real-World Details & Performance The fit on the phone is absolute perfection—it snaps on snugly and feels almost like a factory-custom cover with no loose edges or awkward alignment. The translucent matte finish gives the phone a very clean, high-class aesthetic that looks much better in person than standard clear TPU cases. Functionally, the MagSafe magnets are surprisingly strong. Magnetic chargers and accessories lock into place firmly with zero slipping. It has already survived a few accidental drops around the house without a scratch to the phone or the case itself. While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy. Pros & Cons Pros: Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely. Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps. Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look. Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost. Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection. Cons: Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time. Final Verdict If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!

This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.

I was concerned at first that the edge of the case on the back where the lenses are located would raise the phone too high and not allow charging when the phone was laying down on a charge mat, but that was not the case. Although, I did discover that exact positioning is important as just laying it down doesn’t always mean the phone is charging. So, I had to make sure to watch the screen when I wanna charge to make sure the mat and the phone aren’t position to charge when needed. All in all, this is a pretty solid product and I haven’t seen any yellowing in the plastic case as of yet, but it’s only been a couple months since I’ve been using it so maybe after a year I’ll reassess again. If there was one thing that would bug me about this case, is the raised lip of the back of the case surrounding the lenses. There was already a raised area on the phone for those lenses and this case just makes it that much more pronounced. I can only guess that the raised lip area on the back of the case is to further protect the lenses, but that also makes it harder for easy positioning for charging, and makes the phone bulkier when being placed into a pocket or bag. Still, this protects my phone and does what I want it to do so the raised area on the back is a minor issue that I can live with for now. Would I get another one? Hmmmm, maybe. Too early to tell at this point. But I won’t say no if something better comes out on the market.

review_title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
body_en: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

review_title: Great, not too bulky, yet very protective case - Just avoid Amazon shipping!!
body_en: For the money especially, this is a great case. Unlike the defender series or others like it this doesn’t have the P.I.T.A. two-sided case that locks together and is difficult to remove. Some reviews say it’s hard to put on, they’re clearly doing it wrong as it’s VERY easy. It’s a 2 part design, so while it comes together, it’s key to put the rubber part on the phone before snapping the hard plastic cover in place. No doubt people saying it’s a tight fit tried both at once. That’s more difficult and puts strain on the plastic. I’m the worst about dropping my phone. ai must have dropped it (iphone 8) at least 75-100 times minimum, and I don’t even worry about breaking anything anymore. The lip of it sticks out just enough to protect the screen, and the dual layering is ultra shock absorbent. It’s also pretty thin considering the amount of protection. I gave a 4 for durability and sturdiness as over time the outer plastic snapped on me and the inner rubber cover has a few worn areas, but at $20, replacing wasn’t particularly bothersome and it certainly lasted a good 6-9 months of hard use - better the case than my screen! Still a 5 in total as sometimes something has to break, and so perhaps it’s better being a little less sturdy. To anyone asking, of course it fits a 7, there is no big difference in the shape of 8 and 7. Idk if the lip would protect the plus as well since the screen is bigger, but that’s an overall risk the Plus phones have. Finally, I wish I could rate Amazon delivery separately. If you live in a city apartment building or even a house and won’t be home, they don’t bother reading delivery instructions (which always has info to access my mail room / lobby). It’s probably Amazon’s fault for having impossible schedules, but the drivers will *sometimes* try to buzz once (not always), then ignore the delivery instructions and leave the box outside if you’re not home or can’t answer. When I wondered where my replacement case was, a quick review showed some lady walking by, noticing the pile of boxes left, and took a couple small packages on top before walking quickly off, one of course was mine. Almost more infuriatingly, customer service put it down to “delivery error” and said they’d blame the shipper.. yet Amazon is the shipper. So they blame themselves and do nothing to fix it, and outsourced customer service means people that can only answer a few basic questions before they get confused and off script. This time they promised me they were working with delivery drivers to fix the problem, yet it’s been happening for at least 2 years. If my neighbors didn’t look out for each other and bring in anything left outside, much more would have been stolen by now. And still they have my sensitive door access info, which I don’t give out lightly.. and never use it. How it’s cheaper to replace these items than just fix the problem is beyond me. My advice, if 1-day delivery is an option, is to buy it alone so as not to make the $35 minimum and let UPS handle it, since their drivers would never leave packages out on a city street (they also take note of info like door codes, how crazy). It’s to the point where if I see Amazon shipping I dread it and have to try to stay home. At the very least a notification saying the package is outside for anyone to take would be a start. That’s enough about Amazon shipping, just on my mind since the first order got stolen. UPS safely brought the replacement though

review_title: Good Job – Torras O3 fitness iPhone 17 pro max!

review_title: Trust the Drop Rating, Don't Test It. TESTED: Bike drop tested. Perfect.
body_en: I bought this case because of the shock-absorbing rubber material integrated into the frame, and hopefully that will work out when I eventually drop my giant, heavy phone. Reminded me of Mous cases with that shock material, and even better this clear case isn't $85+shipping. The only thing keeping me from giving this case a 5-star review is I don't necessarily trust the durability because the case is so thin, it doesn't pass the eyeball test. However, I do trust that the product will keep my phone in tact, I just don't want to find out. EDIT: Riding my bike through a parking lot, hit a speed bump, it flew out of my jersey pocket and tumbled onto asphalt. Totally works. Hit all 4 corners, no scratches, no cracks even on my screen protector. Changing review to 5 stars. This thing is thin, and also the real deal. Almost want to buy a 2nd one in case they ever stop making it. Great news to prevent drops, all outward materials are very grippy and have a reliable feeling in the hand. The button action is very nice too, very easy to press both the power and volume buttons; you don't feel like the phone is going to rocket out of your hand when you try and turn your phone on, like the Speck Presidio case I returned. The main reason I tried so many cases was button action, and this case is great. Floating buttons FTW. Also, the camera is further protected than most cases with a little extra material in the lip. The ridge goes far enough past the 3-lens array you can visually see it protruding past the cameras, unlike other cases I've tried so far where it looked questionable. No question here, you're not putting your cameras down on the table. Keep in mind, we're talking like an extra 0.02" of material making the difference here. Don't worry, it doesn't show up in your ultrawide. The blue is also a great compliment to the Pacific Blue phone. It's close enough that it blends in spectacularly, my favorite part being the blue on the frame showing through the clear outer coating. It reminds you of the true color of your phone, which you lose if you get a case with black edges. I don't only want to see the blue when I put the phone down, I want to see the blue when I'm using the phone too. I'm already covering up the blue stainless steel frame of the phone itself. review_title: been buying for years great investment
body_en: I’ve been an OtterBox loyalist for years, and their new Commuter Series case for the iPhone 15 Pro is another home run. As someone who is constantly on the go and tends to be a bit rough on my devices, I need a case that can provide serious protection without being bulky or cumbersome. The OtterBox Commuter Series delivers on all fronts. The slim, pocket-friendly design of this case is a game-changer. It adds just the right amount of protection without making my phone feel overly thick or heavy in my hand. The dual-layer construction, with a hard outer shell and soft inner lining, provides excellent shock absorption and impact resistance. I've already dropped my phone a few times, and the Commuter Series case has kept it safe and sound. One of my favorite features is the port protection. The covered charging and headphone ports keep out dust, dirt, and debris, ensuring my phone's ports stay in pristine condition. The raised edges around the screen and camera also provide an extra layer of safeguarding against scratches and scuffs. Overall, the OtterBox Commuter Series case for the iPhone 15 Pro is an absolute must-have. It strikes the perfect balance between protection and portability, all while maintaining the sleek, modern look of my device. If you're in the market for a reliable, high-quality case that can withstand the rigors of everyday use, I highly recommend this one. It's worth every penny.

As someone who has a history of accidental phone drops (and let's be honest, who doesn't?), investing in solid phone protection is not just a preference, it's a necessity. The OtterBox phone case I recently purchased has once again proven why this brand is synonymous with top-tier durability and peace of mind. This case is an absolute tank, and if you value your phone's survival, look no further. Design & Build Quality (5/5): My OtterBox case feels incredibly robust and well-engineered right out of the box. The multi-layer design, typically combining a hard outer shell with a softer inner slipcover, provides excellent shock absorption. Despite its protective qualities, it doesn't add excessive bulk, maintaining a surprisingly comfortable grip. All ports, buttons, and cameras are precisely cut, ensuring full functionality without compromise. The materials feel premium and durable, built to withstand daily wear and tear. Protection (5/5): This is where OtterBox truly shines. I've had several unintended "gravity tests" since putting this case on my phone – drops on concrete, tile, and even a minor tumble down some stairs. Each time, my phone emerged completely unscathed. The raised edges around the screen and camera offer crucial protection against direct impacts when laid flat. The sealed port covers (on some models) are also fantastic for keeping out dust and lint, which can be a common issue. If you're prone to dropping your phone, or if your lifestyle demands extreme durability, this case is an absolute must-have. It shrugs off impacts that would shatter an unprotected phone. Ease of Use & Accessibility (4/5): While the protection is phenomenal, the case is snug (as it should be for protection!), so taking it on and off isn't a five-second job. However, once it's on, it's on to stay, which is precisely what you want. Buttons remain tactile and easy to press, and access to the charging port and speakers is unobstructed. Wireless charging also works perfectly with the case on. Value for Money (5/5): An OtterBox might seem like a significant investment compared to flimsy, cheap cases, but consider it an insurance policy for your expensive smartphone. The cost of replacing a cracked screen or a damaged phone far outweighs the price of an OtterBox. It's an investment that pays for itself the first time it saves your phone from a catastrophic drop. Overall Impression: The OtterBox phone case delivers exactly what it promises: unparalleled protection. It's a rugged, well-built, and highly effective guardian for your device, giving you complete confidence that your phone can handle whatever life throws at it. If you prioritize durability and want to avoid the heartache (and expense) of a broken phone, I wholeheartedly recommend an OtterBox. It's a small price to pay for genuine peace of mind. Pros: Unrivaled drop protection: Seriously tough! Durable, high-quality materials. Precise cutouts for ports, buttons, and camera. Excellent shock absorption. Good grip, despite its sturdy build. Protects against dust and debris (on models with port covers). Great long-term value, saves on costly repairs. Cons: Can be a bit bulky for some preferences (a trade-off for protection). Not the easiest to remove/install frequently. If you want your phone to survive, get an OtterBox. It's that simple.

review_title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
body_en: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

I dislike those rubbery cases because it's been my experience they are very difficult to get out of the front pocket of my jeans, they don't last and they let dirt and sand get into the case interior. FINAL COMMENT: This case is well worth it price, buy it. ORIGINAL REVIEW: 12 2023 Received my Flip5 few days ago along with samsung ring case. Was not pleased with the ring case as unlike the Flip4 ring case the ring only attaches to one side-the back side of the case, offers no hinge protection at all and relies on two sided tape to hold front on. Might be fine for some but not for really active users. This Beatle case was not cheap $36 but it seems well designed and of good quality. FIT: The Flip5 fits in it well. Phone functions well in it, all buttons work well, USB C cables all fit. PROTECT: Good corner and camera protection. Much easier to keep a grip the phone. HINGE: covers the entire hinge, sturdy but dose not automatically close when the flip5 is folded. It's a ez movement of the index finger to snap it closed, and it seems to stay closed until the phone is opened. OPEN-CLOSE: The phone opens and closes easily, in-fact more easily then with out any case as it's easier to get a grip with this case on it, however unlike the original Motorola DPC500 Microtac flip phone, the Flip5 can't be easily opened one handed with or without this case, although it can be done with this case, it's takes a little practice and nimble fingers. KICKSTAND: Kickstand works well with phone when vertically oriented but not as well when horizontally as the hinge protector interferes and makes it rock a little, it still works only will be a little lopsided. FRONT SCREEN PROTECTOR: touch still works well however the screen protector plastic seems a bit soft. Mine already had some small marks on it when it arrived, hopefully the screen protector can be ordered separately and easily replaced from Supercase. Another reviewer here wrote that he put a tempered glass screen saver on the front display and removed the one from the supercase, sounds like a good workaround. HOLSTER: again seems well designed and well manufactured. The Flip5 fits well in it when oriented with the front screen inward toward the hip and the usb port down. Easy to get the phone in and out of the holster and it seems quite secure when in it. While I can remove the phone from the holster one handed its not a fluid movement, where it is a simple task when using 2 hands, quick, simple and effortless. Returning the phone to the holster is a simple one hand operation, it snaps in and you know it's secure. The belt clip is robust, the clip rotates and is about 1" wide, should accommodate a belt of 1-5/8" wide, seems easier to use with the clip towards the front, but gives you the choice of any position 360°. I don't think anyone will need to worry about the phone falling out of the holster. Also seems comfortable to wear even if you have some belly roll, Dwane Johnsons abs not required. OVERALL FIRST IMPRESSION: I like this case, I'm glad I purchased it, I'd buy it again. I was concerned about it being to big, it's not. Good Job Supercase!

Likes: - Carbon Fiber look and Tough Design Aesthetics - Protection - Integrated Kick Stand Dislikes: - Front cheap feeling screen plastic protector that does not hold up well to oil, dirt, and cleaning overtime - Kickstand works, but has sharp edges that pokes. Would prefer if corners and edges were smoothed out - Not all USB-C cables may be able to plug in to charge with the case installed - Hinge flap protection feels vulnerable to breaking if dropped at certain angle as it is kept closed by a spring and not magnets. Only time will tell.

review_title: It does the job very efficiently, I'll gladly trade damaging a $30 case over a $1000 phone any day.
body_en: I can't believe that there are one star and two star reviews when the phone case does its job - protect the phone when dropped. Drop it far enough or hit it the right direction and any case will break! The trick is to NOT have the phone break! Plus the complaint about having to flip the hinge protector down. I just opened and closed my phone now and my hand on the back automatically closed the hinge cover. It's really a non-issue, yet listed as a complaint. I've never left it open. I've dropped my phone a few times without any damage to case or phone. Here is my evaluation after a year of use. The Beetle cover makes the phone a bit thick when in pocket, but that's part of the price of having some protection, like the 1980s big bumper blocks for the 5 mph crash thing. I could live without the stand, which could thin the case a bit. Still it does its job. Still better than having one of the giant phones that no longer can fit in one's front pants pocket. The Flip fits about any pocket, even with the Beetle case. I need that as a motorcyclist. But no way I'm having even the smallest phone fit comfortably in the side pocket and no way I'm sticking my phone half hanging out of a back pocket. So the Beetle does the job as well as possible. The case also is just wide enough making it not fit in my ProClip phone holder in my vehicle, almost but not quite fitting. But that's more of an issue for the ProClip than the phone case. Nice part is that the lower portion of the Beetle case is that it slides off easily and the phone fits the ProClip then. So I can live with the situation decently. Again, the stand could go away for me, maybe a case that doesn't have it, but I know that features like that sell others on the case. I forgot that it was even there, never using it. I've recently tossed the belt clip thing, not having ever used it either. Be nice without the extras for my use. So, in spite of minor issues, it does deserve a five star for the past year I've had it. I sure hope if I drop my phone that the case will break first. I'll trade $30 for $1000 damage any day.

The little plastic thingies that attached the stand connector to the bottom of the phone case have both broken off and now that part is just in the way to where I can't use my stand now. I'm really disappointed because this is advertised as such a tough case that can handle anything. This hinge is the Achilles heel of this case. So instead of spending more money on the same case, I'm just going to use my hot glue gun to glue that little flap up to the stand so that I can still use the stand part, but it won't be in the way now. All in all, this is a great case until that hinge breaks and renders your stand basically useless. Quite the disappointment for what I paid for it.

body_en: I picked up this tortoiseshell case when I wanted something protective for my new iPhone 15 Pro but with a vibe that fits my Hawaii laid back style. I liked that it uses sustainable materials and still looks chic rather than plain. The goal was to have something practical that would shield the phone and still feel good in daily life. In everyday use it holds up well. It fits snugly, buttons and ports are easy to reach, and the grip feels secure without being bulky. The built in magnets keep MagSafe charging reliable and compatible with accessories, which makes a lot of sense for me since I use wireless charging most days. What stood out is how the look stays stylish without shouting, and the case resists scratches while handling minor bumps. The texture helps me grip the phone more securely, and the pattern hides fingerprints better than I expected. A small caveat is that it does add a bit of heft and a touch more bulk than ultra slim options, so it takes a moment to adjust when slipping the phone into a pocket. review_title: Yes, Some Of Us Still Use the iPhone 13 ;)
body_en: I am still using an iPhone 13, which is kind of funny considering we are getting close to the iPhone 18 generation. I do not see much reason to replace a phone that continues to do what I need, especially when a decent case helps keep it looking almost new. This magnetic case has been a good match for that purpose because it protects an older phone while adding features that make it feel a little more current. The fit around my iPhone 13 is precise, and I like the coverage around the edges and corners. After years of owning the phone, keeping scratches, dents, and other everyday damage away from it matters to me. A case cannot stop every possible accident, but this one gives me enough protection that I am comfortable carrying the phone throughout the day without treating it like something fragile. When I take the case off, the phone underneath still looks remarkably good for its age. MagSafe is another reason I enjoy using this case. My magnetic chargers and other accessories connect without having to remove anything first. The magnetic hold feels secure during normal use, and charging has worked as expected. Being able to continue using newer MagSafe accessories is especially useful because it keeps my iPhone 13 compatible with the way I use my other devices today. The kickstand may actually be my favorite part. I watch videos, news, and other content on my phone fairly often, and being able to set it down instead of holding it the entire time is convenient. I can place it on a desk, table, or countertop and watch hands-free while doing something else. It is also handy during longer videos when holding a phone eventually becomes annoying. The case feels substantial without making the iPhone unnecessarily cumbersome. The buttons remain easy to press, and I can reach the ports without fighting against the case. It gives an older phone a refreshed appearance while preserving the familiar size and feel that made me keep the iPhone 13 in the first place. Overall, I have been very satisfied with this case. We may be approaching the iPhone 18 era, but my iPhone 13 is still going strong, and this helps me keep it that way. Between the protection, MagSafe support, and kickstand, it gives me several reasons to continue using a phone that still has plenty of life left in it. Pros: • Helps keep an older iPhone 13 looking remarkably well preserved • MagSafe support works nicely with magnetic charging and accessories • Kickstand is extremely useful for watching content hands-free • Worth the value Cons: None

review_title: Good basic phone case, with stand and see-through backing.
body_en: The case I have is for the iPhone 13/14, and it is currently installed on my personal iPhone 14. It fits snugly and is thinner and less bulky than the one it replaced. The back of the case is mostly made of translucent plastic, so you can see the Apple logo, and the base color of the phone case (mine is black, so no real whoop there). I like that it is a bit slimmer than the one I previously had, and it fits a bit better in my pocket now. This case also has a small flip out stand (see photos below), so it can be used to stand the phone at an angle for hands-free viewing. My third-party Qi wireless charger also works fine with this case. The hole for the Lightning charging port is a decent size and still allows use of a Lightning cord for charging. It is a bit snug, but seems slightly more roomy than the previous case (I do not have to fiddle as much to get the plug inserted (like the last case). The case has a slight ridge around the face of the phone, and a raised lip around the camera section on the back side of the phone. This is to prevent the screen and the camera lenses form coming into contact with the table surface. The front ridges are smaller than my previous case, but good enough as long as the table surface is not rough or too uneven. This case is nothing outstanding, but it does work well and fits the need for a basic protective case for the phone.

This case strikes an excellent balance between slim design and everyday protection. On an iPhone 13, it feels sleek in hand without sacrificing durability. The translucent matte back keeps fingerprints to a minimum and gives it a clean, modern look, while the subtle blue accents add just the right amount of style without being overdone. Functionally, it delivers where it matters. The buttons remain crisp and responsive, and the raised edges around the screen and camera provide added peace of mind for daily use. MagSafe compatibility is spot-on. It snaps securely into place on chargers and accessories without any alignment issues. The built-in stand is the standout feature. With multiple viewing angles including portrait, landscape, and a lower angle for browsing, it adds real versatility for calls, streaming, and desk use. When not in use, it folds flat and stays out of the way, without feeling flimsy. There is a slight increase in weight compared to ultra-thin cases, but it’s a reasonable trade-off for the added functionality. Overall, this is a well-rounded case that combines style, protection, and practical features into one smart design.

Unlike bulky pop-sockets or detachable stands, this integrated solution is always there when you need it, never in the way when you don't. Military-grade shockproof protection gives me confidence that this case can handle the inevitable drops and bumps of daily life. The raised edges around the camera and screen add extra peace of mind. For anyone with an iPhone 14/13 looking for a MagSafe-compatible case with a hidden stand and clean aesthetics, this is a fantastic value. review_title: Deciding between the Belkin and Anker Charger? Get the Belkin!
body_en: Over the past few months, companies like Anker and Belkin have introduced new charging stations that support Qi2.2 charging at 25 watts. Unfortunately, these products come with an extremely high price tag, as is common when they are first introduced. When spending such an exorbitant amount of money on a 3-in-1 charger, you want to make certain you carefully research all the available products to make the most informed choice. I bought both the Belkin MagSafe charger and the Anker Prime 25-watt charging station. In the end, I returned the Anker and kept the Belkin. The Anker was the most tempting purchase, given its unique design that included a display screen built into the stand that provided data on the exact charging wattage of each device. The screen also includes a clock and information on the current cooling level. I must admit, Anker's unique overall design and incorporating a screen make for a highly innovative product. The problem is, the Anker did not perform as expected. While charging my Apple Watch Ultra, it would only charge between 0.5-1.0 watts. My AirPods would only charge at about 3.4 watts max. Both these devices should be charging at 5 watts, but they never reached that level. Anker claims that "For watch models that support fast charging, the power can reach 3W - 5W when the battery is low. However, the power fluctuates during the charging process and does not remain at a high level continuously." However, even when my Apple Ultra Watch was near empty, it never reached 5W charging while on its stand. Despite the absence of a built-in screen, I noticed that the Belkin MagSafe Station charged my watch at a faster rate. My iPhone 16 Pro Max charged at a variable rate, which is normal for these chargers. You should only expect 25-watt charging when the phone is below 50%. Any charge above that will be slower. Another thing that I like about the Belkin over the Anker is its elegant design and small footprint. The stand looks very classy, has a padded charging base, and doesn't move when quickly grabbing and removing my phone. Anker also remained in place under the same circumstances. A win for both products. At the time of this review, the Anker costs $40-$100 more than the Belkin. I wouldn't mind paying more for the Anker if it performed as well as the Belkin, which, for me, did not. Furthermore, I had several frustrating issues dealing with Anker support when returning my unit and obtaining a refund. What I learned here is that just because a company puts out what appears to be a high-tech product with a pretty screen doesn't make it the better choice. If it doesn't perform as advertised, the consumer loses. I am having a much better experience with the Belkin. It's a solid charger that works as promised.

I had 3 less expensive generic 3-in-1 chargers for just over a year... they worked okay, but I was never completely happy... then about a month ago the weak magnets started to cause my Apple watch to start off charging but then lose the connection and let the watch die overnight. So I started looking for better solutions and found this one. First, I generally believe that "brand name" vs. "generic" is often just an excuse to charge more. I really balked at $129 for a charger. In the end however, I decided to take a chance and took the plunge. WOW! What a difference! First, the magnets are much, much stronger... dropping connectivity will likely not be something I ever worry about again. And because the connection is so much better, and coupled with the huge (power wise) 45 watt adapter... all 3 of my devices (iPhone, Apple watch and AirPods) all charge much faster and reliably, even with all 3 on the charger at once. Second, the information I found regarding the cooling fan and a "hum" appears to be overblown... I can't hear a thing! (But I also have other devices nearby that I can hear so it could just be drowned out; except, even with my ear right next to this charger I could not hear anything. So, don't let the fear of a fan scare you off. The only negative thing I can think of is that the arm for the phone is adjustable, you can lay the phone completely back to 90 degrees so that the screen points up (or very close to 90 degrees) if you want. It seems to be a friction kind of adjustment, I do not see any way to tighten or loosen it... it holds position pretty well so far, but I could see this becoming an issue later. And the folding arm for the phone will be useful if I ever travel with it... fold it down for compactness and through it in a suitcase... perfect. Overall, not the least expensive by far... but so far, the quality is the best I've found. I'll wind up with one or two more over time most likely (unless something even better comes along).

review_title: Great Charger for Apple Users, Just a Few Minor Drawbacks
body_en: Overall, this is a great charger and I’m very happy with it. It looks clean on my desk, charges all of my Apple devices in one place, and seems to charge faster than most chargers I’ve owned. A couple of downsides: the magnetic connection can feel a little loose at times, and you have to get your phone centered just right or it may slide off. It also makes a bit of noise, which can be distracting when you’re trying to focus and get work done in a quiet office. It’s definitely on the expensive side, but for the convenience of charging three Apple devices at once, I think it’s worth the price. If you’re invested in the Apple ecosystem and want a clean, all-in-one charging station, this is a solid choice.

I absolutely love this Belkin 3-in-1 Charging Station. The build quality feels premium right out of the box, and it looks incredibly clean and modern on my desk and nightstand. The Qi2 25W charging is noticeably faster than my older MagSafe charger, and the built-in cooling fan is a fantastic feature because my phone stays much cooler while charging. The fan is also surprisingly quiet. I really appreciate being able to charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all in one place without dealing with multiple cables everywhere. The magnetic alignment is strong and secure, and the adjustable viewing angle makes it great for StandBy mode and FaceTime calls while charging. Belkin did an excellent job with the design, performance, and overall convenience. If you want a high-end wireless charging station that actually feels worth the money, this one delivers. Highly recommended.

Having all three devices — iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch — charged simultaneously from one cable in one spot is the kind of quality-of-life upgrade that's hard to go back from once you have it. Everything snaps and seats exactly where it should with no fiddling. Belkin has been the reliable answer in this category for a while and the MagSafe lineup continues that. review_title: Great charger, but weak MagSafe magnets hold it back
body_en: This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked. First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it. Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of. I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice. Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product. If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it. You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. A surprisingly light bump can cause the phone to fall off the charger, and for something you may use every day for years, that matters. If you’re comparing this with the Anker Prime, which costs roughly $30–$40 more, the additional cost may be worth considering if it provides a more secure magnetic connection. Over several years of daily use, $30–$40 isn’t much of a premium to avoid an annoyance you’ll potentially deal with every day.

review_title: Compact in Size, Fast Charging, Saves Space and Great for Travel
body_en: I love this 3 in 1 charger! Say goodbye to all of the charging cords! It is small and compact. I bought the white one to match my furniture. My Apple Watch, AirPods Pro and iPhone charge quickly. The iPhone phone will fast charge to 50% in about 1/2 hour. The watch will fully charge in a similar amount of time. I love that the charger is compact and folds up for travel. The other Belkin 3 in 1 charger that I have is a side by side and takes up a lot of space. With this new design the old charger has been relegated to the guest bedroom.

review_title: Works well with iPhone 17 and Apple Watch 11
body_en: Quickly charges both my iPhone 17 and Apple Watch 11 simultaneously. Have not tried Apply EarPods charging so I cannot comment on that feature. The small charger footprint and single charge cable have significantly reduced the clutter associated with multiple charge cables on the table. Completely satisfied with this purchase!
Great charging, sleek profile, strong magnetic, quick charging, easy to use, and it’s been durable the past year so far. Definitely would try it before knocking it.

review_title: Nice looking charger with very annoying quirks/bugs
body_en: It's cool that this is the "official" charging dock that Apple endorses. When it works, it works well and it feels quality, with all hinges feeling sturdy. Time will tell after folding it hundreds of times whether the hinges will hold up, but I feel optimistic. This is one of the few options you have unfortunately for 25W charging if you have a newer iPhone, as they tend to be really expensive. Watch charging works fine and reasonably well, but it seems like the pad doesn't shut off and the watch continues to get warmer as it sits fully charged. Phone charging doesn't seem to have this issue, but it might be whatever cooling tech they have keeping it room temp-ish. The part I hate the most about it is the airpod charging area. It has an annoyingly bright white LED that lights up when you put it on the charger, and it takes forever to start charging, if it even does that. I've woken up contless times to my airpods not having charged at all, even though I put it down as correctly as possible. Even when I move it back and forth on the charger it takes forever to finally register the airpods are on there and frankly it's a really poorly functioning charger that tarnishes an otherwise decent dock. Even when it does successfully charge, it does the same thing where the charger doesn't shut off after fully charging and the airpods are really warm when I pick the case up. All in all, a decent charger but don't expect the airpods charger pad to work well. Frankly, I expected better for almost $100 and I'm pretty disappointing overall.
Para el iPhone 16

My husband is so happy with this. It seems like the folding mechanism is sturdy enough for frequent travellers but we just leave it stationary on a shelf. Easy to use, quick charging on a multiple devices, space saving, and aesthetically pleasing. I think it is expensive for what it is, but after researching cheap brands it seems like you get what you pay for unfortunately and I hope this will last years.
Love it works as it should

review_title: Mass capacity and reliable power backup
body_en: I am thoroughly impressed with this 40000mAh portable charger. It holds an incredible amount of power, allowing me to charge my phone, tablet, and other devices multiple times over on a single charge. It's a bit hefty, which is expected for this massive capacity, but the build quality is solid and the charging speeds are excellent. Highly recommend for long trips, camping, or emergency backups!

review_title: May Not Charge at Rate Claimed
body_en: When i plug my phone to charge it says super fast charging which ive never seen before. Ive seen fast charging never super fast. Cool 😎 but it only shows 7.7 watts on the display. 🤔 but i like this charger. It does what I need it to do. There's no its taking to long or overheating issues etc. The size form factor and display all nice. 3 ways to charge nice and price wasn't bad though could be lower. Happy with the purchase. Ugreen may become the new Anker having better prices for quality products.

review_title: Excellent power bank for ROG Ally – doubles playtime easily
body_en: I’ve been using the UGREEN Nexode 20000mAh 130W Power Bank with my ROG Ally, and it has been outstanding. It easily doubles my gaming time, turning the Ally into a truly portable handheld instead of something that constantly needs to be plugged in. The 100W output is no joke — it keeps up with demanding devices without throttling, and fast charging works exactly as advertised. I can game while charging without noticeable slowdown or excessive heat. The TFT smart display is also a great touch, giving clear info on power usage and remaining battery, which is very helpful. Build quality feels premium, it’s compact for its power capacity, and having multiple USB-C ports makes it versatile for charging other devices like phones, tablets, or even a laptop. If you own a ROG Ally or any high-power handheld, this power bank is absolutely worth it. Reliable, powerful, and well-designed.

review_title: Power bank that actually has power!
body_en: The battery life on this is what makes this product so worth it. You can charge this, and it will keep the battery life for months even when it’s not in use. Every other power bank I’ve had would lose its charge if it was idle or not in use. It does have some weight to it, but it’s very compact for the most part since it fits in the palm of my hand. It’s great for traveling and hiking long distances. Even on hikes in the heat it has no gotten warm or overheated.

This is a somewhat heavy (weighs about a pound), but powerful battery. I don't mind the weight, I expect that from a 20k battery. It feels solid and well built. I like the display and how it shows the negotiated voltage and amps so you can see what it is doing. I also like that it has a trickle charge mode for lower power devices like my watch and earbuds. Most batteries will shut off because there isn't enough of a power draw, in trickle charge mode the battery will not shut off for 3 1/2 hours. Please note that they recommend that you use a minimum 65 watt charger to charge the battery. You can use less power, but the battery will take longer to charge. With the more powerful charger it takes a little over an hour to fully charge. One day my M4 MacBook Air was down to around 25% and my phone was around 40%. I plugged both into the battery at the same time. I charged my phone to 80% and computer to 100% and the battery was down to about 10% remaining charge. The computer was drawing around 60 watts the majority of the time. One thing that has left me curious is that I have yet to see it either receive or draw more than 3 volts @ 20 amps since it says it is capable of 5 volts. Both my charger and computer should be capable of 100 watts, but I also know that devices negotiate with the charger so it doesn't bother me that it is less.

This is a really awesome power bank. It has extra features like a setting for lower power draw for older devices that wouldn't work with higher wattage output. It also has a great display that shows power draw from attached devices. It's a solid feeling compact brick but not too heavy. It'll fit in a pocket but you'll definitely notice it and will look awkward. The included cord and carrying pouch are a plus. It charges relatively fast if using a fast charger. Just note only 1 port outputs 100W and the other two will split the remaining 30Ws between the two. Another thing would be the outside plastic may be susceptible to dents if dropped. Overall, it's a great power bank and I recommend getting this one if you are looking for this form factor & a pretty high capacity.

review_title: A Power Bank to rule them ALL!!!!!!!!
body_en: The UGREEN Nexode 20000mAh: Seriously, Ditch Your Old Power Brick Okay, let's be real. Nobody gets excited about a power bank. But the UGREEN Nexode 20000mAh is the one exception that actually makes charging your gear feel... well, fun. The Dashboard You Didn't Know You Needed Forget those four little blinking lights that leave you guessing. The absolute best part of this power bank is the built-in Smart TFT Display. It’s like a tiny, high-tech dashboard for your charging life. You can instantly see: Real-time Wattage: Is your laptop actually pulling 60W or 100W? The screen tells you exactly how fast the juice is flowing. No more guessing games!Battery Percentage: The precise percentage remaining, not just "half-full-ish."Time Remaining: This is the MVP feature. It estimates exactly how long the power bank has left before it dies, or how long it’ll take to charge itself back up. Pure genius for planning your day.Power to Spare (For Your Laptop, Too!)This isn't just for topping up your phone. The 20,000mAh capacity paired with the high output means you can fully charge a MacBook or another hefty laptop while you’re stuck waiting at the airport or working remotely. And since it has multiple ports, you can charge your laptop, phone, and earbuds all at once without breaking a sweat. If you’re a digital nomad, a student, or just someone who uses their gadgets a lot, you need this. It’s reliable, it’s fast, and the smart display turns a boring chore into an easy, informed process. Grab one—you won't regret it!

if you need a power bank charger that can last long, charges fast, and can quickly charge multiple devices at one time, this is worth it, especially if you get it on sale like I did (usually 89.99, I got mines for 69.99). Functionalities are amazing on this unit, durable and long lasting, can take with you anywhere, highly recommended! *one year later and it’s still here, very reliable and helped me out in plenty of situations, especially when I’m on the go, I will say that it will drain more when you connect the more power hungry devices, but it’s still a winner in my book

review_title: je la recommande a 100% sans aucune hésitation
body_en: ESSENTIAL.... I have tested some power banks, but this one.... To begin with: Total recharge in less than 2 hours which is rather fast given the capacity. In fact... I needed something efficient and powerful to accompany me on long drone hikes. I have a mini 4 Pro 3 battery combo, and no need to explain to those who use it that at some point the batteries can melt in the sun at high speed and that we can remain frustrated by missing a last shot due to lack of battery. I left on a 12Km hike quietly, 1 first empty battery, which I plugged directly into this power bank: Charged at 35W (+- 35min of charging, identical to my charger at home) the time to walk around, to empty a second battery, the first was already at 100%... final result, I returned home less having consumed the equivalent of 6 drone batteries... there was still 33% left on this one which also allowed me to charge my phone. Well, it still weighs 450g; but I highly recommend it for this type of use. I came back happy to have really enjoyed this walk, my drone shots, without frustration of having missed a single one

review_title: Muy buena batería, me salvó en el apagón
body_en: I bought this portable battery from UGREEN and the truth is that it has been a success. It is powerful and charges your cell phone, tablet and even your laptop without breaking a sweat. The other day, with the big blackout, it was my lifesaver: I was able to have all my devices working without worrying about being stranded. What I liked the most: • Fast and efficient charging: Charge my laptop and mobile at the same time without losing speed. • Information screen: Shows the battery percentage and charging power, which is very useful. • Compact design: Despite its large capacity, it is easy to transport. Of course, as a negative point, the price is somewhat high. But honestly, because of the quality, the power and the peace of mind that comes with having it, I think it is worth the investment. In short, if you are looking for a reliable and powerful battery, and you don't mind paying a little more for quality, this one from UGREEN is a safe bet.
