This UGREEN power bank is one of the best I’ve used—it feels solid, well-built, and the 20,000mAh capacity is perfect for travel since it’s the max allowed for air carry-on. Despite the power, it’s surprisingly compact and comes with a pouch that keeps everything together, which is great for not losing cables on trips. Recharging the power bank itself does take a few hours, but that’s expected given its size and capacity. Overall, it’s a high-quality, dependable charger that gives me peace of mind compared to cheaper brands. Worth every penny, especially when on sale.

review_title: Compact and light charger. Does the job, would recommend.

review_title: Exactly what I needed for my trips!
body_en: Bought 2 of these for my upcoming travel and very impressed so far. Charges my phone and iPad very quickly without draining the entire battery on the power bank.

Very reliable and fast charger. Lightweight to carry. Very convenient with the two attached charging cables. It does get a little warm and sometimes the cables won't stay tucked away, but it is a minor thing. I'm glad I bought this.

I originally purchased this portable charger for an upcoming camping music festival, but I’ve ended up using it far more often than I ever expected. It’s small enough to fit in my purse, so I find myself grabbing it all the time. It has saved me in airports while traveling, at hotels when I forgot a wall charger, and even during nights out when my fiancé realizes his phone is almost dead. I’ve even used it to recharge a portable speaker after it ran out of battery one evening. The built-in charging cables are probably my favorite feature because we no longer have to remember extra cords. It has connectors for both my iPhone 14 and my fiancé’s iPhone 17 Pro, and those are the only charging ports we use anymore. I also like that the battery pack itself can be recharged in multiple ways, which makes it even more convenient. Pros: * Holds plenty of charge for multiple devices * Fits easily inside a purse or small bag * Built-in charging cables eliminate the need to carry extra cords * Works with both my iPhone 14 and my fiancé’s iPhone 17 Pro * Can also charge other devices like portable speakers * Great for travel, hotels, concerts, festivals, airports, and everyday emergencies * Multiple ways to recharge the battery pack itself * Excellent value for the price Cons: * Takes a very long time to fully recharge (at least half a day, sometimes longer) * Slightly bulkier than some ultra-compact battery packs Overall, this has become one of those products I never realized I needed until I had it. It has bailed us out on so many occasions that I now keep it in my purse almost all the time. The long recharge time is definitely its biggest weakness, but once it’s fully charged, it lasts a long time and has been incredibly reliable. For the price and convenience, I would absolutely recommend it.

This power bank has quickly become my favorite among the various ones I own. It stands out for being lightweight, making it easy to carry around, and it comes with built-in Lightning and USB-C cables, which is incredibly convenient—no more hunting for extra cables. It supports fast charging, which has been a game-changer for keeping my devices powered on the go. The LED display is a fantastic feature, as it provides a clear and accurate view of the remaining battery percentage, helping me plan when I need to recharge it. I’ve used it to charge both my iPhone and GoPro cameras, and I’m genuinely impressed by the speed and efficiency of the charging. On top of its functionality, the overall build quality feels sturdy and reliable. Given its performance and features, I think it offers excellent value for the price. Whether you're traveling, commuting, or just need a dependable power source, I highly recommend this power bank.

This battery charge is my favourite out of all the ones I've had. It has a digital display so you know when its charge to 100%, 2 different charging cables attached on the back to charge your phone with depending on the style of your mobile phone. i- phone or Andriod. Charges it self quickly and your phone when plugged in to it. Great value for money. I have one and now my teenage children have them as well as their so good.

Why did you choose this product over others?: I’ve been using this power bank for different phone and it charges like lightning and flawlessly! The sweetest part of this power  bank us the built-in cables, so I don’t have to search for a cable.  It’s also incredibly portable for that reason, easier to hold without a separate cable that would be unnecessarily long and would keep coming loose. The two built-in cables (USB-C and lighting cable) are a super fast in charging and it has more port for extra phone for family and friends to keep their phones charged for a decent amount of time using this power bank. I’ve used it for my Samsung S24which requires a lightning cable and for other relatives’ phones who need the USB-C so it really makes you the life saving king. Weight: Is a light weight power bank. You can pocket it with your phone. Heat level: It doesn’t heat while you are using it. Very impressive piece Works well: charges all the phone at super fast rate

This power bank stands out for its practicality and well-thought-out design. Right from the start, the packaging gives a premium feel, and it’s great that a USB-C cable is included for charging the device itself. Small details like this make a difference, as not all power banks come with the necessary cables. One of the features that impressed me the most is the built-in cables. They sit completely flush against the body of the power bank, which means they don’t stick out awkwardly. This is a huge plus, as it prevents them from catching on things when placed in a pocket or bag. This also makes carrying the power bank much more convenient, as you hardly notice it’s there. The LED display is another standout feature. Unlike power banks that use tiny LED dots to indicate battery levels, this one has a clear and easy-to-read digital screen, showing the exact percentage of charge remaining. This removes any guesswork and makes it much easier to know when it needs recharging. It’s a small but extremely useful detail that makes a big difference in daily use. Build quality is excellent. The power bank feels robust and secure in hand, with a well-constructed design that doesn’t feel flimsy or cheap. A feature that I particularly appreciate is the curved edges. It might not seem like a big deal at first, but having owned power banks with sharper edges in the past, I can say that those can be uncomfortable to hold, especially when using the phone while it’s charging. The rounded design of this one makes it comfortable to grip and prevents any discomfort when carrying it around. Performance-wise, it delivers exactly as advertised. The fast-charging function works effectively, and it has been able to charge devices quickly without any noticeable drop in performance. The multiple ports are also a bonus, allowing several devices to be charged at the same time without slowing down the charging speed. This makes it incredibly useful for travel or when multiple gadgets need power. Another great incentive is the included warranty extension card. By registering the product, you can extend the standard one-year warranty by another year, providing extra peace of mind. This is a welcome addition and shows that the manufacturer stands behind the quality of the product. Overall, this power bank has exceeded expectations. Its combination of practicality, build quality, and fast-charging capabilities makes it a fantastic option. The attention to detail, from the flush cables to the easy-to-read display, shows that a lot of thought has gone into the design. It’s a reliable and well-rounded choice for anyone needing a portable charger, and I’d highly recommend it. My Ratings 1 = Lowest 5 = Highest - Packaging: 5 - Ergonomics: 5 - Value for Money: 5 - Ease of Use: 5

review_title: Will not buy any other charger

Everything stays in place, and all three devices charge efficiently and simultaneously. Build quality is top-notch—premium materials, sturdy feel, and a clean modern design. review_title: One of those products that just quietly works
body_en: I bought this charging station for my wife as she is deep in the Apple ecosystem (I'm on the Android side), and she’s been using it for about 6 months now. She's happy with it. The MagSafe thingy holds the iPhone securely in place, even with a case on, and the Qi2 charging is surprisingly fast and reliable. She usually puts her phone on at night, and it’s fully charged by morning without fail. It also charges her Apple Watch and AirPods at the same time. The non-slip base is a nice touch too, though I wish it stuck to the surface a bit more, sometimes it doesn’t keep the whole thing as steady as I’d like. Maybe the whole stand is a bit too lightweight... Just for fun, I tried putting my Samsung Buds on the bottom charger, and it actually worked! So it's not limited to Apple devices, which is a nice bonus. If you’re deep in the Apple ecosystem (or live with someone who is), this is a fantastic addition to your/their setup. Highly recommend it.

So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.

review_title: Perfect for bringing batteries back to life
body_en: Great little charger that’s perfect for maintaining and bringing batteries back to life. It’s compact, easy to use, and works with both 6V and 12V batteries. The smart charging features take the guesswork out and help prevent overcharging, which is a big plus. It’s not the fastest charger since it’s only 1A, but it’s ideal for trickle charging and keeping batteries in good shape. Overall, very reliable and worth it.

Okay, I did NOT expect this little thing to work, but it did and might for you IF you have patience. My Grandfather who was MoAT (Mechanic of All Things) owned back in the day what I thought were REAL chargers, they were so big and heavy they had to be put on wheels and rolled around, they had giant switches that'd illuminate and while I'm probably purely imagining this they were plugged into 220-volt outlets. This thing fits in the palm of my hand, just as pictured, smaller than most mobile phones. "Huh," I said, "this should be comical." I hooked it up and, as others have said, figuring this thing out is NOT straight forward, the instruction manual is weak to say the least, the good news is, as I found, there are many intrepid experimenters who, like me, bought it on a whim and did some trial and error which it'd seem 99% of them got the thing to work to their needs, just like me hence, I'm taking the time to write this review. What this lacks in coherent features or instructions it makes up for it in the end by eventually (boy I mean eventually) getting the job done, for that honestly I'm giving it a generous five stars, because it did what I wanted it do against all odds, just like the Phil Collins song. ("Just take a look at my car now, 'cause it's finally starting here.") To get the to point, this took TWO WEEKS to charge a completely dead battery in a completely dead system. If it'll help anyone I own a 2000 Lexus RX300 that is, in fact, drinking age, if I could find a small ute-friendly bar to have a couple with me of which, in terms of trusty old friends, this boring beige over beige has been one of my best now with over 270,000 miles with no reason, per the Lexus dealer, to give up the ghost before 300,000. Toyota quality and then some with only wearables and maintenance needed BTW, the car has only had one issue, eating car batteries every four or so years. Being a cheap bastard and Lexus parts are pricy I've chosen battery over a slightly-off generator which brings us to the recent hullabaloo and the need to be the Noco Genius, though it'd prove not straightforward as I hoped. Hooking up the Noco Genius you get a slowly blinking light, like a heartbeat, that will tell you nothing really. Also there's a force-charge setting where you hold the button (there's only one button on the whole thing, this thing is basic) it supposedly will force a charge into a battery... this doesn't work, at all. After some digging it supposedly only does this if a battery is below some arbitrary limit which, my battery was completely dead, kaput, nada, force charge only made the 6V light go on which, apparently, is what others experienced. Point being, don't hold you breathe. I kept trying to charge the battery but it didn't budge, didn't budge, didn't budge, then I had a thought and said to myself "self, what if I unhook the battery, THEN charge it?" As in, is it because it's also hooked to my car hence current is going other places? Mind you, this thing is only one (1) amp, that's very little, if you're looking for a quick charger or something to charge and jump your car, this ain't it, have you seen the size of this thing? Ha no, no, but it will trickle, very slowly, a charge into your battery... if it's not hooked to the car. Listen, some people this may work when the battery is not hooked up and, in fact, I hooked my battery back up AFTER this thing actually worked and then hooked up the Noco to it and it did, in fact, go from red blinking to green, sooo, yeah, that happened. But I'm burying the lede here: The Noco charger worked for me but ONLY after it was hooked to the battery without being connected to the car. Total time to charge the battery not hooked to the car? About 36 hours. Great? Eh, there's a pandemic, I'm not really going out much so had time on my hands, not to mention my wife's car. In summation, IF you have even a completely dead battery or run down battery and IF you don't have to go anywhere in the next two days and IF you're comfortable unhooking the leads from your car to your battery so that it'll only be charging the battery itself this Noco Genius is, er, uh, genius! It really works! It works and for the cheap cheap cheap money its worth every penny. If this thing cost even 50% more I'd be taking down stars but this thing cost less than a steak dinner (back when I ate steak) so suffice to say it got my battery charged all the way up, hooked up to my car and after the computer was all "what the... ??? Was I in a coma" my car fired right up and ran, I even drove it around a bit. This would be a good thing to own for just-in-case as its just in case money. If you have any situation close to mine, get this trickle charger, if you need the big guns, well, open up your wallet and say ah. Luckily most of us, probably 99% of us, if your battery is run down, this will do the trick. Best of luck!

I have two of these. They are not exactly the same model (I think one of them is an older version of this model). The older one, I have had in the garage for several years to keep the batteries in the cars up when they are not driven very often. Some people say these are not for car batteries and I won't argue with them but the one I have out there definitely keeps the battery in my 2001 Corolla charged. And in fact, we had an incident where someone left a dome light on in that car and drained the battery to the point to where there was absolutely no response from anything electrical in the car. We started the car with a jumper pack, pulled it in the garage and connected it to the Noco and let it do it's thing. That's been at least a year and that battery is still going strong in that car. I purchased this one off Amazon to use on various SLA batteries I have around. I have two jumper packs with 18 AH SLA batteries in them. One of them had been sitting in the garage for several years due to the fact last time I tried to charge it, it wouldn't charge. I was going to order a new battery for it from Amazon but I figured I kind of needed an extra charger for SLA batteries anyway and this Noco unit was less than the price of a new battery for the old jumper pack. I figured it would be a long shot to try and charge that old battery and get any more life out of it but I thought it would be interesting to see what would happen. Can't be a tougher challenge for a SLA battery that's been sitting in a garage dead for years. Well, that jumper pack doesn't exactly have easy access to the battery but after some fighting with it, I got it open and popped the clamps on the terminals. The charging light began to pulse and after about a day, went green (was still pulsing but was pulsing green). It finally went solid green. I left it plugged in a few days. I have one of those miniature inverters that plugs into a cigarette lighter (that particular jumper pack doesn't have a built-in inverter but does have a cigarette lighter plug). So I plugged it in and tested it with a clamp light. So far, seems to be working about as well as you'd expect for a jumper pack battery that is probably approaching ten years old now. Or maybe better than you'd expect. It's only a 12 watt LED in the clamp light but my main goal was to get every last bit of value from any SLA batteries that I can. I'd definitely have a use for a small inverter like that in a power outage and if you have an extra battery that you can plug it into, so much the better. I believe the built-in charger on that jumper pack just may have died or was not up to charging it's battery for whatever reason. Remains to be seen how much more life I can get out of such batteries but it's definitely worth the price paid.

review_title: Reliable. Battery was ready when needed
body_en: In January 2026, the temperature dropped to -25°, without wind-chill, over 3 days. The electricity went out. I needed to start my emergency generator, and the battery was dead. I start the generator every month and run it for 1 hour to maintain the battery. This battery was only 7 months old. I was lucky. I had a battery for the sump pump in case of emergency, and I was able to use it. Here it is the end of August 2026, and we've been experiencing thunderstorms daily. Last night the electricity went out. I've had the battery on the NOCO Genius 1 since January. I installed it and the generator started right up. The battery has been on the charger for 7 months, so if there was a problem with the charger, I'd know by now. The charger is reliable and it protects the battery. Choose the right one by amperage of your battery.

no, the value for money for this product is excellent along with its usefulness and functionality. The cable length is perfect and is versatile on all my different batteries. It ensures that when I look at it, the light is on I know it’s charging and when I disconnect and start my vehicles up or install the battery into one of the vehicles it works peace of mind it’s worth the price. The value for the money is way better than buying a new battery I have four of them and they’re all hooked up to cars and farm equipment. Definitely will not stop using this type of product. Highly recommend if you want to save money get this and not worry about your batteries.

review_title: Works with a REALLY low battery
body_en: My wife has a 1995 Mercedes SL320 that she did not drive all winter and well into the new year... when she opened the garage door and tried to start it the battery was dead, drained by MANY months of the old style mechanical clock running without the car being started so the battery could charge My (brand name withheld) several year old 10 amp 'smart' charger would not work because the battery was too low to be detected So, I looked for a different charger with a FORCE mode to get a dead battery to start charging... I connected this one at about 7PM at night (it never would go into force mode, since the battery had 'just enough' charge to be detected) and when I get in the car at 7AM the next morning the battery had enough of a charge for the dash lights to come on, but not enough to run the starter The PDF I downloaded shows that this 1 amp charger will take 'about' 23 hours to charge a 30 AH battery... the battery in her SL320 is a 100 AH model, so I will let the charger run for another full day before I try to start the car again (or maybe 2 days to get the charger enough time to work) So far, this charger is doing exactly what I need (I thought about a larger model to charge quicker, but decided that slow charging was good enough... she hasn't driven her car since last Fall, so she can now wait a day or two)

review_title: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions
body_en: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions I bought this because my car battery had gone dead after the car had been sitting for a while. I wanted something I could connect and leave charging rather than just jump-starting the battery again. So far, I’ve been impressed with how simple it is to use. I connected it to the battery, selected the appropriate mode, and it began charging without any fuss. The indicators make it easy to see what it’s doing, and at the moment it seems to be working exactly as intended. My one criticism is that there is no conventional instruction manual included. Instead, you scan a QR code and go online for the instructions. That worked fine for me, but I don’t think it’s a particularly good choice for a product like this. Not everyone has a smartphone readily available, and battery chargers may be used in garages or emergency situations where having basic printed instructions in the box would be useful. Other than that, my first experience with it has been very positive. It’s compact, straightforward to connect, and remarkably easy to operate.

I do recommend this product because it fulfills its function, which is to charge small level batteries, for motorcycle batteries it is ideal and it takes care of the charging cycle, so you can connect your batteries with complete confidence and the maintenance mode seems like a great feature to me.

The charger is also compact and easy to use, making it convenient for my desk, nightstand, or while traveling. Overall, this is a great wireless charger for the iPhone 15 Pro Max. It’s simple, convenient, and works as expected. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for an easy-to-use magnetic wireless charging option.

review_title: Works perfectly, just a nerrow range of uses
body_en: First, this charger is fantastic at charging fast. I have had no problems with charging any phone fully in half the time my old wireless charger took. The caveats: The charger has two states. It is either fast charging, or it is off. It will not work at all in a car because it doesn't supply enough amps. It won't work with wall plugs under 25 watts (5v, 5A). It doesn't just refuse to fast charge, it won't even power up. So this only works if you have a high-amperage adapter, or a high power computer port. The other issue is weight. The device is small and surprisingly light, but that means if you pick up your charging phone, the charger comes with it. Great in a car, but it won't work there. Terrible on a nightstand or desk. I'm constantly prying off the charger just so I can use the phone. So great in any situation where the above two issues don't matter.

I highly recommend these chargers for anyone with an iPhone 12 or later who's charging port has become useless. With this two pack I glued one to the wall in my apartment, the other is attached to a vent clip in the car. The mag safe feature allows me to slap my phone on the wall or vent and the phone is secure (even works through my off brand silicone case). I haven't had a single failed charge since switching to wireless charging. So simple but still life changing

I ordered this wireless charger because my charging port stopped working. I didn't expect much from wireless charging, but l was wrong. My phone was charged very fast. I have since had my charging port fixed, but l still prefer the wireless charging pad. I bought the 2-pack and have one on my nightstand and one on my desk at my office. It worked well with my Samsung Galaxy 24.

review_title: No more fluff in the port excuses
body_en: I’ve always found charging my phone overnight a bit annoying – constantly trying to get the cable in the right position, and still waking up with a low battery more often than I should. This MagSafe-style charger has completely removed that hassle. Now it’s just a case of placing the phone down and letting it attach magnetically, which feels a lot more reliable than fiddling with cables in the dark. Since using it, I’ve stopped waking up to a nearly dead phone, which is exactly what I wanted from it. It comes as a simple package with the charger itself, a USB-C cable and a USB-A converter, so you’ve got a bit of flexibility depending on what plug or setup you’re using. The magnetic alignment is strong enough that the phone stays in place easily, even if you move it slightly on the bedside table. What stands out with this set is having two chargers. It makes it easy to keep one at the bedside and the other in another room or take it for travel, so you’re not constantly unplugging and moving things around. It also supports faster wireless charging, so it doesn’t feel slow compared to wired charging overnight, especially when paired with the right adapter. It’s more than enough for overnight use and day-to-day top ups. Case compatibility is decent too. It works through most standard slim cases without issue, but for the best magnetic hold you’ll want a MagSafe-compatible case or one with built-in magnets. Thicker cases do weaken the snap-in feel a bit. Price wise seems to be normal for the price of 2. Overall, it’s a small change that makes a big difference in day-to-day use. No more cable faff, no more guessing angles – just put it down and it charges. Exactly the kind of simple upgrade that makes life easier.

review_title: Carga rápida, tamaño mínimo y magnífico precio. Totalmente recomendado
body_en: Si estás buscando jubilar los dichosos cables de una vez por todas y te llama la atención el nuevo estándar de carga inalámbrica Qi2 y tienes dispositivos que aceptan la carga inalámbrica, quédate por aquí porque te voy a contar detalladamente mi experiencia real con este pack de 2 cargadores magnéticos. Después de estar trasteando con ellos a diario, usándolos tanto en el escritorio de casa como llevándomelos de viaje, aquí te dejo mi análisis a fondo, sin rodeos, con lo bueno, lo genial y también con esos pequeños detalles que conviene saber antes de lanzarse a por ellos. 📦 ¿Qué nos encontramos en la caja? De primeras, lo mejor de este producto es que es un pack doble. Te vienen dos bases de carga inalámbrica magnética de color violeta oscuro (tampoco es demasiado oscuro). Visualmente llaman la atención ya que tienen un perfil ultra delgado (apenas unos 5 milímetros de grosor) y pesan poquísimo (unos 54 gramos). El chasis es metálico, lo que le da un toque premium muy limpio, y el cable viene integrado con conector USB-C y un acabado trenzado que se nota bastante resistente al trote diario (dobleces, tirones en la mochila, etc.). ⚠️ Un detalle crucial de inicio: El pack no incluye los adaptadores de pared (los enchufes). En la caja solo vienen las dos bases con sus cables. ⚡ Rendimiento y Velocidad: ¿De verdad carga a 25W? Aquí hay que ponerse un poco técnicos, pero de forma sencilla. Estos cargadores cuentan con la nueva certificación Qi2 / Qi2.2, que es básicamente la evolución universal del sistema MagSafe de Apple. Promete hasta 25W de potencia máxima. En el día a día, con los teléfonos compatibles más recientes, la velocidad se nota un montón. En apenas 30 minutos te puede plantar la batería en torno al 50%, siendo notablemente más rápido que las típicas bases inalámbricas antiguas de 15W. Pero ojo, que aquí viene el "truco" de la potencia: 1. El enchufe importa: Para exprimir esos 25W de punta, necesitas conectar la base a un adaptador de pared de 30W o superior con salida de 12V (el típico cargador rápido potente que uses para la tablet o el portátil). Si lo conectas a un enchufe antiguo de menos de 20W, la velocidad caerá en picado. 2. Carga desde el portátil: Si eres de los que, como yo, viaja mucho y conecta la base directamente al puerto USB-C de tu ordenador portátil en una reunión o cafetería, la potencia real se verá limitada por la del ordenador (suele dar entre 10W y 15W). Sigue siendo comodísimo para mantener el móvil con energía mientras trabajas, pero no irá a su velocidad punta. 🧲 El imán y el ajuste magnético: El cargador lleva internamente imanes de neodimio N52. En dispositivos de la manzana o teléfonos preparados nativamente para alineación magnética, la experiencia es súper cómoda: acercas el teléfono por la parte trasera, se "pega" solo en la posición exacta milimétrica y empieza a cargar. Es ideal para la mesita de noche porque no tienes que andar tanteando a oscuras a ver si ha encajado en la bobina. Dado que es mucho más pequeño (aproximadamente la mitad) que las bases de carga inalámbrica, si tu dispositivo no tiene la alineación magnética has de asegurarte que realmente está bien colocado, ya que además no tiene ningún led que indique que está cargando, sólo puedes saberlo por lo que te indica tu dispositivo. A tener muy en cuenta con Android y fundas: • Si usas dispositivos como los últimos Samsung Galaxy o Google Pixel, o incluso si llevas el iPhone con una funda convencional, necesitas obligatoriamente que la funda sea compatible con MagSafe/Qi2 (las que llevan el anillo magnético integrado). • Si intentas usarlo con una funda de plástico normal o de piel gruesa sin imanes, el agarre se debilita muchísimo y el teléfono se soltará con cualquier movimiento. En algunos terminales Android sin funda o con carcasas inadecuadas, el imán puede sentirse algo flojo, así que el secreto para que no se mueva nada es una buena funda magnética. 🥶 Gestión de temperatura y seguridad. Al ser tan sumamente compacto y delgado, la disipación del calor es puramente pasiva a través de su carcasa metálica. Durante las cargas rápidas intensas, vas a notar que el cargador y la trasera del teléfono se calientan bastante. Es un comportamiento normal en la carga inalámbrica de alta potencia, aunque en ciertos modelos de teléfonos más pequeños o compactos (como ediciones SE o similares) esa sensación de calor puede ser un poco más acusada de lo esperado. Por suerte, incluye chip inteligente con protección contra sobrecalentamiento y detección de objetos extraños, por lo que corta el flujo si detecta anomalías. 🔍 Lo que se echa en falta (puntos a mejorar) Para ser totalmente honestos, hay un par de detalles de diseño que podrían haber redondeado el producto: • Sin indicador LED: El disco no tiene ninguna lucecita que te confirme visualmente que está pasando energía. Tienes que fiarte del pantallazo o la vibración de tu propio móvil al colocarlo. • Tamaño reducido: Como el disco es tan minimalista y delgado si no usas una funda que guíe el imán de forma automática, al principio te puede costar un par de intentos centrarlo perfectamente sobre la zona de carga trasera a la primera. ⭐ Conclusión: ¿Vale la pena? Rotundamente sí, sobre todo por la versatilidad del pack de dos unidades. Por el magnífico precio que tiene, es ideal para dejar uno fijo en tu zona de trabajo habitual (el escritorio de casa o la oficina) y meter el otro directamente en la mochila o el neceser de viaje. El color violeta oscuro es super original y elegante, rompiendo con el aburrido monopolio de las bases habituales de siempre. Si tienes claro que necesitas un adaptador potente en casa para sacarle los 25W y usas fundas magnéticas adecuadas (o tu dispositivo tiene alineación magnética), este kit te va a dar una comodidad muy importante en tu rutina diaria, ahorrándote el engorro de andar buscando y rompiendo cables físicos a cada momento. Una compra de lo más práctica y recomendada.

review_title: Great if your charge port has commitment issues
body_en: I use this with my iPhone 8 because sometimes the charge port is finicky so I have to use wireless charging, and I gave the second one in the 2 pack to my cousin who has an iPhone 14 Pro Max. The magnet connection is strong, it snaps on tight and doesn't shift. The slim design is great for when it's stuck to the back of your phone and you're using it so it's not bulky in your hand. For my iPhone 8, there's no magnets in the phone, so it doesn't attach, but it works fine as a normal Qi pad if I centre it and it doesn't make my phone hot. It charges my phone at 7.5W. That's an iPhone 8 limit, not the charger's fault. My cousin's 14 Pro Max gets 15W, since 25W Qi2.2 only works on iPhone 15 and newer. No wall adapters are included so you need a 25W+ USB-C PD brick to get fast charging on phones that support it. With my iPhone 8, a basic 10W brick is enough. If you use a weak adapter with a newer phone, charging will be slow. For the price of a 2 pack, it's good if you need a backup for port issues or want Qi2.2 speeds on a newer phone. The strong magnet is great for MagSafe phones, and it still functions as a standard wireless charger for older models.

Set of two magnetic chargers in lemon yellow color. At my house, we all have iPhones: 12, 14, 17, and these cats fit all our phones perfectly. They replace old basic chargers with less efficient cables and prematurely wear out the phone's charging socket. This helps extend the life of our old iPhones which are no longer able to charge with the cable. Charging is fast and efficient. The magnet is super effective. And the charger remains discreet, plus I love the color!!!! I recommend ++++
Love this charge station it’s a must for the Iwalk charger love it so convenient also has extra usb to charge extra stuff at same time ! Very convenient great price too
Great phone chargers

review_title: Love this for multiple iWalk chargers!
body_en: At first, I wasn't sure if this was ultimately worth it, but after acquiring 3 iWalk chargers (we use them a lot during travel and also out and about while our kids run our phone batteries into the ground), I finally decided it would be easier to just have a dock than managing all the individual charging cords. My only regret is not purchasing it sooner. This dock is absolutely not just a useless gimmick - it makes packing iWalk chargers and charging them during travel exceptionally easy, and is also super convenient for home. It charges the devices quickly and efficiently, frees up outlets, and, honestly, just looks nice. If you have more than one iWalk, I'd definitely recommend the charging dock.

It was great for a few months then stopped charging. It still lights up and turns on like it's working but will no longer charge any of the battery packs!  This has become an expensive battery holder and no longer a battery charger. I have to charge them individually with the charging cable which totally defeats the purpose of this purchase. Company only honors warranty if purchased from website. I would stay away from this piece of junk. This is one time I should have listened to the bad reviews!  Overpriced typical "Made in China"  money grab.
Love my iWALK charger station

review_title: Works for i walk o ly
body_en: This charger is great but will only work for the i walk battery.
I love that you can dock multiple of these. It charges quick. If I were to change anything I wish it would size better when charging. The item falls off pretty easy.

I buy a lot of portable chargers and this is awesome to keep them charged. The color is nice and comfortably fits the iwalk portable chargers. It doesn’t fit other brands of chargers though but that’s ok. I haven’g had any issues with durability as it usually stays on my dresser.

This Anker 20W USB-C charger set is exactly what I needed. It charges my iPhone quickly and efficiently, and the compact design makes it easy to carry when traveling. The included USB-C cables are durable and work perfectly right out of the box. I also appreciate getting two chargers in one pack, making it convenient to keep one at home and one at work. Anker's quality is outstanding, and everything feels well-built and reliable. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a dependable fast charger at a great price!

I've had these cables and power bricks for about 2 years now, every since I upgraded from an iPhone XS to the S24 Ultra, and I haven't had any issues! The length is great when I'm lying in bed or sitting on the couch and want to use my phone while it's charging. Having a USB A and USB C connector is handy too if I need to dual charge I try to buy Anker products whenever I can. I'm always impressed with the quality of everything I've used by them I know that you could spend less for similar products but you really are paying for quality! The fast charging works great when I need a little bit of extra charge on phone Don't hesitate to buy this, it's worth every penny!

I’ve bought these chargers for our iPhones and my kids Amazon kids tablet several times. They work well and charge fast. Plus I like the cute green and purple colors. They work with every case that I’ve tried and they don’t wear out easily like some other top brands. These are a must have imo. They’re very affordable too.

Great charger with reliable fast charging! The Anker 20W USB-C Charger Block works great, is compact, and delivers the performance you expect from a trusted brand. One important tip: make sure you are using a fast-charging compatible cable as well, because the charger can only perform as well as the cable allows. Pair it with the right cable and it’s an excellent charging solution.
The block is compact, with two ports so two items can be charged simultaneously. The 5 foot cord is very convenient.

review_title: Worked well for 18 months, then died
body_en: Used it daily with an anker magsafe charger for my iPhone 13. It worked well for 18 months, now it seems to have gone bad. I don't know if that's a decent life span for this or not, but I'm a tad disappointed.

I have purchased this 2-pack probably 3 times now. They work! Fast charging, long and durable cable, thin wall block (helps not to take up 2 plugs with one block), and now the cool colors to choose from.

Huge fan of Anker products across the board. I’ve been using their Mac dongles and external batteries for years without any issues, so buying this 2-pack charger set was a no-brainer. They perform great, fast-charge reliably, and customer support is top-tier if you ever need anything. Easily my favorite tech accessory brand!
The charger is very good, it fulfills its function with quality.

review_title: With both USB-A and USB-C, it’s like the Swiss Army knife of wall plugs.
body_en: Purchased for $19.95 in November 2025. This is my third time ordering this charger set—partly because they’re great, and partly because the kids keep “borrowing” them. Anker has always been a dependable brand in our house, and this set just reinforces that. Each charger has both a USB-C and a USB-A port, which comes in handy when you need to top off two devices at once. The included USB-C cables are solid quality. They’re not the most flexible, but based on my past experience, they hold up really well over time and don’t fray or loosen at the connectors like cheaper ones tend to. Charging speeds are excellent—fast, consistent, and reliable. After a long charging session, the brick gets a little warm, but that’s expected with higher-wattage chargers. It’s never hot enough to worry about, just something you notice if you touch it. Overall, these have become my go-to chargers for phones, tablets, and just about anything else. Anker continues to be a brand I trust and look for whenever I need reliable charging gear. TLDR Reliable, fast, and durable. Dual ports are convenient, and the included cables last a long time. Gets slightly warm during use, but nothing concerning. Great value and performance from a trusted brand.
The chargers worked very well, I gave one to my mother, and I use the other, a Samsung and iPhone and they both charge super fast, one of the best chargers in my opinion

review_title: Bought a second set because they're great
body_en: I actually bought this Anker Charger 2-Pack on sale for the second time because my first set held up so well. Why I like this bundle: => Better cables: It comes with two USB-C cables, and they are 5 feet long. Most cheap chargers only give you a tiny 3-foot cord, so the extra length is a huge plus. => Dual ports: Each block has both a USB-C and an older USB-A port. I can use the new fast cables but still plug in my older tech without needing new bricks. => Speed: The 20W charging is noticeably faster than the old standard cubes. No real complaints at all. Anker makes reliable gear, and getting two blocks plus two long cords on sale is a killer value. Highly recommend it.
Muito bom

I've gone through more charging stations than I'd like to admit, and most either take up too much room or require a tangle of cables. This one keeps everything much cleaner by charging my phone, Apple Watch, and earbuds in one compact unit. What impressed me most is how portable it is. When folded, it's small enough to slip into a backpack or carry-on, making it a great travel companion. I especially like that the charging cable retracts into the base instead of becoming another cord to wrap up before packing. The magnetic phone charger holds my phone securely, even in StandBy mode, so I can use it as a bedside clock while it charges overnight. My watch and earbuds also charged consistently without having to fiddle with positioning them over and over. The built-in lighting is a nice extra. I normally don't care for RGB effects, but it's easy to switch off if you prefer a darker bedroom. It's nice to have the option instead of being stuck with lights that stay on all night. The only drawback I found is that the built-in power cable isn't very long. If your outlet is tucked behind furniture or far from your nightstand, you may need to rearrange where you place the charger. A slightly longer cable would have made it even more versatile. Overall, this is a well-designed charging station that reduces clutter and travels well. It feels sturdy, charges reliably, and combines several useful features into one compact package. I'd recommend it to anyone looking to simplify their desk or bedside setup.

review_title: One of the Best Charging Stations I've Used
body_en: This charging station has been fantastic. I love that it supports my phone, AirPods, and other USB-C devices all in one place. The retractable cable keeps everything neat, and the RGB lighting can be turned off with a simple touch if you prefer a cleaner look. The rubberized base keeps it stable, and everything feels well built. My only minor observation is that AirPods with thicker protective cases can be a tighter fit on the charging pad, but it hasn't changed how much I like the product. Overall, it's become my primary charging station.

review_title: Great Angle Adjustment, and turns my phone into a clock
body_en: The adjustable angle on this charging station is what really sold me. Once your phone is set on it, you can tilt it just right so the display is easy to see, and I've actually started using it as a nightstand clock. When I wake up in the middle of the night, the motion wakes the phone display and shows me the time without me having to pick it up or fumble around. That angle adjustment is mainly what I use it for, though I can also see it being handy for propping up your phone to watch something while it charges. The flip up piece for the watch works great too. My older Apple Watch 6 fits on it fine and charges reliably every time. I've also used the front part to charge my AirPods, and that works well even with a small silicone case on them. Charging speed is right in line with other wireless chargers I've used, nothing faster or slower than expected. It folds down into a small cube that's easy to toss in a suitcase, so you have one single charger covering all your devices when you travel. Overall this is a great value since you're getting three charging stations in one, and I'm already thinking about picking up a few of these as gifts for some of the older kids later this year.

review_title: Great charging station, just a bit too scrunched
body_en: I love charging stations! The only issue I see with this one is it is very compact - like one bump could send my watch and headphones off the charger. The magnet for the phone charging part is great. The watch charger part is a little awkward because it doesn’t allot much space for your wristband/the extra space needed for where your wristband fits in the slots on your watch face. Once you’ve secured your watch properly on it, it charges just fine. I have 1st or 2nd gen Airpods so I was surprised to see it could charge them too! There is a light at the bottom of the charger - which you can turn off or turn into “nightlight” mode. There are specific colors for charging the different devices, and the manuel explains what this would look like if it is charging properly - I haven’t noticed the lights to work 100% accurately but my devices still charged especially when I had more than one device charging at a time.

review_title: Awesome charger for home and travel!
body_en: I’m really happy with this ANTBOOK 3 in 1 wireless charging station. It’s nice to have one spot to charge my phone, Apple Watch, and anirpods instead of dealing with multiple chargers and charging bases. The built in retractable cord is one of my favorite features. It keeps my nightstand looking clean and is easy to use. My cats like to chew on cords that lay around, so I only have the cord retracted just enough so that my cats can’t chew on it and it’s still usable. The RGB lighting is a fun touch without being over the top, and it gives my nightstand a nice modern look. I especially like that I can turn the RGB off at night when I’m sleeping if I feel it’s keeping me awake. The charging station itself feels compact and doesn’t take up much space on my nightstand. Charging has been reliable, and I haven’t had any issues keeping all three devices powered up overnight. I could really see this charger shining when it comes to traveling. One cord, one block, 3 different items it charges. Overall, it’s a convenient, clutter free charging solution that works well and looks good. I’d definitely recommend it.

review_title: Convenient stand for cable clutter but runs hot
body_en: This charging stand is decent for cleaning up messy nightstand cables and consolidating your phone, watch, and earbuds into one compact spot. The magnetic hold is strong enough to keep the phone securely upright in portrait or landscape orientation, and the weighted base keeps it from sliding around when you grab your device. However, the unit gets noticeably hot when charging multiple devices at the same time. While it does power everything up reliably, the excess heat build up is definitely a drawback if you are concerned about long term battery health. It is a convenient organizer, but the thermal management leaves something to be desired.

We have different iPhones in the house, from a 12 mini to a 15 Pro, and all of them snap onto the magnetic pad without issue. My wife's older Watch Series 3 also charges fine. Good to know we won't need a new station when someone upgrades.

This 3 in 1 charging station is seriously the perfect charger for travel. It folds down into a compact cube that can easily be packed or thrown into a purse. Even the type C cable folds into the back to keep from getting tangled. The light is easily turned off and on and doubles as a nice little night light. The hinges are stiff enough to hold the parts in place without falling closed. I love that it comes with the charging block. It seems like so many things these days just come with the cord but not the block. Unfortunately I couldn’t exactly get a picture of my phone charging but it does charge really fast and the magnet holds onto my phone well. Overall, I am super impressed with this little gadget. It’s so convenient and packs every charging necessity into a great compact size. I would definitely recommend it!

review_title: Decent bedside multi-device charging station for home or travel. Light is a bit bright/distracting.
body_en: The ANTBOOK Model Z1 charging station is a great space-saver that consolidates multiple cords and chargers into a single, compact unit for your tabletop or nightstand. While its built-in retractable USB-C cable makes it highly convenient for travel, it could be a bit short, extending only to a maximum of 25". The included 33W PD power adapter performs reliably. Thanks to a rubberized base and most of its 285g weight concentrated at the bottom, the station remains highly stable and stays firmly in place, though I do wish the magnet was a bit stronger to offer a more secure hold on my iPhone 11 (with MagSafe case; should be very adequate for iPhone 12 and up due to integrated magnets). The capacitive switch on the front, which allows you to turn on/off the light, is also not very responsive (at least on the unit I received), which can be frustrating (see my video). The USB-C output port on the back is a handy extra for charging a watch with its own attachment or another accessory, though it's noteworthy that the output is fixed at 5V and does not support 9V or 12V fast charging. For storage and transport, the station folds down into a cube. While it is not the most compact travel charger on the market, it is still very manageable. It supports MagSafe-compatible phones in both portrait and landscape orientations. It also features a built-in light, activated by a touch-sensitive toggle, which can serve as a nightlight or a charging status indicator -- showing an animated RGB effect when idle and a pulsating solid color while your phone is actively charging (strobing green while charging AirPods, blue while charging iPhone, or alternating between green and blue when both are charging). Unfortunately, the brightness is not adjustable, and I found the light to be too bright/distracting for a dark bedroom, though it does thankfully turn off automatically once your phone reaches a full charge, or you can just turn the light off altogether, as I've done. A slightly annoying quirk is that it goes back to the animated RGB effect in the event of a power failure, but maybe that's a helpful behaviour. Overall, the station functions as expected, simultaneously charging an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods wirelessly. While I am not certain it delivers true "fast" charging, it is more than adequate for overnight use. During my testing with an iPhone 11, AirPods Pro, and Apple Watch all charging at the same time, I noticed a current draw of barely 1A at 9V, which does seem a bit low, but it still gets the job done by morning.

review_title: Convenient travel charger with a clever cord, but has a few quirks
body_en: I grabbed this three-in-one charging station hoping to clear up the wire clutter on my nightstand and have an easier time packing for trips. It definitely succeeds at saving space, reliably charging my phone, watch, and earbuds all at the same time. The foldable design is incredibly compact, and the built-in retractable power cable is a fantastic idea that means I never have to remember to pack an extra cord. It even comes with the wall adapter, which is a great touch. That said, the execution isn't entirely flawless. The retractable cable can be a bit stubborn and occasionally needs some wiggling to wind all the way back up into the base. It also features a built-in light that defaults to a bright rainbow effect. While you can thankfully turn it off, the touch button can be a little unresponsive, and the light itself is just too bright to use as a bedside nightlight since you can't dim it. It also won't give you the absolute fastest charging speeds on the market, but for an overnight charge, it does the job perfectly fine. Despite the minor flaws, it is still a really handy, portable way to keep everything powered up without dealing with a tangled mess of wires.

review_title: Compact 3-in-1 charger with a built-in nightlight
body_en: This 3-in-1 wireless charging station can charge an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all at once, and folds down to a compact size that works well on a nightstand or for travel. It also has a 10W USB-C output port on the back which is useful for charging devices that do not support wireless charging. Phones can be charged at up to 15W, earbuds up to 5W, and watches up to 3W. There's a light built into the bottom of the unit that is operated with a touch button on the front. It can be changed from a night light mode to wireless charging indicator mode (blue for phone charging and green for earbud charging), when nothing is charging the light cycles between the colours. The USB-C cable is built into the unit and retracts when not in use, so there's no worry about forgetting to bring the cable. A 30W AC adapter is also included. The base has a non-slip finish to keep it from sliding around. The phone magnetic strength works okay with my phone case and holds it in place. A practical all-in-one charging station that charges up to four devices at the same time and I like the built-in retractable charging cable. I've used it on my nightstand and it helps keep it very tidy. It will also be great to travel with instead of having to take a number of cables and adapters.

I really like this charging station! The built-in retractable cord is my favourite feature because it keeps everything neat and eliminates the need to carry an extra cable. The additional USB-C port is also a great bonus for charging another device when needed. The compact size makes it perfect for travel, work, or keeping on a bedside table without taking up much space. Being able to charge multiple Apple devices in one spot is very convenient and helps reduce clutter. The different coloured RGB lights are such a fun touch. They add a little personality to the charger, and I like that the lighting can be adjusted depending on your preference. Overall, this is a practical and stylish charging solution that is great for anyone who wants a portable, organized way to charge their devices. I would definitely recommend it.

review_title: A Versatile, Compact Charger With Great Feature Set
body_en: I’ve been using this for a little while now and it’s been a solid upgrade from the pile of chargers I used to have on my nightstand. The main reason I got it was to charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time without dealing with three separate cables. It does that without any issues. I’ve tried it with an iPhone 15 and an older 13, a Series 9 Watch, and AirPods Pro, and everything sits properly and charges consistently. Nothing super fast, but reliable enough for overnight or desk use. The retractable cable is one of the better features. review_title: Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often
body_en: I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time. As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The other button I believe is for what kind of charge you want(trickle, decharge, repair) but since I have a brand new battery I simply keep it on trickle charge. The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. I keep a smoke detector next to the NOCO and battery just to be safe. I got the NOCO on sale during Prime Day so it is definitely a good value for the money. So far so good.

Luckily, able to look on line and find plenty of videos, however, this does not negate the need for an instruction and care pamphlet. The unit feels solidly built and works as expected. While it did not resurrect my battery as it claims it can do (not in all situations), mine was 5 years old, lead acid and probably just to far gone for help. However, it is doing a great job charging my marine battery and using it to keep it charged until used again. I like it. Much more compact than the older styles and easily able to mount to a wall or post as a charging station. I would definitely buy again.

review_title: Pretty neat device, very capable as well

Was ready to pull the trigger and decided to see if something better was out there, thus buying a Genius 10 instead based on YouTube reviews. The build quality is really good in my eyes, looks like tough ABS polymer, very nice cords with that good feeling wire jacket insulation. The new clamps are nice looking and very practical to me. It's heavy and awkward to store, so I bought the Noco case as well; I thought the other case was too small in size. I ran some test with it, on a 12V Honda Lead Acid and Group H8 AGM battery and was happy the results. It was more intuitive than the 1970s version I have with 30 amp boost that is scary to use. What I like with Noco or Genius, it's several tools in one unit, so every 3 or 4 months, I can use the Genius to check the status of all my batteries, well that is the plan at least. One neat thing, using the 12V output to keep a battery online while changing a battery, so the cars computer keeps running and doesn't reboot from removing the battery causing weird things to happen. I have no regrets in my purchase and bought the case to enhance it more. I think the price is reasonable as well considering what a $100 buys today.

review_title: Saved me from buying a new battery!
body_en: EDIT 2/26/24: I am now the blocks "AAA". Been helping people start their cars when jump starts with cables have not worked. Definitely handy to get other people out of an otherwise expensive pinch. I have a car battery that I purchased around 2016 (date of review 1/3/24). The car itself does not get driven much, at most 2-3 times a week no longer than 15 minutes one way. Throughout the years I've drained it by leaving the car lights on. Its always required a jump start after that to get going again. Recently I've been an idiot and been leaving my lights on more frequently. Eventually it required me to jump start everytime I wanted to turn on the car. It was becoming a hassle and I was about to call it quits and purchase a new battery until I came across Project Farm's review on battery chargers. This was at the top of the list so I figured to give it a shot. I was not disappointed! I charged it for 4 days straight, put it in my car, and it started right up. Not surprised considering it was just charged but the real test laid ahead. I was going to be out of town for two weeks and leave the car sitting. I came back two weeks later and the car started up, no hesitation whatsoever, as if it was a different battery! The NOCO Genius 10 saved me about $150-200 at least in a brand new battery. On top of that, I can now use it for other batteries in the event of any similar issues. The instructions on the other hand are a bit confusing and had to rely on YouTube comments to piece it together. For those who are confused at what to do, I did not do a 12V repair (function which this unit has) as it requires the battery to be completely charged first. All I did was charge it straight for 4 days uninterrupted. When first put on battery to the charger it will be in standby mode. You push (or hold depending on what you need) the MODE button to select your desired option. I was charging a lead acid battery so I selected 12V. The meter at the top slowly advanceD from each of the four bars until the final bar was pulsing green which indicates its charging to full (over 80% I believe). The green charging light continued to slowly pulse even on the 4th day but I took a gamble and disconnected it from the battery. For the battery to be 100% charged, the green light should stay solid. That means my battery worked 2 weeks later after sitting and it wasn't even at 100%. The unit can also force a charge on batteries that are extremely under voltage. Thats a separate setting that I haven't had to use yet. It can also charge AGM and Lithium but I believe the 12V repair function is only for lead acid. Unfortunately I had to go through 3 separate orders because the first two were from Amazon Warehouse and I encountered issues with both, consecutively. I ended up getting frustrated and just purchased a brand new charger. Pros: Solid build quality Excellent cable connections with weather covers Compatible with a wide variety of batteries Repair and Force charge batteries Cons: Poor instructions Charge is slow BUT I think thats how these chargers work TL;DR Try this first before rushing to get a new battery it is a good investment that can save you a lot of money

review_title: Reliable Smart Charger That Brought a Neglected Battery Back to Life
body_en: I purchased the NOCO GENIUS5 to maintain the batteries in vehicles that don't get driven regularly, and it has been one of those tools that quickly proves its value. Setup was straightforward. The included connectors are easy to use, and the charger automatically detects the battery and selects the appropriate charging mode. I especially appreciate that it can be left connected for maintenance without worrying about overcharging, which gives me peace of mind when storing a vehicle for extended periods. One of the batteries I used it on had been sitting for quite a while and was struggling to hold a charge. After connecting the GENIUS5 and allowing it to complete its charging cycle, the battery recovered enough to reliably start the vehicle again. While no charger can fix a battery that's physically damaged or completely worn out, this unit did a good job recovering a battery that I initially thought might need replacement. The charger itself feels well-built and the display indicators are easy to understand. I also like that it supports both lead-acid and lithium batteries, making it useful for multiple vehicles and equipment around the house. A few things prospective buyers should know: The 5A charging rate is ideal for maintenance and general charging, but it isn't the fastest option if you're trying to charge a large, deeply discharged battery in a hurry. The indicator lights are simple and functional, though some users may prefer a charger with a more detailed digital display showing voltage and charging status. Overall, this is a dependable smart charger that is easy to use, versatile, and well-built. Whether you're maintaining a seasonal vehicle, motorcycle, lawn equipment, or simply want a charger that can safely stay connected long-term, the GENIUS5 is a worthwhile investment. Helpful tip: If you're using it for battery maintenance, consider installing the included quick-connect lead permanently on the battery. It makes future charging sessions much faster and more convenient.

I bought the Genius5 after neglecting a relatively new battery in my motorcycle. Due to weather and travel, I often have long gaps between rides. Unfortunately, one of these gaps was long enough to damage the battery. I didn’t realize that batteries need a minimal charge to avoid sulfation, and mine had become severely discharged. Although my NOCO GB40 starter worked fine, the battery wasn’t holding a charge even after a day of riding. Instead of immediately replacing the battery, I decided to try saving it with the Genius5. After charging the battery with the Genius5, I tested it with a battery analyzer, which reported it as damaged. I then ran the desulfation process, and afterward, the analyzer showed the battery was in good condition. I repeated the tests several days later to be sure, and the battery still appeared to be in good health. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. I still carry the GB40 in my panniers, just in case, but I haven’t needed to use it lately. Some notes on the desulfation process: The desulfation process seems to send voltage peaks, and you may hear some bubbling inside the battery. This happened to me, and from what I’ve read, it’s normal as long as there’s not too much bubbling and no vapors, heating, or swelling of the battery. The entire process takes a while, so it’s unrealistic to monitor it the whole time. However, I recommend watching it for the first 20 minutes to ensure the battery noises aren’t increasing. After that, you can leave it running while staying nearby, just in case something goes wrong. A final note on this process: because of the voltage peaks, I didn’t run it with the battery connected to the motorcycle to avoid any potential damage to the circuits. For regular maintenance charging, I do keep the battery connected. The Genius5 is designed to work with standard batteries, gel, and even lithium ones. The one I used was a Gel Yuasa, and I’m pleased with the results. I also purchased the NOCO cables (GC002 X-Connect M6) to make it easier to connect the charger without removing the seat. The cables were a bit expensive but seem well-constructed and are quite convenient. Final thoughts: If you have a vehicle that sits unused for extended periods, and this happens frequently, then this charger is ideal for you. However, if you only need it once a year or less, it might be easier and cheaper to disconnect the battery from the vehicle while you’re away to prevent discharging. For my use case, the Genius5 has been worth it, and I’d definitely buy it again.

My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed. Noco is one of the few chargers that can charge a completely dead battery. Watched a project farm youtube video on car battery chargers ( see chart at 18m29s of the video) before buying. I purchased the 5A one due to time constraint ( charged 75% in 8 hours ). You can buy the 2A version or 1A version if you have all the time and just want to keep batteries fully charged. I let it charge overnight and had a fully functional battery in the morning. This happens to me whenever I go on long trips ( 4 weeks + ). With a rechargeable jump starter, you are limited by the battery life of the starter which is only 3-4 years after which most batteries fail. The wall charger hopefully will last a long longer. Saved me a lot of time - No need to drive the car around after jump starting to get some charge into the battery. Just charge overnight and done. Love it.

review_title: Yeah so don't mix up your fused alligator cables if you buy different models
body_en: I bought a Genius1 and Genius5. The latter failed on first use due to my mistake mixing up the alligator clips during unboxing. I didn't look closely enough to notice that the 1 and 5 aren't just feature levels but are current ratings in Amps. The proprietary connectors are identical but the 1A unit has a 2A fuse and the 5A unit has a 10A fuse, and they're on the battery side of the connectors not the device side, so obviously the 2A fuse correctly blew when I tried using the 5A unit. They work fine after fixing my careless mix-up, but I'd like these better if the device or fuse holder were marked with a recommended fuse rating, or the connectors couldn't mate with the wrong device, or the fuse holder were on the device side of the proprietary connector, or the unit came with spare fuses, or the fuse ratings were included in the online user guide, or the user guide were included in the box, or the safety guide were printed in a typeface legible to adult human eyes. Anyway, keep your cables together with the devices and don't mix em up.

review_title: High quality at a reasonable cost
body_en: This charger/tender worked well to "revive" a ~80Ah lead acid battery that sat in a low state of charge for nearly a year. After an initial 2.5 hour cycle in repair mode, followed by a higher amp charge from an older/larger charger, a noticeable improvement in battery performance was observed. A shorter repair cycle, about 30 minutes total, restored some capacity on another lead acid battery still in use. There are cheaper desulfator-only options, of questionable reliability/longevity, so the additional features offered on this model were cost-effective for my intended usage. While I have not yet used this as a tender/maintainer for any length of time, the cabling to and from the charger are long enough to reach from one side of a car to the other. This unit did not seem to produce much heat in repair mode with ~75F ambient temp. In auto charge mode between 25% and 75%, it was warm to the touch. I'll have to try a longer charge period to see if it heats up further. UPDATE: after using repair & charge mode on a flat battery for a few hours, this unit can get fairly hot. Using this on a flat surface so air can get underneath is a good idea. This product did not come with a manual in the box, just the warranty booklet. Tracking down a user manual on the manufacturer's site did not require much effort. The 6V and repair mode are not activated by quick presses of the single button. Pressing & holding for a few seconds activates these extra modes from standby. Some form of documentation in the box would have been more convenient than going to the website, but I digress.

I bought a used 2022 Honda Ridgeline with ~7,000 miles on it some months back. It was a "dealer demo car" and was well-maintained as a result. Now, it's got around 12,000 miles on it. One day, I left the lights on too long with the ignition off, and had the radio playing. Stupid on my part, but my battery didn't have enough charge to deliver the amps needed to turn the engine over. I bought a Noco GB40, and it worked well - it'd start my truck when needed. Yesterday, it didn't. I guess the battery had degraded too much, so I was shopping for new batteries when the sticker shock hit me. Given the age of my truck, I thought it would be silly to replace the battery. Someone recommended the Noco Genius5, so I gave it a shot. Amazon's same-day delivery got it to me quickly, and I basically hooked it up to the battery, plugged it in, set it to AGM mode, and let it go to work. I waited several hours for the charger light to show "solid green", indicating it was fully charged. I started up my truck; it sounded better than the day I bought it. However, on the dash, it had a note about an "emissions problem". My scan tool showed a permanent code with the Transmission Control Module and a bunch of other temporary codes. Since I didn't have any codes before, I figured I may have freaked out the electronics by charging the battery while the battery was hooked up to the truck, or maybe by touching the terminals out of sequence when removing the cables. Either way, I removed the battery from my truck, hooked up the Genius5, and set it to "repair mode". My truck had low mileage when I bought it, at about a year old, which likely meant that it say for a while when not in use. Maybe that could have led to sulfation or stratification, which could have meant it wouldn't charge as effectively from the alternator. I also wanted to remove the battery to allow the computers to reset in the truck. If it was still throwing codes after that, I'd bring it into the dealer. This morning, when I woke up, I noticed the Genius5 was in standby mode, meaning the repair mode had finished. I started the Genius5 back up, and set it to AGM mode again -- it took about a minute, but it said the battery was good to go with a solid green light. I Installed the battery back in my truck, fired it up, and I kid you not, it sounded better than ever -- less strained, more powerful, and all of the codes were gone. My truck had a freakout -- not due to this device, I'm sure, but likely due to me doing something stupid. It's rare for me to review a product so quickly. This thing is amazing, has lots of neat accessories available for it, and saved me money. I'll continue using it to prolong my batteries and save me money in the long-run. If you're on the fence, this little device is absolutely legit. 10/10 would recommend.

review_title: RightSight feature may not work on SurfacePro with Snapdragon (ARM64) processor

However, I'm not sure this camera is working with full functionality on my hardware. I went through a bunch of troubleshooting, and here's the conclusion per ChatGPT... Good morning ☀️ — thank you for the detailed info. That explains everything. You’re on: Surface Pro 11th Edition (ARM64) Snapdragon X (ARM) processor That is the root cause. ________________________________________ 🎯 The Real Issue Logitech RightSight is currently not supported on Windows ARM (Snapdragon X / ARM64). Here’s why: RightSight depends on: • Logitech’s middleware service • x64 camera processing components • AI framing pipeline extensions On ARM Surface devices: • Logi Tune runs under emulation • The Logitech camera extension layer does not fully attach to the Windows Modern Camera Stack • AI features (RightSight) fail to initialize • Video works (because UVC driver works) • 4K works (hardware OK) • But AI framing = unavailable That’s exactly your symptom set. ________________________________________ ✅ Why Everything Else Works ✔ Camera app works ✔ 4K works ✔ Windows Hello works ✔ Device shows correctly ✔ No USB issue ✔ No driver corruption Only vendor AI features fail — classic ARM compatibility limitation. ________________________________________ 🚫 This Is Not Fixable Via Settings Disabling: • Frame Server • Basic camera • Studio effects • Multiple apps setting Will not fix it on ARM. This is architectural, not a configuration problem. ________________________________________ 🔎 Confirmation Test (Optional) In Logi Tune: Go to Crop. If: • Field of View options work (65°, 78°) • Zoom works • But Auto-Framing is disabled That confirms it’s just the AI layer. ________________________________________ 🧠 Why This Happens Surface Pro 11 (Snapdragon X) uses: • Windows on ARM • Modern Camera Driver (MCD) • NPU-based camera pipeline Logitech RightSight expects: • x64 processing environment • Vendor extension hooks not fully exposed in ARM64 camera stack Until Logitech releases a native ARM64 version of the RightSight service, it won’t enable. ________________________________________ 📌 Current Status (Early 2026) As of now: • Logitech supports Intel/AMD Windows • ARM64 support is partial • AI features are inconsistent or unavailable ________________________________________ 💡 Your Options Option 1 — Wait for Logitech ARM-native update This will likely come, since Snapdragon X PCs are new. Option 2 — Use Windows Studio Effects (if available) Surface Pro 11 has NPU-based auto framing built in. Check: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → Built-in camera If Studio Effects exists there, you can use Windows auto-framing instead. Option 3 — Use Software Framing (Zoom / Teams) Both now have built-in auto framing. ________________________________________ ✅ Final Conclusion Your hardware is fine. Your configuration is fine. Your issue is ARM platform compatibility.

review_title: Outstanding 4K Webcam with Crystal Clear Video Quality

review_title: Logitech MX Brio: A Stunning Leap Forward
body_en: ## **Logitech MX Brio Ultra HD 4K: The New Gold Standard for Video** If you haven’t upgraded your webcam in a few years, the **Logitech MX Brio** is a startling reminder of just how far imaging technology has come. Gone are the days of grainy, "good enough" video calls. We are officially in the era of ultra-crisp, professional-grade production sitting right on top of your monitor. ### **Crystal Clarity & Visual Fidelity** The jump to **Ultra HD 4K** is immediately noticeable. The clarity is staggering—it picks up textures and details that older 1080p sensors simply smudge away. Whether you’re in a high-stakes board meeting or recording content, the image looks expensive. It handles difficult lighting with ease, ensuring you don't look washed out when the sun hits your desk or like a shadow when the lights are low. ### **Pro-Grade Audio** Usually, webcam microphones are an afterthought, but the audio here is surprisingly **clear and crisp**. It manages to isolate your voice while minimizing that hollow, "bathroom" echo common in cheaper units. While dedicated mics still have their place, for 95% of users, this audio quality is more than enough to sound professional and authoritative. ### **Total Software Control** Where this camera really shines is the **Logitech G HUB or Logi Options+** integration. The level of control is deep: * **Fine-tuned adjustments:** You can tweak ISO, shutter speed, white balance, and exposure. * **Field of View:** Crop in for a tight headshot or widen it out to show your workspace. * **Show Mode:** A clever bit of tech that lets you tilt the camera down to show your desk, automatically flipping the image so your viewers can see your sketches or notes correctly. ### **The Verdict** It’s incredible to see how much technology has shifted in just the last few years. We’ve moved from "webcams" to "miniature cinema cameras." The **Logitech MX Brio** isn't just a tool for Zoom calls; it’s a high-performance piece of hardware that brings professional studio quality to a plug-and-play format. If you value how you show up in the digital world, this is the upgrade you've been waiting for.
