review_title: Astoundingly effective, whisper quiet, highly recommend.
body_en: I bought a $90 tower purifier which took a long time to clear the air and which was noisier than a jet engine. I lived with it, but when the Canadian wildfire smoke descended upon us in NYC, I loaned it to my downstairs neighbor, who had elderly and special needs family members, and I ordered this as a replacement. It's more than double the cost of the other unit, but based on the reviews from the New York Times and other review sites, the quality and performance are well worth the investment. So I splurged and got this unit. While I was waiting for it to arrive, the air pollution got really bad and I had been coughing, eyes were watering and I was forced to wear an N-95 mask at home just to breathe. When the purifier finally arrived, I turned it on and the sensor light went red to indicate the high level of contamination in the air. I opened the doors of every room of my apartment to let it go to work and after a few minutes at full power, the light turned from red to purple, and about 5 minutes later, it went blue. I took my mask off and the air was pure and fresh. It is an absolute superhero at cleaning a large volume of air very quickly. I was thoroughly impressed. The sensor is very sensitive and will turn purple if you are just cooking something that releases strong scents into the air (sauteeing onions and peppers, etc.) and it goes red if you're burning anything. Another upside is that my kitchen smoke detector has stopped going off if I'm grilling something, because the purifier keeps the air quality under control. At the highest setting, it's about as loud as my old purifier at the middle setting, which is to be expected, as you would only set it that high to quickly clear out a room or if there's smoke from cooking, etc. But the massive volume of clean air it blows out in exchange for that short term annoyance is staggering. However, at the 2nd highest setting it is barely detectable, producing a pleasant, white noise background sound that you quickly tune out. It makes falling asleep very easy, and if you have the air conditioner on you can't hear the purifier at all. At it's lowest setting, it blows out a nice stream of air but is utterly and completely silent. You couldn't even hear it at night time in a small, quiet room with the door shut. Amazing. They say you never regret buying the best. They know what they're talking about. This is worth every penny and then some. 5 stars, all day.

review_title: Ok, Let's Clear The Air For A Moment.........
body_en: .........This Coway Air Purifier is outstanding, and I am not sure why it gets any bad reviews at all, unless someone just receives a bad unit from the factory (it happens, folks). Also, we have not had any of the bad "odors" that some people have complained about, either with the Coway air purifier itself, or with the replacement filters. However, the black colored model does look a lot like a large subwoofer, if that bothers anyone....lol. I did a LOT of research for an air purifier to replace the Bissell "My Air" air purifier that we had in our master bedroom, and this Coway air purifier kept coming up as a top pick everywhere. The Bissell "My Air" works well, but it's just too small to keep the air in our large master bedroom suite constantly clean, especially with our ever-shedding German Shepherd puppy always being in the bedroom with us at night. This Coway air purifier came well packed. It was double-boxed, and reinforced with cardboard packing material inside, and shrink-wrapped (no damage to the boxes or Coway unit at all). This Coway air purifier is very easy to setup. All that needs to be done is to open the front panel and unwrap the plastic around the charcoal and HEPA filters. Then replace the front cover, plug the unit in, and turn it on. Just don't forget to unwrap the filters before turning the unit on. This Coway air purifier is fairly quiet on the first 2 fan speed settings, but it gets pretty loud on the 3rd setting. However, the fan moves a LOT of air on the 3rd setting. The Auto and Eco modes are nice features, and they both seem to work well. We just keep the Coway air purifier in Auto, with the ionizer turned off, all of the time, as the ozone produced by the ionizer irritates my throat while sleeping with the unit on all night. I actually tested the dust sensor function in auto mode by shaking a dust rag in front of the Coway air purifier, and the fan speed ramped up from setting 1 to 3 for about 5 minutes, until the air was clean again, and then it went back to the 1st fan speed setting automatically. The dust sensor sensitivity is also adjustable by pressing the fan speed and ionizer buttons simultaneously for 2 seconds. Then use the fan speed button to adjust the 3 sensitivity levels (the unit is set to the middle "standard" setting at the factory). We have not had to change the dust sensor sensitivity level, as it seems to work well on the standard setting. Also, it is recommended that the dust sensor be cleaned with a cotton swab every 2 months. It is located behind the little door on the upper right of the unit. The large, bright power LED also indicates the dust particles ptesent in the room. Blue is clean air, purple is semi-dirty air, and red is really bad air quality. If the bright LED bothers anyone at night it can be turned off by holding down the ionizer button for 3 seconds. The 1,4, and 8 hour timer is a handy feature, if needed, but we never use it. We just run this Coway air purifier in Auto mode all of the time, and it works like a charm. It uses very little power (around 36 watts on high with the ionizer off), so I don't feel any need to constantly turn the unit on and off. The charcoal and HEPA filter indicator lights come on individually when it is time to change the appropriate filter, and the lights are reset by holding down the filter button for 3 seconds. The filter change timer can also be factory reset by holding down the filter change reset button for 2 seconds when neither of the filter change indicator lights are on (if the filters are changed early). The manufacturer recommends cleaning the washable mesh pre-filter every 2 weeks, changing the charcoal filter every 6 months, and changing the HEPA filter once a year. The charcoal and HEPA filters are NOT washable, and must be replaced. Only the mesh pre-filter is washable and reusable. I would take these filter cleaning/changing intervals with a grain of salt, and mileage may very, depending on the air quality in the individual home. I have seen many 3rd party companies that make the filters for this Coway air purifier. Most of them are much cheaper than the OEM Coway filters, and they have good reviews. However, we have only used the OEM Coway filters so far, and while being kinda over-priced, they work very well. Oh, and as previously mentioned, don't forget to clean the dust sensor every 2 months or sooner, as well. The rest of this Coway air purifier can be wiped down and vacuumed out as part of regular maintenance. Overall, this Coway brand is an excellent air purifier, and I highly recommend it, especially for anyone with allergies, asthma or pets in the house. It also filters cooking odors very well. Just keep in mind that this Coway air purifier is fairly large, so it needs plenty of room to function properly. Also, the shiny piano black model does attract finger prints like a magnet, if that bothers anyone. Oh, yeah, and as I previously mentioned, the black model looks a lot like like a large subwoofer. It is a unique design for an air purifier, to say the least. However, those minor "issues" should not detract anyone from purchasing this great Coway air purifier. Pick one up today!

I've been using the Coway Airmega AP-1512HH for several weeks, and it's easy to see why this model has been recommended for so many years. **Setup & First Impressions** Setup took less than 10 minutes. The filters come pre-installed in protective packaging, so make sure to remove the plastic before turning it on. The purifier feels well-built without taking up much floor space. **Noise** One of my biggest concerns was noise since I use it in my living space. On the lowest setting it's quiet enough that I barely notice it's running. Medium is still comfortable for everyday use, while High moves a lot of air but is noticeably louder—which is expected when you need maximum filtration. **Air Quality Sensor & Auto Mode** The air quality indicator is surprisingly responsive. It increases the fan speed automatically when cooking odours or dust are detected, then returns to a quieter setting once the air clears. I rarely need to adjust it manually because Auto mode works so well. **Air Quality** I noticed less lingering cooking smells and the room feels fresher overall. Dust also seems to accumulate more slowly on nearby furniture. While I can't measure microscopic particles at home, it has made a noticeable difference in day-to-day air quality. **Maintenance** The washable pre-filter is easy to remove and clean, which should help extend the life of the HEPA and carbon filters. The filter replacement indicator is also a nice reminder instead of trying to remember the schedule yourself. **Pros** * Quiet on low speed * Excellent Auto mode with responsive air quality sensor * Compact footprint * Easy filter maintenance * Eco mode helps reduce power consumption when the air is clean **Cons** * High speed is fairly loud (although it moves a lot of air). * Replacement filters are an ongoing cost, so it's worth factoring that into long-term ownership. Overall, this has been a reliable air purifier that balances performance, ease of use, and noise very well. If you're looking for a purifier for a bedroom, office, or medium-sized living area, I'd have no hesitation recommending this model.

review_title: Compact, Smart, and Perfect for a Bedside Table

review_title: Air feels good and clean no real issues with it.
body_en: It's really nice to have, bigger than I expected, but that's even better. It works nicely, and I enjoy having a way to see the air quality on my phone. I used to always get a runny nose due to dust in my room whenever I cleaned, but this has helped me not get as many runny noses anymore. I can see very little, if any, dust in the air (like when you see it in the sunlight). I tested it by blowing out a match in front of it to see if it really detects stuff; it went to max fan speed, which makes me believe this is working. Speaking of fan speed, it's really cool and nice to feel; I honestly replaced my AC with this most of the time. The main reason I would not give it 5 stars would be the lights. I hate sleeping with any type of lights, and whenever I change it using the buttons, it sometimes leaves a light on even in night mode, which in turn I would need to fix by going on the app, which allows me to turn it off. Other than that, the air feels very fresh, and I can hardly smell anything; it feels clean and nice in the room I use it in. It does need to be connected to an outlet instead of battery, which makes it hard to put it in the middle of the area without a cable being in a way, but for it's price, i would say it's really good, the filters aren't too expensive and I would only need to replace them once every 6 months based on how much im using it.

review_title: Efficace, silencieux la nuit, je l’adore, sauf pour le bouton du dessus
body_en: The purpose of this purchase was initially intended to purify the air in my room in winter, when it is very cold and the windows are stuck, or at certain times of spring, when there is too much pollen in the air to be able to ventilate. I received this item perfectly protected and with packaging from the manufacturer that I found clever. Once received, I immediately turned on this air purifier to check if it was in working order. Getting started: Thanks to the instructions also redirected in French, getting started was easy. I am satisfied to have been able to read the explanations in my language (I am French-speaking). By pressing the button on the top once, it is silent mode for night or rest; pressing twice is normal mode; by pressing three times, it is full power mode. Observing this process: There is no button that seems to depress, so sometimes I brush the top and can easily change modes, sometimes you have to press harder. I haven't been able to figure out where the "sensor" is if there is one. This would be the only negative point I would have to point out. No remote control for this first price, it suits me perfectly for my room. This is sufficient for my use. Filtration result: I left the purifier running for about 1 or 2 hours (duration at random), then I returned to my room. It’s incredible how fresh I felt! I immediately felt the difference, to the point that I decided to use it again now (not just for winter), because I was so happy, delighted and impressed with the result. Use in silent mode: Although I am very sensitive to noise in general, I slept several nights with the air purifier running in silent mode. And it went very well, to my great surprise. My breathing comfort has significantly improved thanks to this device. Other modes: Normal mode is bearable during the day, but perhaps not for many hours at a time if the person remains in the room. Very good rapid efficiency. Full power mode is very noisy, so use it when it's temporary. Personally, I used it when I changed my sheets to wash them, while having aired before or after. If I use it, I close the bedroom door. On the other hand, although I am delighted with my purchase, I falsely believed that there was an air quality display with an indicator light. I got mixed up with the photos I looked at. So it would be desirable to indicate that there is no remote control, no connection with the telephone, no air quality display. This device suits me perfectly, except that I would perhaps have preferred to invest in the model just above which has the air quality indicator. Conclusion: I am very satisfied with my purchase, despite the difficulty I sometimes have knowing how to press the top correctly (I always succeed). Depending on our budget, we will possibly invest in a second model from this specialized brand, which would have a light indicating the air quality. I must point out though that I chose this for its “skills”, and this model among the range according to the size of my room and the affordable Black Friday price. In short, thank you to the brand for existing in Canada. Be very alert about model comparisons. Finally, I would say that this model would be perfect in a bedroom, whether for a child or a baby or adults, or in a small room intended for teleworking. Happy shopping!
It makes almost no noise, it works perfectly. I recommend it.

We got this air purifier a few months ago. My husband and I absolutely love it. Just to follow on what I’ve read in other reviews: The automatic mode works well. We didn’t know how to make it work first. But then, we realised we just needed to make sure the unit was on, and leave it on Auto mode, that’s it. The timer works well too. It Does the work, fairly silent and the air feels fresher. You can track PM2.5 from your phone, and even turn on or off the device as long as it is connected to your WiFi. On top of performance, the design id appealing. We love it!

This air purifier keeps the air in my daughter's room clean. We have smokers in the adjacent unit to us and the smell drifts into her room. This unit gets rid of that smell efficiently . It is quiet on the lowest setting but does get noisy when you turn it up. The good thing is we usually only need on the low setting

The smoke from wildfires promoted me to buy this air purifier. I have two other air cleaners in different rooms that work well but I specifically wanted a quiet one for the bedroom and I crossed my fingers and ordered it. Set up was easy, just plug it in and set to Automatic. I didn't install the app and do not intend to (I'm so done with an app for every appliance). It was very quiet until the air quality detection kicked in (red indicator light = poor air quality) and the fan came on full. Even at maximum fan speed it was quieter than my other cleaners and within an hour the room went from "very polluted" (red indicator light) to "excellent" (blue indicator light). When the AQ got to blue, the fan speed reduced to a quiet maintenance level, perfect for sleeping. The manual explains the indicator lights, settings for fan speed and recommendations for filter change. There's also a WiFi indicator light: the instructions to install an app and connect to your network seem clear in case you want the graphs & reporting from an app. Overall I gave this 5 stars because it didn't force me to install an app, it's quiet, does an excellent job quickly cleaning the air, has clear instructions, and is an attractively designed & easy to maintain unit. One more thing: I ordered this along with some other items that weren't available until 2 days later so to save trips, selected Amazon to ship altogether. I had regrets about delaying delivery as the smoke hanging over my city got worse the next day, and was pleasantly surprised when I was notified the air cleaner had shipped and was out for delivery! Whoever or however that decision was made, I'm grateful.

My wife had a pretty severe asthma attack and her doctor recommended an air purifier. I bought the KNKA APH4000 based on price and positive reviews. This turned out to be a fantastic purchase . It is quiet unless the air quality is bad and it kicks into high gear. It is still tolerable and pretty quickly brings the air quality to safer levels. Most of the time my machine keeps it steady between 007 and 009. If iI use the stove the air quality gets quickly worse and the machine reacts instantly. With the recent issues my area had with wildfire smoke, this purifier keep levels inside my house tolerable and my wife did not have any further issues with her asthma. My favorite feature on the APH4000 is the LED color bar. It goes from green to blue to orange to red depending on the current air quality. Not only is it extremely cool looking, but you can see from across the room if the air quality has dropped. The digital readout also shows the actual air quality index number. I am very impressed with this unit and am very glad I made this purchase.

Okay, I don't normally jump on here to review products, but this filter is one of the most well-made items I've purchased in years. It works flawlessly and quietly. Setup was easy and I daresay fun. Everything fits together perfectly. It moves a ton of air for its size. Operation is a cinch. And it's markedly improved the air quality in our house, as well as reducing the amount of dust that gathers on everything. I move it around the house sometimes, just to give each room a little boost. I will probably end up buying another one at some point.

review_title: Beyond thankful I chose this unit!
body_en: Lots of positives with this unit. Glad we purchased it and I’ve recommended it to family and friends. Pros: -Does its job surprisingly well for the price and makes a huge difference in our home. Performs very well and covers our entire main floor. No complaints in coverage. -Very accurately monitors and displays Air Quality. -Affordable and competitive filter replacements widely available and that aren’t so proprietary that it makes them needlessly complex/expensive to manufacture(whether due to shape or enforcing official filters only with detection systems). This is a common grift with other brands where they deceptively cheat customers by designing their filters to be cost-prohibitive preventing generic options and competitive pricing… OR by even using “”smart”” features that prevent you from using unofficial filters enabling for more predatory pricing and gouging. Some other brands may even shut down and force filter replacements sooner than necessary for additional profits. Essentially hooking you with the unit itself and bleed you dry with the filters with no alternative options… I have ZERO concerns of that type of practice with this unit. Always will have plenty of options because with this design(standard shape and construction) suitable filters are/can be easily manufactured by competitors. -I also particularly like that it doesn’t want anything to do with your phone or your home WiFi network. I don’t want or need that. Those features are often a headache and are almost always a very real security concern without many or any added benefits. This is simple and perfectly effective without it. “Cons”/Notes: -Not really a con and this could easily be seen as actually another positive and speak to why it works so well… but it requires 2 filters for every replacement cycle meaning one for each side. They are very affordable though and last 3-6 months just as described. $40 for a 4pk which is enough for up to 12 months! Can’t beat that. Having one good sized filter for each side actually aids in its ability to intake air, so hard to call that a true negative—in the grand scheme it’s probably another positive. We’re quite pleased with this air purifier and seriously debating on buying a second for another floor of the house. Seems rather smart to stock up with a couple years worth of filters in this economy which I will be doing. Being able to keep up with filter replacements is the most important factor in ANY air purifier purchase no matter the brand… neglecting this can actually make your air quality worse rather than better by allowing captured fungi and bacteria to grow on the filters and be redistributed throughout your home. This unit and its filters are a great choice and won’t become cost prohibitive to keep well-maintained. Such a win. Very thankful I chose this unit.

Its much smaller than you think and is very quiet, especially on the lower settings. Easy to set up, just take the filter bags off and pop the feet on. The controls are easy. I have a 100lbs great pyrenees that is hard to bathe regularly. She gets a little stinky occasionally and is noticeable in my 1050 sqft house. One of these in my living room has solved that problem with just the regular filter, not even the pet one. I did order a couple pet filters for when the regular filter is done but I dont see needing the pet specific one for my purposes. I even got a 2nd for the cat litter in the basement. We have an off brand rotating box that is great but still some smell. One of these purifiers in the basement with the regular filter takes care of that too. Granted, we buy him good food so he is not a smelly cat by any means. The house smells better than ever.

We have been using this unit for a week now, it works great. It took a few minutes after unpacking, and reading the instructions, to actually find the power button. The control panel is pretty much invisible, until you plug the unit into power. Then things become obvious, and actually quite easy to use. I also appreciate that it does not require an app, or any such nonsense. It's a machine that you can plug in, turn it on and it does exactly what it's supposed to do!😁 Plus, it does a far better job of removing wildfire smoke and agriculture dust from the air than we expected for something of it's size and price. It's not silent, but reasonably quiet when it's at the lower speeds.

review_title: Amazing | it actually works | should be 5* but there is always room for improvement
body_en: Amazing little things. I felt/ smelled the difference within a few hours of plugging them in. The air just felt a lot cleaner. It does have the option of adding scented oil on a little sponge. I have not used it because I think it defeats the purpose of clean/ neutral air. But it feels great knowing it has such a feature. The filters must be some type of high tech because they work great. And the unit itself is super quiet/ silent. Currently I cannot think of ways to improve this amazing little unit.

The air purifier I had was too fussy for me, as I had 3 HEPA filters and a carbon fiber filter to take out & replace at different times. This purifier is a mighty little guy, at least half as big as my other unit, but much more powerful & less fussy. I got this around the first of June this year. I followed all the directions, as stated in the included booklet. I keep the booklet under the unit for future reference. I turned the unit on and noticed how quiet it is. I turned off the light on the panel because I didn't need yet another light to add to the other gadgets that also came with their own little lights. I set it on "auto" and walked away, letting it do its thing. I have a 936 square foot home, with a full basement. I figured this unit was more than capable of handling the upper level, as I keep the basement door shut & I rarely go down there. It has its own filtration system anyway, for my husband's wood shop. This unit is so quiet that I had to check it to make sure it was still running & to see if the panel light changed color so I could clean the filter. Nope, it was still working, doing its thing. A few days ago (almost halfway through August now), I was watching TV & saw the panel light go on. It was red! Red means the air quality is bad because the filter needs cleaning. The fan also kicked into gear where I could hear it, which told me that it sensed the change & was working on pulling more air through a filter that needed cleaning. I took both filters out, vacuumed them both, and cleaned the covers & the areas around where the filters fit. I put it all back together, then pushed the fan button until the number read 3 & walked away. I watched as the panel lit up in red, then changed to blue, which is better, but I'd rather it be green, which is best. That was yesterday. I'm checking it now & it is green! My husband has COPD & he was coughing more than usual yesterday. I noticed that after I cleaned the filters (front & back) and ran the unit on #3 for about an hour, his coughing was much less. Today the air seems less dense...lighter...cleaner. I keep this in the livingroom, which is open to the kitchen. These are the rooms we spend the most time in, so this is where the unit is. For us, this unit works perfectly. It's less fussy, with only two filters to buy...one for each side. They vacuumed easily with my little stick vacuum (Shark) using no attachments, just the handheld portion of the machine. Just turn this little guy in & he can take it from there. I would think you would have to get another unit if you had a bigger house, but for us, this exceeded my expectations.

review_title: Small, quiet and light weight but out performs units twice its size.
body_en: This works and performs very well. Great settings with a digital read out that shows you how bad your air is. I baught another one 1 day later because it is so good. Easily cleans air for up to about 1500 sq.' I put one with me in my work shed and its amazing how 2 seconds of 2 stroke smoke makes this thing take off when on automatic because the smoke that unfortunately smells so good is toxic as hell to breath but it was an eye opener to see. Not only did it out perform all the others I tried but was also the quietest by far. runs Set it on auto and forget it. Has night light if you use it where you sleep and not only does it have digital read out it changes color when it hits certain bad air thresholds. Filters are easy to pull out and wash too. What's interesting about this design is it pulls air in from front and back and then forces it out through both sides and because of this the dirty intake air is being filtered through the two biggest sides which allows more air to be filtered in a shorter time period and why it is so efficient with such a small foot print. It takes up very little space and is easy to move where you want to use it with its built in handle on each side and because its so small it makes it light as a feather. It also has 4 fan level settings, an eco mode, an auto mode wich cranks up the fan higher when it detects bad air and a pet mode that really cranks it up to get rid of the dander that people are so allergic too. If you are always sneezing from pets or allergies vacuum often and get you one of these and it will amaze you how it will get rid of those irritating allergies within a couple of days. I can actually breath through my nose when I sleep now cause my nose isnt clogged up anymore so I wake more rested cause I am sleeping so soundly and sleep without waking up100 times trying to breath. It will also help if you snore because your nose will no longer be clogged. I picked it up on sale which the price is awesome compared to anything that has specs anywhere as good as this one. I tried 5 different brands of air purifiers and this one hands down beat them all in everyway possible. This fan spins at a higher rpm too and is still quieter than all of the others that I tried.
purifies a 132 m2 office it really surprised me recommended
It is a very good product, it has a PM2.5 particle sensor, and in automatic mode, the fan speed increases or decreases depending on the pollution levels.
Muy bueno
I loved it, as soon as I can I will buy another one
Ok

I was slow to warm up to this appliance in my kitchen. I bought it to quickly cook a corned beef for St Patrick’s day. When it arrived I promptly threw away my old rusty but well used rice cooker (how many appliances can I really fit in my cupboard anyway?). It did a wonderful job, but honestly having never used a pressure cooker before I felt like I was programming a sensitive bomb that may go off in my kitchen at any moment! Every little beep or noise was frightening! I almost peed my pants when I released the pressure valve and loud hot greasy steam erupted from its behind angrily! That was not a fun clean up job! So after St patties was over it sat for months till I eventually pulled it out again to try making rice (yeah no I can’t seem to cook it on the stove). The rice cooked great in about the same time it took my old rice cooker. I now love my pot because of what happened last week. We got home late and I grudgingly wandered into the kitchen late one night wondering what I was going to make for dinner. I found a small jar of Thai peanut sauce and a freezer burned chunk of raw chicken way in the back of my freezer. I tossed both in and set it for 12 minutes. I didn’t expect it to actually work, but what came out was a pot full of juicy Thai peanut chicken I tossed over rice! So Yummy and quick and easy! I’m excited to see what else will work well now!

I’m very happy with my Instant Pot! It’s easy to use, cooks food quickly, and makes meal preparation so much more convenient. I love that it has multiple cooking functions in one appliance, which saves both time and space in the kitchen. It’s also easy to clean. Great quality and definitely worth the purchase. Highly recommend!

Over the years, I have purchased hundreds of items from Amazon, and for the most part, got what I expected. I never reviewed any of them. But from the moment I received my Instant Pot, I felt that I had purchased something that not only exceeded my expectations, but will make my life easier (and more delicious)! I am a holistic nutritionist and a follower of a lower carb/paleo/primal lifestyle (and yes, it is not only a food regimen, but a lifestyle). Many of the meals I prepare require advance planning and preparation, and I am OK with that, realizing that it is an investment in my family's health and wellbeing. I was looking for something that would support my food choices and perhaps make it a little less time-consuming. I have used a crockpot extensively over the past years and while I appreciate the ease of use and the ability to put a meal on the table soon after I got home in the evening, there is that "everything tastes the same" factor I was running into with my family. So I began thinking about ways to cook my meals faster and realized that a pressure cooker may be the answer. But, I am scared of pressure cookers. Even though my head tells me that people have been using them for many years with no problems, my heart said there was a strong chance I could blow up the entire kitchen, myself included. I had no idea there were electric, programmable pressure cookers out there that would virtually eliminate that worry until I began researching them, first on Amazon, and then on other websites. I eventually purchased the Instant Pot over the others because of the stainless steel insert (no aluminum), the size of the pot (I wanted a larger capacity), and the ease of use. The day it arrived, I plugged it in and began reading the manual. The manual was very helpful, even included a suggested trial run to familiarize one with the basics. My first meal was potato soup (I know potatoes are not low carb or paleo, but once in a while you gotta have potato soup). I was amazed at how easy and delicious it was to make this soup that would normally take a couple of hours. I just coarsely chopped the vegetables, threw those in the pot, added the seasonings and the liquid, started the pressure cooker option, and in 20 minutes all I had to do was use my immersion blender to puree the soup, add some cheese, stir and it was ready to eat. AND the soup was every bit as good as my slower version that keeps me tied to the kitchen to stir and monitor until it's done. That is the hidden beauty of this appliance, that while it's cooking your food, you are free to do other things such as harass your kids to get their homework done. No more watching over a pot! My second recipe was lemon pepper chicken wings. There is a searing option, so first I browned the wings in a bit of butter, then added lemon pepper, salt, and 2 more tablespoons of butter. Put on the lid, set the pressure cooker for 25 minutes, and out came the most delicious, fall-of-the-bone wings just loaded with flavor. The family went wild! I also made mushroom gravy (no flour) pork chops in 30 minutes in the pressure cooker - the gravy was so good my son ate in on top of some gluten free noodles the next day for lunch - and a breakfast meat loaf in the slow cooker, also a winner. I am also using this to reheat food since we don't use the microwave anymore and I'm finding that it seems easier and makes less of a mess than going stovetop. That's a pretty long review for a first-timer but I am so enthusiastic about this product that I just had to share.

Really love this thing. We use it mostly as a pressure cooker and slow cooker, so I can't speak to its other functions. Very easy to use; built-in timer is very helpful. Plug it in, put items in pot, and let it go. Cleaning is pretty easy. Very satisfied with the quality of the cooking; everything is cooked through, tender, delicious. Excellent purchase and heartily recommended.

review_title: Easy to Use and Very Convenient
body_en: I’m very happy with this Instant Pot. It’s easy to use, cooks food quickly, and makes preparing meals much more convenient. The 6-quart size is great for everyday cooking, and I love that I can prepare different types of meals in one appliance. It has saved me a lot of time in the kitchen. Definitely a useful addition to my kitchen!

review_title: From Pressure Cooking Novice to Culinary Master
body_en: As a self-proclaimed cooking enthusiast, I recently embarked on a culinary adventure with the Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, and boy, what a game-changer it has been! This marvel of a kitchen appliance has not only simplified my cooking process but has also elevated my meals to a whole new level. Let me share my delightful experience with you. First off, the title of "7-in-1" is no joke! This versatile appliance seamlessly transforms into a pressure cooker, slow cooker, rice cooker, steamer, sauté pan, yogurt maker, warmer, and even a sterilizer. It's like having an entire kitchen arsenal in one compact device. I couldn't help but admire the sleek stainless steel design that added a touch of elegance to my countertop. Getting started was a breeze, thanks to the user-friendly controls and the accompanying free app, boasting a whopping 1900 recipes. The app became my culinary companion, guiding me through various cuisines and offering endless inspiration. I was particularly thrilled by the app's meal planning feature, which made my life much easier. Now, let's talk about the real magic—the pressure cooking feature. It dramatically reduced cooking times, allowing me to prepare mouthwatering stews, roasts, and soups in a fraction of the time. I recall the first time I attempted a beef stew, and within 30 minutes, the meat was tender, succulent, and bursting with flavors that would typically take hours to develop. One evening, I decided to put the slow cooker mode to the test. I loaded the pot with ingredients in the morning, set the timer, and left for work. The aroma that welcomed me upon returning home was heavenly, and the slow-cooked pulled pork was an absolute hit with my family. The sauté function came in handy for browning meats before pressure cooking, while the steamer proved ideal for preserving nutrients in vegetables. I even dabbled in homemade yogurt, and the results were surprisingly delicious. The Instant Pot Duo truly opened doors to endless culinary possibilities. Now, let me share a funny mishap. One evening, I forgot to put the sealing ring in place, resulting in a bit of a mess. However, I quickly learned from my mistake and now double-check everything before cooking. It was a small hiccup amidst the joy this appliance has brought into my kitchen. I must say, the Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker has also provided some hilarious moments in my kitchen. One incident stands out vividly in my mind. I decided to try a new recipe for a creamy pasta dish. With all the ingredients prepped and ready, I excitedly added them to the Instant Pot and set the cooking time. As I eagerly awaited the delicious outcome, I couldn't help but notice an unusual amount of steam escaping from the pressure release valve. Confused, I quickly consulted the instruction manual and realized my rookie mistake—I forgot to seal the venting knob! I rushed to rectify the situation and twisted the knob into the correct sealing position. However, when I went to release the steam, a comical mishap occurred. In my haste, I turned the valve too quickly, resulting in a spray of creamy pasta sauce shooting up and hitting the ceiling! It was as if I had accidentally created a pasta-themed work of art on my kitchen ceiling. My initial shock was quickly replaced by uncontrollable laughter. I couldn't believe the mess I had made. After a good laugh and a quick clean-up, I realized that even in moments of culinary chaos, the Instant Pot Duo had a way of bringing joy to the kitchen. It's not just a cooking appliance; it's a source of entertainment and shared laughter with friends and family. Despite the occasional mishaps, the Instant Pot Duo has consistently delivered incredible results. Its ability to tenderize meats, infuse flavors, and create delicious meals in record time has truly amazed me. The convenience of having multiple cooking functions in one device has not only saved me time but also precious kitchen space. In terms of improvements, I would appreciate a more detailed user manual. While the free app provided great recipes and guidance, a comprehensive manual would have been helpful for understanding all the features and settings. Additionally, the 3-quart capacity is perfect for smaller portions and side dishes but can be limiting for larger family gatherings. I've discovered another delightful aspect of the Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker that I must share. It has become a game-changer when it comes to meal prep and leftovers! As someone who values efficiency and convenience in the kitchen, the Instant Pot Duo has exceeded my expectations. With its various cooking functions, I can now prepare large batches of meals and store them for later. This has been a game-changer for my busy schedule. One of my favorite experiences was making a big batch of chili on a Sunday afternoon. The Instant Pot allowed me to quickly cook the flavorful chili using the pressure cooker function. After enjoying a hearty dinner, I portioned out the leftovers into individual containers and stored them in the refrigerator. Throughout the week, I simply reheated the chili in the Instant Pot using the warming function, and voila! I had delicious and piping hot meals ready in minutes. Gone are the days of reheating leftovers in the microwave, resulting in uneven heating and compromised flavors. Additionally, the Instant Pot Duo's versatility has made meal prep a breeze. I can use the sauté function to quickly sear meats or soften vegetables before adding them to a slow-cooked recipe. The ability to switch between functions seamlessly saves me time and dirty dishes. Moreover, the Instant Pot Duo's stainless steel cooking pot is a breeze to clean. The non-stick surface prevents food from sticking, and any remnants are easily removed with a gentle scrub. This not only saves me precious time but also ensures that my dishes come out perfectly cooked each time. While I have had countless positive experiences with the Instant Pot Duo, there is one minor drawback worth mentioning. The steam release valve can sometimes be a bit tricky to clean thoroughly. Its design includes small crevices where residue can accumulate. However, with a little extra attention and a small brush, it's manageable. In conclusion, the Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker has revolutionized my cooking experience. Its versatility, ease of use, and impressive cooking capabilities have made it an invaluable addition to my kitchen. From quick weeknight dinners to elaborate weekend feasts, this kitchen marvel has never disappointed. With the Instant Pot Duo by your side, you'll transform from a cooking novice to a culinary master in no time!

My 8-quart Instant Pot arrived yesterday mid-day. This is my 4th or 5th electric pressure cooker, and it is replacing a Cooks Essentials 6-quart electric PC whose interior pot's non-stick lining had chipped. I also have some smaller Kuhn Rikon stovetop PCs, which permit really quick cooking for the recipes that fit into them. I "must" have a large electric pressure cooker for 5 things: 1) I love to cook a whole chicken and make my chicken soup completely from scratch. In the U.S. our grocery stores have big chickens. 2) I am hooked on my own Corned Beef and Cabbage, because I cook the corned beef the night before, and remove the fat after a day of refrigeration. It tastes "cleaner" but still has lots of flavor. 3) Recipes for beef stews might limit the volume of potatoes, carrots, and onions to fit in the pot. An 8-quart pot allows me to use a larger cut of beef, and add more potatoes without jeopardizing the PC's ability to come up to pressure. 4) PC recipes that take longer than an hour test my patience for hanging around. I like to "set it and forget it" for a while. 5) Ribs. Ribs take up a lot of space, and most people don't limit themselves to a proper "single" portion. Set dry-rubbed ribs on a trivet in the PC and let the water's steam produce moist ribs. No BBQ sauce is needed! I still use my smaller stovetop PCs for: 1) 3-qt is perfect size for rice. I prefer PC rice to rice cooker rice - less scorching. I freeze extra cooked rice. 2) 2-qt is perfect for simple dinner for 2 - and fast - it takes little time to come up to pressure or for natural release. 3) 5-qt braiser holds a full-size round cooling rack, allowing me to steam 4-5 chicken breasts or quickly steam asparagus. 4) I use the 5-qt braiser when I need a truly "quick release" to add foods in stages. With a stovetop PC, you take the PC to the sink and run cold water on the lid to reduce the pressure quickly. You can't do that with an electric cooker. So, how about the 8-quart Instant Pot? 1) The inner pot is high quality. Soaking solves a lot of cleaning problems in stainless steel. 2) The silicone gasket fits very snugly. In fact, after I did my preliminary sudsy wash, it seemed like torture to get the gasket to fit correctly. I thought I had fit it correctly... until I tried to do the Water Test and I was unable to lock the lid in position. Thank goodness some kind souls on the Instant Pot Community page on Facebook helped me identify the problem. (When you get your 8-qt pot, observe carefully how the gasket fits before disassembling for washing.) Today,when I reassembled my IP, I patiently positioned the ring in one spot and patiently coaxed it into place, so apparently this old dog could still learn a new trick. (It is important that the gasket and the lid both be completely dry!) 3) The 8-qt. machine is BIG, and TALL. Inside the Instant Pot shipping box was the product box with all the graphics as you might see on a store shelf. The product box also had a plastic strap to coax the product box out of the Instant Pot shipping box. The product box had styrofoam reinforcement of the product at top and bottom. So the product was well protected during its shipping!

Test 1: Chicken broth (Option: Slow cook). I made the same broths and soups that I made in my slow cooker. I found it very convenient that I could schedule a time to cook and then it would just keep the food warm. Test 2: White rice (Option: Rice). I decided to venture into pressure functions and make rice with the default option. It was a resounding success. The rice was fluffy and soft. Nothing stuck to the bottom of the pot. Test 3: Roasted chayotes (Option: Sauté). While it was fun to do this in the IP, it was a little clumsier to cook in this mode than if I did it in a conventional skillet or pot. However, this option is useful for reheating. Test 4: Brown rice (Option: Manual). Because it is a harder cereal, the Rice option is not enough. Still, I got a successful result using manual mode. Test 5: Oatmeal with apples (Option: Porridge). The final result is not pleasing to the eye but the flavor is impressive. From that day on, Instant Porridge has become the star breakfast of the house. Test 6: Chicken broth (Option: Soup/Broth). I tried making chicken broth under pressure, and it was another success. During this time working at home, the IP has been a great ally because I don't have to worry that the food is going to burn while I'm in a meeting. I have made dishes that I had never dared to cook before (e.g. mole de roca with loaded rib and suadero), and I have optimized my time in the kitchen with dishes that I would normally have to pay attention to such as beans, lentils or rice. Honestly, I was a bit worried because of the analysis of price vs features vs brand. I was mostly satisfied with my previous one of a "big brand," but my wife was not happy because it did not come with a metal insert. And, of course, we all have our prejudices - and I have a wife with a crapload of those! Well, she went on a trip, and I had no cricket on my shoulder... so I took a chance! he-he-he-he!! (drumroll, please!) It honestly SEEMS a bit pricey, I will not deny that. YET, when comparing features, its HUGE capacity, the "stainless steel insert," it came very much cheaper than the main-brand ones. Now, I am honestly not sure if it is stainless steel. However, I have had this now for... let me do math here... the root square of... add the cosene... and dividied by Saturn's PI... IDK... 2 months? I am super impressed! I generally use it for rice. but not just boring white rice. I make rice with beans, rice with meat, sticky rice, basmati rice... and I recently used the pressure-cooking feature. It works just as, or better than, advertised! Only features that that are slightly annoying is that you have to press the one button a bunch of times until you get to the function you desire, and that I still have not figured out how to change the time once I engage the function. To be fair, for the latter, I have not opened the instructions manual (of course, I am a guy!), but I honestly have not needed it - it was mostly a curiosity. I will just let the wife figure it out in... 4 weeks, when the peace is over in the house! Sigh... Caution: DO NOT leave it unattended. IT WILL overcook your items! Because of the metal insert, it conducts heat very well! Its warming option is very, VERY effective. Honestly, just shut it down and leave the lid closed if you want to keep the food warm for another hour or so, then reheat it as necessary. You will also save on power. I wish I remembered where the heck I got it, but it is great now, whereas it was just meh back then. Something I wish it had was a way to easily lift the insert while it was still hot. I happen to have some hook-like thingys that easily attach to the insert sides, but I wish they came with it. But that is it. I love this! Anyway, GREAT purchase. Obviously, I have used it quite enough.

Over the years, I have purchased hundreds of items from Amazon, and for the most part, got what I expected. I never reviewed any of them. But from the moment I received my Instant Pot, I felt that I had purchased something that not only exceeded my expectations, but will make my life easier (and more delicious)! I am a holistic nutritionist and a follower of a lower carb/paleo/primal lifestyle (and yes, it is not only a food regimen, but a lifestyle). Many of the meals I prepare require advance planning and preparation, and I am OK with that, realizing that it is an investment in my family's health and wellbeing. I was looking for something that would support my food choices and perhaps make it a little less time-consuming. I have used a crockpot extensively over the past years and while I appreciate the ease of use and the ability to put a meal on the table soon after I got home in the evening, there is that "everything tastes the same" factor I was running into with my family. So I began thinking about ways to cook my meals faster and realized that a pressure cooker may be the answer. But, I am scared of pressure cookers. Even though my head tells me that people have been using them for many years with no problems, my heart said there was a strong chance I could blow up the entire kitchen, myself included. I had no idea there were electric, programmable pressure cookers out there that would virtually eliminate that worry until I began researching them, first on Amazon, and then on other websites. I eventually purchased the Instant Pot over the others because of the stainless steel insert (no aluminum), the size of the pot (I wanted a larger capacity), and the ease of use. The day it arrived, I plugged it in and began reading the manual. The manual was very helpful, even included a suggested trial run to familiarize one with the basics. My first meal was potato soup (I know potatoes are not low carb or paleo, but once in a while you gotta have potato soup). I was amazed at how easy and delicious it was to make this soup that would normally take a couple of hours. I just coarsely chopped the vegetables, threw those in the pot, added the seasonings and the liquid, started the pressure cooker option, and in 20 minutes all I had to do was use my immersion blender to puree the soup, add some cheese, stir and it was ready to eat. AND the soup was every bit as good as my slower version that keeps me tied to the kitchen to stir and monitor until it's done. That is the hidden beauty of this appliance, that while it's cooking your food, you are free to do other things such as harass your kids to get their homework done. No more watching over a pot! My second recipe was lemon pepper chicken wings. There is a searing option, so first I browned the wings in a bit of butter, then added lemon pepper, salt, and 2 more tablespoons of butter. Put on the lid, set the pressure cooker for 25 minutes, and out came the most delicious, fall-of-the-bone wings just loaded with flavor. The family went wild! I also made mushroom gravy (no flour) pork chops in 30 minutes in the pressure cooker - the gravy was so good my son ate in on top of some gluten free noodles the next day for lunch - and a breakfast meat loaf in the slow cooker, also a winner. I am also using this to reheat food since we don't use the microwave anymore and I'm finding that it seems easier and makes less of a mess than going stovetop. That's a pretty long review for a first-timer but I am so enthusiastic about this product that I just had to share.

Excellent purchase and heartily recommended.

The good: I like the look, it certainly looks PRO and the steam release guard (aka a cap) and the switch to release the steam are welcomed additions. The handles are great and definitely help when you're wanting to lift out a pot full of boiling hot chicken stock. The display works well and there are other features like a beep reminder incase you missed the original beep when the cooking finished. I also love the ability to save favourites, extremely useful especially when considering one of the Pro's flaws. The bad: The interface of this is a big step back from the previous generation Instant Pot that this replaced. It feels like the mini computer inside this struggles to keep up with what you're asking it to do, especially when it comes to setting a time. The lag of the timer as you turn the dial is awful. And as you're adjusting the timer there is a constant beeping sound which is just really annoying. You can actually turn off the sound but that also stops all the useful notifications like when your food is cooked so there's not really a good solutions here (besides being able to set a common time / pressure combo as a favourite which helps). They also changed the Yoghurt setting so my previous sweet spot of 9 1/2 hours like the older model no loner worked. With this Pro model it was taking 16+ hours to make a quite awful yoghurt. After a little research I found out the temperature of its default setting is 42° which is too low. I bumped it up to around 45° and now I get my great yoghurt in 9 1/2 hours again. I have no idea why they changed this but fortunately I have saved this setting as another favourite and no longer use their setting. Overall, besides those quirks, the Instant Pot Pro does all the things you would expect from an Instant Pot. The handles are very useful and I can't imagine going back to the handle-less pots.
