I had to take the food out and cook it in the oven. I sent the pot back The third time I ordered a 6 quart instant pot pro which looked beautiful, but had the exact same problem. There was also a problem getting the lid to come off the pot I had to take a butter knife and push down the steam release so that the lid would release and allow me to remove it even when I was not using the pressure cook mode. The slow Cook function absolutely would not preheat I did an experiment by putting water in the pot and turning it on for eight hours in the morning with no food in it and it never came up to temperature. Seven hours later it was still blinking preheat and the water inside was like 150°F. I contacted instant pot and they wanted me to do this almost tremendous task of taking a video showing the problem taking several photographs explaining the context of the problem blah blah blah blah. I said no I am just going to send it back until I can get one that actually works. That brings me to my fourth and final order of the instant pot Pro 6 qt. I know that it will shock you, but I had the exact same problem. I could not believe it. I looked it up online (as I should have done in the first place)and found that this is a common problem with this product. It just will not come up to heat on slow cook. One YouTube video said that it takes hours for this particular model to come up to temperature and you will need to have an instant thermometer handy so that you can check your food every few hours to ensure that it's actually cooking appropriately. I don't know about you, but when I slow cook food it is my expectation that that food is going to cook, even if I am out working in my garden or running a quick errand to the store. Why would I be on standby for eight hours when I can probably cook it in the oven in one or two and have a somewhat consistent result? Well, I did contact instant pot (again) and they required me to send photographs, and an explanation, and the whole rigmarole, which I did this time only to get a reply just a couple hours later where I was told the same thing : if you were going to cook something on slow cook it can take up to four hours to preheat on a longer cook. My reply back to instant pot was that several sites on the Internet know that there is a problem with the instant pot pro in that the slow Cook function does not work correctly. The Internet knows that this is a flaw. Amazon is becoming aware that this is a flaw. And I believe that instant pot knows that this is a flaw yet they refuse to either correct the problem or honor their warranty. I am sad to say that I will never buy another instant pot product after the runaround that I was given by this company, who refused to assist me, will not honor the warranty, made excuses for a faulty product, and ultimately just basically said if you don't like it go return it (literally). So I am. GOOD NEWS-- UPS will pick it up for free.

review_title: Great pressure cooker for everyday family meals
body_en: I’ve been using this Instant Pot Pro for over 4 months, and it has become one of the most useful appliances in my kitchen. The 6-quart size is perfect for a family of four — enough space for stews, soups, and batch cooking, but not too bulky on the counter. Cooking results: • Pork and beef come out incredibly tender — the meat literally falls apart. • Potatoes with meat turn out soft and perfectly cooked. • Homemade beef stew cooks in about 30 minutes, which still surprises me. • I also made beef “tushonka” and it turned out excellent. • I tried making pilaf once — the rice overcooked and the bottom browned slightly, so this recipe needs some adjusting. Ease of use: • Very simple controls, intuitive interface. • I really like that the exterior has no physical buttons — it makes wiping the surface quick and easy. • The inner pot handled the dishwasher perfectly. What could be improved: • The lid is not very convenient to wash, especially around the silicone parts. • An extra sealing ring is included, but it doesn’t completely prevent the pot from absorbing strong smells from previous dishes (paprika, curry, etc.). I haven’t tested sweet or dairy recipes yet because of this — I’m sure the aroma would transfer. • The steam release is very hot and can splash, so you need to stand back when depressurizing. Overall, it’s a great appliance that saves a lot of time and consistently delivers delicious results. I rate it 4 stars, mainly because of the lid cleaning and lingering smells, but I’m still very satisfied with how well it cooks.

review_title: Eficacia, Sabor, Tranquilidad sin mucho esfuerzo!
body_en: I bought the Instant Pot and it was genuinely one of the best decisions for my kitchen. I use it several times a week and it has solved things that were a pain before, especially when meat or chicken is frozen. Literally: from freezer to served plate, without drama. One of the moments where I loved her the most was at Christmas. I was able to make the entire dinner in about 2 hours, when normally I would have spent all night cooking. Soft meats, well cooked, with flavor, without being stuck to the stove or stressed by time. The pressure works great, the results are consistent, and it gives you a lot of peace of mind knowing that you can cook even when you didn't plan anything in advance. It is ideal for: frozen chicken or meat, stews, broths, rice, “everyday” meals and also for special occasions. At first the buttons are a little intimidating, but it's a matter of using it a couple of times. Then it becomes automatic in your routine. Plus, the inner pot is easy to clean and the safety system feels very reliable. I'm not exaggerating when I say it saves me time, energy and stress. If you cook at home and want good results without spending hours, it is totally worth it. I recommend it without hesitation and I would definitely buy it again and in fact I'm thinking about buying more sizes :D.

review_title: Muito mais que uma panela de pressão
body_en: Great product. Inner stainless steel pan that can be removed and used on the stove. It makes cleaning easier and will last forever. I make yogurt in pots in a bain-marie every week. I pasteurized whole eggs with the sous vide function. Quiet when using pressure, which works wonderfully.

After my previous Instantpot stopped working one day. It was time for a new one. This one I chose as it had sous vide function. I have used this function twice now. I am quite impressed with it I must say. This Instantpot has ten functions. It is bigger than my precious one at 8qt. While I don’t cook for many I do not regret choosing the bigger version. What I enjoy about this particular Instantpot is the following: -The steam release is so much more easy to use. Just slide down to open and slide up to close. -The stainless steel liner with handles is the best update to this device ever. Silicone handles make it so easy to remove a scorching hot pot. -As with my previous pot this one has the dial to adjust time, temp and such. So easy and handy. -the cord is attached rather than having to plug it in the pot each time. As of yet I haven’t use this Instantpot for anything else. I can’t imagine it be any less than my other Pot. One thing I can think of that I’m not so impressed with: -There is a small slot to slide one thickness of your cord in the back, to hold it. It is fairly useless as being able to hold more cord would have been so much more useful. Even a nice Velcro strap to fold the cord up would have been so much better. Is this InstantPot worth buying? It is in my opinion a solid buy. It has more than one use and is a well built product.

Product was working fine till unexpected malfunction happened. The Tokion team was then extremely helpful. Provided me multiple options for repair through warranty and when all solutions were exhausted, full refund was issued upon shipping back the item
The product demo was given by Mr. Zafar Khan. The demo was really good and detailed. Made things so much easier. And the product is really convenient and amazing to use. Must buy.

This is a game changer! I use it almost every day. It makes cooking soups, stews, and rice incredibly fast and easy. The meat comes out so tender. The stainless steel inner pot is high quality and super easy to clean. Worth every penny!

review_title: Indispensable upgrade to the classic slow cooker
body_en: When my old slow cooker committed suicide (our neighbor's construction work caused the inner stoneware liner to leap off of the drying rack and shatter on the floor), I took advantage of the opportunity to upgrade to an Instant Pot. I'd been hearing so much about how fast and easy they make cooking. The first week I had it, I made a different recipe in it every night. Lasagna, macaroni and cheese, hearty mushroom and barley stew, and many others. We quickly realized that the Instant Pot cooks pasta completely differently from the regular method of boiling it. And it tastes amazing. The pasta cooks through completely, yet remains substantial to the bite. We cook all of our pasta in the Instant Pot now, even if it's just spaghetti, not a full meal. We've sautéed in it, steamed, pressure cooked, and even made rice. Everything came out perfectly. I think I'd prefer to sauté things on the stovetop, simply because I don't like reaching down into a hot pot to stir things. But if you're a college student with no stove, it gives you a great option for more styles of cooking. One helpful tip I'd add is when releasing the pressure valve, make sure your Instant Pot is well away from walls and windows. Otherwise, you'll have to clean starchy water stains off of them. Now, I make sure it's got plenty of clearance, and that there's nothing on the counter that I don't want getting wet, and it's fine. I just wipe up the moisture that condenses as part of kitchen cleanup. We love the instant pot so much, we haven't put it away since we got it! We use it a couple of times a week at least.

First time pressure cooking user and I was nervous. That being said, I’ve used this a dozen times now and I love it! Easy to use, and a great addition to a busy life. This instant pot makes the process of cooking so much better. Rice isn’t sticking to the bottom of the pot, the short ribs I cooked were tender, and the chicken breast I JUST cooked were juicy and cooked through! The size is big enough to cook 4x4 short ribs standing up, 2x big chicken breasts laying down (you can squeeze a 3rd). I also made stir fry rice in it easily. Easy to clean as well. I love it!

review_title: Why I bought the Instant Pot IP-DUO Plus60 9-in-1 Multi-Functional Pressure Cooker, 6 Qt
body_en: Instant Pot IP-DUO Plus60 9-in-1 Multi-Functional Pressure Cooker, 6 Qt - I've wanted a PC for a long time and have done a lot of research. I was originally leaning towards the PPCXL because that's what my cousin has, but I did some more research and ended with this one, waiting until the Duo Plus came out. So, since I'm the 4th reviewer, here's some of the thought process I went through in deciding to get the DUO Plus and also some thoughts on the IP vs the PPCXL and also other considerations on accessories, size, etc. So far, I've only had it a few days, but overall satisfied and plenty of online support for recipes and helping you decide the post PC for your needs. **Why I went with the Instant Pot (IP) duo60 Plus - Three new preset buttons - cake, egg, sterilize. It also had the yogurt function which other IP do, but not some of the other makes. Large LCD Screen with Digital Display Mute button for those beeps in the night when cooking yogurt etc. Plus / Minus button for both time and pressure Keep Warm Selector can be selected to on or off at anytime. Delay start of 24 hours and keep warm for 10 hours. Lid rest (right or left side) **Why I went with IP vs PPCXL - Food Grade 304 (15/8) stainless steel pot vs stainless steel with teflon coating. I felt I could scrub and treat the pot however I wanted and not worry about scratching and what utensils to not use. Yes, you can buy a replacement inner pot for a Teflon pot, but after I spend $100+ I really don't think I should have to buy a replacement inner pot. Some of the FB group users are fine with the Teflon pot, but there are also a lot of complaints, so it might be in the handling, but every Teflon pan I ever had eventually got tossed out because of the coating coming off. IP came with some of the accessories you pay for on the PPCXL. It had the trivet with handles, condensation collector, Rice Paddle & spoon and a couple intro guides/cookbooks. Free shipping for IP. PPCXL site wanted $29.99 Buttons weren't quite clear on PPCXL site so it made me think they were hiding lack of selection on preset buttons. Also, confusing on what you were buying - regular PPC or PPCXL. A lot of their verbiage refers to PPCXL, but not necessarily when you go select your items for your shopping cart. Yogurt Button - The IP has this and the PPCXL doesn't. The IP allows you to bring the milk to 185 in the IP, cool to 120 (I will be using the quick cool method in the sink) and then put in yogurt mode for incubation (8-12 hours). The PPCXL doesn't have this and you wrap it and put it in the oven. Warranty on IP is 1 year and I went with the Square Trade Warranty for 4 years for an additional $14.37. No deductible, no hidden fees, no shipping, transferable. PPC has 60 day money back/replacement. After that up to one year you have to pay $24.99 for shipping. Their extended warranty if $15 for 3 years. Slow Cooker Mode had a low, medium and high heat button. IP has a + and - sign to increase or decrease the time. Others you have to select a preset and keep pressing to increase, you can't decrease time. Overall ratings - IP 4.7 and PPCXL 4.1. I read through a lot of comments by verified buyers and the PPC owners seemed a lot more upset with customer service. I looked through a lot of Reviewers who do this for a living or at least blog and they leaned towards the IP. I messaged with the PPCXL people online and you can tell they've been coached for answers knowing what their down faults are and not really answering the question or referencing what you know is a negative. There are more IPs on the market and most recipes are geared towards it from a "preset button" perspective. IP has a left and right handle that will hold your lid tilted. I belong to a Pressure Cooker group - there are a lot of complaints about other manufacturer's instructions, quick start guide, etc. Lots of issues with lids locking, not pressurizing etc and I really don't see this for the Instant Pot family of PCs. **Sizing - I measured my crock pot which was 6 quart, so that's what I ordered. It's an OK size for 2 people, but since you can only fill it 2/3 full when cooking under pressure you should take that into consideration. I figure on a roast, I will do the meat first, then veggies. The 6 quart will hold four pint canning jars for sterilization. **Accessories - What else to buy? I got the OXO Good Grips steamer with extendable handle and a pack of 3-IP Rings color coded (dark for savory meats, orange for desserts and I will use the clear for yogurt). I had read they were dishwasher safe, but not 100% as they might keep flavors. On my next order I'm looking at 2 cookbooks (IP Electric Pressure Cooker Cookbook for $9 and IP Obsession for $12). There are plenty of Facebook Group pages you can join for recipes too and online reviewers. Just type in what you are making followed by "in a pressure cooker" or "in an IP". I'm also buying IP Silicone Mitts for easy removal of a hot pot since I will be making yogurt ($10). The only negative of the Instant Pot is you can't get a 10 quart and if I had a REALLY big family that would be the only reason, but based on the above, I would probably just buy a 2nd Instant Pot. I hope this is helpful. I did a lot of research and felt the need to share it. I will update this as I use it and get additional questions. 8/9/2017 update - I've been using my IP for a few months now. I use my steamer basket and trivet a lot. I make a "bowl" out of heavy duty foil and put on the trivet when making a whole chicken and it makes trivet clean-up easier. I bought an IP plain glass lid for slow cooker & yogurt mode. I don't use my extra rings cause I use my plain lid for yogurt, so no use to swap rings. I didn't get the silicone mitts. I realized I didn't need them. My inner pot doesn't get that hot on yogurt mode. I like the 2 cookbooks. I use Bar Keeper Friend to clean the pot. Still really happy with my IP-DUO Plus 60. I'm part of a FB PC group and I don't see complaints on the IP. Very happy with my purchase. 12/29/2017 update - So on Black Friday I bought the 3 qt Instant Pot because I felt like I need to have twins. It's a great size and great for sides and especially my 2 quart of yogurt I make at least weekly, so it doesn't tie up my 6 qt IP. We winter in FL and I was able to "sneak" the 6 qt into the truck and now I have the 3 qt here too. I made an entire Thanksgiving dinner for Christmas (Irma got in our way last month repairing) in the 2 pots. In future years, I'll prob just bring the 3 qt cause it fits better in my cabinets in the mobile home.

review_title: Pretty good, but saute stew meat on the stove or in small batches.
body_en: Am pleased overall with functionality and ease of use. Couple things to consider if you're on the fence: This relates to the saute feature only: if you're sauteing anything more than a medium onion or trying to brown a decent amount of cubed stew meat you should probably fire up a pan instead (or brown in smaller batches). It gets hot enough but seems to struggle STAYING hot enough and you'll risk overcooking whatever you're trying to brown. After you pressure cook a savory meal the lid gasket retains the smell so strongly that you'll think you forgot to wash the lid. Consider swapping the spare gasket (included) for sweet/rice type dishes. I've only had my instapot for a couple weeks so there might be a better way to deal with this. Otherwise it's a pretty solid purchase!

review_title: Instant Pot Duo Plus: Multifunctional Electric Pressure Cooker for Fast and Easy Cooking
body_en: The Instant Pot Duo Plus is one of those appliances that truly makes life easier in the kitchen. It combines several functions in one appliance: pressure cooker, slow cooker, rice cooker, steamer, yogurt maker, sauté function, sterilizer, and even sous vide cooking. This allows you to prepare a wide variety of recipes without needing multiple utensils.
This Instant pot is great. The size is perfect for cooking for 6 people. I love the stainless steel pot and it has all the functions I need. Very secure and easy to use. Love it!

The Instant Pot Duo Plus has completely transformed the way I cook! Having nine appliances in one saves so much counter space, and it makes preparing meals faster and more convenient than ever. Whether I'm pressure cooking soups and stews, slow cooking, steaming vegetables, making rice, or even preparing yogurt, it consistently delivers excellent results. The controls are intuitive, and the preset programs make it easy to cook a wide variety of meals with minimal effort. I especially appreciate how quickly it cooks while still producing tender, flavorful dishes. The stainless steel inner pot is durable, easy to clean, and holds up well with regular use. The build quality is excellent, and the safety features provide extra peace of mind while pressure cooking. Overall, this multicooker is a fantastic investment for busy households or anyone who enjoys cooking with less time and effort. It's versatile, reliable, and one of the most useful appliances in my kitchen. Highly recommended!

review_title: Outstanding and Informative Instant Pot Demo by Suman from hyderbad
body_en: I recently had the pleasure of attending an incredible Instant Pot demo by Suman, and I must say, it was an exceptional experience! Even though it was conducted through a video call, Suman's professionalism and expertise shone through, leaving me thoroughly informed and eager to start cooking with my Instant Pot. From the very beginning, Suman exuded enthusiasm and passion for the subject matter. His friendly demeanor and clear communication style made it easy to follow along and grasp the essential concepts. He began by introducing himself and setting the agenda for the session, ensuring that we knew exactly what to expect. Throughout the demonstration, Suman showcased an impressive depth of knowledge about the Instant Pot. He not only explained its various features and functions but also provided practical tips and tricks to make the most out of this versatile kitchen appliance. His step-by-step instructions were easy to understand, and he patiently answered all our questions, never rushing or making us feel hesitant to ask. One aspect that truly stood out during the session was Suman's attention to detail. He paid careful attention to every aspect of the Instant Pot, from proper handling to recommended cooking times for different dishes. He also emphasized safety precautions, ensuring that we understood how to use the Instant Pot responsibly and avoid any potential hazards. By the end of the demo, I felt confident and inspired to explore the vast array of recipes and possibilities with my Instant Pot. Suman's expertise and professional approach left a lasting impression, and I am grateful for the invaluable knowledge he shared during the session. Thank you, Suman, for the outstanding demonstration – you've made me an Instant Pot enthusiast! Overall, I rate Suman's Instant Pot demo with a resounding five stars!

I was about to buy a slow cooker when the instant pot came across my search and after reading a lot about it on the internet, I decided to spend a little more than I had planned and bought it. And I don't regret it! The pot is simply wonderful, especially for someone like me, who works outside the home and has a husband and two children to feed. It is not that the instant pot is faster than a conventional pressure cooker, since like any pressure cooker, you have to wait for it to reach the appropriate pressure, then there is the cooking time and then the depressurization to be able to open it, but the BIG difference is that since it can be programmed you simply forget about it and you don't have to keep an eye on anything, which for someone with a lot of activities is a magnificent help. It has many functions (pressure cooking, slow cooking, rice, grains, steam, sauté, yogurt, sterilize, etc.) and the instructions come in English, French and Spanish. It is very easy to use and clean, as well as being incredibly quiet. The recipe book it contains is very, very basic, but on the internet you can find a lot of super simple recipes, and on Amazon you can find recipes in books and Ebooks at very reasonable prices. A month after purchasing it, I already cooked rice, chicken, vegetables, meat, oatmeal, rice pudding in it with very satisfactory results and very easy. Give it a chance, you're really going to love it. Update: After using the pot for 3 months, I am still very satisfied with my purchase, it cooks super easily in it and above all without taking care of anything. The only thing against it that I find is that the packaging ring that comes with the lid keeps the smell of what you cooked. No matter what you wash them with, it will keep the smell. Although that is not a problem for cooking, you will not want to prepare oatmeal or vegetables if the packaging smells like chicken or meat. The solution I see is to buy one or two replacement packages and use them for different types of food, maybe one for sweet things, another for savory things, and another for dairy products.

It's one of those things like cell phones, microwaves, the internet that you wonder, "how could I exist for so long without it?" It makes life much easier in the kitchen and is very easy to understand and use. I am an elderly person and I don't like having to learn new techniques but it is very easy to use. I bought the mini 3 quart Duo Pot which is more than enough for my husband and I. The truth is, don't hesitate to buy one. I am so happy and pleased with this purchase.

review_title: Tamaño adecuado para cocinar para dos personas.
body_en: I have another one that is just as big and I like it a lot. I bought the smaller version for a small trailer and with this I feel prepared to cook a wide variety of foods.

review_title: I've used these for well over 15 years and have loved every minute.
body_en: If you have never used these before and are looking for a pot that cooks just about anything in less than it would normally on the stovetop, take the leap. I did so many years ago. My reason for getting this in the first place way back when was because I used to make rice everyday. After several expensive rice makers, they all had the same thing in common after a year or so. The non stick pot inside would start to peel away and to replace these was almost the price of what the Instant Pot was at the time. So the NUMBER ONE REASON I bought Instant pot in the first place was for the Stainless Steel pot on the inside. Amazing, and I pray that they don't turn to the non stick pots ever. I know that some of the other products they have do have the non stick pots, like in the air fryers. I do have an air fryer with the non stick and I am not happy about that, but I love the fryer aspect of it. There you have it folks, as a general rule of thumb, I tend to replace electronic cookware after about 10-15 years. I use these almost every single day, so I am very pleased with the company. Customer Service is also very responsive, so all in all a good choice. Real bang for your buck!

This cookbook is a great resource for anyone new to the Instant Pot. The recipes are easy to follow, well-organized, and use simple ingredients that are easy to find. I like that it includes a wide variety of meals, from quick everyday dishes to more complete options. The instructions are clear and make cooking with a pressure cooker feel much easier and more approachable. Overall, a very helpful guide for beginners.

review_title: ​"This cookbook is a lifesaver for beginners!
body_en: The instructions are incredibly clear, making pressure cooking feel effortless. With over 2,000 days of variety, I never run out of healthy meal ideas. The recipes are mouthwatering and actually save me time in the kitchen. It’s a complete guide that has truly mastered the art of easy, delicious home cooking. Highly recommended!"
I am fascinated by this book. Every single Saturday I am doing something different and easy for my whole family.
Súper rico
Set it and forget it. I can fold laundry while dinner cooks on its own.
Was not a good looking book. Don't waste your money
Clear instructions and tons of recipes. My Instant Pot finally gets daily use.
Cheap ingredients, minimal food waste. Saves me money on groceries every week.

review_title: Perfect Mini Multi-Cooker for Everyday Meals
body_en: I absolutely love this Instant Pot! The 4-quart size is perfect for small families or meal prep, and it doesn’t take up much counter space. It heats up quickly, cooks food evenly, and the 7-in-1 functions make it incredibly versatile. The controls are simple to use, and cleanup is fast thanks to the nonstick inner pot. It’s a stylish, reliable appliance that has made cooking much easier. Highly recommended!

I like the shape of this one and the death of this one much better than my old 3 quart instant pot let me explain. The old 3 quart mini instant pot was taller and smaller around. So if you’re a person that had a six or an 8 quart instant pot you had to re-buy all of your accessories. And I am in process of downsizing. I gave away my big six and my eight cord instant pots in favor of just having one smaller one and I chose the Rio. It’s is big around as the six and 8 quarts, but it’s not nearly as deep so it’s not as deep as the other instant pot mini design which I don’t think is available anymore I’m not sure this one is bigger around so it’s easier to get a chicken in there a whole chicken And maybe a little bit of carrot and vegetables. Don’t go over the line inside, but it’s much easier at least with your liquid. It works OK see if your chicken wing is sticking up or the very top of the breast, but it doesn’t work for the liquid to go up any higher than the line in there so be sure and note that because that will be a difference, but it holds 4 quarts in total so you should be fine but so far everything that I have made in it. I have been happy with and I like the ease of being able to put a small roast or a whole chicken in there without stuffing it up on its side or something like that I like to put it in the correct way so that it comes out easier. This is the second one of these Rios that I bought. I gave the first one away because someone came and wished they had one and they were in a situation that I think it could’ve been quite helpful so I gave them my first one and now I got one of these brand new beautiful white ones just very pretty.

review_title: Instant Pot (nombre de la marca) * Electric pressure cooker (olla de
body_en: I honestly didn’t expect to love this Instant Pot as much as I do. It has made cooking so much easier and faster for my family. The wide design is perfect because I can cook larger meals without everything feeling crowded. I’ve made rice, soups, stews, and even yogurt, and everything comes out delicious every time. The controls are simple to use, it heats up quickly, and cleanup is super easy. If you’re looking for a versatile, high-quality multicooker that saves time and delivers great results, this is definitely worth it. I highly recommend it!

I absolutely love this Instant Pot! The 4-quart size is perfect for one or two people. It doesn't take up much space on my countertop, but it's still big enough to cook a full meal. Before this one, I used a 6-quart Instant Pot to make bone broth. It worked great, but I actually prefer this smaller size. Now I can make fresh, smaller batches two or three times a week instead of one big batch. For some reason, it just feels so much better, and I enjoy having freshly made broth more often. It's very easy to use, and I love how versatile it is. I've already used the pressure cooker, sauté, and slow cook functions, and everything has turned out great. The stainless steel inner pot is also very easy to clean, which is a big plus. It also looks really nice on the counter. The Sea Salt color is simple and modern, and the compact size makes it easy to store or move around if needed. If you're looking for an Instant Pot that doesn't take over your kitchen but still does everything you need, I highly recommend this one. It has been a fantastic purchase!

I am so happy with my Instant Pot RIO Mini 7-in-1. It has quickly become one of my favorite kitchen appliances. The 4-quart size is perfect for small families, couples, or meal prep. I love how versatile it is—it works as a pressure cooker, slow cooker, rice cooker, steamer, sauté pan, yogurt maker, and food warmer all in one. Everything I’ve cooked has turned out great, from rice and beans to soups and tender meats. It saves me so much time, and cleanup is incredibly easy. The controls are simple to use, even for someone new to pressure cooking. If you’re looking for a compact, reliable, and multifunctional cooker, I highly recommend this one. It has made cooking faster, easier, and more enjoyable. Pros: ✔️ Perfect size for everyday use ✔️ Easy to operate ✔️ Cooks food quickly and evenly ✔️ Multiple cooking functions ✔️ Easy to clean Rating: 5/5 Stars – Highly Recommended!

review_title: Nice Instant Pot With a Couple of Drawbacks
body_en: PROS: 1) Aesthetically pleasing appearance in my upgraded light kitchen, much prettier than my other black and stainless Instant Pots. Even the panel is mostly white. Color is a soft white or very light off white, not stark white which I was hoping for. 2) Much quieter than my other 3 and 6 quart Instant Pots. No loud obnoxious beeps. 3) The release button is on the front of the lid rather than next to the pressure release spout making it much much safer to use. 4) The glass lid from my 6 quart Instant Pot unit fits this container so they are interchangeable. A huge plus since the unit doesn’t come with a cover for refrigeration. 5) I love the wider shorter bowl which makes it easier to cook and serve. 6) I like that it has both high and low temperature settings for Slow Cook unlike my 3 quart Instant Pot. CONS: 1) Cord is cheap and flimsy, nothing like the more substantial 3 pronged cord on my other Instant Pot units. This was a huge downgrade. And it’s black, an eyesore on this otherwise very pretty unit. Should have used a better quality white cord. review_title: Interesting Recipes, but Not a Strong Cookbook
body_en: I had a hard time deciding what to make of this book because I genuinely liked many of the recipes, but I do not think it works particularly well as a cookbook. The ebook version, at least, jumps into the recipes without much of an introduction or any meaningful explanation of Instant Pot cooking. Even if a cookbook is not specifically aimed at beginners, I still expect some basic guidance about the equipment, settings, timing, and common techniques. The recipes themselves are often appealing, but many are too simplified. They give you the basic idea without enough detail to make me feel confident that the finished dish will turn out exactly as intended. I appreciated that every recipe includes a picture, but the images did not work for me. Many look overly artificial, and some do not appear to match the actual recipe. For example, a recipe calling for a bone-in turkey breast is paired with an image that appears to show a boneless one. That kind of mismatch makes the visual guidance much less useful. What is missing most is personality. This feels like a collection of recipes rather than a thoughtfully constructed cookbook. There is very little context, technique, voice, or guidance to make it feel special. The saving grace is the recipes themselves. There is a surprisingly interesting range of dishes, and quite a few sound genuinely worth trying. That variety is what brought the book up to a middle rating for me. To be honest, parts of this cookbook frustrated me more than I expected, but there are still enough promising recipes here that I would try several of them.

review_title: Durable non-stick pot and features that other models at this price don't have
body_en: While this is a pretty standard pressure cooker for this price point, I chose this one because most don't have a sous vide function. Overall I am happy with it. I have a higher end brand at home, but purchased this during an extended stay with family and it's been perfect in that context. So far I have not noticed a big difference between this model and the name brand. In at least one respect, this model is better. The non-stick pot seems far more durable than the name brand. I haven't been careful with this pot, and in a few weeks of heavy use (like once a day), there's no discoloration or dinging through the non-stick coating. As noted, it has a sous vide function. Don't sleep on this, getting pre-marinated meat at the market and popping it in the water bath without even opening the packaging is incredibly nice; the meat turns out great, it's incredibly forgiving, and there's zero clean-up. It's particularly choice for dinner parties where everyone hangs out beforehand and you want to be able to serve hot food as soon as everyone sits down. Only down side compared to a standalone sous vide is that you're limited to the area of the pot (though the pot is big so it fits most jobs), and the time to heat the water is long compared to the standalone. A few minor quibbles: the yogurt function is not great.. There is no built-in boil function, so that must be done independently. I had been very happy with the name brand version, as there is very little scalding, which is the big down side of doing it stove-top. You can use the saute function to boil in this model, but you have to babysit it more. The non-stick pot does a pretty good job of avoiding scalding but I don't trust it enough to walk away like you can with other models. Given no boil feature, the Comfee basically holds the milk to the yogurt temperature. That means you have to have a thermometer to test the temp yourself prior to adding the cultures, or risk killing them. Other models self-regulate and let you know when you can add the cultures. You also cannot easily add time if you check the yogurt and it's still too runny. A minor issue, but a surprising one. I'll still use this to make yogurt, but I'm guessing the sous vide function is a better way to do the post-boiling steps. Second, the manual is pretty worthless. The model works like most pressure cookers, but the buttons are not quite consistent with other brands ("Level" is not the best choice of description). So, I wouldn't give this model to, e.g., my mother who's never used a pressure cooker before, as it would likely be too confusing. I'm a frequent user of other models and have been for years, and I even found it a little less clear than I'd like. On top of this, unlike name brands, there is no real quick start guide or recipe book. Not an issue for me, but might be for some. Third, the pressure valve is a little subtle and a little spitty(?) It always takes me a second to feel out which way is sealed and which is open, as the markings are faint and the rise between the two is subtle. Fancier models either make this really clear, or automatically seal when you close the lid. The valve on this feels very old school. And because the release is manual (turning the valve by hand rather than sliding a button, e.g.), it requires more care to quick release the pressure without burning yourself. The release spigot tends to spit a little, so I find I need to be very careful. On other models, I would trust my pre-teen kid to be able to use it without any worry, but for this model, I'd be worried they'd hurt themselves from carelessness. Finally, the choice of included extras is a little unusual: a rice cup (3/4 cup, as you'd get with a rice cooker), a rice paddle, a deep serving spoon, and a trivet. I didn't notice markings inside the bowl that show how much water you add per rice cup serving, so I'm not entirely sure why the rice cup. The rice paddle is an unexpected positive, though I suspect most people who are frequent rice eaters probably already have one that came with a rice cooker. Still, perhaps a good thing for college students or others who have limited space for small kitchen appliances who may actually use this as a rice cooker. I do like the included spoon, as I keep it in the pot when not in use and thus always have it for serving directly from the cooker. The fact that it's right there is a good way to never use metal on the non-stick surface. All that said, the durability of the pot is a much bigger deal than the minor negatives, all of which can be worked around. At this price point, the features and build seem on par with more expensive models, other than the throwback valve.

review_title: I guess I like kitchen gadgets now...
body_en: I was always pretty anti-kitchen gadgets. The InstantPot seemed like just another thing that did stuff I could already do on my stove or oven. Boy, was I wrong. I honestly am in disbelief how much I love using this thing. It is so versatile that I use it more than anything else in my kitchen, except maybe the sink. The reasons why? Well, for starters it’s super easy to clean. Instead of making a mess with multiple pans and pots and lids with food stuff splattering everywhere, the InstantPot is one thing that’s fully contained. When the timer ends I take out the food, clean the pot, and wipe down the lid and little “gutter” and that’s it. Two, it’s so FAST! Now, granted some things will feel like they take the same or similar amount of time when pressure cooking because the machine has to build pressure. BUT, the difference is that I can set this and LEAVE! When it’s ready it beeps and I can choose to keep the food warm or have it stop cooking when the timer is done. What really sold me on finally purchasing this is the air fryer attachment. I’ve been wanting an air fryer so this was much cheaper than buying everything separately. I will say that while I do love the air fryer it’s probably not the best on the market. When using a two-tiered basket, whatever is in the top portion *will* be more cooked than the bottom. This is a problem I will try to fix by simply removing the top portion when it’s cooked and letting the bottom cook longer until it’s done. Not ideal, but for delicious air fried food ans the convenience of having these capabilities from one machine at this price, I’ll make do. I recommend purchasing an InstantPot cookbook to accompany this. It will help acquaint you to how this machine can be used, even if the cookbook is more oriented towards one of the models without the air fryer. What do I use this for? So far I’ve made vegan chana masala (yum!), vegan banana bread (yum!), air fried Brussels sprouts (yum!), truffle fries (you get the idea). I’ve also used this to steam food to make dog food for my pup with allergies. One of my favorite things to use this for is dry goods!! I will dump a whole bag of dry beans or quinoa or whatever in the pot, add spices, water, set it, and it’s done to perfection so quickly! I’ll then can everything and freeze it so I have beans and quinoa on hand all the time whenever I need them for a meal! It’s the best! Not to mention the pressure cooker seems to really INFUSE whatever you’re cooking with the spices you choose. The beans I’ve made with this I’ve eaten plain they were so so tasty! I live with roommates but this has been the best purchase ever. I’m lucky to have the room to store it, but it’s also great because they can cook on the stove or in the oven if they want, and I have everything I need right in this InstantPot so no one has to wait on anyone to clear out before they can do their own thing. Things I wish it did differently: - I wish the display showed seconds. Minor inconvenience but the display in general makes it feel cheap. - I wish the display showed what setting it was on and what action it was currently doing. For example, a small icon for “pressure cooking” so you can remember that you chose the correct setting. Or a little icon that showed it was building pressure so you don’t think you didn’t hit “start” or something before waking away. Also, something that showed the current temperature inside instead of what you set it to so you know how things are cooking or heating up/cooling down. - A persistant beep every minute or so when food is finished cooking.

body_en: I bought this as a beginner’s guide to using my Instant Pot, and it has been a helpful introduction. The recipes are straightforward, the ingredients are easy to find, and the instructions are simple enough to follow without feeling overwhelmed. I especially liked that it covers a variety of meals, from soups and stews to meats, vegetables, and desserts, so there’s plenty to try. That said, it isn’t perfect. Some recipes are fairly basic, and experienced Instant Pot users may find them too simple. A few dishes also needed a little extra seasoning to suit my taste, but that’s easy to adjust. Overall, it’s a good cookbook if you’re new to pressure cooking and want reliable, uncomplicated recipes to build your confidence. It’s a practical starting point and has already given me several meals I’ll make again.

review_title: Great Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners
body_en: I’m really enjoying The Latest Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners. It’s a great option if you’re new to using an Instant Pot and want plenty of recipe ideas to get started. I especially like that it offers a large variety of recipes, so it doesn’t feel like you’re making the same few meals over and over. The recipes are easy to follow and make using the Instant Pot feel much less intimidating. Having a cookbook with so many different meal options is also helpful when you’re trying to plan meals for the family or simply want to try something different. The book is nicely organized and makes a good addition to the kitchen. I also appreciate that the recipes cover different types of dishes, which gives you plenty of choices depending on what you're in the mood for. Overall, I think this is a useful cookbook for anyone who has recently purchased an Instant Pot or wants more ideas for using one. It would also make a nice gift for someone who enjoys cooking but wants to save time in the kitchen. Definitely worth having if you’re looking for a variety of Instant Pot recipes in one place.

I’m very happy with this cookbook! The recipes are easy to follow, making it perfect for beginners and anyone looking to get more out of their Instant Pot. I like that it includes a wide variety of meals, from quick weeknight dinners to hearty comfort foods. The instructions are clear, the ingredients are easy to find, and the recipes have turned out great so far. It’s an excellent value for the price and has already given me plenty of new meal ideas. I definitely recommend it to anyone who wants simple, delicious Instant Pot recipes.

review_title: A Simple and Helpful Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners
body_en: If you’re just getting started with an Instant Pot, this cookbook makes things really easy to understand. It’s a great guide for beginners who want to learn how to cook simple and tasty meals without feeling confused about how the appliance works. The book explains things in a clear and friendly way, so even someone using an Instant Pot for the first time can follow along. The recipes are simple and practical, with a mix of everyday meals and a few more interesting dishes to try. Each recipe has easy steps that are not complicated, which makes cooking less stressful and more enjoyable. You’ll find different kinds of meals in the book, including soups, meat dishes, grains, and even desserts, so there’s something for different tastes. One of the best things about this cookbook is how it focuses on making cooking easier and faster. It shows how the Instant Pot can help you prepare good meals without spending too much time in the kitchen. The recipes are designed to be straightforward while still giving you meals that taste really good. Overall, it’s a helpful cookbook for anyone who wants to start using their Instant Pot and cook simple, satisfying meals at home.
Lots of recipes but I would have liked the pictures in colour
Instant Black and White. Would have been better with colour photographs. Reason for 4 stars
I’ve been using this for quick weeknight meals, and it cooks everything evenly. The app recipes are helpful, and having so many cooking functions in one appliance saves both time and counter space.

review_title: I like that the app has a "Timed Venting" option
body_en: Updated 12/29/24 - My Instant Pot timed venting wish has finally come true, so I just changed my rating to five stars. They added a new app option when timed venting is selected, so now you can choose the amount of time you want to vent the pot. It takes the guessing game out of using the timed venting feature. It's the addition I have been hoping for ever since they added timed venting to the app. Updated 9/27/24: They just added a new notification feature to the app and I really like it. You get a push status notification when the pressure cooker starts preheating, then moves to the cooking cycle, then goes into venting mode and when it completes the venting cycle. It's particularly helpful to get notified when it goes into the venting process in case you want to precisely time the venting based on what you are cooking. It's a helpful enhancement. Original review - I have an older model 6 QT Instant Pot Pro and I wanted this new one for its ability to connect to wifi, so I can use the app to control it. I especially like that the app has an extra venting option that is not available on the panel of the Instant Pot itself. It's a "Timed" option (see photo) that I actually discovered by accident when I was programming a cooking cycle. It's not explained anywhere in the documentation or even in the app, but it's very helpful when doing grains where I want it to natural release for a few minutes and then quickly finish the release without manual intervention. This is where the "Timed" option comes in. It seems to kick in about five to seven minutes after natural release starts. It varies, maybe based on how full the pot is, but since there's no documentation, it's just a guess on my part. It works great because I can be anywhere in the house and not have to rush to my kitchen to manually change the venting to quick release. I really love being able to monitor the progress from my iPhone and see when it has finished whatever cycle I've chosen. The cooking pot itself is different than my older model. It has two handles on it so it makes lifting the hot pot out of the unit so easy. I also like that it automatically seals itself when you lock the lid. No more manually turning a small knob from venting to sealing. That makes it foolproof. It cooks the same way as my older model, but these new options make it my preferred pot. It doesn't have as many preprogrammed settings as my older model, but I never really used those anyway. I like to use the standard pressure cook option and choose the cooking times and the pressure and venting levels myself. I took one star off because "Timed Venting" is not a feature on the unit and it's not explained in any documentation, but it's offered as a feature in the app. I think they need to point that out somewhere and not leave it up to consumers to find it by accident or have to guess to see how it works.

review_title: Techies like us, love having Bluetooth accessibility! Great InstantPot!
body_en: Our original InstantPot just "bit the dust." We LOVED having it and it produced many, many wonderful memories meals for us. While we mourned the passing of our "Old Faithful" InstantPot, I decided to start researching other electric pressure cookers and again, we came back to InstantPot and wanted to see what options they had. After reading all of the reviews and articles on this particular model, I told my wife 'PLEASE, PLEASE get me this one for Christmas!" She said, you can go ahead and order it but you're not allowed to open it until Christmas! Like anyone, I said YES!!!! I opened it and then downloaded the app being that it is Bluetooth compatible. I cannot tell you enough, what a pleasant surprise it was, to see just how easy it was to set up and connect via our home WiFi. I can now use the app to set the time, the release time, etc. It's amazingly friendly to use and works great. One thing I will tell you is that if you, like me, use the Saute' mode, to first brown meat, you can NOT start hte InstantPot in this mode via the app. You must physically hit the start button in order to have the Saute' mode come on. Yes, you can set it up in the app but cannot physically start the InstantPot in this particular mode. I know I"m repating myself but I want to make sure that everyone understands this. To me, it's a safety feature and I can appreciate why it's done this way. The last thing you want to do is to accidently have your InstantPot start in this mode while you're away or remote. PROS: Excellent quality, every time I turn it on, it immediately conects to the WiFi and can be accessed via the app CONS: None noted at the time of this review.

There are a ton of youtube videos, showing you not only how to use it but how to make one pot dinners. It's easy to use, wifi is easy to set up which afterwards connects whether you are using the app or not, to show remaining cooking time. I only have basic cooking skills, so I prefer to watch the youtube videos for recipes than the app for now. Food prep always takes the longest, but once you have everything ready, put the food in, close the lid, set the time and wait for it to finish. When you set a time according to a recipe, that is the actual Pressure Cooking time. The unit has to preheat before Pressure Cooking time begins, and that's several minutes depending on the model. Then the unit has to vent the pressure (choice of Natural, Pulse, or Quick Vent.) Be careful with Quick Vent as it may make some meats tougher than if you simply waited for the Natural vent process. If you enable push notifications, it will tell you when preheating has ended and cooking has begun, and of course when cooking has ended and venting has begun (you'll likely hear the venting process from the next room. Everything but the base is dishwasher safe on the top rack, BUT, you should use a milder soap like when washing by hand, not the regular somewhat harsh dishwasher soap. The stainless steel pot didn't come quite as clean as it should have, so a little scrubbing in the sink made it bright again. You could always wash it with your regular dishwasher load (but not the other parts (lid, sealing ring, some small vent parts.) I'm pleased with my purchase and have planned a whole week of cooking meals in it. I'm currently using a simple recipe of chicken, onions, honey, soy sauce, and garlic. Smells good.

review_title: Connectivity problems at first but resolved now and great product

If not, this is sadly being returned. Lots of nice upgrade features from my very old instant pot so I will be sad if I have to return it. review_title: Better Features than Older Models - But Several Important Differences
body_en: This is my second instant pot. My IP Ultra model recently died so I had to upgrade. Here are several important differences from previous models: 1) The inner pot has two hand holders - this is great because the previous models would swirl around when stirring. This new version prevents that from happening. 2) The cord is not removable - not a huge deal, but wondering why they would make this change. The cord is located in the back left corner. So plugging into an outlet on the back right made for a strange bend in the cord. Wondering why they can't simply place the cord in the back middle. Not a deal breaker for me, but you should be aware of it. 3) Steam valve: this works a bit differently than other models. No way to manually vent or release steam. It has to be done through the control panel. It is possible to change the setting mid-stream, but there is a delay of a few seconds once you input on the control panel. 4) Older IP accessories may not work - I used to do Pot-in-Pot cooking with a 2 level PIP on top of a trivet. This worked fine in my Instant Pot Ultra. But the first time I tried it in my IP Pro Plus, the pin got stuck, and the lid locked closed. I couldn't open it because the pin needed room to clear. I managed to figure a way out to open it by turning the pot upside down. But this new IP seems to have a slightly lower clearance. So you'll have to use a shorter trivet, or a shorter PIP. Otherwise your lid may get stuck in locked mode. The bluetooth/wireless feature seems nice, but I tend to use the pot while I'm at home anyway. So I'm not sure how helpful it will be over time. But you do have the ability to turn on the IP while you're away from home. It involves downloading an app and connecting your IP to the wifi. The phone app gives notifications when the pre-heating is done, so thats a nice feature. The other main reason I bought this was because of the pressure canning. You can fit up to 4 quart size mason jars to can food. This is really nice. Because of its higher temperature/pressure abilities, this IP can theoretically cook food faster vs older models. I haven't tried it out yet. They also have a feature called "Nutriboost". This is simply a feature where the IP lets out steam periodically. Food in the inner pot then gets agitated. If this is done periodically throughout, then the food gets stirred. Its good for things like risotto and dhals where you want a smooth consistency. Its a nice feature but the name is a little misleading -- nothing about this boosts nutrition. It is simply a fancy way to stir your food while pressure cooking.

UPDATE: Received replacement and it's the WRONG (older model with fewer features) in the box! This is insanity. Our previous Instapot died 3 days ago, and we needed another before Thanksgiving. The new one clearly arrived in a VERY used condition. Looks like someone cooked a few meals in it, then used it as a bowling ball. Shame on the manufacturer store for trying to pass this off as new. Returning immediately. Update 2: The replacement pot was in the correct box, but had a different Instant Pot in it. The ouside of the box very clearly says Instant Pot, and the device inside also is an instant pot, the same model as our old one but not the upgraded version we bought. Contacted Instant Pot directly to see what can be done about getting the WRONG item in the RIGHT box. Their incredibly lame and disappointing response is "We don't sell that" I can find the exact same model we ordered on their website. The one they "don't sell" Final update: Contacted Amazon and explained the situation. They immediately refunded our money (thank you). We ordered again without much hope. To our surprise, the package that arrived today was the correct pot in the correct box finally Buyer beware, the device itself is fantastic but if your box comes with tape all over it you probably didn't get what you ordered. I am leaving this at 1 star because Instant Pot customer servicw was absolutley abyssmal and refused to even try to correct the situation. I would buy from a local appliance store vs. online because of this...getting what we ordered has been a lot of uneccesary drama. The pot itself can be reviewed now: The set in handles that keep the pot from spinning around while you sautee are fantastic. They fit firmly in place and make lifting the pot out easy. The liner pot is MUCH higher quality than the regular instant pots. The disc bottom is thicker than the original pots, and fully 3 ply clad, and it shows. There is no convex in the center of the bottom so you can keep food where you want it. The steam release is variable and no touch. The 3 setting options are great and require much less attention/timer setting. It is also MUCH quieter than previous models. The Keep Warm setting can now be used as a reheat setting, with a high, medium, low and custom temp. The Nutriboost setting is useful for gently shaking the pot while cooking to help blend better and keep food from sticking to the bottom initially. The buld seems very sturdy, very pleased over all with the additional features and functions of this pot. Would recommend, but suggest buying in person to avoid getting scammed.

I had an old Instant Pot duo for two years and I loved using it, I ended up getting this one because of the canning feature on it and I’m absolutely obsessed! The app works amazing with it it cans my beans beautifully genuinely love this Instant Pot! I think my friends are getting tired of hearing me. Talk about Instant Pot cooking. review_title: Pleasantly Surprised after I decided to Ignore a negative review.
body_en: Instant Pot Pro Plus Exceeds Expectations: I was initially hesitant to upgrade my old pressure cooker to the new Instant Pot Pro Plus, especially after reading a concerning review about its Wi-Fi connectivity and the company's financial troubles. However, after some research and a prompt response from Instant Brands' customer care, I decided to take the plunge when the price dropped again. Upon receiving the Instant Pot Pro Plus, I was delighted to find that my worries were unfounded. The Wi-Fi connectivity worked flawlessly after a bit of patience during the setup process, and the automatic venting and improved inner pot are significant improvements. Despite concerns raised about the company's financial situation and app issues in the June 17, 2023 review, I have not encountered any problems. Prior to purchase, I sent an email concerning the app issues and their rapid reply satisfied me that Instant Brands has addressed previous issues, and I am confident in they will support this product moving forward. It's worth noting that Instant Brands was purchased by affiliates of Centre Lane Partners in November 2023, which has likely contributed to the company's stability and product improvements. In conclusion, the Instant Pot Pro Plus has greatly impressed me with its performance and features. Don't let past concerns deter you—this appliance is worth every penny. (I did notice the price went up again after I ordered mine.) I am completely satisfied with my purchase and would highly recommend it to anyone in the market for a versatile and reliable pressure cooker.

I am a huge fan of the Ninja brand. I absolutely love my Ninja glass air fryer, so when I was looking for a new electric pressure cooker, I was torn between buying this Ninja model with its ceramic-coated interior (which is not the cheapest option on the market) or choosing a stainless-steel interior cooker from another brand. In the end, I decided to trust Ninja again, and I can honestly say I do not regret my decision. After using it for several weeks, I feel ready to share my experience. The Pressure Cook function is amazing. It can cook meals in about 10 minutes, which honestly seemed unbelievable to me at first. I have made beans, meats, and different dishes, and I was impressed by how quickly everything was ready while still maintaining great flavor and texture. I also love the Sear/Sauté function because it allows you to brown and sauté your ingredients before pressure cooking. After that, you simply switch to pressure cooking, and the results are delicious. I absolutely love this cooker and truly believe it is worth every penny I spent on it. The quality, versatility, and ease of use have exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable and high-quality multicooker.

Honestly, I was a bit worried because of the analysis of price vs features vs brand. However, I have had this now for... let me do math here... the root square of... add the cosene... and dividied by Saturn's PI... IDK... 2 months? I am super impressed! I generally use it for rice. but not just boring white rice. I make rice with beans, rice with meat, sticky rice, basmati rice... and I recently used the pressure-cooking feature. Only features that that are slightly annoying is that you have to press the one button a bunch of times until you get to the function you desire, and that I still have not figured out how to change the time once I engage the function. I happen to have some hook-like thingys that easily attach to the insert sides, but I wish they came with it. But that is it. I love this! Anyway, GREAT purchase. Obviously, I have used it quite enough.

review_title: a true culinary treasure for anyone
body_en: **The Ultimate Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners** is a true culinary treasure for anyone embarking on the Instant Pot journey. This cookbook masterfully combines ease of use with a delightful array of recipes, making it an indispensable resource for both novice and experienced cooks. From the outset, the book is incredibly user-friendly. The introduction provides a comprehensive overview of the Instant Pot, demystifying its functions and features. This is perfect for beginners who might feel overwhelmed by the appliance's versatility. Each recipe is meticulously laid out with clear, step-by-step instructions that make the cooking process straightforward and stress-free. The diversity of recipes is simply outstanding. Covering everything from hearty breakfasts to satisfying lunches, delectable dinners, tempting appetizers, and mouth-watering desserts, this cookbook ensures that you never run out of delicious ideas. The breakfast recipes, in particular, are a standout, transforming the most important meal of the day into an exciting culinary adventure. Lunchtime and dinner options are equally impressive, providing a wide range of flavors and ingredients that cater to all tastes and dietary preferences. One of the most commendable aspects of this cookbook is its focus on using fresh, wholesome ingredients. Each recipe is designed to maximize flavor while maintaining nutritional value, making it easier to eat healthily without compromising on taste. The appetizers and desserts chapters are particularly delightful, offering a variety of indulgent yet easy-to-prepare treats that are sure to impress family and friends. The vibrant photographs accompanying each recipe are both inspiring and helpful, offering a visual guide to the finished dish. This not only enhances the overall cooking experience but also makes the cookbook a joy to flip through. In conclusion, **The Ultimate Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners** is a must-have for anyone looking to explore the full potential of their Instant Pot. Its combination of easy-to-follow recipes, diverse meal options, and practical advice earns it a well-deserved five-star rating. This book truly makes everyday cooking a delightful and effortless experience. Highly recommended for anyone eager to transform their culinary skills!

review_title: Perfect for Quick and Easy Meals
body_en: For years I have been reluctant to purchase an Instant Pot. I am not quite sure why, other than being apprehensive that I would not be able to come up with enough ways to use it. When I was surprised with one as a gift, it made me realize it was time to come up with recipes my family would enjoy. When I saw the title of this book, The Ultimate Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners, by Jodi Gutierrez, I took the plunge and purchased it. I am rarely as impressed by a cookbook as I am this one. It does not just provide tons of recipes, but also a great guide on the Instant Pot Duo Mini too! One of my favorite things about this cookbook is that it includes a 4-week meal plan. If I were to want a stress-free month of breakfasts, lunches, dinners, and desserts, this would be perfect to follow. Even if you do not plan to use the Instant Pot every day, it makes it easier to meal plan for one day, a few days or a week at a time. Another thing I love is the wide variety of recipe options. My family loves variety so I am certain this book is going to enable me to keep every meal interesting. They also have quite the sweet tooth, so I am looking forward to treating them now and then to many unique desserts. I had heard about doing cheesecakes in the Instant Pot, but now I know I can do filled apples, doughnuts, lemon curd, pudding, and so much more. Ending reliance on boxed desserts is exactly what I wanted to do. With pudding taking just 5 minutes prep time and 15 minutes cook time using wholesome ingredients such as heavy cream, egg yoks, and whole milk, I can feel good about treating my family. Speaking about the prep and cook time, the recipes provide this information which is something I love. There is nothing worse than planning a meal at the last minute and finding out it takes hours longer than you expected. I do not know about your family, but mine does not appreciate waiting for dinner! The nutritional information per serving is also provided so you can cook based on your family’s dietary plan. The Ultimate Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners truly has something for everyone. Plenty of meat dishes, seafood, vegetable, breakfast, poultry, and more. Some of the first ones we will be trying are the healthy seafood gumbo, simple lemon octopus, teriyaki pork roast, simple Mongolian beef, Hawaiian pulled pork, and homemade chicken wings. I feel this book is going to be a game changer every day and especially during the holidays due to so many being perfect for pot lucks and family gatherings. You will not be disappointed if you get this cookbook.
Most recipes are usable and easy to make Book itself is poorly made

review_title: Not a quality book but good basics
body_en: This is a good Instant Pot Cookbook designed for the Instant Pot Duo. If you don’t have the Duo, don’t worry—the recipes all work. My initial reaction was one of surprise because all the recipes are in black and white, which was a bit disappointing. I prefer color recipes because I like to see the finished dish, and I believe color photos give a better sense of that. The book offers a wide range of dishes, from stews and casseroles to all the main proteins. It also includes a decent vegetarian selection, and you can easily swap ingredients without affecting the dish. Additionally, it features some simple dessert recipes. It covers essential fundamentals, which is helpful for beginners like myself. It’s a good purchase, but pairing it with a quality companion recipe book would be beneficial. Some Instant Pots come with an app, which I find to be very helpful. I haven’t used this book extensively yet, but it provides a solid foundation. The publisher and author could improve by investing in better photos of the recipes and printing in color. As a photographer, I believe those simple changes would lead to more positive reviews and possibly more sales. The overall quality, however, disappointed me.

I have been using this COSLUS electric toothbrush for theee months now and I’m genuinely impressed with what you get for the price. Best of all when you register the product you get a two-year warranty. First off, the cleaning performance is solid. It has a strong sonic vibration that leaves my teeth feeling smooth and clean, comparable to other higher end electric toothbrushes I have purchased in the past. It’s noticeably more effective than manual brushing, especially around the gumline. The battery life is another BIG win. I only charged it every 3-4 weeks. For travel or everyday use, that’s really convenient. It also comes with multiple brushing modes, which is nice to have depending on whether you want a deeper clean or something more gentle for sensitive gums. The build feels lightweight but not cheap and it’s easy to hold even when wet. The included 6 brush heads are a good bonus and they seem easy enough to replace when needed. Charging is simple with the included base and everything feels straightforward with no complicated setup or app required. If I had one minor complaint, it’s that it doesn’t have the “smart” features or premium feel of much more expensive brands like Sonicare or Oral-B. But honestly, at this price point, that’s expected and not a dealbreaker for me. Overall, If you are looking for an affordable electric toothbrush that does the job well without unnecessary extras, this is a great pick. It’s an excellent balance of performance and value and with a two-year warranty, why not?

This sonic toothbrush arrived in a sleek, well-designed travel case that immediately stood out. The case holds two brush heads (one for current use and one individually wrapped spare), and what really impressed me is the built-in ventilation. If you’re someone who brushes in the shower (🙋🏽‍♀️), this detail is huge. Bonus: the toothbrush itself is fully waterproof, so no concerns there. The toothbrush is lightweight, slim, and comfortable to hold, making it feel more premium than bulkier electric brushes I’ve used. It features a 2-minute smart timer with 30-second quadrant pauses, which helps ensure even cleaning throughout the mouth. One feature I genuinely appreciate: if you stop mid-cycle—say, to sign for a delivery—the brush resumes exactly where you left off when you turn it back on. That level of thoughtful design doesn’t go unnoticed. There are 5 distinct cleaning modes, and with each mode change there is a noticeable change in brushing pattern, particularly through the blue bristles and angled top bristles. The toothbrush overall is well designed and aligns comfortably with both teeth and gums, providing a thorough yet gentle clean. The brush head shape feels intentional, not generic. COSLUS includes 6 brush heads, which equals approximately 18 months of use based on the recommended 3-month replacement schedule—an excellent value and a big plus for long-term ownership. I’ve only just started using this toothbrush, so I can’t yet speak to battery longevity or how the blue indicator bristles fade over time. That said, I’ll be more than happy to provide an update after extended use. Overall, this toothbrush checks all the boxes: smart design, strong performance, thoughtful features, and great value. I’m excited to continue using it and would absolutely recommend it to anyone looking to upgrade their oral care routine. Great value and works WELL!

It is an amazing bargain. I have been using the product for only several weeks, but so far it runs as well as my very expenive electric toothbrush. Being that it comes with extra brushes it is an excellent price point for what, so far, is an excellent product.

review_title: A true Sonicare replacement but pulling the heads off takes serious grip strength
body_en: I finally refused to buy another $100 Philips Sonicare after my second one died exactly when the two-year warranty expired. I picked this COSLUS up at full price strictly because getting the handle a travel case and an 18-month supply of brush heads cost less than one pack of name-brand refills. I honestly expected a hollow rattling piece of cheap plastic. Instead the matte black handle has a solid weight to it and the motor delivers that intense high-pitched sonic hum that instantly foams up your toothpaste. After brushing twice a day for six weeks my teeth have that perfectly slick feeling you normally only get leaving the dentist chair. The battery performance is what really convinced me to keep it. I left the wireless charger in the box and haven't plugged this thing in once since day one. I even took it on two weekend work trips without the cord and the motor hasn't dropped a fraction of its power. It does the standard 30-second stutter to tell you to switch quadrants which is great for mindless early morning brushing. I am capping it at four stars for two very specific physical limitations. First the five cleaning modes change the rhythm of the brushing but you cannot adjust the actual intensity up or down. If the standard mode is too aggressive for your gums you just have to switch to the softer pulsating mode. Second the replacement heads lock onto the metal shaft so aggressively that taking them off requires an absurd amount of force. I actually had to wrap a hand towel around the brush head just to get enough grip to yank it off without snapping the plastic. If you have arthritis or hand mobility issues you should definitely skip this. But if you just want a reliable powerhouse of a toothbrush and don't mind wrestling with a piece of plastic every three months this is a massive steal.
