I love that it comes in beautiful colors (I got the sage green and LOVE it!) plus it comes with enough charge to get started on your clean teeth journey. It’s lightweight and just plain beautiful it feels so durable due to it being constructed out of aluminum much better than all those overpriced plastic electric toothbrushes and the bristles are soft enough to clean my teeth without damaging my gums. Perfection in my opinion glad I found this company so I can still use electronic toothbrush and have confidence that I am not adding to the garbage problem of the world.

review_title: Great clean and great for arthritic hands
body_en: This was bought to replace a sonicare that was on its last legs. I am extremely impressed with the build quality on this toothbrush, and how easy it is to push the buttons with arthritic hands. The brush heads are fairly soft, but the cleaning modes are very impressive. The first night I used it my teeth felt cleaner than they had in a long time. I also love the charging setup, as being able to replace the cord if it becomes damaged is ideal in my books. I have not needed to charge it yet as the battery was very charged from factory. I think this is a great alternative to a sonicare, and has the added bonus of being a bit more eco-friendly.
Love the toothbrush but the device that is supposed to clean the toothbrush doesn’t work. Battery died and the included charger will not charge the toothbrush cleaner

Sleek. Modern. Clean modes are great. Love the uv brush cleaning dock and timer. Vibration isn’t too much on your hand. Battery life is top notch. Durable. Size isn’t too large. Looks great on my counter. The dock it sits in is also very sleek and modern. Loved it so much. I bought two! 100% worth it.

I love this toothbrush. The head of it with the bristles I wish was a little bigger. Just typically cause I use my toothbrush to brush my tongue too and it’s just a little small for that. Otherwise, I love the UV light that’s easy to install.

review_title: Excellent for the price! Love the compost feature.
body_en: Love this toothbrush! I am the most excited about the sustainable and composting heads. The bristles do not fall off in your mouth like a lot of other brushes. We have been using ours for about a month. My teeth feel clean after brushing. A warning, it is a little intense but just takes some getting used to. Especially switching from a manual. I haven't hadbto charge thembyet. The replacement heads are very affordable but it already comes with 5 total heads. Definitely worth the price! I bought 3 total.
Love this toothbrush. Great price. No plastic bristles, and the uv cleaning add on is awesome as well. I said to my husband I swore my teeth felt the cleanest ever from brushing. Worth it!

review_title: I could be a new convert to sonic toothbrushing!
body_en: I've been a diehard round head electric toothbrush user for years, and I'm not very familiar with using a sonic one. But I wanted to give it a try and compare the "after brushing" feel between the two. My 1st impression, after admiring the high end look of the simple cardboard packaging, was that it appeared to be a no frills, easy to use electric toothbrush. Just one button does it all ~ on and off, as well as selecting which of the two speeds you want (gentle or deep clean). Simplicity rules, and I love that! None of that "3 long presses for this, or 5 short presses plus 1 long press for that." Just press ~ brush ~ go. Easy peasy! As directed, I charged it for a full 7 hrs before my first use. There's really no learning curve as it has many of the same features my round head electric toothbrush does, such as a short pulse to move on after 30 seconds. One thing that made me laugh ~ after 2 minutes, I wasn't expecting it to just completely shut down without warning. That's all, bye bye, time to go! lol I'm used to 4 short pulses saying you're finished, but it doesn't just shut down in mid-brush! The 28,000 vibrations per minute caused my nose to itch incessantly for the whole two minutes, but I hope that wouldn't be an issue once I got used to it. I like that this toothbrush is very lightweight, small-ish in size, has a nice wave-shaped brush head with medium-soft bristles, a 28 day battery life and an optional magnetic mount that I probably won't use. Also, and important to me, is that you can order brush head refills right from this site ~ no hunting around to find what you need. It's right here! Also , the whole plant-based description is very interesting to me. For example, the brush heads are made from cornstarch, and can be mailed back to the company after use for recycling. Kudos for that! There's info in the enclosed Quick Start Guide about where to send them. Bottom line: this little brush did what it's supposed to do, and I enjoyed how unique and different it was to use. My mouth felt totally refreshed, and I think it probably did a better job of plaque removal than my round head toothbrush does. For all these reasons, I could easily be converted to sonic toothbrushing!

review_title: Vendor gets an A+ for helpfulness.
body_en: When I received my SURI NEW Core Sonic Electric Toothbrush I was pleasantly surprised by the good build quality and attention to detail. The magnetic charging base is a step up from my last toothbrush that had problems with water getting into the USB connection. Before I used it the first time I charged it up as described in the instruction sheet. But, I found it odd the instructions specify use of a 5V 1A power adapter. All of my 1 Amp power adapters have a USB-A output. So I used a USB-A power adapter with a little A to C converter I happened to have. This worked great. I asked the vendor about the limitations specified in the instructions. They responded quickly and courteously with the following answer. "Yes, you can use any USB-C charger from a trusted brand that is certified to the relevant safety standards in your country. The only requirement is that it uses USB-C; the charger’s rated voltage and current do not need to be exactly 5V/1A." So, we can plug it into any USB-C power adapter we have. Cool! As far as using it goes, no problems. Bristles are a bit softer than I usually use but that is what my dentist recommends. I also note the brush motor flickers every minute or so. Then I realized it is telling me to move onto the next quarter on my mouth. And then it shuts off. Since I generally brush longer than the average bear, it was shutting off before I was done. But, no problem to just turn it back on. This brush is fairly compact and will fit nicely in my camping gear. The claimed 4-week run time is a bonus.

I'm a current Suri rusher coming from the prior generation of Suri toothbrush, and I was eager to try this new model. I would definitely say the company has been listening to critiques and has created a significant upgrade over the previous "core" model. I like how it is lighter than the old model, so my hand doesn't get tired after holding it up for a few minutes. The base is more stable than before, it stands up straight when I place it on the counter while my old one tended to topple over. The color is attractive, and looks the same as it did before. The brush heads are also the same, which is great, those didn't need to change at all. It is a soft brush head that cleans very well, according to my dentist! Charging is soooo much easier than before, thanks to doing away with the copper pins that tended to corroded and had trouble lining up. The brush's LED also lights up much brighter than the old model which makes it much easier to see when the brush has successfully started charging. My only downside is the pressure-activated button is a bit harder to press than the old touch-sensitive button. However, I'm getting used to it and wouldn't say it's a deal-breaker. Happily, the battery has already lasted a month without needing to recharge. Same good battery life as before.

review_title: I really like the Core Sonic 1.0, but there are a few annoyances
body_en: The Core Sonic electric toothbrush looks like a premium toothbrush. From the moment you unpack it, you see a really nice box. In the theme of sustainability, most of the packaging is made of cardboard, but it looks so much nicer than your usual cheap plastic packaging. There is nice colored printing showing everything that is included. The items are neatly stored and there are manuals included. Everything just screams quality. If I were just going by packaging, this would be a 5 star. Inside the box is your electric toothbrush, one plant-based brush head, a magnetic (mirror) mount with adhesive backing, and a magnetic stand/charging cable. The toothbrush is attractively colored and I like the fact that there are different colors to choose from when buying. It is not bulky and would be perfect for traveling (unfortunately, no case included though). There is only one brush head included and at time of ordering, there are replacement heads being sold in a 3pk for around $19. It seems a little expensive, but given that they are plant based, I can understand the pricing. The brush cover is a snap on type. It does not cover three back of the toothbrush though, do you may want to use a different cover if you are traveling. The magnetic mirror mount seems like a good addition, but I don't want to want to attach adhesive to my mirror and my mirror is also a good foot higher than the counter so I wouldn't trust using it personally. Next comes one of my cons. The included charger is proprietary, so you are reliant on the manufacturer's charger. The stand is magnetic, but since it is lightweight, the toothbrush can easily be knocked off balance accidentally. The cable is also non-removable so if it is damaged, you need to replace the entire base. And while the cable is USB C, this requires you to have an open USB C charging brick. I have a bunch of USB C cables, but I don't actually have many open USB C chargers. I would have much preferred just a USB C port so I can use my own USB C cable so I can easily connect it to one of my many open USB C cables. I guess the built in cable helps with waterproofing, but it is a bad inconvenience. Luckily, the battery is supposed to last about a month, though I am not sure how accurate that claim is. As for usage, there is only one button, so it can't get any easier to use than turning it on. You turn it on and then you can press the button again for a stronger brush. The toothbrush will remember the last used setting. And there is supposed to be a pressure sensor to tell you if you are brushing too hard. I don't have this problem so I can't comment on how well this feature works. During brushing, it will pause a bit at 30 seconds and then turn off at 2min, so pretty standard compared to other electric brushes. The bristles are a good stiffness and not overly soft. The brushing is also at a good level for me. So I really have no complaints about the usability during brushing. I will say that the handle is a little on the skinny side, so if you have larger heads, you might fumble around a bit as you adjust during brushing. Overall, I really liked this brush and would recommend it as a travel brush due to its compactness.

This is a review of the SURI NEW Core Sonic Electric Toothbrush, currently listed at $75.00. This is a new release from SURI offering a budget-friendly version of their popular SURI Pro 2.0. As a longtime user of Oral-B electric toothbrushes, I was completely surprised by this SURI. It cleans differently. At least it feels and sounds like it cleans differently. My Oral-B does an excellent job; this SURI does an excellent job also. I've used the SURI exclusively for the last 2 days, and my teeth feel very clean. I chose the Nightfall Blue color, which is a deep blackish blue. I charged it overnight before first use and installed the magnetic mirror mount so it would be ready to hold the brush once charged. The mount is very sturdy, and the brush attaches magnetically and securely. It's a great way to keep the countertops clear and the brush from getting splashed whenever I wash my hands. Other factors that make this a good choice for me: - Sleek, lightweight case -Recyclable brushheads -Travel brush cover -Travel lock button (so it won't accidentally turn on in your bag) -4 week USB C rechargable battery I cannot attest to battery performance at this point. I will update this review if the length between charges differs dramatically from the 4-week claim. At this point, I am very pleased with the SURI, intend to keep using it, and find it a good value.

review_title: Even better than the first version
body_en: I've had the SURI 1.0 for over a year and love it! I don't expect anything less from this model! Even though this is the slightly less "lux" version, it hits all the high notes... Smooth, sleek modern lines, no bulky mouth feel like with older electric toothbrushes. It charges pretty quickly and keeps a charge for weeks!! The charger works well and has a very small, compact foot-print. I bought the 1 0 with travel case for over $100, so to me this new model at $75 is a pretty good deal. It doesn't have the cleaning travel case--but that makes this brush great for a back-up brush, or weekend home or gym-bag brush, etc. I do prefer the more earth friendly body of the pro 1.0--which is aluminum and the replacement heads are minimalistic and color coordinated, which looks more high-end to me--but they last a while last a while either way--its pretty eco-conscuous, generally speaking! The bristles are also sturdy but gentle and there are two modes of vibration to choose from, to suit your comfort level. I love this brush! It also doesn't hurt that opening the box is a gift experience in itself! Highly recommend.

review_title: Great clean and excellent for travel
body_en: I’m really impressed with this electric toothbrush. It gives a noticeably deeper clean than a traditional manual toothbrush, and the sonic vibration makes brushing feel quick and effortless. The pressure sensor is helpful for making sure I’m not brushing too aggressively, and the built-in two-minute timer makes it easy to stick to the recommended brushing time. The battery life is a major plus. Being able to go weeks between charges makes this especially convenient for travel, and USB-C charging is easy and familiar. I also really like the compact travel cap and magnetic mirror mount. The mount keeps the toothbrush off the counter and saves space in the bathroom. The brush itself is lightweight and comfortable to hold, and the bristles have a nice balance of softness and firmness. I also appreciate the focus on more sustainable materials and the recycling program for used brush heads. Overall, this is a thoughtfully designed electric toothbrush with great cleaning performance, convenient features, and excellent battery life. It feels like a significant upgrade from a basic manual toothbrush.

review_title: Does an effective job of cleaning and is good quality
body_en: This Suri electric toothbrush is high quality, is user friendly, and works well. I like the travel cover for the brush head, which keeps the bristles clean at home or on the go, making it easily portable. It seems to do an effective job of cleaning and is good quality. This toothbrush thoroughly cleans my sensitive teeth without irritating my gums. It comes with a stick on magnetic toothbrush holder which is a handy feature, but I probably don't want to put a sticker on my mirror. It has an appealing appearance - I ordered the Haze Green. It comes with a c charging cord on which users will recharge it standing up on the charging base - it does not include a c block for plugging it in so users will have to provide their own. It is a fair value for the money.

review_title: Fantastic Cleaning Performance with Incredible Battery Life
body_en: The SURI Core is a phenomenal sonic toothbrush with an incredible battery life. Having already used the SURI 2.0, the Core feels just as capable, with the cleaning performance and power seemingly just as strong. If there is any difference in power between the two, it certainly isn't noticeable during everyday use. The long battery life is another major advantage, making it easy to forget about charging for weeks at a time. The only real annoyance I've found is the charger compatibility. Unfortunately, the Core doesn't appear to work with our existing SURI 2.0 charger because the shape of the bottom is different, meaning two separate chargers need to be kept around. It would be great to see SURI develop a more universal charging solution across its range in the future. Aside from that inconvenience, this is an excellent toothbrush that delivers fantastic cleaning performance and battery life.

Unsurprisingly this Suri brand toothbrush is now the top brand in the UK. This is my second one (accidentally left my last one in a hotel abroad:( ). If you’re looking for a top British electric toothbrush, this brand is a great choice. I see that it now boasts 17,000 verified Trustpilot reviews, so it’s clearly well loved and comes with clinically tested dentist-approved design. I really like the slim handle and the sonic cleaning is powerful, helping remove significantly more plaque than a manual brush, and the pressure sensor plus 2-minute timer make brushing simpler. Battery life is impressive too, giving up to four weeks per charge, and USB‑C charging makes it easy to keep going. It’s also light and travel-friendly, with a plant-based travel cap and a tidy Magnetic Mirror Mount for your bathroom. I also really like the brand's eco-focused approach,from its recyclable heads to its bio-based handle and B Corp certification. Trust me - you'll probably agree in a short time that this is the best toothbrush out there.

review_title: A Report from the Front Lines of Oral Hygiene
body_en: Dateline: A Bathroom Sink, Under the Unforgiving Glare of the Vanity Lights. For years, the act of brushing your teeth has been a sleepy, half-conscious affair. A dull, buzzing ritual performed on autopilot before you either face the horrors of the day or collapse into bed. You thought you knew what an electric toothbrush felt like. You were wrong. You were living a lie. I am here to tell you about the Philips Sonicare 4100. And I am here to tell you that it is a different beast entirely. It sits in your hand with a comfortable, substantial heft—a proper tool, not some flimsy, skinny wand. The handle is sturdy, the build quality immaculate. It feels like a serious instrument for a serious job. I applied the paste, brought the brush to my teeth with the casual indifference born of long habit, and thumbed the power button. And was immediately jolted awake by a profound, high-frequency thrum. This was not the gentle back-and-forth of a lesser brush. This was a jump scare. A sudden, powerful hum that felt like I was holding a swarm of microscopic, hyper-caffeinated jackhammers against my teeth. This is the "sonic" part of the name, a technology that vibrates with a speed and intensity that is both shocking and deeply, profoundly effective. You can feel the difference. It's a sensation of being deep-cleaned, of having years of coffee stains and bad decisions power-washed into oblivion. There are smart features, of course. A pressure sensor that gently chides you if you're pressing too hard, a built-in coach to keep you from savaging your own gums. A timer that dutifully guides you through the quadrants of your mouth. The included cap for the brush head is a simple, welcome touch of practical genius. But we must address the one, single, baffling decision that holds this marvel back from pure, unadulterated perfection: the charger. In a world that has finally, blessedly, begun to standardize around the glorious, universal USB-C port, Philips has chosen to tether this futuristic cleaning wand to a proprietary, old-world charging base. It is a strange, frustrating relic, a small annoyance that requires its own dedicated spot on your counter, unable to join the happy family of your other modern chargers. Even so, that one grievance is a whisper in the face of the roaring, high-frequency hurricane of cleaning power this toothbrush provides. The Sonicare 4100 is an impressive, powerful, and brilliantly effective piece of technology. It transforms the most mundane of daily chores into a high-performance event. A five-star champion that will leave your mouth feeling cleaner than you ever thought possible.

I’ve been using this Sonicare toothbrush for a little while now, and I’m really happy with it. It leaves my teeth feeling much cleaner than when I use a regular toothbrush, especially around the gumline. It’s comfortable to hold, the vibrations aren’t too harsh, and the built-in timer helps me brush for the full two minutes without having to think about it. The battery life has also been great, so I don’t have to charge it very often. It is powerful and cleans my teeth really well.

I used Sonicare for years but started buying less expensive toothbrushes. I wasn’t happy with most of them and was surprised to see a Sonicare toothbrush at this price. It had good reviews so I purchased one. It works really well. The toothbrush head is small enough that I can get it to my back teeth and the built in timer lets me know that I’m brushing long enough. My teeth feel cleaner and look whiter so it is definitely worth the price.

review_title: Best toothbrush you'll ever have until it inevitably breaks too soon
body_en: Pro: The best toothbrush I've ever owned. My dentist actually asked me what toothbrush I use because my teeth are so clean when I see her. Con: I only had this toothbrush for 2 years before the on/off button broke. Pro: Incredibly strong battery. The buzz off the toothbrush when it wouldn't turn off due to the broken on/off button could be heard across the house. Con: When it broke, it would NOT turn off. No matter what I did. Would not turn off. I took a hammer to it in the driveway, wouldn't turn off. I tried to drown it in the sinknand the water somehow made it LOUDER. Pro: Incredibly durable. Literally indestructible. Con: I had to drive it a mile away from my house and throw it away in a public trashcan to escape the incessant buzzing from the broken on/off button. Pro: I bought it again because it's literally the best toothbrush ever. 4 stars lol

Tried another brand. This Philip new to me works great and movements a bit stronger works well,for me. I will recommend but this order only one brush. Overlooked and good to have extra brush head. Charger base is usb plug type. May need own 120v usb power plug

It was great while it lasted. But almost one year to the date, it won't hold a charge. I have to leave it on the charger non stop when not using which is inconvenience on the tiny counter space. So here's the situation: Should I just buy another which may also not be long lasting or find one a little more expensive and has a longer life span?

My son absolutely loves this toothbrush. It does a great job cleaning his teeth, is easy to use, and the battery lasts a long time. It feels well made and has made brushing much easier for him. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a quality electric toothbrush.

review_title: Pretty good, but start button failed after 1.5 years
body_en: My wife and I both share the base and use separate heads daily. This review reflects this type of usage. 1.5 years update: The battery charges normally and lasts several days between the both of us before needing a fresh charge. The clean feel after brushing is nice on either strength setting. We love the timing beeps that remind you to brush a new area. The base part charges fine, but the start button no longer functions because the rubber waterproof cover slightly ripped and water nuked it :( The unit performed flawlessly for 2 people of daily use for 1.5 years. 18 months. So we bought it for $40 with multiple heads to replace. That equates to about $1.11 per user during that time before it died. That’s better than any manual brush of similar quality. Not bad. I wish I could repair the button, but it’s built to be disposable after its useful lifespan.
Easy to use, powerful and effective, light.

The price of the 4100 bounces around everywhere all the time from £35 upwards so if you can get it for around that price, it represents good value for an electric toothbrush. This is my second one, and they do the job. Simple to use (one press at the start for normal vibration or two presses at the start for a bit more vibration) and then a two minute timer starts, with a vibration every 30 seconds until it stops. Brushes last about 3 months but aren't outrageously expensive - I just bought a load to last a few years. Excellent delivery and packaging as usual.
Limpa bem
Great product

What more do you need? Two levels, a pressure sensor for when you're stressed, and a timer. Battery life is still perfect even at level 2 for 7 days. Charge it every 9 days and then it's fine. I would buy it again and again.

review_title: Lasted 12 years before I had to buy it again! Superior clean without the hefty price.
body_en: After an incredible 12-year run with my first Oral-B Pro 1000, I finally bought it again! The battery on my original brush finally bit the dust, and toward the end, it would only stay charged enough to get me through 24 hours of teeth brushing (if I was lucky) before dying. However, I loved the performance so much over the last decade that replacing it with the exact same model was an absolute no-brainer. Here is why this brush is a classic: Hygienist Approved: My dental hygienist once told me that it really doesn't matter how fancy or expensive an electric toothbrush is—any solid electric toothbrush is far superior to a manual brush. This model gives you that elite, professional clean without making you pay for unnecessary, over-hyped tech features. The One Minor Con: If I have to name one downside, it is the noise. Even brand new out of the box, it does sound a bit like it might be powered by hamsters while it is working. But just because it doesn't sound whisper-quiet doesn't negate the fact that it is a remarkably solid, heavy-duty toothbrush. A Note on the Color: The color is fun, but the listing is a bit misleading. I thought I would be getting a mint green, but instead, it is definitely a powder blue. I much prefer green to blue, but eh, whatever—it still cleans my teeth perfectly! If you want a proven, durable electric toothbrush that will last you for years to come without draining your wallet, this is the one to get. Highly recommended!

Let me start this review by saying that when I was younger, much to my parent's dismay, I neglected to brush my teeth. I would brush them but not as often and as thoroughly as a child should. This was partly due to my very bad gag reflex and partly due to the fact that it felt painful (?). Anyway, I've had yellow teeth my whole life (I'm 29) because of it. I never got braces (thanks again gag reflex) but my parents tried everything to get me to have better oral hygiene and to have a more aesthetically pleasing smile. Now that I'm well into adulthood, my smile being so yellow, and also very crowded, was starting to bother me. I knew I had to give in and fix one or the other. (To be clear if you have crooked teeth don't feel like you have to change yourself just for society - after 29 years, I can say that I truly wanted to change the yellowness purely for myself). I've gotten healthier in almost all other aspects of my life. I decided to make the plunge and buy this in hopes it would help get my teeth cleaner and help reduce plaque buildup. Not just for aesthetics, but for actual oral hygiene. So, I've used it twice a day for 3 days so far and my brother commented on how "white" my teeth look yesterday evening. That felt very good to hear, not gonna lie. I think this toothbrush is amazing for the price. I love how tiny the head of the brush is. It fits into my small, overcrowded mouth perfectly. I was worried that it would take forever to brush my teeth since I wasn't doing the work, the toothbrush was. However, it takes about 2 minutes and 30 seconds or 3 minutes if you're extra thorough. It allots 30 seconds to each section of your mouth, it will do a variation in the vibration to let you know when the 30 seconds is up and to move to the next portion of your mouth. It doesn't automatically shut off after 3 minutes (that I know of) if you want to go back and do another section of your mouth, which is nice. As for the pressure sensor on the toothbrush, mine does not work. It doesn't indicate any color or anything. It just appears to be a normal electric toothbrush. I may have gotten a "bad" toothbrush since it's not working, but to be honest, I truly just wanted something that would do a deep clean and this toothbrush does that. However, all the other reviews mention the sensor working so if that's something you're looking for, I would still highly recommend this toothbrush. I think mine might just be a dud in that department. The charging took several hours to be full on the first day. I keep it on the charger to ensure that it is always fully charged. If you don't have your charger with you and you need to rely on it without it, I'm told the battery lasts up to a week. Which, is very impressive for a $50 toothbrush. Amazon says that it has Bluetooth connectivity but I do not see any indication of that on the boxes or in the manual. My parents bought me an electric toothbrush when I was little, but I was too young to appreciate it. Now that I'm older, I think this is a great option for any person of any age. I do recommend it!

I have used the Oral-B electric toothbrushes for many years. I’ve been told I have a small mouth and the small round head of this toothbrush is perfect for me. It makes every brushing like going to the hygienist—smooth clean teeth. It has a timer for a total of 2 minutes, with a change every 30 seconds to move you through the front and back of both sides of your mouth. I wouldn’t use any other toothbrush.

review_title: A great value that comes with power
body_en: This is the most powerful electric toothbrush I have ever used! I ordered this toothbrush to replace a manual one that I had. My dentist recommended an electric one so I picked this one up. This is amazing! My teeth have never felt so clean When you first get it, it will come with no charge, so make sure you charge it. In the box, it includes the toothbrush and a charger. You don’t get any extra heads so make sure that you order some. When you do use it though, you will love how clean your teeth get! My teeth have never felt so clean! I use it every day. It is waterproof, so you can take it in the shower, which is perfect for me since my mornings are rushed. It is enjoyable to use and to hold, it’s terrific! One thing I really enjoy about it is the two minute timer. It keeps me accountable to actually brush my teeth for a long enough time, and it doesn’t allow me to brush for a longer time than I have to. It pauses every thirty seconds, so you can brush each quadrant of your teeth for thirty seconds, so you can give one section of your teeth the attention it deserves. With the pros out of the way, I do want to talk about a few cons. There are way too many settings to use. I know that it’s nice to have many options to choose from so we can pick what we want, but you don’t need three different ways to brush your teeth. Most of the time I just click the on button and don’t bother with the other settings and turn it off when I’m done. The other settings aren’t even that different. You can see that in my included video The battery life is also not the best. Some people have reported getting a week or two’s worth of battery, but I’m finding I have to charge mine every five days, which isn’t a dealbreaker, but I travel a lot, so it’s not ideal. Speaking of not ideal, they use a proprietary charger which really makes this toothbrush not travel friendly. You need to take so many chargers with you for your phone and laptop. Those might have the same charger, like USB-C, but this doesn’t. So, you need to take this charger separately. Another thing is that you need to really keep the toothbrush, charger, and any surface it touches, clean and dry. Otherwise, wherever you put this, bacteria will start to build up. If you don’t clean your charger every other day, bacteria will start to build up and it’s gross. The included picture doesn’t do it justice, and that’s just on my sink. Despite my complaints, I really enjoy this toothbrush. It’s relatively inexpensive compared to other electric toothbrushes, it has lasted me a long time, and it’s powerful. I do recommend it!

review_title: Great electric toothbrush but head replacement gets pricey!
body_en: Great, lightweight electric toothbrush with several different replacement heads to choose from. Lower upfront cost to purchase the toothbrush than other brands or models within the Oral-B family. Recharges fast and is easy to take on trips too. Only issue is with the price of replacement heads - that is where they get you. Just do your research as the brush heads need replacing every few months and it adds up.

review_title: Don’t be frightened when your teeth feels clean for the first time!
body_en: Absolutely phenomenal. People weren’t lying when they said it feels like you just came from the dentist. I don’t know how it does it, but if you brush the same way you brush with a manual toothbrush, alongside the intense vibration, it feels like it removes 100% of plaque, especially the plaque that’s hard to get behind each tooth. Also, at first, the vibration may feel a little intense, but you’ll get used to it. But if it’s too strong, just press the button and it will go to a slower mode. I highly recommend the strongest mode for the most effectiveness. But hands down, this is the best toothbrush I’ve ever got in my life. I will say, because the brush is small, I usually apply the toothpaste on my finger and place it in my mouth manually, then brush. But that’s my personal preference. I just prefer more toothpaste. And it sits well on the charging pad. I honestly have no complaints.

I love this brush and wish I had gotten one years ago! After learning from my hygienist how to use it correctly, this brush made brushing so much easier than a regular toothbrush and I can feel that the cleaning is so much more thorough. Love it. Well worth the ~$50 cost.

review_title: This is a bit pricy over time but it works well
body_en: Love this. Power runs about 5 uses for me. Good buy, only thing worth noting is that the new heads are like 15$ a pop which is expensive in the long haul.
شكرا لكم على خدمتكم

review_title: Great cleaning, versatile options for brush heads, charge lasts, but only 1 speed setting
body_en: One of my best purchases. I used to clean my teeth with a manual toothbrush, thinking that if I spent enough time and diligence, it would provide the same level of cleaning as an electric toothbrush. I was wrong. After my very first cleaning with this device, I felt a level of clean teeth only experienced when I leave the dentist's office after a cleaning. And it wasn't just a subjective feeling. When I returned for my 6 month cleaning the next time, there was barely any tartar or plaque build up - all had been removed by this toothbrush. I also noticed that my level of bad breath and tonsil rocks declined significantly. Turns out a manual cleaning is nowhere near as good as this machine. I have purchased this toothbrush for familty and friends, telling them it has changed my life. I wish I had this device as a child! The toothbrush comes with interchangebale heads, so that you can pick the one that works best for you - sensitive teeth, hard brush, whatever. Oral-B makes these products available, but you can also purchase no-name brands as well. It does create quite a bit of vibration in your head that I found a little scary at first. However, despite having sensitive teeth and gums, the toothbrush never harmed them. The toothbrush ahs a pressure sensor that stops once you put it too tightly against your teeth to prevent this. There is supposed to be 3 levels of speed for the brush. Mine doesn't seem to have them - has shown in the video. It's not that I don't know how to operate it - the toothbrush I purchased for my family (in white instead of pink) had those features, as advertized. In the end, I don't feel that having those 3 levels are important, except perhaps to get used to the sensation of vibration in the initial phases of use. The toothbrush comes with a plug and charger. It seems t o keep its charge for 4-5 days (I only use this toothbrush once a day for 4 min). Then the little light at the bottom of the toothbrush turns from green to red, alerting me that it is time to charge it (so I can usually travel without the toothbrush charge if it is for a trip that is less than a week). The charge itself happens very quickly - it seems to be charged within 20 min. I highly recommend this spinning toothbrush. It has changed my mouth's health!

review_title: Limpieza profunda y guiada, excelente cepillo
body_en: I have been using the Oral-B Pro 1000 CrossAction and I really like it. The cleaning is deeper than with a manual toothbrush: it helps remove plaque and care for the gums more efficiently. The built-in timer makes it easy to complete the recommended two minutes, guiding 30 seconds in each quadrant. In addition, the round head reaches difficult areas much more easily than a conventional brush.
You can feel the difference :)

review_title: Great battery life, best toothbrush hands down
body_en: 1000% my favorite toothbrush I’ve ever purchased. The battery life is outstanding I think I’ve charged it twice ever. It does a great job of cleaning and the thing stands up to some beating in my luggage while traveling. Plus it’s pink so that’s a plus!

I got the pink one rechargeable. It’s very small considering I have the original one and it was like holding a handle of a rake or something. It’s very wide. This one is perfect. I like having so many different options for the brushes. The charging station is nice because it’s small and you just set the toothbrush right on it. It comes with a plastic cap that goes over the brush to protect it from whatever’s flying around the bathroom. For being something so small it has multiple functions to it to help in your dental care.

charge lasts about a week with brushing twice a day which is perfect for me. it has a timer for all 4 quadrants so every 30 seconds, so you know when to switch sides. it only vibrates, no circular motion but my dentist told me the vibration is what actually helps the most. works way better than a manual toothbrush. i’ve had for a while and it’s worked great. switching out the new heads is so easy too

review_title: Kids actually Use It! Great purchase/buy.
body_en: I bought two of these Philips Sonicare 4100 toothbrushes—one for my nephew and one for my niece—after their older electric toothbrushes finally stopped working. Honestly, I wasn’t sure how much of a difference they’d notice, but it’s been a huge upgrade. They both love them and are actually brushing two to three times a day now without being reminded, which says a lot. The brushes are simple to use, gentle but still feel like they’re doing a really good job cleaning. I’ve noticed they mention their teeth feel “super clean” after using them, and that’s exactly what you want, especially for kids building good habits early. These brushes are known for being effective at removing plaque while still being gentle on gums, which makes them a great choice for daily use. Overall, great value and a really solid upgrade from their older brushes. Definitely recommend if you’re looking for something reliable that actually gets used!

review_title: Just as good as the expensive ones!
body_en: I have had the same Sonicare for about 11 years, and it’s still working. The original I have is a much more expensive sonicare than this one but when I tell you this toothbrush does the job well!! It was just time for an upgrade and I was worried about something a little less expensive not being good/ but this is great! The only thing about the pricier versions- they usually come with a wall charger and a case, but I didn’t care because this one will be my home toothbrush. It comes with charging cord - you just need your own box. A lot more lightweight than my more costly one too- which is nice
Very pleased, noticed a difference with my teeth!

review_title: Best Electic Toothbrush You Can Get
body_en: My dentist told me that I needed to switch to an electric toothbrush so I found the specs and review to this one to be good. The brush head isn't too small like the other ones I saw, and it has two power speeds. It may be uncomfortable to use on your teeth at first if you switch from a manual toothbrush. But let me tell you, that your teeth will get so much used to it and after a while, it won't even bother you. I find that my teeth are just as clean as if coming from a dentist's office. My teeth feel so smooth and I can tell that it has gotten rid of any plaque or bacteria I may have. I have permanent retainers on the bottom of my teeth which can be a pain to clean and floss. But with this electric toothbrush, I can tell that it's cleaner than it has ever been as I glide my tongue around the area. I just visited the dentist and the hygienist was going about how clean my teeth are and how well I take care of them! And how I have absolutely no plaque, and I am doing the right things, and that I should keep doing what I'm doing. I was using a battery-powered brush that was cheap from Walmart but having to replace the batteries is a hassle. The fact that this is rechargeable and the change holds for a VERY long time is what I think is the best thing about this toothbrush. It may not come with a wall adapter, but you can contact Sonicare and they can send one in for you to use. Their idea is to conserve the environment by doing so which is fine by me. I just used a wall charger I've had and it does the job. If you're on the fence about buying this one, or any electric toothbrush-don't be. Its the best investment you can make for yourself and your oral health and I have not looked back on buying this. 10/10 recommend.
Weak battery with low operating time, and less brush power than my older Sonicare model. Died completely in roughly 18 mos and would not charge afterwards. My older model lasted 5+ years! Avoid this.
Will update when it fails.

review_title: Wish I had purchased it years ago
body_en: I've been using a manual toothbrush for years. I never felt like I could get my teeth clean enough with them, but I didn't want to shell out the money for a pricey electric toothbrush. After having gum recession from brushing too hard, I decided to try an electric toothbrush out. I bought it for $55, and honestly, I love it so much I would've paid $85 for it. It works great, it's comfortable to hold, super easy to use and it gets my teeth so nice and clean. It makes brushing so much easier, and I love the pressure sensor, it stops me from brushing so hard. The heads are a wee bit pricey to replace, but they only need to be swapped every 3 months, and all of the Philips ones are interchangeable. I've been using it for about 3 weeks and only had to charge it once so far. I love the pink colour, and I love that it doesn't have any nooks or crannies to trap water and grow mold like toothbrushes 15 years ago had. Highly recommend, it's the best purchase I've made all year.
Really poor quality!! Needs recharging every week and after a year the battery life has gotten worse. Need to recharge it every other day!!

review_title: Good value for money, but feels a bit 'too light'
body_en: Can't fault it. Very good value for money. The only thing I'm not used to, is it being much lighter than all the previous models I used (and currently use). This feels kind of 'hollow' and very light, while the older models are more solid and heavier. But my partner prefers that. Otherwise, like I said, does the job, and good value for money.
Excelente!

review_title: Not as weak as they say
body_en: This is my 1st electric toothbrush. I ordered it over the oral b smart 1500 because it's cheaper and I found more people who swear by it than oral b. Later on, I read comments where people who have this 4100 for 10+ years say that the newer 2021 version has only half the power of the old version. Someone on reddit showed images of the inside of the new and old versions and the new version has a small plastic toy-like motor, while the old version has a big copper-wrapped motor and an old version user said "now I understand why the new version is lighter and less powerful". I was disappointed on the new version and tried to cancel the order but I couldn't. Once it came, I decided to try it and to my surprise, it brushes my teeth way better than my manual soft-bristled and hard-bristled toothbrushes(I use both manual brushes daily compared to my daily usage of the electric toothbrush 4100 C2 head of medium bristles. If you have gum sensitive issue, buy the S sensitive or G2 optimal brush head. If you want hard-bristled, buy W diamondclean brush head). I don't know how good the old version was but this newer version definitely brushes better than any manual toothbrush unfortunately it doesn't not come with a travel case. Update 5/16/2024: I bought the Oral B smart 1500 because it was on sale and I wanted to see how better it is compared to the sonicare. The oral B package looks nicer and bigger than the Sonicare but upon opening the smart 1500 package, I saw hair all over the toothbrush. I did read many customers saying on reddit that their Oral b toothbrush were repackaged, but I can't believe I'm a victim of this nastiness. It also took 2 weeks to reach me from Hawaii and since it says "made in China", I think the seller is located in China. I'll return this and I'll advise you to buy the Sonicare instead of the oral b if you don't want to be cheated receiving a used-repackaged toothbrush. Update 05/22/2024: On 05/17/24, I bought the Oral b smart clean 360 which has exact power as the smart 1500 that I returned but the smart 360 has 5 modes and a button to change the mode while the smart 1500 has 3 modes and no button to switch between the modes. The advantage of the oral b smart clean 360 is that the brush heads cost is cheaper than the Sonicare 4100 and I find it better at whitening my teeth than the Sonicare. That's all the advantages there. The things that I don't like with it are many, so I'm just going to name the most annoying ones: 1) The brush heads are too big compared to the Sonicare(see picture): Putting Oral b brush heads in my mouth is like putting a golf ball in my mouth(my head and mouth are wider than the average US male). 2) The brush heads have holes(see pictures) that trap saliva+toothpaste and creates more noise when the brush handle needle rotates in the presence of the liquid mixture, and moisture will be also trapped easily in the holes(most customers complain about Oral b brush heads design. Oral b corrected the needle issue with the IO version but the IO introduced a shallow hole which now traps moisture in the brush handle). When I'm using the Oral b with no choice but to have my mouth wide-open, it forces my mouth to produce more saliva which gets mixed with the toothpaste and enters the brush head and creates more noise. 3) Rattling noise: The Oral b smart clean 360 isn't as noisy as people say. It's the quality of the noise the problem. It's a very unpleasant rattling noise as if you're hearing an old car engine with broken parts in it. That noise gets worse when liquid enters the brush head holes. 4) The charger is not round like a perfect circle: You must put the Oral b brush handle in a specific position to charge it and if you place it wrong, it'll fall and might break. 5) The Daily Clean mode is rough and combined with the big brush head the experience is bad, but the smart clean 360 has more mode which make it smoother and better than the smart 1500 but not as good as the Sonicare 4100. 6)It has no auto-stop mode: You keep brushing without knowing how long you have been brushing your teeth. To summarize, the oral b non-IO brush heads are cheap but very badly designed for a pleasant toothbrushing. I won't recommend it if you're shorter than 6 foot tall or have a small mouth.

review_title: Replaced my old Series 2 Sonicare with this one and can highly recommend this 4100 Model.
body_en: I was replacing my "old" Phillips Sonicare, specifically the HX6240, which was a series 2 model. Loved it. I found newer brands of electric toothbrushes seemed to be including 2 features I did not want, sending my data; and, reminders to brush a new area every 20 sec for 2 minutes. The latter called Brush Pacer results in 6 reminders. I prefer 4 reminders, the Quad Pacer Timer, 4 - 30 sec increments. Easier to keep track of where I already brushed. This new 4100 had the Quad Pacer, was not info invasive, and I could use the same brush tips I liked. The Lithium Ion battery on this new one lasts longer than the old NiMH one. It can sit on a "similar looking" charging base to the old one. But the new model is charged via a USB type A cable base and cord. You can use any standard USB charger you already own for phones or tablets. This model includes 2 Pressure sensitive settings, which is all I need. It is lighter and has a slimmer profile. One unexpected thing is that you can actually charge the new model on the older model's base. My spouse still uses the older model, and when we have extended travel together we take just one charger. Its turned out to be the perfect replacement electric toothbrush for me. (Photos: Older Model is on your left.)

This is my second one. My first Sonicare 4100 lasted until it finally wore out, so I bought the same model again. It’s one of the most affordable Sonicare electric toothbrushes, but it still does a great job. It cleans well, the battery lasts a long time, and it’s simple to use without a lot of unnecessary features. If you’re looking for a reliable electric toothbrush at a reasonable price, I definitely recommend this one.

This item does not last very long. Iffy quality. The price is great for what it is, and it has what feels like a solid vibrational capacity, though. I bought this three years ago, and it became dysfunctional. The on/off button wore down to its metal interior, and then that button became unreliable, not working 60%+ of the time. I am debating buying another one when other options exist with maybe a higher price point but longer durability.

review_title: Love it but have to buy it again every year and a half.
body_en: I'll soon be buying my third. I had one and it died after a year or so, so I switched to that other popular brand but kind of hated using it. So I came back to this one and it also died. Maybe I just got two lemons, I thought, so I bought a third and after 16 months it also died. I'm in a dilemma. I don't like using that round-head brand but I am now pretty sure that I'm going to be buying this ever 1.5 years. Crap in terms of lifespan but good while it works.

This brush has everything: A low price, high quality, both gentle and vigorous settings, is light weight, and I love how small they’ve made the brush head since my last model, because this allows for more precise access between teeth and behind molars. Thank you.
I like it, teeth feel cleaner and the timers while brushing are very helpful. Battery seems to hold up very well.

review_title: minor accidents and there goes your 3 digit electric tooth brush
body_en: Sonicare loses cleaning power after minor drops I’ve now gone through three Sonicare toothbrushes in about two years. In my experience, even a minor drop can make the vibration much weaker. The brush still turns on and vibrates, but the power drops so much that it no longer feels like an effective electric toothbrush, even with a new brush head. That is the most frustrating part: it does not completely fail, so at first glance it seems fine, but the cleaning performance is clearly reduced. At that point, the main advantage of using an electric toothbrush is basically caput.. This has happened to me twice, and it makes the product feel far less durable than it should be for normal real-world household use. For a premium toothbrush, I expected better resistance to minor drops and better long-term reliability. I still think Sonicare is a great product, but after this repeated experience I would strongly advise buyers to be very careful with handling and not assume it can tolerate everyday bumps or falls. Planned obscolecence? Sad if it is. I am sure it should not take more than a minor cushioning, internal or external to make the product more rugged.
Amazing

I had never used one and heard that they were very good and worth it. Because of my sensitive teeth I didn't opt ​​for the ones that rotate, I went for this one that vibrates and I thought maybe it would be something Meh! …Far from reality. It's a super brush! It feels VERY POWERFUL at low speed you can even feel your teeth in danger haha ​​but it doesn't cause any harm, on the contrary, with the manual ones I was hurting my enamel and above all there were parts that felt difficult to reach. I got this one on sale, it only comes with one head and it's small, it reaches difficult places and feels gentle on the gums, I definitely recommend it for sensitive teeth. There are many head options for different purposes. Only 2 speeds and very easy to use. I would buy it again without hesitation.

review_title: From manual brushing to automatic brushing!
body_en: I can't believe I waited this long to switch. This is my first time ever using an electric toothbrush, and I am seriously surprised by its effectiveness. My teeth have honestly never felt cleaner, it feels like I just walked out of a professional dental cleaning every single time I brush. One of the most useful features is the built-in timer. It pulses/vibrates every 30 seconds to let you know exactly when to switch to a different quarter section of your mouth. It completely takes the guesswork out of making sure you brush for the full recommended two minutes. Battery life has also been great. A single charge easily lasts for about a week, if not slightly longer, which is perfect since I don't have to keep the charging base cluttering up my bathroom counter all the time. Before buying, I noticed this model is highly recommended by many reviewers due to its incredible bang for the buck. Now that I've been using it, I totally agree. You don't need to spend hundreds of dollars on a fancy toothbrush to get amazing results. Highly recommend!

review_title: True longevity & happy to purchase 2 more
body_en: Oral-B Pro 1000 Rechargeable Toothbrush has not disappointed me. I’ve had my own since 2019. It still functions beautifully. The one thing I’ve noticed is the battery charge doesn’t last as long as it did when it was new. I could go 2 weeks or more without charging. Now it’s about 1 week & I need to charge. I do brush morning & night for the full 2 minutes. I love everything about it. I don’t have sensitive teeth thus my teeth can handle the deep cleaning it provides. I really don’t recommend this if you do have sensitive teeth as I feel it would be too harsh. The timing function works wonderfully for it tells me when to move onto the next area of my mouth. ••To prevent a yukky mess that drips down I have learned 2 things: I thoroughly run water under the brush while it’s running to fully clean it. This, however, doesn’t prevent yuk from your brushing from forming down where the brush head meets the toothbrush. I became tired of a toothbrush that had dried toothpaste on it even though I thought cleaning the head was enough. Unfortunately the yuk does collect at that area & begins the mess. To prevent that I do now take the head of the brush every time I use it now. I just sit in to side in a dry cloth. Hence a clean brush. Since my purchase I’ve purchased 2 more. One for my husband who was told by his Dentist he needed an electric toothbrush because he was developing gingivitis. He loves it because it’s so easy to brush now. The toothbrush does all the work. At first he was doing the brushing & ruined the head a little. So a reminder this does the brushing for you. You only need to move the brush around your mouth. Since having mine I haven’t had one cavity. One thing my hygienist did mention when I first got it was I wasn’t getting high enough to my upper gums. Now I make sure I do. I also purchased one for my 15yo Son as his Pediatric Dentist said it was okay & recommended that he start early with an excellent choice in toothbrushes. For $50- the price hasn’t changed since 2019 - this is well worth getting. For multiple reasons as I feel I thoroughly cleans my teeth. Once I began using this my mouth felt clean & fresh & it does every time I use it. I also feel using an electric toothbrush has saved $ I’d be spending on dental bills. The cost always swayed me away from making the purchase but I’m glad I did. Obviously since mine still works since 2019 there’s definite genuine quality with Oral-B. The box does state it comes with a 2 year limited warranty & there is a 60 day risk free trial. The paperwork details are in the box. For all I’ve written I highly recommend this Oral-B electric toothbrush & I don’t feel you’ll be disappointed. ••I do not purchase genuine Oral-B brush heads. From the beginning I’ve purchased a generic version from Amazon which have worked perfectly. My pictures reflect how nicely it’s packaged upon its arrival.

review_title: Oral-B Pro 1000 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush is a High-Quality Product!
body_en: I purchased “Oral-B Pro 1000 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush” on the recommendation of my dental hygienist, who suggested the brand to help manage my gingivitis. After my previous Oral-B lasted over a decade, I was happy to stick with the same reliable brand. I find this model to be extremely effective; it does all the hard work for me, and the built-in timer works perfectly. It is a high-quality product that offers great value and dependability. While I am giving it a 5-star rating, there are three minor drawbacks: the battery life is somewhat short, the motor is noticeably loud, and the power button can be a bit difficult to press, especially with wet hands. Despite these small issues, I highly recommend this toothbrush and am confident it won't disappoint!

review_title: Does a very good job on plaque
body_en: I have always used a standard manual brush. I was skeptical of electric because it seemed like the little head only moved in short back and forth spins (instead of complete circles) making it less effective. In addition, I assumed that you could not apply any pressure, or the head would stop moving. My dentist recommended I try one to help with plaque build up that I seem to accumulate quickly on the inside of my lower front teeth. So, I bought this one (my wife has had one a few years). Some observations: - It does a very good job keeping plaque off. I actually started using this brush halfway between dentist appointments. I found that it could not remove already present plaque (at least not what I had), but that once removed by the dentist, this brush does a great job keeping it off. Much better than a manual brush. For that alone I am sold. - The small size is very good for getting around back teeth / wisdom teeth. It also gets you to focus on a tooth at a time (vs. the sawing motion across many teeth) - which actually took no more time. Overall, a session might take very slightly longer than manual, but is certainly more thorough. - You can press down pretty hard, and the brush keeps oscillating. Although, in my experience, there is no need. I tend to use less pressure than a manual brush. While the brush head is doing a short back and forth spin (vs. a total 360), that seems just as effective (perhaps more so, since you get both directions of spin very quickly on all surfaces). - The brush does a pulsing vibration after 2 minutes. You can just ignore it and keep brushing. It also does much lighter pulses every 30 seconds, to help you time your session into groups of upper front, upper back, lower front, lower back. Again, you can ignore all this and just brush at your own pace. - If two people in the same bathroom are using this type of brush, there are two good options. One, have both people use the same base, and just switch out the head (they are color coded for this reason). Or two, give each person their own unit, but keep just one charging base out. The charge need is so infrequent, that its easy to just leave one brush standing on its own, and the other on the charger; then just switch out when a charge is needed. This clears up counter space and cords. - We have purchased the generic (and less expensive) replacement heads. In our experience, they were identical to the originals in materials and make. I am sure there is a lot of quality variation, but it was not hard to find good options. - My wife and I have what appear to be identical models, except we did one black, one white to make them easy to keep separate. Mine, the white, only turns off by pressing the off button 3 times (since it cycles through modes using the on/off button). This is the only thing I really do not like. The black one turns off with one click. Perhaps it is a setting, but we can find no way to change it. So, I find myself holding the brush in my mouth (to stop splatter) while finding the button (see below), and pressing 3 times. - The on off button is a little hard to press. It is flush and shallow. I always manage to get it on and off, but sometimes it is surprisingly hard. Recently, it would not turn on, and I thought it must have lost its charge. Turns out I just had to press very firmly. This can be a challenge when turning the unit off. You tend to keep it in your mouth (to prevent splatter), and so finding and pressing the button is sometimes a little harder than you would think. I think for most people, this is just a negative to be accepted. But for people who are older, or not dexterous in the hands, I think this would actually make the brush impossible to use. Overall, I am happy with it, because it prevents plaque, end of story. If I could change one thing, it would be a single press, easy press on\off button.

review_title: Best clean from a toothbrush ever
body_en: First of all I was very reluctant to get this because a lot of the reviewers were giving very negative feedback about this. I don't exactly agree that the problems are as bad. People were definitely complaining that the toothbrush is too slippery cuz there's less rubber grip and people are also saying that it's hard to turn it off. I definitely see those issues but they're not enough to say that it's not a good toothbrush since you can just get the next model up for closer to 75 to $100 or higher and get the one that's much better this is definitely more of a budget type toothbrush. The other thing is that it doesn't turn red when you're brushing too hard it just slows down instead and also there's no battery meter to tell you how much is left. These are all concerns but not if you're spending $40 on this device which I think is an amazing price for a machine that does the best clean of my teeth I've ever had. I literally feel like I just came back from the dentist every time I use this. This is much smaller than I'm used to but it's great it does get slippery but not enough to say that it's a flaw when you paid $40 for this really nice toothbrush. The toothbrush head is extremely soft and honestly I might only use this type of heads because it's just doing such a good job cleaning my teeth.
Been working good no issues. Good quality for the price. Had a higher end model same brand with more features but this one works good.
Works as advertised. My wife and I have been using Sonic electric brushes for many years - we just may like this better. Seems to do a much better job cleaning our teeth. I recommend this product.

This is my 2nd toothbrush ordered, the first one lasted about 2 years until it eventually stopped holding a charge. The second one has lasted only 9 months. When I first received it, I had to press the power button about 3 times to get it to turn on or off. The previous brush had this issue occasionally, so I thought nothing of it. Now I am having to press the button about 10 times before it will do anything, even with a full charge. While it is still under warranty, it requires sending it to Oral-B for review, leaving me without a toothbrush in the meantime. So unfortunately I bought another one. I otherwise like the toothbrush and it does what it needs to do for the price.

This is my second oral-b electric toothbrush, I love them, I won't go back to the traditional ones. My teeth feel cleaner and brushing my teeth is easier. A tip to keep the base of the charger and the body of the brush clean is that when you finish brushing your teeth, do not put the brush directly on the charger. First separate the brush head and body, rinse them well, dry them and then put only the brush body in the charger. Update (Sep 12, 2024): almost two years after the review, my brush and charger are still in excellent condition. It's just a matter of taking care of it and keeping it clean.
Very good toothbrush and same as the pictures
Works well
Powerful in cleaning and soothing the gums. Suitable for an orthodontist or prosthetist.
100% functional and product quality

review_title: A Nice Upgrade From My Oral-B Pro 100
body_en: I recently upgraded from my old Oral-B Pro 100 to the Oral-B iO Series 3, and I can definitely tell the difference. The brushing experience feels much smoother and quieter, and my teeth feel noticeably cleaner after each use. One of my favorite improvements is the pressure sensor. It helps me avoid brushing too hard, which is something my old toothbrush didn't have. I also like the different cleaning modes they're simple to switch between and let me choose what feels best. The brush head glides comfortably over my teeth, and the handle feels solid and well-made. Battery life has also been great so far, lasting several days before needing a recharge. If you're still using an older Oral-B model like the Pro 100 and have been thinking about upgrading, I think the iO Series 3 is well worth it. It feels like a much more refined brushing experience, and I'm really happy with the purchase.

review_title: Very nice looking, powerful and inexpensive. A great purchase!!
body_en: What a bargain!! This is replacing our old power toothbrush and upgrading to something much better. The cleaning modes are delightful, and the recharge time is efficient. Keeping the brush assembly in the holder and protected from the elements with the plastic case is such a great idea. The quality of this Oral-B toothbrush is second to none, as expected. The power and vibration of the brush is something we'll have to get used to, but that's a given considering our old one is well over 10 years old. 2 thumbs up on this product.

Really like this toothbrush. Holds a charge well and I really like the brush heads they seem to clean very well. Has a 2 minute timer and lights that help you to know if you are applying the correct amount of pressure. I'm pleased with it and happy I bought it.

review_title: Its a good toothbrush would recommend if your in the market
body_en: I’ve been using the Oral-B iO Series 3 for a few weeks now, and the difference compared to a standard electric or manual toothbrush is night and day. It leaves your teeth feeling amazingly smooth, like you just stepped out of a dental cleaning. ​What makes it great: ​Unreal Cleaning Power: The round micro-vibrating brush head gets into every spot with zero effort. My teeth have never felt cleaner or fresher. ​Smart Pressure Sensor: This is probably the best feature. The light indicator shows green when you're using the right amount of pressure, red if you're pressing too hard, and white if you're too soft. It takes all the guesswork out of brushing and protects your gums. ​Built-in Timer & Modes: The built-in 2-minute timer pulses every 30 seconds to let you know when to switch quadrants, making it super easy to ensure a complete clean every single time. ​Solid Battery Life: Holds a charge really well for daily morning and night use, and the charging base takes up very little counter space. ​If you’re thinking about upgrading your oral care routine, this toothbrush is worth every penny. Highly recommended!

I always forget to write reviews after I buy stuff on Amazon. I should try to do it more because it is helpful when you find a review that is real. So, I bought this toothbrush to replace another brand that I bought about a year and a half ago. The old toothbrush just wasn't doing a good job at cleaning my teeth. I have always had problems with cavities and plaque build-up. The only sure-fire way of getting all of the plaque for me was to use Plax prior to brushing. Still, I find myself in the dentist's office every six months with a hygienist jack-hammering my mouth with water pick to get my teeth clean. It's embarrassing and it makes me feel anxious about my gum health. I saw the Oral-B iO Series 3 here on Amazon and it was discounted. According to Oral-B it is really good at getting rid of plaque. I took the manufacturer at their word, and bought it. Holy crap, ya'll! This thing is amazing! The iO3 has a round brush head similar to the polishing tool your dental hygienist uses. I've used cheaper Oral-B electric toothbrushes that also have round heads, but they weren't as robust as the brush head on the iO3. The bristles aren't hard, but they are dense and arranged in a way that they can hug your teeth while brushing. You can get that brush on every surface of each tooth (except directly between the teeth, of course). The motorized handle has a pressure sensor that changes color based on how hard or soft you are pressing. If you get it just right, it lights up green. The iO3 also helps you time your brushing so that you the recommended two minutes. It pulses when it's time to change to a different quadrant. It doesn't automatically shut off when the two minutes are up, however. That's fine with me as I will just continue brushing other parts of my mouth like my tongue and the roof of my palette when I'm done with my teeth. There are supposedly three types of brushing settings to choose from, but I have only used the default cleaning setting. The other two setting are supposed to be for sensitive teeth and whitening. The default works just fine for me. The build is solid and feels good in my hands. I like that the handle comes with two brush heads, a travel case, and case for the brush heads. I like to take my brush head off and put it in the case after I'm finished just because I'm paranoid about having a toothbrush exposed in the bathroom. It's nice to have the option to shield it from germs. So, TLDR, this is a great electric toothbrush. My teeth haven't felt this clean since the last time I went to the dentist. Oral-B did a fantastic job of designing a product that makes brushing easy and will almost certainly result in you having a positive visit at the dentist, and may help reverse gum issues and prevent cavities. I definitely recommend you buy this product if you are in the market for an electric toothbrush.

review_title: A noticeable upgrade from the Pro 1000!
body_en: I previously owned the Oral-B Pro 1000, and while it did a good job cleaning my teeth, this model is definitely an upgrade. The pressure sensor is one of my favorite features. When I press too hard, the light changes color, making it easy to know when to ease up. It's a simple feature, but very useful. It's also noticeably quieter and smoother than the Pro 1000, and the battery life is much better. Overall, brushing just feels more comfortable and enjoyable with this model. I'm very happy with this upgrade and would definitely recommend it.

This is by far the best toothbrush I have ever used! Thinking that was better then just using my regular manual one. My husband bought this in black about a month ago and liked it and it was on sale so I decided to jump and get it as well. I've been using it for a week now and my mouth still feels as clean as it did the day I came home from the dentist with a cleaning. Its not loud at all and I love the 30 second interval vibrations it gives you so you know to move on to the next quadrant in your mouth. Over all the best thing I've bought all year. Would recommend it to everyone.
