review_title: Good: Great cleaning - Bad: MESSY -- a 2 min brushing turns into 4 mins of cleanup
body_en: To be clear, the cleaning power gets five stars. However, this is the messiest toothbrush I've ever used. The brush heads have two holes in the back, and you might think you could _hold_ it a certain way to keep toothpaste and spit from getting everywhere. You would be wrong. If you've never had a smart electric toothbrush, the ideas here are very cool and mostly useful, but be prepared to have a LOT more cleanup when done than simply rinsing the head under the sink and wiping your mouth. Pay close attention, or you'll have stains on your shirt. Toothpaste WILL be on your chin, your hand, and dribbling down your arm, unless you keep your elbow raised for the duration! I love the ideas and how well it cleans my teeth, but for the reasons mentioned above, I can't really recommend this to people I actually like.

My roommate was raving about this toothbrush that he bought for himself a month ago. He knows I try to take good care of my teeth, and encouraged me to consider getting one, I’ve been using a manual toothbrush for my entire adult life. I had a ver basic electric toothbrush when I was a teenager, but it was not great, so I was skeptical, as I thought I did a pretty great job caring for my teeth with a manual one, but OH MY GOD was I wrong! I took a leap of faith and bought the io 5 with three different heads. I got it on sale. Well, very first time I used it, I felt like I had gone to the dentist to get my teeth cleaned and polished. My teeth feel sooooo good. I am currently also using the app, which is sorta fun, it maps out and tracks where you have brushed and how long, and the pressure guide is very helpful! It also tracks flossing, tongue cleaning and mouth wash rinsing, and you get trophies for completing a full mouth cleaning routine. It’s really helped me to commit to consistent oral care. If you don’t have benefits to get dental cleanings, I genuinely and honestly strongly suggest that you get this toothbrush. I honestly don’t think I’ll ever need to go get a dental cleaning done now that I have this tooth brush. Also, if you don’t have dental benefits, it is very much in your best interest to get this toothbrush, as dental repair is very expensive and having this brush is likely going to greatly reduce your risk of serious tooth problems. Also, I learned that it has a dual oscillating plus micro vibrations, which is why it cleans so well. I will undoubtedly buy another one of these when the time comes, maybe even level up and get the top of the line. Have only had it for a few days, so I can’t speak for its longevity or durability yet, but if it craps out, I’ll update my review. Seriously, do yourself a favour and get this toothbrush.

For a product from a well-known brand like Oral-B, I expected much better durability and quality. It was working fine at first, but suddenly it just stopped turning on, and there was no visible damage or misuse on my end. review_title: Elevate Your Dental Routine with this electric Toothbrush!
body_en: As someone who values a sparkling smile, I was eager to try out this cutting-edge device, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. From the moment I started using it, I could feel the difference. The advanced technology behind this toothbrush delivers results like no other. Within just one week, it's clinically proven to provide 100% cleaner teeth and healthier gums compared to a regular manual toothbrush – an impressive feat by any standard. What sets this toothbrush apart is its Smart Display, which offers real-time personalized coaching. Paired with the accompanying app powered by Artificial Intelligence, it guides you through each brushing session, ensuring every surface of your teeth receives the attention it deserves. It's like having a personal dental assistant right in your bathroom. But the benefits don't stop there. The built-in 2-minute timer with quadrant intervals ensures that you're brushing for the recommended duration and covering all areas of your mouth evenly. Plus, the pressure sensor alerts you if you're applying too much force, safeguarding your gums and enamel from potential damage. In terms of convenience, this toothbrush excels. The rechargeable battery lasts impressively long – I've found myself needing to charge it only once a month, if not less frequently. And with the included travel case, maintaining your oral hygiene routine on the go has never been easier. Whether you're jetting off on a vacation or simply heading to the office, your dental health remains a top priority. Of course, like any product, there are a few areas for improvement. While the toothbrush does alert you when the battery is low with a flashing red light, a battery indication meter would provide even greater peace of mind. Additionally, addressing the maintenance of the brush head to prevent bacteria buildup would be a welcome addition to the product's features. Overall, the Oral-B Power iO Series 5 Limited Electric Toothbrush has exceeded my expectations in every way. It's effective, user-friendly, and backed by the trusted Oral-B brand. If you're ready to take your dental routine to the next level, look no further – this toothbrush is a game-changer.

Omg I love this! The brush handle did come with some dust on it but I cleaned it with a wet towel and looks brand new. I love how gamified my brushing routine has become. review_title: A Game-Changer for My Dental Routine — Noticeable Results and Effortless to Use
body_en: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I’ve been using this electric toothbrush for close to a year now, and I absolutely love it. Before this, I was using a regular manual toothbrush, and I truly had no idea what I was missing. The difference is enormous — this toothbrush cleans my teeth so much better and leaves my mouth feeling like I just left the dentist. One of the things that really convinced me it was working was my six-month dental appointment. My hygienist actually commented on how clean my teeth looked compared to previous visits. I hadn’t changed anything else in my routine except for switching to this toothbrush, so that alone made me a believer. It’s rechargeable, which is incredibly convenient, and the battery lasts a long time before needing to be plugged in again. The design is sleek — I have the white one, and it looks great on my bathroom counter. It also offers multiple brushing speeds, which I didn’t think I needed until I tried them. Being able to choose the intensity makes brushing feel more personalized and comfortable. The best part is how effortless it is to use. I don’t feel like I’m doing much of the work anymore — the toothbrush does it for me. My teeth feel cleaner with far less effort, and once you experience that, it’s hard to go back to anything else. Final Rating: 5 Stars — Amazing performance, noticeable results, and a must-have upgrade from a regular toothbrush.
This is a great electric toothbrush, rechargeable, very quiet, with a soft brush
Easy to use and great for beginners. My teeth have definitely been getting whiter from the settings. Would recommend!

I really enjoy my Oral-B it works great and cleans better then the standard old school toothbrush. The only thing I would like to see it have instead a smooth finish where you hold it a rough finish so it don't slip out of your hand. I guess it's ok like it is but for me personally if it had a serrated type grip it wouldn't slip out of my hand. I would recommend product it works great.

review_title: Charger is not for globally use
body_en: It is nice and working but the only problem i have is the charger, i cant use it here in the philippines since we are using 220v power and the charger is only for US use 110-130v. Seller should have put all the neccessary description especially the power voltage since they are selling it globally. Other than that everything is good. Shipping only takes 7 days for this one and the peach/pink one is 9 days. Ordered both separately.
Great! Different gauges are kind of annoying because you have to click through the three settings to turn off but good product overall

review_title: Torn between this and the other brand
body_en: Been a Sonicare user for 10-15 years and decided I wanted to try the Oral B. I didn't want to spend a lot, so I found this one and ordered it. Things I like: Love circular motion of the brush instead of the up an down movement of the Sonicare. Love that it has a sensor to alert you if you are brushing too hard. Such a simple feature and hopefully it shows on my next dental visit. Battery seems to last a long time between charges. I am going on two weeks without charging which is great for travel. Like that the handle stays cleaner compared to my older Sonicare because of how it is designed. Toothpaste and water run down it and does not have a place to collect. Things I don't like: The brush had by design traps water whereas the Sonicare brush design seems to drain water better. I rinse my toothbrush and then lay it brush side down on a towel to let it dry before standing it up on the counter or charger. If not, I worry about it not drying fully and things growing. I hate that it doesn't have an auto shut off. It does vibrate every 30 seconds but it doesn't shut off. First time I used it I probably brushed for 3.5 minutes before I realized it wasn't going to turn off. Overall the quality doesn't seem as nice. Maybe this would be different if I had spent more money on a higher end model, but because this something I was just buying to try, I didn't want to spend a lot. If I was completely sold on this brush, I would upgrade for sure. I really am torn between the two brands of brushes. Now if someone would make one that has the best of both. :)

I finally updated my old Oral B Pro electric toothbrush that I have used for 10+ years when it was on sale during Prime days. I figured why switch if it wasn’t broken. But I had noticed the charging was not what it used to be and the outer plastic felt like it was getting loose. I was shocked at how much cleaner my teeth felt with the Oral B Pro i02. I’m not sure that it is the brush, it might be the more expensive Oral B replacement brush heads. Either way you don’t need to buy the more expensive Oral B i09 with so many modes. The more reasonably priced i02 is all you need. I may return the Waterpik flosser my hygienist recommended for easier flossing of my back teeth. I bought it for a great price during Prime days too. I haven’t opened the box yet. My new electric Oral B i02 toothbrush works so well, I think the waterpik is an extra step that maybe is no longer needed.

Bought 2 of these, one for myself and my husband. Love them. Easy to use, my teeth feel cleaner and actually looked whiter and I haven't changed anything else except the toothbrush. I also got them to help protect our gums because I had some recession from brushing too hard. I was worried about mixing up whose toothbrush was whose, but each brush head has a different symbol on it, so it's easy to tell apart.

review_title: Great toothbrush with excellent battery life
body_en: Amazing tooth brush that was on sale and it works as expected. Wanted to wait a bit before providing review. 5 months in and still works like a charm.
It’s hard to keep clean, tiny crevices that need to be scraped off.
Great. Need to order more brushes!!

review_title: AJELU Pink & Blue Gradient Rechargeable Sonic Electric Toothbrush
body_en: I’ve really been enjoying the AJELU Pink & Blue Gradient Sonic Electric Toothbrush. It looks great with its gradient design and feels lightweight yet well-made. The multiple brushing modes are a nice feature and make it easy to customize depending on my needs whether I want a gentle clean or a deeper polish. The vibration is strong but comfortable, and my teeth feel noticeably cleaner and smoother after each use compared to a manual toothbrush. I also like that it’s rechargeable, so I don’t have to constantly worry about batteries. The battery life has been solid so far, and it holds a charge well. Overall, it’s a good value for the price, works effectively, and adds a little style to my daily routine.
the item was good quality and the price was excellent and it works great!

I was amazed at how wonderful this toothbrush works. I bought so many over the years and never satisfied. After I brush my teeth it feels like I just had my teeth cleaned and polished at the Dental office. In fact, I like it so much I went back and purchased one for my daughter & one for my sister.

This electric toothbrush works really well and leaves my teeth feeling clean and smooth after every use. I like that it’s rechargeable with USB because it’s convenient for travel and everyday use. The different settings are a nice touch, and it’s pretty gentle on my gums while still feeling effective. The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because it takes a little time to get used to the vibration strength and I wish the battery indicator was a bit clearer. Overall, it’s a solid toothbrush for the price.
I love it! It's a great value for the price! Had another brand for years, but I really love this toothbrush better than my old one! Plus, it's rechargeable

Love this tooth brush, I've bought before for myself. This one was for my husband. All the different cleaning settings are amazing and I love that is has a lot of replacement heads. Great price, quick shipping, good quality, overall great product.

Id give this product and company 10 stars if I could! A great electric toothbrush that work just as well as ones 10x the price. When mine stopped holding a charge a quick message to the seller resulted in a replacement. Its so refreshing to see a company stand by their product. 10/10 product and company.

I bought three of these. Two are still working and one is not. The attachment for the toothbrush is loose and pushes inside the tube so the toothbrush doesn’t attach to the notch to hold it in place. I missed the return window. I’m going to contact seller and see if they will replace the broken one. Other than the broken one The toothbrush itself works great. It keeps charged for awhile before needing a charge and there are a few options for comfort level. I like the toothbrush head as well.
satisfied with this toothbrush. Great battery life. several modes but not all useful

This Toothbrush is amazing. I've never been able to own a Toothbrush like this one. Coming from a certain OB type one its certainly refreshing to have a toothbrush that works in a completely different way and cleans even better than my old one ever did. It has a 'sonic' vibrating motor inside that is very powerful and moves the brush head considerably more than my old toothbrush so it can reach more area of the teeth and get into places your old one couldn't. The toothbrush has many settings, Clean, Polish, Milder, White and Massage (Each Setting Shown in the video). A con of the device would possibly be that even though it comes with a USB-C charger that it does in fact take 2 hours to fully charge, which if your in a hurry to get somewhere and it has died, you can bet you will be leaving the house without brushed teeth. However the pro fact here majorly outweighs the con, this is because the actual life of the battery is immense. When I purchased this product about a month ago, before writing this review, I have only charged it once and it still seems to have loads of power left. Once! A single charge in an entire month! In certainly did not expect this. This is absolutely amazing given that my last toothbrush had the life expectancy of a few days to a week. Even less as the old toothbrush was very old and I thought it was time for an upgrade, and you can bet, I got one! The actual brush head has lasted the entire month too. Its not warped in any particular way that makes it look old but in fact makes it still look brand new. (As shown in the video). This, coupled with the 8 extra brush heads leads to the conclusion that this toothbrush might last an entire year, or more, without having to pay any extra money for replacement brush heads, something which I found myself constantly doing with my old Toothbrush which in turn cost a lot of money just for the heads themselves. I also noticed that the toothbrush works and cleans your teeth even without Toothpaste, of course I only tried this as a one off experiment to see what all the fuss was about regarding the sonicare technology and to see if it genuinely cleared the plaque off my teeth and to my surprise, it did a good job. (This may not be the same result for everyone as this was only tried once, and not again, so please do not take my word for it.) All in all, I would say that this product is a very good one, its affordable, uses newer sonicare tech instead of a rotating brush head, saves you money in the long term and can last an entire month on a single charge! Id definitely recommend this product to anyone, especially someone like myself who needed an upgrade from an outdated one to a cheap affordable one that gets the job done and done well. Would definitely recommend. Thank you for reading. P.S. I would like to add, at this time of posting this review, I cannot upload any photos or videos due to a problem with my phone, however, I can assure that upon reading this review, you should be able to use the given information (and other information on reviews on this product) to be able to possibly make a good decision to upgrade to a brand new toothbrush that is definitely worth the upgrade. Thank you for reading.
Soft toothbrush heads, come with a large supply, battery life is great, effect at cleaning teeth, good quality and pretty, so many different settings and quite powerful
delivered with several replacement brushes, several brushing modes, works very well, holds the charge for a long time, very good value for money 👍🏻
so far so good. having the extra brush heads is handy

Take in mind when you read most electric toothbrush reviews, they are coming from manual so OF COURSE YOUR TEETH FEEL AMAZING AND CLEAN, but what about when you’re coming from a really good electric toothbrush (Phillips Sonicare and another cheaper one that both felt like improvements after manual) and there are so many choices without a clear understanding what makes one $79 while another is over $200? I started to go a little crazy trying to figure it out. I asked one dentist to suggest and she said either oral b or sonicare (she doesn’t sell them at the office) while another said oral b (he did sell them) so that was not really helpful. When pressed my dentist who doesn’t sell them prefers oral b and she likes the smaller head. I GET THAT NOW! It’s like I’m polishing each tooth and wrapping the head around the tooth almost and I LOVE THAT! I think the Phillips isn’t getting in between near as well. The thing about either brand is that there is such a wide price range that I couldn’t tell the real $100 difference other than maybe an app and possibly more cleaning modes but that’s about it. I decided to go with oral b to try this round more precise head and went to their website to take the quiz to see what was best for me and this is where I landed. I wanted to stay under $100 (and you can on Black Friday and other big sales but I missed it and paid $119 which isn’t terrible if it’s significantly better than my last electric). I just used it for the first time and MY TEETH FEEL AMAZING , in fact my whole mouth feels so clean. I’m someone who buys a firmer bristle head (NOT HARD but I need to feel scrubbed if makes sense). I think sometimes I may be hard on my gums trying to really scrub my teeth but the happy medium is in this oral b brush head! I’m just not clear which one it is as it came with 2 and says one is ultimate clean and the other is gentle care. I’m assuming it’s ultimate but it’s soft but really dense and just scrubs but it’s gentle on the gums. Love it. Very satisfied. It’s not loud at all and it’s got a great light sensor that indicates when you’re at the perfect pressure. I actually found it quite helpful and it’s clearly visible even if you’re not looking in the mirror. I’m kind of excited about the app because after a long lifetime of heat checkups, something has gone wrong and I’m facing some pretty big restorative dental work so perhaps I’ve been slacking I don’t know But I’m trying to be very diligent and that’s part of the reason for the new purchase. I also felt like my old one wasn’t getting me as clean as it used it so it could be I needed something more aggressive. This is really perfect and considering the price tags you can easily go up to on the big name models, I think this really is the sweet spot for an electric toothbrush ESPECIALLY IF YOU’RE NOT COMING FROM MANUAL. If you’re coming from manual, any real electric toothbrush will be so impressive but I needed to be impressed after exclusively using electric. This is it. I’ve got no doubt about the battery life.. they are all that way.. the travel case is a great touch and it’s nice. Nothing like having your electric toothbrush go off in your closed suitcase when you’re all packed. lol. I was always able to get off brand replacement heads for my sonicare that were great at a fraction of the price. I’ll be interested to see if I can get a real match to this one otherwise it may be worth it to stick brand name. Here’s to your dental health and perfect check ups.

review_title: Great toothbush - your dentist will love you again
body_en: This is truly an amazing toothbrush. I find this does a much better job of cleaning my teeth and removing plaque. The features are pretty cool-it's the little things, right? You can change the colors of light (where the pressure sensor is) with multiple options. It has a magnetic charger at the base. The case has a charger feature which is a great feature-it comes with a cord and a power adapter-you can't even get that for $1300 cell phones anymore. It even has an interactive display-yes I like the smiley face when I'm done. I haven't tried the app yet, I've been brushing for a long time without one but I'll give it a shot because I do enjoy technology. This is quieter than my first Oral B but still sounds like a small drone in my head, still fairly quiet. The bristles are comfortable. Battery life is pretty good so far. Best part? I got it for a great deal when it was on sale last week. This is light years better than their competitor (rhymes with monic air) which I purchased for a lot more and wish I had returned when I had the chance. I hate it so much I'm willing to give a $200 toothbrush away. It may not be the newest in the iO line but I'm really impressed so far. Time will tell on how durable it is but I'm going to stay with the Oral Be family.

I have been using this for a month, I normally only brush once a day because of my rushed schedule. I have noticed a whiter smile and cleaner feeling teeth. My son loves this, every night I brush my teeth with this using the app and at the same time he copies the directions with his normal toothbrush. It takes us 2 min 20 seconds to get a perfect clean score and at 10yrs old he is ok with that. The app shows you when to change sections of your teeth and how much pressure to use with customizable colors. its a little spendy but worth it for the clean feeling . It lasts about 6 brushes per charge and can charge in or out of the case. The app is easy to use and even with out the app the brush communicates to you through color about how much pressure to use.

review_title: Great Value, Thoughtful Design, and a Noticeably Better Clean
body_en: This toothbrush turned out to be a great purchase. I spent a lot of time comparing models, reading reviews, and trying to stay within a reasonable price range, and the Oral-B iO Deep Clean with Protect checked all the right boxes. It feels well-designed and comfortable to use, and the clean is noticeably better than a standard electric toothbrush without being harsh on my gums. The brushing experience feels controlled and thorough rather than aggressive, which I really appreciate. Setup was easy, charging is straightforward, and overall it feels like a quality product that delivers exactly what it promises. I’m very happy with this purchase and would recommend it to anyone looking for an effective, reliable electric toothbrush without going overboard on cost.

review_title: It's a nice toothbrush - but be watchful of the inside of the brush head, it can become moldy
body_en: Wow. This Oral B is a big improvement over the one I replaced. It’s whisper quiet in comparison, and I really like the pressure sensor light (green if good pressure, red if too much pressure, white if too little pressure). I also like that I can set the brush mode (speed) to “sensitive”, which is what I use exclusively with a sensitive brush head. My older Oral B only oscillated. This newer one both oscillates and micro-vibrates. My old Oral B was about 10-12 yrs old. It still worked perfectly. Buying sensitive brushes had become fairly inexpensive. I’m pretty sure it would have kept on working at least another 5 yrs. However, my hygienist repeatedly told me: “You’re not doing this, you’re not doing that, blah blah blah.” Tiresome. Sometimes the brush would strike under the gum line around a crown and cause lingering pain. I learned about the new Oral B with the pressure sensor and decided to buy one. Here was the surprising thing to me: I wasn’t brushing hard enough, at least according to the pressure sensor. The first time I used it, I was repeatedly in the white zone (too little pressure). Also, here’s the thing that really did it for me, I didn’t really know how to brush correctly. I found a video on YouTube (“Tips On How To Brush with an Oral B Electric Toothbrush” by Murmann Dental Health) that explained and demonstrated exactly how to brush using an Oral B with pressure sensor. That was very illuminating. I highly recommend that or a similar video. The thing that stood out from the video was that our teeth are rounded, so we need to wrap the brush around each individual tooth . I’ve been following what I learned in the video. So far, the brush hasn’t caused pain under the gum line. The IO sensitive brush along with the “sensitive” setting on the device have been a more comfortable brushing experience for me. I’m consistently in the green zone. Hopefully, it all makes a difference at my next dental appointment. I was sorry to see my old Oral B go as it was still useful, but sometimes useful doesn’t mean effective or appropriate for teeth & gum challenges. It can still be useful for other purposes. I have never used the app, so no comment there. The travel case is very nice and will come in handy. The only thing I don’t like about it is it doesn’t include storage for what seems to be a proprietary charger. The charger is two-pin, and I guess it’s supposedly safer to use in wet environments; you may need to include it in your travel bag depending on your travel time. 5 stars from me.

My original Oral-B electric toothbrush died partway through brushing so I replaced it. I thought I was getting basically the same version and for the most part it is the same. This is a Smart version which is new. I liked using the app to set it up the way I like it but there’s no way I’m going to try to keep track of whether I brush each area of my mouth adequately. Otherwise it works well and as expected. I don’t find it to be any noisier than my last one but it did cost quite a bit more.

review_title: Worth upgrading from an older model
body_en: I bought my first oral b in 2016, what would be the equivalent of this model back then. I’ve thoroughly enjoyed it, and used it religiously all these years and it’s still going strong but the rubber face is starting to degrade so I figured I’d upgrade. I was NOT expecting the technology to have advanced so much, it is MUCH more powerful than the old style, with much less vibration and noise. It feels like I’m achieving the same clean in half the time with this one, and the new brush head style doesn’t have that stupid hole that dribbles toothpaste slobber all over your face like the old one. The screen is an added “cool factor” but doesn’t really offer a life changing upgrade aside from being able to see the battery percentage. The new charging dock design is nice, makes it easier to wipe clean without the little peg in the middle. All in all, this is a very nice upgrade and well worth the price. Here’s to the next 10 years of compliments from my dentist!

review_title: Best Toothbrush Ever - and it Smiles at You!!
body_en: I never thought I'd pay this kind of price for a toothbrush, but this one is absolutely worth the cost. It is comfortable to use, and the brush head works great, I love that it has timing and buzzes so that you know if you've brushed long enough in each area. The charging is one of the best parts, because you just set it on the charger and it works. Took it on vacation and the carry case is the best, it keeps the brush clean and best of all, it charges while in the case. This is so easy to use, and I'm glad I took the chance and bought this. And even as an adult, there is something satisfying about a toothbrush that smiles at you when you've done a good job of brushing.
Plugs are totally inappropriate for Australia. I don’t know if there is a safe adapter. I couldn’t find one on the Amazon website that even seemed possible I’m about to return i

review_title: Meilleur brosse à dents avec un suivis avec l’application
body_en: After several weeks of use, I can say that the Oral-B iO7 electric toothbrush has far exceeded my expectations. From the first use, you feel a real difference in the cleanliness of your teeth. They are smooth, clean and feel like a professional cleaning at the dentist. The grip is excellent and the brush is very comfortable to use. The different brushing modes allow cleaning to be adapted according to needs, whether for daily, gentle or more intensive cleaning. The pressure sensor is a great addition, as it helps avoid brushing too hard and protects the gums. Battery life is very good and recharging is simple thanks to the magnetic base. I also like the Oral-B app, which allows you to track each brushing session, see if all areas of the mouth have been properly cleaned, obtain statistics on your habits and receive advice on improving your technique. This is a very useful feature that helps you adopt a better oral hygiene routine. Strong points: * Exceptional cleaning and feeling of very clean teeth. * Quiet and very pleasant operation. * Multiple brushing modes suitable for different needs. * Effective pressure sensor to protect gums. * Detailed monitoring of brushing with the Oral-B application. * Personalized advice and progress statistics. * Excellent battery life. * Premium build quality. * Convenient magnetic charging. In summary, the Oral-B iO7 is a very high quality electric toothbrush that offers a brushing experience significantly superior to a manual brush. The features connected with the app add real value by allowing you to track and improve your brushing habits over time. Despite a higher price, the performance, comfort of use and features more than justify the investment. I recommend it without hesitation to anyone wishing to improve their oral hygiene.

The brush is good, it is easy to set up and in general it is very simple to use and the results are quite good once you learn how to use it well. However, I would recommend purchasing this brush elsewhere, since they sent me a previously opened product, I noticed this because the packaging came resealed with Amazon tape, and there were some scratches on the product and its accessories, and they were a little dirty and everything came out of order. I was too lazy to return it because it was shipped internationally so I kept it, the only thing I'm sure was new are the heads because they did come sealed in their original packaging. I'm giving it two stars because giving it one doesn't do the brush justice.
Brush works great. Only problem is the recharging case does not charge itself and therefore is a big waste.

review_title: Oral B rechargeable electronic toothbrush series 7.
body_en: I absolutely love this toothbrush. I had an old Oral B that just fell apart after 12+ years. It's an excellent product. Does a great job and the battery lasts quite a long time. It's a bit costly even on sale but well worth it. Any Oral B product is very good as the less expensive ones will do a great job too!

review_title: A great option over a standard toothbrush
body_en: What started as having just one of these in our household has turned into the whole family using these Sonicare toothbrushes. Having considered all the various models this particular one proved perfect for our use case. We have 5 of these in our household. We do have the white and black models and either are based on preference but over time I tend to think that even though the black (this model) might show residue easier that also makes it easier to see and clean and it's possible the white could discolor over time. The travel case is a nice feature to have. Have not traveled with it as of yet to see how functional and how much room it may consume if trying to travel light but it's there. The is not enough room to also store the charger in the case but will hold the handle and the brush (separated from the handle) in the included durable travel case. It does come with two additional brushes which is nice. The charging base is a standard two prong plug. Be cautious as some models seem to have a USB charging base that would require an additional purchase of a charger to charge in a standard outlet. This model has three settings with lighting for each. The bottom of the two buttons easily move through each setting with each press. There is a low battery indicator as well. Brushing with this is amazing. It's much more effective than a standard toothbrush or any standard electric toothbrush used over time. Even the kids notice how much cleaner their teeth seem after a use. Brushing harder is not good on teeth as any dentist has told me over time so this brush helps regulate how you brush. You don't have to brush with the Sonicare. The Sonicare does the brushing. You can simply slowly guide the brush over your teeth and let the Sonicare do its job. If the brush is pressed too hard against the teeth the Sonicare vibrations will halt as a sign you are trying to brush too hard. Overall this device is highly recommended and it's even better if you watch for a good deal that does or had occurred periodically.

It took me awhile before I figured out how to not spray the mirror but this tooth cleaning tool is fabulous and I recommend it ASAP. My dentist was so impressed he ordered them for the office to sell. It charges but I never leave it off the charger. You can message your gums, clean as well as remove particles in your teeth. Fabulous. The brushes get accustom but once you do it’s easy peasy. Teeth are white and very clean.

I have had better service from this unit than previous Philips Sonicare models, so I'm a happy fellow. Charging is easy; just place the unit onto the charging pin on the platform. Material is sturdy and quite waterproof and it is a good weight for sturdy application without fatigue. I've tried to wear the battery down for travel and couldn't do so over a couple of days continuous discharging and still going strong. It's especially good for gum care along with tooth cleaning. I also like the 2-minute operating length with beeps every 30 seconds.

review_title: I like brushing my teeth with it
body_en: I am a lifelong manual medium bristles toothbrush user. Over the years, I have seen electric toothbrushes in my friend's and family's bathrooms and never thought I would ever want to use one. After doing some research, I decided to buy this electric toothbrush. At first, I was not sure if the small brush head would do as good of a job as my standard size manual toothbrush. It took me two days and four brushings to get use to it. The small brush head did a better job at cleaning my teeth. I can not believe how clean my teeth feel after brushing 2 minutes with this toothbrush. Even my gumline has felt cleaner after brushing with this thing multiple times for a week. With my manual toothbrush, there were times I could feel that my gumline was not as clean as it should be. Never once did I irritate my gums while brushing like I did with my manual toothbrush many of times. The electric toothbrush pressure sensor prevented me from doing that to my gums. The 2-minute timer for the clean mode is good for me. After brushing teeth, I switch the intensity to the gum care mode to clean my gums. I like how the brush head replacement reminder and pressure sensor can be deactivated if you do not like those features. My traveling case struggles to stay closed. I may have to buy a different one for traveling with this electric toothbrush. I am impressed with it and wished that I would have bought one of these years ago. 1-24-26 I'm not impressed with the charger. If I use the toothbrush until the battery indicator starts to flash auburn color LED, it takes more than eight hours to fully charge the battery. There is not enough counter space for me to keep the toothbrush docked on the charger. My Philips Norelco All-in-One Series 9000 Trimmer, Wahl Pro Series Detail Trimmer, and Wahl Lithium Ion Pro Rechargeable Cordless Hair Clippers all charge faster than this thing. Heck, a Dewalt 6Ah battery chargers faster than this toothbrush.

After 3 years it's time for a new one. It held the charge for weeks and was reliable. Eventually it started to wobble and the head doesn't get the same contact to clean as well. I didn't realize how long I've had it. Pretty good.

This toothbrush is great, gets my teeth clean, easy to charge, etc but whats even better is Philips customer service. This model stopped working after about 6 months of use, and I reached out to customer service and they sent us a brand new -upgraded- model. WOW!

after trying this i could never go back to a normal toothbrush, actually life changing, the heads last a couple months easily, the battery lasts for long enough to not bother me, and its very comfortable to use, insane value for money, i got it for 55$

I purchased a Philips Sonicare toothbrush expecting it to last much longer than six months. Unfortunately, after only a few months of use, it started becoming noticeably louder and the cleaning performance seemed to gradually get worse. I contacted Phillips customer support directly through their website. They sent me a new upgraded version at no charge under warranty. It was a quick and easy process. I did learn that this model has been discontinued, likely due to product faults, but given they honor their 2 year warranty with an upgraded model, I was very pleased. 5 stars for Phillips - I just can’t recommend this particular model of sonicare
excellent product

review_title: My Old Fave Got Replaced, And This Did Even Better
body_en: I bought this toothbrush because my old model that’s no longer made had quietly become my go‑to—and I’m thrilled this one kept all the features I loved and then added a few extras. It came highly recommended by my dentist, and I’ve been using it steadily since. It gives that same clean, confident feeling and upgrades things like pressure sensing and smarter modes. Pros: Pressure sensor alerts you if you’re brushing too hard, love this for protecting my gums. Three cleaning modes (Clean / White / Gum Care), gives flexibility depending on what my mouth needs. BrushSync tech: the handle knows when the brush head needs replacing, so you’re not guessing. Travel case included, long battery life, solid extras. Cons: It’s a bit more expensive than my previous toothbrush, but honestly, worth it for the functionality. If you absolutely cannot stand any kind of tech beep or smart reminder, the extra features might feel like “too much.” I’m still waiting to see how long the rechargeable battery lasts compared to the old model. Final Thoughts: If you’re upgrading from a standard electric brush or your model is now discontinued (like mine), this one hits the spot. It keeps the trusted parts I loved and adds smart features I didn’t know I needed. Would absolutely recommend for anyone serious about brushing right.

review_title: Great set especially if you have dental implants

### Design and Build Quality: The Oral-B Pro 1000 features a simple, ergonomic design that is easy to handle. It has a rubberized grip that ensures a secure hold, even when wet. The toothbrush comes with a single CrossAction brush head, which is angled to effectively reach between teeth and along the gum line. The design is durable, though it lacks some of the premium materials found in higher-end models. The toothbrush is available in a few different color options, typically white with blue or black accents. ### Cleaning Performance: The Pro 1000 is equipped with a 3D cleaning action that oscillates, rotates, and pulsates to break up and remove plaque. This technology, combined with the CrossAction brush head, provides a thorough cleaning experience that is superior to manual brushing. Many users report a noticeable improvement in the cleanliness of their teeth and a reduction in plaque buildup. However, it doesn’t offer the same level of customization or advanced features as more expensive models, such as multiple cleaning modes or pressure sensors. ### Battery Life: The toothbrush operates on a rechargeable battery that lasts about 7-10 days on a full charge, assuming two minutes of brushing twice a day. The battery life is decent, but it falls short of some higher-end models that offer up to two weeks or more. The Pro 1000 does not have a battery level indicator, so users need to be mindful of when it needs to be recharged. ### Features: The Oral-B Pro 1000 is relatively basic in terms of features. It includes a built-in two-minute timer with 30-second intervals, which helps ensure users brush for the recommended amount of time and spend equal time on each quadrant of the mouth. However, it lacks additional features like multiple brushing modes, Bluetooth connectivity, or a travel case. This simplicity might appeal to users who prefer a straightforward brushing experience without the need for extra bells and whistles. ### Value for Money: The Pro 1000 is competitively priced, making it an attractive option for those seeking an effective electric toothbrush without spending a premium. It offers solid performance for the price, providing a significant upgrade over manual toothbrushes and some lower-end electric models. While it lacks some advanced features, it delivers on the essentials of oral hygiene, making it a good value for most users. ### Conclusion: The Oral-B Pro 1000 CrossAction Electric Toothbrush is a great option for those looking for a reliable and effective toothbrush without the complexity or cost of higher-end models. It excels in basic cleaning performance and ease of use, making it suitable for both new and experienced electric toothbrush users. While it doesn’t have many extra features, it covers the essentials well, providing good value for money.

review_title: Great for the price, just needs some tweeking
body_en: So I've waited about a month since I putchased this toothbrush to give you an honest review. The toothbrush works really well, you can see and feel that the majority of what you're getting are the toothbrush heads. I've been using the type with blue and white brissles and it's held up well. Now, I liked how the toothbrush head clicks and locks into place, so you know it's not going to fall off. The handle is fairly easy to hold but nothing spectacular about that. Additionally all the heads and the extras you get are great, BUT to charge you have to use the supplied charger, why not a universal type USB-C that everyone is using nowadays. Secondly I feel slightly uncomfortable that the charging port does not have a cap on it, so the toothbrush handle ends with a flat, blunt edge where you use the adapter to charge. And if you're like me, I brush my teeth in the shower in the morning, so I know it's being exposed to water and toothpaste ECT. That is the only reason for the 4 stars and not 5. -No universal charger port, no cover to the charging port and handle is fairly inexpensive feeling, however it is a good toothBRUSH and for the price you pay it is worth the investment. I feel if they fix those few things they'd be right up there with Phillips and other well known toothbrush makers. 4 out of 5 with potential to be a solid 5 with some fine tooning.

Item is as described. I got the peach pink color and I would just call it pink. It’s pretty. It arrived charged. Thorough user manual. I love that it is quiet; my old one was clanking loudly. I love that it is well regarded by the industry experts for a price that is very reasonable. I’ve only had it a few days; so far so good.

First, there are two types of electric toothbrushes. True electric and ultrasonic. True electric toothbrushes have heads that spin, etc. They provide spin or rotation to the bristles needed to brush your teeth so all you have to do is move the brush across your teeth. If this is what you want, then skip this set. Then there are ultrasonic toothbrushes, like this one. These toothbrushes have heads that just vibrate. There is no spin or rotation to push the bristles between and around your teeth. You still need to physically run the brush back and forth, in a circular motion, etc, for them to work. With that clarified, this brush works great. The head a nice size - not too big, not too small. The bristles are firm but not scratch off your enamel hard - as long as you don't use too much pressure. The head has longer bristles on either side that reach between your teeth and along your gum lines. The toothbrush stops vibrating for a moment every 30 seconds and then turns off at 2 minutes. This allows you to time your brushing by quadrant (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right). This makes it easy for those non-morning folks who suddenly realize they've been brushing one tooth for 5 minutes (you'll understand if this is you). The vibrations take a bit of getting used to - in some modes they can tickle your gums. Each mode is supposed to be for a specific use: White, Clean, Soft, Polish, Gum Care. The modes appear to simply change the amount of vibration - white being the strongest and gum care being the weakest. I would suggest just finding the mode you are most comfortable with and staying with that. Yes, you DO need to put the brush in your mouth BEFORE you turn it on. Just like you put the lid on the blender before turning it on. If you don't, then there WILL be a mess. This is not a failing of the toothbrush, it is simply the nature of the beast. I like that it comes with 8 heads. I've had other electric toothbrushes only to find after 3-6 months that I couldn't get replacement heads for them anymore. At this price point ($20 as of this review), if I can't get replacement heads after going through the 8 included, then I've still spent less than if I was buying standard toothbrushes. The heads do fit snugly and securely. The more you switch them out, the weaker that connection will be, and a head could come out during brushing due to the vibrations. I recommend you buy separate toothbrushes for each member of the family rather than trying to share and switch heads out daily. The toothbrush holder is simple but effective. It keeps the head protected while allowing it to air dry and it holds the toothbrush for convenient access. I attached the cover to a textured high gloss wall next to the sink and it has stayed in place without issue. The cover opens with just a light pull on the toothbrush so there is no fighting to get your toothbrush out. Overall, I highly recommend this toothbrush if you are looking for an ultrasonic (vibrating not spinning or rotating) toothbrush.

review_title: Powerful dual Sonicare set with great features
body_en: I purchased the Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9000 Electric Toothbrush as a 2-pack (black and white) and have been very happy with the overall quality and performance. Having two handles in one package is extremely convenient—for example, one for home and one for travel, or one for myself and one for a partner—without needing to buy a second set separately. The build quality feels solid, and both brushes look sleek and modern, with a premium finish that matches the price point. In terms of brushing performance, the sonic cleaning is excellent. My teeth feel noticeably smoother and cleaner compared to a standard manual toothbrush, and the different modes make it easy to tailor the experience to daily cleaning, gum care, or more intensive polishing. The pressure sensor and timing guidance are genuinely useful; they help prevent brushing too hard and encourage you to cover the full mouth evenly, which is a nice touch for long-term gum and enamel health. The app connectivity is a bonus, especially if you like data and feedback. It can help reinforce better brushing habits and highlight areas you might be missing, though it does add a layer of complexity—Bluetooth pairing and checking the phone during brushing isn’t for everyone. Battery life has been good so far, but you do need to stay on top of charging both handles, especially if you’re traveling frequently or using multiple modes. Overall, this dual-handle DiamondClean 9000 set is a great choice if you want top-tier cleaning performance, smart features, and a premium look, and you value having two brushes in one package. The cost is on the higher side, but if oral health and convenience are priorities, it’s a strong investment.

Love my Sonicare! Gave the black one to my son. Price was fantastic and the settings are great. The charger cup is super cute and the rechargeable case is a must! I needed a new toothbrush, and was very happy to find this set. I got it during Amazon prime day and it was much cheaper than I have seen it in stores. I had the same diamond clean, but the last version of it. This one definitely vibrates with more intensity. It cleans really well. The quality is great. I had the glass with my last toothbrush and the glass can still fit on top of this charger or you can use it with the plastic charger. I have been using it with the plastic charger instead of the glass. It seems more compact that way. It charges with no issues and it has an app that connects to the toothbrushes and it tells you how long that you’ve been brushing each day and how many times a day that you’re brushing and it gives you goals. I really like that new feature. It’s makes it fun to be able to see how long I’ve been brushing my teeth.

Okay, if you are reading this and the price is higher than $199, WAIT. It goes down to $199 fairly regularly-- at least it did 2-3 times this year (including prime day), and did last year for Black Friday sales. I LOVE my sonicare. You will have to pry it out of my cold, dead, hands. It makes brushing so much easier, and I like the light when you are brushing too hard, which I've heard dentists say is a pretty bad thing. The battery life is great-- a solid 2-3 weeks out of one charge. I love that I can charge it, go on a week's vacation, and not worry about bringing the charger. I just throw a cover on the brush head and toss in my carry-on (note: since it is a rechargeable battery, please put it in your carry-on). The cover for the brush head is useless, so use something else when putting it in luggage. It has 4-5 different modes-- whitening, gum sensitivity, deep cleaning, etc. I like the whitening one, which is 2 min 40 seconds. It buzzes every 20 seconds to get you to move on to the next section. You can choose from strong, medium, or mild vibration. And the strong one is STRONG. I feel my head buzz when I use it, lol, so I normally stick to the medium. My teeth feel so much cleaner when using this, and I love the discipline it gives me. However, I have seen this vary in price from $199-399. Please don't buy it when it's at its high price. You can get a much better deal!

I’ve been using the Philips Sonicare DiamondClean electric toothbrush and I’m really impressed with the results. It has a very comfortable brushing experience with gentle but effective vibrations, so it doesn’t feel harsh on gums. The battery lasts a long time, and the charging glass/travel case is actually very convenient and looks nice on the counter. review_title: ★★★★★ Great upgrade from a manual toothbrush
body_en: I’ve been using the Sonicare 7300 for a few weeks now and it’s made a noticeable difference in how clean my teeth feel. The pressure sensor is genuinely useful — it lights up if I’m brushing too hard, which I didn’t realize I was doing with my old brush. The SmarTimer keeps me honest about brushing the full two minutes, and it pulses every 30 seconds to remind you to switch quadrants. Having 12 different brushing settings might sound like overkill, but I actually use a few of them — the gum care mode is gentler on my gums, and the whitening setting feels more thorough for the odd coffee stain. Battery life is excellent — I’m easily getting close to the advertised 21 days on a single charge, so I’m not scrambling to find the charger during travel. The included travel case is a nice touch and keeps everything protected in my bag. Only minor gripe: it’s a bit pricier than a standard electric toothbrush, and replacement brush heads add up over time. But for the overall brushing experience and results, it’s worth it. Bottom line: A solid, feature-packed electric toothbrush that’s easy to recommend if you want something better than a basic model without going full premium.

review_title: A new level in toothbrush performance, but no wall plug and an intrusive app
body_en: This toothbrush appears to live up to the extravagant claim on the box. I have no way of knowing if the amount of plaque removed is actually 2000% more than what my previous Sonicare could do, but it is a huge improvement. I used to believe the job of an electric toothbrush was to pound my gums into submission, but this model is far more gentle and does a better job of reaching the tricky trouble spots my dentist never tires of pointing out. So I do recommend this product with almost no reservations. But before you open the box you should know that the power cord is a USB-A plug, wall unit not included. Phillips says this is to cut down on electronic waste, which is such an obvious euphemism for "it saves us money" that you wonder why they even bothered. Also, the Sonicare 7300 has Bluetooth connectivity, and you can download an app and connect to, um, your toothbrush. I said what the heck I'll give it a try. The app says it values your privacy but then it doesn't let you complete setup unless you agree to send all data to Phillips so they can help you with suggestions for improving your dental hygiene. Then the home screen comes up and it's a dental chart, at which point I killed the app and uninstalled it. Perhaps you might find such detailed help useful, but I'm not interested in being an unpaid beta tester or belonging to a floating focus group for future products. I've been using a Sonicare for years and will continue to do so. But the way this product is packaged and presented seems to make it just another way that big business is trying to carve off a big slice of my conscious awareness. And I’m getting tired of that. But before you open the box you should know that the power cord is a USB-A plug, wall unit not included. Phillips says this is to cut down on electronic waste, which is such an obvious euphemism for "it saves us money" that you wonder why they even bothered. Also, the Sonicare 7300 has Bluetooth connectivity, and you can download an app and connect to, um, your toothbrush. I said what the heck I'll give it a try. The app says it values your privacy but then it doesn't let you complete setup unless you agree to send all data to Phillips so they can help you with suggestions for improving your dental hygiene. Then the home screen comes up and it's a dental chart, at which point I killed the app and uninstalled it. Perhaps you might find such detailed help useful, but I'm not interested in being an unpaid beta tester or belonging to a floating focus group for future products. I've been using a Sonicare for years and will continue to do so on the advice of my dentist. But the way this product is packaged and presented makes it just another way that big business is trying to carve off yet another slice of my conscious awareness, and I’m getting tired of that.

review_title: A good value for the uses you'll get out it.
body_en: this toothbrush is a good value for the money, since it is packaged with a charging base, travel case, and 3 replacement toothbrush heads. You can also set it up to auto deliver the heads when they get worn out. The auto delivery is easy to do, just follow the instructions that will be on the Amazon website. The appearance is black, with other colors available. The size is right for the use by family members of all ages that are capable of using it. The handle is durable and sturdy. The handle is light weight and not too heavy to use. The vibration will take some getting used to, as it tickles the gums, for first time users. It will clear up in about a week or so. It has green LEDs that show the current charge, then turn amber when you need to change the brush head. I recommend it to anybody that needs a reliable toothbrush, that isn't a hard-to-find item.

review_title: The Toothbrush That Thinks It’s Better Than Me… and Honestly Is
body_en: The Philips Sonicare 7300 doesn’t just clean your teeth — it judges your entire dental existence. In the best way. The first time I turned it on, I swear it sounded like it was saying, “Move aside, amateur, I’ve got this.” And it did. This thing blasts plaque off your teeth like it’s clearing a runway. My mouth hasn’t felt this clean since the day I grew my first tooth. The pressure sensor lights up like a tattletale every time you brush too hard. The timer keeps you honest. The brush heads feel like they were engineered by NASA for enamel. And the clean afterward? Unreal. My teeth are so smooth I’m convinced I could butter toast with them. It’s powerful, it’s smart, it’s slightly condescending — and it’s absolutely fantastic. Five stars. My dentist is going to weep with joy.

This toothbrush is amazing. I've had an older model for years. This model is a dramatic improvement. From the function, clean teeth feeling, to less operating noise - this brush is a winner. Also, the charging stand uses a USB cable that does not come with a plug-in charging block.

You think you spent 200 dollars on a toothbrush, but you use it and you think, “Man, I should’ve gotten this sooner.” Your teeth never feel cleaner. It automatically shuts off after 2 minutes and it has a pressure sensor. Although I found myself not wanting to put much pressure on my teeth at all because this thing vibrates so loudly and fast that if I pressed any harder, my gums would be obliterated. The charging base is cool. It doesn’t come with a charging brick, though. You can also charge it with the included travel case, but that requires Philip’s proprietary charger. (Which is also included.) Luckily, it shares the same charger as Philip’s water flosser so I can just carry one charger while I’m travelling for both. Finally, it comes with two extra brush heads. So you have 9 months of brush usage before you’d buy a replacement.

review_title: Lighter touch than others; higher vibration speed; does a fine job on only one battery.
body_en: I have always used the Arm & Hammer Spin-Brush, and now that it is no longer available, had to find a replacement. I specifically wanted one that used batteries, so I don't have to fuss with a charger when on a trip. I was frankly concerned that there were no two-battery units like the Spin Brush, worried that a one-battery unit would not be as aggressive as I would like. And when I first used this one, it seemed less forceful, so my concern remained. Over a few days I realized that this brush vibrates a a much higher rate than the old two-battery Spin Brush, so it seemed to be doing its job just as well as my old device. In fact, it finally occurred to me that the whole idea of an electric toothbrush was to increase the brushing action rate compared to manually brushing; therefore faster is better, offsetting any lack of aggressive power. I have come to believe that this brush is every bit as good as my old one, even with only one battery. One thing I should mention though, is after several weeks I failed to notice it was moving slower. Just as an experiment I put in a new battery and voila! It began spinning at a much higher rate - I hadn't noticed it slowing down, and will now pay attention as it may need a battery every two to three weeks. That's not a problem as my old Spin Brush needed two batteries over 4 to 5 weeks, so it's basically a "break-even" on battery usage. It's been over a month since I got this brush, and in fact ordered several because they are very well priced on Amazon; I waited to review it honestly and can now say I am comfortable with the lighter touch and faster speed as a better solution to power toothbrushing. I hope this doesn't get discontinued in a couple of years now that I find it so useful!

review_title: Works well ... but wears out FAST!
body_en: Mixed feelings on this one. I've been using it for quite a few years now. I like how it works, when it works. It's just that the brush heads and the brush itself wears out a lot quicker than I like. I generally have to change the heads once a month or so. What happens is while that the bristles themselves aren't really worn down at that point, the head itself loses its back and forth rotation. It might "appear" to be still be turning, but check it in the mirror when there is pressure on it, i.e. against your teeth and gums, or test it against your fingernail, and you'll see when it's no longer effective. At that point, it's just basically vibrating in your mouth without cleaning anything. Folks who use this regularly should check for this. It took me a while to realize that after a month or so, I was merely pretending to brush my teeth but not really cleaning anything. Also, once the head wears, the seam/gap between the main piece and the rotating brush part loosens and widens quite a bit and pinches the insides of your mouth. The brush itself tends to wear out after about 4 to 5 months, where once again it still "appears" to be working, but if you check carefully, you'll find that even if you put a new head in there, the rotating properties diminish greatly. I think the inner mechanism simply wears out by then, and no longer connects and moves the brush head as well. Yes, once again, let's all thank corporate America for "Planned Obsolescence". I used to use Sonic Care. The $125 model I bought was good, but no longer held a charge after 2 years. How convenient for Sonic Care. Then I tried their battery operated $40 model, which worked OK but had a really stupidly designed battery cap which allowed water to flow into the compartment. Wow, that's TITANICALLY STUPID!!! Anyway, found this and works OK ... and have been using it since. However, not without the stated reservations. If one were to change the brush and brush heads as often as necessary (which I do), it's not really all that cheap to use. It's actually pretty expensive to use. About 10 to 12 heads and 2 or 3 brushes a year. Do the math. If I find a better alternative, I'll switch without too much nostalgia, ha ha. Note: I do want to state that my brushing routine is probably a lot more thorough and longer than most (about 5 minutes per session), so others may get a longer "effective life" than I get. But still, can't imagine their recommendation of changing the heads every 3 months being adequate. Folks who use this really should monitor the "TRUE effective life" of their brushes and heads, otherwise you might "think" you're brushing your teeth, but might actually be doing nothing to effectively "clean" them. Hope this is helpful. Cheers

review_title: Cheaper than a filling & totally worth the investment after 9 months of use
body_en: My dental hygienist recommended this toothbrush about nine months ago. When I mentioned how expensive it was, she said, “It’s still cheaper than getting a filling.” That changed how I looked at the price, so I went for it. The guided brushing app takes the guesswork out of whether I’m actually brushing everywhere. I used it twice a day in the beginning, which really helped me build better brushing habits. Nine months later, I don’t use the app every time anymore, but I still check in here and there to make sure I’m staying on track. The pressure sensor is also super helpful! My dentist mentioned that many people damage their gums and teeth by brushing too hard, and this makes it very obvious when you’re using too much pressure. I’ve had two dental cleanings since switching, and both were probably the quickest I’ve ever had. My dentist and hygienist said everything looked great with very little cleaning needed and mentioned they commonly see this with patients using an Oral-B iO. The brush heads indicate when they need replacing, which for me has been roughly every three months. They’re about $10 per replacement head, so that’s another ~$40 a year to factor into the cost. Not cheap, but reasonable enough for me considering how well the toothbrush has performed. My only complaint is that it’s can be a bit messy. Even after rinsing the head and shaking off excess water, some water/toothpaste tends to run down the handle once it’s on the charger, so I clean the charging base a couple times a week. It’s definitely an investment, but after nine months of daily use and two great dental checkups, I’m very happy I bought it.

So if you use it more than I do you might need to charge it 2 or 3 times a month. Although I don't travel, I like that it came with a travelling charging case. I just see it as an extra charger in case something happens to my regular one. review_title: Daily Brilliance: Discover the Habit-Forming Magic of the iO 9 Series
body_en: Overall Satisfaction: I give the Oral-B iO Series 9 a solid 5. This toothbrush is amazing and well worth the higher cost compared to other series. Main Purpose: I purchased this toothbrush to maintain optimal dental health and minimize the need for extensive dental procedures. Ease of Use: The toothbrush is excellent, and you can even turn on the phone to track your performance. It offers awards for meeting specific goals, some of which can be challenging to achieve. Performance: The Series 9 comes with additional sensors and a flat magnetic mount for convenient charging. While the battery drains quickly, it's not an issue for short 2-3 minute sessions. Features: The ability to visually track cleaning habits is a standout feature. With multiple modes available, I typically use sensitive, whitening, or daily settings. Durability: The toothbrush is very durable, and despite the quick battery drain, it's not problematic for regular use. Value for Money: Although expensive, the toothbrush pays for itself when considering the savings on dental bills, primarily limited to cleanings. Comparisons: Compared to other Oral-B models, the Series 9 is more advanced, with the phone app being the most significant difference. It provides detailed information about brushing habits and areas that need improvement. Pros: Maintain Oral Health: Keep your teeth clean and healthy with advanced features. App Integration: Track your brushing habits and receive feedback on the app. Charging Options: Charge the toothbrush using the magnetic mount or the convenient travel case with an attached cable. Cons: Lack of Apple Watch Compatibility: It would be more convenient if the toothbrush worked with the Apple Watch, eliminating the need to pull out the phone for information. Additional Tips: For a clean toothbrush and to avoid hardened toothpaste, use the travel charger instead of the magnetic mount. Cleaning the head after each use and washing it with water is also recommended. Recommendation: If you're looking for a top-notch toothbrush that not only ensures oral health but also provides insightful data through a dedicated app, the Oral-B iO Series 9 is worth the investment.

review_title: A baffling design flaw in a very expensive toothbrush
body_en: I bought the Oral-B iO Series 9 expecting a premium product. The toothbrush itself has a lot to recommend it, but the charging base has one of the worst design flaws I have encountered in a consumer product. The iO9 is a relatively tall, expensive electronic device, yet while charging it essentially balances upright on a small, shallow magnetic base. There is no meaningful post, socket, collar, or other mechanical support to keep the handle from tipping sideways. Because the handle is so tall, it takes remarkably little lateral force to knock it off the charger. This isn’t a hypothetical concern. I had a previous Oral-B toothbrush fall from its charger and break. With this one, I eventually stopped keeping it conveniently in the bathroom because I didn’t trust the charger to keep it secure. I actually improvised a second magnetic support against the handle when I kept it elsewhere, which dramatically improved its stability. What makes this especially frustrating is that the problem is neither difficult to foresee nor difficult to solve. Competing electric toothbrushes use charging designs that mechanically locate and support the handle. Even a modest post, recess, collar, or other positive restraint could dramatically reduce the chance of an expensive toothbrush being knocked onto a hard bathroom floor. For a flagship toothbrush at this price, this is particularly difficult to excuse. Oral-B put enormous engineering effort into the iO’s display, sensors, pressure detection, Bluetooth connectivity, brushing modes, and app integration. The company should have put comparable thought into the much simpler requirement that the toothbrush remain standing securely while it charges. Prospective buyers should know about this before purchasing because it isn’t something obvious from the feature list. If you buy one, be very careful where you place the charger

review_title: The best basic Sonicare you can buy!

Things to point out: • Brush head swap: You do get a brush head included in the box however there are different brush head options that you can purchase separately at the store. • Build quality: It feels well-made, like other Sonicare products. The built-in 2-minute timer is a nice touch to help me stick to the dentist-recommended brushing time too. It’s lightweight, easy to use right out of the box (just pop in the batteries and you’re ready), and being compatible with various Oral-B heads means I can swap to softer or more advanced heads later if I want. For the price, it’s a reliable and practical daily toothbrush that genuinely improved my oral care routine.

I've never bought into the hype of "electric toothbrushes," but I thought I would give this relatively-cheap one I saw discounted on Amazon a shot. Mainly because it came with 10 replacement heads and if the batteries ever went kaput, I could just use it as a normal, albeit bulky, toothbrush. After using it every day over the last month, I have to say that I have rather mixed feelings about this rechargeable toothbrush (words I thought I would never say). First, the positives, and there are some to be found here. The battery life, in my experience, has actually been fairly good. Though, that could likely be attributed to how low-tech this tech toothbrush actually is (we'll get to that later.) The brush is lightweight as well, allowing you to maneuver it easily. The three vibrating modes do work and offer some variation for you to test and see which you like best. The brush also has an internal timer that briefly stops the vibration every 30 seconds, ultimately shutting off after 2 minutes. I personally found this to be annoying at first, but now kind of like knowing how long I've been targeting a specific area for. And finally, yes, you could use this as a "manual" toothbrush if your forgot to charge the battery. Keep in mind that the bristles are incredibly soft, so if you like your normal toothbrushes with some tensile strength, this one might not be for you. Now for the "bad," or mediocre I guess I should say. The Teetheory toothbrush is little more than a vibrating wand with a brush attachment affixed to it. The bristles don't move, sweep, rotate, or oscillate like a more premium electric toothbrush would, so leave that fantasy behind now. Yes, the bristles do technically move, but that's just because of the vibrating motor that your brush head is on. The bristle movements are incredibly fine and gentle, to the point that you question if it's really doing any good at all. In terms of cleaning power, this is probably far from dentist-recommended. Also, if you have sensitive teeth, I wouldn't recommend this toothbrush. The vibration is all along the top portion of the brush, so if you even graze your teeth, you'll get a rather uncomfortable sensation. I personally don't have very sensitive teeth, but every time I've used this brush, I make the mistake of touching my teeth with the plastic, non-brush portion and it doesn't feel pleasant. Now, with a product like this, you have to take into account the price you're paying, which is significantly less than that of a premium electric toothbrush. I'm aware of and totally understand that. But judging this product on merit alone, I can't really say that I would wholeheartedly recommend it. Does it clean your teeth well enough? Yeah. Does it do it so well that I'll never use a normal toothbrush again? Not really. If you're truly gung-ho about dental care, would suggest spending the extra cash for a premium electric toothbrush. Specifically, one of the electric toothbrushes that actually spins. If you absolutely must have an electric toothbrush for cheap and you don't really mind it being low-tech, this will do you just fine, I suppose. As for myself, I will continue to use this brush for the foreseeable future, and hope to see if the reviews others have posted about the brush not working after a few charges are anomalies or something everyone should expect.

review_title: Slightly expensive, but a beast all around!

Ergonomically, the base of the unit fits well in my hand and is easy to maneuver. The buttons are placed in great positions so I can change the brushing modes or intensity levels easily on the fly. I keep it on a shelf mounted in the battery charger at home, but I have travelled with it a few times and the battery holds a good charge for more than a few days easily. I've never had a situation where I've taken it with me and had it run out of battery. It cleans very nicely and isn't too bulky to have any issue reaching the back molars and has great maneuverability while brushing. I like the fact that it's not very loud as far as noise, and it has convenient 30 second notifications to let you know how long you've been brushing. I typically do one quadrant for 30 seconds for a total of 2 minutes, so it's nice to have the 30 second 'buzz' go off and let me know it's time to move. Two of the coolest features about this electronic toothbrush: (1) - the pressure sensor that let's you know if you're brushing too hard. It's easy to see the light come on when I tend to put too much pressure on the head. (2) I use it in the shower so it's nice that it's mainly waterproof (even if it's not sold as that in the description) but I have been using it in the shower for a while and it's not had any issues. The travel case is nice to have when you need to pack it up and head out on the road. I stay away from home about 4-5 times a year for work and it packs up really nicely and the case obviously keeps it protected. If I had one complaint it would be the unit cost and the replacement head cost. When I first looked them up, I thought the price was crazy!! But it's held up and continues to be my favorite toothbrush of my life, and I've had many in my 50 years on this planet. If you're thinking about getting an electronic toothbrush, this one definitely delivers.

review_title: Each of these lasts about three to four months! Planned obsolescence.
body_en: I thought I'd come by and warn folks about these electric toothbrushes. See, Sonicare is a very famous brand of dental hygiene products, and the technology used here is proven to be very effective. Rapid gentle motion of a set of soft fibers-- you know. We all get it. So I've been using Philips Sonicare for many years, and I'm certain that my oral health has benefitted from that. The trouble is, Philips can't build one of these that lasts more than half a year. I keep having to replace the units because the power switch fails. One after another. The last purchase was 10 April. That's right-- just over three months ago. The rubbery membrane covering the power switch has cracked open and water has leaked into the switch, and the switch has failed. It either won't come on, or if it does finally come on, I can't then turn it off. Can you imagine? In the year 2024? Philips can't design and manufacture a power switch on a toothbrush that lasts more than a few months? Well, of course I know the answer. It's supposed to fail, and I know it. It's planned obsolescence, and I know it. I wanted to let you all know. These are very worthwhile products from the perspective of one's oral health. But the company is ripping you off intentionally. I'm at this moment going to another brand and I will not buy a Philips product of any kind again. It's a matter of principle to me. I won't. I refuse to bow down to these greedy and wasteful and arrogant corporations who try to manipulate me into more sales by intentionally manufacturing failure into their products. They are intentionally trying to arrange for us to develop habitual purchasing of their products, in repetitive cycles, again and again, and they're attempting to teach us to accept miserable quality as inevitable and only customary. I realize that this has become par for the course, and to many people it doesn't matter-- they're not bothered by constantly buying a new item, over and over and over again. I really don't care. I'm a discriminating and conscientious and logical person, and I refuse to participate in this kind of idiocy.
