review_title: Sound not as good (lacks bass even on Bass mode) as I'd hope, and some tech issues
body_en: Update 3: I am not doing "never ending updates" but just typing this to say that the issue STILL hasn't come back. The one thing I have noticed is that i am getting NO WHERE NEAR the "30 hour playtime" ... even 20 maybe pushing it. I am disappointed in that but overall ... I dont mind the speaker. Something in my reviews I thought of mentioning is that while this speaker doesn't sound as dynamic as others ... a "more even sound ... even if that means it lacks a 'thump' in the bass"... IS NOT always a bad thing ... say my Tribit XSound Surf ... listening to smooth jazz at night at low volumes ... it has "too much" of a thump ... this speaker not having that in my view ... makes this one better in some cases .... same way with my DOSS Soundbox Touch having a similar sound (but better mids/highs i think) Update 2: been a few days and "constant use" since the last update. The issue with no sound has NOT come up again yet ... and while i forgot what i have rated the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra (3.5?) i may have to bump that up to 3.75 (not to get crazy with decimals) when i say this ... but i'd give this a 3.5... yeah with certain genres it seems "flat" and lacking bass i'd like (I like a clean bass at best ... not overly done, so i am no "bass head") but other times my new favorites the Tribit XSound Gos have a "subwoofer like sound" (WHICH IS WHY it is my favorite ... at times) but late at night at low volumes i wish i could turn that extra bass off ... I BRING THAT UP due to the fact that THIS SPEAKER sort of has THAT type of sound. So with say easy listening, instrumental, and some jazz stuff in that exact situation ... i DONT DISLIKE the Tribit ... I just like the "lack of bass" (so to speak) more. I cant remember if i recommended or didn't recommend this in my original review.. to me now i'd say this is "ok" (even if that sound issue comes up where i have to play sound in a different app to get it back again, issue comes up) ... you can do better "bang for buck" but ... this is not terrible either. Update 1: Ok after trying what another reviewer said and trying to reset the speaker (pressing power button and holding for at least 8 seconds) I got things to work again. I also couldn’t get any sound in Kodi with my local media but after opening up another app and playing audio fine in that, (same device), then going back to Kodi sound in there worked again. I cant explain what happened but as I said others are having this issue too, but someone mentioned this and it worked for me. Now I plan on sort of doing part of what I planned to in the original review, I have a few other BT speaker, which include an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, two Tribit Xsound Surfs, two Tribit Xsound Gos, a DOSS Soundbox Touch and a Braven BRV1BCB BRV-1. Versus the Tribits: - to me while I wish the Xsound Surf had better battery life (ONLY ADVERTISED at 10hr) … I would still say either the Xsound Surf or the XSound GO are the better option. They are my favorites and just overall in the same price range … they are just a better value and MUCH better sound. Versus the DOSS Soundbox Touch: - This is where it is interesting. I have not done an “A-vs-B” comparision head to head but out of all my speakers, this speaker sounds closest to this one. If I remember, the bass on the DOSS seems lower at lower volumes but while not like other speakers I have or a “Sub woofer” type sound. It gets more “present” as the volume goes up. It sounds clear and balanced but not for “bass heads”. I think the DOSS may sound better than this one, however its close … I think this speaker’s tuning in the mids are a little off but like the DOSS I’d say both of these speakers are a more “balanced” sound without a subwoofer like “thump”. Versus the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra: - note: I can only compare this to the Ultra model … I hear that if you go down in Oontz models they don’t sound as good. - This is where I wish I could take the extra bass in the Ultra and put it in the X10. The bass is there in the Ultra but while not muddy in MY VIEW. It CAN “linger” a bit. Where it slightly effects the low mids and mid-mids depending on the track. This I feel is exactly what the X10 here is MISSING, EVEN ON Bass Boost mode in the built in EQ. - Build quality – even if the Ultra is NOT my favorite speaker, I still totally recommend it and like it… the build quality alone (not the only thing) blew me away, for the sub $40 price I paid for it. Versus the Braven: - I admit that I do not use this as much as I should. This was gifted to me by someone who had no use for it and .. .well I love this one. It has a decent thump in the bass but not overdone. From what I remember this sort of reminds me of a Tribit tuning … a Good V-shaped sound but clean and not “forced” or overdone. (sound wise) “Everything is where it should be” Summary: I still cant say I recommend this due to the problems I had BUT if its a “ok this is a dumb fix to a problem that shouldn’t exist in the first place” (almost a James May quote) thing if I have the no sound issue again… Ok … I am ok with keeping this and I am not as “upset” (I don’t want to ham that up) about it. The bottom line is (say the “360 sound” that is just fake marketing … If it was “this looks like a JBL Flip but this is not 360 sound .. it just LOOKS the same” … ok then) … I just cant “trust” this speaker… not until I have more time with it and it behaves fine … I will be GLAD to do a second update to report the good news, if that happens. ---------------------------------------- Original Review I was going to write a more in detail review, comparing this speaker to various others I have but unfortunately things are not looking great. I am not 100% saying I am returning this already, but it looks like it may go in that direction. I will list some Cons but .. .things are not all bad when it was working correctly… Hopefully I can not some things as I go. Cons: - Sound quality – ok this is not all bad … but I knew this would lack bass … I get it but even with a V shaped EQ on top of the speaker (same I have set in the same app for ALL others I have) ..and even in this speaker’s third EQ setting “Bass Boost” there is a lack of bass in most genres, people would typically listen to. HOWEVER one of my use cases is late at night listening to say intrumental, Jazz, or Classical music. The lack of a big “Thump” in the bass (which CAN be overdone in other speakers I have heard) … wasn’t too bad and with those genres at lower volumes … the sound quality wasn’t bad. Really I’d never call it “muddy” but even bass boost (built in EQ) sounded like there was a lack of “average bass”. ALSO THIS IS NOT 360 sound. Sure you hear sounds from all sides but the two speakers are only facing one way (the exact opposite side of where the buttons are) … that is the direction things sound “clearest” … the sound is different on any other side and with the lack of bass … including the “bass” radiators on the side as part of the “360” is laughable in itself. - Voice pompt – this wouldn’t be too bad if it wasn’t SO LOUD … late at night it a bit loud compared to say where the volume is set … “BLUETOOTH MODE” “BLUETOOTH CONNECTED” … again I’d like just a beep or something like a ton but even the voice wouldn’t be that bad IF it was a “few clicks” lower in volume. Unsure (Pro? Con?) - Build quality – I WILL SAY this doesn’t feel super cheap, but others like my Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, or any of my Tribit speakers, just feel better. I also have to say I have never had a JBL Flip or any other speakers with an “all over” grill … and I knew I was getting this so maybe versus other speakers, this “style” makes it feel less solid … I could get a JBL Flip and think “oh … they ‘feel’ the same” build quality wise. ------------------------- My main issue – I was thinking of MAYBE returning this, having my sights on a Tribit speaker I have not experienced yet, but with the other Tribit speakers I DO have, blowing me away overall, I have kept my eye on a sale for that one. Not even a week into owning this speaker, while all devices connect to the speaker, the speaker outputs ZERO audio from any COMFIRMED CONNECTED device in bluetooth mode. I do admit PART (but just half at best) use-case is the microsd card slot and one reason I wanted this speaker. In addition to Rain and Ocean waves (“sound machine style”) I wanted to load a microsd card up with that sort of stuff and say maybe smooth jazz and sort of use it as a “custom” sound machine. Right now the microsd card slot function STILL outputs audio and it doesn’t sound bad … but with no sound no matter what I do (including a speaker reset) working … in under 7 days of having this…. I cant even trust this will last. I do note that many of the negative reviews also mention this exact problem. I can live with the sound quality being “meh” at best for typical genres and this only being a good speaker in specific use-cases but now there is no audio for any bluetooth … that is a deal breaker. I just CANT recommend this speaker. While my Tribit speakers are my favorite, I will say I have an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra and sound wise it has the opposite problem (bass tends to … not make things muddy… but it’s bass “lingers a bit too long” at times) … I still LOVE and recommend that speaker.

review_title: A major smart-home upgrade, with better sound and one minor design drawback
body_en: I bought my first Echo in April 2015, back when it was simply called the “Amazon Echo.” Eleven years later, it’s still running strong. Since then, we’ve accumulated an Echo for nearly every room in our home. My daughter, who was born the same year as that original Echo, had been relegated to using it in her bedroom. We finally decided it was time for an upgrade. I wanted her to have access to Alexa+ so I could teach her how to use AI appropriately, and we also needed another Matter hub, as her room is tucked away in the corner of our apartment, and the smart shades in there weren’t always responding reliably. Since installing the Echo Dot Max, her room (and our entire smart home) has become noticeably smarter. The Matter-compatible shades now maintain a strong connection. We have them programmed to open every morning to help wake her up and close again in the evening for privacy. The built-in temperature sensor has also been surprisingly useful. It allowed me to create a routine that automatically turns on her otherwise “dumb” air conditioner when the room reaches a certain temperature. We’ve also been using Alexa+ for everyday questions, weather, music, and those random things families find themselves noodling over. I can monitor my daughter’s activity and help make sure she’s using it appropriately. Compared with the old Alexa experience, Alexa+ is a huge leap forward. It understands more natural questions, handles follow-ups, remembers some conversational context, and is far less likely to respond with the dreaded, “According to an Alexa Answers contributor…” For casual home use, it can answer many of the same kinds of questions I would normally ask Claude, which I pay for separately for my business. Prime members also receive access to Alexa+, which makes the Dot Max a much more capable device than the older Echo speakers we own. The sound quality is good. I still prefer the speakers in the original full-size Echo, but the Dot Max sounds much better than the various standard Echo Dots and Echo Shows we’ve owned. For a child’s bedroom, it is more than adequate for music, audiobooks, and general Alexa use. Because Wi-Fi can be spotty in that corner of our apartment, I was also interested in the built-in eero extender capability. It only becomes useful if you already have (or later purchase) a compatible eero router, which I don’t currently own. Still, I’ve been considering switching to eero, and it’s nice to know her room is already somewhat future-proofed if I do. I was also happy to see that the Dot Max comes in Amethyst (purple). The color makes it feel unique without resorting to an overtly childlike design. It looks attractive on her desk and, depending on your frame of reference, resembles either the Death Star, Olympic Stadium in Montreal, or Spaceship Earth at EPCOT. I did run into one strange problem while trying to pair an Amazon Mickey Mouse clock. No matter how many times I tried, the Dot Max wouldn’t recognize it as an Amazon gadget. I eventually paired the clock with my original Echo, left it connected for a while, and then tried pairing it with the Dot Max again. Somehow, that worked. I’m not sure whether the clock received a firmware update or whether it was simply dumb luck, but it has remained connected since then. My other complaint is the placement of the indicator light. On several older Echo devices, the light is on top, where it can be seen from almost any angle. Here, it faces forward. Unless Alexa gives an audible response, it can be difficult to tell whether she heard you when you’re standing behind or beside the device. Those are relatively minor inconveniences, though. Overall, we love the Echo Dot Max. It has improved the reliability of our smart-home devices, added useful automation through the temperature sensor, and given my daughter a much better Alexa experience. It has assimilated quite nicely into our growing family of Echo devices. Its great-grandfather, meanwhile, has been reassigned to the bathroom.

review_title: Product Is Excellent — Purchasing Process Was Needlessly Difficult
body_en: Product Review: The Echo Dot Max itself is excellent. The sound quality is impressive for its size, functionality is solid, and Alexa performs exactly as expected. Once everything was set up, the device worked great and feels well designed. I genuinely enjoy the product and look forward to continuing to use Alexa devices in the future. PURCHASING & CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE (Important Context): I want to provide context around the purchasing process, as it required a significant amount of time, persistence, and unnecessary stress. I originally attempted to purchase two older versions of this product (used). After multiple payment processing issues, I was forced to cancel and attempt to repurchase, at which point the items disappeared entirely and could not be located. After contacting customer service, I was told that no new or used stock of those models remained. After the representative spoke with a supervisor, I was offered a price-match arrangement on the newest model instead. I received an email confirming this offer and was instructed to complete the full-price purchase and then call back to receive reimbursement of the price difference. I followed those instructions exactly. When I called back, I was told by another agent and supervisor that the reimbursement could not be processed until the item was delivered. I waited, received the device, and called again. At that point, despite prior confirmations (now involving multiple frontline agents and supervisors), I encountered repeated resistance to honoring the agreement. The call turned into hours of back-and-forth, during which I was repeatedly told the reimbursement could not be done, despite written confirmation stating otherwise. During this process, I was repeatedly encouraged to end the call without resolution or to be transferred to the Echo/Alexa specialist team, with the suggestion that they had authority over the purchase. This created additional DELAYS & DEFLECTION, even though the issue was not related to product functionality but to a previously confirmed purchase arrangement. The situation became EXTREMELY STRESSFUL, as the purchase required funds I had set aside for essential insurance payments, and an NSF would have resulted in penalties I could not afford. The prolonged uncertainty was disheartening, especially after relying on information that had been repeatedly confirmed. After several hours of persistence and refusing to allow the issue to be dismissed or deferred further, the agreement was finally honored and the matter was resolved. Additional Observation: After everything was resolved, the original models I was told were unavailable suddenly appeared back in stock. I was then able to purchase the two used devices (used) as I originally wanted at the reasonable price they were still listed as. FINAL THOUGHTS: The product itself is outstanding, and I’m very happy with the Echo Dot Max and the additional Echo devices I later purchased. My hope in sharing this experience is simply that internal communication and consistency improve, so customers are not placed under unnecessary financial stress after relying on confirmed information. Despite the ordeal, I remain a satisfied Alexa user and appreciate the final resolution to some respect. But, overall, it does NOT MAKE up for, nor compensate for the Uneeded, undue TIME & STRESS endured, especially after I had mentioned my current Ongoing HEALTH Related Battle. My Opinion: While the product itself is excellent, this experience showed me how difficult it can be for individual customers to resolve issues when information is inconsistent across multiple representatives.

The IPX7 Waterproof Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker has honestly impressed me more than I expected. It was recommended by my brother, and for the price, it performs better than a lot of bigger-name brands I’ve tried. The sound quality is crisp and clear, with no noticeable degradation so far even after regular use. It delivers enough volume and fullness to work well indoors or outdoors without sounding muddy or overly distorted. Connection has also been straightforward. Devices pair quickly, and the USB-C support is a welcome feature compared to older connection types. Having both USB and Type-C compatibility adds a bit of convenience and flexibility depending on your setup. Battery life is another strong point. It holds a charge for a long time, which makes it reliable for extended use or outdoor settings. The tradeoff is that it’s not a particularly fast recharge, so you’ll want to plan ahead rather than expect a quick top-off before heading out. The waterproofing is another plus, especially for outdoor use or keeping around a work area where accidents happen. Combined with the long battery life, it feels like a speaker designed more for actual use than just shelf appeal. Now comes the real test: durability. In this era of planned obsolescence, the question is how well it will hold up after a year or more of regular use. That’s ultimately what separates decent electronics from genuinely reliable gear. Still, first impressions are strong. The overall design feels practical and time-tested, with a bit of an old-school sensibility that focuses more on utility than gimmicks. Overall, this speaker punches above its price point. It’s practical, sounds good, connects quickly, and avoids a lot of the overhyped branding that bigger companies rely on. For the money, it’s been a solid buy.

It connected to my phone and my tablet without a second wasted. It looks good, sounds amazing and is going to be difficult to beat . It's fairly heavy for it's size which surprised me. It's really that good. You won't be disappointed if you buy one . It's versatility and functionality are as impressive as it's sound quality. I went for a ride in my hot rod Jeep CJ5 and had no problem hearing the speaker loud and clear. And my jeep isn't exactly quiet but I heard every note and verse without any problems. Can't wait until I get the 2nd one I just ordered. Im not exaggerating, it really is that good ! Update... I received the 2nd speaker and it is just as I expected as far as sound quality and performance. They sound fantastic and the difference between having a single speaker and having a 2nd speaker is significant but not as significant as I expected it to be. I thought that the bass and mid range sounds would increase and that would improve the only thing I think needs improvement with these speakers. That's the Bass and Midrange sound quality. They have Bass and Midrange sound but I think it could be or should have been much better with 2 speakers. There was a improvement but not as much as I expected There would be. There aren't 2 passive radiators on the rear that I can see. There's a long oval shaped thing that I guess is what they are calling w passive radiator. Even using my Dolby Sound app on my phone and the different sound levels and music type preset equalizer settings still produces little or no noticeable Bass or Midrange improvements in reality. 1 speaker sounds good and 2 sound much better than 1. But 2 don't improve the sound quality and range of performance the way I expected it to. The speakers are really good considering the price. They could even be described as Great. But they certainly could be better than they are . But at the current price point they are a fantastic bargain and are impressive without question. In a bedroom or small house they are undoubtedly going to be loud and sound great. But outside even having 2 of them turned up and separated by about 15 feet. They weren't as impressive or good as the 1st speaker led me to believe 2 of them would be. Definitely not bad , and a improvement over just 1 speaker. But definitely not the improvement as far as sound quality and overall volume one might anticipate. The stereo sound improved as it should have. But improvement in Bass or midrange sounds that I expected with the addition of another speaker just weren't what I expected or have experienced with other speakers in the past . Still a Great buy . But the addition of a second speaker linked to the first didn't provide the sound quality or volume I expected them to. They sound good but I expected there would be a more noticeable improvement in sound quality and volume with the 2nd speaker than I've observed.

Bought this Bose speaker to use in the bathroom while showering. Sounds pretty good, even over the sound of the water running. Doesn't crackle or sound frizzy and is really clear. Connects to Bluetooth devices seamlessly. Its a great size for a small bathroom because it's not big or bulky. Really appreciate the small, slim design. The battery lasts for a decent amount of time, considering it's size. On a full charge and being used daily for about 2 hours, we charge it once - MAYBE twice - a week. It will drain about 10% daily. We don't leave it on the charger when it's not in use. Charge it only when the battery is low. It won't take long to charge either. The volume is good for what we use it for. We don't try to blast it for the neighborhood to hear it but sounds good outdoors around a group of friends by the fire or for background tunes while having a card night with buddies. Even works well and sounds good in the garage while working with power tools. Would probably even be great on a river float. Very happy and satisfied with this little speaker.

The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

I picked this up for the boys, and it’s been a great addition to their room. The setup was quick, the sound quality is surprisingly good for its size, and they love being able to ask Alexa questions, listen to music, and hear bedtime stories. I also appreciate the parental controls and kid-friendly content, which make it easy to manage what they can access. It’s a fun device for them and gives me a little extra peace of mind.

I got this for my 2-year-old, and the design alone was a huge win. The little owl look is really cute, and I paired it with the stand so it sits on a tree-style bookshelf in his room. It actually blends in like decor, which I love. So far, he hasn’t tried to grab or play with it much because he thinks it “belongs” on the shelf, which is honestly a plus. It feels like a kid-friendly device without being distracting or constantly handled. Where it’s been most useful is during our nighttime routine. We use it to play music and control other Alexa devices, which makes winding down a lot smoother. It’s been reliable for that and easy to use hands-free when my hands are full. I know there are additional kid-focused features available, but I haven’t fully explored those yet, so I can’t speak to parental controls or educational content at this point. This works really well for routines, but if you’re specifically buying it for advanced kid features, you may need to spend some time setting those up and testing them. Really nice if you have your hands full and want to adjust your digital thermostat, set up an alarm, play music. Best for: parents who want a cute, simple smart speaker to support daily routines rather than a fully interactive toy. Keep in mind, you need to purchase the nest separately but they are very cute together even though it blocks the blue light at the bottom that let’s you know the owl is thinking.

review_title: Boo! I'm not paranoid about who's listening
body_en: I'm almost 70 and if someone wants to listen in on my world they will be very disappointed. But really; I love this little owl. I live pretty much alone in an upstairs studio apartment and I'm a reader. I wanted the Echo Dot so I can my l just say what I need and someone is cheerfully there to help. It was easy to set up and it was easy to understand after I realized that ask the online info about the hows, what's, an do this was out of date because the new Alexa app radically reconfigured the app. Even when I asked my Echo Dot for help finding Communications it was telling me as if I had the old version. Once I told the Echo Dot I have Alexa V2.268 I learned everything from the Echo Dot itself. I can now waking up to music I like and not the only FM radio station I can get. Now I have my music waking me up and it continues to play more of the same until I say, from my bed, to stop. While I'm getting dressed I ask what's the weather and if there's any news I should know. I have it figure out the calories of the breakfast I'm going to make. We talk about things I'm interested in and it says goodnight and that's nice when you're alone living above a family that reminds me of the joy I had. I ordered the kids owl. It was much less in cost but I wanted the Owl. But getting the kids echo, I got a full year of Amazon kids... not my cup of tea but it says it's a nice perk if you have little kids in your life. The Owl is cute but it has black creepy eyes so I used a paint marker to give him life and sparkle. I did make a child profile just to see how the Echo Dot is with kids and it's wonderful. It asked me to pick two things. I picked a mouse and a log with a hole in it. It created an original audio story that was 3 minutes long and beautiful. I set up notifications about Mom phases, asked for help with the etymology of the word WATER, and asked science questions. It does ask questions back to build your identity of likes and dislikes and that might feel creepy but if you know your child better than the daycare does there's no problem trusting the Echo Dot with your 7 year old up. The music quality it great and it's customized to be just for me and my taste in music. I always buy... today one came on sale with $5 in savings but it was limited time. I saw the spinning orange glow at it's base, meaning I have a message, the Echo Dot out it in my shopping cart but it could have just bought it for me. Yes, you have to be an adult and if you have kids you're going to have to turn that option off in the Alexa app. I deleted the kid profile and unsubscribed from my free year of Amazon kids because that was ridiculously lame. Is Big Brother listening?... Big Brother has been alive since the malls had teams of people asking shoppers if they have time to share their shopping experience. Now the Internet just sells your whole life to the highest bidder... progress and convenience is always listening and watching us. I'm getting another for the living room sso I can talk to my grown kids from my Echo Dot and have use it as an intercom for a guest if they sleep over. My downstairs neighbor has one and offered to give me their info at I could intercom them if ever I needed help. But... the Owl needs a glint in his eyes so as that and have fun at any age.

They enjoy being able to listen to their own music (and because it’s a kids profile, I’m not worried about what will come on randomly) and setting timers for reading or other activities. Only giving it 4 stars because sometimes it completely messes up what the kids asked for or doesn’t respond at all. Overall happy with the purchase as a whole.

This is technically a 4.5 star rating but I didn’t want to be petty and give 4 stars since there’s no 1/2 star option haha. I’m a child free adult that loved the aesthetic of the kids galaxy echo so much that I took advantage of the trade program of my older dot and got a few dollars off just to get this! The speaker itself goes perfectly with my living room decor and blends in wonderfully. Perfect sound and does the job. I had zero problems deactivating the Alexa kids safety feature so that I can play and do what I please listening to music and giving commands. My reason for taking a half star off is the unsightly WHITE cord. Sweet baby Moses man! Lol. It sticks out like a sore thumb and takes away from the sleek look of the dot. Either a black cord should have been included OR if amazon is going to make more cool color themed dots (Adults should be included) the cords should match the speaker. I’m going to look into the echo stage to go wire free but it makes more sense just to up the price of the dot to make it completely wireless with the option for battery or charging. In lieu of buying all of these pointless accessories. There are more basic speakers that have this capability. Echo should follow suit!

review_title: Very easy to set up, easy to use, fun and educational!
body_en: I absolutely LOVE this Echo Dot!! I got this for my daughter for her 6th birthday and so far we LOVE IT! It was super easy to set up which I thought it would take an hour to do but you just plug it in and download the Amazon kids app and it walks you right through the set up and your ready to go in 10 min or less! It is so cute and this thing made bed time routine magical! You can set an alarm for bedtime and wake up and it will alert her half hour before bedtime to clean up your toys and brush teeth, etc. and my daughter instantly gets up and listens to it when for me it’s usually a struggle and fight lol I was amazed! It made it fun for her and she gets to create bedtime stories with it to listen to before bed and it put her right to sleep! This thing is great she loves playing her favorite songs during the day and making up stories and learning new facts, you can ask it anything educational and it has the answers I definitely recommend this to anyone with children it’s not only fun but educational and teaches healthy routines and responsibility and learning and fun!

review_title: Bose Compact TV Subwoofer is a Great Value!
body_en: I recently bought this compact Bose soundbar on Amazon for $199.00. I can honestly say that it exceeds my expectations! Right out of the box you get the sense it’s a high quality product! The construction is solid and robust. My Bose soundbar is connected a recent model Samsung 32” QLED television via the HDMI Arc terminal. The audio quality is quite good IMO. Blindfolded you would swear the speaker was much larger. It’s got great high frequency response and the middle frequencies are crisp, balanced, possessing outside speech clarity. The bass is somewhat attenuated but given the compact size of the speaker it’s still very respectable. If you’re so inclined you can connect compatible Bose subwoofer to supplement the bass frequencies. I believe the Bose subwoofer represents a terrific value in the crowded home speaker market. I’m giving it 5 Stars since it exceeds my expectations!
Very pleased with this item. Easy to set up and pair with my Apple devices. Works well with both my phone and watch. Great sound for a speaker of its size and cost. A real value!

Pros - compact, good size for a 40-55" TV - better sound than most built in TV speakers I've heard; not going to fool you into being in a theater without a sub or surrounds, but not meant to, so does the job it was built for - mostly easy setup, plug and play with a Samsung LCD TV from 2022 - does not require much space - good for bedroom TV or guest room TV Why not five stars? - power cable is way too short and plugs in at one side of back instead of center, making setup and positioning a pain - white power led on front is distracting - no bundled HDMI cable for eARC - remote uses coin battery instead of more common AAA - rubber feed to prevent vibration only at two sides, needed to add a middle foot to prevent rattle against TV stand since the stand was narrower than the speaker - otherwise I would need to position it well in front of the TV taking up more space - could do without silver Bose logo on top/front for a cleaner look - maybe make it gray or black - remote's "Bass" button has no visible or on screen feedback or menu to tell if it's on or off that I can find, and audio isn't different enough except for high volume movies to notice

review_title: INSANELY good for a small office/bedroom
body_en: I was looking for a small home office set up (10 X 12 room) and wanted something that was uncomplicated but also sounded really good given the room size. It's used primarily for music, but I'm often in meetings with up to 20 other people, so I wanted something with a voice clarity option. I figured I was going to have to sacrifice one for the other, but the speaker really delivers! What was most amazing to me was the level and quality of bass, which I didn't think was possible with a standalone sound bar, and a small sound bar at that. When I bought this, I also bought the bass module 500 which I've since returned, as it was completely unnecessary. The speaker produces a very balanced soundstage. I placed the soundbar across two studio monitor speaker stands with a 15 degree tilt, super highly recommended if you're planning to use this for a home office solution. This is absolutely not a speaker as a standalone in a larger room, but it's perfect for a small space. No subwoofer needed. You can literally feel the bass.

This Bose TV Speaker has pretty good sound quality for the tv because it does sound better than the tv speakers and better volume and the speech is a little clearer, but that's about as far as it goes. I purchased this sound bar after looking at many, but mostly because I have been a Bose fan for many decades and in the days of them becoming to where they are now everything was exceptional until I received this product. Service is nonexistent never got a answer for a simple question I sent earlier so just imagine how it is with a real problem.

This is my third and hopefully final soundbar in my hunt for something that just works. I did a bit of research that landed me on the Bose TV Speaker. This is for a living room with a 20' ceiling and a TV mounted above the fireplace. With young kids, the TV is usually on their shows during the day or mom and dad trying to watch something in the evening. We aren't looking to be fully immersed in booming action movies, dialogue is the focus. The last one I had would drown out dialogue with background music and I was always trying to adjust the levels. This is perfect, I don't have to fiddle with it and it does a great job of staying consistent and I never have an issue hearing dialogue. It connected easily to my Roku TV and even supports Roku TV integration, allowing me to adjust things through the TV interface. I like that it's relatively small while packing powerful audio. The only problem I had may have been due to my TV - when I connected to the Bose over Bluetooth it messed up the hdmi-arc connection and my TV was no longer powering the Bose on and off, I had to factory reset the TV to resolve this and I haven't tried the Bluetooth connection since. Bottom line is that I didn't want to spend more than $200 and I just wanted something that would just work - apparently that is a unicorn in today's age of soundbars - and the Bose TV Speaker is that unicorn

review_title: Finally, a simple solution to the madhouse of audio alternatives for television
body_en: I had a Bose one piece sound system many years ago. Really enjoyed it. It eventually gave up so I started down the dark hole of soundbars. In about 10 years I've had 3 and with each one there was always something that wouldn't sound right, mainly when someone talks and there's music in the background, only the music that's supposed to hang back instead blares like a foghorn and drowns out the dialogue. I have to admit the last one, a Vizio, soundbar only, no subwoofer or surround speakers, did it's best to keep the dialogue to within reach. It's main issue was it wouldn't cooperate with a Vizio TV, wouldn't maintain a setting if you had the ability to pay it. So, I'm back to the simple Bose TV Speaker. Ya got two settings, bass and dialogue. There are others but they don't involve audio. It plugs into my Vizio TV via HDMI eARC (cable not included), but it does come with an optical cable and I plugged it in but isn't required. ARC allows my TV remote and Fire Stick remote to control the soundbar volume which is the only thing you really need to control once you set the soundbar with it's own remote to be controlled by other devices and the sound setting you like (your choice of two or both at the same time, why not go for it). I can hear music, I can hear voices, I can hear them both at the same time and anyone who says you need a small room to use it in is probably wanting more than the bar can deliver regarding audio. It's plenty loud. Where I sit fairly far from the TV and the room is kind of open concept leading to not open concept, like rooms elsewhere. I can hear it through out the house. Good bass too. Okay I said two settings but the bass actually has 3 levels. The longest portion of the entire setup from unpacking to connection and listening was the unpacking. It's packed pretty well. Good things come in small packages they say, this is one of them. I recommend this to anyone who doesn't require sound bouncing from the holes in their shoes and from the coffee mug sitting beside them. It's a great sounding speaker that removes the requirement of having to take a course or two in sound engineering and makes listening to TV simple and comfortable and enjoyable again, you don't have to constantly change the audio settings to work with the video. It just works.

This is a truly excellent product that fully lives up to expectations. The sound is big and the complexity of setup is small, although to make it work with my older Sharp Aquos TV, which lacks HDMI ARC, I had to buy a dongle — an HDMI audio extractor that pulls the sound out of the main source HDMI and shunts it to an optical jack that can communicate properly with the Bose device using the supplied optical cable. More modern TVs won’t need that. For those whose TV had great video but the audio sucks, this is the cure. It would be worth it for full price but it was nice to get this one as a Prime Day door-buster sale item. I know the days of Bose products being made in Framingham are long gone but this particular item is built in Thailand, which is an ally or something like one. As an ABC shopper I’ll settle for that.
Excelente produto

Good option, the quality of course feels different from a commercial bar, at first I thought it didn't sound good and it lacked power but you have to know how to configure it, I put it with HDMI and it was configured with the izzi remote control to turn it on and off with the TV, when I change the volume of the TV the amplifier mode comes out and I put it at 40 and it sounds quite loud without voice amplification mode (which seems like a pretty loud extra) I'll sometimes remove this function now when sleeping because it sounds very powerful, in reality the bar is quite good I thought I would need the bass module by force but it lowers well for a bar to the level of a 2.1 creative bar that I had before (60/80rms approx) the truth is you just have to move it, play with configuring it and that's it, the volume without this mode that appears on the TV the level is difficult to raise and you think it doesn't go up, the quality is very good and I hear very different from the previous bar even if it were 2.1, if you are very happy and the quality is too good, for the price it is a great purchase, do not hesitate to order it.

review_title: Great sound for the room — simple, reliable upgrade
body_en: I picked up the Bose TV Speaker to replace my old CineMate Bose system that finally died, and so far it’s been an excellent, hassle-free replacement. Setup was plug-and-play with my existing Bose TV’s optical out and it started working immediately. I haven’t used the Dialogue Enhancer feature, but even without it the speaker delivers clear, natural-sounding audio that suits my room very well. The unit is compact but sounds bigger than it looks. The bass has respectable weight for such a small speaker — not a home-theatre rumble, but enough to give action scenes and music some presence. The included remote is simple and intuitive, and overall build quality feels solid and understated like other Bose products. Pros: - Smooth setup — truly plug-and-play - Clear, balanced sound that fits the room nicely - Compact footprint; good for smaller living areas or bedrooms - Solid build and easy-to-use remote Cons: - Not a substitute for a full surround system if you want immersive multi-channel audio - Won’t match a dedicated subwoofer for deep bass Would recommend if you want an easy, reliable upgrade from an older compact Bose unit — great for improving everyday TV sound without fuss.

review_title: Som limpo e de excelente qualidade
body_en: I recommend the purchase. Satisfied with the acquisition

This speaker has some THUMP, the volume is great and plenty loud. My friends have said it’s surprising how loud and clear it is despite the small size. It’s very easy to carry around because of the handle, and it provides clear sound. Battery life is amazing, I’ve been able to use it for a whole week without charging! (Approx 3-4 hrs per day of music playback) for my ears this speaker does a fantastic job, even better than my JBL. It may be a bit expensive, but if this is the last speaker you’ll ever need then does the price really matter if you’re only paying it once?

This is essentially the perfect bluetooth speaker. The sound quality, especially after dialing the EQ, is as good as it gets. Clear bass, sparkling highs, powerful mids. I just don't see how you could get better in this form factor. Speaking of which, this thing is small, about the size of a hiking boot. Coupled with the excellent handle you have an extremely convenient package for carrying with you around the house. You could even travel with it if you don't mind the significant weight. It's built very solidly, the quality is satisfyingly obvious. The bluetooth functionality is flawless. Just turn it on and it syncs to your phone within 5 seconds EVERY SINGLE TIME. Not sure why it's taken so long to get this tech reliable. The app is great also. Yes, it's expensive, but it is absolutely worth the price, considering it enhances my life pretty much all day long.

review_title: Durable, Great Sound Quality - Worth It
body_en: Fantastic speaker—well‑built, durable, and quick to charge. The size is perfect for pool days, parties, or tossing in a bag for travel. I bring it on trips for hotel‑room music, and around the house it never loses connection, even when I’m in another room or out in the backyard. It’s waterproof, so shower use is fair game. It charges via USB‑C, and that same port can top off your phone in a pinch. There’s also an AUX input if you ever need it. Multiple devices can connect via Bluetooth (though that can get chaotic), and it can pair with other Bose speakers. Once you’ve paired your device the first time, it reconnects automatically every time you power it on. Sound Quality: The sound is excellent. You can tweak the EQ in the app, the bass is strong and clean, and this thing gets loud without losing clarity. Treble stays crisp, and overall it’s one of the best‑sounding speakers in its size class. Is it worth the price? I’d say yes. Plenty of speakers check the same boxes, but if you want a bougie speaker that performs - this one is for you.

As a long-time owner of the first-generation Bose SoundLink Mini, I had high expectations for the Bose SoundLink Max, and it did not disappoint. This review covers various aspects of the speaker, including sound quality, durability, ease of use, compatibility, setup, and design. The SoundLink Max lives up to the Bose name. After testing it with a myriad of musical genres, I was blown away by the fullness of the sound. The bass is so powerful that you can feel it, yet it does not drown out the mid and treble frequencies. It is worth noting that the initial EQ settings are flat, which might be why some users have complained about the lack of fullness. This could be addressed by repurposing the shortcut button for quick EQ adjustment. The SoundLink Max meets the IP67 standards, making it rugged, dustproof, and waterproof. Weighing nearly five pounds, it is heavy, but this is an acceptable trade-off for the durability it offers. In a pinch, you could even use it as a brick or a weapon for defending yourself from zombies! Using the SoundLink Max is straightforward. Press the power button, then play to start enjoying your music. When it’s time to change settings, the buttons are clearly labeled. The Max charges via a supplied USB-C cord and power block and can also serve as a portable power device. This is my main point of contention and it is not specifically with the Max, but with Bose as a whole. They have partnered with Qualcomm/Snapdragon for their HD Audio, which is currently confined to the Android ecosystem. As an iPhone user, I felt a little left out in the cold. Straight out-of-the-box, the Max was nearly ready to go. It took two seconds to pair and less than that to start charging, thanks to the included USB-C cable and power brick. The Bose app was easy to find and quick to install. I was able to set up an account and start using the app right away. While the setup was easy, more emphasis should be placed on the necessity of using the app to achieve the best sound, as the default EQ settings are a bit flat. The SoundLink Max boasts a sleek and simple design. There are no unnecessary lights or reminiscent designs to distract you—just a rugged exterior that protects the speakers while delivering excellent sound quality. The rope handle is a nice feature that accentuates the rugged yet simple design. They are easily changeable for other colored handles and shoulder straps, which are available at a steep premium on the Bose website. The Bose SoundLink Max is a phenomenal portable speaker that lives up to the high standards we expect from Bose. After several days of testing in various locations and with different music genres, I have not been disappointed. While there have been some reports of less-than-fantastic sound quality, this issue is easily resolved by adjusting the EQ settings in the Bose app. The final question is, is the SoundLink Max worth the $400 price tag? The simple answer is yes, it is worth every penny.

review_title: Get it on sale not full price! But 100% worth it!
body_en: Best speaker I’ve ever heard. Bose speakers are extremely well known for their audio clarity and excellent sound. The bass sounds clean as could be and you can hear every single instrument and vocals in any song. From edm all the way to rap this speaker kicks a$$ at anything you throw at it. Of course it’s not going to be as loud as competitors like JBL but it for sure beats any speaker in clean and extreme bass and the clarity in sound. Is it worth the $400 price tag???. Absolutely not but definitely buy it if it goes on sale! I compared a bunch of speakers to this one because I’m a speaker guy and I love to collect them but Bose knocks every single one out of the part with this one!

review_title: Sounds like a box of farts, and not in a good way. Maybe it is broken?
body_en: When I first unpacked this product and listened to it, I was completely won over. What an amazing first impression. Excellent soundstage. Wide, detailed, clear, everything you could want. Unfortunately, once you take the volume to even close to 50%, which you'd want to do in many situations and certainly outside, and it all falls apart. Hero to zero in the blink of an eye. The bass has a fart-like quality to it which ruins everything. The only way to make this sound acceptable is to use the EQ to take the bass pretty much to nothing or even a negative setting. In which case, you could buy almost any other Bluetooth speaker for less than half the price that is going to sound just as good. Many of the reviews talk about bass and presence, but that's only true at really low levels. At least assuming the unit I was sent is working to factory spec. And don't get me wrong, I'm not listening to music at window rattling levels designed to annoy the neighbors. I'm not even listening to tracks that I think are especially bass heavy. As an example I listened to Clocks by Coldplay. Hardly a hardcore bass fest. The opening bars sounded amazing. But as soon as the gentle bass chords joined the music, the speaker lost itself. I tried the product on a hard wooden stool. A hard wooden deck. A patio table. A different patio table. A few feet away. A few meters away. It really didn't matter. I played with numerous EQ settings. But the bottom line is that it just can't put out bass in any real capacity unless you are willing to lower the sound to a background volume. In which case, it's amazing. To me, the bass being available in such a quiet and tiny sweet spot, makes it kind of worthless to include it at all. I have a pair of B&O Explore speakers, that sound amazing and can be set as a stereo pair. If you buy them well you can have two of them for $100 less than this Bose. What they lack in bass, they more than make up for in incredible sound stage, stereo separation and can go toe to toe in terms of detail. The thing is, they also KNOW they can't do much bass, so they don't even try. Bose, is trying too hard to make bass happen that apparently isn't possible in this system. Just like I don't drive my car at 100 mph ever, I want it to be capable of that. I want it to accelerate from zero to sixty in under seven seconds, even though it's not how I drive. And when it comes to speakers, I want to know that if I want to turn up the volume a little, it isn't going to sound like a box of farts. I tried to give it every opportunity to impress, but it failed at everything except very quiet listening levels. I was mainly streaming from Apple Music, and I even looked for songs offered at their highest bitrate or including spacial audio technology. For the price they are charging, there is no way I keep this item. It is already in the box ready to go to UPS. Maybe it would be different if you have a different sound source, are using a different streaming service, are using AUX or Android. My tests were iOS based, and bluetooth streaming. Tracks that I have previously tested on my Marshall Woburn II speaker as an example, with the same source equipment.
Get’s pretty loud! Great low end base! Sound great! BT connects quickly and has good range! Great portability! It seems to be pretty durable.

review_title: Great Sounding Speaker ... If You Are Patient
body_en: *FIRST IMPRESSIONS: Listening to music as it comes out of the box, I had two impressions,something is missing from the music and what is that painful squeael in the treble area. while they may sound bad out of the box, the hardware is capable of greatness with the right tweaks. The rest of this review provides information about the basic setup and configuration of these speakers and what needs to be done to improve the sound. * PROS: Sound great; full spectrum with clear highs and lows, but takes work to bring it out. In fact, for the best sound, you'll need an equalizer. Once equalization has been applied, they can have the clarity found in a pair of much higher priced speakers; they have great lows, but can't match the 28Hz lows of the Cerwin Vega D-9s but the highs are reasonably close. Fairly easy to pair with another speaker but see below. * CONS: All detailed below with solutions: 1. Out of the box, it sounds much worse than it actually is. The default equalization was for marketing. The bass is pushed up 4 dB, the midrange down 2 dB and the highs up 5 dB. This may be impressive for a short time, but you may eventually be dissatisfied as the center has been cut out of the music and you'll cringe at the outlandish scream at 6.3 kHz. 2. Connecting to the Bose app involves an overlooked step, Bose should fix this. 3. Interconnecting speakers as a stereo pair is a bit tricky. 4. Serious power management problem which Bose should also fix. 5. Most buttons lack tactile icons for the visually impaired, but they are easy to find and count. For this device, there are six buttons arranged in a single horizontal row on the top front from left to right as follows: (1) power, (2) Bluetooth, (3) link, (4) Volume down, (5) Play/Pause, and (6) Volume up. Note that the function of the Play/Pause button may be affected by your music player and bluetooth configuration. Now for the details: * SETUP: - Connecting To The Bose App: It is hard to get The Bose app connected so you can take advantage of built-in features. This complaint appears often on the Google Playstore. - Getting Into The Configuration App: Download and install the Bose app from the web; it is in android and Apple download sites as well as the Bose web site. For best results, connect your phone to the speaker via bluetooth. Open the app and follow instructions until you get to a page that ought to be showing your device name and which contains the "Add Device" link. * NOTE: Before clicking this link be certain that notifications are enabled on your phone and that you will be alerted when a new notification arrives. Note to Bose, this ought to be stated on that page as a reminder to users. Assuming it has the right device, click the "Add Device" link. You will almost instantaneously get a notification. Open it and click the "Pair" link in that notification. If you are too late or something else happens, go back to that add device link and try again. * CONFIGURING THE SPEAKER: There are two areas of interest in the Bose app, one allows you to make some adjustments to the equalization for the speaker. The other allows you to control automatic power down parameters. - The Built In Equalizer: The built in equalizer has only three frequency bands for you to deal with, the bass, midrange and the treble. By default, these bands are set for marketing impact, to impress casual shoppers with the amazing highs and lows this speaker can produce, but you may find music reproduction very disappointing. If you want this primarily as a portable speaker, use the equalizer controls to produce a sound more to your liking. However, this won't clean up the sharp power spike at 6.3kHz., for that, an external equalizer is required. - Correcting The Frequency Response: If you have an Equalizer on your phone or computer, that equalizer will be far better than the one built into the speaker. Suggested Equalizations are given below. * POWER MANAGEMENT SETTING: Disguised as a profile area is the settings area (top right corner of the apps home page. The primary area of concern is the power setting. By default it is set to automatic. That means the speaker will turn off after 12 hours, even if plugged in. This is a battery safety feature. However, if you're using the speaker at home and have it always plugged in, you can set it to "Never," but be aware that this could be a problem if your power fails for you take it with you and fail to power it down first, the result could be a drained and if it goes long enough, damaged battery. The risk is yours, balance that risk against your convenience. Note to Bose, you should disregard the power down parameter if the speaker is plugged in. I consider not doing so a major engineering defect on your part especially as it could lead to battery problems. NOTE: Keep in mind Listening at high volumes or with very heavy bass will eventually cause the unit to shut down, even while plugged in. Also, under those conditions, the discharge time on full batteries without being plugged in is only three hours. To completely recharge the batteries after a shutdown will take about 5 hours. Recharge time from shutdown can take far longer if you try to turn it on again after a shutdown. * Personalizing The Sound: First, be aware that we all have different preferences in how music sounds, but here is what I did. I am using Equalizer APO on windows, but there are several similar apps for Android phones - Wavelet, Poweramp Equalizer, Echo Equalizer). For Mac users, you can achieve these same results using SoundSource (with an AU plugin) or the 'Expert' mode in eqMac. Unfortunately, iPhone users will have to buy and setup a dongle (an external Bluetooth transmitter with built-in DSP). to apply equalization parameters and transmit the sound via bluetooth. - Equalization Suggestions: The Bose Digital Signal Processor (DSP) is always active. It generally acts like the loudness contour in older amplifiers. It greatly increases the bass at low volumes and reduces the bass amplification as volume increases. It is also intended to produce the "Bose Sound" that is "full, meaning exagerated lows and highs." The response curves and filter/equalization settings below assume moderate volume. They work against the built in DSP settings to extend the frequency range where the response is considered "flat," that is, the range in which the volume stays between + or - 3dB. That is the normal standard for top grade amplifiers and speakers to ensure that you hear the music as intended by the artists who produced it. The following is the list of frequency and power level, in dB that I'm using to correct the factory tuning and achieve a more balanced, high-fidelity sound. I found the following frequency adjustments to be effective. These values help neutralize the sharp spikes and restore the midrange that is missing out of the box. NOTE: These values assume the default Bose equalization has not been changed. If you have altered them and don’t remember what they were, you can do a full reset on the speaker to put it back into factory configuration. This requires a very long simultaneous press of the volume up and volume down buttons. The Bose will eventually respond with a burp. - Equalization Suggestions: Preamp: -3.0 dB For Copy/Paste (Equalizer APO,) copy the following line exactly as written into your config file: GraphicEQ: 100 -2; 250 -3; 630 2; 1000 3.5; 1600 2.5; 4000 -3; 6300 -6; 10000 -4; 16000 -2 For Manual Entry (Mobile Apps & Screen Readers): 100 -2 250 -3 630 2 1000 3.5 1600 2.5 4000 -3 6300 -6 10000 -4 16000 -2 - Alternative Approach - Filters If the program you choose for the frequency corrections has the capability of specifying filter points, a more surgical approach, you might consider these filter specifications: Filter Set 1: Preamp: -3.0 dB Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 1.0 Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -2.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 3: ON PK Fc 1000 Hz Gain 2.0 dB Q 1.0 Filter 4: ON PK Fc 2500 Hz Gain 1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 5: ON PK Fc 4500 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 6: ON PK Fc 6300 Hz Gain -5.0 dB Q 3.0 Filter 7: ON HS Fc 10000 Hz Gain -1.0 dB -Alternative Filter Set: Filter set 2 In the following, the lines with the # sign are comments. They are the settings recommended on the internet, I found them to give a booming bass, so I substituted the lines that are not commented out. Make your own choice. Preamp: -6.5 dB #Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 1.0 #Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -2.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -3.5 dB Q 1.0 Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -4.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 3: ON PK Fc 1000 Hz Gain 2.0 dB Q 1.0 Filter 4: ON PK Fc 2500 Hz Gain 1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 5: ON PK Fc 4000 Hz Gain -3.0 dB Q 1.5 Filter 6: ON PK Fc 6300 Hz Gain -6.0 dB Q 3.0 Filter 7: ON PK Fc 10000 Hz Gain -4.0 dB Q 2.0 Filter 8: ON HS Fc 13000 Hz Gain 4.5 dB * A comparison of frequency response curves: Bose out of the box: Effective Range +/- 6dB; 60 Hertz to 14,000 Hertz • Using the Equalizer settings: Effective range +/- 3dB;110 Hertz to 5,000 Hertz., limited by that massive cut at 6.3 kHz. Using the first Filter settings: Effective range +/- 2.5dB; 55 Hertz to 15,500 Hertz. Using Filter settings #2: Effective range +/- 3dB; 52 Hz to 16,500 Hz Clearly, the filter settings are the winner. feel free to adjust the equalization values to your own satisfaction, and if you feel the need, you can supply intermediate values. If you increase the power too much, and get distortion from clipping, reduce the preamp value. * Making A Stereo Pair: This area is considered to be a bit flakey, perhaps because people forget critical details or their timing is a bit off. so be prepared to repeat if required. To make a stereo pair. On the speaker you want as the left speaker, do a long press and then a quick second press of the third button from the left (the Shortcut/Link button). After the speaker tells you to do so, do a single quick press of the third button from the left on the second speaker, this will be the right speaker. Be patient, the speakers takes longer than one would expect to respond to the button presses on each speaker; allow 30 to 45 seconds for each speaker. As a side note on volume, I normally listen to these speakers from 20 feet away with the volume set at 55%, so they have sufficient power to fill a large room. * Final Verdict: If you want a "plug and play" perfect experience, this might frustrate you. But if you are willing to spend 10 minutes in the settings and Equalizer , it is likely the best-sounding speaker in its size class.
I am very satisfied with the product that deserves 5 stars. Also, the seller ADENX is a seller that you can shop with peace of mind and really cares about customer satisfaction.

review_title: La calidad de los materiales es muy buena, el sonido es muy completo.
body_en: I really liked the quality of the sound and the materials, it really feels like a good quality speaker; I already have other speakers from the brand, I was surprised by the bass that this one can have, the compatibility with other speakers is limited, I would have liked it to have compatibility with more previous speakers, the volume is good at 70 or 75% but going past it loses some clarity not only in the bass in the full body, it doesn't sound bad but not ideal.

If there were two ratings, one for the speaker and one for the Seller (Amazon), Speaker gets 5 Stars and Amazon gets 2 Stars. The speaker doesn't deserve a low rating due to Amazon. I watched a lot of reviews and had a hard time to decide between JBL or Bose, only because of the Bose price. I already have 2 Bose Soundtouch 300s and 1 Bose Wave Sountouch, so I already knew the rich sound Bose puts out. Because of the sound quality of my previous Bose I figured I would take a chance on the Pricey Bose Soundlink Max. Before I go any further, I do need to say first, Amazon should be ashamed of themselves, selling OPEN BOX for BRAND NEW. I don't believe this is the fault of Bose, it is Amazon Re-Selling their returns, as I bought 2 Bose Soundlink Max's "Shipped by Amazon" and both were OPEN BOX which was not stated in the selling add. They were at a good sale price, but i dislike not being told they were OPEN BOX, especially when paying close to $400 CAD for 1 speaker. Even though the speakers are outstanding I am thinking of returning both speakers due to this unless Amazon can do something about it. 90% of my purchases are through Amazon, and having this done disgusts me. Back to the Bose Soundlink Max. This review is based on only one evening of trial. For starters I had no issues with the bluetooth, it was very easy to connect both my Samsung phone and Samsung tablet, and that was without the Bose App installed. Once I was linked, I started playing all types of music. Pop, Dance, Rock etc, and with a bit of bit of fine tuning with the built in EQ on Samsung, this little speaker fills the room with such amazing rich sound. I read a review once where it said this speaker sounds great out of the box. It sounds ok, but tune an EQ on it and it is amazing. I would shut the EQ off and On while playing and listening to this speaker through an EQ makes a world of difference, which BTW would be the same with any speaker. The build of the speaker is very nice. Does not have a cheap plastic feel. A good portion of the speaker has a grippy silicone feel. The weight of the speaker alone tells a lot about the build Quality, Not too heavy, but also not too light, its very solid. The carry handle is very sturdy and well connected as well. I still need to try the linking feature between the two speakers. Will update soon

review_title: Great Sound, Premium Build, and Perfect for My Desktop Setup
body_en: I picked up the Marshall Emberton III during Amazon Prime Day for just $99, and it has been one of my favorite purchases this year. I was looking for a single speaker to sit in front of my computer monitor instead of using traditional left-and-right desktop speakers. The rectangular shape fits perfectly on my desk and gives me the clean, soundbar-like setup I wanted. On top of that, the retro Marshall design looks fantastic and feels very premium. I also own a JBL Flip 6, and both speakers sound great. However, the Emberton III fits my desktop needs much better. I really like that all the controls—power, Bluetooth pairing, and volume—are conveniently located on the top, making them easy to access without reaching around the speaker. The sound quality is excellent, with impressive volume, clear audio, and surprisingly punchy bass for its size. Whether I’m listening to music, watching YouTube, or using it as my everyday computer speaker, it performs beautifully. Overall, I’m extremely satisfied with this purchase. If you’re looking for a stylish, well-built Bluetooth speaker that doubles as an excellent desktop speaker, especially at the Prime Day price, I highly recommend it.

It's very easy to use, with an intuitive interface that makes the experience even better. I bought it while it was on sale, so it was a great value for the price. review_title: Great speaker! But don't make the mistake I did.
body_en: Purchased in February 2024. Great audio quality and high volume. If anything, I'd say the battery life isn't quite as long as the similar name brand products. My mistake: I was using a wall charger with a USB A to C adapter at the end of the charging cable. Bad mistake, because USB A doesn't carry enough power to charge this speaker properly. As a result, even though is appeared it was charging, my speaker started malfunctioning, and I eventually thought it was defective. As a last ditch effort, I found a high wattage Samsung USB C only charger and connected it to USB C only cable. Like magic, my speaker started charging, again. Problem solved. Works great now!

was having a hard time choosing between this, and Oontz angle 3 Pro, and a Doss Soundbox Pro. Im looking for something primarily for the house to be used in a bedroom/office. I dont like letting my batteries drain so I cant vouch for battery life on each one, but im not worried. Below is why I would choose each model, hopefully it helps you. Also if it matters, I listened to Radiohead-The National Anthem and Skrillex-Rumble to test the speakers. --Why I chose the Doss Soundbox Pro: I hate to admit it but the price....and I actually chose this one over the Tribit and Oontz after my sound tests. The sound was on par with the other 2 (similar wattage to the Oontz) and I liked this one just a hair more than the Oontz because it was a little crisper sounding where the Oontz was a little fuller...if that makes sense. So with the sound being the same, the fact that I could ALSO pair multiple Doss speakers for a multi speaker set up just like the Oontz (this is a great feature for when entertaining guests/having a small party/get-together), and considering I'd primarily be using this in a bedroom (where the powerbank wouldnt come in as handy like the Oontz has).....I had to choose this one. Its the smallest and has a strap across the backside of it so you can easily attach it to a backpack, bike, UTV/ATV or any type of bar....the straps so tight to the body of the speaker that you can even put it on something as small as a car antenna and itd hold securely. They dont list the wattage and this had the lowest wattage of the bunch at 10w compared to the other 2 at 20w/21w each.....but it was without a doubt equally as loud as the other two with trebles and bass being on par with the other two. Id really like to see how loud and clean a tribit with higher wattage sounds if this 10w speaker matched the higher wattage speakers I compared it to in my test. --Why I would choose the Oontz Angle 3 Pro instead: This one was the biggest and beefiest which I am a fan off....but I dont want you to think its a brick. its still plenty light where it wont feel like a burden lugging it around. This one also has a ocean/boat theme color pattern which is sweet and almost swayed me since i will be using this on my boat too. The other thing that almost swayed me was that the speaker can be used as a powerbank!!! So this ones sound is just as good as the other but the standout features are the looks, and the fact that it can be used as a powerbank which can come in very handy. Its not included but they have a bracket mount that clamps on to stuff.......not sure how it would hold up to movement and things like that but there is that option out there. These can also be paired with other Oontz speakers for a multi speaker set up. --Why I would choose the Doss Soundbox Pro: I hate to admit it but the price....and I actually chose this one over the Tribit and Oontz after my sound tests. The sound was on par with the other 2 (similar wattage to the Oontz) and I liked this one just a hair more than the Oontz because it was a little crisper sounding where the Oontz was a little fuller...if that makes sense. So with the sound being the same, the fact that I could ALSO pair multiple Doss speakers for a multi speaker set up just like the Oontz (this is a great feature for when entertaining guests/having a small party/get-together), and considering I'd primarily be using this in a bedroom (where the powerbank wouldnt come in as handy like the Oontz has).....I had to choose this one. review_title: A good unit with many features, and perhaps a tad pricey because of those features
body_en: In the world of Bluetooth speakers, this one struck me as a tad pricey, but not overly so. I am hoping for quality of build to let this thing last many years, and we'll see how that works. Meantime, the sound is nice. I use it mostly to listen to podcasts (including podcasts with music) and to stream stuff from Amazon music and Pandora, and the sound quality is OK for me for those purposes. I haven't used the bass emphasis button, finding I don't need that for what I listen to. The lighting feature is amusing, but I keep it off to lengthen battery life. The speakers provide a stereo sound, but I can't really discern a stereo result. Which is OK, I wasn't really expecting much in those regards, considering the speakers are so close to one another. The unit pairs with my iPhone extremely quickly. Haven't had it long enough to assess battery life (which can be a function of volume, use of lighting effects, use of the bass effect, and perhaps the phase of the moon). Overall, it meets my expectations fully and feels like it is well made.

This speaker is great. So far the battery life is superb and it gets very loud! I use this speaker in conjunction with a NUX Mighty Plug for guitar on the go. As expected with such a small speaker box the bass isn't extremely powerful but it sounds very crisp and full range if placed in the corner of a room with solid walls. I had a problem with the unit powering itself off at first until I realized it wasn't a low battery but an 'auto-off' feature when not playing anything. Searching this on the web, I didn't find anything on either their website or manual regarding an 'auto-off' feature for this model. Some suggested that DOSS has a firmware update available that disabled it. I spoke through email with a very nice person named Lizzie with their Customer Care team. Lizzie explained that units with the Version ID of VS3582 do not require any firmware updates to enable or disable this feature. If yours is a VS3582 then all you need to do in order to enable/disable the 'auto-off' feature is a button combo of Mode+Power and you'll see if flash red twice for off, green twice for on. Hold the bass button to cycle through lighting options (low, high, off). So far this little speaker has impressed me with what I intended to do with it and all my expectations are met. I am considering a 2nd one for stereo play! Hopefully Lizzie gets a raise soon

PACKAGING: The SoundBox Pro from DOSS is not only protected by a simple bag, there is also a plastic mold tailored to the speaker in the box. Otherwise there are very good instructions for use (also in German) a USB A to micro USB cable and a 3.5mm jack - jack connection cable. DESIGN: The speaker is rubberized all around, on the short sides you might suspect leather, but it is the rubber coating with a leather pattern. The keys are easy to reach and have a clearly noticeable pressure point. Small LEDs provide additional information. On the back behind the rubber cover there are Micro USB, 3.5mm jack and a Micro SD card port. At the front, a grille protects the two active and passive speakers. There is a plastic frame all around that is illuminated by LEDs, very stylish. FUNCTION: In terms of sound, the SoundBox Pro should not be underestimated. The volume is decent and the sound distorts minimally at max setting. The bass comes across well for such a small box, it can be compared to a kick bass so it's crisp. You get a long rumble if the speaker is placed on a surface that can vibrate a little, e.g. a wooden table. However, you can still change a lot using the equalizer settings on your cell phone. Stereo pairing is a great function that worked flawlessly for me. I couldn't detect any delays and there is no echo effect. The lighting effects are beautiful, especially at a garden party. These are best seen at night. For me, this is a function that certainly has a great effect in some situations (e.g. calm music in the evening on the sofa with pulsating LEDs). CONCLUSION: I don't want to miss the boxes. If I bought two, there was a discount during the promotional period. It definitely makes sense to go for it here and create a great soundscape through stereo pairing. If Bluetooth isn't the right choice, you can also connect directly to a 3.5mm blade (always connect to the master for stereo pairing) or alternatively songs on Micro SD.

We don't leave it on the charger when it's not in use. Charge it only when the battery is low. It won't take long to charge either. The volume is good for what we use it for.
