The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

review_title: I FINALLY GOT THIS SPEAK AND LOVE IT!!!
body_en: The Bose S1 Pro+ Wireless Speaker is a masterful blend of portability, power, and premium sound quality, making it an excellent choice for musicians, DJs, and music enthusiasts alike. Bose has set a new standard with this portable PA system, offering unmatched versatility and audio excellence. Design & Portability The S1 Pro+ boasts a sleek, modern design that’s both professional and stylish. Its compact form factor and lightweight build make it incredibly easy to transport, while the integrated handle ensures a firm grip. Despite its portability, the speaker exudes durability and feels solid, a testament to Bose’s commitment to quality. Sound Quality True to the Bose name, the sound is where the S1 Pro+ truly shines. Crisp Highs, Full Mids, and Rich Lows: Whether you’re playing soft acoustic tracks or pumping out bass-heavy dance music, the speaker delivers with remarkable clarity and balance. 360° Sound Coverage: The unique design ensures even distribution, making it perfect for both intimate gatherings and larger events. Automatic EQ: The speaker adjusts itself to the environment and placement, ensuring optimal sound whether it’s on the ground, elevated, or tilted. Features & Functionality Wireless Connectivity: The S1 Pro+ comes with seamless Bluetooth pairing, making it easy to stream music from any device. Built-in Mixer: The integrated three-channel mixer with reverb and tone controls allows for quick adjustments, ideal for performers and presenters. Battery Performance: With a rechargeable battery offering up to 11 hours of playtime, this speaker ensures the music keeps going all day (or night). Expandable Options: Pairing with other Bose speakers is effortless, allowing for an even more immersive experience. Use Cases The Bose S1 Pro+ is incredibly versatile, excelling in: Live music performances. Outdoor parties and events. Corporate presentations. Small to medium-sized DJ gigs. Personal use for those who value top-tier sound. Pros Exceptional sound quality with Bose’s signature audio precision. Portable yet robust design. Easy-to-use controls and a built-in mixer for versatile applications. Long battery life for uninterrupted playtime. Cons Premium pricing might be a consideration for budget-conscious buyers. No dedicated app for advanced customization. Final Verdict The Bose S1 Pro+ is a game-changer in the portable speaker market. It combines professional-grade sound, user-friendly features, and unmatched portability, making it an excellent investment for performers, event organizers, and audiophiles. Its premium price is justified by its quality and versatility, ensuring it remains a favorite in any setting. Rating: 5/5 If you’re looking for a portable speaker that delivers uncompromising sound quality and functionality, the Bose S1 Pro+ is in a league of its own.

Overall Impression This is my second speaker from the JBL Charge line, and once again, I’m impressed. The Charge 6 builds on what already worked well in previous models while delivering dependable performance, strong sound quality, and easy usability. Design & Build Quality The speaker feels sturdy and well-constructed without being overly bulky. It’s portable, easy to move around, and sits securely on a variety of surfaces. Whether placed on a kitchen counter, coffee table, or taken outdoors, it feels durable enough for everyday use. Setup & Connectivity Setup is quick and straightforward. I’ve had no issues pairing the Charge 6 with any of my devices. Bluetooth connection is stable and reliable, something I really value, as I’ve owned other speakers that occasionally failed to appear or dropped connection. In this area, the Charge 6 performs consistently well. Sound Quality For a speaker in this price range, the sound quality is impressive. Volume: Gets surprisingly loud for its size. Clarity: Remains stable and clear even at higher volumes, with minimal distortion. Bass: Punchy and full without overpowering the mids and highs. Vocals: Crisp and easy to distinguish. The overall sound profile feels balanced and energetic, making it versatile for different genres of music. Compared to the JBL Charge 5 I upgraded from the Charge 5, which already delivered excellent sound. The difference here isn’t dramatic, but the Charge 6 feels slightly louder and punchier, with a bit more fullness at higher volumes. It’s more of a refinement than a complete redesign, but a noticeable and appreciated one. Ideal Use Cases This speaker is well-suited for small to medium-sized rooms and performs great for small outdoor gatherings or backyard settings. I liked it enough to purchase a second unit and place one in each corner of my living space for a more balanced, room-filling setup. The stereo pairing through the JBL Portable app is simple and works seamlessly. Whenever I have friends over, the sound quality consistently gets compliments. Battery Life JBL advertises up to 24 hours of playback (tested at 50% volume). In my experience, listening at around 60% volume yields approximately 17–19 hours on a single charge, which has been more than sufficient for daily use. If I had one minor critique, it would be that battery life drops more noticeably at very high volumes. For example, during an all-day beach trip or extended outdoor event where the speaker is running near maximum volume, you may need to recharge sooner than expected. That said, for normal day-to-day listening and typical gatherings, battery performance has been dependable and not a deal breaker for me. Final Verdict The JBL Charge 6 delivers strong, punchy sound, reliable connectivity, and solid battery performance in a durable, portable design. While the upgrade from the Charge 5 isn’t dramatic, it’s a meaningful refinement. Overall, it’s a great value for the performance it provides and an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a versatile Bluetooth speaker.

review_title: The Ultimate Audio Wingman: Why the JBL Charge 6 Brings the Boom Without the Bulk!
body_en: We all know that feeling of finding the perfect piece of gear that just clicks with our lifestyle, and that is exactly what happened when I got my hands on the JBL Charge 6. In a sea of portable speakers that overpromise and underdeliver, this crisp, white beauty stands out as a true heavyweight in a surprisingly compact package. I am always on the move, whether I am out working in the garage, heading to the beach, or just kicking back by the backyard fire pit, and I need a device that can keep up. What struck me immediately about this particular model is how it completely redefines what a mid-sized portable speaker should be capable of handling. It is not just about making noise; it is about delivering a premium experience that seamlessly integrates into whatever crazy adventure my weekend throws at me. ​Let us talk about the absolute core of this device: the sound. The Bold JBL Pro Sound alone is phenomenal, but the real magic here is the AI Sound Boost technology. I have listened to countless audio setups, and I can confidently say that this proprietary audio processing algorithm fundamentally changes the game. It actively analyzes the music in real-time, pulling maximum acoustic performance out of the drivers while keeping distortion virtually non-existent, even when you crank the volume all the way up. The low-end bass kicks with a satisfying, punchy depth that you can feel in your chest, while the mids and highs remain exceptionally crisp and clear. Whether I am blasting classic rock anthems or heavy hip-hop tracks, the soundstage feels massive, filling up the entire patio or living room with rich, immersive audio that makes you forget you are listening to a portable unit. ​Now, an incredible-sounding speaker is useless to me if I have to baby it, which is why the rugged build of the Charge 6 is such a massive win. This thing is built like an absolute tank. It boasts serious waterproof and drop-proof credentials, meaning I never sweat it when a sudden rainstorm rolls in or when someone inevitably knocks it off the picnic table. I have watched it take a tumble directly onto hard concrete and brush it off like it was nothing, keeping the tunes rolling without a single hiccup. Adding to its utilitarian charm is the newly integrated, sturdy removable carrying strap. It sounds like a minor detail, but having that secure strap makes hauling it around infinitely easier. I can sling it over a bag, hang it from a hook in the workshop, or just keep a solid grip on it while hiking, all without compromising its sleek, streamlined white aesthetic. ​Perhaps the most crucial factor for a device that travels this much is endurance, and the battery life on the Charge 6 is nothing short of legendary. JBL packed this beast with up to 28 hours of playtime, and it absolutely delivers on that promise. I have taken it on multi-day camping trips and never once had to reach for a wall charger. But the absolute lifesaver is the built-in powerbank feature. We all know how fast smartphones drain when streaming high-quality music outdoors, so having the ability to plug my phone directly into the speaker to juice it back up while the playlist keeps pumping is incredibly practical. It is the ultimate two-in-one companion that ensures neither the party nor my phone dies prematurely. This speaker does not just meet my high standards for portable audio; it utterly shatters them.

review_title: Honest review of the JBL Charge 6 portable bluetooth speaker
body_en: At almost 60 years old, I’ve experienced just about every kind of audio system imaginable — component stereo systems, high-end car audio setups, premium headphones, earbuds, home theater systems, and portable speakers from many of the biggest brands. Because of that, it takes quite a bit to genuinely impress me when it comes to sound quality. The JBL Charge 6 absolutely impressed me. What JBL accomplished with this speaker is remarkable. The sound is incredibly powerful considering such a small footprint. This thing is compact enough to fit easily into almost any backpack, yet it produces bold, room-filling sound that feels much larger than the speaker itself. The audio quality is excellent. The highs are crystal clear, vocals sound clean and detailed, and the bass is deep, punchy, and robust without sounding muddy or distorted. Even at higher volumes, the sound remains balanced and enjoyable. The volume range is outstanding — this speaker gets surprisingly loud while still maintaining clarity. I’ve owned expensive audio equipment over the years, and honestly, the sound coming from this little speaker is shocking for its size. Whether indoors, outdoors, traveling, relaxing at home, or using it near water, the JBL Charge 6 consistently delivers an impressive listening experience. Bluetooth connectivity is fast and simple, and the portability is one of its biggest strengths. JBL also did a great job with durability. The waterproof and drop-proof design makes it ideal for everyday life, travel, and outdoor use without constantly worrying about damaging it. Battery life and durability seem to vary somewhat based on user experiences. Many people report excellent battery life that lasts all day, while others feel it could be better depending on usage and volume levels. Most users praise the rugged build quality, though a few have experienced durability concerns after heavy use. Overall, this speaker exceeded my expectations. After decades of owning and listening to high-end audio equipment, I can honestly say the JBL Charge 6 delivers an incredible amount of performance, clarity, and power for such a compact portable speaker. Small speaker. Massive sound. Very impressive product from JBL.

Setup was straightforward through the Alexa app—created a child profile, set parental controls (time limits, content filters, activity monitoring), and the included 6 months of Amazon Kids+ kicked in right away. Sound is surprisingly good for such a compact, rounded speaker—clear vocals for stories, music from kid-safe playlists, and Alexa answers questions appropriately without adult content. The silicone sleeve feels durable and kid-proof, plus there’s a physical mic-off button for extra privacy peace of mind. My son loves asking for bedtime stories, animal facts, jokes, or playing songs—he’s obsessed with the pup look and calls it his “DJ buddy.” We’ve used it daily for routines like morning alarms or homework help skills. No issues with connectivity or quality after a couple months. At $49.99 with the free Kids+ trial (worth about $30), it’s a great value compared to bigger Echo Dot Kids models. Highly recommend for ages 3-10ish—perfect balance of fun and parent-approved safety

The compact size is perfect for smaller spaces, and it doesn’t take up much room on a shelf or bedside table. The sound quality is impressive for its size. It provides access to interactive games, quizzes, and stories that can keep kids entertained and engaged. Overall, the Amazon Echo Pop Kids (newest gen) is a fantastic choice for families with young children. It combines engaging features with strong parental controls, making it a practical and enjoyable device for kids. Highly recommend for a fun and educational addition to your child’s tech collection!

Since you're looking at this particular set, I'm going to guess you've probably set a limit to how much you want to spend on what's likely going to be your every day set of knives. You might own more expensive (and arguably better) knives, but you’d rather not see them used by anyone who is not as concerned as you are with their integrity and longevity. You’ve also seen first hand the difference between the Wusthof Gourmet series and the classic Wusthof, and you also know Henkel doesn’t quite cut it. If I guessed right and you’re considering buying this set for these or similar reasons, do not hesitate: buy it right now! These knives are a cut above your usual value knife sets. Cool, sexy looks, sharp blades that stay sharp, full tang, well balanced overall, sturdy but ergonomic handles with no sharp lines. They even sound great - you know, that tuning fork ring they make if you just give them a gentle tap - so it’s really easy to pick up the right knife with eyes closed if you have perfect pitch! :P Everything most knives in this price range aren’t. I actually ended up liking these knives so much I now use them more often than my Global set. This is not to say the Globals are not the superior knives, it’s just that these Dalstrong knives are *perfectly fine* for most things someone who cooks for pleasure and not for a living will find themselves using them for. I will say that one of the knives I received had a small flaw - a crack in the side of the handle that looks like it occurred on riveting. I contacted Dalstrong support. Three days later I had the replacement. No runaround, no BS. They looked at the pictures I sent and just replied asking for my shipping address. Honestly, how often does that happen? (Thanks Rachelle for the terrific customer support experience!) You may rest assured that whatever issue you have with the product, they’ll make it right. I believe other reviews mentioned the awesome customer support as well, and I can confirm these guys really stand by their product. After the very positive experience with this set, I do think I’ll try some of their more premium knives soon (they’re still not even close to premium-priced). In short: These are value-priced knives that have none (or close to none) of the shortcomings you’d expect for the price, while blowing some of the established choices out of the water in some regards. Certainly the modern, streamlined looks will strike some conversations (yes, I know, that’s highly subjective).

I received the Dalstrong Gladiator knife set a couple of weeks ago and I am very pleased with this purchase. I did not comment on durability as I have had this set for a minimal amount of time. I would be surprised if they failed to deliver over the long haul and will comment further should they not. Overall, this set is aesthetically pleasing and does very well what it is supposed to do. I highly recommend this Dalstrong set.

Received the set today. With that in mind, I’m writing the review about the individual set that I got, not the Dalstrong product line. Delivery: The knives came individually wrapped and tip-protected. The set split between 3 boxes, the block and 2 boxes packed with knives. All neatly packed. Each knife, as I said, with a plastic tip protector, sheathed in cardboard and wrapped in bubble wrap. In my case, observing the packaging that I received, it’s beyond me how could anyone cut their fingers to the bone unwrapping, as some reviewers said they did. Construction: Superb. Simply superb. No lose parts, no unfinished surfaces. I’m not sure where other reviewers found “sharp edges”, in mynindividual case - superb construction. Block: again, having read other reviews I was expecting sloppy glue job, cracks in the block etc. What I received is far from that - a superb block. Yes, the logo is plastic. I don’t care. The block is hard wood. Nicely finished. Period. The socket for the sharpening iron is a bit through - that’s what gives you the clue, it’s wood. Not plastic glued witn veneer. It is solid wood. Balance. I’m not a professional, rather an amateur chef, but I cook for the family of 5 a lot. And I mean it - a LOT. I love it and yo me working with a good tool in the kitchen is as important as cooking a lamb kabob to juiciest perfection. These knives are very well balanced. The 8” chef just asks to put it in action right away - the weight of the knife is right there, comfortably fit in your hand. I chopped up 3 onions with it just for the pleasure of the experience. Bagged the onion - will put it to a good use tomorrow. Again, right out of the box, the knives that matter are reasonably sharp (and not excessively), offer good balance and are nice looking tools all around. Bottom lime: great delivery. Great packaging. Awesome set. I cannot speak for the long term performance just yet. Having read some other reviews that claim that the blades developed rust, I resolved to hard washing and wiping the blades with a lightly oiled paper towel. Something I do anyway. Will update if detwct any issues going forward. That’s why I keep the “durability” section vacant our now.

I bought this set 9 years ago. After using them thrice daily cooking for a family of five they're still great! I have obviously sharpened them, several times, over the years, but the handles and block still look good. The honing tool also works well between sharpening sessions. The knives are well balanced and the grips are a comfortable shape and size. No rust has ever occurred on the knives, but I always clean and dry them quickly after use. I wish this set came with a carving fork, but I didn't know that it I wanted that 9 years ago.

review_title: Best knives I have purchased to this day
body_en: OK guys hello! And welcome to my review! I will inform you that I purchased a white set 18 piece block and upon arrival it was like any other Amazon package. I read the reviews and was quite amazed at some reactions. I have only owned them for 3 weeks so far, no I have not ridden over them, jumped on them or thrown them off the roof and had them break..... I unpacked them and the block from the boxes and the knives were sharp enough to cut my arm hair with just grazing them. That was a pretty good start. The block itself is very smooth, nice wood cuts. Love the finish on it and fits on the counter with finesse. Once I set the block up I was eager to try out the knives. The ergonomics of the these knives are great, they fit well. Smooth, not bulky, and easy to adhere to. Tried the 🍅 test with the chef knife and it passed, the paper test needed some more testing but they are great. I have used the slicing knife for chicken and brisket, I have used the chef knife for all my general slicing, steak knives for steak and they are all.performing above the expectation for the price!. This set is a must have for your kitchen, seriously authentically pleasing, comfortable, and great to use. One con is they shouldn't go into the dishwasher and that they have to be cleaned and dried. They shouldn't be left in the sink for too long. So overall I would recommend these knives to intermediate/ expert level cooks just for daily house hold cooking and outings. Though you do need to sharpen them after a week of use. Easy to sharpen though. They recommend a whet stone from their shop, but the rod works fine.

review_title: Un magnifique produit et des couteaux de qualité.
body_en: I bought this product (on promotion) and the quality of Gladiator knives is high with exceptional sharpness and hardness. I would never have spent the sum of €1000 requested at the start... The set of knives is uniform with 3 rivets on the handles and a magnificent finish. The maintenance of the knives and the quality of the handles is top of the range with a lifetime guarantee. The walnut block is also magnificent but we had to return the whole thing because the wooden block was split. Unfortunately, this is a recurring problem with this type of block. We returned the product and took a Dalstrong set with 6 knives for a less imposing magnetic wooden storage of 12 knives. Besides, we see the knives all the time, which is more practical and nicer. The knives are of an even higher range (Phantom). Too bad for the wooden block, well finished with stamp underneath. The return was hassle-free. We are really looking at real durable knives, far from what can be offered in very “pretty” sets but with poor durability.
The plastic handle cracks

review_title: Outstanding product, even better customer service.
body_en: The first set that arrived had a minor (and I mean minor) finishing flaw which niggled at me enough to make mention of it to the seller, wow! This seller goes above and beyond in satisfying their customers, this is the sort of customer service that major companies only dream about, they are truly top tier! As for the product itself even the one with the minor flaw was good, the replacement flawless. The knives themselves I have been using for a couple of weeks or so and they are showing no signs of wear and tear, keeping a sharp edge and haven’t even needed to see a steel let alone a sharpener yet. The weight and balance is all there plus slicing through my fillet steak like it was butter even shocked me, and I’m an ex Butcher by trade. On top of that the block looks great on the worktop, even the wife was impressed after whinging about the cost lol. I would highly recommend this product and I will purchase from this company for the rest of my life so long as they keep up their standards as I was so highly impressed with the care they gave me as a customer. In fact I have already lined up my next purchase ‘the Obliterator’ cleaver which is part of this range. Honestly I am so happy...of course if the knives start showing signs of rust or ruin within an unreasonable time frame I will update this review.
Great quality they feel good to use retain their sharpness for ages!!

Very pleased. Good quality. Definitely recommend.

body_en: This is easily the finest set of knives I've ever owned. Granted, that may not be saying much given the ones I've owned before, but I did spend many years in the restaurant industry, so I've had exposure to quality cutlery. Using these, it's actually a pleasure to cut and dice food. Not only are they sharp as a razor, but the balance is wonderful. I highly recommend these, especially at this reasonable price!

review_title: Decent knife set for the price
body_en: This 3 PCS Shinobi Chef Knife Set from Cutluxe comes beautifully arranged in its own box which on itself can even be gifted . The knives themselves are gorgeous looking with beautiful wooden handles which are obviously ergonomic. They definitely add to the richness of the kitchen and the knives themselves ooze quality. They can give a run to my branded knife sets any time as the three knives amongst themselves can take care of all my kitchen needs from cutting meats (chicken and fish), vegetables and fruits or breads and cakes you name it. The blades are very sharp and one has to be quite careful but the grip is amazing and that give you the sense of safety that you need when handling these. Once I am done my job with these, I wash them in warm water with soap, rinse and wipe them off. I do have several knife sharpeners so once the blade gets dull I can always polish them. I do recommend as the price is almost one third of my branded set but does the same job.

I recently received the Shinobi Chef Knife Set by Cutluxe, and I am very impressed with their performance and craftsmanship. This 3-piece set includes a chef knife, a santoku knife, and a paring knife, all designed with Japanese-inspired aesthetics and razor-sharp blades. The first thing I noticed was how incredibly sharp they are, they literally glides through vegetables, meats, and fish without any resistance. The high-carbon stainless steel used in the blades makes them durable, and I can already tell they’ll last me a long time. The ergonomic Pakkawood handles not only look great, they are comfortable to hold, giving me great control while chopping or slicing. I also appreciate the full tang design, which ensures the knives feel solid and well-balanced in my hands, even when performing more delicate tasks. The knives feel and look professional at a great price point. Cleaning them is a breeze, and they maintain their sharpness after several uses. Honestly, I was skeptical, but after using them, I can confidently say these are great knives. If you’re looking for knives that combine beauty with performance at a reasonable price, this set is definitely a solid choice.

review_title: Fantastic quality for such a low price !!
body_en: Now, to be quite frank, I don’t treat my kitchen knives very well. I did need to get some new ones, and I decided to give this set of 3 a try, and i am NOT disappointed. review_title: Sharp, beautiful, and sturdy knife set!
body_en: I have wanted these Henckels knives for a long time and finally got the opportunity during a Prime Day sale. I can't say enough good things about these knives. They are sharp so be careful! review_title: Once you pick up one of these knives and use it, you will know your decision was correct
body_en: I'm pretty sure that this set I just bought is the fourth set in my lifetime. No question of which is the best set and it's the Henckels. My, what a beautiful set of knives, with one for every need in the kitchen or at dinner. The steel is high quality and the blades are thin, a combination which is ideal for ease of use. What strikes you is the hefty handle and the slender blade, providing a great balance in the hand. And, of course, they come razor sharp and also an excellent sharpener is provided with the set. I don't think there is a competing set of knives on the market which can compare.

bought these knives to prep dinner. I wasn’t expecting to enter a committed relationship. The first time I used the chef’s knife, it slid through a tomato so effortlessly that I had to look around to make sure nobody saw me smiling. The sharpness is downright scandalous. Carrots? Paper-thin. Steak? Like butter. My old knives watched from the drawer in shame. The balance is incredible, the grip feels just right in your hand, and every slice is so smooth it should probably come with a warning label. Cooking has become dangerously enjoyable. Honestly, I haven’t felt this much excitement in the kitchen in years. If you’ve never whispered, “Oh… wow,” after slicing a bell pepper, you’re about to. Five stars. Sharp enough to cut vegetables… and dangerously close to stealing my heart. ❤️🔪

review_title: Great set, review after a year of use
body_en: I've had this knife set for over a year now. I have no cons to it at all. I use the honing rod probably every other time I use the big chef knives, and they're still as sharp and beautiful as the first day I got them. Every single knife is sturdy and feels solid. I hand wash all the sharp blades, but I do run the serrated ones through my dishwasher sometimes because I'm lazy 😅. I like that the prep knives lay on their sides in the block, I think that protects the blades better. The steak knives fit in vertically, but I just put them in upside down so they don't rest on the cutting edge. I don't like how close the honing rod is to the bread knife right below it, but that's not too big of a deal. The knives and block look beautiful on my counter, and everything seems to be great quality. I am glad I bought this and am considering buying one for my daughter.

I am very happy with this knife set. They arrived razor sharp. Unfortunately, the spine is also very sharp and I keep cutting my fingers on them, thus the four star rating. I still recommend them, just be careful.
This knife block is wonderful. Every type of knife you could need and they have a great weight and feel to them. Most importantly, they are super sharp and work great! Highly recommend this block.

review_title: Decent quality blades that are easy to keep sharp
body_en: The steel is arguably soft, but that is typical of european (particularly german) blades. The iron content of this stainless steel is high and the nickel content may be low. If left wet for long, it may develop rust spots. However, you should always clean and dry a knife after using it anyway. If taken care of, these blades will last many years. They will cut what you want and retain a nice shape. The chef's knife is great. It is the primary knife used in my kitchen. It is comfortable to use, slices through most anything with relative ease. After about ten to fifteen diced onions I like to hone the blade again to keep work quick and easy. A dull knife is much more dangerous than a sharp one they say. Despite frequent maintenance, it does an excellent job and doesn't fatigue me. The santokus are of decent quality, and feel excellent for everyday tasks. The larger one has a good weight and feeling allowing for prolonged veggie extermination, and the smaller one is light and maneuverable to really slice and shape whatever you need. The paring knife is a razor blade with a handle basically. If the chef knife is too big or unwieldy for a task, the lil guy will step up with no issue. The bread knife is sharp. It WILL cut bread. Cake too, I bet. There is another smaller serrated knife but I have yet to use it. The scissors are nothing special but provide you something to open any package of food. The steak knives are beautiful but have lesser quality steel than the bigger knives. These will straight up form rust spots if left in the sink overnight, esp along the handle and spine of the blade. Just clean them after use and they should stay pretty and sharp for ya. The included file is useful to keep my blades honed. I'd say this set is a pretty solid value for your money if you are looking for a good set of knives for the kitchen. If you don't sharpen your knives or prefer a cheap kitchenaid knife, this isn't for you. For the home cook who uses their knives for everything and appreciates them, I recommend them.

review_title: 200 reasons to skip washing the butter knife.
body_en: These are good quality for disposable knives. They’re sturdy, heavy duty, BPA-free, and heat resistant, so they can handle both hot and cold foods without feeling flimsy. They’re definitely nice enough for parties, cookouts, and other events, but honestly, that’s not why I got them. In my house, apparently nobody wants to wash the butter knives after using them, so I decided to solve the problem! Now here’s 200 reasons why nobody (ME!) has to for the moment lol! For everyday home use, having a big supply of sturdy disposable knives is just convenient. For 200 in the pack, I think they’re a decent bulk value and exactly what the main in the house dishwasher (Me again!) calls for. One buying note: the presentation you receive is much more basic than what’s pictured online. I received them in plain brown cardboard with no identifying graphics, just a small sticker and barcode on the side indicating what the item is. So if you’re expecting the presentation shown in the listing, just be aware that what you receive may look quite different.

This box comes with a nice quantity of plastic knives. I didn't count them, but there are a lot in here, so I'll assume they're all present & accounted for. The knives don't feel extra strong to me. They feel like they'd snap in half if I tried to run it through some thick peanut butter. They're cheap (in quality, not in price) but still handy.

These knives are a great value. They aren't quite as heavy-duty as some of the more expensive name-brand disposable options, but they are noticeably better than many similarly priced plastic knives I've tried in the past. Those tended to be flimsy, undersized, and prone to bending, while these feel sturdy enough for everyday use. I brought some along on a recent camping trip and was pleasantly surprised that they had no trouble cutting through steak. (Although, to be fair, I deserve some credit for cooking a pretty good steak.) It was convenient not having to dig out my metal knives and then deal with cleaning them afterward. My only minor complaint is that the clear plastic on the business end has a slightly wavy appearance. It doesn't affect performance at all, but it is noticeable if you look closely. Then again, if your guests are closely inspecting the appearance of your disposable knives at a gathering, you probably should have used the metal ones in the first place. Overall, these are a solid choice for parties, camping, picnics, or any situation where you want a durable disposable knife without paying a premium.

review_title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
body_en: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

review_title: A perfect addition to my kitchen
body_en: While visiting my sister, I used her set of Cuisinart knifes. She place the time of purchase somewhere between 5 and 7 years, and they were wonderful. Easy to handle, not to heavy, and a great variety of knives for cutting different types of foods. The steak knives are the best I have ever used, the Santoku (the blade is wide in height and snub nosed) cut a left over roast into very, very thin slices for hot roast beef sandwiches. In early July, I purchased the Classic Forged Triple Riveted set of 15 knives and the block, because the set held most of the knives I was looking for and they fit right into my kitchen décor. And, my struggle of 59 years in my kitchen, trying to cut vegetables, fruits, meats and breads and struggling with knives has come to an end. It is such a mental and physical relieve to start a meal knowing that cutting "whatever" will no longer be a struggle. My new knives are the best I have ever purchased and I have purchased a lot of knives. Wish I had know a long time ago about Cuisinart knives, didn't know that they made anything but electric appliances for the kitchen. A little bit of a down side, be prepared for a larger than normal knife holding block, and it is heavy, but again the length of the knives make it necessary and are worth the block size and weight. Would I recommend them to my best friend.....in a heart beat! But...would I purchase this set again, no, but I would purchase the solid metal handle set, as the paring knife handle has cracked from the rivet to the edge of the handle. I care for my knives, I hand wash and dry them and put them away, I am concerned that if one handle cracks after a month and a half of use, how long before another on cracks. Overall, I would have given this set of knives a 5 star except for the cracked handle.

"Quality you notice from the very first cut! This Cuisinart set not only looks amazing in my kitchen thanks to its impeccable design, but the sharpness and balance of each knife make cooking much more efficient. An investment that is truly worth it."

A little warning for you all if you get these - and I'm embarrassed to even discuss this: When you fill the knife block with the knives - make sure the sharp side of the big knives are all turned to the middle of the block. review_title: The Zenith Collection is the Best Essential Kitchen Knife Set on the Market for the Price
body_en: A Little about me: I Have Been a Knife Enthusiast, Collector And Former Knife Maker For Over 40 Years. (Information Below From Various Research) A Little about PAUDIN: PAUDIN is a Fairly New Up and Coming Knife Company that was Started in 2017 By David XIAO. The Company has been in Business for about 9 Years and the Steels are Obtained From Different Parts of the World that is Manufacturing High Quality Knife Steel Like Japan, Germany, Sweden Etc. Etc. No One Actually Knows Where each Steel is Acquired Because it is a Company Secret. Although PAUDIN Is a Recent Upstart, PAUDIN Makes the Knives in Yangjiang, China - A City Famous for Knife Making for Almost 1500 Years. PAUDIN has been Producing High Quality Knife Sets that are Functional and Beautiful for the Price. About the PAUDIN Zenith Collection 5 PCS Kitchen Knife Essential Chef Knives Ultra Sharp Set. These Knives have all the Best Qualities of the Chef's Essentials in the Kitchen. The Knives Include an 8" Chef Knife, an 8" Bread Knife, a 5" Santoku Knife, a 7" Nakiri Knife and a 5" Utility Knife that are All Essential Favorites of Chef's. Each of the Knives is Full Tang Which means the Blade is the Full Length of the Knife and through the Handle for Superior Strength. The Handles are Beautifully made From G10 which is a Form of Fiberglass and Securely Riveted to the Knife Blades. The Knives are Perfectly Balanced and Fit Very Well into your Hand. For Me, the Most Important Part of the Knives are the Steel that is Used to make the Blades. The Steel used is CJ14C28N Also Known as SANDVIK Steel, Originally From Sweden. This Steel Has Been in High Quality Knife Making For Many Years. This is a High Carbon Steel that has Excellent Corrosion Resistance and Holds a Good Edge Sharpness at 58-60 HRC on the Rockwell Hardness Scale. The BEST PART-PAUDIN Takes the Hardness to a Whole New Level With Their Custom Vacuum Heat Treating and Cryogenic Quenching Process Boosts the Rockwell Hardness Scale to an AMAZING 63 HRC Which Rivals or Beats the Blade Hardness some of the FINEST Blades ever Made. The Process is Explained in their Listing and Is Extremely Interesting with the Photos. This Supercharged Hardness Makes the Blades Hold an Extreme Edge and Yet Be Resistant to Chipping. These Blades are Amazing For Hardness and Razor Sharpness. This 5 Piece Set is a Great Addition or Start to Anyone's Kitchen. They are Sharpened Beyond Standard Sharpening and Cut Very Easily. The Price on this Set is Also Amazingly Low and PAUDIN Offers Discount Coupons at Close to Almost 50% off. So Don't Wait or Hesitate, Get Yourself One of these Sets and You'll be Happy You Did.

review_title: Sharp knives with a unique heel design
body_en: The knife set by PAUDIN includes 5 popular styles used in today’s kitchens. The set includes an 8” Chef, 8” Bread, 7” Nakiri, 5” Santoku and a 5” Utility knife. According to the product listing, the knives are constructed with CJ14C28N steel that undergoes Vacuum Nitriding and Deep Cryogenic Treatment to enhance toughness, reduce edge chipping risk, and improved corrosion resistance. The edge angle of the blade is listed as 13° and has a hardness rating of 63HRC. The full tang handle is covered with G10 high pressure fiberglass laminate. The included product guide states to use a wood or bamboo cutting board and to hand wash and dry immediately after use. I could not find any mention of “dishwasher safe” in the product guide. I tested all 5 knives and they are all incredibly sharp. In fact, the bread knife is the sharpest bread knife I have ever had and cleanly cuts through hard crust without crushing the bread. The Nakiri, Chef’s and Santoku knives easily cut through a variety of vegetables with very little effort. While the Nakiri knife may look like a mini-cleaver, it is typically intended for cutting soft foods or vegetables. The G10 handles are comfortable to hold, grippy and are thicker in the middle. The heel of the knife has a curved cutout for the index finger, but creates a sharp point where the curve meets the edge of the knife. While this sharp point is easy to avoid on the larger knives, it is not the case for the 5” Utility knife because of the lower blade height. If you typically hold the knife with a thumb and index finger, it is easy to poke yourself because there is less physical space. I’m thinking of dulling the point with a stone to prevent skin punctures. Even though I’m on the fence with the heel design of the blade, this set contains a nice variety of very sharp knives that would be great in any kitchen.

review_title: Sharp Today, But Ask Me Again in Six Months
body_en: New knives are fun. Very fun. There is nothing like a fresh blade. I opened the box like a kid on Christmas. Five knives. All shiny. All new. All grinning at me in a menacing, helpful way. And they cut. Oh, they cut. Ultra sharp, just like the box said. I sliced a tomato and it barely noticed. Thin slices. Clean slices. Slices you could read a newspaper through. I chopped an onion. No sawing. No crushing. Just a smooth glide. The onion did not stand a chance. The onion did not even see it coming. Let me talk handles. Full tang. That is the good stuff. The metal runs all the way through the handle. No cheap little stub hiding in there. It feels solid. It feels balanced. It feels like it means business. That full tang is a good sign. It usually means quality. It usually means the knife will not snap when you get bold with a squash. So far, so good. But here is my big question. The only question that matters. How long will they stay this sharp? That is the real test. Anything is sharp on day one. Day one is easy. Day one is a honeymoon. The blade is fresh. The angle is perfect. The romance is real. Day two hundred is the truth. Will they still glide? Or will I be sawing at a tomato like a caveman with a butter knife? I do not know yet. I cannot know yet. Sharpness fades slow. It sneaks up on you. One day you are slicing like a pro. The next day you are pressing hard and hoping. So I am watching. I am cutting. I am keeping notes like a suspicious scientist. Right now they are wonderful. The full tang gives me hope. The build feels honest. But the jury is out. Way out. The jury went home for the weekend. Let me talk value. Five knives for a fair price. Good so far. If the edge holds, this is a steal. If it dulls fast, this is a lesson. So here is where I land. Great out of the box. Scary sharp. Solid handles. But durability is the whole game, and I have not played enough of it yet.

I bought this as a housewarming gift and it turned out to be a huge mistake. The outer box arrived dented and beat‑up right out of delivery. The knives felt sharp at first, but they dulled super fast after minimal use. Cutting soft tomatoes is already a struggle. Some blades have tiny rough burrs along the edge. There is no proper block for storage either. Embarrassing to give this as a gift. Complete garbage for the price. Stay far away.

These knives arrive sharpened and ready to use immediately, and have been a great addition to our kitchen. These knives are light, but they have just the right amount of small weight so that it can cut through thick meats and fruits easily. The Santoku Knife was probably the most unexpectedly impressive out of all of the knives. At first glance, it seems that the knife is too small to handle for everyday use. However, it is in fact this size, and how well it cuts is what makes it all-rounded. The knife is light, which makes it easier to cut faster whilst having control over it. Until I started using the Santoku knife, I did not realize how unnecessarily big other knives were. The Chef Knife is an average sized chef knife. I mainly use this to cut thicker, harder things. Although slightly heavier than the Santoku knife, it is still light which gives me a lot of control. With how well it is sharpened, it can cut through hard fruits like melon/watermelon like butter. The other knives are also nice and sharpened, and is high-quality overall. The price is quite high, and for this price it would have been nice if it came with a knife holder. However I can certainly say that these are one of the best kitchen knives I've used. I am hoping that the knives will retain its sharpness for quite a while before it will need sharpening.

I’ve been very impressed with Paudin knives in general, and this 5 piece set certainly continues that. The knives are extremely sharp, and the handles are comfortable for my hands. With plastic handles and stainless steel blades, they are easy to keep clean and should last a very long time. It’s a little hard to judge the price; currently they are listed at one price but have a coupon for 40% off…at the list price I would say they are a decent value but that you might find other sets to be a better value; at the coupon price, they are a great value. I didn’t have any particular intention when I ordered this set, but now that I have them, this is going to be my traveling knife set. I’ve gotten used to taking at least one or two knives with me when I rent a summer vacation house, since they never seem to have decent or sharp knives. With the padded carrying case these come in, I can now take a very nice selection of sharp and high-quality knives with me. That’s a win. My final comment, and it doesn’t detract from my rating, is that I’d love this set even more if the santoku and small utility knife were just a little bigger. review_title: Excellent All‑Steel Knives That Perform Better Than Expected!!
body_en: I’ve owned several Cuisinart knives over the years, and this all–stainless steel set is definitely one of their winners. Each knife is forged from a single piece of steel, giving them a sleek, modern look and a sturdy feel. I’ll admit when I first saw the stainless steel handles, I assumed they would be slippery, especially when chopping veggies. Luckily, that wasn’t the case at all. They’re surprisingly comfortable, well‑balanced, and offer a secure grip even during longer prep sessions. The standout for me is the 7” Santoku knife (C77SS-7SAN-25K). It’s a Japanese style incredibly sharp, solidly built, and the longer blade length gives you great control. If you’re used to a 5" Santoku, it may feel a bit heavier and may take a little bit of getting used to, but once you do, it’s hard to go back. Like the rest of the knives in the set, this one arrives razor‑sharp and stays that way as long as you care for it properly. My next best favorite is the western style Chef's knife (C77SS-CF-25K) which is what most folks like including the chefs as it allows to cut a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. It has a curved edge("belly") with a pointed tip. My Third favorite cutting knife is the Slicing Knife (C77SS-SL-25K) which is specifically useful for slicing large cuts of either cooked meat or fish. It has a long, narrow blade with a pointed tip. I found this to be useful for cutting larger fruits like Watermelon, Melons or gourds etc. as the longer blade allows you to cut/slice them their vertical length. To keep these knives in top shape, here are a few care tips I personally follow: Use the right cutting surface: Stick to wood or plastic cutting boards. Harder surfaces like glass, stone, or metal will dull the blade quickly. Hand‑wash only: Clean with warm, soapy water and dry immediately with a soft cloth. Make sure the knife is completely dry before storing it. Avoid scraping with the sharp edge: If you need to move chopped ingredients, flip the knife over and use the back of the blade or a scraper. Store properly: Always use the included sheath. Storing knives loose in a drawer can damage the edge and create a safety hazard. If you follow these simple steps, these knives will stay sharp and serve you well for a long time. Overall, this is a great quality set that delivers excellent value and performance. Highly recommend!

review_title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
body_en: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

The rivets are securely fastened, and the knives feel well-balanced and comfortable in hand. The included blade guards are a fantastic addition. The guards fit snugly and are easy to put on and take off, adding an extra layer of safety when handling the knives. Another standout feature is the ergonomic design of the handles. The handles are comfortable to hold, with a good grip that reduces hand fatigue during extended use. The weight and balance of the knives are just right, making them easy to maneuver and control. The 10-piece set includes a variety of knives that cover all essential kitchen tasks, from a chef's knife to a paring knife. Each knife is thoughtfully designed for its specific purpose, making this set versatile and comprehensive. The included scissors are a useful bonus, adding to the overall value of the set. In summary, the Cuisinart C77CR-10P 10pc Stainless Steel ColorCore™ Color Rivet Set with Blade Guards is an excellent knife set that combines quality, style, and practicality. The sharp stainless steel blades, colorful rivets, and included blade guards make this set a standout choice for any kitchen. I highly recommend this knife set to anyone looking for a reliable and stylish upgrade to their culinary tools. It has exceeded my expectations and has become an essential part of my kitchen routine.

The Ninja K52015 Foodi NeverDull 15-Piece Knife System is an impressive addition to any kitchen for those who want quality, durability, and a stylish design. This set includes a wood series block, crafted in walnut, giving it a warm, high-end look that fits beautifully on the countertop. Pros: 1. Built-in Sharpener: The standout feature is the NeverDull built-in sharpener, which is incredibly convenient. A quick sharpening stroke every few uses keeps the knives in prime condition without needing additional tools. 2. German Stainless Steel: The quality of the German stainless steel is immediately noticeable. The knives are sturdy, corrosion-resistant, and retain their sharpness impressively well. 3. Variety and Versatility: The 15-piece set includes all essential knives, from chef’s and paring knives to steak knives, making it versatile enough for nearly any kitchen task. 4. Ergonomics and Comfort: Each knife feels balanced and comfortable to hold, with ergonomically designed handles that reduce hand strain, especially when preparing large meals. Cons: 1. Block Size: The block is substantial, which is great for stability, but it can take up a bit of counter space. Smaller kitchens may find this a challenge. 2. Price Point: While the quality justifies the price, this set is on the premium side. Budget-conscious buyers might find it a significant investment. Overall Impression: The Ninja K52015 Foodi NeverDull 15-Piece Premium Knife System is a reliable and stylish choice for both casual cooks and culinary enthusiasts. The self-sharpening feature alone makes it worth considering, as it simplifies maintenance and keeps the knives performing like new. For anyone looking for a quality, all-in-one knife set that blends function with aesthetics, this is a top-tier choice.

It’s also a great backup for experienced shooters who want something reliable, portable, and affordable. ⸻ Final Verdict The Canon EOS Rebel T7 is proof that entry-level doesn’t mean low quality. It’s a fantastic intro into the world of serious photography, and once you start using it, you’ll wonder why you waited. Sharp photos, simple learning curve, and real Canon reliability.

review_title: Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality
body_en: Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality I purchased the Canon EOS Rebel T7 as my first DSLR, and it’s been a great experience so far. This camera is perfect for beginners who want to learn photography without getting overwhelmed by too many features. Pros: • Image Quality: The 24.1MP sensor delivers crisp and vibrant photos, especially in good lighting. I’ve taken some fantastic landscape and portrait shots. • User-Friendly: The interface is intuitive, and the built-in guide mode helps explain settings and functions. Great for those new to DSLR photography. • Wi-Fi and NFC: Easy to transfer photos to your phone or tablet using Canon’s app. A big plus for quick sharing on social media. • Battery Life: It lasts a full day of shooting if you’re not constantly using Live View or flash. Cons: • No 4K Video: It records 1080p, which is okay, but if you’re looking to shoot high-quality video, this might be a limitation. • No Touchscreen or Articulating LCD: The screen is fixed and not touch-sensitive, which can make navigating menus slower compared to more modern cameras. • Autofocus in Live View: Slower and less reliable, especially when shooting video or using the screen instead of the viewfinder. Bottom Line: If you’re just starting out and want a reliable DSLR without breaking the bank, the Canon T7 is a solid choice. It’s not packed with advanced features, but it gets the job done and does it well. Ideal for hobbyists, students, or anyone learning the ropes of manual photography.

The Canon EOS Rebel T7 is an excellent entry-level DSLR camera that offers great value, especially with the included EF 18-55mm and EF 75-300mm lenses. Whether you’re a beginner learning the basics of photography or someone looking for an affordable camera with solid image quality, this kit delivers. Pros: ✅ Image Quality – The 24.1 MP APS-C sensor captures sharp and vibrant images with great detail, even in low-light situations. ✅ Dual Lens Kit – The 18-55mm lens is great for everyday shots, while the 75-300mm lens offers solid zoom capabilities for wildlife, sports, and portrait photography. ✅ Built-in Wi-Fi & NFC – Easily transfer images to your phone or tablet for quick sharing. ✅ Simple to Use – The camera is beginner-friendly, with automatic shooting modes and an easy-to-navigate menu. ✅ Full HD 1080p Video – Decent video recording quality for casual videographers. Cons: ❌ No 4K Video – Video recording is limited to 1080p, which may not be ideal for serious videographers. ❌ Fixed LCD Screen – The display does not tilt or swivel, making it less versatile for vlogging or tricky angles. ❌ No Image Stabilization in the Lenses – Handheld shots, especially at higher zooms, may require a tripod for steady images. ❌ Slower Autofocus – Compared to higher-end DSLRs or mirrorless cameras, the autofocus speed is moderate, especially in live view mode. Who Should Buy This? ✔️ Beginners & Hobbyists – If you’re just starting with DSLR photography, this kit is an excellent choice with everything you need to learn. ✔️ Casual Photographers – Great for family, travel, and portrait photography. ✔️ Budget-Conscious Buyers – You get a lot of value with two lenses included. Final Verdict: For the price, the Canon EOS Rebel T7 offers solid performance, good image quality, and an easy-to-use interface. While it lacks some advanced features found in more expensive cameras, it remains one of the best budget DSLR kits on the market. If you’re looking for an affordable way to step into DSLR photography, this kit is a great choice!

What with Tariffs and general inflation, good cameras are VERY expensive now. I must admit I am partial to Nikon, and I wanted a camera with a decent range telephoto lens. This camera tiks all the boxes important to me, I extremely happy with it. The lens is fairly compact for an 18-140mm configuration, is just an outstanding lens.

Occasionally I have to go back to a reference to find what I am looking for, but really, this camera is an amazingly intuitive piece of technology even for a beginner. Your camera takes good pictures goes the joke. It is no joke with the D7500. I have used the Coolpx P900 for ~two years. I have never used a DSLR. The D7500 is my first. The pix with this review were taken on the first two days I owned it. These pix were shot on shutter preferred and manual. I had no idea a DSLR camera could be so amazing and forgiving. If I can do this, imagine what you can do if you have knowledge and experience. I carefully researched DSLRs before making this purchase. You will find that if you do this camera is highly rated. Let those reviews will guide your decision. I got this camera because I wanted a camera I could grow into, a camera that would work for wildlife and action, and a camera that was considered an excellent buy in professional reviews. I also chose Nikon because I was familiar with the layout and language because of my P900. For me it was a spectacular choice. I highly recommend it.

If I could give this 0 stars, I absolutely would. I purchased this camera listed as new, not refurbished. When it arrived, I was initially very pleased. I’ve used Canon cameras most of my adult life, and this one seemed no different—great picture quality, easy to use, and the included accessories made it feel like a solid value. However, that positive impression didn’t last. After just three uses, the camera completely failed on the fourth shoot. I took one picture and the camera stopped functioning entirely. At first, I assumed it was a dead battery. After recharging, I tried again—nothing worked. The flash would fire, but the menu wouldn’t even come up. At that point, it was clear this was not user error—it was a defective unit. Then things became even more concerning. When I attempted to register the camera with Canon, the system indicated that the camera and one of the lenses had already been registered. That should never happen with a product sold as “new.” It strongly suggests this item may have been previously used or resold. About a week later, when we tried again, that warning mysteriously disappeared—which only adds to the suspicion. At this point, we contacted Amazon, since we were still within the return window. I simply wanted a replacement or refund for a clearly defective product. Because we no longer had the original packaging, we were told we had to deal directly with the third-party seller, Beach Camera. This is where the experience completely broke down. Despite receiving a defective camera that failed almost immediately, Beach Camera: Refused a straightforward exchange or refund Opened a vague “investigation” instead of resolving the issue Attempted to offer only $88 compensation for an $800+ broken camera Required me to pay return shipping Charged a 20% restocking fee—even though the product was defective Charging a restocking fee on a defective item is unacceptable. Passing the cost of their failure onto the customer is worse. Thankfully, Amazon ultimately stepped in to make things right, although I now have to cover costs upfront and wait for reimbursement. Without that support, this would have been a complete loss. Bottom line: Most vendors—and Amazon—stand behind what they sell. Beach Camera does not. They failed at every stage: selling a questionable “new” product, refusing to take responsibility for a defect, and attempting to penalize the customer for their own failure. I strongly recommend avoiding this vendor.

review_title: Amazing quality and perfect for beginners!
body_en: I bought the Canon EOS R100 mirrorless camera after reading online that it's one of the best budget-friendly options to get started with photography, and it absolutely lives up to the hype! Its suitability for beginners is fantastic, and the overall ease of use makes learning a breeze. The image quality is honestly amazing right out of the box—the attached photos (including the close-ups of nature and my dog) are some of the first ones I took! The autofocus is quick and accurate, and the speed of the camera is great for capturing moments on the fly. It comes with all the basic accessories you need to get going; I just popped in my 128 GB memory card and was ready to shoot. Highly recommend!

body_en: Great starter mirrorless camera. Excellent picture quality you would expect from canon. I use mine for astrophotography. Very easy to use. Wifi works great.

review_title: Beginner-Friendly and Addicting Camera to get into Photography
body_en: TL;DR: If you're looking into photography as a hobbyist/beginner this is an amazingly compact powerhouse. It doesn't break the bank AND allows you to save your money for lenses. This camera is addicting. It's my gateway to beginner photography and I want to take pictures of everything. I took it to my local Renaissance Faire, take daily pictures of my sister's cats, candid photos of my friends and family, flowers and shops during my wife and I's daily walks, etc. It's so light and compact that the thought of getting larger and longer lenses on this would make it look really silly. Its Continuous shooting mode is fast enough to capture some horse back riding during the Ren Faire and I captured my wife's arrow mid-flight (although blurry) at 1/4000 when we participated in archery. The GUI is so beginner friendly and explains what each mode does (Manual/Aperture Priority/etc.). It actually helped me understand what each is used for so my wife took plenty of pictures with the right settings quickly. If you dig deeper into the menus there's more granular options like Manual Focusing, Viewfinder/Display brightness, Display options, etc. There's a ton and it's a hassle to navigate through them all... Until you find out you can create your own custom quick access menus. These quickly allows me to navigate to my favorite menu options that I frequently tinker with without moving through all of the other options one by one. The body is so small that I was afraid it would easily slip out of my hands. That was not the case as the grips on the right-hand side is grippy enough that it feels like it you can hold it with a light squeeze while adjusting focus with your left hand on the lens. This kit also provides a strap that allows the camera to be hung around your body for quick access. The performance on the batteries lasts for at least a day with heavy usage so I recommend another battery just in case. Unfortunately, it does not come with a charger and the manual's "Charging the Battery" section talks about charging the battery with a charger. So buy a charger that's compatible with LP-E17 batteries. The autofocus' performance is so impressive that it's enticing my wife to get one for herself. Disclaimer: These photos are taken with the Canon RF50mm F1.8 STM Lens, Fixed Focal Length Prime Lens and NOT the lens included with this kit (Canon RF-S18-45mm F4.5-6.3 IS STM Lens).

I didn’t expect to love this camera as much as I do, but it’s honestly been such a good investment for me. The picture quality is amazing—everything comes out so clear and vibrant, even when the lighting isn’t perfect. I’ve taken some of my favorite photos with it already, and it just makes everything look so much better without me having to try too hard. What I really like is how easy it is to use. I’m not super technical, but I was able to figure it out quickly and actually enjoy the process. The autofocus is super fast, so I don’t miss moments, which is really important to me. It also feels really nice in my hands—like it’s sturdy and made to last. I’ve been using it a lot and the battery holds up well, so I’m not constantly stressing about it dying on me. Overall, I genuinely love this camera. It’s made taking pictures way more fun for me, and I find myself reaching for it all the time now. Definitely one of those purchases I don’t regret at all.

I like this camera a lot. I bought it for optical zoom, and I'm very pleased with the shots I'm able to get, which is mostly wildlife and waterfowl. I take all of these types of shots using the SCN>Pet Mode. I learned that little trick many years ago on a Panasonic camera I had. So for my uses, this is a pretty good camera, particularly for the reasonable price. Pay attention to instructions to achieve focus by first pushing the button down halfway. You'll hear a tone and see a green bordered rectangle when the camera feels it has focus. It doesn't always, but you'll get the hang of it to achieve a pretty decent level of what you expect. I used to have an old Easyshare years ago, and operationally, the PixPro is very similar, though far superior. So this was an easy camera to learn for me. Once you've familiarized yourself with its operation, I think most people will find it fairly simple to use. It is also comfortable in your hand. With the kind of shots I'm taking, I'm usually using a tripod. Keep that in mind. I've included 4 photos, which you probably won't be able to see that well, but all were taken on near max zoom except the deer, which I was very close to. The encasement of the camera is a little strange and super easy to mar or scuff. When I tried to clean it with a cloth, I then had scuffs and lint. I found the best thing to clean the encasement with is the red antibacterial Wet Ones wipes. I would not say the battery life is long. But the batteries are cheap. And I bought two of them in a package deal with a double charger. It connects by USB C to my OnePlus car charger, so I'm getting supervooc charging. Very fast! No need to charge slow by connecting to the micro USB! Easy battery in and out of the camera. I rotate 5 batteries including the one that came with the camera. I have no complaints about the regular photos I've taken of landscapes, sunsets, people, etc., but I usually use my phone for things like that. Also, it's super easy connecting my devices, both tablet and phone, to the camera's WiFi. Additionally, the PixPro app works extremely well with both devices, which are OnePlus, but I haven't updated that app on either device. I'm a little afraid it won't work right if I do. If there's ever a need, I'll update it 😉

This is an amazing camera. In a world of technical terms, it does take some time to learn how to use it. Things to do (or) know. This camera does use an (LB-060) reactangular shaped (lithium rechargable battery) which is included but I recommend buying a second battery. It does not come with a memory card. You will need to purchase a minimum of (32gb) memory card. Do yourself a favor, download the user's manual .pdf file from the internet. Just type in the full name of the camera followed by "users manual" and you will have what you need to set up your camera correctly. It has a lot of features that work great, probably more than you need if you are not a professional. After having to purchase multiple cameras, this one is by far the best value for the price. It does take some patients and tweeking but when you are done I found this camera much better than my GoPro 12, in my opinion. Although I wouldn't classify it as an action camera, it does take great stills as well as videos. This is a great value all in one camera! 1080p is so close to 4k it's very hard to tell the difference. That's what this camera is a 1080p but the small difference is worth avoiding all of the 4k headaches.

I was looking for a camera that wasn't necessarily state of the art and expensive, but still had some potential to get pictures of the Milky Way on a vacation. This served that purpose. Easy to understand and work. Lightweight. I'm no experienced photographer, but I'd say this would probably be a great entry level camera to use if you wanted to get into it.

We wanted a camera with a long optical zoom that was affordable, and this one is. It's been fun trying to learn to use it and we've gotten some great shots of wildlife--mostly ducks and birds. It's relatively easy to use for a "beginner," and has some nice features--like charging the battery without removing it from the camera. However, I'm not impressed either with panoramic shots or the color. In fact, we are quite disappointed with colors that seem muted. I know we can brighten shots with a phot editor, but it would be nice to get that true color from the camera itself. I know the reviews aren't great for this product so we were warned. I'm not really sorry I bought the camera, just a little disappointed in the color quality. But if you mostly want it for the zoom capability, this is definitely a choice in the lower budget range.

This is a beautiful camera! So far it has worked for what I wanted it to. I like taking pictures of the birds at the birdfeeders. It’s very easy to use. When you have it zoomed in, you have to have steady hands or it is very blurry. It got a great photograph of this Carolina chickadee.

Ordered this for my wife to take pictures of birds in our yard using a lens hood and UV filter (both must be purchased separately). It has not been used indoors. The major problem with this camera is the lack of a viewfinder. Pictures must be set up using the small LCD screen on the back of the camera. Unfortunately, when you use the camera outside, the screen shows your own reflection looking back at you and you can't see what you are aiming at. I contacted Kodak customer service to see if anything could be done about this: perhaps a non-reflective coating that could be applied to the screen. This was their reply: "...when hit with sunlight the screen will look black and the only thing you can do is hover your hand over the top of the camera to keep the sun from hitting the LCD screen before pressing the shutter button." Unless you have 3 hands or are using a tripod this is an unworkable solution. The shutter and zoom controls are on the right side of the camera so you hold the camera on the right. You need to steady the camera with your left hand when the zoom is extended because the camera becomes front heavy. Using this camera is like standing in a crowd and holding your cell phone over your head to try to take a picture of something you can't really see. Sometimes you get a good picture, most times you don't. It's not point and shoot - it's guess and hope.
