Cleaning is also a breeze, thanks to the removable filter basket and drip tray, which can be easily washed and reassembled for hassle-free maintenance. Energy Efficient and Safe The Elite Gourmet EHC4128 is designed with energy efficiency in mind, featuring an automatic shut-off function that turns off the coffee maker after brewing is complete. This not only saves energy but also provides peace of mind, knowing that your coffee maker is safe and secure when not in use. Ideal for Small Households With its 4-cup capacity, this coffee maker is perfect for small households or individuals who want just the right amount of coffee without waste. It’s ideal for those who appreciate a fresh brew each time without the need to store excess coffee. Verdict The Elite Gourmet EHC4128 Automatic 4-Cup Brew & Drip Coffee Maker is a perfect blend of convenience, quality, and style. With its compact design, efficient brewing capabilities, and user-friendly features, this coffee maker is an excellent choice for anyone looking to enjoy a perfect cup of coffee at home. Whether you're rushing out the door or enjoying a leisurely morning, the Elite Gourmet EHC4128 ensures that your coffee is brewed to perfection, every time. Start your day off right with this reliable and stylish coffee maker!

review_title: Not the best quality if you want something that lasts
body_en: It’s OK, I’ve only had it for a few months and it seems to be struggling despite me descaling it.

I really like the profile of this coffee maker. It is slim and elegant and does not take up space on the counter. It works very well. She makes good coffee. Well, at the 4 cup level, you have to understand that these are small cups which are approximately equivalent to 2 mugs. The permanent and very effective filter. It does not stop automatically. I plugged it into a smart plug with Alexa and once she made her coffee, the smart plug is programmed to shut off after 30 minutes. It's an economical way to make no-waste coffee until it's needed. Yes I recommend it for one or two people.
I returned it as faulty and I’m waiting for my refund

I absolutely love this little guy omg so cute and tiny takes up very little space great for small apartment kitchens. Does the work of the bigger ones and I’m very happy with this purchase. I’ve been drinking a lot more coffee than I wanted to just to use this little guy everyday.

review_title: Good coffee and works hard to please!
body_en: I’m impressed with this little coffee maker! I love my coffee and this maker works hard to please me and has succeeded on all fronts! Great size for one or two people. No complaints or problems, I recommend this little sweetie!
Does the job, I recommend

I bought this exact coffee maker about 3 months ago and I haven’t had any issues or problems with it so I decided to get a second one for my vacation home. The coffee maker is compact and looks nice on my counter. The instruction manual has straightforward step by step instructions for first time use and for normal coffee brewing. However, there are a couple of things in the instruction manual that I disagree with. First, it says “the appliance can be used by children 8 years old and above if they’ve been given supervision or instruction.” I can’t imagine letting my 8 year old grandson use my coffee maker or why I would want him to. Also, it says you should unplug and thoroughly clean all parts of the coffee maker daily. That’s probably a good thing to do but I have only been cleaning mine periodically. And for clarification, #3 under Normal Brewing says to use one level spoon of coffee for each cup. This should say one level Tablespoon for each cup of coffee. Other than those things I found the instruction manual to be helpful and clear. The coffee maker has all the common features found in coffee makers. It can be programmed to go on automatically at a specified time which is convenient for people who work or are in a hurry in the morning. We tried this function and it was easy to do, however, since we are retired we like to prepare the coffee the night before but then press the on/off button when we get up in the morning. The coffee maker has a pause and serve function so you can grab a cup of coffee before the brewing stops. It also has an automatic shut off that turns the coffee maker off two hours after it was turned on. I find this feature to be very important because I often forget to turn it off. There are two other features on this coffee pot that I really like. First, it has a button to make the coffee a little stronger. You just press the “strength” button and a little coffee bean symbol shows up under the time. This slows down the drip and gives the coffee a bolder flavor without making it bitter or too strong. The second thing that I really like is that this machine makes HOT coffee which is the way I like it.

Been hearing the Jeffersons theme song in my head with this thing, because I feel like I'm Movin' On Up, To The East Side. I've been drinking instant, or pour over, or percolator, campfire, etc. And one cup at a time. This one is a tad pricey, but it pays for itself over time, compared to how I normally drink it, for sure. And it negates the need for filters, so you save on those. Definitely comes out cheaper in the long run, compared to instant. Tickled pink to be able to make 10 cups at a time and keep it hot, instead of one cup at a time, and having to reheat it. With this, I can just top it up and make it hot again. So luxurious and timesaving. Love the rich setting for making it stronger. Puts hair on your chest, like I need any more of that. LoL. Love that it stops dripping while you pour a cup! That feature is to die for, because sometimes you really need that first cup, and it's not done brewing, so you make a mess. Not now. Also great to have a digital clock to look at if I don't have my watch or phone, or it's quicker to look at the coffee maker. Built well, works well. Again, price is slightly stiff, but it also holds up its end of the bargain in performance and features. Have to call it a Win.

This coffeemaker is great. I have (and LOVE) a french press, Nespresso and Keurig machines but sometimes you just want to brew a pot of coffee for company without a bunch of steps. I appreciate that the functions are so simple. The “strong” feature is probably my favorite, as I appreciate strong black coffee. This delivers a solid cup without any bitterness or burnt taste. The mesh reusable filter is great, you may or may not feel the need to line it depending on the type of grounds you’re using. But it’s nice to have that built in without a need to constantly go buy filters. The programmable functions are simple too. I always try to test things first without reading the manual since let’s be real, that’s how I roll when I open an amazon package…and while I went back to review everything, it was very intuitive to use without doing any reading at all. This is a solid, basic machine that feels well built and has just the functions I need without a bunch of complicated options I don’t want. Definitely worth the money in my opinion!

review_title: 10 Cup Programmable Coffee Maker: Looks Great And It Works Great Too
body_en: Sometimes I want a whole pot of coffee and not just 1 cup so this works great for me. It is very asthetic looking and goes very will with my Stainless Steel and Black Kitchen appliances. I really like that this coffee maker is programmable and I can set the time that I want it to brew my coffee so that when I get up in the morning my coffee is waiting on me instead of me waiting on my coffee to brew. This has a "strength" feature to it and I couldn't really tell much difference in taste but I already use a very dark - strong french roast to begin with. The touch controls on this are very sensitive and just the slightest touch of the buttons will change the time or the programming so be careful with that. I set it for 10 cups and I get 10 cups, not 8 or 9 cups but actually 10 cups so that is great. The price really makes this a good value too. I really like how well this coffee maker works.

review_title: Sleek, easy to operate coffee maker
body_en: I have two small K Pod coffee makers from this brand that have proved to be easy to use and very long lasting. I was excited to order this coffee maker for when I have several people to make coffee for. This has a sleek, modern look and doesn't take up a huge amount of space on my counter. It is very easy to fill, clean and use and comes with step by step directions to help you walk through the features as you use it for the first time. The directions say one level spoonful of coffee for each cup, I would say it should read Tablespoon. And strangely (at least for me), the directions say that this can be used by a child aged 8 and up. (I am not sure why you would have an eight year old using a coffee machine!) Otherwise this is a nice, basic coffee maker that works well, includes all the convenient features you want from a coffee maker and has the quality and functionality of this brand, which I have come to trust.

review_title: No customer service when things go wrongly
body_en: Stay away!!! I ordered this machine because I have limited space. It made OK coffee but it broke within two months. Since the coffee pot is made and sold via a Chinese company, there is no customer service and I guess no warranty either. I went to their website but the contact information tab doesn’t display contact info. I went to the Amazon online store and again no contact information. Shame on Amazon for associating with such a vendor.

This 10-cup programmable coffee maker is a solid option for everyday home or office use. I like the adjustable brew strength, which makes it easy to customize the coffee depending on my preference. The programmable timer is convenient for having coffee ready when needed, and the pause-and-serve feature is useful when you don’t want to wait for the entire pot to finish. The permanent filter is another nice touch since there’s no need to constantly buy paper filters. The stainless-steel design looks clean and fits nicely on the counter without taking up too much space. The glass carafe is easy to monitor, although it does require some care to avoid accidental damage. My main complaint is that some of the controls and settings take a little getting used to, and the carafe could be easier to pour without occasional dripping. Overall, it’s a capable and convenient coffee maker with useful features at a reasonable value.

This is a no name brand 10 cup coffee maker, and it’s great. The price is so reasonable for all the useful features. It is very modern looking with black and stainless steel accents. The coffee pot is large enough for 10 cups of coffee, and has a pause and serve feature, which is great for people like me who have no patience when a pot of coffee is brewing and I need a cup asap. You can also program the coffee maker to set it up and have it turned on automatically, that is great for the mornings or if you are having a party and don’t want to think about setting up the coffee pot. One feature which was so unexpected was the adjustable brew strength, I never thought of that before, but I have to admit, I really appreciate having it. What a difference it makes with my brew. I am really impressed with this. It is perfect to keep as an extra, use in a vacation home or for everyday use. This coffee maker works really well, is a good compact size while brewing a full 10 cups, and is a reasonable price.

Arrived so quickly. It arrived 2-3 hours after i ordered it which was great because my current coffee maker suddenly quit working that same morning. It was a Mr. Coffee 12-cup that lasted for 13 years so I figured that i got my money's worth. So I thought I would go with Mr. Coffee brand again. Anyway, this time I decided to try the 5-cup because I no longer need a 12-cup as I now live alone. I've only had it for 3 days but so far I love it. It works great. I don't like warm coffee and this little coffee makes makes hot coffee, but not too hot to burn you. It stays hot until you turn it off. It is not programmable but that is not a feature that I'm crazy about anyway. The handle on the carafe isn't too small, just the right size. The carafe has a wide opening which makes it easy to clean and the glass carafe is just the same glass as a 12-cup, only smaller. The basket uses the 7" filters which I was already using in my old unit so I didn't have to buy new ones. I don't like the cone filters and I'm glad this one doesn't require them. I especially like that it doesn't take up as much counter space because I have a small kitchen and don't have much counter space to spare. It doesn't brew as fast as a large coffee maker but that is no problem for me. I turn it on when I get up, then go get dressed. By the time i get back to the kitchen, it is finished. It does have the pause feature if you are in a hurry. So far, I'm very pleased with this little coffee maker and don't share any of the negative reviews. I did run plain water through the unit before making my first pot of coffee to clean it through and through. There was no bad plastic smell, no smell of any kind, and no bad taste of any kind from my first brew of coffee as others have mentioned. I don't grind my own coffee beans but I use Folgers pre-ground coffee, so i don't know anything about grinding your own beans and how this would be any different. i know some people are really picky about that kind of stuff, but I am not. I am more concerned about convenience. If you like stronger coffee, just add more grounds or less water, or both as there is no adjustment on this unit to make the coffee stronger or weaker. As I have only had it for 3 days, I don't know anything about the lifespan of this unit, but so far, I am very pleased and loving the little coffee maker. I will update the review if it doesn't last long. It is perfect for small kitchens, dorm rooms, etc., and is very light wright. It looks just like a 12-cup coffee maker, only smaller, without lots of bells and whistles- just a basic coffee maker. ( I've had 2 Keurigs in the past and neither one lasted more than a year- too expensive to keep replacing every year. I won't buy anymore of those) This little unit is perfect for me. Glad I found it and hope it last a long time.

review_title: convenient sized coffee maker for one person
body_en: Bought a 5 cup mini brew coffee maker to use for travel a few years ago. I remember it produced a pretty good tasting coffee. I broke the carafe and wasn’t sure whether to replace it or not but I’m glad I did. Again this one works pretty well even though there’s no bells and whistles for this coffee maker. Makes as good a cup of coffee as my more expensive coffee maker.

review_title: So glad I hit the buy button!
body_en: For a long time I've searched for Mr. Coffee's 4 cup coffee maker but all I've found here and on eBay is one that's not used. That one is at a ridiculous price when you add in a highway-robbery price for delivery. What would show up in my searches on Amazon was this 5 cup version. I had resisted buying it for about a year, but finally ordered it a few nights ago -- then promptly cancelled the order because some reviews made me think I wouldn't like it. Fast-forward to last night shortly before midnight. I decided to give this maker a chance to prove it was worth buying, so I hit the buy button. It was here, waiting for me when I woke up today. I love it. The design differences between this model and the 4 cup one were things I thought I would hate, but I don't. Really, I have only one quibble. The filters don't fit nicely in the filter holder, but that doesn't affect how they perform. Over time I may be disappointed if the pot's lid gets coffee stains on it. Cleaning this 5 cup model is easier than the 4 cup one is. That's because my hand fits more easily in the pot for drying it, thanks to the bigger size. I also like the finish on this model. It's mostly a matte white which will go with the matte white toaster oven I'll be receiving tomorrow. I also like the on/off switch that is on both models. I use an Echo smart plug that I can turn on via my voice as soon as I wake up: "Alexa, turn on coffee." The switch is always in the on position but the plug is off until I tell Alexa to turn on the coffee. When the maker is on, I appreciate the fact there is not automatic shut off after a certain length of time, like there is with other coffee makers. When having two mugs of coffee, I often don't get around to drinking the second mug till an hour or more later. I want it to be hot when I'm ready for it. Reheating coffee in the microwave is not the same as having the pot on the heat. There's a scientific reason for this. Now about the coffee: it tastes great with both models. I think it takes the 5 cup model longer to make the coffee but it's really not an issue. I will never brew 5 cups. Most often, I will use the 2-cup setting with 3 scoops of coffee. I like it strong. Someone needs to let Mr. Coffee know they are lousy at measuring cup sizes. My mug (which looks bigger in the photo than it actually is) holds 11 ounces. The 2 cup setting delivers a little less than 11 ounces. I think Mr. Coffee uses the usual cup size other coffee makers do: just 6 ounces per cup (not the expected 8 ounces for those of us who use a regular measuring cup for our cooking needs). But the 2 cup setting gives me less than 12 ounces. It's closer to 10.5 ounces. I doubt I'll ever use more than the 4 cup setting which will give me two mugs of coffee. The pot is easier to pour from versus the 4 cup version. Getting the last little bit out of the 4 cup version is difficult, but super easy with the 5 cup version. It's obvious I love this 5 cup model. I hope Mr. Coffee won't stop making it in the future like they did with the 4 cup version. When I need a new coffee maker, I want this model to be here, ready and waiting for me to hit the buy button again. UPDATE: After using the coffee maker for a while I noticed the lid on the pot has a faint stain that I can't wash off. I expect it to get worse over time so I ordered the black version so I could use the black pot in my white coffee maker (see photo). I know it'll get stained too, but I won't be able to see it. Totally worth it. I'm adding two photos to show how it looks if you want to avoid the coffee stains. You can just use the black pot or you can adapt the white pot to accomplish the same thing. Just remove the just the white lid and snap the black lid into the white pot. Photos show what I mean, I hope. This white pot/black lid is what I'm happiest with.
My mother loves the wide mouth cup. Much easier for her to clean thoroughly, the way she likes. It brews coffee quickly and she loves it.

review_title: Great for someone living alone that just wants a small pot of coffee! Works great!
body_en: I bought this for my elderly aunt who’s 87 and still lives alone. She doesn’t like newer technology with too many settings and options. She just wanted a simple small coffee pot that would make body for her each day and this one works great and is very affordable. The only thing is it uses the smaller coffee filters so you’ll need to get some of those. However if you have regular ones they’ll fit you just have to kinda smash them in or cut them. Amazon sells a big pack of the smaller filters for like $3 or less so it’s worth it if you just need a small simple coffee pot

review_title: 5 stars but a disaster-rethinking buying another
body_en: I've been a Mr. Coffee user for 40 years. I love the 4 cup makers. This is the second time since Feb. 2025 that the coffee maker has stopped working. QUALITY of things has gone down with the coffee maker.

Sitting here with my fresh brewed coffee from my new Mr. Coffee maker. Since I'm the only one in the family that likes coffee, this mini brewer is great for two cups. It's a simple machine that does not have all the frills like a 12 cup maker i.e. no timer, smaller carafe, small size, no automatic off heating plate. BUT for two quick cups of good brewed coffee, it's perfect.

review_title: Went with the OG that I grew up with in my mom's home.
body_en: Finally, after FOUR unsuccessful attempts, I found something decent. For the last three months, I have ordered THREE 5-cup coffee makers for my small apt that did not work out. - The first I had to cancel b/c it was never shipped after 2 weeks. - Next one, the timer did not work! - Another one, the plug would not dislodge from the back of the unit's plastic housing - I tried pliers, etc but the damn thing was stuck INSIDE the small compartment and at risk of being completely ripped off if I kept trying. - And then the final one - the glass carafe was as THIN as a light bulb that it broke when trying to gently wash it! This Mr Coffee model is probably not the best for consumers expecting "luxury" quality for such a low price, but it brews, pours, and stays hot with no issue. AND the glass carafe is MUCH thicker and less "delicate" when handling it. The only star left off is that you need to be more careful of how you position the paper filter and the overhead spout that shoots water into it - If done the wrong way, the paper filter may fold at one side, thus leaving grinds on the bottom. STILL at this price, and for my needs, go with the old goat of MR COFFEE - just like mom used.
I already knew the product and it met expectations

The latest update of my 5 star review I wrote 2 months ago is unfortunately down to 0 if I could give a zero star because the coffee maker just stopped working on the day when the so called return window closed! So basically the machine lasted for 2 months. On top of that a customer service agent on Amazon lied to me that I will receive a refund in 24 hours but I got no email stating that the refund was made so I wasted my time and money with the machine and the customer service agent. Simply perfect and the ideal size, I can take it on a trip without a problem.

Our old single cup coffee maker recently brewed its last cup and we decided to splurge for the Ninja Hot & Iced XL instead of doing something more basic. This is an awesome machine! review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker - the BEST actually...
body_en: We've owned several Keurig coffee makers over the years, and we're big fans of single cup brews. Unfortunately, we've also had every single Keurig machine break down on us...which has become very frustrating, AND expensive. Combine that with the fact that our favorite K-cups have gone WAY up in price, it just wasn't sustainable any longer to continue with Keurig. After looking around at alternatives, I found this Ninja coffee maker and I thought the option to brew a full carafe or single cups of coffee to be exactly what I was looking for. For those that use the feature, there is also an automatic brew option, so you can set it before bed, and wake up to a carafe or cup of coffee in the morning without the wait if you should so choose. I can't really speak about the issues I've read on here regarding leaking carafes, etc. because we really only brew one cup at a time. For this purpose, this coffee machine works perfectly. It does take a little longer to brew a single cup than a Keurig, but the coffee and options you have are so much better than a Keurig. Because you can fill your filter basket however you like, you can make your coffee as strong or as weak as you like because you're no longer limited to a pre-measured K-cup. So, the coffee tastes far superior to K-cups, AND overall, it's MUCH cheaper to buy coffee. Also, your coffee options are no longer limited to brands that produce K-cups. You can buy ANY coffee. I know, some people will say you can buy K-cup pods and fill them with your favorite coffee...but I've done that plenty of times, and they ALWAYS taste weak to me. Fast forward to today, we've had this machine for over a year now and thankfully we've had zero problems with it at all (unlike our previous 5 Keurig machines). Personally, based on our experience with this Ninja, I would definitely recommend this coffee maker to anyone who loves coffee, and I would absolutely purchase it again - with zero hesitation. It also is a stunning-looking machine that would look amazing on any countertop. Definitely the best coffee maker I have ever owned.

review_title: 2nd Ninja Coffee Machine and it just gets better!
body_en: Imagine spending $400 on a drip coffee maker and throwing it out in less than a year. Yeap, replaced a Moccamaster with a Ninja Specialty and I could not be happier. Love coffee, mostly drink 4-6 cups of freshly ground coffee a day. I had an older basic Ninja for several years before giving it to my son and wife, thinking it was a win win, so that when I visited I could enjoy a great cup of coffee, while at home I thought I would upgrade to a superior coffee machine (Moccamaster recommended by Wirecutter). The Moccamaster was a rip off. Could not fathom spending that kind of money, just to throw it away. Right? Tolerated it for less than a year then couldn't stand it anymore. In the garbage it went. Lesson learned. Ninja Specialty surpasses my expectation. First it makes excellent coffee. Can choose classic or bold, cup, mug, half or full pot, and the machine adjusts accordingly. The ease of use now is great, don't have to pull the machine out from under the cabinet anymore since the filter holder pulls out the front area. The water reservoir can also be removed from the side and be filled or washed. Has its own scoop that shows how much coffee is recommended depending on the brew cycle. Have not tried the frother yet. Another improvement is that if you want to grab a cup before the brew finishes you just move a lever to the left, which pauses the brew, this is important because all the machines I ever had, when you pull the carafe out, some coffee drops still drip on the hot plate which fizzles and stains the base. What a great great well thought out and tested machine. Highly recommend! Ninja appears to build products that are built around what their customers want while others appear to build products based on profitability and greed, using their brand well initially as a trap then turning their goods into garbage and charging excessively for inferior products. Again, lesson learned.

review_title: 🔄Updated Review — Now 8 Months of Daily Use (see full update below)
body_en: 🔄 Updated Review — Now 8 Months of Daily Use (see full update below) ⭐️Original Review: My husband and I are huge coffee lovers and have tried many types of brewers over the years. This Ninja was purchased in early August, and I intentionally waited until October to write my initial review so I could give a thorough, real-use perspective. I can say with 100% confidence — this is the best coffee maker I’ve ever owned. We are already a Ninja-product family, so I was excited to add this to our kitchen — but this machine completely exceeded expectations. I originally thought I was a simple “coffee + creamer” person, but this opened up a whole new world of drinks I didn’t even realize I’d enjoy. My husband loves experimenting with flavors, foam, and different styles, and he is thrilled with how much versatility this one machine offers. This coffee maker is used at least 4–5 times every single day (no judgment 😅), and every time we use it, we’re able to make something different — hot coffee, iced coffee, lattes, cappuccinos, and more. ☕ What You Get: Coffee maker unit Smart scoop (labeled per serving size) Frother wand attachment Tempered glass carafe with smart funnel Permanent filter + filter basket Flip-top water reservoir De-clogger tool Instruction manual Usage & Features: Cup Size Options: Cup XL Cup Travel Tumbler Multi-Serve Tumbler Half Carafe Full Carafe You can switch between sizes easily with a simple knob turn. Drip Stop Feature: Acts like a quick pause, allowing you to pour a cup mid-brew without making a mess — super useful when brewing larger amounts. Even when making a small cup, it still tastes like a full, properly brewed pot — not watered down like some machines. It takes a few minutes to fully extract flavor, which makes a noticeable difference. ☕ Brew Styles: Classic Rich Over Ice For iced coffee, I fill a cup with ice, add fresh coffee grounds to the filter, and brew using the “Over Ice” setting — it comes out perfectly balanced and not diluted. Frother Wand: One of my favorite features. Add milk or creamer to a cup, place it under the wand, and run it for about 30 seconds — it creates a smooth foam that takes drinks to another level. Cleaning & Storage: Cleaning is simple and low maintenance: Filters remove easily for rinsing All removable parts are dishwasher safe Grounds are easy to discard and clean out When the descale light comes on, running a vinegar + water cycle through the reservoir gets everything back to normal quickly. The adjustable platform is also great — it flips up to fit larger tumblers or the full carafe. ⚠️ Things to Know: This machine does not use pods or K-cups It is designed for ground coffee only Personally, I actually prefer this — it’s much easier to clean a filter than deal with small reusable pods. ⭐️ Original Conclusion: This quickly became my favorite appliance in the house, and I recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, versatile coffee maker. 🔄 8-MONTH UPDATE (HEAVY DAILY USE — 4–5x A DAY) I originally reviewed this after about 2 months of use. I’ve now been using it for closer to 8 months, and it’s still used heavily every single day — plus regular large iced coffee batches. I wanted to come back and share a true long-term update for anyone wondering if it holds up. ☕ Real-Life Performance After 8 Months: •No wear or damage •No cracks or weak points •No rust anywhere •No slowing down or performance issues •Still brews consistently hot coffee every time •It honestly performs the same as it did when it was brand new. Cleaning & Maintenance (Still Easy): Regular hand washing Occasional dishwasher use No buildup or residue issues Maintenance has stayed simple and low effort. Frother Wand (Still Excellent): Still one of my favorite parts of the machine. Works just as well as day one and creates smooth foam quickly. 🔥 What’s Changed Since My Original Review? Honestly — not much. And that’s exactly what you want. The biggest difference now is confidence. After months of heavy use, I can confidently say this machine is built to last. ⭐️ Media Update: I’ve added a new how-to video showing: -Full pot brewing -Iced coffee setup -Reservoir refilling -Removable parts -Control panel and settings ⭐️ Final Verdict: This is still my most used and most loved appliance in my home. If anything, I like it even more now — because I know it holds up under real, heavy daily use. I would absolutely buy this again.

review_title: For under $200, this is a great machine!
body_en: I never write reviews, but if you’re like me, you’re going to research new coffee machines like it’s your second job… hah. So here I am, about a month into owning the 10 cup model with an honest review. I LOVE IT. Between me and my husband, we use it 2-3x a day and have nothing but praise for it. We are not coffee snobs by any means, but we wanted to get away from kcups/nespresso pods (due to the waste) and after using a Keurig for many years, decided to make the switch to this very popular machine. I didn’t have too many requirements other than something programmable and the ability to brew different amounts. I’ll start with the things I love about it: 1. Easy setup + use. After everything was washed and I ran a clean cycle, the machine was ready for use. To brew coffee, you select the size then choose if you want “classic” or “rich”. Once you select, it starts blinking and then will begin to brew shortly after. Brew times are fairly quick, no complaints there. A full carafe (on the classic setting) brews in roughly 8 minutes. The delay brew option is easy to use as well. I usually set up the machine at night for my husband so he has coffee waiting for him at 5:30a when he gets up for work. The machine brews in a few minutes and is fairly quiet — it does beep several times once done, but does not disturb me or our young toddler. I don’t find it loud or disruptive. 2. Features. Honestly, this machine is well equipped for under $200. Several options for brew sizes, the classic vs rich, option to brew a specialty 4oz cup (not espresso since it doesn’t get hot enough, but I’m not picky and it works for a quick at home option), brew over ice, and of course the built in frother. It would be nice if the frother warmed the milk too, but I just pop it into the microwave to heat prior to frothing. Froths nicely! I also really love the included measuring scoop. It attaches to the machine for convenience. I follow the guides for number of scoops and use it every time I need to measure the grounds. 3. The aesthetic look of the machine and feel of quality. It looks nice on my kitchen counter and doesn’t take up a lot of room. Plus it’s nice the frother folds in to make it even more compact. The included glass carafe feels good and doesn’t feel cheap or too thin. Overall I feel the quality of the machine is nice for the price. I read a lot of the complaints, which I’ve had zero issues with. There is no plastic taste/smell anywhere on the machine. I did thoroughly wash each piece and ran a clean cycle prior to use, but I didn’t even notice a smell when I unpacked the machine. Coffee is plenty hot and there is even a “stay warm” feature you can choose after brewing your coffee (it does automatically come on after brewing a half/full carafe), but sometimes I will use the multi serve option and brew it into the included carafe then turn on the stay warm feature if it’s going to take me more than a bit to drink the 2 cups I usually get from it. I have never once had any grounds in my coffee after brewing. You can use the included filter or brew using #4 cone filters. I really love this machine and do not miss my Keurig at all. Of course time will tell if it stands up to daily use, but as of now I’m thrilled with this purchase and hope to have it for several years. Hope this review helps someone! Enjoy ☕️

review_title: This is it! It's finally here!
body_en: This is the coffee machine I've been waiting for! Not yet around in Canada, but ships from the USA via Amazon Canada. I don't need a coffee machine that makes tea, I don't need a spinning whirly gig on the side to froth milk... I need a 'Coffee Machine!' And this is it! Boy does it keep coffee hot and that's on the low 'keep warm' setting which doesn't tarnish the flavor. And what about that flavor, it's amazing whether just brewing a single mug or brewing a complete giraffe (it has a long neck) the flavor is consistent. Love, love, love the cold brew feature. How have I lived without this? Previously I'd brew a pot of coffee and put it in the fridge to cool down, but this baby brews straight over ice, again by the mug, if that's all you need. Again, awesome full flavor without being bitter. It sits under the counter too and because of the horizontal action of the brew basket, you don't have to move the machine everytime you want to brew a coffee. The included measuring spoon attached to the side and 'drip stop' feature make this machine standout from the crowd for sure. Just a good, reliable, well built coffee machine. Nothing overly fancy, it makes good coffee and looks good on my kitchen counter. Purchased in July 2024, haven’t had a single issue as of Feb 25/25.
Love this coffee maker. The price was great and so easy to use. Easy to clean and coffee taste great. Replaced a former maker of the same model. Brew time great.

It works and does exactly what I need it to do. Brew Coffee. What a concept. And you don't need a Training Class on how to use it and how many buttons to push and program it. Easy to use. Doesn't have a bunch of gadgets you have to figure out. Just a regular coffee maker. I'm happy with my purchase. No k cups, no descaling, just makes coffee the old fashion way.

review_title: These work great but don't last long!
body_en: For the past ten years I have been using this 12-cup Mr Coffee model. I never turn it off... use it 24/7. They last from six months to just over a year. I have bought about ten, five through Amazon. It used to be the switch would fail (even though never turned it off), but I replaced switches and would generally get well over a year from them. Then, two of the machines (over the years) developed internal leaks, and I could not find the leaks from the bottom, but they were leaking. Two or three of the machines had heating coil failures. The price has continued to increase over the years, so I bought a 12-cup Black and Decker this time. I have owned it two days and I like it fine. The carafes are interchangeable with the Mr Coffee ones (I have a lot of those), so that's nice. I already ordered my second Black and Decker, because the price is great and I hate being without my daily coffee (hot tea actually). I throw two larger tea bags where the coffee filter and grounds go and make tea most of the time. For the second pitcher I throw one more tea bag on top and so, get two pitchers from three tea bags... the tea bags cost $3.25 for 24 bags, so I get 16 12-cup pitchers of nice strong tea for $3.25.

So in my humble opinion, coffee pots shouldn't be as expensive as some of them are. Pour water over the coffee grounds and into a pot with a heating element under it. With that being said I have seen some coffee pots run in the Easley over $100 range. Now okay I understand if you want to have a clock involved so it can start your coffee for you, that's fine and I'm sure that'll cost a couple extra dollars, and if you want something really nice and prestigious looking because you care what your guests think about what you've spent on random items then yeah drop a hundred bucks on a nice one maybe it's stainless steel or something and has a good company logo on the front of it. Personally, I'm not that difficult. I get up in the morning I push the button on this thing and by the time I get out of the shower I've got a nice hot pot of coffee waiting for me and life is good. The only thing I wish this had and this is only because my previous pot did have this option is that if you don't turn this off it'll just stay on all day and you really don't want to cook that empty pot all day. There is a light on the button so if you're leaving the house and the light is still on yeah you might want to shut this off. And honestly after a couple weeks I got into the habit of making sure I shut it off as I picked up the pot to pour my coffee so it hasn't really been an issue, it was only a problem for a week or two because like I said my previous pot automatically shut off so I got lazy and just let it do its thing. So anyway, if you're just looking for something to make your coffee, and you don't really want to spend $50 or $100, I've had this for quite a while now and it works great. I do have well water which has a lot of extra minerals and crap in it so I do find myself doing a 50% vinegar solution which you pretty much need to do with any coffee pot from time to time but in my case a little more often... And other than that, I expect this thing's going to last me a few more years.

*** updated 1/16/2021*** It’s been a few weeks. I tried one more time but the flavor is still there. Maybe it’ll go away but I had also purchased a pitcher that boils watet for tea and it’s great with a. French press we had that I forgot to use. This product I declare as junk for me and regret the purchase thus rating it a one star. I no longer have incentive to try again so it’s unlikely I’ll come back for another updated review. ******** I’m going to start this review off by talking about filters. There are cone filters and then there are flimsy filters. Until I went back to these flimsy filters, I never fully appreciated the cone filters and this will impact future machine purchases for me. Cone filters pack flat meaning storage is less invasive. The hood their shape and are less likely to spill and the won’t collapse when transferring to compost or garbage. It’s a little thing but I appreciate it. So, the point of all this, is that mr coffee uses the flimsy filters. Surprisingly there are a lot of machines that don’t use the cones, which is disappointing. First impressions: The plastic look and felt cheap. I saw reviews that commented about the cheapness of this machine and shrugged it off. Other machines are made of plastic after all. This plastic looks and feels somehow cheaper. I instantly had a negative association to it. The side windows which advertised visibility from both points was a selling point for me. What was failed to be mentioned is that you can’t read the clear numbers when contrasted against a black background or steam. I wrote the marks in with permanent marker to be able to see when filling. One feature I did like is that the spout moves out of the way and the lid snaps it back into place. Simple and elegant engineering. I would never clean these grounds out when hot though. Recipe for spilt grounds and burns. The prep It requires a washing and a single run to remove the plastic flavor, per instructions. I ran 4 times after I washed and before the first use. The plastic smell seemed gone. The usage The first cup seemed fine. Additional uses the plastic taste and smell crept in strongly. I ran a cleanse through it four more times and it’s still there rendering expensive coffee undrinkable. My wife felt like the first coffee had a weird flavor, so maybe I didn’t notice the first time? The fact we have flushed this so many times and the flavor persists is deeply concerning to me. I’ve owned a few coffee machines and never had this issue persist for so long. I’m going to keep trying and if something changes, I’ll update. I’d like this to be a good machine for me, but it’s not. The water heats quickly! This is a lot faster than my older coffee makers! The lighted switch is more subtle than I’d like. It’s a dot vs the entire switch, but in the end my wife and I turn it off after the last cup and it’s not an issue as we both stay at home now. There is no auto shut off. The drip stop works okay. A few drips will come out if you pull early, but it does stop while you pour a cup. A critical feature for my wife. The carafe pours well at an okay speed without dripping down the side. Some will leak if overly full and you have to pour slooooowly to avoid spillage. This seems better designed. This steams a lot and should not be under a cabinet when running. It WILL damage the cabinets. It’s easy to pull out and push back in. The summary: Would I purchase again? No. Even if the flavor fixes itself, I have concerns about the cheapness of this machine and the plastic used and the health impact. I couldn’t find anywhere that discussed if it was bpa free. I hadn’t been concerned because sunbeam owns me coffee, but after seeing and feeling the cheapness of the plastic, and with the plastic taste still present, I’m concerned. It is cheap, the functionality seems good for just a weeks ownership, but the lack of drinkable coffee is an issue. Even if that’s resolved, there’s concern in the back of my mind about the long term health impact of this machine. Hopefully this is helpful. I’d recommend spending more money as I feel I wasted $28 and will be purchasing a new coffee maker, again.

review_title: BOOM! Five star Fourth Of July ERUPTION! WE HAVE COFFEE!!!
body_en: BOOM! EUREKA I HAVE FOUND It! After years of using several different single-serve coffee makers, I decided to give this Tastyle machine a try, and I have to say I'm pleasantly surprised. The first thing I noticed was that the brewing process is just a little slower than my previous brewer. At first I thought that might be a disadvantage, but it actually turned out to be one of its biggest strengths. The water spends a little more time passing through the coffee grounds instead of being forced through as quickly, and the result is a noticeably richer, smoother cup of coffee. As I like to joke, it gives the water time to "hang around in the blessed, precious grind and become acclimated!" Whatever the reason, it simply tastes better. Another feature I really appreciate is the larger puncture needle for the K-Cups. It has a much larger opening than other machines I've owned, which should make it far less likely to clog with coffee residue or mineral scale over time. That alone could mean a much longer service life. The controls couldn't be simpler. Everything is straightforward and intuitive without unnecessary buttons or confusing programming. If you can make a cup of coffee, you can operate this machine. Cleaning is another area where this brewer shines. The square-shaped water reservoir and brew chamber make it easy to reach every surface with an ordinary kitchen sponge. The removable K-Cup holder is easy to rinse after each use, and I like being able to empty the reservoir, turn it upside down, and let it dry. That should go a long way toward preventing mineral buildup and keeping everything fresh. I also have to compliment the documentation that comes with the machine. The owner's manual is clear, well-written, and actually useful—something that's becoming increasingly rare these days. The included recipe book is beautifully put together and offers some genuinely creative beverage ideas that make you want to experiment beyond your everyday cup of coffee. It's also lightweight and has a very small footprint, making it perfect for apartments, RVs, offices, or anyone with limited counter space. Finally, let's talk about value. At around $39, this coffee maker delivers performance that, in my opinion, rivals machines costing considerably more. Even if it eventually wears out years down the road, replacing a $39 coffee maker is a lot easier to swallow than replacing one that costs three or four times as much. Overall, this has been one of those rare purchases that exceeded my expectations. Sometimes simple engineering really is better engineering, and this little coffee maker proves that you don't have to spend a fortune to enjoy an excellent cup of coffee every morning. In an era when many products seem designed to cut corners, this one feels thoughtfully engineered from the first cup to the last.

I first saw this coffee maker being used by a friend at the office, which is what led me to buy it. I really like how compact and space-saving it is, and the operation is super simple with no learning curve. Instead of buying K-Cups, I use the reusable filter that came with it, which makes it more convenient and cost-effective. It brews quickly, is easy to clean, and fits perfectly into a small workspace setup. Overall, it’s a very practical single-serve machine for everyday use, especially if you want something simple, fast, and low-maintenance.

The Tastyle Mini Hot & Iced Coffee Maker is one of those compact, budget-friendly machines that looks great on paper especially if you want something small, versatile, and easy to use. After spending time with it, I found it to be a solid performer for hot coffee, but a bit misleading when it comes to its “iced coffee” functionality. The biggest strength of this machine is its simplicity and convenience. It’s very compact and lightweight, making it perfect for small kitchens, dorms, offices, or even travel. It doesn’t take up much counter space, and setup is basically plug-and-play. It also offers good flexibility—you can brew using both K-cups and ground coffee, which is a nice bonus at this price point. The brew size options (roughly 6–14 oz) give you some control, and the coffee comes out quickly, usually in just a few minutes. For hot coffee, it performs reliably. The temperature is solid, the flavor extraction is decent, and it’s consistent from cup to cup. If you’re mainly looking for a straightforward single-serve hot coffee maker, it absolutely gets the job done. This is where expectations vs. reality don’t quite line up. Despite being marketed as an iced coffee maker, it doesn’t actually brew true iced coffee. There’s no rapid cooling system, no cold brew function, and no real temperature adjustment that results in a chilled drink. Instead, what it really does is brew hot coffee, just slightly adjusted, and expects you to pour it over ice. It’s essentially the same process you could do with any basic coffee maker. So while technically you can make iced coffee, it’s not doing anything special to justify the “iced” label. This feels a bit misleading, especially if you’re expecting something closer to a Keurig-style iced brew system that compensates for ice melt. The Tastyle Mini is a good little coffee maker—as long as you know what you’re getting. It's great for hot coffee Compact and easy to use Works with pods and grounds If you want an affordable, no-frills hot coffee maker, it’s a solid choice. But if you’re specifically buying it for iced coffee, you might end up disappointed. It doesn’t truly brew iced coffee, it just helps you make it the manual way.

My last coffee maker was the keurig duo. After 3 years it started making noises and brewing the wrong cup suzes. I searched every coffee maker for a replacement and found this ninja. I loved everything about it especially the ground coffee basket. It has an attached frother on one side and slide in basket on the other side which holds the ground coffee basket. The ground coffee scoop attaches to the side. It was packed in the ninja box in another. Everything was wrapped separately. It took a lot more time unpacking it than it did to set it up. I followed all the instructions step by step. It was actually quite easy. I flushed the water thru as instructed. Afterwards I put in a peets kcup hit go. It brewed the coffee which was surprisingly too hot to take more than a tiny sip. I really liked this machine and it came in moss green. I left for an hour. When i came back my counter was flooded with water. I immediately thought it was from my old keurig and i hadn't noticed it. I noticed to water tank only had a little bit of water in it. It still didn't click until i refilled the water reservoir and put it back on. Slowly water started seeping from underneath the machine. The water in the reservoir had bubbles. I immediately took the reservoir off and put it on a dry paper towel to look for a crack. There wasn't one and the water wasn't bubbling off the machine. The water was still coming from under the machine because it was already in there. I thought check with Amazon online. I put in the info and the reply was i can get a refund. I didn't want a refund i wanted to exchange it. Nope have to return to kolhs not whole foods or Amazon fresh right below me. I decided to check the instruction sheet again. Ah troubleshooting. There's a section on leaks. The very last scenario is if leak is coming from under the machine call customer service. I call and was pleasantly surprice how easy it was to get to talk to a person. Kellie was very personable. I explained the leaking from under the machine. The impression i got from her was this isn't a common problem we did a video chat she looked at the machine i showed her where the water was coming from. There are 2 empty holes on the bottom. I showed her i can stick my pen up into them. The other holes like those have a screw in them. There are also non skid dots on the corners. She had me put the reservoir with water back on. It took maybe 30 seconds and i said bubblesare starting to form which she was able to see. Luckily i had the dry paper towel where it was as the water began seeping out for her to see in real-time. I told her i thought it was coming thru the holes i could stick my pen into. I was on the phone with her for 30 minutes. Yes they would send me a new machine but even if i cut off the cord the needed this one back. They won't pick it up. I would have to take it the FedEx. There isn't a FedEx anywhere near me. There are a few UPS but it can't go there. They can't send the new until they get they get the defective one. It would a few weeks to get the new one. I thought shark/ ninja would want to look over the machine to find the defect. Then i thought why did i bother and go thru all of this when i can return it to amazon and reorder it. I wasted at least 30 minutes on the phone with shark ninja and didn't get anywhere while water was still leaking from under machine. I thought i was a doing a good thing in case other people were having the same problem. After reading many of the good reviews i decided to read the bad. I'm not the only one with a leaking machine. I packed everything up and put the machine and all parts back into the box to return to amazon. I was going to reorder one even tho they were out of the green before i got to return this one. In 2 or 3 days the price went way up. Now they have 3 different models of this machine. The one i had with the frother was 99.00. I think it's now 30.00. I can do without the frother i only cared about the ground coffee basket. I've been using my french press because i don't have a machine. I have been loving this coffee maker! I have had a favorite coffee maker for years, and it suddenly died. I agonized over a replacement, because I liked that one so much and used it several times a day. It is still made, but the reviews reflected that it is not made for durability like it was when I bought it. I absolutely love this Ninja! I generally use coffee pods, so this is right up my alley. It is so quiet! It will make a variety of sizes for ups, mugs, travel mugs, and iced coffee. One of the features I look for is the ability to brew a strong cup from a pod. The “rich” function on this machine, does the trick! It doesn’t just run water straight through the pod, so that the flavor is lacking. It puts water through the pod in increments to get as much flavor as possible. I used the “over ice” function for the first time yesterday, and it also works slowly enough to pull as much flavor as it can. It was delicious! The brew time is really short, and yet the coffee tastes wonderful, and the temperature is perfectly hot. The machine and it’s components are very easy to clean. It takes up more space from front to back, but has very slim lines and looks good on the counter. The water tank is easy to remove, clean, and fill. I know a couple of people have mentioned having an issue with “exploding pods.” I had this happen ONE time, but I immediately realized why. When you put the pod in the machine, if you just pull the lid down, it may not fully puncture the bottom of the pod appropriately. This causes the hot water to overfill the pod, and it bursts from the pressure. There is a super simple fix!! All you have to do is place the pod in the machine, and press it down, so you feel it puncture the bottom of the pod. THEN close the lid to puncture the top! That’s it! Nothing difficult or time consuming. Just press the pod down before you close the lid. Problem solved! I haven’t had any issues since! 😊 I really am enjoying the ease of use and versatility of this machine. I think it is well made, and will be used for a long time. It is sturdy, without being bulky or heavy. The materials are sleek and easy to clean. I looked at dozens of coffee makers, and read SO many reviews before I made this purchase. The comments about the potential “exploding pods” had me a little concerned, but as I said, that won’t ever be a problem for me after realizing what can cause the issue. I’m an extremely picky person when it comes to my beloved coffee maker, and this Ninja has won me over!

review_title: Quick, Easy, and Consistently Good Coffee Every Morning
body_en: Here’s a solid, helpful review you can use or tweak: ⸻ I’ve been using my single-serve Ninja coffee maker daily, and overall it’s been a really reliable part of my routine. It heats up quickly and brews a cup fast, which is perfect when I’m rushing in the morning or heading out for a long shift. I like that I can choose different brew sizes without wasting coffee, and it consistently comes out hot and smooth. The flavor is better than I expected from a single-serve machine—no weird aftertaste, and it handles both regular grounds and stronger brews pretty well depending on how I set it. It’s also pretty easy to clean, which is a big win for me since I don’t want extra chores first thing in the morning. The only downsides are that it can be a little noisy while brewing, and the water reservoir isn’t huge, so I end up refilling it more often than I’d like. But honestly, that’s minor compared to the convenience. Overall, it’s a great compact coffee maker that does exactly what it’s supposed to do—quick, consistent coffee without any hassle. Would definitely recommend it for anyone who wants something simple but dependable.

review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker for Strong Coffee
body_en: When my name brand (not K) coffee maker went to the big coffee bean in the sky, I decided that $200 was a bit pricy for something that lasted only 4 years. For the most part, I grind beans and use the filter. We don't drink a lot of coffee and I like being able to customize each cup. So I went on a search for the ideal single serve coffee brewer. After trying 2 other brewers, each with problems, I decided to give Ninja the old college try. Boy, am I glad I did. My husband for the most part, drinks a regular cup of coffee with cream and sugar. I make a hot latte every day. I have a really good moka pot, but I wanted a machine capable of making a really strong cup of coffee, which doesn't seem to exist in the majority of name brands. I gave up on the big K a long time ago. I don't use the frother. Maybe one day I will. What caught my immediate attention is the large (and I mean LARGE) filter coffee holder. It holds at least 1/2 cup of coffee! It's ginormous. I use 3 scoops to 12oz water, set on "rich" for my latte, mixed with 8oz hot milk. At first I thought I did something wrong, or that it was defective. A little water came out, and it stopped. On try #3, I decided to let it sit. Sure enough, after a minute or so, it continued. (Perhaps I should have looked at the instructions first?). Lol. What it was doing was allowing the water to soak into the grounds, to extract the coffee. This is the first time in our almost 40 years of marriage, that my husband said his coffee was too strong (and he lived in Germany for 20 years). The maker automatically detects whether you have inserted the filter or kcup. The display is intuitive and easy to program. It remembers your last setting. The brewer is Ninja quality. I've owned several Ninja appliances over the years, all still going strong. If you want a regular cup of coffee, Ninja will provide. If you want a truly strong cup of coffee, Ninja will give it to you. If anyone thinks it doesn't brew a strong cup, they're either not using enough coffee, they're using the wrong blend, or they haven't tried using the filter. Also, all accessories are stored onboard. There's a nifty drawer on the right side that stores the filter or kcup holder, while your using the other. It's a very well thought out machine. The price is very reasonable.

review_title: Excelente cafetera, llegó rápido y funciona perfectamente
body_en: The package arrived very quickly and the coffee maker arrived in excellent condition, with all its original packaging and completely new instructions. I've tried the coffee maker since it arrived. It turned on without a problem and I tried both brew options: ground coffee and K-Cup pods. They both work very well. Some things I recommend checking if you plan to buy it: First, it is important to do a first brew cycle without coffee before using it for the first time to clean the internal system. Second, if you live in a place with a high altitude above sea level, it is advisable to level or adjust the coffee maker following the instructions in the manual. I definitely recommend reading the instructions before using it. Third, if you use ground coffee, it is very important to use medium grind for best results. It is also important to know that this coffee maker uses Keurig-compatible K-Cup pods. Does not accept Dolce Gusto or Nescafé capsules. These K-Cup type capsules are easily available; For example, I found them at HEB. Overall, the coffee maker works very well. I've already tried several of the coffee styles they offer and they all work well. It is a very versatile coffee maker. I highly recommend it. In my case, the equipment arrived brand new and has worked perfectly so far. I also purchased the insurance from Amazon in case I ever needed it, but so far the product has worked excellent. Very good product and an excellent purchase.

It is a complete beauty, it fascinated me, it is super practical, simply perfect

It is an excellent low-cost option compared to other products that offer less diversity of preparations. It's super easy to use. It takes up very little space and I really think it is a plus that it accepts ground grain. A very nice design

Buy this!! I love waking up to the smell of coffee, and this machine does it right everytime. It is also is so common sense to use that you could program it without reading the instructions. Added bonus: no k-cups needed! A single cup is easily brewed with the environmentally friendly reusable single basket. This is the one!

So, like you all ,I've been a coffeeholic for many years. Like you ,I've struggled to have a decent maker in my kitchen. I recently finished up with my Cuisinart mod#CHW-12. Had it for 5yrs. It got to point of no longer producing a well tasting cup. We did the Vinigar cleaning etc. So, i spent MANY hours searching online for a decent Maker. Problem was the abundance of poor reviews encompassing many manufacturers! It's now 2018 and we have trouble creating a Kit Coffee Brewer thats decent! I did a switch and desired a maker that will produce a single cup as wife n i both have coffee at different times and mostly need the one 16oz cup. In searching for the 12cup Carafe / or single cup Maker ,my choices became limited. Read the reviews and pulled the trigger on this. It's only been 1wk now but i can honestly state that it is the BEST maker I've ever used! I ran a full 12cup Carafe first off, thn dumped. Then did same for the single cup side. ( full 14oz). Then ran 12cups clean water through for both. Then did the Coffee that I'll drink. No issues. Had to play round wth the exact amount of grounds for the single side so to get the outcome i desired. Has clock, easy to pre prog., and, the single side will turn off when done. The Carafe side will stay on (hot plate) for 2hrs after brewing complete. You can simply press On/Off button to turn off anytime. For those who have an over-spilling issue with the grounds within the gold filter basket?, you are using TOO MANY grounds! The single side comes with a gold reusable filter which also encompasses two - Level markers. One is min and the other is Max. If you fill above the Max level, WELL, overflow of grounds will prob. occur. On the Amazon site you'll see the Reusable filter for the Carafe side in " frequently ordered with". I also ordered that as i don't like paper filters. It performs well. Water level for Carafe is helpful. It's towards the right rear, on the side. It's accurate. Brew time for 12 cups was good. I've learned to warm up my Mug when using single side as it is not as hot as Carafe as no hot plate for the Mug. I use single side to run water for tea as well. What would make this model perfect? If it sounded out a tone when brewing is complete. It also has No charcoal filter as with my Cuisinart. No biggie as i always have used filtered water to begin with. Coffee is better when there's no Chlorine in the H2O! Filling either the Carafe or single side is easy and Max level markers are visible enough to get it right. Carafe pours very well and i like that the Carafe lid stays attached as u simply press thumb to open but it's not required to pour. Single side grounds chamber pulls out easily. Single side has a bottom (under mug/cup) that reverses to then become a elevator to bring cup higher if you'd like. I brewed a cup at lowest level without any spill or splatter. It drips slow enough that i don't believe i need to elevate my mug. This model also looks fantastic, Beautiful! Has a "Bold" brew mode for both Carafe n Sing. The brewing is slower, so u gt a richer brew. Light on clock only on when unit is ON. Has seperate green light that indicates you are using "Program" mode. I don't use "Pods" but if i did the manual states that "Senseo" Pods will work. Note that unit will only brew one side at a time. It cannot brew both sides at once. Very pleased so far. If any issues I'll update here. P.s. if Manufacturer reads this, you may want to consider modifying so to have an end of brew audible tone! Jst a thought. Update!; 1/5/18. Jst did 2 Lg mugs for me ( nine- 8oz cups), using Carafe of course. Wife then needed to do her single 14oz using of course the Single serv side. When throwing the slide switch over to Single, it turns off the Carafe side. So, yeah, hot plate under Carafe is still hot, but, it's now off. So, in future, wife does her single, first, then i do Carafe. UPDATE ; 1/22/18- 3wks now and NO ISSUES! When removing coffee filled Carafe, absolutely no spilling onto hot plate. The spring loaded valve above, performing well. Reviewers having the Hot plate discoloration or burning may be turning unit on with a Hot plate thats dirty. I make sure plate is clean /dry before and after ea. use. I make sure bottom of Carafe is clean/ dry as well. Wife using single serve ea. day and says " best cup of Coffee ever"! Update; 4/17/21. NO issues, all still good. UPDATE!!! - 10/10/21- So, finally I'm now considering buying a new one of these as this one is intermittently not pumping enough water up and into Coffee basket. About 12× now in past 6mon's I've had to pour out Carafe into another cup, place Carafe back, then pour my Coffee,(that looks like Tea), into the grinds basket and do a Double Drip, sometimes twice to get color I wish. I got roughly 3.5 years out of this Maker. I guess that's good considering Everything's made in Cheapo China. If/when I buy a new one, I'll post back. Have a good Coffee! UPDATE: 11/14/21. So, I purchased this exact model once again on 10/12/21. After 1 month, I can honestly state that it's a great difference between original and new. New machine brews perfectly as did the original one up until the 3yr mark. No issues to report with this New Maker( Same model as first one). Pictures here are of 2nd maker,(2021).

review_title: Very happy with this coffee maker!
body_en: Delighted with this coffee maker! It arrived on time and in good condition. I had a very expensive coffee maker that quit working and thought I would save some money and try this Hamilton Beach version. SO glad I did! The set up was easy and that first morning I was very happy with my hot delicious, coffee! The single serve option is important to me and it works perfectly. I LOVE having a single cup of coffee without using a k-cup! Highly recommend this machine!

It's about what you'd expect for a mid-range Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Normal price of $80 feels a bit steep, but I think it's worth what I paid for it on prime day. It does what it says on the box/product listing and it works better than the dollar store coffeemakers you'd find in an economy hotel room. Looks to be of quality from afar, is somewhat cheap and plastic feeling when you actually use it. Just sturdy enough that I'm not concerned that I'll break it. Single serve and full carafe functions do not share a water tank, and you fill the single serve reservoir with exactly as much water as you want to brew into coffee. Pretty intuitive and I guess pretty standard for this type of coffeemaker. But if you are used to filling the tank once a week and brewing a set 6oz or 8oz this is not that. "Brew Options" button toggles between bold and regular brew strength.... And that's it. There's no way to set brew temperature, but the default temperature is fine. It brews a single serve in about 3 minutes or so. Faster than a drip coffeemaker of yesteryear but if you're expecting it to be as fast as a pod system you're looking in the wrong place. The thing that matters most though is how the coffee comes out, and I have to say it's worth the extra hassle of using loose ground coffee and filters as it's much better than pod-brewed coffee. The slower brew speed results in a better coffee. Much more cost effective than pods too. The reusable single serve filter is surprisingly easy to rinse out. For $50 it's not bad. I would not pay $80 for this. At a price point of $80 I expect to at least be able to choose a brew temperature, even if there are a few pre-sets instead of by-degree. If you can get this for under $60 and you are specifically looking for a coffeemaker that doesn't use pods, then I can recommend it. Otherwise at full price, I don't think it offers enough to differentiate it from other $60 coffeemakers to justify the extra $20. It does have a clock in it and the ability to set a time to automatically start brewing at a set time, which is a feature I really don't use, but for some maybe this will make the $80 asking price worth it as I am not sure if this feature is commonly available in cheaper options.

I am so happy with this dual coffee machine! Just FYI it doesn’t use pods. The one cup feature has its own small basket which you use your own coffee. Coffee temperature is perfect. Is is very easy to use, and I have not had any leaks. It has helped to make more space in my small kitchen by combining the two features and has saved me some serious money not having to buy pods! I would definitely recommend this product.

After struggling with fancier more expensive coffee makers it was nice to go back to a simple machine that just functions without leaking. My wife loves it and it’s great we don’t have to clean up the countertop after every use. Basic and reliable but that’s all we wanted.

review_title: Outstanding coffee maker with carafe and single cup brew option w/o KCups
body_en: I absolutely love this coffee maker!!! I was looking for a maker that offered both, a carafe and single cup option without using KCups, and this one does. It has a convenient small gold filter that you fill with your own ground coffee. If you want the gold filter for the carafe side, you have to buy it separately. Otherwise, use paper non-cone filters. It also brews both sides at a nice high temperature. It’s easy to use and has all the standard options. I give it a solid, five-star thumbs up!

review_title: Great coffee maker- single cup or full pot
body_en: This the best coffee pot I've ever owned, seriously. I appreciate good coffee and regularly buy beans from a local roastery. I am not a barista nor do I claim to be a coffee expert. I enjoy good coffee and a drip coffee maker is good enough for my daily habit. This maker can be used to brew single cups on one side or a full pot on the other side. Typically, I am the only coffee drinker in my house. Sometimes we have guests. This coffee maker allows me to serve both situations easily. To use the single serve side, I fill the cup that I'm planning to use with the correct amount of tap water and add it to the single serve side of the maker. This is accessed from the top under a small lid that flips up. This side is designed to only hold enough water for a single serve amount of water. I don't use manufactured pods as I prefer fresh grounds but this maker apparently can handle pods too. I grind my beans or use pre-ground coffee and add that to the slide out tray on the single serve side just above the cup location. There is a metallic mesh screen that holds the grounds on the single serve side and I find that I waste less coffee than when I try to make only 1 or 2 cups in a large pot. The single serve side has a nested set of plastic circles that sits under a tall mug when not needed. These little circular risers can be un-nested and stacked to allow a shorter cup to be closer to the dripping coffee (see photos). This allows the maker to accommodate a variety of sizes of cups. The single serve side takes about 2 minutes to brew. I think the coffee tastes great and I can control the strength of the brew based upon how many grounds I add. The full carafe side is much like any basic drip-coffee maker. There’s a small reservoir that holds enough water to brew a full pot of coffee. There’s a flip lid and a basket for coffee grounds. You can use paper filters or buy a separate metallic, re-usable mesh filter that fits inside this basket. I like these baskets as it’s less wasteful than using paper filters daily and I don’t have to remember to constantly purchase filters. I’ve used the same mesh filter for over 7 years now. It doesn’t filter as finely as paper filters do and the last sip of coffee contains a small amount of grit / sediment but this seems normal to me now. If someone doesn’t like this idea than I would warn them not to drink the last sip. It’s pretty easy to avoid. The coffee maker has a very obvious and easy to use manual switch that selects whether you are brewing a full pot or a single serve. Only one side can be used at a time. You simply move the switch to the left or right as the illustrations show to select which side you wish to utilize. I frequently use the timer feature. Prior to work I have one 16 oz metal travel mug filled, warm and waiting for me when I wake up in the morning. The display is bright when you touch a button and dims to normal again after about 30 seconds so it doesn’t light up the kitchen at night like a beacon. There is a single bright green LED light that indicates that the timer is set and ready to go. Personally, I like this feature as it is an obvious acknowledgment that the timer is ready to go at the time that I programmed in. Some might find this too bright but it’s hard to imagine it being a nuisance to most people. Other reviewers have indicated the their carafe broke instantly upon the first use. I’ve used my carafe several times without issues. I also noticed that a new pot is around $10 so if it does break down the road, I can probably replace it easily. Some said that it tastes like plastic, I haven’t experienced this. Some said that it leaks after 3 months – I’ll try to update this review later but so far so good – no leaks. Others say it takes too long to brew. I think it takes about as long to make coffee as every other coffeepot that I have owned and if you set it up the night before, you won’t have to wait for it. It can be ready for you whenever you tell it to be ready. I even read that some people were annoyed that they had to slide the coffee pot out from under a counter in order to add water to the top of the coffee maker. I once added felt pads to the bottom of a coffee maker to make this process easier. Without a dedicated water line and a commercial coffee apparatus, I’m not sure how the manufacturer would avoid this overly burdensome task. You have to add water somehow; that’s how coffee works. I have not had any negative issues at all with this coffee maker and I’ve been using it daily for over 1 month. It’s easy to use, it’s easy to program and I like that I can make a full pot or single cup depending on my needs. I definitely recommend this unit.
Wonderful coffee maker! I have one in use and bought another one just in case, before it goes out of production.
It is a good coffee maker, it performs its functions and is easy to clean.
I am so amazed the versality of this Hamilton Beach coffee maker of Single and full pot brew. The product output is awesome! Good brewed coffee every single morning is a heavens gift!
