review_title: Great brew station but fatal flaws
body_en: The Hamilton Beach Brew Station is my all-time favorite coffee machine. We have purchased four of them to date after trying a cuisine art unit that routinely leaked all over the counter. None of the four Hamilton Beach units ever leaked. The controls are easy to use, and the unit makes exactly the coffee we enjoy. We do occasionally clean the metal filter at the bottom of the Coffee Tank by pouring some “clean that pot” liquid and following the instructions – does a nice job. We also use filtered water along with both a metal filter and a paper filter in the Filter Basket for very consistent taste. Excellent job Hamilton Beach. Hamilton Beach Engineers get your act together: Unfortunately, there is a flaw in the design that causes unimaginable frustration and very limited product life of maybe a year. The flaw ruined the first three Brew Stations that we bought. We discovered that the Coffee Dispenser Bar would no longer release coffee from the Coffee Tank (see A in Frame 1 of the figure). Pushing that Bar should force the plastic Lever B (in Frame 2) toward the front of the unit. One can see, by tipping the Coffee Tank backward, the plastic Coffee Release Valve C (in Frame 3); the valve has a very stiff spring to prevent coffee from accidently dripping out. At first, it seems the lever B fails by no longer making contact with the valve but placing a pad between B and C does not help and eventually Lever B breaks away. We found that Lever B is quite flexible in a failed unit compared with a new unit. This means Lever B in a failed unit does not have the rigidity to open the Valve C to release the coffee. Moral of the Story: Hamilton Beach, please consider making the Lever B and associated components out of metal. A couple of events might be occurring (or both). First repeated pressure on the Lever B might fatigue the plastic. Second, the Lever B is next to the high temperature heating element and high temperature is well known to deteriorate the strength of plastic. After all these years, this defect cannot be a surprise to the company. Perhaps replacement parts are available. We only finally figured out the problem when we were in a position to compare failed and new units. Finally, we plan on returning the new unit that arrived today because the Lid hinge was apparently damaged during shipping – the plastic protrusion forming a hinge was broken off – the Lid flaps around. But again, we absolutely love the Hamilton Beach Brew Station but definitely not the nasty flaws. Update: Engineering and quality control departments need massive downsizing: The new Brew Station leaked all over the counter. First one with this flaw out of the 5 we tried. Surprising the Hamilton Beach lawyers don't start to worry.

review_title: Stylish, easy to use, perfect cup of coffee
body_en: Best coffee maker I've owned, if course not expert though. I've owned a few regular drip machines with the carafe and one keurig, the basic model that you can get at Walmart for $59. I loved that the keurig made my. Coffee right then and there when I wanted, AFTER it healed up and I refilled the water if it needed it. And I couldn't really. Choose the strength of the coffee without sacrificing. Size of my cup. I'm sire other models are different but I don't want to spend over $50 on a coffee maker so that was pushing it plus the pods are Expensive compared to bying it ground by the pound I absolutely love this machine though. Yes, there's a few minor annoyance, like any machine. Really it's just that I have the thing under my counter so to lift the lid all the way to clean or fill it up I have to pull it out from under. That doesn't really bother me at all though. That's really it for coma on it in my opinion though. It looks stylish. I love that the water tank comes out to fill, I love that the coffee reservoir has a basket. Handle to make it easier. To clean, I love how simple it is to work and program. I love that my coffee is waiting for me in the morning, no matter what. It comes out cooler than the keurig did but it's the perfect tempature in my opinion. I little hot at first but that's good. I read some reviews complaining about filling thick or large mugs? I haven't had am issues and I have some ridiculous mugs, some of which are LARGE..... And thick.. Haha So I don't think you have to worry. The drip trays a little small, but it does its job. It's also really awesome that there's an iced. Coffee feature. I worked at a Dublin donuts in high school so I know it's not made the Dr way and K love that this machine is able to make iced coffee. It really is so so. Please bjt stylish, and it does its job perfectly. Overall its the best machine I've ever owned or have seem put of friends and familys. I highly recommend!

Returned the first because it made a funny noise and the clock didn't work right with no problem and have had the replacement for over a year and I love it! Makes a nice pot of coffee while keeping it hot and fresh for four hours

I love this coffee maker! This is my 5th or 6th of the same coffee maker. I've tried others in between - some are nice, however, with arthritis, this is so much easier on my hands! I don't have to lift the entire pot. With this one, all I have to lift is my cup! I get it ready the night before and when I wake up the next day, I have fresh, hot coffee waiting for me! If I use it during the day, it's fast, I can sneak a cup before it finishes brewing. I set the timer for how many hours I want it to stay hot and it turns off automatically. I can't say enough good things about this coffee maker.

review_title: HB knocked this one out of the park!
body_en: UPDATE: May 17, 2016 After ~8 months of daily use, we've discovered that somewhere along the design chain something was either overlooked or ignored. As I said in my first review, there's a lot to love about the redesign of this unit. But something's not right. About 6 months in, the reservoir that holds the brewed coffee began to leak. I contacted HB and was told I had to pay $5.99 shipping and they would send a replacement. Fine. The new reservoir works fine. No leaks since. At least no brewed coffee leaks. (BTW, turns out, bleach is the culprit for that. Simply put, DON'T use bleach at all, to remove coffee residue inside the filter rack or the hot beverage reservoir. Not even just a tiny amount. But for the next issue, almost from the start, we started noticing a large amount of condensation on the lid that covers the coffee filter assembly. Since there's nowhere for the water to really go, it just pools into the two channels on either side of the hotplate underneath the coffee reservoir (Photos A & C). There are only two ways to remove that water. 1) Take the BrewStation apart, flip it over & dump out the water, or 2) much more simply, use a turkey baster to suction out the water. Repeat at least every other day because there's up to 1/2 cup of condensation created every day (B). If you don't get rid of the excess water, one fine morning, you'll be greeted by a thin layer of water all over your counter. This problem was completely absent in the first unit we purchased. Other than this nuisance, the Brewstation is a great alternative for keeping coffee hot without burning it as do traditional coffee makers. As I mentioned in my original post, this design is convenient for those confined to wheelchairs to be able to get their own coffee themselves. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Our first Brewstation lasted about 6 years, so buying another didn't require much thought. Consumer Reports pooh-poohed this line because its brewing temperature is about 10° higher than the "optimal" 185°, but I don't really care. We live & care for my wife's invalid mother, who is confined to a wheelchair. Since there's no decanter, she can get her own coffee easily by herself. Plus, because of the machine's unique design, the coffee will hold for the full four hours without tasting like the gear oil from a poorly maintained, 1967 model dump truck. Versus the old model, I love the removable water reservoir and the light on the display is much brighter. While we seldom make iced coffee on purpose, it's nice that the feature is built in. Also, this one is about$15 cheaper than the original we bought in 2009. My only negative is that the front panel of the coffee reservoir gets *extremely* ' HOT! Ordinarily, it's not a problem. But if, for example, you're cleaning the machine and run consecutive brew cycles, the "chrome" plate on the front, even though it's plastic, will scorch your bare skin. You've been warned! Otherwise, this coffee maker is a winner! Hamilton Beach knocked this one out of the park.
I have been using this brand for years. It is a great coffee maker.
I chose this one because I had one like it before. It’s easy to use and clean

review_title: Si es un producto muy recomendable
body_en: - Delivery time, very good. The indicated day arrived. - Product, arrived in its original packaging, brand new coffee maker and at first glance in very good condition, I just received it. - Functionality, very easy to operate, works perfectly, very practical without a jug when serving directly into the cup. - Coffee flavor, just like other drip coffee makers of the same brand, since it is the same preparation principle. In short, I do recommend the product, for its functionality, quality and aesthetics. It is what it is, electric drip coffee maker.

The product arrived ahead of schedule, well packaged and undamaged. I'm satisfied with the quality, but the base for receiving the dripping coffee is loose. This is harmful, as you have to put it in place several times.

review_title: Brews 12 Cups Quickly And No Glass Carafe To Break
body_en: The Hamilton Beach 47950 BrewStation was purchased to replace my old Hamilton Beach BrewStation that, after 12 years, finally started dripping from the reservoir. Their new design has some pluses and minuses. Too many pluses to list them all, and the minuses are two: 1) it isn't that easy to clean the reservoir and 2) you can't pour from the top of the reservoir into a thermos. My old BrewStation had a spout built into the reservoir and made it easy to brew 10 cups, pour 8 into my thermos and the remaining into my insulated mug. This models reservoir is multiple parts with openings at the top in a few places and is not sealed. So trying to pour of the top of the reservoir just makes a mess and you loose half the coffee down the drain. It require you to use the built in push to pour spout at the bottom of the reservoir. I use a measuring cup with a handle to accomplish what used to be a quick and simple task. It works, but takes more time and means I have another item to wash. Other than that, I love the coffee maker. It brews 12 cups very fast and exactly how I like it. It has a timer for how long the warmer will stay on and is programmable so you can set it up before bed and your coffee will be ready when you wake up. It has an "iced coffee" setting , a "bold" setting and a setting for a small batch of coffee "1-4 cups". If you are in need of a replacement coffee maker or are looking to buy your first one, this is a great choice.

review_title: Arrived damaged and not working return a nightmare
body_en: Unfortunately this item came in a damaged box and would not power on. Such a shame as we were really looking forward to having this in our home. We have started the return process and hope to source another soon. So disappointed it didn't work 😳

I bought one a 3 years ago I cleaned it regularly. When I cleanedit this time it won’t turn on after cleaning. Doesn’t even light up. Talked to my friends they said that thought was crazy to expect more than 3 years. It worked great until that last cleaning. Did I do something wrong? Great coffee maker up till this so I did order another one it is on its way. It I need coffee NOW. LOL

review_title: Compact, Quiet, and Still Going Strong After a Year
body_en: This Keurig single-serve coffee maker has been great for everyday use, especially if you don’t want a large machine taking up counter space. I’ve had mine for over a year, use it every day, and it still works just as reliably as it did when I first got it. It brews incredibly quickly, usually in around 30 seconds or less, and it’s surprisingly quiet while running. I also love how small and lightweight it is. It’s easy to move around, pack up, or take somewhere else when needed, so portability is definitely one of its strongest features. I’ve had no issues using different pod options with it. It works with the regular coffee pods I buy, including Starbucks, as well as the reusable pod options I’ve tried. I like having the flexibility to use either prefilled pods or my own coffee without needing separate equipment. Pros: * Excellent space-saving design * Very quiet * Brews in around 30 seconds * Small and lightweight * Extremely portable * Works with multiple pod options * Compatible with reusable pods * Easy to use * Reliable for daily use * Still working great after more than a year Overall: This has proven to be a really dependable little coffee maker. I use it every single day, it takes up barely any room, and I can have coffee ready incredibly quickly. After more than a year of regular use with no issues, I definitely think it’s a great value for the money.

review_title: “Beautiful color, easy setup, and great coffee!” ☕💚
body_en: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Love the color and how easy it is to use! I just received my new Keurig, and I’m really happy with it so far! The dark green color is absolutely beautiful and looks even better in person. It fits perfectly on my coffee station without taking up too much space. Setup was quick and easy right out of the box. Within a few minutes, I had it ready to brew my first cup. I like that it has multiple cup-size options, and it fits my travel mug without any issues. The coffee brews quickly, is nice and hot, and the machine is much quieter than I expected. Overall, it feels well-made and is perfect for anyone who wants a simple, reliable coffee maker without a lot of extra buttons. If you’re looking for a compact Keurig that looks great and makes a good cup of coffee, I would definitely recommend this one!

review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker – Fast, Easy, and Great-Tasting Coffee
body_en: I’ve been using the Keurig K-Express for a while now, and I’m very happy with it. It’s compact, stylish, and fits perfectly on my kitchen counter. The Warm Stone color looks modern and elegant. The coffee brews quickly, and I love the Strong Brew option because it gives my coffee a richer, bolder flavor. The 42 oz water reservoir is convenient since I can make several cups before needing to refill it. It’s incredibly easy to use and clean, making it perfect for busy mornings. If you’re looking for a reliable single-serve coffee maker that delivers great coffee every time, this is an excellent choice. I would definitely recommend it!

First, an introduction, this will take some going through, bear with me. First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died. So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now.... This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that. But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew". All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

review_title: Mine did not last a year.
body_en: I loved this keurig for my family. It was perfect for my dsuggter, who had just started drinking mainly decaf coffee. Bought in Oct 2025, and it just stopped working after I cleaned it with descaling solution in June 2026. I had previously cleaned it earlier in the year without any issues. Not sure what went wrong. Not sure if I will buy another one. It was a good thing while it lasted.

I absolutely love my new Keurig K-Express! From the moment I took it out of the box, it was incredibly easy to set up and start using. Within just a few minutes, I was enjoying my first cup of coffee. What impressed me most is how quickly it brews. Mornings are busy, and having a fresh, hot cup of coffee ready in about a minute is a game changer. The Strong Brew button is one of my favorite features because it gives my coffee a richer, bolder flavor without any extra effort. The compact design fits perfectly on my countertop without taking up a lot of space, and the removable water reservoir makes refilling simple. It has been reliable, easy to clean, and consistently brews a great cup every single time. If you're looking for an affordable, dependable single-serve coffee maker that delivers great-tasting coffee and is simple to use, I highly recommend the Keurig K-Express. It has exceeded my expectations, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase!

I got this to replace my original Keurig. The old k50 or whatever it was. This thing takes up less space, looks more sleek, and works better than the original. It's faster, the coffee tastes better, it has the strong button. Also, I keep my coffee maker in my bedroom, and with the old one if you wanted it to be ready to make a quick cup of coffee it had to be turned on which meant that it had lights illuminated. I had to cover them with tape. This new one can go from being turned off to making a quick cup of coffee immediately. And after 5 minutes it automatically turns any illumination off. That means it doesn't make light in my bedroom at night. It's just a way way better version. It's quieter. I love it I'm so glad I got it. I will say that I got this brand new, and it was a really good deal, and I can see why because the manual includes an offer for discounted coffee that expired over two years ago. I'm guessing Keurig punched out a few too many of these models and they've been sitting in a warehouse for too many years. My advice is buy it now before it goes out of stock. It is an excellent coffee maker.

Very bad product, I used it for less than six months and it no longer works

This product is advertised on an Australian site in Australian dollars but I can’t connect it to 240 power even though I’ve tried two different adapters. I will try to ring keurigs number tomorrow to see if I can get any satisfaction.

I returned the item 9 days ago and no sign of my refund. I will be insisting on a refund to return the item as it cost me £35 to return with Parcel Force, that was the cheapest option.

review_title: We got this and got rid of all our other coffee stuff
body_en: Love this machine. Had to get a replacement unit. The first one had the pump glitch out during setup. Which our read is that it’s a known possibility. Return and replace was easy through Amazon and this unit has worked really well. Makes great coffee, easy to clean, and everyone in the house loves using it. Looks great too.

review_title: Create the perfect espresso with Jura!
body_en: This machine is perfection. It creates the absolutely perfect and most delicious espresso from whole beans or ground coffee. You will never have to buy a coffee again! The process is so easy and the taste of the espresso is superb. Worth every penny! And it’s sleek, white design makes it the best addition to any kitchen. It adds that touch of luxury and elegance while not compromising one bit on quality.
Incredible! Best coffee ever! Highly recommend, not just the best coffee, but using coffee beans saves lots of $$$

expensive yes! it really makes good coffee if you can handle the price. our favorite things about it is you can make ground or whole bean and its very fast....It takes a while to figure it all out but its fairly easy......

Love this Jura. Have had an Ena and a Gaggia for many many years, but the Jura is heads and shoulders above both. Blows away the coffee quality of my Gaggia Prestige, and is soooo much better looking and well designed. Perfect for someone like me who only wants espresso and americanos but wants them super tasty and easy.
It’s just great, no fuss espresso or coffee machine

If you’re looking for a short term coffee solution to get you through a few months of great coffee, this machine is for you. Easy to use, very convenient, makes a great cup of crema. It doesn’t have all the bells and whistles, just straight espresso and coffee which is exactly what I wanted. I’ve been diligent - religious even about replacing the filter on time, using official Jura tablets for descaling and cleaning. Over the last few weeks, coffee started to come out of the spouts slower and slower. Now it won’t make coffee at all. It’s clearly clogged somewhere. As a last ditch effort. I’ve run 2 back to back cleaning and descaling operations (yes using official Jura tablets). Nadda. She’s done for. Jura support has been useless. Placed multiple calls and no real results. I’m sure if I take the whole thing apart piece by piece I could fix it, but that’s not what I do or how I want to spend hours of my time. So I spent $200 a month for 7 months of great coffee. Funny to think I could have actually saved money going to the local coffee shop every single day.

review_title: Excellent Coffee Quality but Much Louder Than Expected for a Premium Machine
body_en: I’ve been using the Jura E4 Piano White Automatic Coffee Machine for a while now and overall the coffee quality is excellent. The espresso it makes is rich, creamy, and very consistent. The flavor extraction is impressive and definitely delivers a café-quality cup at home. However, for a machine at this price point, I expected it to be much quieter. The grinder is quite loud, and recently I’ve noticed the noise has increased even more when the machine turns on and off or when it starts grinding the beans. One thing to keep in mind if you have a baby at home, the machine is loud enough to wake mine up when we use it early in the morning. So if you’re hoping for a quiet espresso routine while the baby sleeps, that might be something to consider. Performance-wise, it’s great, and the coffee is fantastic, but the noise level is definitely something to keep in mind. Pros • Excellent coffee quality • Very rich and creamy espresso • Easy to use Cons • Much louder than expected for a premium machine
love this machine

review_title: Awesome little coffee pot! And brews fast!
body_en: This coffee pot is so great! I wasn't expecting much, but it has impressed me. I bought this for one purpose. My husband was having a high risk, complicated surgery, and I was going to be living in the hospital with him during the time he was in there. I like MY coffee, and I want my own coffee even away from home. It dawned on me that I couldn't take my huge, double sided multi-use coffee pot with me. I started looking for something other than a keurig, and I found THIS! I read reviews. I figured for $22, it's worth a shot. This thing is awesome! It comes with a cup and lid, and a little coffee scoop (i still used my own. The one that came with it is smaller than mine.) It has one button. If you hit the button while it's not plugged in, it still sets it to start. As soon as you plug it in, it will start. It's important to read the instructions that come with it and follow them. It takes about 3 minutes to brew the cup. It takes a little practice to figure out how much water to use to leave room for sugar/ creamer, but it brews great coffee. I am not sorry I bought this, and I've even sent the link to friends who also love their coffee. I've only had it for about a month now, but I even use it at home in lieu of my $120 coffee pot. I even had a few nurses comment on it and say what a good idea to bring a small coffee pot to provide those small comforts of home. Job well done, Elite Gourmet!

I received this about a week ago and it has been PERFECT. When I first received it, I fell in love with the color (as it is my favorite) and size. It was nicely packaged and in perfect condition. I ran the first cycle through with just water and wiped it down like the manual said. I only made one cup each day using the tumbler included I used cold bottled water and poured it in the tumbler leaving space for creamer. Because I wanted to make sure I have the right amount after fully brewed. *Today I went to make a cup as usual since ive had it.. And noticed the water I was pouring in was coming out of the bottom fast but not all of it. It was about 2 inches or so less of water that I initially poured into the Tumbler that was leaked out. I wiped it up and continue to press the blue power button. And it brewed fine (minus the amount leaked in the beginning) without any more leakage. I will make another cup later on today and do a update. * Tumbler is very nice to have and keeps coffee hot/warm for a hour+ ...As long as you keep the lid locked after you sip. Easy to clean, I like the reusable filter it comes with. I just dump the used grounds in a plastic sack and toss it. Rinse filter quickly and dry fast. Long as you don't use super fine grounds then the filter is perfect!. **All in all I LOVE this and recommend for occasional coffee drinkers. Especially with limited space and no need for full size.... I'm just waiting to see if it leaks again later today when I update! ****Another update: I have had this for a while now. I usually only make one cup per day. I clean it right after I am done and I make sure it is unplugged. This is a great machine for someone who is maybe just a single coffee drinker in the home or if it's just two people. It has not leaked since that one first time. Which I do think now the only reason there was water was because it dripped from the cup and I didn't notice. So I think this actually didn't leak on me as I thought. I'm still using it everyday and it is wonderful. ***Well OVER 1 YEAR UPDATE*** So this little single coffee maker is the best!!! I use to almost everyday, once a day. And it is still working just as good as when I first got it. I love this thing and definitely definitely recommend!!! Just make sure to always unplug it when you're done and don't make a bunch of cups back to back. At least I wouldn't recommend that. But if you are on the fence of ordering this and you only have one coffee drinker in the house, this is the perfect one!!! ✨☕

This cute little personal single serve coffee pot is exactly what my mother-in-law needed and I’ve made sure that she got one. It comes with its own mug. The brew time was very quick and the coffee tasted just perfect. No need for filters as it has its own little basket that is washable. But we decided to purchase the coffee pads, the little round coffee pads look like coffee and a teabag. Couldn’t find them in the store so I purchased them on Amazon. I told her not to fill up the water too high in the mug before she poured it in because she’s gonna be putting her creamer in it. She’s 80 years old so sometimes you have to remind her of things. But all in all, it’s a great little coffee pot and I’m glad I purchased it.

I love this single serve drip coffee maker. It is easy to use and clean. There is a slight issue, liquid is accumulating INSIDE the coffee tumbler that came with coffee maker see attached video. I have no idea how it gets inside and it doesn’t seem to drip out. Other than that I am very happy with this purchase.

This coffee maker has been a game changer for coffee at work. Gone are the days of relying on mediocre office coffee that was always somehow empty when I wanted a cup. This product is easy to use and brews a great 14oz cup of black coffee in less than 90 seconds. The reusable filter is easy to clean with a quick rinse. I opted for optional paper filters instead and all I have to do is simply dump the puck of used coffee. The LARATH brand basket coffee filters here on Amazon fit perfect. 14oz of water + ~4 tbsp of ground coffee is all you need. This is equivalent to one large cup of black coffee or 2 medium cups if you split it and add milk. Overall the machine is relatively quiet and will not disturb others around you. The insulated cup is poor at keeping heat but if you plan on finishing your coffee in less than an hour than it's a non-issue. I'd highly recommend this cheap little machine for (Large) single cup drinkers and those seeking a more convenient black coffee experience at your work desk. Hopefully it lasts me a long time, but for the price, I won't be upset if it's done in a couple years and that's okay.

It's fast and brews a good cup of coffee. I love the size, it doesn't take up much space on my counter and it's cute. I ordered a couple more cups for it, which was easy enough as the cup it came with, the bottom started peeling off. I still love it and would buy it again.

review_title: Works as intended, didn't last long
body_en: I bought this coffee maker in October of 2024, it just died this morning in June 2026. It was a good coffee maker while it lasted, it's easy to clean and easy to use. The single cup brewer I had before this one lasted at least 10 years so I had been hoping to get more life out of this one.

This little cutie is perfect. I just needed something that would make one cup of coffee and was not too expensive. The travel mug is a big plus. No searching for cups and it’s a Beautiful mint Green so no one else can claim it. The brew time is quick and reliable. I’ve used cold water bottles straight out of the fridge and the coffee still comes out piping hot. For the price I’m impressed with this gadget. The filter is easy to clean and the coffee mug fits in the cup holder on my lap desk.
I liked it a lot and it is very practical.

I have bought seven of these over the course of two years. Not because they break but because they're so good and a number of family members have asked for one as a gift after seeing mine. My husband (his is in black) and I both have one for work and we have one for the house. All three of ours get heavy use and they're still going strong! The other four have been bought as gifts and everyone who has gotten one absolutely adores it! I got one for my work Secret Santa and they have been delighted to use it every day since it is much more affordable than pods. It makes a cup of coffee, assuming max fill, in less than 3 minutes and it is delicious every time. It also brews at the right temperature. This little coffee maker is punching way above its weight class in terms of value and it comes out on top every time.
Works perfect
It really is impressive, how in a matter of seconds it starts preparing and your coffee is ready, totally recommended

So far it arrived well, it is small and easy to use, simple, like any coffee maker, you just add water, put the coffee in its filter and press the power button, you wait for the glass to fill and that's it, everything is normal, the glass is made of stainless steel, thermal and practical, if you just want a coffee without further details it will be useful to you

I have a love/hate relationship with Ninja products - I really love them. But I strongly dislike the warranty. And I hate the lifespan. Once they are done - they're done. I have had a couple of Ninja blenders that surpass the crushing and blending power of my 30 year old beehive Oster - but their life expectancy is about five years. This was a very strong consideration in purchasing a $200 coffee maker. I am not a coffee connoisseur - I typically drink one cup daily - very strong with cream only. But it has to be a perfect cup. I want to enjoy every single sip. I found a Ninja coffee system, brand new, at a thrift store locally for $15. The coffee was amazing. Perfect every single time. When my son moved to his own place, I gifted it to him and started researching one for me. Since I am the only coffee drinker in the house now (no, I'm not crying because he's gone, don't be silly) I considered a Keurig. But I honestly do not like the quality of the coffee from those machines - have tried several but it is not at all to my liking. However, the amount of wasted coffee I was dealing with really started bothering me and decided I needed an option for one cup. This machine is really perfect. The one cup option that I thought I settled for because it is a K cup option turned out to produce an amazing cup of coffee. I THINK it is because the Ninja makes three holes into the K cup rather than the standard one hole other machines use? It may also be the water temperature gets super hot. I do not know, but I really appreciate the depth of flavor from the K cup option on this machine. Another nice option that I never thought I'd want is the frother. It seems silly to me, but one comment in the Ninja manual stated that a cold cup with cream steals the heat from the coffee and changes the flavor - so I toyed around with the frother, using the microwave for 30 seconds and then blending the coffee and cream - its fantastic. This week I had a fever and opted for tea over coffee - I remembered the hot water option on this machine - it gave me two options - hot water and boil - I selected boil and my tea was steeping in no time at the perfect temperature. I absolutely appreciate that the water runs through a separate dispenser so my tea did not have any coffee residue or discoloration or flavor. I plan now to retire my stand alone boiler. The reservoir on the Ninja is adequate for my one cup daily - it is very easy to remove and fill or even fill while in place - I prefer the side option, but like that it can be attached to the back to save space. I don't think that would make much difference because this machine is very big - it does not fit under my standard cabinets. I bought this as a birthday gift for myself and if that last son hadn't left at the same time, I likely wouldn't have spent that much money on myself - but I was pitiful. I am extremely happy I did because the cost is worth it. I am very hopeful this machine will last past my 5 year expectation. Since I do not purchase coffee daily, I cannot state that I have saved money - I mean, I have because I'm not making half pots just for myself and wasting most of that - but if I were a coffee shop customer, I would absolutely think I'd save money with the frother thing and the quality of the coffee - It is really a great machine and I very highly recommend you purchase it. I was debating between the Keurig Duo Pro and this machine and given the quality of the K cup coffee from this, I haven't once looked back - there is no way in my mind the Keurig would produce the same quality cup from the K cups. Enjoy

We tried every aspect of the Ninja DualBrew Pro except espresso. My husband drinks coffee; I drink tea. Thumbs up on the Keurig pod coffee. The machine brewed HOT coffee with outstanding flavor. The boiling water feature for my tea boiled at least 2 ounces away in steam. I’m at 5500 feet altitude and had already performed the calibration process. The tea was so flavorful; much better than my normal BUT it was lukewarm even after heating the froth. LOVE the froth attachment. My husband’s coffee, brewed with the silver permanent coffee filter, was lukewarm. I tasted it, it was brewed on Rich and it was very tasty. I will try the heated coffee cup option but I’ve never had to do this previously with our little thermal carafe coffeemaker. I had it on delay but it never started at the designated time. I am finding the stopper for the coffee pot is difficult to seat on the pot. I’m not sure you could ever make espresso because the water does not get hot enough. So we’ve got pros and cons. It’s a beautifully designed machine that is so versatile but we like HOT coffee and tea. UPDATE: Changed to 5 stars. We generally brew coffee and tea one cup at a time. So the lukewarm issue pertains to carafe made coffee. When brewed with ceramic mugs, the coffee and tea is HOT. I think the "heated mug" option discussed in the instructions would resolve the lukewarm coffee/tea brewed in the carafe. Also, I resolved the Delay problem. It has to be done every night. I just assumed if it was set up and in Delay, it would work like my other coffee maker. You have to actually turn it on. After using the Ninja for a while, we both really love it. It makes outstanding coffee and tea and it's sort of fun to use. Update #2. After 1 month use, First, the coffeemaker would not “read” the pod adapter so could no longer brew pod coffee. Then while on the phone with Shark/Ninja customer service, the coffee feature went out. So now, I can only boil water. The customer service was excellent. I should have a new coffeemaker in 3-5 days, no shipping fees because it broke within 90 days. This reminds me of the Cuisinart toaster/airfryer/oven I got which did not work but the second one broke too. After spending so much time on the phone, I just gave it away. We’ll see if this coffeemaker makes it to the 1-year warranty without breaking. Still love it though. Update 2: received a new coffeemaker unit without any of the accessories within 3 days. The pod unit works perfectly. All the issues mentioned about lukewarm coffee does not seem to be a problem anymore probably due to single use in a ceramic mug. I really love this coffeemaker!

Have had Keurig, Cuisinart and other brands including other dual coffee makers and this is the best I've used so far. I mainly use the speciality and rich settings for a cup. Sometimes both for 1 large cup. Depending on time of day, cup size and mood. I don't use the provided carafe since I'm the only one drinking coffee. Also not a fan of iced coffee so that options a pass. Haven't tried the frother yet but I'm sure it's awesome and I will eventually give it a shot. Bonus for me is using size 4 filter and ground coffee for a 16 ounce cup. The cups I use are 14 to 20 ounces (variety for me is a need) and usually settle on 10 to 16 ounces for a cup. Use 2 pods (specialty+rich setting) or grounds or both for 1 cup. Again variety. This makes such good coffee that I would definitely purchase again. This is an expensive machine even on sale but I have no regrets with the purchase. Also on the larger side so may not fit under all cabinets. Very disappointed with the lack of a filter. Have purchased one and installed it already but the lack of one being provided is surprising. I have other Ninja appliances in my kitchen and hopefully I will be as happy with this one as I am with those long-term.

I've been using Keurigs for many years but when I ran across the CFP301 on sale, I was intrigued enough to give it a try. I really liked how you could set so many brew sizes and the ability to brew 1/4 carafe if I wanted a few cups without having to make two individual cups. I actually planned to use it mostly with reusable pods, like I've always done with my Keurigs, so I ordered a set that would work with this machine (most will not). The pods I bought look to be good quality, but I've never used them. I've been using pods for so long it never clicked that with a machine like this, using reusable pods makes no sense whatsoever. Just use a regular filter, add your coffee and set the brew size to the size cup you want. But there's more. Much more. With a Keurig or other pod-style machine, you are limited by the size of the pod. They can work a little magic by slow-walking the brew for a travel mug, but it was always weaker than a standard cup and there was little you could do to remedy it except for maybe brewing two pods into one cup. With the Ninja, I can simply adjust the amount of coffee and select the desired brew size. Done. Delicious. This machine, like all of the Ninja products I own, is well engineered. The moveable tank is a fantastic idea and is easy to use. The flip-down cup holder? Awesome! The foldable frother? Very cool, and the way you can just pop it off over the cup to take it to the sink is slick. Even the "smart" scoop is a very nice touch. Everything is so easy to use and convenient. The carafe is well designed and easy to clean. The insert for the carafe ensures the hottest coffee is circulated from the bottom up. Nice! I've had no issues with the temperature of my coffee. It has been nice and hot every time and the hot plate under the carafe makes sure it stays that way. When using a thermal travel mug, I'll either let it cool for a few minutes or plop a small piece of ice into it. It's hot. For filters, I am using Melitta #4 and folding the seams as recommended by Ninja. These are affordable, especially if you buy them in multi-packs. The result is delicious, ground-free coffee. I've read several reviews complaining about grounds in their coffee, but they don't mention their particular setup. Are they using a permanent filter? Pods? I don't know, but I'm not getting any and I'm not sure how I could using the paper filters. As for any negatives, which I feel compelled to include in any review, the only things I can think of are insignificant. The build quality is great, but it is a lot of plastic. For the price-point, it's definitely as good as I think one could reasonably expect. As long as it holds up to plenty of use, it looks good, works very well and I'm happy with it. I do wish there was a little capacitor to power the clock temporarily during brief power outages or if you unplug it for a few minutes. This is a tiny complaint, but I already have two other clocks on other appliances in my kitchen and it's a minor nuisance having to reset all these clocks every time the power blips. I haven't had the machine long enough to do a long-term review but if anything changes, I will update my review. So far, I am very happy with my purchase and highly recommend it. Edit (11/2023): I've been using this coffee maker for five months now, and I would now be lost without it. I absolutely love the versatility. My most recent development was to dig out my old 34 oz. French press, which fits nicely under the filter basket. For the best, boldest coffee, I measure the proper amount of coffee into the press and add 24 oz. of hot water from the Ninja for my normal 2 12 oz. cups. Easiest way ever to use the press. If I need a whole pot or just quick cup, I just brew like normal. If someone has a favorite K-cup, the insert works as expected. Selecting the brew size for coffee or water has been consistent and accurate. I really, really love this coffee maker.
extremely versatile and most importantly high quality coffee maker. pods and grounds work well and coffee tastes better than our old keurig. also, the iced mode works very well.

Let it be known: I love coffee, things that make my life easier, and multi-functional products. Unfortunately for Ninja, I also love to criticize, and I certainly have some issues with this coffee maker. But before that, what's good about it? It is incredibly easy to switch from K-Cups, grounds, or hot water needs. Since I moved to grinding my own beans, I no longer have much of a use for the K-Cup adapter, but it is incredibly easy to use and clean. Strangely, Ninja didn't put notches in the K-Cup holder, so if it seals just right it will take some prying with fingernails to get the pod out, but as someone who doesn't really use it, I don't find it terribly annoying. I also really appreciate that this brewer uses a shower/fountain head for the grounds, since that way the water doesn't just drill down the middle of your coffee, and has the best chance to evenly disperse throughout the basket. So I don't want to get too long-winded on what's great, because this machine just has so many little things that I'd end up writing a dissertation, and I think other people have already covered what's great. What I do want to talk about, is the little things that stick out as "odd or annoying." My biggest complaint comes from the dial used to select brew sizes; not in its physical function, but what sizes Ninja has selected. It seems that Ninja decided to base their sizes on things like "A big cup" or "1/4 of a carafe," instead of actual "number of cups." Because of this, you get measurement options like 15 or 28oz. This is hardly the end of the world, but if you grind your own beans you have to end up doing some weird mental math for "well that's 2 cups and 3 oz, so 2.5 cups, which means I need 25 grams of beans......" Like I said, not the end of the world, just weird. What is another weird inconvenience is the Keep Warm button; it only lights up/lets you click it once you get into sizes it deems worthy of the carafe. And the smallest size? 28 ounces. So if you want to make 2-3 cups of coffee, but leave it in the carafe since you only want 1 cup now, you have to choose your batch size, wait for it to brew, and then turn the nob to 28oz so it will let you press Keep Warm. I understand the minimalism-chic choice to have as few things lit up as possible, but this is truly the definition of Form Over Function. Ninja won't let me keep 18 ounces of coffee warm because they decided I should just put it all in a big travel mug. Now, none of these issues would stop me from recommending this coffee maker. Coffee is such an expensive hobby/interest that a 150$ coffee maker is still technically mid-tier, so I don't expect it to be flawless. It has a lot of functionality that I think a lot of people will find enjoyable, and makes a great cup/carafe of coffee quickly and easily. But because of weird choices by Ninja I can't say it is a 5/5. It is a solid 4/5, and worth your time, but definitely not perfect.

review_title: High quality rich drip coffee for a reasonable price.
body_en: Everything we wanted. Classic and rich brew modes are perfect. Make a range of sizes from small cup to full carafe. With high quality coffee ground to medium and rich brew it tastes identical to the best local coffee shop around. We got goldtone reusable mesh filter to fit. Has the k-cup option if you want to try a speciality. Brewing any size cup as drip with bloom only takes a few minutes. Consistent temp and quality out. Can’t wait to try the frother soon.

review_title: An awesome single serve brewer that is about as perfect as it gets.
body_en: You're looking for a coffee maker. Maybe a big multi-cup jobber isn't right for you, and you're trying to pick between the many options available. I too was in the same boat and after being disappointed with a recent Keurig purchase (dang chemical taste), I decided to find something that might work better for me. I will be honest that I dug out an old single serve coffee maker. Think of one of those little brewers you'd see in a cheap hotel. However, it worked, and was easy to clean with the stainless screen. I just found the flavor a bit lacking, and it didn't brew hot enough for me. I do own a couple other Ninja appliances that have worked well, so when I saw they offered a single serve coffee maker that would take normal grounds and pods, I decided to pull the trigger. The biggest plus was it has a water tank, so I can fill it with filtered water and make many cups of coffee using without having to fill it each time. I opted for the XL version to get the added water capacity. Getting into using the machine, it was easy to set up. Washed a few parts and I was off to the coffee making races. I normally brew around 12 OZ, and I use Gavina coffee. SInce it's not exactly like my other single serve brewer, I knew I'd have to tweak the amount of grounds being used. I landed on two slightly mounded tablespoons for a 12 oz brew. In terms of the build quality, I really like it. I also like that I can fit my big coffee mug without any issues. That is one big factor that can irk me, not being able to use my travel mugs. However, this machine has no problem in that area. Nothing feels cheap on this machine, and it looks nice as well. So how does it brew? Great! It gets plenty hot and brews the best cup of coffee I've had in a long time. I first tried the classic mode and it was good. However, when I switched to the rich mode, wow. It really enhances the flavor of the coffee and tastes excellent. Also, unlike the Keurig brewers I've bought over the years, this one has ZERO chemical/plastic taste. Good to go. I did run about 5 cycles through the machine before using it though. This thing is awesome and I'm glad I bought it. I didn't test the frother since I normally don't froth anything, but in terms of it making a great cup of coffee, it's a winner. I also love that it saves settings in between uses. So if I dial it in for the way I like my coffee, it has the same settings the next day. SImple but many brewers do NOT offer this. In terms of critiques, I only have one. It's cleaning out the filter assembly after brewing. It has a diffuser lid and it just makes smacking the filter assembly to knock the grounds out more difficult. I wish the lid was designed differently, but it's a very minor annoyance. Besides that, this thing is a home run in my book. I hope it lasts, but I can tell you sipping on a cup of coffee I brewed with this machine, it's the best I've been able to brew from this Gavina blend. Updates: 1. The removable basket which holds the grounds has a diffuser for the hot water to distribute over the grounds. This is not just a clip on, it's a twist lock, and is a bit cumbersome if it comes loose. It fell off in the garbage can a few times until I realized you really had to push and give it a hard twist to lock it on the lid. 2. I have moved on to using disposable filters which greatly reduces cleanup time and also puts less sediment into the brewed coffee. ASIN: B0FQV6H53G 3. The brewer continues to work great. Super happy with it!

It arrived ahead of schedule and in perfect condition. The functions menu is very complete and is very intuitive and easy to use. The size is perfect and it is not cumbersome. I additionally purchased the suggested reusable filters and they are perfectly functional and you avoid the waste of paper filters. I also bought the reusable capsules. They are a great option to reduce plastic waste. Recommended.
It's good but I'm not won over

We've had our Ninja K-Cup & Drip Coffee Maker for a while now, and it's one of the best kitchen purchases we've made. The flexibility is what really sold us. We use the drip side to brew a full pot and have the timer set so we wake up to fresh, hot coffee every morning. It's such a nice way to start the day! The single-serve side is perfect when only one of us wants a cup, and it also makes excellent iced coffee. We use it all summer long. Another feature we use all the time is dispensing hot water for tea. It's quick, convenient, and means we don't need a separate kettle sitting on the counter. It's easy to use, brews great-tasting coffee, and has become part of our daily routine. If you're looking for a versatile coffee maker that does much more than just brew coffee, I highly recommend the Ninja. It's been worth every penny! ☕🧊🍵

When we received this product we didn’t realise it was a USA plug but the seller vertex went beyond and above to help us find a converter - unfortunately after an amazing start the machine blew a fuse so we begrudgingly returned it - Canay @ Vertex was amazing and made every transaction so easy and hassle free Canay deserves 100+ for all the help we received a big massive thank you and I’m praying for the day this amazing product becomes totally UK friendly and once again a big shout out for Vertex and especially Canay 😍

Haven't had a drip coffee maker of any kind for the last 10 years. I have been using a french press for the last five years and before that my coffee was made in a percolator. A friend introduced us to the variety available in coffee pods, which my wife loves, so that kind of made up my mind. The Ninja CFP301 seemed to have it all and it meant I could do coffee from grounds as well as from pods. We buy beans from a local roaster and the quality of the finished coffee matters a great deal along with the versatility of using k pods. I can't begin to say enough good things about our Ninja coffee maker. We keep 4 or 5 different types of coffee beans on hand and this machine has made great coffee from them all. The fact that it dispenses hot water for tea, etc as well as makes coffee is a bonus in a small kitchen, so no more kettle on the counter. The footprint of this machine is not as big as I feared so it fits well on our counter top. The brew styles work a charm as does the milk frother. OK, so you have to heat the milk up first in the microwave instead of steaming it hot...no problem. The 'Specialty' brew style is worth having the machine for all by itself. While it doesn't produce the crema that true espresso machines do, it makes a cup of espresso from ground coffee that looks, smells and tastes close enough to genuine espresso that making lattes and cappuccinos is easy and a great complement to my kitchen. The conversion from grounds coffee to k pods is simple and I even bought reusable pod capsules that work very well. If there is a con of any kind it's that the warming plate keeps the coffee a bit hotter than I like so that a pot of coffee doesn't age well. I turn it off after a few minutes. I heartily recommend this coffee maker and have done so to all of my coffee fanatic friends.

Looks nice, works well. However..... It advertises a removable water filter with measurements on it in the water reservoir for the K cup. This doesn't have that, it has a plastic measurement piece that is screwed into the reservoir, but that's not a deal breaker for me. Love that it does not take forever to brew a 12 cup pot, and that it shuts off after 2 hours rather than burning the coffee in the carafe/pot. I DON'T like that you can't just turn it back on to continue keeping the coffee that is in the pot hot longer. Simply turning the maker back on does not turn the hot plate back on. Also, I don't like that just touching the hour or minute button, even accidently, changes the time on the clock. So, if you're not paying attention, you could change the time without even knowing it! And lastly, the measurement on the pot does NOT match the measurement in the water reservoir. If you put water in the pot up to the 12 cup line, it is only up to the 11 cup line in the reservoir. And if you add water to the reservoir to take it to the 12 cup line, it overfills the pot up to the top of the pot so it is spilling out before you can remove the pot from the hot plate. UPDATE: I purchased this on April 27th 2026, it is now July 11th 2026, the brew later light quit working about a month or so ago, and we noticed last night that the hot plate has developed crack in it, still seems to keep the pot hot for the 2 hours though.

review_title: Patronage has a new loyal fan and customer
body_en: This coffeemaker out-performs all brand names of higher-end units--most especially Keurig. We have used this coffeemaker every day for 15 months (we are avid coffeelovers!), and it is uncomplicated, reliable, and makes very good coffee, both individual cups and pots. Looks great on my counter, brews quickly, pours cleanly, and is easy to clean. My final $300+ Keurig lasted just 7 months with more-than-routine maintenance. So glad I tried this coffeemaker!!!! I'm a loyal fan!!

review_title: Defective Pantrymade Dual Coffee Maker. No return! No refund!
body_en: Doesnt deserve 1 star. Don’t buy this coffee maker. After only 3 months of using this coffee maker the indicator lights on the single serve side of the pot went out. After 4 months brew light in the carafe side went out. After 7 months, of use everyday, this morning, 8/22/26, the carafe side stopped brewing coffee mid process.. I contacted Amazon and found that the window for retuning item was 1 month and I would need to con tact the seller.. I couldn’t find any customer service number or link for Pantrymade after going to the store info on Amazon. and was told to contact Amazon.. so I’m out of $100.00 plus and cannot get satisfaction for a broken coffee maker. DO NOT BUY THIS defective product. IT WILL NOT LAST!! You’ll only loose your money. Unsatisfied Customer left holding a bag of wet coffee grinds!

review_title: Prettiest coffee maker I have ever owned!
body_en: This company has engineered the heck out of this coffee maker! They thought of everything. The size, finish and elegant digital display are the first of many impressive features. It includes a fine mesh filter for the carafe side and on the K cup side they included a fine mesh filter as well. So the single serve side will brew a K cup or your own bulk purchased coffee grounds. The plate that the cup sits on is stainless not plastic and they curved the back side as well. It just shows how much thought was put into the design. I could go on but let me say that I have purchased two Keurig K Duos in two years at $200 each. I said never again but when the second one went I ordered this one and then went to Walmart and ended up getting a K Duo because I had to have one. Now that I have received this beauty I packed up the Keurig. It’s now in the garage. I’ll keep it in case this one goes on the fritz. I’m tempted to get another one of these just to have on hand because I just like it so much! For everyone but especially those who want a beautiful coffee maker for their cute coffee bar; don’t hesitate to grab this or at the least put it on your special occasion wish list. Lastly, I haven’t brewed a cup yet but given the attention to detail that they put into this machine, I have no worries. I’ll have a delicious cup of coffee in the morning. You will not be disappointed if you purchase this coffee maker. It functions differently from the Keurig but I’m so over them. Hope this honest review will help you make a decision. UPDATE: This coffee ot crapped out this morning. It won’t brew. We have softened water so I don’t understand why it only last just under 1 year. We loved this pot so very disappointed!

review_title: small reservoir, but good coffee maker
body_en: I like the functionality and the space it takes up is a perfect fit, however the lack of a water reservoir for the K-cup dispenser makes it a little less then optimal for repeated individual cups without having water close by. First world issue!.

Brew Time is super quick. Very easy to clean. I like the two options to brew using the 12 cup pot or single use. My guest will love this addition to our coffee bar. The only downside I have found is for the kcup side, if you fill the water to the max line it will make that full amount, it will fill up 1-1/2 12oz cups. So don't add much water

This WAS a really nice coffee maker until it wasn't. It stopped working after 2 weeks and after some investigation I noticed there was not grate in the water reservoir on the big side and that allowed some missed coffee grains to get stuck in the heating chamber. If you order one anyways check to make sure it has the grates in the water reservoirs and then it would probably be a good coffee maker. Also it's very likely this was a used one they sent since there was some scratches in weird places.
I really like this product. Whatever the situation is, it is a delight to be able to make a pot of coffee or a single cup. It’s nice to have one product that can do both.

Love t his machine! Comes with removable easy to fill water reservoir. Has single cup filter add on, so you can make a single cup without having to go out and buy k-cups. Has a regular and bold brew on both the carafe and single cup options. Easy to clean. I can't say enough good things about this pot.

I got this back in 2020 and loved it so much I got my parents and in-laws one as well. All 3 are still working and going strong. Best coffee maker ever. I recently had some trouble with mine, it stopped brewing on the pot side. Come to find out it was just a clog from hard water build up. I highly recommend this product and so do my family members. No issues from any of them tht could not ve fixed by cleaning the unit. The needle on my parents unit has gotten clogged, and they have to clean that out regularly. Mine has never had an issue but I rinse mine after a few uses anyway. If you take care of it and do regular cleanings it will last you forever. (We clean with a white vinegar soak on both sides )

I love it. I had the generation before this one for about 5 or 6 years it was great to, untill it could'nt tell there was water in the single cup side. Hope this lasts as long. And you can't beat the price!

review_title: Great coffee maker with k-cup capacity
body_en: Excellent product. Love being able to brew both a k-cup of coffee or a full pot. It's extremely convenient for my husband to brew a k-cup or two in the morning before he heads to work. Super easy to use and program. Very cost effective as it combines k-cups and a regular coffee maker in one. Does not take up a large amount of space. Con: the cord to plug in to the wall is quite short.

We loved this coffee pot so much we bought another just like it for my dad. Love the efficiency of having a k cup and regular pot together saving counter space. It gives 4 different size options for k cup brewing. Even shows amount of total brewed as it fills the cup. Also has clock and delayed brewing options. We had a keurig combo pot before this one and it died at 11 months. We’ve not had this one quite a year yet, but it doesn’t seem to be slowing down any.😊

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I recently purchased the Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker, and it has quickly become an indispensable part of my morning routine. Here's why I'm giving this versatile coffee machine a glowing five-star review: **Versatility and Convenience:** The Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker lives up to its name by offering an incredible level of versatility. Whether I'm in the mood for a single cup or need a full carafe for the morning rush, this machine has me covered. The ability to switch between brewing methods with ease is a game-changer for a household with diverse coffee preferences. **Quality of Coffee:** One of my initial concerns was whether the convenience of a 2-way brew system would compromise the quality of the coffee. I was pleasantly surprised to find that this was not the case. Both the single-serve and carafe options produce rich, flavorful coffee that satisfies my coffee shop-quality expectations. **Ease of Use:** The Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker is remarkably user-friendly. The intuitive interface allows me to select my brewing preference without fuss, and the clear markings for water levels eliminate any guesswork. The simplicity of switching between brewing modes means I can enjoy my preferred coffee style with minimal effort. **Sleek Design:** Not only is this coffee maker highly functional, but it also boasts a sleek and modern design that looks great on my countertop. The compact footprint is a significant plus, considering its dual functionality. It's a stylish addition to my kitchen without taking up unnecessary space. **Durability and Cleaning:** After several weeks of use, the Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker has proven to be durable and easy to maintain. The components are sturdy and well-made. Cleaning is a breeze, especially with the removable parts being dishwasher safe. This ease of maintenance ensures that the machine continues to perform at its best. **Eco-Friendly Options:** I appreciate the eco-friendly aspect of being able to use a reusable filter for the single-serve option. It's a great way to reduce waste and save money on disposable pods. The inclusion of this feature reflects a thoughtful consideration for both the user and the environment. **Value for Money:** Given its dual functionality, ease of use, and the quality of coffee it produces, the Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker offers excellent value for money. It's a versatile appliance that caters to all my coffee needs without requiring multiple devices. In conclusion, the Trio 2-Way Coffee Maker has exceeded my expectations in every way. It combines versatility, convenience, and quality into one sleek machine. For anyone looking to upgrade their coffee experience with a device that can handle the demands of both single-serve and carafe brewing, I cannot recommend this coffee maker highly enough. It's a stellar addition to any coffee lover's kitchen arsenal.

review_title: So many choices. This one hit the mark.
body_en: Very pleased with this unit. We usually make a 10 cup brew in the morning, although this unit can make 12. We also use the "bold" taste setting. Ten cups brews on the slower bold setting in about 14-15 minutes. The water reservoir for the carafe side has a very large opening making it easy to fill with the carafe. The carafe pours nicely without dripping, unlike our last coffee maker. And, I see Amazon has multiple sources for replacement carafes - good to know since it is glass. The pod side (single serving) works fine. Nice for the occasional mornings when we only need a single cup or two.
Bought this to replace our previous two-in-one. Works great. The single-serve lets you set a cup size (up to 14 ounces) and brews in moments. Our previous one took quite a while. Highly recommend!

Excellent coffee maker, great quality of material, easy and intuitive programming, a great success that you can make a preparation individually (consider that the compatible capsules for this coffee maker can only be obtained online since they are not found here in Mexico and the other brands are not compatible), however, the accessory to put ground coffee of your preference gets you out of that trouble, without a doubt I recommend it 100%

review_title: Your regular and Keurig coffee in one
body_en: We're so happy with this coffee maker. After years of spending around $60 on a Black and Decker type carafe coffee machine that only lasts a year, we decided to invest in a better one. We're so happy with it, it delivers good HOT coffee and the single serve works for Keurig cups and your own blend (comes with two filters for these purposes). You can even use both to make tea. They have seperate water reservoirs. Very happy!
Excellent coffee maker, highly recommended
I love this coffee maker has both options single cup or full pot. Easy to use. Love it!!!!
The coffee maker is very cool. I have a question, could you tell me what type of capsules this coffee maker uses?
It's a coffee maker. Works great. less filling! Ha Good buy!

review_title: So much better than the last pos!
body_en: Basic coffee pot capable of making a large, hot pot of black goodness that helps me 'get through this thing called life'. I am going all the way (5 star) for this basic drip maker. Obviously you can spend $400 and get a superior machine but in the basic coffee pot category? This one is great. Our last machine was so bad we celebrated when it died. Our last pot went through paper towels and cuss words like they were in competition with each other. Trying to pour from the carafe was a bloody nightmare with coffee dribbling off the pot mid pour. I hated that friggn thing. So did my hubs. This pot is so easy to pour from. It makes NO MESS. This one is easy to pour water into the back. There is no missing the pour area unless maybe you are drunk. (Note: Resulting cup of coffee may vary if/when there is alcohol involved.) It has a standard reusable basket for grounds right in the front that is super easy to clean, etc The auto shut-off works TOO GOOD for all day drinkers. I appreciate the safety feature regardless. It does it's job. I just have to keep turning it on. That is a personal preference that has more to do with my addiction than it does the integrity of the coffee pot. It has a timer so you can have that baby cooking up your first morning pot while you are still drooling on your pillow. Anyways, Good pot, good coffee. I really hope his one lasts longer than the last one. If it doesn't, I will probably look for an upgraded pot with the same carafe. Good luck!

arrived on time & packet very well. This was a replacement for an old Black & Decker, so i went with the newer basic model since it lasted so long. This is the classic coffee maker style thats been around for ever. PROS: makes HOT coffee, the donut shape hot water dispenser does very well, no paper filters have fallen over with this design, still has the timer, and the best new feature is the STRONG setting thats for making 1 to 2 cups at a time, plus it save coffee too, also when 30+/- brews happen it tells u its time for cleaning & has a built in cleaning mode. CONS: the lighted buttons glow are very dim & are especially hard to see in a bright room, the carafe or pot lid that one usually uses the thumb to push down to open the lid, your thumb has to go down into the side handle a little & its unconformable tight area especially with big thumbs. All in all its a great basic automatic drip coffee maker and i hope this one last as long as its predecessor B&D model. Would buy again.

review_title: Great Value and Great Customer Service
body_en: We initially purchased the coffee maker in March 2024 and rated it 2 stars because it worked well and then it completely failed within about three months. We're updating the rating and giving it 5 stars because Black & Decker was really great about replacing it for us and the new one has been working exactly as it should for at least a year since then. In the past, we've purchased much pricier coffeemakers, but now that we're retired and far more budget conscious, this coffee maker is perfectly fine -- even for total bougie coffee snobs. Our coffee tastes pretty great! It's a standard 12-cup model, reasonably quiet, the brewing time is reasonable, the coffee stays hot in the pot and we've had no leakage problems or any other issues. This coffeemaker really is a pretty great value for the money.

I debated over getting this. I didn't really 'need' a sneak a pot feature or a programmable timer, but I love the features now that I have them. Glad I spent a few dollars more to go with this coffee maker.

review_title: YOU GET WAT YOU PAY FOR
body_en: CHEAPER THAN MOST UNITS, BUT YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR. I GOT THE UNIT TODAY AND RIGHT FROM THE START I GOT MY FIRST SIGN THAT I PROBABLY MADE A MISTAKE. I HAD TO USE KITCHEN SCISSORS TO GET THE COVER OFF THE POWER CORD PRONGS (strike 1). I WENT TO PUT WATER IN THE CARAFE AND NOTICED THE WATER LEVEL MARKERS WERE SO THIN THEY WERE BARELY VISIBLE. I HAD TO KEEP TURNING THE CARAFE UNTIL THEY WERE READABLE (strike 2). THE MANUAL SAYS THE ON/FF BUTTON LIGHTS UP. ALL I SAW WAS A TINY PIN POINT SIZE LIGHT INDICATOR HARDLY NOTICEABLE. THE MANUAL ALSO SAID THE BREW BUTTONS LIGHT UP, IF THEY DID THE LIGHTS MUST BE ON THE INSIDE BOTTOM, I DID NOT SEE ANYTHING. WHEN I WENT TO PLACE THE BASKET INTO THE UNIT I HAD KEEP WIGGLING IT BEFORE IT FIT IN (strike 3- it is out) . WHEN I AM STRUGGLING IN THE MORNING TO GET MY FIRST COFFEE I DO NOT WANT TO FUSS WITH A CLUTSY COFFEE MAKER. I JUST GOT IT AND IT'S GOING TO THE DUMPSTER.

I have had Mr. Coffee drip makers for many years and have loved them. But when I needed to replace my old one, I decided to try this Black and Decker. It is simple which is what I wanted. I love the strong brew feature which is what I always use. And the spray water head is great because it gets water throughout the coffee grounds rather than just coming out through one little hole. It makes a rich tasting cup of coffee. The only thing that bugs me is that when I lift the lid to take out the filter basket, water drips down the back of the coffee maker. But overall I am very happy with this coffee maker and highly recommend it!
Perfect basic coffee maker with the ability to set brew time. Came perfectly packaged and undamaged and works amazingly well.
Good quality! Good price!

At first, I wasn’t too sure about this coffee maker, but now that I’ve gotten used to it and know how to use it. It’s actually a good coffee maker I like Black & Decker. And it makes pretty good coffee. At first, I didn’t give it a very good review. But it’s not the coffee maker. It was just the person who was trying to make the coffee. Now that I know how to use it it works good.

I'm happy with the functionality of this machine. It brews my usual 8+ "cups" of coffee in 11 minutes and keeps it at a good temperature for the stated 2 hours. Capacity is 12 5oz. "cups", which is consistent with other coffee makers. It pours without dripping and the interrupt function works well. While the clock is easy to set and very visible the on/off light is difficult to see unless viewed straight-on from a high angle, as may be evident from the three photos I'm attaching. This makes it easy to leave the heat on after the pot is empty. Improving the light is the one and only change I'd ask for.

review_title: I'm done with expensive toys - this works GREAT
body_en: I've spent decades spending absurd amounts of money trying to find the perfect coffee maker. After spending nearly a month in a rental house that only had an inexpensive coffee maker - and LOVING the coffee I'd get from it - I finally shopped around for something like it. I landed on this particular model and couldn't be happier. I feel silly for having invested so much over the years on coffee makers that didn't last nearly as long as they should have (for those prices). If this one breaks down after a year, who cares? I'll get another! At this price, I can afford to buy a new one more often. (Have been using it for a couple of months now. Perfect coffee every time. Super easy to operate, program, and clean.) ***UPDATE JUNE 2025: Still going strong! Not a single thing has changed. Carafe and basket cleaned in dishwasher daily without issues. All features working perfectly. Still very happy with my decision to go low-tech and basic.
I love this coffee maker, and I like how simple it is to set up and that it has the round water dispense over the single drip and the Strong feature

review_title: Pricey up front, but saves money for us in the long run, and the coffee is great!
body_en: Wow, I'm really happy with the Philips 5500 for our home. The taste of the coffee drinks are far above the pods we were using. I recommend watching some videos to see how to adjust the machine so that the coffee is to your taste and not too bitter or too watery, etc. I love the customization options because all of us have different preferences. Everything is really easy to clean and take care of. This has replaced four separate machines for my coffee drinking family - a Nespresso, a Keurig, a plain coffee machine, and a separate milk frother. It takes up a lot less space, and it's quiet. It's easy to use, even for older people. It's not a cheap machine, but we were spending a small fortune on individual coffee pods for our family of coffee drinkers. The cost of the beans is a lot less than buying pods. The machine itself is also really quick compared to our old suite of machines. I hope that it ends up reliable in the long run.

review_title: 10/10!!!! Love it!!!! I’m a coffee snob🤷🏻‍♀️😍
body_en: Loving this so much! Did my research and very happy! I love all the options and the fresh ground beans every time. Easy to set up and use. Plus you can customize each drink. I love I can add an extra shot to my latte macchiato. You can even save profiles for others using it. I like the milk canister and it’s easy to use and simple cleaning. Everything is simple cleaning and comes apart so quickly. I get about two-three uses from my milk reservoir. One trick I have learned, roll up a paper towel to plug the milk reservoir while storing in fridge. All in all I love this machine and highly recommend.

review_title: It delivers what you want I like the different profile settings
body_en: I bought an espresso machine, and I love it.
