body_en: The best entry chair that exists, the only defect was the abusive tax from the government that hates poor people

Overall the quality is ok and delivery is fast. However, the tread was defective till the screw sheared off at right arm after slot during fixing so now got one screw missing. See the photo.. not sure it affects the safety?
Easy to assemble with clear instructions. No additional tools required. Easy to adjust and very comfortable.
Reluctant at first to buy without trying and to my great surprise I am extremely satisfied with my purchase I highly recommend it

review_title: Finally a chair that doesn't destroy my back
body_en: I sit at my desk for 10+ hours a day, and my old chair left me with constant lower back pain. This one is a complete game changer. The adjustable lumbar support actually stays where I put it, and the recline function from 90° to 135° lets me shift positions throughout the day. The mesh back keeps me cool, and the seat cushion is firm but comfortable. Assembly was straightforward and the casters roll quietly on my hardwood floors. For the price, I honestly didn't expect this level of quality. Highly recommend for anyone who spends long hours at a desk.

review_title: Quiet casters and solid build – finally no more squeaking
body_en: My last two chairs started squeaking within a month. This one is built differently. The metal base feels heavy and durable, and the casters roll smoothly with zero noise – even on my tile floor. The recline mechanism works like a charm, and the chair stays locked at whatever angle I set. The seat is wide enough for comfortable sitting, and the foam hasn't flattened out after weeks of daily use. Assembly was quick and the instructions were clear. I've recommended this to a few friends already. Solid chair for the price.

review_title: Great for tall people – finally a chair that fits
body_en: I'm 6'3 and most chairs feel like they were designed for someone much shorter. The headrest on this one actually reaches my neck, and the lumbar support hits the right spot on my lower back. The seat height goes up high enough for my long legs, and the recline function is smooth and secure. The mesh back is a lifesaver in warmer weather. Assembly was easy and the chair feels solid underneath me – no wobbling even at full recline. If you're over 6 feet, give this one a serious look.
It has a professional appearance and style It adjusts easily and sits with comfort The mobility moves with ease.

review_title: Great budget gaming chair, highly recommend!
body_en: I’ve been using this chair for about a week now and overall I’m really happy with it. It’s way more affordable than those big-name gaming chairs, but the quality is definitely there. The leather feels soft and premium, and it’s super comfortable to sit in for long hours. Putting it together was mostly straightforward, but connecting the seat and the backrest can be a bit tricky. Unlike other chairs that use a heavy metal bracket to link them, this one relies entirely on the armrests to secure the top and bottom. It takes a little patience to get the holes lined up perfectly. Pro tip: Do NOT tighten the screws all the way at first. Loosely catch all the screws in their threads first, and once everything is lined up, go back and tighten them all down. For the price, you really can’t beat it. Great value for a solid gaming chair!
Nice quality and not too hard to put together. I wish there was a way to bolt the seat to the bottom part though.

My son absolutely loves his new gaming chair. He put it together by himself in no time. He said it's very comfortable and such an upgrade from his basic desk chair. His new gaming setup is a major upgrade. Very durable chair for a 10 year old. Big enough that he'll grow into it just fine as well.
Made well. Quality fabric. Comfortable. Nice looking and affordable.

Very nice and comfortable chair. Arrived fast and in good condition. Assembly was pretty straightforward, push in the wheels, screw in the arm rests, attach the back rest and place everything on top of base, done. I have spent couple of hours a days in the chair and it feels good every time. I really like the design. Good purchase
Really nice !! Screws would do good with a screw gun but other than that I love the chair I got it for my son
Liked the chair but assembly directions could better than just pictures. Otherwise it was not too difficult.

This is the first review I have written. There are two things I want when I purchase a product, Quality and Communication. HapGift provided both second to none. Having used it for a couple of weeks I can say the chair is as advertised and It is a quality product. More important though, is the quick response to a problem I had. It was apparent Amazon shipped me a pre-opened box and parts were missing. I contacted HapGIFT who not only responded immediately but resolved the problem within a few days. You cannot please everyone, but its nice to know this company will make every effort to do so.
Beautiful but the comfort in the sitting position is not comfortable in the long term
Uncomfortable and the head pillow is hanging from the top like a backpack. Good price but very poor quality

I just received this chair today, so my product review is mostly on the packaging, instructions, and assembly. The product was well-packaged, and it was obvious when I unboxed it that a lot of care and thought went into packing it in the most efficient way that would also protect the parts. I was positively impressed with the packaging. I was also incredibly impressed with the instructions and assembly process. I am used to cheaper products where the parts only half fit or important components are missing, or where the instructions were confusing and unclear. This chair's instruction manual was very clear and concise. The diagrams were easy to understand and neat. The screws came labeled and separated and also included the scew types and sizes/lengths, which is handy in case you need to pick up extras at a store somewhere. But they also included one extra of each type of screw, washer, and cover, which I appreciated during assembly. (I didn't find myself worrying what would happen if I dropped a screw, which is something I would normally be distsracted by while working.) The only things I would take points off for were these: 1. The instructions said the chair came with gloves for assembly, but no gloves were included. That was fine with me, but why mention them if you won't include them? The instructions even later say not to use the chair if not all components were present...but all the important ones were, so I assembled it without gloves (as I probably would have done anyway, since it was for me and not another person). 2. It matters which side of the seat is the front, but the sticker was confusing. The instructions show a sticker placed on the side that is the front, and that is where my sticker was placed. However, the sticker says "FRONT" and has an arrow pointing somewhere. In the instructions this arrow pointed to the front. On my seat, however, the arrow pointed to the back. So am I supposed to believe the sticker placement (it was diagonal, so it looked haphazardly slapped on) or the arrow? On that particular step the piece you are screwing into the seat can fit both ways, but thankfully there is a later step where it becomes obvious which side is the front vs. the back. (The arm rests can only be attached to the back.) So I wish that had been clearer up front, but otherwise it was okay. Recommendations for assembly: - To attach the wheels, apply firm, direct, straight-down pressure. I tried screwing them on at first but you just push. Make sure they go in the whole way like the picture shows. - When they say to tighten the screws to only 60%, it's a helpful tip, because you can't fit the armrests on both the seat and chairback at the same time with the screws completely tightened. Just tighten them enough to fit the pieces on, then later you can tighten up the screws. So far I find the chair to be very comfortable and I'm exceedingly happy with it. The lumbar support seems like it could potentially be a little chafy or scratchy, but I'll give the chair a chance before deciding if it's problematic or not. Like I said, I only got the chair today, so I can't speak much to its long-term comfort, durability, or longevity. But I was so impressed with how easy and straightforward they made the assembly that I had to write a review to show my appreciation.

review_title: Very Comfortable Ergonomic Chair - Great for Long Work Days!
body_en: I’ve been using this ergonomic office chair for a couple of weeks now and I’m genuinely impressed. For the price, it offers excellent comfort and support. What I like: • Very comfortable padded seat and backrest — I can sit for 8+ hours without back pain. • Good lumbar support and adjustable height/armrests. • Holds up to 330 lbs easily (I’m 240 lbs and it feels very stable). • Smooth rolling wheels and sturdy base. • Easy to assemble (took about 20 minutes). The mesh back breathes well and doesn’t get hot. It looks professional in my home office too. Overall, this is a solid ergonomic chair. If you spend a lot of time at a desk, I highly recommend it. Would I buy it again? Yes, definitely.

Comfortable for the price. The seat could be a bit better, but for a budget friendly ergonomic chair, it's well made and has helped a lot with my back pain caused by my previous desk chair. Assembly wasn't terribly difficult, though I did have one screw with damaged threads. Luckily they ship spare screws in the kit, so that was a non-issue. Rollers work great on my small rug and hard flooring and don't tend to tangle cords or cables too much. Size wise, works great for my frame (5 ft 6 in) but for someone more than a few inches taller than myself, you should probably look at another chair.

review_title: Great ergonomic chair for working from home!
body_en: Super comfortable and easy to assemble. The back support and headrest are excellent, and the flip-up armrests are very convenient for saving space. Highly recommended!

review_title: Not Recommend. Uncomfortable and a waste of money.
body_en: Not recommended. Buy something else . I should have paid a little more and gotten a much better chair/experience. Comfort: Fail. Bottom line is that chair is just uncomfortable. - The seat cushion does not feel good on my but after just 15 minutes of sitting in it. I had to put a bed pillow on it to make it somewhat useable for more than an hour. - Lumbar support is very disruptive and just feels horrible, would prefer to take it off. - Headrest is horrible. I am not tall (5 foot 8) and the headrest was so low on my shoulders which is very uncomfortable and clearly a design flaw. The tippy top of the head rest is below my ears, so literally no head support. It would be even worse for anyone taller than 5 foot 8. which would be most people. - Arm rests are not height adjustable and are incorrectly height designed compared to low head rest. - Last time, I bought a slightly more expensive chair and it was significantly more comfortable. - Better than a $20 folding chair... which isn't saying much. Building it: Fail - I followed the directions and also did it a second time in a different order. Either way, the alignment was very difficult to get into the screw holes. Quality: Fail - Feels cheap

review_title: Surprisingly long life for a lesser priced chair
body_en: I waited 16 months to write this review. I’m at the top end of this chairs capacity, I’m 340lbs and 6’6” tall. I use this chair as my 44hr a week office chair. It took 16 months for something to finally give out. A wheel caster finally collapsed. I ordered new ones next day and was back up and rolling. I bought this chair for $99.00, a great investment. It’s hard to find office chairs for larger people so I wasn’t expecting a long life for such a lower price item, let alone be comfortable. From my experience, this was a great find.

review_title: Leaned back and snapped the back support. Durability is suspect
body_en: Chairs really comfortable, only problem was it broke when leaning back on the left side rail. I’m no where near the weight limit, was leaning back and heard a snap. Busted all the way through-so durability is in question.
Excellent product comfortable chair took about 20 minutes to put together much better than my experience trying to purchase one from eBay would purchase from this seller again

review_title: Comfortable and Stylish Chair with Just a Minor Assembly Issue
body_en: Overall, this is a great chair, and I’m really happy with my purchase. The assembly process wasn’t too difficult, though I did encounter a bit of trouble when it came to attaching the headrest. It may have been something I was doing wrong, but that part of the assembly felt trickier than it needed to be. I think it could be designed in a way that makes attaching the headrest a bit easier. Aside from that, the rest of the assembly went smoothly and didn’t take too much time. In terms of comfort, the chair definitely meets my expectations. The seat is comfortable, and the support it provides is just right for long hours at the desk. This is my first time using a mesh chair, and I have to say, I’m impressed with how well it breathes. The mesh design keeps me cool and comfortable throughout the day, even during extended use. It’s a significant upgrade from the traditional padded chairs I’ve used in the past. The lumbar support is also a nice touch, and it helps me maintain good posture, which is important for me since I spend a lot of time working at my desk. The chair also looks great! The modern, sleek design fits well with my home office setup, and I love how it adds a touch of sophistication to the space. It’s not just functional but also stylish, which is a bonus. The neutral color and clean lines make it versatile, so it can fit into a variety of different spaces, whether at home or in a professional office setting. While I’m optimistic about the durability of the chair, especially with the mesh construction, only time will tell how long it lasts. I’m hopeful that it will hold up well over time, but as this is my first mesh chair, I’ll be keeping an eye on how it performs with daily use. So far, everything feels sturdy and well-built, and I don’t foresee any issues, but it’s always something to consider with a new type of chair. All in all, I’m really pleased with this chair. It’s comfortable, stylish, and relatively easy to assemble, with just a minor hiccup when it came to the headrest. If you’re in the market for a mesh office chair that offers good comfort and looks sharp, I would definitely recommend this one. It’s been a great addition to my workspace, and I’m looking forward to using it for years to come.

review_title: Satisfied customer good value for the price
body_en: Arrived a couple of day early which was a pleasant surprise. Assembly instructions were straight forward and easy to follow making assembly a simple task. The chair is comfortable and easy to adjust to my specific needs. The lumbar support is firm and comfortable. The price was right and I would recommend this chair as a good buy.

review_title: Not a great seat, but the back support is good and the build quality seems quite good honestly.
body_en: Disclaimer - this is an initial review - only had this chair a few days Size: 6'4" ~280lbs The good: the materials and build quality overall is pretty good, not sure what more you could want for a <$500 chair. The only thing that worries me is how long the mesh will last. I'd be happy with 3 years to be honest for the price ($180 at time of purchase). The lumbar/cervical neck support is very good. This is pretty much why I bought it. It will help me force myself into a good posture since my neck is such a mess, both lumbar and cervical. The head rest is actually quite good. It could be slightly stiffer to stay in place maybe, but it's pretty nice. The smell - call me weird but the smell of new plastic in a room for a day or two is a pro not a con for me. It honestly looks pretty nice, not a huge plus for me but it does look sleek. The bad: The reviews saying the seat is uncomfortable are right....at least so far as it is a very narrow seat. If it was ~3-4 inches wider, it would be a 10/10 chair for me at least on initial use. The edges are a bit harsh on your hips if you are north of a 38" pants size. If you're sitting pretty straight, not really a problem. The mesh feels fine, it's not as good as a cushion but the tradeoff of breathability is worth it I would say. What I did right off the bat to help with comfort a bit was get some pipe insulation foam I had laying around in the garage, cut it in half, and lined the front half of the seat underneath with it. Just kinda stuffed it in there up against the edges as much as I could. Does it help? Actually....kinda, ya. I'd say it makes it a good 15-20% more comfortable at the edges. Picture attached (you can kinda see through and see what I did). Edit: I used the other half of the foam for the back half. So I completely lined the edge underneath with pipe insulation. It does actually help. I also figure this will keep the edges of the mesh from fatiguing as quick since it shouldn't pull down on it as harshly over time. The casters it comes with are pretty bad. If you buy a chair for <$500 though, you should be buying a ~$15-20 set of roller blade casters to swap in. I ran the stock casters for a day as the roller blade ones I got here on Amazon for $16 didn't come until the next day. The stock ones work, but they're quite slow. In my opinion, any reviews saying that the caster input area welds failing were partly due to the stock casters being slow in the first place. This makes you need to push more, and puts more pressure on these spots - making it more prone to failure. The welds to me don't look bad to be honest, and it doesn't worry me - if they failed I'd just reweld them myself. The arm rests are way too adjustable. They are honestly not bad, but they don't need any more adjustment than literally just going up and down. THIS WAS THE #1 REASON FOR NARROWING MY SEARCH DOWN TO THIS CHAIR - for playing guitar flip-up armrests are a must for me, which narrows down the search dramatically, as anyone reading this knows. But the arm rests aren't bad. Conclusion: As a big guy, this is a good chair that will help with posture. The seat is too narrow if you are size 38 or greater pants - it's undeniable. Hopefully the mesh holds up - if that is the case I'll be plenty happy for the price. If this chair gets a better version in the future with literally just a wider seat, I will absolutely buy it when this thing is worn out in (hopefully) like 3 years. NOTE: THE TOP LUMBAR SETTING ISN’T A SETTING IT IS THE RESET. So many people in reviews, including myself thought the lumbar didn’t stay set - it does, just the top most spot is NOT a setting it is meant to unlock it and reset to the bottom.

I am honestly shocked how well this was packaged! not one part came out loose. things were packaged together but inside that packaged also. High quality parts. The bolts/screws had the lock tight stuff around the threads. Definitely no question if they were tight enough. Easy to follow directions. Only step 5 isnt labeled like the others, But Easy to open the package and see which one you need. All the tools you need came with it. The Allen wrench actually had a decent handle on it. The barch support feels great. It's comfortable for now. we will see how many hours until its not. Most of the bolts came with one extra. Out of the many things I have bought and had to put together, This one! freaking awesome. It looks good, besides the chrome pieces cover the bolts, I can change that. So far ,new, there is no noise from it.

review_title: It’s not comfortable. Id like to return it.
body_en: To be honest. I had high hopes for this chair. Now. I hate it, I don’t know who is sitting on this for extended time. I can’t. Its supposed to be for bigger people. Im not huge. Its not wide enough with the arms down. I changed the wheels because it didn’t roll correctly. I added a pad because its too firm. The mesh is supposed to be more comfortable. The support is more stiff than relaxed. The design of the head rest is awkward. You’re supposed to be able to adjust it. It got locked into place. Now the height of it is too low. I misplaced the directions. I know there is a way to re-adjust it. Its just not clearly noticeable; such as a knob or button. As far as quality, its well made, as far as sturdiness goes. The thing is that when i go to sit down, there is that lip in front. I have to have an arm down on the chair, hold onto it, then sit down, otherwise the chair rolls away and I would fall on my butt. So, in that way- its not really safe. Even though I have this cushion on it, its still hard and my back hurts all the time Im sitting there. Not immediately, but soon afterwards. If I could return it, I would. That’s the thing about furniture, tho, isn’t it? Once its together, you can’t really take it apart and rebox it and send it back. It takes a week or so to figure it. Then the box is gone. Maybe if it were a little higher. I don’t know. Im fairly sure its all the way up. So yeah. Make sure your surface is really flat. Even changing the wheels doesn’t help. It moves well enough when you’re not in it. But trying to get in it and moving around in it is a different story. Also. I always feel like I’m leaning forward unless I intentionally sit back against against the back of the chair. Then it feels awkward where the headrest is and the back support. I don’t know. Im not a happy camper. Its the second mesh chair. Neither are actually comfortable. There really isn’t enough padding if you’re a bigger guy. This is supposed to support up to 400lb. Well its not breaking, but it’s also not comfortable.

Comfortable, helps my back pain, would definitely order again if someone alse in my family needed it and would recommend to friends, Height is very easy to adjust. Study and does not feel loose or cheap. Able to move around and stay in place perfectly.

review_title: Supportive, Customizable, and Surprisingly Comfortable for Long Hours
body_en: After spending 8+ hours a day at my desk, I finally upgraded to the CAPOT ergonomic mesh chair—and the difference is night and day. It’s not just a chair, it’s an adjustable support system designed for serious desk work. ✅ Pros Comfort: The seat cushion is firm yet breathable, and the mesh back keeps me cool even during long sessions. Lumbar support is adjustable and actually targets the lower back instead of just being decorative. Durability: Frame and components feel solid—no wobble or flex after assembly. Rated for 400 lbs, and it absolutely feels like it could handle that without strain. Weight: Despite its heavy-duty rating, it’s surprisingly lightweight when rolling or repositioning thanks to the smooth PU wheels. Custom Fit: Between the 3D headrest, 4D flip-up armrests, and 3-level tilt lock, I was able to dial in the perfect seated position. Great for switching between typing, video calls, and relaxed browsing. Color: The matte black finish with subtle texture gives it a professional and understated look—perfect for a clean setup. Ear/Head Support: The headrest cradles comfortably behind the neck and base of the head, reducing fatigue without forcing posture. Low noise level. ❌ Cons Armrest Adjustments Take Getting Used To: Lots of movement axes, which is great—just not intuitive at first. Assembly Takes Time: While everything is labeled and packed well, it took me a solid 40 minutes with careful attention. 📝 Final Thoughts The CAPOT chair nails what most office chairs miss: true adjustability without feeling gimmicky. If you’re someone who switches between focused work and laid-back browsing, this chair adapts right along with you. It’s now a core part of my productivity setup, and I’d confidently try other CAPOT ergonomic products moving forward.

I would love to give this product 5 stars, as the chair itself is WONDERFUL. Very comfortable, great for back support, and the ability to make micro-adjustments for lumbar support are game changing. After just over 1 year of daily usage for work, the material is still in great shape, very breathable, and comfortable. Unfortunately, the portion of the chair legs where the wheels attach have broken twice within the past 5 months. I reached out to the seller initially, and they graciously provided a replacement leg the first time free of charge, but now the leg has broken a second time in the 2 months since the initial replacement (I did not reach out for a second leg replacement). For context, the chair is rated up to 400 lbs and I am ~250 lbs, so my weight being that far below the limit could be a contributing factor? Either way, I do not think that metal chair legs should not be breaking at the welding point when the user is well under the max weight limit. I have opted to purchase a replacement chair base from another seller as well as a floor mat in hopes that this will remedy the issue. The chair itself is 11/10. The base is 3/10 with regular usage, at least in my experience.

review_title: Good chair. Its not perfect but for the price its excellent.
body_en: So far the chair has been amazing, easy to assemble it took me about 30 mins to build. its comfy, and its wide enough to sit in with extra room. It also has lift arms that you can put up and take them out of the way. This makes it a good purchase.
Excellent achat
Very good products! Highly recommend to buy

review_title: Good chair overall with some improvements
body_en: Overall the product is good! The seat is very comfortable, the neck support is excellent and the arms are great. My only complaint is the lumbar support. It doesnt stay in place so I have to keep rising it every 2 seconds and its quite annoying and its also intense and feels a little uncomfortable even at the correct position. So the overall chair Id rate it a 4/5, the lumbar 2/5.

review_title: Hurts to sit in longer then 10 mins
body_en: Absolutely horribe to sit in longer then 10 mins. The seat is very uncomfy and causes pain. It was easy to built but just absolutely uncomfortable.

I’m not sure what more you can ask for out of a chair at this price. Easy to assemble, looks pretty good, easy to operate, cushion, lumbar, and neck support are all really good and better than I was expecting. I love the foot rest and the ability to set the exact recline with ease. I’m 5’10” 170 lbs and this chair is very comfortable and foot rest is perfect. For larger people this chair may not be perfect, but it would likely get the job done. If you want something that looks fancy, this isn’t your chair. It looks nice and it’s sturdy, but not fancy. All parts are heavy black plastic. Are there better chairs out there. Yep. Do they cost 3x to 10x more? Yep. I’d say you get 90% of the chair for half the price of name brand “budget” gaming chair options. I’d be surprised if anyone who bought this chair didn’t rate it 8 out of 10 or higher.

This chair is a lot nicer than I had anticipated after reading some reviews. It was packed extremely well and the directions and assembly was super simple! They pack all the hardware in an easy access package that's labeled for every step in the assembly process. They also give you the tool, an Allen wrench, that works on each bolt and screw. The chair is well designed and comfortable. The seat is firm and thick! Don't get me wrong, it's not hard by no means. It has great cushion. It's just well built. Should last for years. It's sturdy! It's not a cheap chair. I bought the textile version at an incredible price and that's great marketing because after putting this baby together, I'd have no hesitations about buying another in the faux leather because I now know the quality is really they from this manufacturer. Highly recommend.

review_title: Absolutely worth it! A great deal!
body_en: This chair has been a fantastic purchase! I thought I would have to get a super expensive chair to get the comfort and support I wanted but this one was very reasonably priced and I got it on sale too. It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.) It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat. All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

This is actually a pretty solid chair. Was easy to put together, I’d say it took me about 35-40ish mins to put it together. I like the color, was a bit lighter than I expected tho. The material is very soft and comfortable, I like how it feels and everything. The seat padding is pretty firm, but not uncomfortable, could be a tad softer tho. I might need to break it in more. It reclines well and the leg/foot rest is solid and sturdy. The neck rest pillow works well, but I do wish the lumbar pillow was a tad thicker and actually strapped to the chair. My only gripe is the left arm rest wiggles a bit, that’s it. Over all happy with my purchase, would get again in a different color just to have or would give one as a gift.

Really happy with this gaming chair. The lumbar and neck support are fantastic—I can sit for hours working and gaming without my back aching. The build quality feels very solid and sturdy. I also really like the fabric; it’s soft, breathable, and much more comfortable than leather/PU leather, especially for long sessions. Definitely recommend it!

review_title: Very Comfy and Holding Up Great
body_en: I ordered this chair on August 6th, and after a little over two weeks of regular use, I absolutely love it. It is much more comfortable than my previous chair, which I had been using for years, and I can sit in it for long periods without feeling uncomfortable. I also haven't noticed any degradation in the cushioning, materials, or overall comfort so far, which is a great sign. The only downside I had was the assembly. There wasn't really a clear manual included with the chair, so figuring out exactly how everything was supposed to go together was a little confusing. I had to rely on YouTube videos to figure out some of the assembly, and finding a useful video was a bit of a hassle. Once I figured everything out though, the chair went together fine. Overall, I am very happy with the chair. It has been a major comfort upgrade from my previous chair and after a little over two weeks of use, it still feels just as good as when I first put it together.

review_title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
body_en: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. review_title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Excellent ergonomic and very comfortable chair
body_en: I bought this TRALT chair to work several hours a day at the computer, and it has exceeded my expectations. The adjustable headrest helps maintain a comfortable neck posture, while the fold-down armrests are very practical when I need to save space. The chair feels sturdy and stable, even with extended use. The seat is wide, padded, and comfortable, and the casters glide smoothly. Assembly was also easy thanks to the included instructions. Overall, it's an excellent option for its value. I recommend it for those who work from home, study, or spend many hours sitting at a desk. 👍🏻💺✨

* Comfortable for long sitting sessions – Many reviewers say the mesh back and thick seat cushion remain comfortable during 6–10 hour workdays. * Easy assembly – putting it together in about 20–30 minutes using the included tools. * Good lumbar support – The ergonomic back design is frequently mentioned as helping reduce lower-back fatigue. * Excellent value for the price – Buyers often compare it favorably with chairs costing significantly more. * Sturdy construction – Users appreciate the metal base, smooth-rolling casters, and solid feel, especially considering the budget price. * Breathable mesh back – Helps keep users cooler than fully padded chairs during extended use. * Adjustability – The height adjustment, recline, and armrests are commonly cited as making it easier to find a comfortable position.

review_title: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
body_en: I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended. Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame). The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for). While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down. Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes. Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

review_title: Decent chair but not for us taller people
body_en: I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with. For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive. After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected. The good: 1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal. 2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems. 3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me. 4. Appearance. Very nice. 5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy. The not so good. 1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

My feet hit the floor, it has a pillow that sits under my neck, back support and even the foot rest. I love that it reclines as well and impressed with how well it came together. I’m very excited to bring to work and finally be comfortable! Price: I got this on sale for 109$. It’s normally 129$ but 20$ shipping. I wish it would stay at 99$ all around since the shipping isn’t free. It was a super heavy package though so I get it. Style: I got all black so it blends in at work and it’s as pictured. I wish the logo wasn’t so big and bright for those who don’t use this as a gaming chair but I may use a black sharpie & color it to make this more discreet. Size: If you are on the shorter side, this is a great chair. Great for kids obviously and tinier adults. Not sure this is a heavy duty chair for the regular sized adult so keep in mind. Delivery: said it would take a week but came next day which was impressive and I was very happy with that. Arrives in great condition. Setup: the directions are so so. My husband put this together and it took wayyyyy longer than it should have because some of the directions were mislabeled. Screws numbers were added that weren’t needed for this chair and some of the images were so tiny you couldn’t see much. For some reason we had the biggest issue with the footrest. We had to do it like 3xs b/c we couldn’t tell from the image how it actually sat. Got it done none the less and worth the struggle. Bottom line: worth the buy and seems good quality for the price but I’ll see how it hold up when I bring it to the office for actual use.

review_title: Sturdy, very cute, easy to put together!
body_en: I didn't expect much for how much it cost. I thought it would be okay, but knew I couldn't afford a super fancy chair, so didn't my hopes up. It's actually a fantastic chair! I'll start with the TINIEST gripe. It was filthy. GROSS. I had to get a magic eraser to get the grime off of it, grease and stuff from the factory. But it's a gorgeous pink and white chair, feels so sturdy and comfortable. Great support for your back, and that's even without the lumbar pillow that comes with it. I will say, the instructions were clearly written by ChatGPT. Awful. But the pictures were just fine, so it was actually easy to put together, haha. So don't fret if you read it and it's confusing. The diagrams are accurate and easy to read. It also didn't take long at all to put together. OH! I personally didn't want rollers, as I have a pup and didn't want to squish toes. So I bought office chair gliders to replace the wheels (which are beautiful, sadly, would've loved to use them) and they fit just fine! So if you're like me and wanted to change them, they're compatible. But the wheels are super cute. :) Honestly so pleased with this chair. I am very happy with it, and look forward to using it while I work and draw and game for a long time to come.

Packaged very professionally, Easy instructions to follow, and most importantly super comfortable for whatever your needs are, Gaming, working, editing, etc. Highly recommend this chair fit my set up great, looks fantastic, very adjustable and definitely a bang for your buck chair. It feels very stable as well definitely not falling over or going to fall apart!

review_title: DO NOT BUY - ITS NOT AS IT IS ADVERTISED.
body_en: We purchased this chair because it is advertised to be a gaming chair for an adult up to 400 pounds. Weighing in at 235, we figured it would be comfortable to use. IT IS HORRIBLE! Very uncomfortable. Looks pretty but it is made for a teenager, not an adult. DO NOT BUY IT! THE RETURN POLICY IS A JOKE! They want you to return it in its original packaging with no tags removed or it be used - or they can charge you up to 100% of the cost. I guess you have to decide before assembly if it will fit or be comfortable. I should have ordered a workable crystal ball. You have to buy a big box to ship it back in and you have to pay shipping. Do you know what it costs to ship something this size? We would wind up owing money instead of getting a refund. DO NOT BUY THIS FOR AN ADULT. IT IS HORRIBLE. --- There, now I am happy. I may not get my money back, but I hope this will save others from buying this falsely advertised item.
Great chair! I weigh 270 lbs and this thing is holding up. The arms come loose and the foot stool is way too short and flimsy to be effective.

review_title: Good quality chair for the price!

This might be a decent chair, but it is nowhere near worth $200 if I didn’t wanna go through the hassle of having to disassemble everything for the return I would

review_title: Just okay. Wouldnt buy again, but not upset with it

The assembly wasnt too complicated but the instructions were extremely hard to follow (the instructions showed very tiny pictures that were hard to see, and the written instructions only said to fasten the screws down, no actual worded instructions on how to assemble it). The locking mechanism for the leaning is different from any chair and kinda awkward to use because it goes so far down that you have to reallllyyy lean sideways to unlock it and re-lock it, which makes it awkward to lean back or forward to adjust it. The footrest is garbage because it goes straight out but not far enough, making it so your feet dont actually rest on it but rather your lower calves do (or if you do out your feet on it youll be in an awkward squat position) and its held with extremely thin aluminum rods run through plastic screwed into the bottom which means the footrest has give and feels like itll bend or break easily from putting any substancial weight on it. I also had a shipping delay of 5 days after it was supposed to take over a week anyways, which was an inconvenience. Its not necessarily a bad chair, especially if youre a shorter persom who can use the footrest comfortably. review_title: A good chair for your money
body_en: Took a while to put together, but it was worth it. It’s a very comfortable chair and as advertised it seems to be exceptional quality so far very pleased.

This office chair looked nice in the listing photos, but it’s even better in person. I ordered this for my home office space which previously had an armchair that my kids broke by tipping in it. I love the light gray color of this one, since my desk is gray wood, and I love that it is a leather-type material that can be wiped down, since I have messy kids. It has a nice, stylish sleek look to it that elevates my office space. The chair was easy to assemble, but it does come with some assembly needed. It took about a half hour to get it assembled. My twelve year old did it though, so it might take an experienced adult less time. The chair is just as comfortable as you would hope for it to be. It has decent cushioning, and the lumbar pump works impressively well. The material is soft and doesn’t stick to your skin or make noise when you move. This chair is adjustable in height. For reference, I am 5’6”, and at max height my heels are about 3” off the ground. In the middle setting, my heels just touch the ground, with a couple more inches to drop. As far as width, I would say it’s standard for a full-sized office chair. I am about average in size, but I do think it’s more accommodating for larger adults than many others, due to the fact that the sides are mostly open, and the arms easily lift up. It’s also a pretty deep seat bottom and tall seat back. The build is also very sturdy. I couldn’t ask for a better office chair. I’m super happy with the overall quality, features, and design of this chair. I can’t imagine that it would disappoint anyone who bought it.

review_title: Comfortable adjustable-lumbar chair, kind of annoying to assemble
body_en: I don't have much experience putting furniture together. This was probably the most challenging piece I've assembled so far. The two armrests were by far the hardest part. Start to finish, it took me about an hour to put the thing together. First, the instruction manual also has a typo worth knowing about. One step lists screw (11) as M6 x 25 mm, while the parts legend and the screw bag both show M6 x 30 mm. This happened right in the middle of the hardest part. I spent a while convinced I had the wrong screws before realizing it was just an error in the booklet. At least the parts are labeled, with FRONT printed on the seat plate, so orientation wasn't a guess. Still, the typo cost me a lot of wasted time. Not worth deducting a star in the review, but a real annoyance. Once it's together, though, the chair is really comfortable. I like office chairs with soft arm support. These armrests stay comfortable through long stretches of sitting. The headrest pillow is a nice touch and gives good support when I lean back. My favorite feature is the inflatable lumbar support. With a pronounced lower back curve, I find pumping up the lumbar makes a real difference. A separate back cushion isn't something I've needed. The faux leather feels pleasant to the touch. There wasn't any chemical smell when I started using it. Because it's a leather-style surface, it breathes less than a mesh chair. Where I live it gets hot and humid, so that's definitely a tradeoff. Anyone who sweats a lot might want a different material. The wheels roll smoothly across wood floors without sticking or catching. Moving it around my workspace is pretty easy. Overall, the assembly could be smoother or better documented, but the comfort, the adjustable lumbar, and how easily it rolls make this a solid office chair... once it's put together.

The Mr. Picky I live with is loving this chair after rejecting many others. It is super comfortable and looks and feels like quality furniture. It is high enough to support his frame of six feet and support his neck which was a problem with other chairs we tried. It was very easy to put together and only took me 40 minutes. I just have a few notes to make it easier for you. There is a QR code to scan for a video or the chair comes with an instruction booklet in the bag with the seat of the chair. I showed in a picture that you may have to move the arm piece a little to see all four holes that will attach the arm to the back and seat cushions. The instructions talk about 25 and 30 mm screws in the instructions book where you attach the arm but there are only 30 mm screws included and only these are needed. One tip not mentioned is you need to lean the back piece on something like the box to make it easy to attach the arm and then the seat cushion also to the arm. These are all minor and I hope will save you time when you put together this chair. I think it is well worth the cost (and even more) and it is so comfortable to sit on. The wheels were able to easily glide on my low pile carpet. It is an added bonus that the arms lift up to push the chair closer to your desk if needed. It looks good in any office or even a living room.
Nice quality. A bit stiff, but comfortable

This office chair is very comfortable and easy to adjust for all-day use. review_title: My first gaming chair. Very pleased
body_en: Pretty comfortable chair. I am 6’2” and I weigh around 260lb and I have plenty of room to sit comfortably with room to spare. I game for hours at a time in it and it stays comfortable throughout and I have actually fallen asleep in it. Is not at all prone to tipping and I have tested this. Was also pretty straight forward to put together. Took less than an hour. Very pleased with it.

Woooohooo! I have been looking for months for an office chair that matched my brand colors. This chair was easy to put together. I love that the arm rests move as I recline. The stitched design on the top is noticeably crooked. Thankfully the head rest pillow covers that. I was looking for a chair that would support my mom's weight when she comes to visit. It says it supports 400 lbs. She is closer to 300. However, the seat is not very cushioned. It's not hard plastic, but not comparable to memory foam either. I need this chair to use for creating content videos, crafting, and other office tasks. It will serve its purpose and didn't cost too much. For someone on a very strict budget, I am happy with it., but I'm curious how I will feel after sitting there, on and off for 8+ hours crafting, recording, doing LIVEs and editing. The unknown is the reason for rating it a 4 instead of 5. Also, it arrived a day early, love that.

review_title: Comfortable and Good for the Price
body_en: Assembly was a little difficult and took some time, but once set up, the chair is comfortable and works well. For the price, it’s a good value overall.

I’ve ownedI’ve used a lot of office chairs, but this is easily the most comfortable one I’ve had. Highly impressed with this chair! It's very comfortable for long hours of sitting, and the breathable mesh is a great feature. The adjustable headrest and back support work perfectly. Great build quality for the price—definitely a fantastic value for money. Highly recommend!

review_title: Great Lumbar Support for Long Work Days but that’s about it…
body_en: What I immediately noticed with this chair was the lower back support. It actually supports the lumbar area well enough where I don’t feel like I need to add an extra pillow behind me, which is a huge plus since I sit for long periods working from home. The chair was also pretty easy to assemble and the overall structure feels sturdy once put together. The adjustable headrest and reclining feature are nice touches, and the chair rolls smoothly without any issues. The only reason I’m giving it 2 smis because the the chair has a permanent tilt to the front and so sitting in it, I don’t feel balanced, there no lever for me to recline like most chairs and the material could feel a little more premium, especially on the seat cushion. It’s not terrible by any means, just not as high-end feeling.

review_title: Great mesh back, wish the seat matched it
body_en: Comfortable chair overall. The mesh backrest is the standout part, it holds up well and actually breathes, so my back doesn't get hot and sweaty during long sessions at the desk. Adjustments for height and the headrest are easy to dial in too. My one gripe is the seat itself. It's a memory foam cushion rather than the same mesh material as the back, and it's noticeably harder and doesn't breathe the way the backrest does. I wish they'd carried the netting material through to the seat, since that's really the part that matters most for all-day comfort. As it stands, the back is great and the seat could use some work.
This is such a great product initially I didn’t realize it’s so comfortable. It’s also very easy to install with a great prize. Definitely worth a try.

I like this chair. Size and style match the product description/images. Assembly really went pretty well. Everything lined up well and screws went in without too much trouble. It's a little bit of a hassle to put the seat cushion on, but there's enough slack in the assembly (before snuggling it down) to let you get both sides lined up. Size feels good to me, and I like the adjustability of the product. You do have a overall height adjuatment for the seat to the ground. The lumbar support can also be adjusted up and down a bit. At first I thought it looked really odd - like it stuck out way too far - but after sitting in it for quite a while I really think it is comfortable. You can also move the headrest up and down to position it right where you want. One potential downside is that the armrests are at a fixed height - which happens to be just right for myself - but that can be lifted up and out of the way if they interfere with your desk. There's also a locking mechanism to keep the chair fixed upright or allow it to tilt. The force needed to tilt can be adjusted via a large tension handle underneath, but I found it just right out of the box. As far as comfort - the material is made of a mesh like fabric, which breaths really well, but it that material on the armrests does feel a little rough on the forearms near my elbows, but only just barely. The seat cushion is very comfortable, and overall, I think the chair is really very comfortable to sit in for long periods of time.

I would definitely recommend this chair.

review_title: Ok quality- small, almost child sized

Now, I am 5’1 and a smaller built person (not to be a pick me, this is just for the sake of the review) but I would’ve been a little more let down if I was any taller or had a wider bottom and would probably return it. The quality of this is okay but has good attributes like the leg rest and the reclining feature. I wouldn’t call the pull out part under the chair a foot rest by any means bc I would have to fold up my legs a little to get my feet on there. I know that gaming chairs get a little pricey but I would’ve at least liked a bigger chair for the cost. If you’re someone who is taller or is looking for good support or a sturdy chair I probably wouldn’t pick this one with longevity and comfortableness in mind. The arm rests are a little loose, even with a good tightening. I wouldn’t trust this chair when it’s reclined if I was heavier. The back rest is also not very tall and the overall height of the chair itself is shorter than most run of the mill gaming chairs. I tried to include as many measurements as possible. I’m going to be spending a lot of time in this chair so if anything goes awry or I think something is worth mentioning I will update with review (if I can figure out how). This is good for kids or small-statured people in general. The value for the coin is ehh. For the average adult… probably not… spend your money on something better.

I love the mesh back, as it has some softness, give, and breathability. The head and back support are a little hard, but they probably need a bit of wear to break in well. The chair was easy to put together. With an allen ratchet it took me about 25 minutes. This is not my first chair to assemble, so a first timer with the tools provided might take an hour or so. Not an issue for me, but that is a possibility I guess. Recommended if you want the gaming chair look and can spend a bit more than a budget chair.
