review_title: Exceptional all-day comfort and premium build quality at an affordable price
body_en: After more than 45 years of purchasing office chairs and office furniture, I can confidently say this is one of the finest office chairs I've ever owned. It delivers exceptional comfort, outstanding build quality, and remarkable value for the price. The chair is solidly constructed and feels extremely durable. The lumbar support is excellent, providing the right amount of support without feeling intrusive. The seat cushion strikes an ideal balance between firmness and softness, using a high-quality, resilient foam that remains supportive even after extended use. I spend between 8 and 12 hours a day in this chair, and it remains consistently comfortable from morning to evening. One feature I particularly appreciate is that the backrest stays exactly where I set it and doesn't gradually recline or rock. The height adjustable armrests are another standout feature. They offer excellent support and can be lowered enough to slide comfortably beneath my desk, preventing any interference while I work. The reclining function and retractable footrest are thoughtful additions. While I don't typically use my office chair as a recliner, it's a feature I'm glad to have available when needed. It's one of those extras that you may not use every day, but you'll appreciate having when the occasion arises. Assembly was straightforward, thanks to the clear, well-written instructions. From opening the box to sitting in the finished chair, the entire process took approximately 38 minutes. Overall, this chair has exceeded my expectations in every respect. It's comfortable enough for all-day use, exceptionally well built, and offers features and quality typically found in much more expensive office chairs. I would not hesitate to recommend it to anyone looking for a premium office chair at an excellent value.

review_title: Great chair; very comfortable and worth the purchase.
body_en: What I have learned from many years of purchasing and putting together chairs like this is it's always best to buy a chair upon which the arms are separate from the body of the chair. There are many chairs on the market that are put together such that the entire support of the chair rests on the arms connecting the bottom of the chair to the body of the chair. That is way too much pressure on the screws that hold the arms on. This chair is not like that. You can actually put this chair together WITHOUT the arms and the chair will function properly. First, the parts of the chair were packaged very nicely. Everything was wrapped separately inside the box to protect against damaging the soft fabric of the two parts of the chair (back and bottom). Very easy to put together - intuitive and the directions were better than many I've seen. When you apply the arms, there is "give" in the application point of about an inch where you can tighten the arms closer to the body or farther away from the body giving yourself more space. I chose to tighten the screws farther away from the body so I can sit cross legged. When you apply the back of the chair to the bottom, there is the same "give" in the application point of about an inch where you can give yourself a "deeper" seat or a "shallower" seat. I chose to tighten the screws farther away from the seat so I can sit cross legged. The arms of the chair will adjust higher - which I use while I am on conference calls to appear more "relaxed". When I want to pull my chair closer to the desk, I can adjust the arms down and they slide under the desk perfectly. The leg rest slides out pretty far - I'm surprised how far this goes - and you can slide further away or closer to you depending upon if you want to extend your legs straight out or cross them. When not in use, it slides neatly back under the seat. I do not personally like to use a recline feature on an office chair. To me, it's asking too much of a moderately priced chair to perform that function (even if advertised as a main feature). That is not what an office chair is for - and I feel it's just going to wear certain points out faster than necessary. If I want to recline or relax, I go the couch or bed. Instructions for the recline feature on this chair is included but I did not try it. I believe there is also a "rock" feature. Again, I'm not going to use my office chair as a rocker. I am pleasantly surprised the back of the chair is just higher than the top of my head. I'm tall (5'9") and I am usually disappointed in the height of chairs. This chair does not have an adjustable head rest but it's just the perfect height for me. From the looks of the chair in the pictures, it really looked like it would be "huge" and just a bit "too much" and I would be swallowed up by it. It's just the perfect size. Not too big that it takes up too much space around my desk but big enough that I feel the chair hugging around me. I think this is going to really help my posture too because my old chair was so uncomfortable that I found myself always sitting on the edge of it like I was trying to get away from it (LOL) and this chair encourages me to actually sit back and relax into it. I purchased the beige chair because it was one of the three colors that was going to arrive quickly. I didn't want black again and I'm not brave enough for white. The beige is a beautiful color. Very calming. I am very pleased with my purchase and hope the seat holds up. Obviously the seat is the first thing to wear out on a chair no matter the size of the person using it. The back of this chair is so comfy though I hope if the seat does wear out quickly, a cushion will help because this chair is a dream.

review_title: Excellent and Comfortable (and BIG) Office Chair
body_en: A very large and very comfortable office chair. This is a review for the EXCEBET Big and Tall Office Chair in light grey color. I am 5'10" and 215 lb., and I would not want an office chair that is any bigger than this one. It is super easy to put together, and there are videos to show you how. The material is PU leather which is a kind of faux leather - but it's very soft, and pleasing to the touch. See pictures. I included a picture of the EXCEBET chair along side a normal sized office chair so you can clearly see the difference in form factor. Side-by-side, the regular office chair looks kind of puny. I think even Bigfoot would be pleased to sit all day in this EXCEBET chair. The reclining option is also very nice, but I should mention that it is not the same experience as a recliner sofa. The footrest is somewhat narrow, so you have to keep your legs together when reclining. Overall, I highly recommend this chair. It's not really expensive for all the value that is provided. I hope it lasts at least 5 years, which is the typical service life for an everyday-use office chair.

Ok first of all I should explain my quirks. I'm very fidgety and fussy. Cant help it it's just the way I am. This chair isvery well built and directions were very plain and clear. No problem putting this together about 1/2 hour. I like almost everything about this chair. It's comfortable execpt for me the back is a little to upright.I would like it to lean back a little more. But being able to set the back to lean back is good but a little too stiff to hold it in this position. Now I may be missing something but thats just how I feel.I also like the leg rest it works well and feels solid. But I'm happy with the solid build and it dosnt pop and make all kinds of noises. Because of my fidgity nature my wife would be after me for moving so much if it squeked or popped like the last new chair I bought.

For reference I'm 6'2 and 275lbs (~125kg). I work in an office 5 days a week, 9am to 5pm so I needed something that would at least let me be comfortable while I type my life away. Assembly was fairly easy, just make sure that when you get to the part where you have to put the back rest and the seat together that you actually keep the 4 screws that attach to the back rest loose so that it will fit into the slot of the seat. In terms of cushion I'd give it a solid 7.5 maybe 8 out of ten. It's not a recliner couch you have at home, but for an office chair at this price it's pretty dang close. It's definitely enough to make you start dozing off if you're not too careful. The main reason why I went for this one though was for the leg rest. Kinda have to get used to it to find the sweet spot because if you're fully upright and you try to use the leg rest the chair will lean forward a lot due to how it's built, it's not the most sturdy thing in the world so you gotta balance it out by reclining a bit. For a big and tall chair the leg rest isn't as big or wide as I would hope for it to be, I find myself really squeezing myself to try and fit both of them on and end up just crossing my legs most of the time, but it's still comfortable. I'd give it a 7/10. In terms of back support and the firmness of it, I haven't had issues with it or my posture, but for those that slouch, do be careful as it's not built fix or support poor posture. I'd give it a 6/10, but in my opinion this shouldn't take away from the overall score since that's not really what these are for, if you want ergonomics and good lumbar support you go for chairs designed for that. If you want casual comfort at the workplace and you're able to get up and walk around a lot then this is fine as it's not killing your spine as long as you're not fully set into it all day without breaks. Overall for the price I would highly recommend it. There are a few other chairs I'm looking at that's more expensive than this that'll surely beat it, but for fast delivery and pretty dang good comfort for a big fella, would definitely recommend.

review_title: Doesn't Have Advertised Features (ex. Rocking) & Support Doesn't Honor Free Replacements Advertised
body_en: UPDATE 5: The seller responded and AGAIN refused to honor their advertised free gas cylinder replacement, even though the original they provided failed within 3 months. Their excuse was that we were past the return window. The problem with that excuse is that we contacted them well within that window with a replacement request, and they repeatedly pretended not to understand the request, then to reject it. So they're stalling customers until they can say you aren't eligible for anything anymore. Also, if you read reviews, you'll notice a "warranty department" is mentioned, and that's who supposedly sends out the replacement parts they advertised. This apparently doesn't exist. Strongly suspect there might be some fake reviews in here given the way the company uses false advertisements and a complete lack of support. Will be reporting them to Amazon today. You should note, they seem to have removed the image that offered the free wheel replacements (though I believe I still have a screenshot for that report I'll file). But they do still mention free gas cylinder replacements in the original is too high (which is what I originally requested). I've now had to spend more money on replacement wheels because the seller lied about offering free replacements (the rubber ones safe for hardwood floors). And now I'll have to buy another cylinder for it. 100% not letting this go. I'm so tired of companies selling furniture items here with false advertising, knowing it's too difficult for most customers to return those items. UPDATE 4: Exactly 3 months from the day we ordered this chair, and after refusing to honor their advertised offer for a lower replacement cylinder, the original gas cylinder for this chair failed. No one using it uses it roughly. No one using it even comes close to the advertised weight limit. It was just being used in a stable position and suddenly failed. We reset it, and it failed again within minutes, making the chair unusable for us. I'm going to contact the seller one more time and insist on a replacement cylinder given they outright advertise they provide one, but if they refuse again, I'll be taking it up with Amazon, because this combination of quality issues and poor support is not acceptable. UPDATE 3: I definitely cannot recommend this chair. After weeks of use (with the wrong wheels and gas cylinder size because the company refused to honor their offer to send replacements), this chair causes a lot of pain. Lower back pain in particular is really bad. I suspect it's due to the combination of the very hard seat (disappointing given I looked for a spring-based seat intentionally -- if they're there, they're too small to be of any use as you still feel like you're sitting on a hard board) and the lack of lumbar support. Despite their description, there is basically NO lumbar support with this chair. It's incredibly painful even after minor use. I may even have to go back to the old chair this was replacing as the entire point was to reduce pain and increase comfort, of which this chair does neither. It's poorly made. It feels very unbalanced if you lean at all (especially with the lack of proper tension to prevent you falling backwards all the way). Way too many cracking and creaking sounds for a chair this new being used well below its advertised weight limit. Not supported at all by the seller (other than offering minor refunds to keep the junk and figure out how to dispose of it yourself at a loss). Just overall feels unsafe, uncomfortable, and I can't trust either the chair or the seller. UPDATE 2: After several back-and-forth messages with the seller here on Amazon, they've repeatedly ignored requests for the free replacement wheels (needed if you use it on hardwood floors) and the free replacement gas cylinder (if the original is too high) that are advertised on this page in the product images. After ignoring the request repeatedly, along with any tips on getting the tension to actually provide... tension... they flat out refused to honor their advertised offer for those replacement parts. All they did was offer a very small refund if we're willing to keep the chair... without the wheels needed for our floors... without the appropriately-sized canister... and without any reasonable tension function to lean back safely (forget "rocking" as noted in the description because this chair can't do that). It would cost us more to buy our own wheels and canister than what they offered, and that still doesn't address the false advertising of this being a rocking office chair or the unsafe lack of tension for the recline function. I would absolutely never do business with this company again, and we'll be contacting Amazon to see what can be done about them refusing to honor what they advertised. Extremely disappointed after a very long search for a replacement chair. UPDATE: This page, in the images, says the company will provide free replacement rubber casters / wheels if needed (which you need for hard floors), and a free lower replacement gas cylinder if the chair is too high (which it is for my wife). After asking them to send these multiple times via Amazon's messaging system, they've so far refused to do so (will update if they sort this out soon). They've also responded to questions about fixing the lack of tension and the misrepresentation about this being a "rocking" chair (it's definitely not; just reclining), and all we ever seem to get is a copy/paste response offering a small partial refund if we agree to keep the chair. We keep trying to tell them we're hoping to keep the chair, but we needed info on getting the tension to increase and we need the replacement parts they offered to make it work. But they've mostly ignored specific questions and just keep saying the same things. Until the last message where they said they couldn't send replacements for the "missing parts," even though we never said anything was missing. We're just requesting the parts they offer to send right in their Amazon description. Not happy with support at all so far. -- ORIGINAL REVIEW I have mixed feelings on this chair. First, it feels like a sturdy build. And if you're on the larger side, the cushion offers plenty of support -- firm, but mostly comfortable. The exception to the seat's comfort is that the front edge is very firm, and it can cut into the back of your thighs, negatively impacting circulation. This was the problem with my old chair and why I was replacing it. Normally I prefer a higher chair, but this is causing issues even at its lowest setting. The seller does mention in the images they'll send a lower cylinder if necessary, so if I keep the chair and receive that, I'll update on how that affects the pain at the front of the seat. The seller also offers to send replacement wheels if you need the rollerblade-style kind for hard floors. The plastic ones are extremely loud and totally inappropriate for hard floors and their protective mats, so it's nice they provide this option. But if you know you'll need them, I'd request them early. Otherwise you won't be able to fully assemble things until they arrive, or you'll have to risk damage to your floors using the defaults until the replacements can be swapped in. While I like the sturdy sense I get from the chair, there are two big problems for me. I've contacted the seller hoping I'm just not figuring out the settings properly, but I'll update if appropriate later. 1. The description advertises this as a "rocking" office chair. With office chairs, that means something very specific -- the back and seat move in unison in a true rocking action. This looks like the seat can angle back a bit based on the video, but it doesn't seem to do that when "rocking." All it does is lean the top back. That's not a rocking office chair, which was an absolute requirement in me choosing this as a replacement for my old chair. Again, I'm hoping I just missed a control or something and that this will work as-advertised. Oddly though, when the foot rest is out, the seat itself does seem to recline back, so it clearly *can.* It just won't rock otherwise? And if you have heavier legs, or longer ones like I do, the leg rest isn't really usable because your center of gravity will get thrown off (and that's the one thing that doesn't seem sturdy in general). So, for a chair advertised for bigger users, are we simply not "allowed" to use the rocking function because it's tied to the leg rest?? 2. I'm also having issues with the tension knob. All the way in one direction and the back of the chair practically falls backwards the moment you touch it. All the way in the other direction and there's barely any more tension that that. It leads to a very insecure feeling unless you lock the "rocking" function, which again was a major deciding factor in choosing this chair. I'm hoping I'm missing something here too because I've never seen an office chair with this lack of tension. Other than that, the back is comfortable, and I like that the arms are adjustable (width during installation, and height while in-use). Aside from the rocking and tension, two things would make this chair near-perfect though: 1. Adjustable lumbar support. Fixed lumbar support is all but useless in an executive chair because if you're sitting properly you're not going to be leaning back all the time. Proper lumbar support doesn't require you to recline back. It should help you stay upright and maintain your posture. 2. I agree with another reviewer who was disappointed in the lack of head rest. For all the padding on the back of this chair (which is soft, yet dense enough it feels like it will hold up for quite a while), there's no real head rest. The head area is relatively flat and sits too far back, so your head won't even touch it unless you're lying back in more of a reclined position. The only other comment I'll make for now is that any reclining is pretty loud. There's a surprising amount of squeaking and creaking for a new chair. If I keep it, I might see if something needs to be greased. But if not, just know that could be an issue if that sort of noise bothers you. Oh, and like another reviewer, my box also arrived quite damaged. The entire bottom was split open. At first we were afraid we received a used chair after ordering a new one, but the internal pieces seemed OK and everything was there. But if multiple people are receiving damaged, open boxes, I'd make sure you have somewhere sheltered for this to be delivered. Had this been left by our garage in the rain (as many larger packages are here), the chair would have been ruined before we even opened it.

review_title: Great Chair...bit of a read, but good info maybe...
body_en: This is a bit long, but maybe will help someone. The chair is great. I have been looking for a chair for several months, and finally settled on this one. My only hang-up was that I really wanted genuine leather, which this chair is not. The chairs with genuine leather are either (a) priced well over $1k, or (b) are cheap junk. This chair replaces my old, genuine leather chair, that was less than 3 years old. Unfortunately, it fell into the "cheap junk" category, as I came to find out. I had ordered that chair, just based on the leather...and in fact that is the ONLY part of the chair that held up. I replaced the base when it broke, replaced the hydraulic lift when it broke, and had to re-work the arm rests so they would stop falling off. The sides and back were also deteriorating...so quite literally, the ONLY "good" part of that chair was the actual leather itself. So, apologies for the back story, but that leads me into the review of this chair. In putting it together, I could easily see that this chair is hands down much more well-made than my old one. The base of the old one appeared to be a cast metal or some kind. Problem with cast metals are that they tend to be brittle...which is exactly what happened to me…one of the legs broke off with no warning. This chair's base is welded steel...I'm pretty confident it's not going anywhere. Second is the comfort. Lesson learned from the old chair is that if it appears to be thin padding, it definitely is. After a year or so, I had to add more fill to the old chair to keep it from being so "flat.” It was filled with some sort of cubed foam. This chair has the spring-cushion seat, and bolstered back with lumbar support. It is very comfortable, and the padding is 2, maybe 3 times thicker than the old chair. While the covering of this chair is not genuine leather, it does have a very good feel, looks to be of high quality, and is breathable - which would have been my biggest complaint had it not been. The arm rests are generous in size, and fit comfortably under the desk without hitting. I probably could have done without the footrest, but suppose it may be nice to have at some point. The tilt features work very well...plenty of firm resistance, but not so much to force you up straight, or be horizontal with a simple lean back...the tension is just right. Putting the chair together was easy...took me maybe 30 minutes, and half of that was easily spent just unpacking all the parts, as they were well protected in the box. I would agree with what some others have said about needing a second set of hands with getting the back on. I managed okay, just me, but probably should have had my wife come help...but you know, men can do it all on their own... So, all in all, I'm very happy with this chair, thus far. Hopefully it will withstand the test of time...if I can even get three years out of it, that's okay...I feel a lot better about getting a $2-300 chair every 3 years, than I do about spending $700+ each time. Some photos for reference...you can see how thick the padding is, compared to the other chair.

I wish I could fully express how long and hard I was searching for what I'd begun to call my "Goldilocks chair." I had incredibly specific things I was looking for: - a padded seat (I work and game at the same desk, so I spend the majority of my day in my chair) that was wide enough for me (a 5'7", plus-sized woman) to sit cross-legged - padded armrests (surprisingly difficult to find) that wouldn't get in the way - or could be moved out of the way - if I did sit cross-legged - a back that would recline (not rock, which was sometimes hard to differentiate in product descriptions) - my white whale: a footrest to prop my legs up on for crochet and reading I ordered a possibly insane number of chairs only to return them (and for some of them, eat the cost in my depseration); I tried finding search points I could compromise on (especially that footrest - I'd all but resigned to get a tiny ottomon for my itty-bitty space under the desk); I took to Reddit forums and talked to friends, family, coworkers, family's coworkers; I gave up and continued on sitting in my old gaming chair that was quite literally falling apart several times, only to resume the search when I had the emotional fortitude to do so. This chair was like a God-send. It fulfills *every* *single* *one* of my criteria. The back, seat, and arms are plush, but supportive and (after wearing it in a little) incredibly soft and comfortable without feeling like it's going to go flat on you. After lifting the armrests high enough I'm able to cross my legs without pressing against them at all. The reclining feature is exactly what I needed (though for my purposes, I mostly just need the recliner to lock at a preferred angle for day-to-day use; the seat does tilt back some when you recline, which can be annoying, but *how* annoying depends primarily on *why* you're reclining, and whether or not you have room under your desk for your footrest to be a little higher than usual.) The back is tall enough for me to rest my head against with no issues. The footrest can be fully extended or pressed against the seat as an extra cushion for when my legs don't want to cross quite as tightly as usual (or it can be used as a tiny platform for my yarn ball!) And the pale purple and design on the cushion are pretty! At the time it felt like a gamble; I'd been burned so many times. But when this came in and my husband put it together it fit me like a glove. Everyone has different needs, so I don't know if this will meet yours or not, but I couldn't be happier.
Extremely comfortable and good quality

review_title: Comfortable, stylish, and great value for the price!
body_en: I’ve had this chair for a few days now, and I’m really impressed with how much comfort and quality you get for the price. The setup was easily understood based on the instructions & it took me about 20–30 minutes. Once assembled, it looks sleek and felt sturdy. The functionality is great for a basic gaming / office chair & it is very easy to move around unlike others that you have to drag with you. The lumbar support & adjustable recline are perfect for long work or gaming sessions. The padding is firm but not too stiff, and the armrests sit at a good height. I use it daily in my office for video editing & gaming, and it’s made a big difference in my posture & comfort. Overall, this is a solid, budget-friendly chair that doesn’t feel cheap. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a stylish, ergonomic upgrade without breaking the bank.

review_title: Its much better than nothing and much cheaper than higher quality chairs
body_en: I'm a big believer in "you get what you pay for" and I usually advise to save up, make one purchase, make one investment and don't worry about it for a few years. But something about this chair's value really scales, especially if you can grab it on sale. I got mine in white for $75 including tax and shipping. Many quality gaming chairs cost hundreds of dollars. There a handful of cheap office chairs you can snag for $60. This chair compared to one of those generic office chair is worth the extra $15. If you're looking at this chair for $90 or higher, then the former statement is true (save up). Anyway. I've had this chair for a day now and it isn't perfect. I'll go over what I like and what I don't like. Appearance: It looks nice. Doesn't look or feel too cheap. The base is metal with plastic feet. Many chairs have plastic base with plastic feet.+1pt Functionality: This chair has a handful of features-- You can adjust the height. +1pt But it only has about a 3in range -1pt It has a lock to let you remain upright and can be unlocked so you can recline back. +1pt It does NOT have a way to lock in the reclined position. -1pt Comfort: This chair is pretty comfy. It has a removable/adjustable head pillow and a removable/adjustable lumbar pillow as well. +1pt It is a little stiff. Some people may like that. It also may break it after a while. I've only had it one day so I will update if something new develops. The chair has a *mostly* comfortable width to me. It measures 19" for arm to arm. But it has this little "cushion" that tries to contour your legs that makes it a little uncomfortable to sit with my legs spread even a little. I have to keep my knees closer together than I normally would to keep the "cushion" from digging into the side of my legs. Because of this, there is really only about 16" of room for your butt or the sides of your thighs. I'm about 5'10" Male 215lbs size 38 pants XL shirt. I think I am at the cusp of being able to comfortably sit in this. It was not made with larger people in mind. It does state a 250lb weight limit while we're on the topic. -1pt Assembly: I've assembled several office chairs before and this process was similar and just as easy. +1pt If you aren't experienced or if you struggle with Ikea stuff, you may find it difficult. The hardware that they include is kinda junk. If you have the luxury of using your own hardware (or hand tools at least), I would highly recommend it. I had one bolt that had really junky threads from the factory and I couldn't do much about it, just had to cross thread it and tighten it the best I could. I had another bolt that stripped and the thread never would grab. Luckily there was one extra included in the packaging and I ended up being able to tighten it without cross threading. I think I got lucky. 90% of the assembly was smooth sailing and the few snags that arose, I knew exactly what to do. Again, if you aren't experienced with this, it could easily turn into a headache and a return to amazon over poor quality hardware

At roughly a year-ish of ownership. It became my main office/computer chair, replacing a pretty standard office chair originally bought at staples/office depot. Work from home so in this chair a pretty consistent amount of time, beyond leisure time/work outside of this. Pro's - pretty durable. I'd say its gotten its fair share of wear and tear and it's still holding pretty well. No rips that I see, arm supports still holding strong, can lean back and shift the chair up/down with no issues. Head rest isn't half bad, same with the included lower lumbar support. (Sort of) Con's - It's a little smaller width wise than I'd realize. The good of this means it kept its form over time - the bad is it isn't very comfortable after extended periods; depends what you're expecting. This sturdiness also translates to the occasional bit of not so comfortable sitting with the family jewels. I bought it the intent to see if this style of chair is worth it, considering some of the competitors want $500 for these. It's good for the price point, but with some shortcomings so to me, it was worth it over spending $500 and having the same complaints.

review_title: Great for the price, needs breaking in
body_en: I’m really impressed with what you get for the money here. The racing style looks sleek and the white accents really pop. Assembly was straightforward and took me about 20 minutes. The lumbar and neck pillows are a nice touch, and they actually make a difference during long gaming sessions. For a budget chair, it feels sturdy and the PU leather is easy to wipe down. The Ergonomic Office Chair is a sleek and versatile seating solution designed to enhance comfort and productivity in any workspace. Whether you're gaming, working at a desk, or attending virtual meetings, this chair offers exceptional support and style. With its high-back design and built-in lumbar support, the chair promotes proper posture and alleviates back pain, ensuring long hours of seated comfort. The ergonomic features extend to its adjustable armrests and height, allowing users to customize the chair to their specific needs. Crafted with premium materials, including PU leather and a sturdy base, the chair exudes durability and sophistication. Its racing-inspired design adds a touch of flair to any office or gaming setup, making it a statement piece as well as a functional one. Additionally, the chair's swivel and rolling capabilities provide effortless mobility, allowing users to move around their workspace with ease. Whether you need to reach for documents or pivot between screens, the chair facilitates smooth transitions without the need for constant readjustment. Overall, the Ergonomic Office Chair combines comfort, support, and style, making it an excellent choice for individuals seeking relief from back pain and enhanced productivity. Whether you're a professional or a gaming enthusiast, this chair offers the perfect blend of form and function for your daily endeavors.

review_title: This review is all over the place but informative!
body_en: Initially worried about the reviews I've read about the arm rests and some other things, and the price almost pushing me away from buying this chair. Finally pulling the trigger I can say with confidence they either fixed what people were talking about with the arm rests (made them closer to the chair and more adjustable) or people just expect a love seat or couch. The chair is perfect, not a single problem putting it together, I had it together in 20 mins. The chair is extremely solid and doesn't squeak at all. not only does the back of the chair recline super far like most gaming chairs, it has a separate paddle to set how far the base (place you're butt goes) reclines back to avoid having to sit back against the chair using you're weight to recline which is a massive bonus for me. some chairs require weight to recline but without being locked this chair reclines with ease. The adjustability of this chair is everything you would need. I work from home and this chair keeps me comfortable all day and all night for gaming sessions. Its a stiff chair but not too stiff, Stiff in the best way. when I first sat in it I was concerned it was going to be too stiff but after pulling 6-8 shifts for 2 weeks without standing up during, it has kept me comfortable and with 0 pain compared to my last gtp office gaming chair. after returning my Secret labs titan due to discomfort, I went from a 300$ gtp office chair to this. It has all the features you could need whether you are strict about posture, or you just wanna sit back drink a beer and watch movies or even console game its perfect. I wanted to stick to a gaming chair style but have that lumbar support and some other stuff. and I found it all in this chair. I'm 6,2 at 215-225 pounds. chair fits me perfect. I would 100% recommend trying it out if you want all the features in a gaming chair, while still keeping as much of that ergo you can with the style of chair. the pillow is actually super soft and squishy too. Its actually comfortable to use compared to other brands with really stiff pillows more for look. The chair looks leather in the mock ups, but its far from, its hard to explain, it's sort of a matte leather underarmor t shirt material. smooth and grippy but not sticky like leather. that may sound weird but in my opinion its the perfect material for a computer chair. its almost like a smoother suede material. Only negative I guess I would give them which wont effect anyone using this chair on carpet, is the wheels are pretty stiff if you dont have the weight of the chair on them. they wont freely spin if you flick the wheel with you're hand but they spin just fine. definitely not a hard floor friendly wheel, which I don't know of much other then buying roller blade computer chair wheels for commercial office spaces. all in all doesnt effect me all and the chair moves just as easily as any other on carpet. TO ANSWER SOME QUESTIONS IVE SEEN PEOPLE ASK ONLINE... 1. you cannot feel the diamond stitching at all on your back even after long sitting sessions. 2. the arm rests are more adjustable then secret labs and the gtp office chairs and not too far away from the chair (anymore?). 3. the price is steep until you feel the quality and durability of the materials they use, the weight and thickness of all the bolts, plastics, metals and fabrics show the quality. 4. how does it compare to secret labs? in my opinion the secret labs are super over hyped and over priced, yes they last a long time. but in my opinion they are super uncomfortable. for 150$ less then the titan, this chair takes the cake. All in all this chair is a 10/10 FOR ME. I know chairs fit everyone differently but I found the only chair I'm going to be sitting in until the tc600 or up comes out! sorry for the all over review if you made it this far, I just had all these questions when I was buying and I think this wraps up most of them. 500$ is alot for a chair but this is 500$ well spent in my book. I posted pictures I thought would best explain the chair. there is simply not enough reviews or info on this chair online yet with this model being less then a year old and being expensive I hope this helps you! cheers and good luck on you're chair hunt. p.s I am not sponsored by corsair although I wish I was, I just really like the chair :)

This is is such an upgrade from my last sub $100 chair. The adjustable back support is worth the cost alone. I was hunching over in my last chair and now my posture is correct. These chairs are made of soft fabric. I am 5’4 and it adjusts to my height. There is a qr code for build instructions on the top of box when you open it. The arm rests can be adjusted multiple ways. There is a tab on each arm that lets you move them up and down. I didn't notice this at first, so I couldn't reach the arm rests till I moved them up. The box is very heavy and very large. You will need 2 people to pick it up or you can turn it on its side and roll it like i did if you don't have help. Cons: The fabric has a break-in period and might feel stiff at first, but it will adjust the more you use it. I recommend getting a memory foam cushion if this bothers you. There is a primer-like new smell but will go away in a few days. You might want to open a window during this period if it bothers you. Since the arm rests move if you pull on them, I recommend grabbing the wings near the top of the chair to move it.

First I want to start off by saying I really wanted to love this chair so badly! I was so excited to buy this and get it into my office setup, but it really fell short of expectations. The 3 star rating is for the $550 price point - I was able to get it on a considerable sale, so for the price of about $300 it’s more worth it and would give it 4 stars but I cannot recommend this chair at full price. Cons: - My office does get warm with my gaming computer and this chair absolutely gets hot after sitting for a couple hours compared to my old mesh one, not sweaty but uncomfortable. - The back has awful padding. The lower portion with the adjustable lumbar feels like a rock pushing into your back if you actually use it so I have to keep it almost all the way depressed. Then right where it transitions from the diamond stitching to the flat part where the wings are, it’s like there’s a metal rod going across (likely the top of the adjustable lumbar thing) but man it’s really not comfortable to lean back into or use that fully reclined position. So overall the lower back is really hard, then there’s this middle that’s extremely plush, and then at the top middle back below your shoulder blades it’s hard as a rock so it’s unfortunate. Not as comfy as most good reviews make it out to be but it’s also not unbearable just being picky due to price point. - It squeaks!!! I was hoping a few of these reviews were just a couple bad batches but nope. Same thing others have said, right where the metal hinge is on the left side, if your sitting and using the rocking feature it creaks and squeaks every time you rock. Thats something that was just fully unacceptable for a chair at this price. - The hip bolstering really digs into the sides of my legs if man spreading and hurts after a while. - Overall the chair just doesn’t seem too sturdy/stable on the base. It has a fair amount of play when moving around but again not the end of the world it’s still fairly solid. Pros: - The bottom cushion is actually really comfortable for me sitting in it all day long even though it’s more on the firm side. It’s also big so even at 6’2 with all height in my legs I can kick a leg up. - While the backing is annoyingly uneven, I think it promotes much better posture than my other chair. - It looks just so good!! and it is definitely made out of good premium materials, I do see this chair lasting a long time! - Building it took maybe 15 minutes and you really don’t need any instruction, it’s common sense for anyone who’s ever put something together. - The pillow is so comfy! - While the wheels are stiff, and the chair is heavy I was worried about how it rolled on carpet but man it’s a breeze! It rolls really well around the room on carpet. - For the most part it’s a chair that I can sit in all day and it’s comfortable. The backing is borderline making me want to return it, but I got a great discount so I’m sticking with it. - Oh and the arm rests! At 6’2 I have longer arms but what… they are perfect for me. They aren’t too far forward or too far back at all. That’s why they have the 180 design if you want to get closer to your desk just flip them around and scoot up! Overall, again don’t buy this chair at full price you’ll likely be disappointed as the creaking and the back padding are my biggest complaints. If you can get 40%+ off it’s more worth it but be warned if you’re looking into something that’s plushy. It’s very firm. But it’s really pretty to look at!

review_title: Great chair for a killer price.
body_en: I have had a Secret Lab chair that I have been using for work for the past 6 years and have had my share of issues with it (their warranty is a joke). When I had to return to the office and took my Secret Lab back, I needed a chair for home. I refused to pay over $500 for a new chair. I looked into this one and got it around Christmas time for $250. At that price, this chair is a phenomenal value. It is a little smaller than my Titan XL but accommodates my 6-ft 280 Lb frame without complaining. It looks awesome. The green that I have really feels like a master chief OD green. (I'd love to embroider a Chief helmet on the back). The adjustment of the lumbar is great and I was able to make it more comfortable and supportive than my Secret Lab. My only gripe is the armrests don't lock into place. While they are great for their adjustability and range of motion, they can easily move when you are adjusting or really "in the zone." That's really the reason for 4 stars because the armrests are what you interact with the most after the seat itself.

Had this thing almost a year now with about daily use. People are right saying it's stiff. It's well made with nice materials but really lacking in cushioning. The recline and rotating/extending arm rests are nice but it doesn't make up for the low comfort overall. For the price you can definitely find something more comfortable, but if you need something presentable and you're not sitting in it for 8hrs a day it's decent.

Chair was easy to setup. Heads up, there are no instructions in the box, but a QR code to scan to get both a written and video manual. All parts are very sturdy and you can tell that the quality is top notch. Chair is relatively firm, looks amazing, and has great lumbar support. Wheels seem a little tight, but I'm sure it will break in over time. Many people ask if you feel the "diamond" pattern stitching, I do not notice at all. A nice bonus is the magnetic head pillow! It is very soft. I debated between this and the Secret Labs Titan Evo, and tried both out before I bought. The Titan is a bit more firm, this is a bit more cushy. I think for the value (before the occasional discounts), this chair is a better value.

Definitely not worth the price. The seat feels good kind of feels like you’re sitting on a firm bubble. There are side bolsters on the seat with tubular metal so those will hurt your legs if you try to man spread. The quality of the tilt mechanism is absolutely terrible. The main issue with this chair is the absolute window, licking engineering that went into the back rest. I don’t think these companies genuinely test their products before they release them, but you can 100% feel the support bar that holds the lumbar system at the top of the back rest. It is immediate as soon as you sit in the chair no it is not the lumbar itself it is a brace that holds the mechanism. Also, I am 5 foot 10 and the side bolsters of the back rest make contact with my arms in certain positions and is far from comfortable. Do not let this chair deceive you it does not hold your upper back. You get an uncomfortable bar at the middle of your back and the only other point of contact is the head pillow. body_en: My old office chair no longer worked after 30 years, but what else could you ask for after that time? I have broken discs and was looking for a chair in which I could spend at least half an hour or an hour and I had already made a bad purchase. Even if you are promised that a chair is great for your spine, that doesn't automatically mean that I can still sit there. Of course, money was limited so I thought to myself, then try something that is not so common for an office chair and lo and behold, I sit very comfortably in this gamer chair. review_title: Comfortable, multi-adjustable and durable desk chair
body_en: This is an excellent desk chair, especially for long hours at the computer, but i have to confess that it's taken a little time to get used to it only because this chair and my old faux leather desk chair (also sold on amazon and pictured below for reference) are at totally different ends of the spectrum. The new VIOLET mesh computer chair is extremely comfortable even after spending most of my days and nights sitting in it since i spend many, many hours daily working, communicating and gaming on my desktop computer. the chair may appear to be lightweight; however, it's got a decent amount of weight to it because of the high quality materials used to make it, especially the solid metal parts that make up the strong and stable base. In my opinion, the ability to adjust the arm rests, seat height and lumbar support proved to be a godsend, which i was not expecting, because it all enhances the versatility and functionality of the chair. Being able to change the chair to recline a bit is probably very useful for many, but I prefer a sturdy, stiff, upright chair back, so i adjusted it accordingly at a set in place 90-degree angle. The lumbar support is especially helpful to maintain proper posture and spinal alignment, yet again there was a small issue in that i generally sit with a slight forward lean or, as stated earlier, with my shoulders directly over my hips. in order to have full back support, you must lean back slightly, and that's an awkward position for me in any chair. the arm rests can be moved down at your sides or in an upright position as if there were no arm rests at all. and i have found myself switching back and forth between the two depending on what i am doing and how much movement i require in the chair. they can also be moved forward and backward a short distance, which i did find a little bothersome when the arm rests were down and i bumped them when i happened to move my arm(s) a little. they do not lock in place, but i'm positive that this is just another little concern that i can easily get used to since the old chair's arm rests were not adjustable at all. did i mention that it's PURPLE!?! not the only reason, but definitely one of the main reasons, that i purchased this chair over every other chair i looked at. and there were a lot of them under consideration. it comes in several different colors, including the traditional, brown, white and black, among others, which i really liked a lot since my room of course has a purple theme going on, and this fashionably attractive and functional chair fits in perfectly with the decor and further brightens up the space! i am so happy with this purchase even though it took me 3 hours and not 15-20 minutes to assemble. and that was all on me because (1) i am really slow and methodical when i'm doing new things, taking care with every step to do it right, and (2) i am not handy in the least and can barely hammer in a nail these days. as advertised, all tools, primarily the allen wrench, are included. no parts were missing, and nothing was damaged upon delivery. and, best of all, i can say that i assembled it all by myself perfectly on the first try, so it was well worth the time and effort spent.

It’s comfortable enough to sit in for hours, and I like that I can easily adjust it to fit my posture. Overall, it’s an excellent value for anyone looking for a supportive and comfortable office chair.

review_title: Good chair that's pretty easy to put together with 5 year warranty
body_en: Here are my comments and concerns with model YX001 only. The instructions have a few issues imho: black letters/words printed on a dark/darker background, I literally could not read them at times and had to go to another room with a spotlight to make sure I followed directions. A box around the words are fine, but not a colored box. The 6 star gear shims (piece I) on the arms really needs a better way to identify instead of “placed in the direction of the instructions”. I am not having any issues with the arms so I assume I may have gotten it right. There aren't any instructions when to tighten all the screws that you were told to leave untightened, that could lead to an issue if when you finally get the chair finished and see step 8 saying Done and try to sit in it. Not impossible use the included Allen wrench (great it is included!) to tighten the screws from step 4 to Done because the T-handle will not fit in the now put together space. We have a bunch of regular Allen wrenches so I was able to complete the tightening required. Overall assembly was not that difficult and the time to accomplish it was not longer than expected. While the above caused some delay, the chair is still fine after 4 weeks of continuous use. The chair itself: the lumbar support is very nice and easy to adjust. The arms are attached to the back and the seat seemingly to give more support for them when getting in and out of the chair. The arms lifting up and away is nice. The seat, after a couple of weeks, seems reasonable, not too soft or too hard, the mesh back is nice, and the gas lift feels and sounds solid. The chair would be worth 4.5 Amazon stars, except… I’ve had a lot of office chairs (including work) over my 50+ years of sitting in front of a computer daily: cheap chairs, relatively expensive, and in between. I have a glass floor mat and the chair does not roll freely. There are flat spots on the wheels and it takes effort to get the chair to start to roll anywhere on my mat while sitting in it. The description says they are soft to reduce noise and they do on my mat. When on glass all chairs still make a noise due to the nature of the mat, so that’s not an issue. Compared to the rest of the chair the wheels aren’t up to what I expected and I am concerned about their longevity being soft with a non-circular shape. Perhaps on carpeted floors this might be hidden. Lastly, be aware the description says Lifetime Warranty, however an included index card says 5 years IF you send them an email, which I did, but was ignored for a couple weeks. Only after using Amazon to complain about them were my inquiries finally answered. It is indeed only 5 years (NOT lifetime) which is still a decent amount of years for a chair. I will update this if any issues appear within 5 years.

review_title: I packed a whole city and almost got arrested!
body_en: I packed a whole city and almost got arrested ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I am a traveller with a problem: too much stuff. I had already checked two suitcases and still had luggage that could fill a small village. So I bought this SHRRADOO Extra Large Travel Laptop Backpack because I needed something that could swallow my belongings without looking suspicious. When it arrived, I was honestly disappointed. It looked small. I thought, “This thing can barely fit a rat, let alone my entire life.” But then I started packing. And packing. And packing. Different compartments, hidden pockets, secret zip zones, nice color combinations, travel friendly, this bag is like a magician’s hat. I fit clothes, shoes, gadgets, snacks, and maybe a small city and the entire Amazon. I am pretty sure I probably packed a house and a car too. The zippers are strong. The fabric is tough. And when I put it on my shoulders, the straps were so soft and comfortable I almost cried. I thought I had won. I walked past the airline ground support with confidence, they didn’t suspect a thing. But then came TSA. The scanner lit up like Christmas. They saw the entire city inside my bag. I was flagged. They searched it and found the Mayor tucked in one pocket. Everyone was shocked. How did I pack so much? Lesson learned: the bag is amazing, but it will make you look like a suspect when you packed a city! Now for the aftermath. When I arrived home, my shoulders and back were screaming for mercy for three days. I could barely lift my arms as they ache from the weight. But you know what? It was worth it. I carried my whole world on my back and survived to tell the tale. If you need a backpack that can hold everything and make you feel like a superhero (with back pain), buy this bag. It is a beast. 10/10. Would pack a city again 😂🎒🌆💀

2024 update 4yrs in this bag is STILL going strong. I’m starting to see others rocking this brand on their commutes. This bag has traveled no less than 30k miles by car, train and planes. It’s my go to travel bag. The absolute best. (2021) I wanted to write this review after 1yr of use. This bag has held up extremely well! On par with LL Bean for quality and durability but with thicker material. The reason I picked this up is because I needed something bigger than my deluxe LLB to fit my 17” laptop in that would also accommodate the laptops protective zip case. I looked at several different brands and ultimately landed with this one because of the great reviews and the warranty. What sold me was the law student review with all her textbooks. Yup if it can carry all those around for 1yr of law school this bag has the durability I need. If you want to save money on a weight fitness vest you can easily throw a couple 20lb weights in this thing and run up and down flights of stairs for a fraction of the cost and plenty of weight scalability. For normal users this bag is amazing. There are plenty of storage pockets and device protection within those pockets. This bag can carry anything. And in my case it has. From overnight bag to technology bag and everything in between. I’ve packed 17” laptop (in case) with iPad chargers cables and VR headset along with water bottle and snacks to bring to a friends. I’ve carried board games and clothes. Hiking gear etc. everything has fit and stored very well The straps and top handle are sturdy the zippers remain resilient. They do not catch and seal and track seamlessly no hiccups or jerks along the way. Sometimes it’s tight around the 17” laptop in its protective case and the zippers still work well and seal tightly despite the stress out on them. I’ve loaded this thing up with easily 50lbs of gear and hauled it on my back and it has stood the test of time There are no rips or tears in the materials, handles, straps or zippers. The water bottle netting is holding strong, too. I love all the pockets for organization purposes. I love how deep and wide this pack is. Deep enough to hold the big laptop. Wide enough to accommodate an oculus headset alongside in the middle pocket. Enough protection that I feel comfortable carrying these gadgets in the bag. This has become my go to bag for everything. Several times I have thought to buy another one. I don’t have a use for 2 but I enjoy it so much because of its versatility and durable reliability that it might be nice to have a backup. Friends and family are amazed but how much I fit in this bag. They go to lift it and I say don’t pick it up that’s heavy, I’ve got it. They laugh and go to pick it up and pause to gather their strength and lift and are impressed that I carry it around and then the fact that it holds so much. This bag keeps me strong and in shape for sure. It is also strong. Outdoor enthusiasts will love this bag. It can carry ski boots, hiking gear, gym gear, sports or sparring gear, picnic supplies, weekend away bag, tailgating gear, you name it. This bag carries it all. At this point I see it lasting many years to come. If anyone needs a backpack I will buy/recommend this. For the price ($25-30) and durability (1+yr) it’s unbeatable.

review_title: Fantastic travel / work backpack at a great price!
body_en: I bought this backpack in early August and used it daily as a teacher. Ten months later and at the end of the school year, this backpack is still going strong with little to no signs of wear. Style: This backpack looks sleek with a touch of vintage appeal. The color is great, which helps if you want to maintain a low profile while using it. There's a small pocket up front, a medium pocket behind that (with a separate zipper pocket inside for safekeeping valuables; and slots to hold several pens), and the main storage area has a separate laptop sleeve. One of the photos has my school-issued 13-inch laptop. It easily fits in the slot with plenty of room to spare. The sides of the backpack have two mesh-like pockets that can hold small items. Comfort: The handle on top along with the two straps have thick padding. It's comfortable carrying the backpack whether you use one strap or two. Durability: My backpack is still in great condition after heavy use for the past ten months. This includes tossing it on the rear seat of my car, placing it in my trunk, and having it rest many times on the carpeted classroom floor. The back and bottom of the backpack still look great. I will easily be able to continue using this backpack for at least another full school year. Cargo capacity: My everyday carry included our school-issued laptops, plus a power cord, an iPad (with protective case), an external hard drive, about half a dozen pens, a pad or two of paper, and other assorted items. Even with all that stuff I can fit more in there if needed. Overall value: Excellent. This is such a great backpack that I bought one for my wife, and she uses it at her school. If you're looking to save some money but still want a durable and useful backpack, do not hesitate. Buy this backpack with confidence.

I used to use a Nordace backpack that was supposed to have 2 laptop pockets, but one of them was very much not meant for laptops, and was disappointed so I looked elsewhere. I am so glad I found this one. It is far more lightweight than my Nordace one, plenty of pockets and zippers for organization, inner pockets and a back pocket for security (I personally keep my wallet in an inner zipper pocket since the back pocket is a wee bit small). It also looks exactly like the picture (which is very exciting to me). Here's a bit of a breakdown: Pros: - Large laptop pocket (fits my 16" laptop) - Lots of pockets - Against-the-back security pocket - Very breathable - Very light - Feels high quality and durable - 3 bottle-holder pockets (2 outside, 1 inside) - USB charging for portable batteries - Strap for attaching to luggage - Waterproof Cons: - Likely won't hold larger items like textbooks (at least, it doesn't hold my large ones) - Security pocket is small - Doesn't have 2 laptop pockets - VERY tight outer bottle holder pockets I, personally, got this for both work and school so I can carry both laptops together. It doesn't have 2 laptop pockets, but the one that it does is MASSIVE. The strap is actually loose even after putting both laptops into it so it can easily fit larger laptops. I went on a work trip and it was perfect. Half the time, I forget how much stuff I have in my backpack because of how light it is and how well it disperses the weight. I also appreciate that it's slim. My previous backpacks have always been bulky and I always felt awkward while trying to squeeze down the aisles of a plane to get to my seat, but it wasn't a problem this time. I do wish the outer bottle holder pockets were a little looser and larger so that I can fit my larger water bottle into them, but it isn't too big of a deal for me since I like to carry my bottle for the most part. Overall, this backpack is AMAZING for the price that it's set at and I hope more people find this. This has honestly been life-changing after having so many poor backpacks. review_title: Perfect Travel Backpack with Plenty of Storage
body_en: I bought this backpack for my mom, who takes long international flights every other month. She wanted something comfortable to carry on her back with plenty of storage and compartments to keep everything organized. I spent quite a bit of time comparing different brands and styles before choosing this one. There are travel backpacks that cost a couple hundred dollars, but after comparing features, I realized many of them offer the same functionality. This backpack stood out because of its excellent reviews and unbeatable price, and I'm so glad I chose it. My mom absolutely loves it. The backpack has so many compartments that it's easy to organize travel essentials, electronics, documents, snacks, and personal items without everything getting mixed together. It also holds much more than it looks like it can. She packed it with everything she needed for her trip, and it handled it all with ease. The backpack is comfortable to carry, feels well-made, and has held up very well through multiple trips. It's practical, lightweight, and perfect as a carry-on for long flights. One thing to keep in mind is the design. It's simple, practical, and more functional than fashionable. If you're buying it for a younger or teenage daughter who prefers trendy or stylish backpacks, this may not be the most appealing option. However, for anyone who values organization, comfort, and functionality over looks, it's an excellent choice. Overall, this has been an outstanding purchase. In my opinion, there's no need to spend two or three times more on a travel backpack when this one delivers everything you need at such an affordable price. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for great quality and exceptional value.

This may be one of the best travel purchases I've made in years. I bought it to use as my airline personal item for a business trip, and it made traveling incredibly easy. The bag fit perfectly under the airplane seat while holding my leather work backpack, a small purse, my medications, TSA liquids bag, and both my work and personal laptops. The padded laptop compartment kept my electronics secure, and I appreciated having a dedicated protected area instead of everything shifting around inside the bag. This bag really shines for airport travel. Going through TSA was quick and stress-free because my liquids and electronics were easy to access without unpacking the entire bag. The pocket layout is extremely well thought out. Once I arrived at my destination, I simply removed my work backpack and left this bag in the hotel. It was the perfect travel organizer and protected my nicer leather backpack during the trip. It's lightweight, comfortable to carry, surprisingly spacious, and exceptionally functional. For the price, I honestly couldn't believe how well it performed. I would absolutely buy it again and highly recommend it to anyone looking for an affordable, well-designed travel bag.

review_title: The carry-on personal backpack/item that almost made me enjoy flying!!
body_en: I absolutely LOVE this backpack! After taking it on my trip, I can confidently say it earned a permanent spot in my travel lineup. The number of pockets is fantastic. I had a place for everything without digging around like I was on an archaeological expedition. The top handles made it easy to grab, and I especially loved that I could wear it as a backpack while navigating the airport. My shoulders were very thankful. I flew American Airlines, and it fit perfectly under the seat in front of me. The photos are from Main Cabin (not First Class), where I had just a little extra legroom. On my return flight, I was in standard coach, and it still fit under the seat just fine. The only difference was that, when I had the bag packed to the brim, it was a little harder to slide out and access things during the flight. My only tip: Pack anything you’ll want during the flight (headphones, snacks, charger, Kindle, etc.) right at the very top of the bag. Once it’s tucked under the seat and fully loaded, you probably won’t want to go spelunking for that granola bar hiding at the bottom. Overall, this backpack exceeded my expectations. It’s roomy, comfortable, TSA-friendly, and fit exactly as advertised. If you’re looking for a personal item that maximizes space without looking enormous, this one is a winner. I would absolutely recommend buying! ✈️🎒

review_title: Great slim bag with a weird laptop holder
body_en: I spent more time than I would care to admit looking for a solid backpack, but good ones are expensive and I didn't feel like buying a few to try then return. I wanted a backpack for my office job to carry my tablet, laptop, work binders/folders, blender shaker bottles, and small knick-knacks to and from work and between different offices. These were my requirements: - Holds my laptop in a sleeve (preferably padded/protected) - Tablet sleeve big enough to hold my Kindle Scribe Colorsoft - Stylish and slim with plenty of room - Good quality without breaking the bank - Side water bottle cup holders with straps to hold down my insulated blender bottle shakers - Plenty of pockets for smaller items (gum, chargers, charging blocks, pens, etc.) - Something I could use for an overnight or couple day trip I hated it for the first 20 minutes I owned it because I thought it did not have a general large interior compartment area with folder dividers as shown in the product images. However, I quickly realized the zipper track blended in too well with the bag and I simply missed it (it's right in front of the larger top handle). This backpack nailed it. Even the tablet compartment hold my kindle scribe securely, though I'll likely only use that when traveling as it's a tad too snug. The only thing I don't care for is how the laptop compartment is only a side entrance zip and the "sleeve" is a plush arm that secures the laptop in place with velcro that you have to remove and reattach every time you move your laptop in it. That seems a bit odd and is slightly tedious to do, but I assume it's for easy access; they should really include that in the pictures of the product. Also, I understand that the backpack essentially zips in half to open up 180 degrees for quick airport security laptop checks, but I almost never fly, so that may be useless to me. I've read other reviews that claim the bag opens up on its own because of this feature. I've only had it a week so far but that hasn't happened to me yet and I don't see how it would unless the bag was packed full and only partially zipped shut. Overall I love this bag, it meets all of my requirements and then some. It also redistributes the weight well due to its longer size, so more weight in the bag somewhat feels like less. Highly recommend.

review_title: What is your backpack purpose? Repeat customer for Swissgear products
body_en: This is my favorite brand of computer backpack. My household has been using this brand for over 20 years. For many years they were used daily. The inner liner on the tiny pocket of my previous 20 year old backpack finally tore so I purchase this one as a replacement. Mainly used for travel and anyplace I have to tote a laptop too. So far, things are going well. I will update if that changes. Material and workmanship: Sturdy and quality. I understand sometimes there can be defects and I would hope they stand by their warranty. So far all is good. Size: This is a good size. Small enough to fit under an airline seat, big enough to hold the essentials. I use mainly for all types of travel. I can fit a change of clothes, medications, umbrella, bose headphones, airpods, water bottle, snacks, wipes, tissues, etc. I travel with a macbook air always and sometimes a heavy lenovo laptop. It holds both. Pockets and design: This is a slightly different design than my last one. I went with this one because it was on sale. For the overall purpose ( to haul all my stuff around,) it serves the purpose. I kinda wish I spent a little more and got the similar model I had before. -The laptop compartment has a padded velcro adjustable strap. I do not know if this is necessary but it is there. It is removable. Compartment is roomy enough to hold 2 laptops. This compartment only has a "one side" zipper. It does not zip all the way around. I found this a little annoying since my last one had a zip around. I am sure I will adjust to it but I prefer to pull my laptop out of the top instead of out the side. The downfall of one zipper, you can not zip tie or put a lock on the zippers. Depending on where we were traveling, we would zip tie the zippers. It does have a tiny pocket on the top. Not quite sure what I would use that for. - Next compartment for a tablet. It is padded around the sides and has mesh in the middle. This one unzips all the way around. TSA friendly design. Have not tried this out with two laptops yet so I don't know how that will go with tsa. The tablet pocket is small so maybe ipad mini size? The ipad pro would not fit. They could have designed this to be bigger. I was thinking of getting a laptop sleeve and using this compartment for my macbook air when I travel with 2 laptops. - main compartment: has a mini pocket for phone but I use for my airpods. Has a divider for books, papers or whatever. I actually use it for wipes. Can fit a change of clothes in a packing cube, medications, headphones, snacks and everything I need. There is a mesh zipper pouch on the top. This is great for cords or whatever. - top front pocket- I have a love hate relationship with this one. Easy to empty your pockets and phone into when going through tsa but a pain to get stuff back out. You have to dig around a little. I will probably need to separate things in little bags to make this pocket work for my needs. I miss having a small top pocket for things like chapstick and eye drops. Making two pockets, iphone sized and a small one for little things, would have been my ideal solution. - bottom front pocket: this one is fine. Big enough for epipen, inhaler, key hook, hand sanitizer, tissues, gum, some toiletries, misc stuff. Also has some loops on outer part of pocket. - side zipper pockets: there are small size zipper pockets on each side that are deep. These are ok. Weird shape. Can fit a small umbrella or a standard plastic water bottle. Space for other things but I don't have that many skinny long things going in a backpack. Pocket is deep so if you wanted to put money or something way down at the bottom of this pocket, this would be hard for anyone to just grab out of your bag. You can not fit a water bottle or similar item in the mesh pockets on the outside of these ones if there is stuff in the pockets. - mesh stretchy water bottle pockets: The pockets are a little small. These can hold a smaller sized water bottle. There is a strap to help secure. It would be better if there was a loop at the top to hook a carabiner on it, to secure a water bottle. I have lost a water bottle before out of this pocket. Sometimes I use the strap to tie a sweatshirt or raincoat to it. Backpack Straps: padded, thick work well. Have a few loops for whatever. Back is padded enough. Comfortable enough to carry around for a few hours. Overall, a good backpack. When shopping for a backpack, think of your purpose and what you want to put in it. Does it have the right sized pockets for your needs? The price was right for this one and I will use it until it breaks.

review_title: Great color and quality, love the 2 compartments
body_en: This JanSport backpack has exceeded my expectations. The color is vibrant and true to the product photos, and it doesn't look faded or off-tone in person. The overall build quality is impressive - the fabric feels durable and water-resistant, the zippers glide smoothly, and the stitching along the seams looks reinforced and well done, so it should hold up to daily wear and tear. What stood out most is the 2-compartment design. The main compartment is spacious enough for books, folders, and everyday essentials, while the dedicated laptop compartment is padded and keeps the laptop secure and separate from other items, which gives extra peace of mind when carrying it around. The ergonomic shoulder straps are cushioned and comfortable even after wearing the bag for extended periods, and the weight is distributed well so it doesn't dig into the shoulders. Overall, this is a well-made, functional, and good-looking backpack that combines style with practicality. It's great for school, work, or travel, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable bag with good organization and a nice aesthetic.

If you’re looking for a backpack that can handle everything, this JanSport Big Laptop Backpack is definitely worth checking out. What I love most is the amount of space. It has two large main compartments, a dedicated padded sleeve that fits up to a 15-inch laptop, plus multiple front pockets to keep all of your smaller essentials organized. There’s even a side pocket for your water bottle, so everything has its place. The quality is good, and it’s made with durable recycled materials that feel sturdy for everyday use, whether you’re heading to school, college, work, or traveling. The ergonomic S-curve shoulder straps and fully padded back panel also make it comfortable to wear, even when it’s packed full. One thing I am a little concerned about is the weight limit. Since this isn’t made from the thick, heavy-duty material of the original classic JanSport backpacks, I’m not sure how well it would hold up if you constantly overload it with very heavy books or gear. For everyday essentials like a laptop, notebooks, and personal items, it should be perfectly fine, but I probably wouldn’t recommend stuffing it with excessive weight on a regular basis. Overall, if you need a spacious, comfortable, and well-organized backpack for everyday use, I think this is a great option. And with over 35 colors and patterns available, there’s a style for just about everyone. You can find it linked right here on my Amazon storefront.
