review_title: Great productivity monitors with fantastic value
body_en: Never heard of the brand, price too good to be true, so risked buying one, then bought another one. These replaced my dual Samsung 27 inch Viewfinity S80D 4K IPS. My review is from my experience after a few weeks using these as external monitors for my macbook pro. First, the cons: 1. Noticeable IPS glow, poor viewing angle, bad HDR compared to S8 (although S8 wasn't stellar with its HDR). 2. Poor out of the box colors for both monitors, need calibration. 3. Subpar build quality, not robust, cheap feeling plastic indentations for monitor settings located on the back, screen can bend so must handle with care even when taking it out of the box, whereas S8 was a tank. 4. Basic monitor stand, only horizontal orientation, whereas S8s monitor stand was robust and could rotate to vertical. 5. As other reviewers mentioned, VESA 75 mount is not located in the center of the monitor, but at the lower half, making vertical orientation tricky, but more on that below. 6. S8 brightness could be controlled by macOS keyboard's brightness keys, these cannot. With those issues you might wonder why I am giving this 5 stars. That will depend on what you are looking for in a monitor. I use these for work, and these are the pros that made me get two and replace my S8s: 1. Increased vertical size due to 3:2 aspect ratio feels significant for me. One in horizontal orientation, the other vertical, feels extremely spacious for reading and coding. 2. Very light weight and very thin, which means easily supported by my VESA monitor arms, and I'm able to adjust these to the back edge of my desk without any fear of it falling or tipping over my monitor arms set up, increasing distance to the screen, significantly reducing eye strain. The default monitor stand, although basic, does not take up any room, has very little depth compared to the S8, so even without monitor arms, you can push these to the very edge of your desk, way further than my S8 with its large monitor stand. 3. Guessing due to its light weight, these do not shake at all when I'm typing. Zero shake with the stand or attached to monitor arms, whereas my S8s shook all the time when I typed on my keyboard with their default robust monitor stands. This is by far the most important factor for me, since I'm typing the whole day. 4. The text is very sharp and crisp, which reduces eye strain for those working with text a lot like I do. 5. I appreciate the minimal, light weight, slim, and bezel-less design. You are just paying for two large and crisp panels, nothing more (just pretend the speakers aren't there). I was eyeing BenQ's 28 inch "programming" monitor before, but didn't buy it because it was too thick, comes loaded with unnecessary software and a ring light, weighs 3x more, and costs 4x more. Neither pro or con, just notes having used these for two weeks: 1. Factory colors leaning towards red with too much glow, turn black boost in setting to zero, set to RGB, and use software calibration. With macOS screen calibration I got these pretty close to my S8, and fairly close to my macbook pro's screen. It doesn't hold up to a LG OLED for movies, but these beats the LG OLED for work. 2. My initial concern with poor viewing angle becomes almost a non issue as I pushed these to the back edge of my desk with my monitor arms. 3. The matte coating is above average, not as good as my S8, but I work in very bright room and these are perfectly fine for both light and dark modes. 4. Despite the fact that the VESA mount is way off center, these are so lightweight, you won't find any issues rotating these to vertical and keeping it that way provided you have a solid VESA monitor arm. A VESA monitor desk stand probably won't work without an bracket extension. 5. I'm assuming these are not thunderbolt, because I could not enable daisy chaining with my macbook pro despite having 2x DP ports per monitor. I ended up using a DP for one, and HDMI for the other. The DP enables 60hz, HDMI is only 50hz, but I can't tell the difference when I'm working. No noticeable latency. For the price and my use case, this is a 5/5.

review_title: Fantastic productivity monitor for the money. One downside: max brightness
body_en: This is for the 28-inch 4K+ 3840x2560p monitor. Raw score: 4 stars Value for money: 5 stars Rounding up to 5 stars overall Setup hint: there is a stupid gamer-oriented setting called "black boost", and by default it is set to 5/10. TURN IT OFF. When on, the colors all look washed out and low contrast. This is NOT a gaming monitor. When "black boost" is turned off (set to zero), contrast is just fine. Not earth-shattering, but perfectly adequate for productivity (I do coding and research on mine). Note: screen sizes are misleading! This is a 28" 3:2 aspect ratio monitor. It has 18% more area than a conventional 27" 16:9 monitor - same width, 2.4" taller! The display area is even 1/4" taller than a typical 32" monitor (which is usually actually 31.5" diagonally), but 4" narrower. For productivity, I prefer the layout of two of these over two 27" or 32" 16:9 monitors. I am using a pair of these with a docking station for a MacBook Pro. They don't have USB-C input, don't charge your notebook, and don't daisy chain like $1000+ displays. But they cost a SMALL fraction of the cost too. I actually replaced my mid-grade LG 4K 27" display with these. The image quality is roughly on par, and the anti-reflective surface is better in my visually noisy environment. I'm actually perfectly happy to use these instead of my 5K LG monitors attached to my other desktop Mac. There is effectively only one significant downside. They have only a maximum brightness of 270 nits (aka cd/mm^2 or candela per square millimeter). Typical high-quality monitors have maximum brightness of 400-500 nits or more. In practice, 270 nits is enough. In my brightly-lit room, I keep these at 100% brightness. However, in a few years, as the backlight wears, these will definitely get dimmer. Even LED backlights fade over time. Keep that in mind. Still, for the next few years, I expect to be extremely happy with the quality of these. They will become my roughly 50% daily drivers (my LG 5K the other 50%). Other minor nits: The build quality is meh. They have small bezels (about 1/4" top and sides, 5/8" bottom). They have an odd 75mm VESA pattern and it's at the bottom, so they fit oddly on monitor arms. The inputs point down and are so close to the bottom that you essentially can't avoid seeing the cables stick out the bottom of the monitor. They have cheap wall-wart power supplies. The logo on the bezel and during power-up is ugly and looks cheap. But, well, it IS cheap, in a good way. The stand is pretty pathetic, and if you tip it at all, it will scratch your desk. These advertise HDR capability, but ignore it... it's worse than useless on these monitors. They are physically incapable of emitting enough brightness for HDR.

review_title: For the money, I don't know how I could be any happier.
body_en: 28 Inch 3840x2560p display. I replaced a 32" 4k monitor with this. It doesn't sound like the extra vertical resolution is all that much, but it's VERY noticeable in real life. I feel like I can get so much more "stuff" on screen at once, or I can view long chunks of text without scrolling. Plus, the slightly smaller screen fits my desk better, and means I can see everything at a glance instead of feeling like I have to "look around" to see the whole screen. It really seems like this must be using the exact same panel as the "BenQ RD280U 28.2” 4K 3840x2560 3:2 Programming Monitor" that sells for $600! I have no dead or stuck pixels, the backlighting is reasonably bright, and text looks great on either light or dark backgrounds. Really, this monitor gives you such a great display for such a small amount of money I feel like I stole it! Of course the rest of the package is the cheapest possible plastic and pot metal. Nothing about it feels premium, and apparently there is a speaker, but I don't know why they bothered as it's completely useless. Just like with the 3:2 BENQ monitor, you have to use DisplayPort (not HDMI) to get 60hz at full resolution, but it has two, separate DisplayPort connections (along with 2 more HDMI ports), so I had no problem hooking it up. It works fine with an M1 Pro Mac, a Dell laptop using a Dell dock, and a desktop PC, all using DisplayPort. For this price, the only complaint I have is that my desk isn't big enough for me to buy another one! I'd been complaining that there aren't enough 3:2 monitor options. I guess you really don't need a lot of options when you can get one this good for this cheap!

review_title: Not as good as the BenQ
body_en: I own the BenQ version of this and I was hoping this would be close enough that I could replace all of my monitors with it. It most likely is the same LCD panel as the BenQ, but the backlight is nowhere near as good. The monitor's hue is very warm and it's hard to find a setting that doesn't look muddy. It is much less bright which limits how much you can change the other settings because you don't have much headroom. The matte coating is also much less effective. The BenQ softens reflections and diffuses background light. This is a matte screen too but bright lights are much easier to see and the background light causes a general haze on it that the BenQ doesn't have. That said, the resolution is great. 4K+ at 60hz works fine on display port. The sound is bad, but that's not critical. The build quality is low, I see foam padding sticking out between the bezel and the panel. The input placement is horrible and you'd need to use right angle adapters to not have visible cables since the put the connectors so close to the bottom edge. The VESA mount is also really low, but these are resolvable issues. Every corner was cut to bring this screen down to this price point. I'm unsure who this is targeted at. The BenQ is 5x the price, Gawfolk should have made this a bit nicer than this but still cheaper than the BenQ. They could have sold this for twice the price if it was a real alternative to the BenQ. This screen aspect ratio and resolution is premium, so I don't know why they decided to make a low end budget monitor out of it. If you plan to use this in a bright room I'd skip it. If you plan on coding with this 10 hours a day, I would skip it. If you want to have the color and brightness match your other monitors, I would skip it. If you have a creative need for this aspect ratio and resolution, its a dope monitor at a rock bottom price with no reasonable priced alternative and I would recommend it. But I'm returning it and buying another BenQ, which I consider the best productivity monitor on the market.

I am very pleased with this monitor, it has a beautiful crystal clear display. I'm using 4k wallpaper and it is really beautiful and detailed on this screen. The screen size is something I like too. I chose the 28" monitor which gives me plenty of viewing area without occupying my entire desk. The height of the screen is another feature I personally like. It is a taller screen rather than one that is short and long. You get a couple of inches in height that most screens don't offer. I'm talking about the screen itself, not a taller stand. It was easy to put together and took less than 5 minutes. The stand is metal not plastic, which I really like. It attaches on the back, then slides in place. One screw is all it takes to add the feet to the stand. The tilt feature doesn't work so great. It seems tight and I don't want to apply force for fear of breaking the screen. Even though I wish the tilt feature worked better, it isn't enough for me to knock off a star. I'm satisfied with it's position and will leave that as is. There is not much of a frame, it's mostly screen rather than large strips of plastic running around the outside. The only drawback is not having much area for safely carrying or moving the thing. Your gripping area is carefully holding the bottom of the screen. It's lightweight so it isn't too awkward. Another thing worth mentioning is that the price is extremely reasonable for such a nice picture. So far, I'm glad I went for this one, it's a pleasure to look at every time I'm at my desk .

Before I start. I did return mine. But that was no fault of the monitor itself. It just wasn’t the the right fit for me. The monitor is actually pretty good. My office isn’t all the bright but this was perfectly capable of competing with the sunlight coming in from the window behind it. The colors were nice and vibrant. It looked pretty good after I calibrated it. It wasn’t the most solid feeling thing in the world when I needed to adjust it, but it was fine. I think it would be great for someone that likes 4k on 27in monitor, but really just needs a little extra vertical height. The added vertical resolution was super useful while coding and editing photos. My only real gripe with it was that the inputs were really close to the bottom of the monitor. There wasn’t a good way to keep the cables from being visible without ordering some 90 degree connectors. I ultimately returned mine because I need a monitor of similar resolution that’s just bigger. I need all the resolution because I need a lot of info available at one time. When scaling was set to 100% on this monitor, the text was too small for me to read it while scripting. That’s not a fault of the monitor. It was great otherwise.

review_title: Great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160)
body_en: Bought two of them. They arrived last night. Spent far too much time testing them. Summary: great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra width. Huge pro: the resolution. Those extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160) are incredible for usability, either in portrait mode or landscape. Even at 200% scaling (to avoid blurry text caused by the rendering that Windows 10/11 has at anything other than 100%/200%/300% because DPI scaling in Windows 10/11 is atrocious. So in landscape mode, I can see two pages, even at 200%. The portrait mode allows me to have very usable, larger text, fitting a page & the header of the next page. Very clear text. Ahhhh..... Huge Pro: has DC dimming, not PWM. That's critical for my eye strain. I cannot use PWM because my eyes tire quickly. I don't have a physical device, but the app that I use says that the flickering is very low (below 5%). I don't notice anything, in any event. Pro: supports FreeSync, which means G-Sync worked for me on my ancient 1060 card. YMMV, I guess. Pro: slightly above average contrast ratio (for an IPS) of 1,200 to 1. Pro: supports DCR. Probably not a higher end implementation, of course. Pro: has a blue light mode. I don't use that, because I prefer using software for that. Con: the stand is perfunctory. I put it on a $30 stand that I previously bought for another monitor. The 75x75 VESA mounting holes are at the bottom of the panel, which means it works well for landscape but do not work for portrait without significant effort (the monitor in portrait mode is also on a custom stand and to offset the sag caused by the mounting hole placement, I have a small shipping box propped under the sagging side, with more cardboard as spacers to level the monitor. Update: I fixed the sagging by buying two VESA adapters (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0741CFJVW), which allows the monitor to be very close to the center of the monitor stand. Con: although the display is IPS, the panel's viewing angle is not that great. Even looking at it straight on, the right side of the landscape and the right side of the portrait mode monitor are washed out. Think of this as poor man's BenQ RD280U. I don't know if it's the same panel, btw, just the same resolution, contrast ratio, and both have a matte finish. This has 120% sRGB; the BenQ has 100% sRGB. Perhaps this is a prior iteration of the panel used in the BenQ (the BOE MV282CVB-N11). Perhaps it is uses the BOE MV282CVB-N10. I don't know, though as software does not show the panel manufacturer (other than the Gawfolk model, GF005. Small Con: HDMI does not run at 60 hz. But the two DP ports are 1.4 and can easily handle 60 hz. I'm now very tempted to buy another set for my office at work.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Honestly, I wasn't expecting this much quality for the price. The monitor looks great, the QHD resolution is sharp, and the high refresh rate makes gaming feel very smooth. I've been using it with both my PC and Xbox, and everything has worked perfectly so far. The curved screen adds a nice immersive touch, especially in games. Colors look good, the image is clear, and setup was quick and easy. If you're looking for a good QHD gaming monitor without spending a fortune, this is definitely worth considering. So far, I'm very happy with my purchase.

review_title: Monitor's great! Maybe some of the accessories could use some work.
body_en: I really like this monitor. I've been using 1080p as my native resolution since college (back in 2008 at least) so going to 1440p is the first resolution upgrade I've done in over 15 years. I originally had ordered a pair of 1440s from LG but after reading some remarks about the dynamic contrast being locked I bailed on those and ordered these, despite never having ever bought anything from KTC before. This monitor seems to satisfy everything I wanted to accomplish the jump (a larger screen space over 27" to accommodate the increase in pixels while also supporting the higher refresh rate and VESA AdaptiveSync features of my 27" gaming monitors). The monitor is also brighter than I was expecting. 1440p at 32" has a denser PPI than 1080p at 27", meaning text looks cleaner on this monitor than the 27" displays I was using (I've been told that at 32", 1440p is more comparable to using 1080p on a 24" canvas in terms of PPI). The default color temp is maybe a bit on the cool side but it can be adjusted (the default for "User" seems to suit me). I ordered two of these, one for each of my gaming setups, and neither of them have any dead pixels. The description says "165 Hz" but in actuality I managed to run this thing at 180 Hz (which means it's a 165 Hz panel overclocked). I notice the thumbnail for the product says "180 Hz" so go by that. If I had to complain about anything I'd say the accessories leave a little more to be desired. The base is one of those three-point things that looks cool but creates some awkward situations with your keyboard if you have to put the monitor directly onto the desk where your keyboard lives. It takes up less space than I was expecting but I still think I might go for a flatter base. However more importantly the base isn't height-adjustable, which can create issues if you have to set your monitor on a surface where you might want it lower or higher to meet your eye level (it is tilt-adjustable at least, which helps with the desk where I had to put it on a higher ledge). More than the flat base I think this is what would motivate me to get an aftermarket stand solution. Furthermore the complaints about the short DisplayPort cable in the box are indeed correct. For my setups this isn't an issue, they can reach the port without difficulty, but you definitely may need to consider buying longer cables to handle that if your PC isn't directly below your monitor like mine is. Additionally I'd like to say the cable connecting the power brick to the monitor is also really short. There's a decent chance yours could end up dangling if it can't reach the floor from your desk, even if the cable you run from the plug to the brick isn't short.

review_title: Fantastic Value and Immersive Experience — Highly Recommended
body_en: I’ll start by saying that my only suggestion is this: when a monitor is purchased, there should be an option to buy a privacy screen that fits it. However, the KTC 24‑inch curved monitor has met my expectations. Teh Monitors are great, especially for the price range. The 1500R curvature creates a natural, immersive workspace that makes reviewing/creating documents, editing spreadsheets, and creating/watching/reviewing training and/or presentation videos noticeably more efficient and enjoyable. It keeps everything within your field of view, reducing eye strain and helping you stay focused throughout the workday. The monitor(s) provide a crisp, vibrant picture quality, smooth performance, sleek, modern design, easy setup, and great for multitasking. If you’re looking for a monitor that blends style, performance, and affordability, the KTC 24‑inch curved monitor is a standout choice. It’s ideal for gamers, students, home offices, or anyone who wants an immersive display without spending a fortune.

I bought this during a pre-Black Friday sale: an Amazon "Lightening Deal" combined with a KTC coupon that dropped the price well below $200. So, my positive response to the H32S17 is partly based on the big discount I got for my purchase. The monitor is the advertised 32 inch width. The bezels are very small, about 2 mm; however, the panel has a small, black border, which is never utilized. So the border around the display area extends another 5 mm around the left, right, and top. So, the max viewing area, measured by the diagonal corners is 31.5 inches. The build quality is solid plastic for the monitor, and the monitor base does use metal. I can't speak to the amount of adjustment the monitor has on its base since I have mine on a 3rd-party VESA mount. The 1500R curvature is very gentle. I use the monitor up close and viewing content from a distance up to 10 feet away, and the curvature isn't annoying. Be aware, since the panel is a VA, the viewing angles aren't as wide as with an IPS or OLED panel. But there is some viewing angle, especially if you are viewing content from a bigger distance. You don't need to be directly dead center in front of the monitor to get a good viewing experience. The out-of-the-box calibration of H32S17 is not good. You will have to adjust such things like the color hue, saturation, gamma, brightness, and contrast to fit your environment. Some have complained that VA panels aren't very bright. I'm happy with the brightness of this monitor. I never have the brightness maxed out, and I often lower it to 85 - 75% depending on what I'm watching and how dark my office is at any given time. When I finally got it adjusted, the display is vibrant with good color saturation and deep blacks. This wasn't clear when I researched the monitor, so I will confirm that the H32S17 has an overdrive mode that has 4 different speeds. I currently have it on the highest speed, but all the levels do influence the gray-to-gray response times differently. So, this monitor, like any VA, will have some black smearing, but the overdrive, plus the high refresh rate, will mitigate it some. I'm satisfied with the low level of smearing, but I don't play high-level FPS games where smearing would cause problems. I do use the monitor for productivity. Text clarity is very good, whether reading black text on white backgrounds or white text on black backgrounds. I was a little concerned about that when I bought the monitor, but it has exceeded my expectations in this aspect. If you have a decent PC and GPU that can push high frame rates, I recommend connecting the monitor to your GPU with the display port. With a DP connection, the monitor provides a stable 180 frames, which is even higher than the advertised 165-170 hz. I'm extremely happy with that. Overall, this is a budget-friendly monitor that is good for multiple purposes (viewing content, casual gaming, and productivity). It won't compare to the best IPS and OLED monitors, but, for what I paid, I believe I got a quality product.

The overall design is standard plastic with a fairly thin bevel along the top and sides. It's actually nearly identical to a flat 34" monitor I have from 7 years ago. But it's lightweight. I hardly notice the light from the LED ring on the back of the monitor - it's pretty dim. There seem to be no settings to control the LED light, other than turning it on/off. When waking up from sleep, the monitor takes a full 3-5 seconds to turn on after my laptop is awake. A few times, the KTC monitor did not turn on at all. I had to manually turn the monitor off, then back on. So that's not so great. This was not an issue with the last 34" UHD wide monitor that is about 7 years old (which I still use), so it's not the laptop causing the long lag time in waking up. Stand The stand is sturdy enough to prevent the monitor from being knocked over by accident; however, if the desk shakes, the monitor shakes slightly more than my other 34" that is connected to a desk mount. My main issue with the stand is that it does not lift the monitor very high, only about 6.5 inches between the surface of my desk and the bottom of the stand. So the top 3.5 inches of my laptop obscures the bottom of the KTC monitor. And the laptop covers about half of the length of the monitor. That's quite a lot of monitor being blocked from view, a very annoying situation when working with programs that place controls along the bottom of the screen. Screen / Image Quality I did have to adjust the color, brightness and contrast to get a closer match my laptop, which has a very bright, high-end display. Out of the box, the color and contrast of the KTC monitor appear washed out and too gray to me. After increasing brightness, saturation and contrast, I had to bring the black point down quite a lot to get something that does not appear to have a wash of light gray over the colors. As a result, I find my "Custom" color setting way better than any of the pre-installed color modes offered in the settings menu. Gaming I don't game off this monitor; however, with a Thunderbolt 4 to DisplayPort cable, I'm getting full resolution at full refresh rates. I don't need the high refresh rate, but the monitor deliveries in these aspects. Overall Rating I've had the monitor for less than 2 weeks from the time of writing this review, so perhaps my opinions will change over time. I think this monitor is fairly good for its price range, so I'm giving it 4 out of 5 Stars. If compared to higher end monitors, this would probably be 3 out of 5 for image quality. Also, I purchased during a sale of over 30% off. That put it at about half the price of many other monitors at this level, which is pretty good. Knowing the image quality now, I don't think I would buy this monitor at full price. At a discount, totally worth it. I do a lot of 3D and video editing work, so color and clarity are important, but not essential. This monitor is in no way a monitor that should be used for exact color correcting or color matching. But, for doing things like creating textures for 3D assets, game engine editors, and video editing where perfect color is not so important, then this monitor works well.

review_title: If you are on a budget, but want a good product

review_title: Great Monitors For Basic Monitor Use

I’ve been using this Acer 27-inch monitor for a couple of weeks now and I have to say — it’s tremendously nice. What I love about it: • Smooth 120Hz refresh rate – Everything feels noticeably more fluid compared to my old 60Hz panel. Scrolling, gaming, and even just moving windows around feels buttery smooth. The 1ms VRB and Adaptive Sync make fast motion look crisp with very little tearing or ghosting. • Excellent picture quality – Colors are vibrant (especially with that colorful abstract wallpaper shown in the product images), and the flicker-free technology really helps reduce eye strain during extended use. • Great size for productivity and entertainment – 27 inches is the sweet spot for me. Plenty of real estate for multitasking without feeling overwhelming on my desk. • Solid build and stand – The monitor feels well-made, and the stand is stable. Helpful Tips: • Tilt adjustment: The stand allows for easy tilt. Gently hold the top and bottom edges of the screen and push/pull to find your perfect viewing angle. It’s very responsive once you get the feel for it. • OSD menu navigation: The buttons are located on the bottom edge. I saw a video about this monitor being available for $70 on black Friday pricing. By the time I got around to buying it, it was $85. I bought two of them, and I'm very happy, but there's some caveats I think you should know. This monitor does exactly what it says on the tin... and no more. It has one HDMI and one VGA input (why?) and that's it. It takes in audio via HDMI and has a headphone out jack, and even has volume control on the control nub, but no speakers. It takes 19v power from a barrel jack, but you can swap that for a 20v supply from a USB-C brick with the right adapter (you want the 6.0x4.4mm barrel). The HDR is rubbish, the VRR works fine. The picture quality is plenty good but not remarkable. The settings are pretty minimal and sane out of the box, you'll tweak one or two of them and then never touch them again. The stand is a joke. Of the two of these I bought, one of them was missing the 2 required screws to mount the display to the stand. Fortunately, it has a 100x100mm vesa mount on the back, though it doesn't come with screws for that either. I put mine on monitor arms, and threw out the stands. Basically, if you need a 24" 1080p 120Hz display, and nothing else, of good quality, for as cheap as possible, this is it. For everything else, you'll have to pay more.

I was able to dial in the colors to where I like them without a problem. I can't get them dead on, but it's very close. It's very green-tinted and over-saturated out of the box, so be prepared for some adjusting. Viewing angles are also good, and it works fine at 120 Hz without any issues on Windows 11. For build quality and other bits, the whole thing feels solid. The stand is made of metal and requires four screws to assemble, but there's almost no wobble. There's also no height adjustment, but it has a 100x100 VESA mount if you want to get a better stand. Audio output for my external speakers is good too, with no audible noise and plenty of volume. The single knob for menu navigation is the one point I'll put against this monitor, as multiple buttons are always better. Knobs are just finicky and annoying to use. If you want a large 1080p monitor with good colors and a higher-than-60 Hz refresh rate, you can't go wrong here.

review_title: well worth the price for a good budget monitor
body_en: 8/1/25 been a week so far and satisfied with the quality of this BIG BEAUTIFUL monitor for the great low price. a few bits of advice/insights: for the price I paid for the monitor I got the extra Asurion coverage just in case it stops working after the Amazon return period. take into consideration all monitors can only go to the highest resolution offered IF your computer can go that high. if the monitor box says 4K but your computer can only go up to 1080 then that's what you will see = the better the graphics card and processor the better the resolution. do not touch the front screen at all since it is very delicate and can get damaged easily. adjust the monitor settings from your computer if it turns off to often. the built in speakers are not good so plan on buying great speakers if you want to listen to music at its best. all in all, i would recommend this monitor for those on a budget considering all i have mentioned in this review. i will update this review if there are any changes worth mentioning.

review_title: Works fine but ghosting really holds it back
body_en: I bought this monitor as a secondary display for my setup, and overall the installation was pretty easy. Everything worked right out of the box, and for general use like YouTube, Discord, or multitasking, it does the job without any major issues. The size is good, and for the price it’s definitely usable if you just need an extra screen. But... there are a few drawbacks I noticed right away. The BIGGEST one is the ghosting. Whenever I drag windows like Discord or scroll through darker content, there’s a visible trail behind moving objects. In games, the motion clarity isn’t very ideal compared to an IPS monitor and darker scenes smear more than I expected. The stand also doesn’t offer much adjustment. The 100Hz refresh rate is nice to have and better than 60Hz and the overall image quality looks okay but just a bit brighter compared to my ASUS monitor. My recommendation for this monitor: use DP and tweak the monitor settings to reduce ghosting. Just keep in mind that because this is a VA panel and some ghosting will always be there it’s part of the panel technology and can’t be fully fixed This monitor is fine as a budget secondary screen but if you’re sensitive to motion blur or want better motion clarity you’ll definitely notice the limitations. It works, but it comes with compromises. If you want completely clean motion with no ghosting Id suggest going with an IPS monitor instead.

review_title: Clear, bright, and perfect for long work shifts
body_en: Clear, bright, and perfect for long work shifts Review: I use my monitor mainly for phone‑support work, so clarity and comfort matter a lot. After using this monitor daily, I can say it’s been a huge upgrade from my older setup. The screen is bright, text is crisp, and I don’t get that eye strain I used to feel after long shifts. What stands out: • Sharp text clarity — perfect for reading tickets, notes, and customer info • Bright, even screen with no weird dim spots • Colors look natural without being oversaturated • Easy setup — plugged in and recognized instantly • Lightweight but still feels sturdy on the desk For work use: I’m on the computer for hours at a time, and this monitor makes a noticeable difference. The brightness is strong enough to stay clear during the day, but it also dims well at night so it’s not harsh. I can keep multiple windows open without everything feeling cramped. Compared to my older monitors: I’ve used several monitors over the years, and this one is definitely clearer and more comfortable for long sessions. The screen doesn’t flicker, and the text stays sharp even when I’m multitasking across different apps. If you’re using it for phone or computer‑based work: This is a great choice. It’s reliable, easy on the eyes, and the picture quality is better than I expected for the price. Bottom line: If you need a monitor that’s bright, clear, and comfortable for long workdays, this one is absolutely worth it. It’s been a solid addition to my setup.

review_title: equal price to quality but lifespan is < 3 years.
body_en: i do not know why there are so many 1 star reviews but here's my take. i had this monitor since november of 2023 and there was nothing really wrong with it, i quite enjoyed it once i adjusted the colors to closely match my oled phone. the colors were imo above average for this price point although i prefer dark rooms and only struggled with glare in the mornings when the sun was low and peeping through windows. however suddenly today in august of 2026 the monitor has stopped functioning suddenly giving it slightly less than a 3 year lifespan in ideal conditions, i even use a special swivel mount to prevent cable damage and the power brick shows that power is being administered correctly meaning the monitor itself has short curcuited. So is it worth it? i don't recall what i paid at the time but at $200 it is not bad price for 3 years, but its also not ecomical and i would recommend it ONLY if you ONLY have $200 and no more at present and really want a 1440p monitor immediately. You can't complain that you aren't getting oled colors or blacks for this price and i found it acceptable at the time and really wouldn't have needed an upgrade or change if it did not stop working. however it seems that possibly quality control has lately struggled? i do not have a means to find out unless i still am under their warranty. review_title: Budget gaming monitor with a high end feel.
body_en: Typically, i like to wait a bit before reviewing anything i buy online. The Good: - Picture quality on this monitor is really good. 1440p looks crisp and clear and even downscaling to 1080p, while degrading the image a bit, still doesn’t look overly fuzzy. So if you really wanted to play or use this monitor at 1080p you could. (But being a 1440p monitor, don’t know why you would want to) - there is very very little ghosting with this monitor at stock settings, i found that setting overdrive to low makes the ghosting pretty much go away without reducing image quality at all so that what I’ve kept mine on. I’ve attached a video to try and show an example of what it looks like. - Freesync/ G-Sync works well without issues, there was no flickering at all during gaming at 165hz. Gaming felt smooth and i had no issues with stuttering or response time. Just note, 165hz only works with the DP cable. If you decide to use HDMI, you’ll only be able to go up to 144hz. - Talking about the picture quality, the colors are vibrant without looking overly saturated, the blacks, while not being as dark as you’d see on a VA monitor, are still pretty good. Out of the box, you probably wont need to adjust the settings at all, unless you want really want to. - Speaking of settings, i thought that using one button to essentially control everything would be annoying, but it’s actually pretty easy. Just press the button once to access the menu, and then move it in the direction you want to change whatever settings you want and then press the button again to turn off the menu. The Bad: - the monitor did arrive with some stuck pixels at the bottom right corner of the screen , just above the power button. It wasn’t enough to make me want to return it, as it isn’t noticeable when using the monitor for gaming or when using it for day to day tasks. This is more a QC issue more than anything, so your mileage may vary. I’ve attached a picture of it so you can see it for yourself. - although it doesn’t affect performance at all, the RGB lights on the back of the monitor only have the option to turn it on or off and no setting to change the color to whatever you want. Out of the box, it just changes colors in this slow wave like effect. But this is just me being nit-picky. - HDR on thins monitor is pretty bad, it does increase the brightness a bit if that’s what you’re looking for, but it washes out the colors too much and overall just looks too bright imo without manually changing settings in both the monitor and windows. If you’re looking for a monitor for primarily game in HDR, you might want to look at other options. - this one is me being nit picky again, but the USB port on the back of the monitor doesn’t seem to have functionality, seems its just there to use a USB stick to update firmware or something. I plugged a mouse in there and a USB light strip, the mouse didn’t work at all and only half of the light strip lit up. So while a cool feature, doesn’t seem all that useful. I don’t know, maybe it’s in a firmware update that I haven’t done yet? Ill update this if i’m able to figure out more. UPDATE: the USB port on the back works, i ended up swapping out old parts for new ones and it suddenly started working. I tried a LED strip and a mouse and both worked fine. I don’t know why or how this would interfere with the monitor, but it is what it is. Overall, this monitor is really solid for the price, it comes with decent enough features to make it comparable with other options, but keep in mind it is a budget monitor so you won’t get some of the features here like you’d see with higher end models. But if you’re looking to get a gaming monitor with good image quality, good colors, high refresh rate, a 1ms response time and no ghosting, you’d be hard pressed to find a better monitor at this price point.

review_title: Incredible - especially for the price. I took a gamble and hit the jackpot.
body_en: This review is for the KTC Gaming Monitor, 27 Inch 1440p 165Hz 144hz Monitor, 2K QHD 1ms GTG Fast IPS Computer Monitor, HDR, HDMI/USB C/DP Vertical Monitor, FreeSync & G-Sync, Swivel Tilt Height Pivot Adjustable, H27T22. First off, several reviewers left inaccurate reviews based on some misunderstandings of this specific monitor, monitors in general, operating system settings, GPU control panel settings, or game settings. I want to correct these inaccuracies so shoppers can make a more informed purchase: 1. The monitor is 27 inches - NOT 24 inches. Monitors are measured diagonally, NOT horizontally. This monitor measures 27 inches diagonally (while it measures 24 inches horizontally). 2. The monitor does have true HDR (not fake HDR), and it has very strong effects, especially when properly configured. Needing to configure HDR is not a limitation of this monitor. It is a fact of life as it relates to HDR. It needs to be configured in the monitor, AND in the Windows operating system (search "Windows HD Color Settings" and turn on "Use HDR" - presumably, if you're using MacOS, it likely also has something similar to this), AND in each specific game which you want to use HDR in. 3. When using HDR, you want to adjust your color, brightness, contrast, black level, gamma, etc. in the GPU control panel (e.g. NVIDIA Control Panel), the Windows OS, search "Color Management" > then click the "Advanced" tab where you'll find a lot of options; and similar in each specific game. I believe a similar function may exist within modern consoles as it relates to turning on HDR, brightness, gamma, etc. in the consoles themselves. This can be adjusted to be easy on the eyes, and even goes far beyond what is needed (i.e. the limitations far exceed the need and therefore do not restrict your ability to adjust it to your liking). Pros: 1. If IPS panels are supposed to have poor black levels, this monitor completely changes this rule. The blacks are pitch black; like a black hole, they are so black. Again, you have to know what you're doing to properly configure things. So if your blacks don't look black, it is a problem with your configuration, NOT the monitor - unless perhaps you got a lemon, but that isn't likely as this company, while new to consumers, has been producing monitor hardware for decades and isn't as new as they seem. 2. The brightness and contrast are extremely well defined. No complaints whatsoever. 3. The HDR truly puts this monitor in an entirely new class of it's own. The level of detail, the dark blacks, the bright whites (to whatever level you adjust them), the contrast, the color vibrancy/saturation - it all looks so amazing, and it is extremely broad in how it can display images, video, and games. The colors are amazing, and can go far beyond what you need, or dialed back if you prefer. 3. The 1 ms response time, the 165Hz refresh rate, the 1440p (2K) resolution, the G-Sync & FreeSync, the incredible viewing angles of 178° both horizontal AND vertical, and fully adjustable height, swivel, tilt, and pivot, all add up to a monitor without any significant weakness compared to other monitors, and many very solid strengths. Con: Only con for me is the bezel is slightly larger than it appears in the pictures, but for a single monitor setup it isn't too noticable. Summary: Overall, just as the title says, after a LOT of research into monitors, I still felt like I was taking a gamble buying this one, yet it truly feels like I hit the jackpot. I HIGHLY recommend this monitor, so get it while it's hot.

review_title: Excellent Budget Monitor for Dedicated Business Use — Know Its Limits
body_en: I run multiple monitor setups across my office for different purposes — including writing, business operations, and video production. Not every machine needs a high-end display, and that’s exactly why I picked up this KOORUI 22” monitor. This one is dedicated strictly to my business correspondence system — email, documents, and general communication tasks — running off an Apple M1 Mini. For that purpose, I wanted something affordable, clean, and easy on the eyes for long sessions. This monitor fits that role very well. Text is sharp and easy to read, which is the most important factor for how I’m using it. It’s excellent for writing, reading, and basic graphic placement — but not for critical viewing of those graphics. Color is where you start to see the difference between this and higher-end monitors. It’s a bit washed out and lacks the vibrancy and precision you’ll get from more premium displays. Brightness is moderate, but in this case, that actually works in its favor — it’s very comfortable for extended use without eye fatigue. PROS: * Very affordable for what it delivers * Sharp, clean text — excellent for email and document work * Easy on the eyes for long sessions * Lightweight and simple setup * HDMI and legacy VGA connectivity * VESA compatible for flexible mounting LIMITATIONS: * Colors are somewhat muted — not ideal for photo or video work * Brightness is moderate, not high-impact * Lacks DisplayPort and USB-C connectivity REAL-WORLD USE: As a dedicated communication monitor, this is exactly what I wanted. It does its job without distraction and without the need for expensive features that wouldn’t add any value in this role. However, if your work involves photography, video editing, or anything requiring accurate color and high visual fidelity, this is NOT the monitor for that. BOTTOM LINE: For business use, writing, and communication-focused tasks, this is a strong performer at a very attractive price point. For color-critical work… look elsewhere. This earns a solid FOUR-STAR rating from me — and would have pushed into five stars with more modern connectivity options like DisplayPort or USB-C. Recommended for the right use case. The **KOORUI 24-inch Gaming Monitor** is a great option for gamers and users looking for an affordable monitor but with solid features. With a Full HD resolution of 1920x1080p and a refresh rate of 100 Hz, this monitor offers a smooth and sharp visual experience, ideal for gaming, work or entertainment. Below I detail the pros and cons based on my experience: ### **Pros:** 1. **Image Quality**: Full HD resolution provides vibrant colors and clear details, perfect for games and movies. Additionally, Eye-Saver mode reduces eye strain during long usage sessions. 2. **100 Hz refresh rate**: Although not as high as other gaming monitors, 100 Hz offers a smoother experience than the standard 60 Hz, especially in fast games. 3. **Adaptive Sync**: This technology helps reduce tearing and stuttering, which improves the gaming experience by synchronizing the refresh rate of the monitor with the graphics card. 4. **Ergonomic design**: The adjustable stand allows you to tilt the monitor to find the perfect angle, which is ideal for long work or gaming sessions. 5. **Built-in speakers**: Although not high-fidelity, built-in speakers are useful for those who do not want to invest in external speakers. 6. **VESA mounting**: The 75x75 mm VESA mount allows the monitor to be mounted on a wall or on an articulated arm, adding versatility to its placement. ### **Cons:** 1. **Limited refresh rate**: Although 100Hz is an improvement over 60Hz, more demanding gamers might prefer monitors with 144Hz or higher. 2. **Basic Speakers**: The built-in speakers are functional, but do not offer high-quality sound. For an optimal listening experience, it is recommended to use headphones or external speakers. 3. **Limited adjustments**: Although it includes tilt, it does not have height, swivel or pivot adjustment, which could be a limitation for some users. 4. **Maximum Brightness**: The brightness might be a little low in brightly lit environments, which affects visibility in certain conditions. ### **Conclusion:** The **KOORUI 24-inch Gaming Monitor** is an excellent option for those looking for an affordable monitor but with gaming features. Its Full HD resolution, 100Hz refresh rate, and Adaptive Sync technology make it ideal for casual gamers. However, more demanding users might miss a higher refresh rate and additional ergonomic adjustments. Overall, it is a great purchase for its value for money. Recommended for those looking for a versatile and functional monitor!

body_en: this monitor was a HUGE upgrade for me. going from a 24”, 1080p res, 70hz refresh to this beauty was absolutely game changing. it comes with a displayport in box, but you can use an hdmi as well! i’ve had great results from using the displayport though. the movement is smooth and the colors show beautifully! it really makes my (in progress) desk setup pop <3 the only thing i notice is that the built-in speakers quality isn’t the best, but since i have my own speakers i’ve been using this isn’t a problem for me! i only tested with music, so if you’re looking for great music speakers i’d check other options or get external speakers! otherwise, it’s a great upgrade for me! :)

review_title: Amazing Monitor! The Stand? Not So Much.
body_en: This monitor works great and getting it on sale made it even better. 1440p is all you will ever need especially for console gaming. It runs up to 180hz on display port but hdmi it can reach 120hz easily allowing you to maximize your response time for your console and give yourself more time to react. You can quickly switch between different modes for different games and even create user specific modes that you can adjust to your hearts desire. All of the display settings are easily adjustable through the analog button on the rear of the monitor. Also the monitor has settings that can actively adjust your picture for different situations in games (I currently cannot recall the term for it). You can adjust the brightness, saturation, and more. One of my favorite features is the different display presets such as low blue light that can help when working late on the monitor. My only demerit of the monitor is the stand itself is kind of flimsy and is not adjustable. I would advise getting a mount for your monitor of some sort if you are to purchase this monitor. Otherwise this is an amazing monitor I got for an amazing price during Prime Day Deals.

I upgraded from a Sceptre monitor that only did 1920x1080, so this (being at 2560x1440) is a noticeable step up without breaking the bank. It's really sharp, and the IPS panel allows for an easier, more enjoyable time editing photos and videos, as well as gaming. I also just upgraded to an Xbox Series S from an Xbox One S, so gaming at 120fps has added so much quality of life to my gaming experience. I highly recommend this monitor if you're working on a budget-friendly setup, looking for a budget-friendly monitor, or just on the market for a new upgrade that can handle up to 180Hz (which you might never need), and complement our ever-growing technology. Awesome stuff by Acer!

nice monitor! was my first one with a high refresh rate so the difference was extremely noticeable and great. the built in speakers are a nice little bonus despite the mediocre quality because it means I dont need to hook up any speakers if I dont want to wear a headset. It is so crisp I don't need to enlarge the fonts so I get far more information on the screen. Setup took a couple of retries, but the system figured it out pretty much on its own. BUT: When I first tried to get help from the Acer support site, it was down. I tried hours later and it was still down. However, when I tried the next day, it worked fine. Stuff happens.

review_title: Excellent monitor for the price — gaming and work both feel great
body_en: Picked up the ArcticPro 27" expecting decent performance for the price and ended up genuinely impressed. The IPS panel looks crisp and colors are vibrant straight out of the box — no calibration headaches. 1080p at 27 inches is exactly the right balance for me; text stays sharp and games look clean without pushing my GPU too hard. The 144Hz refresh rate is the real standout. Coming from a 60Hz display, the difference is night and day — scrolling, mouse movement, and fast-paced games all feel buttery smooth. Adaptive Sync kept things tear-free with no noticeable input lag. Viewing angles are wide thanks to the IPS panel, so colors don't shift when I'm leaning back or off to the side. Bezels are thin, the stand feels stable, and setup was straightforward — plugged in and was up and running in a few minutes. I use it for a mix of office work, video, and gaming, and it handles all three without compromise. For the price point, it's hard to beat. Highly recommend if you want a do-it-all monitor that punches above its weight.

It is very stable, and if you plan to put it on a mounting arm it wont matter, but if you need to constantly adjust the angle of the monitor you might have an issue on some desks with this stand. However everything else is fantastic. If you are looking for a good budget monitor I can't recommend this one enough, even over other models in the same product line. If you are looking at the flat models, save yourself the disappointment and the $30 and go for this one instead.

review_title: Reliable 27" Screen with Clear Picture and Easy Setup
body_en: I’ve been using the Samsung 27" Essential S3 (S36GD) for a couple of weeks now, mainly with my Xbox, and it’s been a really solid upgrade from my older 24" screen. Setup was easy I just plugged it into my Xbox and it worked right away with no issues. The jump to 27 inches is definitely noticeable. Everything feels more immersive when gaming, and even smaller details are easier to pick up. I’ve been playing a lot of Fortnite on it, and it’s been a good experience. The colors look nice and the image stays clear, even during fast movement. It’s easier to spot things in the distance compared to my old monitor, which actually makes a difference when playing. The picture quality overall is solid for what I need. It’s not a high-end gaming monitor, but for casual gaming and everyday use it does the job well. I didn’t notice any major lag or issues while playing. One thing I liked more than I expected is how slim it is. It doesn’t take up much space on my desk and has a clean look. The stand is basic but stable. The only small downside is there’s not much adjustability, so you have to work around that a bit. I’ve also used it for YouTube and general browsing, and it works perfectly fine there too. No eye strain even after longer sessions. I honestly think this is a great value if you want a bigger screen for gaming and everyday use without spending a lot. It’s simple, reliable, and does exactly what I needed.

It's a great monitor. The color quality is fantastic. I like that it has a built in blue light filter, BUT the blue light filter is a bit ridiculous. I will still use blue light glasses. It was super easy to set up. I am however having an issue getting my speakers to connect. I currently have very old, very cheap speakers though so I think I'm due for some new ones. I am able to bluetooth connect my headset though. It's a great price for what you get. I'd certainly recommend this monitor. I obviously can't speak on durability as I've not had it long enough.

review_title: The Samsung 27” Essential S3 (S36GD) Curved Monitor is an excellent choice!
body_en: The Samsung 27” Essential S3 (S36GD) Curved Monitor is an excellent choice for both work and entertainment. The setup was quick and straightforward — plug it in, connect the HDMI cable, and it was ready to go. The 1800R curve creates an immersive viewing experience that feels natural and easy on the eyes, especially during long sessions at the computer. The picture quality is crisp and vibrant, with rich colors and great contrast for an FHD display. At 100Hz, the motion is smooth and fluid whether you’re scrolling through spreadsheets, editing photos, or streaming videos. The slim, modern design looks sleek on the desk, and the stand is sturdy with just the right amount of tilt adjustment. For the price, this monitor delivers outstanding value — sharp image quality, smooth refresh rate, and that signature Samsung reliability. If you want a curved screen that enhances both productivity and enjoyment, the Samsung Essential S3 is a fantastic pick.

I found this monitor and ordered it quickly. Shipping was fast and it came in undamaged. The Good: Monitor was easy to set up. It is a good size. Screen looks good. The Neutral/Bad: Monitor boasts a 100 hrtz refresh rate. While this is fine for my needs (switch and basic computing) this is probably not good enough for a heavy gamer or someone dealing with advanced graphics. The monitor only has 01 HDMI input. I find this annoying and I have to buy a HDMI switch in order to switch between my nintendo and my computer. The Monitor does not have built in speakers. My last one had built in speakers and I was spoiled with that simple feature. Overall if you are looking for a basic curved monitor with decent specs, I believe this is a good candidate. However if you are looking for something with the most advanced refresh rates and multiple HDMI inputs, you may want to look a tier or two up. I have included pictures of monitor front and the back (so you can see the inputs).

review_title: I'm Not A Gamer And I'll NEVER Spend A Lot Of Money On A Monitor (With Update)
body_en: UPDATE: I have had this thing for almost 2 and a half years now. I am happier with it every day! Two things to note are: 1) I have never seen anything like somebody welding something in a Youtube video!! It's so absolutely bright, it lights up the room a little and I reflexively squint until I have time to realize that it can't hurt my eyes because it's not real life. 2) Much of the time, it has better flesh tones than my big screen Hisense TV out in the living room! I can't recommend it enough. It's not even really a budget monitor; it's just not a gaming monitor! It sure is good for everything else!! I've been using this Viewsonic VX2778-SMHD 27 inch monitor since Jan, 2017, Very nice monitor! But, then I built a dream machine. i7-14700K on an ASRock Z790 Riptide motherboard with lots of SSD's and NVME drives. 48 gigs of very fast RAM and two DVDRW's. I'm pretty good at this and I did my very best not to allow any bottlenecks and not spend money on silly things. It absolutely screams; it gets stuff done fast! I also have an older Intel computer, an AMD computer, and a Raspberry Pi in here. So I have an HDMI KVM switcher and an HDMI audio extractor (audio goes straight to a competent home stereo). So, I don't play any games anymore, but I do want to get stuff done! There came a point where I wanted to make use of this somewhat better video card that's better than anything I've ever used. (Still not for gaming, tho.) I scoured Amazon. I ended up getting an NVidia GeForce GTX 1660 used, that was DIRT cheap! I chewed my nails wondering if it was going to work, but it did and it does! From the first momen, for about 9 or 10 months! I forget how much memory it's got, but it's up there. So, now, I had this video card mostly going to waste (Except for hardware acceleration; that's really nice!) So, I measured how much room I have. If I looked at monitors with really thin frames around the screen and measured and did the math... I decided on 32 inches. I scoured Amazon again and got to this monitor: (KTC H32T13 32 Inch) I had a little trouble. First of all, I'm lazy. I was still building that i7 and I set the monitor aside after unpacking it and went through all my other stuff I had to do first. (The other 2 computers mentioned above both needed some help.) (And the computer room needed some rearranging.) There's also that fact that there was absolutely nothing wrong with the old Viewsoni; there was no pressure... Anyway! From March 22nd until just now - two days ago - it just sat there. I don't even know where the quick start guide or whatever it is, went to, and I didn't want to conduct a lengthy search. Someone wrote that the power button is in a bad place. It's not that bad at all. I spent a little while finding it; reach your hand around the monitor's right side, near the bottom and feel for it. It sticks way out. The only time I have to reach for it is when I'm leaving the computer room to watch TV or go out or whatever. I can't reach it sitting down, but I'm getting up anyway at that point. Then I was totally puzzled, trying to figure out how to set the settings on the monitor. It wasn't bad, but I wanted to tweak the brightness, contrast, hue, gamma, etc. It took me quite a while to figure out that that power button, which is also a menu button (if you just touch it instead of holding it for three seconds) IS ALSO A JOYSTICK! Remember that! You can move it left, right, up, and down. Once I figured that out, it has a VERY logical, easy to use menu, unlike the Viewsonic mentioned about. The next problem I had was that a lot of things were ghosted in the menu and couldn't be selected. Scratching my head, I theorized that probably the video card was running the monitor and I turned to the NVidia Control Panel on the computer. There are at least three different places to set all that on that i7 machine, but it ended up being the screen display settings that did it. I love this monitor now! Plenty bright, fast, 2K, really great picture!! If the power button in the back is even a negative, I don't mind a bit. Everything else about it is outstanding! In about a minute, I had all those settings set. Beautiful bright, colorful screen! Perfect! I also have an older Silicon Dust HDHomeRun dual tuner. I encountered something that's never happened before! Watched "The Rifleman" in black and white. NEVER BEFORE have I had perfect black and white! Always some kind of tinge, usually in the dark places. I mean PERFECT black and white! Then I watched some stuff on Charge! (Streaming) and I adjusted color saturation and hue and got the skin tones right. Absolutely perfect picture, no matter what I do, now!! This is not a cheap budget monitor; this is an inexpensive performance monitor that works extremely well! I completely recommend it and I think it's a super nice deal for the money!!

I have been pleasantly surprised with this monitor. It was listed for only $110 and I got it $10 off so paid only $100 + tax. To get a 1440p monitor for so cheap is really incredible. The monitor does kind of have a cheaper feel/weight to it but it preforms well and that's what counts as far as I'm concerned. It came with an HDMI cable which is adequate for a monitor that only does 100hz. If you prefer Display Port than it has an input for that but you will have to provide your own cable. As someone who pretty much exclusively plays single player games 100hz is plenty for me. When I decided to buy the monitor I couldn't find any reviews for this specific version (24" 1440p 100hz). There were plenty of good reviews for other versions but not for this one. I am glad I decided to go ahead and buy it anyway. It really is a nice step up from my previous 1080p 27" 75hz LG monitor which I think was probably meant more for an office than a gamer. I was not sure how noticeable the jump up in resolution would be but it is noticeable and quite nice. The games look better, text is clearer and easier to read, and I noticed that even the UI for Windows and programs I use like Shotcut just look better and seem to be made with higher resolutions (QHD and above) in mind. The jump from 75hz to 100hz has been less noticeable but again I play single player games, also I prefer to play with a controller, and I come from decades of playing on consoles where a solid 30fps is considered pretty good and 60hz a bit of an anomaly. This monitor does accept an HDR signal but I have not been able to test that out much yet. Also I don't believe it has the HDR 400 certification but at this price this is not surprising and from what I hear HDR 400 monitors aren't really all that great for HDR. The cheapest HDR monitor I've scene recommended costs $280, which is quite a jump up from the price of this monitor. Also Windows reports it as a 10 bit monitor. I'm not sure if that was mentioned in the specs but that is nice to see on a budget monitor (instead of only 8 bit). One thing some people might not like about this monitor is it does not have much customization in terms of brightness and colors and things like that. If you are the type of person who really likes to tinker with those kinds of sliders and settings than this is not the monitor for you. It has 7 different presets that you can choose from but that's just about it as far as the choices go. For me there are a few that I like so I have no complaints and if you like to keep things simple than this could be a positive but if you need to tinker than find a different monitor. It does have crosshair and FPS counter choices in the settings but I have not tried them as I do not have a need for them. Before finding this monitor I had never seen a 1440p monitor at 24". They were always 27" and above when I looked. I have to say that initially I kind of missed the extra screen space with the 27 incher but after a couple weeks I got used to it and honestly do think it is a great size. It allows me to be closer to the screen and actually sit at my desk whereas before with the 27" monitor I had to sit a bit back to be able to comfortably take in all the screen real estate. If you are coming from a smaller size monitor than I think this will be a nice upgrade. If your previous monitor was bigger just know that it might take a week or 2 to get used to the smaller size but I think that once you do, you will not miss the bigger screen. Also the pixel density is pretty high at 1440p 24" as most monitors this size are only 1080p. So in conclusion if you are like me and just want an inexpensive but well made 1440p monitor, than I think you will be happy if you choose this one. This KTC H24T27 is very nice for single player gamers like myself or anyone looking for a 24" 1440p monitor. If you are the type of gamer that plays multiplayer games and needs high refresh rates than obviously this is not the monitor for you, I would suggest something with at least 160-180hz.

The freight forwarder is payed by weight and it is pretty expensive, so I tried to find lightweight options. This monitor was a perfect fit for this requirement. The overall build quality is still pretty decent and more importantly the screen itself is pretty good. Definitely good enough for office work or light color work like web design. I don't have a color calibrator or a really accurate screen to compare, but on it's own they look good. I got three and they all match pretty closely too. The three monitors with an outer Amazon box weight 13.6kg. With the extra shipping I payed around 230$ per monitor. Compared to the alternatives here I'm happy with the purchase. Got two of them for my work setup, and they are clear bright, and work great so far. Not having an adjustable stand is sort of annoying, but I have figured it out, and its not a reason to take a star away based on how affordable they are.

review_title: Excellent Value and great performance for a flat 27" 1440p monitor
body_en: This KTC 27" QHD monitor is a fantastic value with excellent features. Very good blacks with 4000:1 contrast and the 144hz is a legit gaming entry point. The 129% sRGB was a bit concerning to me as it suggested the color accuracy may not be that good, but the monitor has an "sRGB" mode in the menu that is useful for ensuring color accurate work and was the reason why I gave this monitor a chance. Glad I did. Speaking of which, the menu is accessible by a single joystick type button behind the monitor which takes a little bit of contorting to access from below it but its operation is very easy to use and allows for quick navigation within the menu. Would have been better if that joystick was positioned an inch or more closer to the bottom of the monitor. The standard color profile is the 129% sRGB which gives you slightly more of an extended color palette reminiscent of "HDR". No built in speakers, but that wasn't a deal breaker. Now that its on the desk and I'm using it daily, I can see that for me a 27" monitor like this is probably the practical limit for a "flat" configuration vs curved. On a white background, the bottom edges take on a slightly pink hue when you are positioned in the middle of the monitor but its subtle. That is probably reduced with curved monitors. Despite that I prefer it flat. The brightness of the monitor is very good, and almost too much for my eyes. Since I'm working all day in front of the monitor, i need the ability to lower the brightness to comfortable levels. The lowest brightness level is just about where it becomes comfortable for me so it would be better if it had more range for dimming further. It is HDR capable technically and I believe it but have no intention of testing or using that mode sitting at normal distances from it, with the high brightness and 4000:1 contrast, it would work really well if you're eyes can handle the brightness and color intensity. I have it positioned as the main monitor flanked by two 1080p 22" monitors which are slightly angled inward. As a triple monitor setup it works quite well and I plan to find a game where I can span across all three monitors on my desk.

That's where the KTC 32" QHD kicks in, and it has been a great performer so far! Color coverage claims are a bit exagerated (my Colormunki iDisplay rates the KTC screen as 92% of sRGB, not 109%). Still, I got this KTC 32" QHD monitor heavily discounted, so it is fantastic value. Next will come longevity - will update if it craps out early. Otherwise, definitely recommended!

body_en: I’ve been using the LG 27US500-W Ultrafine Monitor for a few weeks now, and it’s been fantastic. The 4K UHD resolution is incredibly sharp—text looks crisp, and colors are vibrant without being oversaturated. Out of the box, color accuracy was already very good, but after a quick calibration, it looked even better. The 27-inch screen size is the sweet spot for productivity—large enough for split-screen multitasking without taking up too much desk space. I mainly use it for photo editing, web browsing, and occasional Netflix, and everything looks clean and smooth. The IPS panel gives great viewing angles too, so there’s no color shifting when I move around. Build quality is solid and minimalistic, with thin bezels and a clean white finish that looks great on my desk. The stand is a little basic—only tilt adjustment, no height or swivel—but that’s easily solved with a VESA mount. Connectivity is straightforward with HDMI and DisplayPort options, and it works flawlessly with both my MacBook and PC.

review_title: Good monitor, but needs manual adjustment for proper color.
body_en: Well constructed and very sharp, but terrible color balance that can be corrected with the included controls. The settings I came up with for natural skin tones and not having your eyes ruined by an extremely bright and blue screen output are these: Set it to theatre mode Cut brightness down to 25 (!). Way, way down. Set red, green, and blue under the 'Color Temperature' to 65, 85, and 77, respectively. Your mileage may vary, but you can use these settings as a starting point and adjust for your personal taste. These settings work best in low to average room lighting; if in a brighter room, you may have to adjust more. I would have given the monitor a 5-star rating, but the default settings are not pleasant at all.

review_title: Good monitor with one minor caveat.
body_en: I got this monitor when it was $149 and while other options exist for a cheaper price and better refresh rate, this has the color saturation option. Basically, you can make the colors pop much more, which is a huge plus in my book as only a few monitor brands have it. It's a huge requirement for me. The 1440p is also a big upgrade compared to my other 1080p monitor, as games and other content looks way better while not being as resource intensive as 4k. However there are a few downsides to this monitor. First downside was getting the monitor to recognize the 1440p signal. When I first set it up, it only recognized 1080p from my mini pc. When I unplugged and plugged the HDMI cable back in, then the monitor discovered the 1440p. Not a huge deal breaker, as I rarely unplug my computers. Second downside however, is a very annoying one. When auto switching from HDMI to Display Port, the monitor sometimes goes into sleep mode, or just bugs out. This is very frustrating as I constantly go from my mini PC (on HDMI), to my Desktop (on Display Port). It'll sometimes work without issue, and other times I have to power off the monitor via the back button for it to work again. But sometimes when powering back on from this issue, the monitor light will be amber instead of white, even though it's not sleeping and fully on. I have to physically unplug and replug the monitor in to fix this. (See the attached photo). Disappointing that this is an issue, given my other 1080p monitor from ASUS never had this issue. So ya, if you can get this for sale under $130 then sure it's a good monitor. If not, find something else that is less buggy.

review_title: Écran fluide et confortable pour le travail et le gaming léger
body_en: The Samsung 24-inch IPS flat screen is a very good screen for everyday use, whether for work, studies or even occasional gaming. The IPS panel offers good viewing angles and fairly faithful colors, which makes the experience pleasant, especially for watching videos or doing light editing. The 24-inch size is ideal for a standard desk, neither too small nor too bulky. The image is sharp and fluid for the majority of uses, and the screen remains comfortable even after several hours of use. The design is simple but modern, which fits easily into any setup. The only weak point is that it is not intended for users who are very demanding in competitive gaming or professional colorimetry, but for general use it does the job very well. Overall, this is a reliable, versatile display that offers great value for money.

The screen size is perfect for multitasking, the visuals are crisp and vibrant, and setup was effortless right out of the box. review_title: One thing I really appreciate is how lightweight and slim it is.

I connected it to my laptop using the included USB-C cable, and within a few seconds it was recognized automatically without needing to install any drivers. I also tested the Mini-HDMI connection with another device, and that worked just as smoothly. The 15.6-inch Full HD display looks sharp and clear. Colors appear vibrant, and the IPS panel provides good viewing angles, which is helpful when I'm sharing the screen with someone else. I mainly use it for spreadsheets, documents, video calls, and web browsing, and the extra screen space has made multitasking much more comfortable. One thing I really appreciate is how lightweight and slim it is. It fits easily into the same laptop sleeve as my computer, so taking it to a coffee shop or while traveling doesn't feel like carrying extra equipment. The built-in stand is simple to adjust, and I was able to find a comfortable viewing angle without any trouble. The built-in speakers are convenient for casual use, like watching videos or joining online meetings. While I still prefer headphones for longer sessions, it's nice having the speakers available when I need them. The overall build quality feels solid, and the connections have remained stable throughout my use. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this portable monitor. It has made working away from my desk much more efficient without adding much weight to my bag. The display quality, quick setup, and portability make it a great companion for a laptop, whether you're traveling, working remotely, or simply looking to expand your workspace wherever you go.
