History More than 20 years ago, Mead Composition books were everywhere in middle school. These were the laptops of the day and back then I used the first-generation Pilot V5 pen in conjunction with these notebooks. And now, more than 20 years later, I've found the Pilot Precise V5 Stick Rolling Ball Pens, Extra Fine Point, Blue Ink, Dozen Box (35335) and the updated Mead Composition Book, college ruled this time around, to be a perfect match for my use. I needed a notebook for making notes to myself, writing ideas, and taking inventory of life. I only recently found that "disposable writings" such as these are better suited to writing long hand, rather than electronically. And having used more expensive notebooks in the past, I found the current-generation Mead Composition book to work perfectly for me. Compared to the others (Moleskine, Clairefontaine, Rhodia) About a decade ago I started using other brands of notebooks, first it was Moleskine which was decent and had some nice touches. However, I cannot currently recommend the Moleskine Cahier Journal (Set of 3), Pocket, Ruled, Kraft Brown, Soft Cover (3.5 x 5.5): set of 3 Ruled Journals as the paper has become rather cheap and the price does not justify the quality, for my needs at least. The Mead Composition book has thicker pages and more quality feeling pages than the Moleskine notebooks, hands down. The same is true for the Moleskine monthly planner in the large size, it is a huge disappointment because the pages are thin and ink bleeds through. Clairefontaine and Rhodia notebooks are top quality, buttery soft pages, solid bindings, made in France, and I highly recommend these notebooks if money is no object and the notebooks are being used for an important purpose. The quality is the highest I've found in notebooks, however, they are four to five times the price of the Mead Composition book and currently too much for my needs. Best value out I became interested in these Mead Composition books after seeing a crowdfunding campaign to bring back higher quality composition books. I learned about the rich history of the black and white cover of the original composition book decades ago. However, the crowdfunding price was nearly $20 for each notebook, so I found that for my use, the Mead Composition book is perfect. The cover isn't thick and hard like it was years ago, the pages are rather cheap, but they are thick thus preventing bleeding from my Pilot V5 pens. The pages do wrinkle easily, but I did count 100 pages, seeing how some other reviewers didn't have all 100 pages. The binding and durability doesn't seem that great, so I would give the quality of the notebook and pages 3 stars out of five, though it is fine for my needs. tl;dr While the more expensive French competition has much better quality, for a disposable/idea notebook for $1.99, the Mead Composition Book cannot be beat based on price and nostalgia factor. Highly recommended.

review_title: Reliable Everyday Companion — Great Value Wide‑Ruled Notebook
body_en: The Emraw Composition Notebook Wide Ruled (2 Pack) offers a solid combination of practical features and budget‑friendly value. With durable hard covers, a sewn binding that helps pages stay put, and 100 wide‑ruled sheets (200 pages) per book, it’s a dependable choice for students, note‑takers, or anyone needing reliable paper. The wide‑ruled layout gives generous line spacing, which is nice for legibility. Hardcover and sewn binding mean it feels sturdier than typical cheap notebooks. The marble‑style cover gives it a classic, school‑friendly look. Some points to watch: Paper quality may be basic; some users report thin sheets or bleed‑through with heavier ink. The binding and cover, while decent for the price, aren’t premium; if you’re very rough on notebooks you might want something more heavy‑duty. If you prefer college‑ruled (narrower spacing) instead of wide‑ruled, this might feel too spacious. Verdict: If you’re looking for an affordable, dependable notebook for everyday use — taking notes, journaling, or school work — this Emraw pack is a strong value. It gives the essentials without frills. If you write a lot with fountain pens or heavy markers, you might want to test the paper first or opt for a higher‑spec notebook.

review_title: Taja Dotted Spiral Journal Notebook — Practical and Stylish!
body_en: I recently picked up the Taja Dotted Spiral Journal Notebook, and overall I’m really pleased with it. This notebook strikes a great balance between quality, functionality, and price — perfect for everyday use! 📘 Design & Build The hardcover feels sturdy and durable, and I love the minimalist design. The spiral binding makes it easy to flip pages and lay the notebook flat when writing or sketching. It’s compact enough to carry around in a bag or backpack without feeling bulky. ✏️ Paper Quality (⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️) The 140 dotted pages use thick, bleed-resistant paper that works really well with a variety of pens — even gel pens and markers don’t bleed through easily. The dot grid layout is great for bullet journaling, planning, or freeform note-taking. 🧠 Functionality The notebook’s size and design make it versatile. I’ve used it for personal journaling, sketching quick ideas, and jotting down reminders — all with ease. The elastic closure band keeps everything secure when you’re on the go. 👍 Final Thoughts For the price, this notebook delivers excellent value. It’s well-made, practical, and looks nicer than many notebooks at similar price points. Whether you’re a student, creative, or just someone who likes to stay organized, I’d definitely recommend it!

review_title: My pick for a notebook companion
body_en: This spiral notebook has become my standard. It is large enough to last a while, but not so bulky to add so much to my bag. I like the elastic to keep it so it opens just where I need it to. The material is sturdy enough to stand up to being carried around for a while. The pages don't bleed through so I can use both sides of the pages. Perfect size notebook for me!

review_title: Great Little Notebook for Work Notes
body_en: I bought these for work and they have turned out to be the perfect little notebooks. They're compact enough to easily throw in a backpack or work bag, but still look polished and professional when you pull them out in a meeting. The elastic band is a surprisingly nice feature because it keeps everything together and prevents pages from getting bent up while commuting around. I also like that there's a date section at the top of each page. It makes organizing meeting notes much easier when you're trying to go back and find something later. I admittedly don't use the first couple pages with the index/table of contents setup and usually skip straight to the regular note pages, but that's more of a personal preference than a complaint. The overall quality feels solid, especially for the price. The faux leather cover maybe feels a tiny bit cheaper up close than I initially expected, but honestly once you're actually using it day to day at work, it still looks sleek and put together. Definitely doesn't feel embarrassing to bring into an office or client meeting. I've tried a lot of random notebooks over the years and this one hits a really nice balance of portability, functionality, and appearance. Would absolutely buy again.

These are my favorite notebooks. I have repurchased and bought for others probably over a dozen times. They are relatively fountain pen friendly. Depends on the ink and nib size but I use a medium nib with Diamine Writers Blood and only have a tiny bit of bleed through if I write over another spot before it is dry (like correcting a letter or something). It does take a second to absorb so don’t flip your page immediately or your ink with smear. Light colored Tom Bows are ok and dark are fine if you don’t build up more than one layer. (Light is pic 3, minimal multi-colored pattern show through in pic 4) The two ribbon book marks are a game changer for me. Price is amazing for what you are getting. review_title: Sturdy, beautiful, and perfect for heavy use.
body_en: I use two of these journals at a time: one to plan my novel, and the other as a diary/braindump combo. I don't decorate the pages or do any impressive bujo designs, so I can't speak to how it would serve as a bullet journal. However, these babies see a lot of heavy writing use from me. I've purchased four of them so far and not a single one has disappointed. Page thickness is great. I accidentally spilled water on a couple pages and it didn't bleed through, which was shocking to me, given how affordable this journal is compared to most others listed. The pages are smooth and easy to write on, so be careful with any pens that might smudge or smear. The paper will certainly make it easier to pick up and spread wet ink on your hands. I'm a ballpoint user and I've noticed that finer tips work best, but even with the standard cheap-o pens, I just give them a minute or two to dry and then I'm highlighting all over them with no problem. It's solidly built. I've never had any issue with pages falling out, or the bookmark ribbons unfurling - and I'm writing in my journal at least 3 or 4 hours a day, constantly flipping back and forth through multiple brain dumps. (If you've got ADHD, you understand what I mean.) The color of the cover and ribbons are absolutely stunning, somehow prettier than the pictures show imo. I personalize the covers of my journals with stickers and writing, and whatever I put on has lasted. Overall, this journal has consistently impressed me by serving me well and I couldn't recommend a better one.

review_title: Fully equal to many expensive Japanese notebooks & lightyears better than Moleskin. And the Price!
body_en: The paper in these RETTACY Notebooks is absolutely fantastic. Smooth to the touch, easy on the eyes, and takes fountain pens as well as ballpoint, rollerball, and pencil all like a dream. The ghosting/show-through through is really minimal, and bleed through almost nonexistent (a tiny bit with a really wet fountain pen). Also works nice with Ranger ink stamp - still no bleed through although there is ghosting/show-through. The lining/grid/dot grids is clear but very subtle and non-distracting. (Do note that the lined notebooks (as opposed to grid, dot grid, or blank) to come with "Date" printed in the upper corner of each page). I think these are easily the equal in quality of Midori MD, Clairefontaine clothbound and Premium C.D. - now, all those (and these) have their own minor aesthetic differences (the Midori paper is creamier and a bit toothier, the Clairefontaine and C.D. is much "slicker"; cover differences, etc.) so everyone will have their favorites - but you won't be disappointed on quality - and how can you beat the price!!!! A million times better than Moleskin

review_title: Best Notebook for Organized and Durable Note-Taking!
body_en: I’ve been using the Five Star Spiral Notebook for a while now, and it’s by far one of the best notebooks for anyone who values quality and durability. Whether you're a student, a professional, or someone who just loves staying organized, this notebook checks all the boxes. Graph-Ruled Paper The graph-ruled paper is perfect for more than just math. I use it for note-taking, drawing charts, and even sketching out designs. The lines are subtle but provide the perfect structure for clean and organized notes, making it versatile enough for various subjects and uses. Ink Bleed Resistance One of the standout features of this notebook is its ink bleed resistance. I’ve used gel pens, markers, and highlighters on these pages, and they hold up well without bleeding through. This makes it ideal for colorful note-takers or those who prefer using different types of pens. Water-Resistant Cover The water-resistant cover is another major plus. I’ve accidentally spilled water on it before, and not only did the cover repel the water, but the pages inside were protected too. This feature is especially helpful when you’re on the go and need a notebook that can withstand a little wear and tear. Durable Spiral Binding The spiral binding is incredibly sturdy and allows the pages to lay flat or fold back for easy writing. It’s also strong enough to prevent the pages from tearing out easily, even when flipping back and forth frequently. Study App Integration The bonus feature is the study app integration. You can scan your notes and organize them digitally, which is a great tool for students or professionals who like to keep digital backups or want to study on the go. The app is intuitive and easy to use, adding another layer of convenience to an already fantastic product. Overall Experience In conclusion, this Five Star Spiral Notebook is the ultimate tool for those looking for durability, functionality, and versatility in their note-taking. The quality of the paper, the water-resistant cover, and the added value of the study app make this notebook worth every penny. I highly recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable, high-quality notebook for school, work, or personal use.

review_title: A Notebook That Becomes One With Your Routine

The cover is soft but protects extremely well. It will last whole year of Geometry. And don’t get me started on the bleed resistance. I constantly mess up highlighting but this just never went to the next page . When I saw the listing, my eyes shot to the price. During the time I bought it, it costed around $7.00. I was willing to purchase it but not ecstatic. I needed a graph paper notebook and this was one of the things I just needed to check off my checklist. But the pages fit just perfect for a class lecture. I would fit all my triangles and shapes into sections with arrow pointing towards them. The pages were always thick enough for me to push hard but not rip them. It was just amazing. I would recommend to anyone and everyone, to buy this. Not for the price, but for the lasting quality it will leave on you for the year you may use it.

I purchased the New Balance 608 V5 while it was on sale, mainly for weightlifting. These shoes aren't the cutest, but they perform well where it matters most for strength training. The sole is firm and very stable, keeping my feet flat and securely planted on the floor during barbell squats. Unlike cushioned walking or running shoes that compress under weight, these provide a solid, stable base that makes me feel more secure when lifting. Because of that firm construction, don't expect a soft or plush feel. The cushioning is noticeably less than what you'd find in walking or running shoes. The comfort is okay, but that's because the shoe prioritizes stability over softness. The arch support is also fairly minimal. I personally wouldn't recommend these for running since the shoes are quite rigid. If most of your workouts involve walking, jogging, or other cardio, there are more comfortable options available. However, if your main focus is weightlifting or strength training and you want a stable platform for exercises like squats, these work very well. The shoes fit true to size, and I had no issues with the fit. **Pros** * Good stability for barbell squats and strength training * Firm sole keeps your feet flat and securely planted * True to size * Great value when purchased on sale **Cons** * Design is fairly plain and not particularly stylish * Minimal cushioning compared to walking or running shoes * Fairly minimal arch support * Too rigid for running and may not be the best choice for cardio-focused workouts Overall, I think the New Balance 608 V5 is a good choice for anyone looking for a versatile gym shoe with a stable, supportive base for lifting. Just don't expect the soft cushioning or flexibility of a dedicated walking or running shoe.

review_title: Lightweight, comfortable and versatile — perfect travel sneakers
body_en: I'm 41 years old, 5'2" and about 120 Ibs. I normally wear a size 6-6.5, and my foot measures approximately 9.2 inches long. I ordered a size 6, B gray Before purchasing these, I owned only three pairs of sneakers: running shoes, black platform Adidas, and white platform Reeboks. However, my platform sneakers aren't ideal for long walks or workouts, which creates a problem whenever I travel. For me they arrived in perfect+new condition.), tried just one on, and the sole+arch+heel support was PERFECT and so cushioned. Loved the look of them, but unfortunately they were just an inch too short for the length of my foot, my big toe was *just* scuffing against the tip of the shoe, even in my thinnest/smallest pair of socks. Truly as advertised, minus the sizing discrepancy - which was user error due to my ignorance of the brand styling and sizing. Honestly if you’re scanning through reviews and at your wits end, just order a single size, or a size and a half up. This is the way of ordering online when you can’t try the product on immediately. The shoe is comfortable and easy to slip on and tie. Laces are a little short but they’re genuinely fine to tie loosely about once, twice if you pull them taut for more length. Easy to replace the laces if you’re particular about that. Such a cute shoe, it was perfect for what I needed - absolutely worth reordering for the correct size, I don’t even mind the return process because I caught a glimpse of a genuinely worthwhile, simple, straightforward shoe that I’ll wear often for walking+working out. Even arrived in an adhesive-lined, resealable, bag for convenient and secure returns if needed be - I got a free return! Just printed the labels and secured them on the bag, and inside. (The default order for me arrived with the resealable adhesive lined bag, and inside of that was the brand’s shoe box, for anyone curious on those details.) Don’t stress! Take the leap of faith on the Skechers D’Lites. Order up a size, and at most a size and a half, so your toes aren’t squished if you need that space. Excited to receive my 10 wides! Edit, Monday August 24th, 2026: 10 Wides came in! Perfect fit with extra breathing room - Got 16,000 steps in already! review_title: Love the look, but sizing way off- has pros and cons
body_en: I'm female but men's sneakers tend to fit better. I like the way these Under Armour sneakers look. They have good symmetry according to the shape of the human foot. I also really liked the lacing system. It was these thick rounded "protrusions" of material so that the laces could go through, and the way these "eyelets" are shaped (thicker and flat) you would need fewer of them to make the shoe lace stretch out over what would be two eyelets. This is good because on one hand it may be trouble to string a shoe lace over a lot of regular style eyelets (holes on the area which I think may be called an "eyestay") but then if you skip putting the lace into some eyelets then , in my opinion it gives the distribution of of the lace on the sneaker a very awkward look, if you can get what I mean. I really dislike lacing systems in which there are just thin strips of string (or sometimes short strips of "ribbon" ) sticking out of the sides on top of the sneaker where the tongue is. If the string or strip of ribbon breaks then it is not easy to repair or is even impossible to repair. It makes the entire sneaker useless. So the lacing system on the Under Armour Men's Charged Surge 4 Sneaker is overall my favorite kind . I also like that the area of the highest eyelet is not rigid and hard. It is important for the upper-eyelet area of a sneaker or shoe to be properly flexible and /or cushioned (though also not of flimsy material). The area of the upper-most eyelet is the area that will push right into your upper foot as you bend your foot in the process of walking or running. This can hurt or cause friction. However , as with other Under Armour sneakers I find that at least certain styles can have odd sizing. I normally use a Women's size 10 so that translates to Men's 8 to 8.5 (which can depend on the style) but I find that in Under Armour I have to use a complete size up. I ordered these UA's in size 9.5. I tried them on. They fit but I was not sure if they would start to hurt my toes should I start walking long distances in them. I could not risk it. I sent them back. I may re-order them in a larger size even though they would look a bit too big. Another thing I did not like about this sneaker is that the sole at the heel part is designed in a way that when you walk with the sneakers on they make a noise like a shoe with a very hard heel with sharp edges would make, not a softer light noise like a sneaker should make. I do wish that this sneaker came in slightly wider widths. It may feel more comfortable than having a rather pointed type of toe-box area. So there are pros and cons to this sneaker at least in my opinion. I would definitely recommend them though. It can depend on your needs.

review_title: Comfortable, lightweight, and true to size
body_en: I work on my feet all day for 10 hour shifts on concrete. I need a shoe that's supportive, comfortable, durable, and lightweight. I've only had these shoes for a day and I can say so far they're comfortable, supportive, and lightweight. The first thing I noticed is they're very true to size. I typically wear a 43 EU wide shoe, so I checked the size chart and ordered the corresponding 11 wide. They fit like a glove right out of the box. I also like the wide variety of colors they come in. It's very hard to find fun, colorful shoes if you have larger feet, much less ones that also come in wide widths. So finding these in my size was a huge plus (I got the raspberry and electric lime on black). I like the thin, stretchy heel cup that hugs my heel rather than the typical thick, plushy heel cups that most shoes have, which is just foam that covers a sharp plastic stabilizer. The first place my shoes always wear out is the heel cup, and I'm being stabbed in the heel with that plastic stabilizer. I'm hoping this shoe won't have that issue due to the different heel cup design. They are definitely supportive and I can feel the arch support on the inside of my feet. I tend to underpronate so arch support is important for me. While they are true to size, there isn't much vertical room in the shoe for any additional insert. I typically put some odor eaters inserts in my shoes (again, 10 hour shifts) and they made the shoe a little snug on top. I'm sure they'll loosen up as they wear in, but it's something to keep in mind if you typically wear an orthotic or use another type of insert. They're also very lightweight. I don't feel like I'm clunking around in a heavy brick of a shoe, like I sometimes get with very cushiony shoes. Shoes that are too heavy tend to fatigue my feet and legs after long shifts. They're not so light that I forget I'm wearing a shoe, but they're also not noticeably heavy either. I wish the toe box was just a little wider, but it's not squishing my toes a noticeable amount. I just tend to prefer a wide, roomy toe box. This one is probably a little wider than a typical athletic shoe, but just not as wide as I wish it was. Overall, so far very happy with the shoe. Will update if I run into any problems, but if they continue to perform excellently I can see myself buying another pair.

body_en: Beyond the fact that I have always been an athlete, I must admit that I have a huge passion for sneakers. I buy them all the time, I can't stop. I have about 30 pairs of my favorite brands, which is quite a few. Naturally, Under Armor is on the list and also among the top positions for preference. They are not among the most "technical" shoes but they are certainly among the most beautiful and comfortable that can be found on the market. These UA Charged Assert 10 are beautiful and well thought out. The fit is excellent, the shoe fits well and the sole, in my opinion, has the right consistency to support a good run, offering cushioning and rebound but without giving in under the weight of the step. To be clear, the sole is made of foam, not the memory type: it is not one of those that give the sensation of walking on hard-boiled eggs like Skechers or like various Nikes. The ultra-soft, slipper-style ones are fine for a few steps, maybe a plane flight but you can't go running or walk on them for tourism for an entire day, not without having pain in your feet. To run you need a sole like the one on these Under Armor ones: not rigid but reactive and supported and the upper cannot be a sock. That also needs to offer some structure on all sides. This is a shoe designed for racing and has the right technical contents. If it is not the sporting performance that interests you and you are considering this shoe as a denim sneaker, well, in my opinion you are still in the right place because on an aesthetic level, these shoes have nothing to envy of Adidas, Puma, Nike and co. As for the numbers, I can tell you that I generally have a 42 and, on Under Armor, I have always purchased the 42.5 with success. HI!

review_title: Great sneaker, one of the most comfortable fitting Skechers I own
body_en: New Review: For Charcoal Grey with Black Accents - Size 13 XW (my first Skechers XW I have ever tried) This review is based on my initial impressions after wearing them for a bit, though (so they last longer) not wearing them for my usual few mile walk. I bought these in 13-W when my usual Skechers size is 13 M and to be fair I think I can get away with 12.5 M but I have always got 13's "force of habit". I saw the great price on these 13 XW’s and despite never trying the Wide Width Sketchers on until today, to took a chance on these. First .. I have a black and gray pair of the Vigor's and while Memory Foam or non-Memory Foam Skechers ... I have loved the fits of all of them. (There is a reason this is my go-to brand, even if my newer Sketchers do not last as long before needing a repair or two, like Skechers bought a few years back). The Vigors for some reason are THE MOST comfortable "model" of Skechers I have, and I have no complaints about any of them. I am just going to sort of aswer my own pre-buy question about the Wide Widths here. I do realize that every single person's foot is different but I will give a little background. Before Skechers, I was not buying the "top brands" (though i did have two pairs of Reebox that lasted a decent amount of time and felt great).... No matter the brand or size I was at the time (talking back in High School)... the brands I went with seemed so narrow that I always went with wide-width ... ALWAYS. Every since I bought my first pair of Skechers, I never needed to... the M aka normal fit was always great. As I said I bought these XW width, because of the sale (nearly 1/2 of the retail price). My question (pre-purchase) was are they like significantly wider… dare I say “comically” wide. Around the upper is where I notice it most and MAYBE right toward the middle left to right (barely) but .. they ARE wider it seems but nothing that would make me want to return them like “oh that is way too much for me”. I have ONE pair of New Balance and it is XW too and it’s sort of the same thing in a way … I prefer the regular fit (say in Skechers I’d describe the 12/12.5’s that SOMEHOW fit me ok .. as “comfortably snug” … I feel the sneaker all around my foot but even the normal fits are NOT TIGHT), but the XW (maybe just tied a tad tighter to make them feel more like the normal fits) are A-OK for me so far. Maybe when I wear these out for a long walk I may change my mind, but I think they will be ok. Assuming I do not have the issues some others have had with the eye-lits holding the laces tearing (for the record I have seen that in negative reviews but never had a pair of Skechers do that to me BEFORE)... I am happy with these. I would go with regular (M) 13's in the future but if a style I like comes up on a good sale XW width … I’d be ok with them I think. The Memory foam is great and as I said the other Vigors are the most comfortable pair of Skechers I have and I already LOVE the fits of all the other models. I am not sure how long the memory foam will last but some people say that when their's go, the "sneakers are trashed" ...eh ... for me I usual have some extra padded insoles that make sneakers feel like slippers they are so comfortable. Even WHEN (and it will go ... it's just nature) the memory foam goes bad so to speak... I will just slip a pair of those insoles I have anyway in and no big deal. The Fit back to front is great (as always with Skechers from my experience) and as far as a few negative reviews go saying how they are the most uncomfortable sneaker they ever had ... I just question A) if they are getting the correct size ... B) sort of the same thing ... do they need wide width for wide feet and getting regular width, maybe? ... The one thing I CANT comment on with this exact pair though i have to say other Skechers I have gotten recent needed to be repaired sooner than I'd like (the Black Downforce model I have comes to mind)... so longevity I cant comment on, even though I admit (note: I wear mine a lot in the sun in Florida summers so maybe adhesive wise holding the sneakers together, the extreme temps and humidity play a role. With Skechers (unlike my one pair of Filas which ... are ok now i admit) there has NEVER been a "break-in" period for me. Years back even with the Reebox that i liked .. there was at least a few day break-in period before they'd go from "ok/good" to "REALLY comfy". One thing I almost missed before finishing this review is that I have a pair of Pebble(brown)/Black "Afterburn - Strike off" sneakers and while i like them I thought the brown in them was going to at least in part be "Suede like". I just noticed that while not all of the grey/charcoal in this pair is ... some is that suede type material … I really like that sort of look, myself .. not sure how long it will stay looking good in the hot Florida summers though. As if i even have to say it, I am happy with my purchase and would recommend these. I just HOPE they last longer than they did for some other people who had bad luck with them. Update after one, 2-4 mile walk. - I have to say that I still do like the regular 13's better but these ... these aren't bad. If anything, AT TIMES it seemed like they were slightly too big and while in a steady stride (I do a constant walk ... not slow... not a run either) ... these seemed almost normal. I also have to say that while I have tied the tops a little tigher... i have not messed with the way they are somewhat losely laced, out of the box. Really right now the ONLY way I'd return these is for the same price or lower, I could return these for a full refund AND get the same exact style and color for instance in 13 M's (regular fit), but even then I'd say these are not bad at all ... if things change more overtime i cant say but "slightly bigger" than I'd like is not bad at all and I got a GREAT deal on these price wise. -------------------------------------- Original Review for a Black with Grey accent.... Size 13 (My usual size) First (even with that title) I want to preference this by saying I have only worn these around the house a bit .. I want to keep them in good shape, longer and I only bought these because they hit a sale price i couldn't pass up, though I love Skechers, dont get me wrong .... could Skechers (any) last longer than they do (say with or without minor repairs)? ... yes I will be honest, but Skechers is still my go-to brand. Like I said in the title, these MAY BE the more comfortable out of the box pair I own ... and with or without memory foam (These DO HAVE memory foam), I love Skechers anyway ... one reason they are my go-to brand is how A) They are the best price versus some other brands when i can catch them on sale B) They do last longer than SOME other brands ... though I do admit it's been a good number of years since I owned some Reeboxs and I always liked them for longevity. Style wise, I love these too ... When I saw the look, "includes memory foam", and the fact that I got them for nearly 1/2 price (note: if a bit higher in price, I'd still say I think they are worth it) compared to the normal Amazon price ... I didn't even think about, I just placed the order and I dont regret it one bit.

These Reebok BB4500 Hi2 high tops are a solid throwback-style sneaker, but they definitely feel more like a lifestyle shoe than anything performance-focused. First impression is good — the design has that classic high-top basketball look and they’re easy to wear with jeans or casual outfits. They look better in person than I expected, especially if you like retro styling. Comfort is decent for everyday use, but not amazing for all-day standing or heavy walking. The cushioning is fairly basic, so after a few hours you can start to feel the lack of support compared to more modern sneakers. Fit runs a bit narrow for me, especially in the toe box, and there’s a short break-in period before they start feeling more comfortable. Once broken in, they’re fine for casual wear, but not something I’d choose for long walks or sports. Build quality feels okay for the price — not premium, but not cheap either. The leather upper holds up well, and the outsole seems durable enough for regular street use. Overall, these are good for style and casual everyday wear, especially if you like the retro basketball look, but they’re not a comfort-heavy or performance shoe.

review_title: Reebok Club C Double Platform Sneaker
body_en: Review: Reebok Club C Double Platform Sneakers I’ve been wearing the Reebok Club C Double Platform sneakers for a while now, and they’ve definitely become a go-to in my rotation. If you’re into classic silhouettes with a modern twist, these are a great choice. Style: The platform sole gives the traditional Club C design a fresh, elevated look—literally. It adds just the right amount of height without feeling over-the-top. They pair well with everything from joggers and jeans to dresses and skirts, which makes them super versatile for casual or slightly dressed-up looks. Comfort: Surprisingly comfy for a platform sneaker. The cushioning is solid, and the shoe feels stable and supportive, even after a long day on your feet. I wouldn’t call them ultra-lightweight, but they’re definitely not clunky either. Fit: They run true to size in my experience. The leather upper is snug at first but breaks in nicely after a few wears. If you have wider feet, you might want to consider going half a size up, especially if you wear thick socks. Quality: Reebok did a great job with the materials—good leather, clean stitching, and a durable sole that holds up well. They’re easy to clean too, which is a bonus if you like that fresh-out-the-box look. Final Verdict: If you’re looking for a sneaker that balances retro vibes with a modern edge, the Reebok Club C Double Platform is a solid pick. Stylish, comfortable, and versatile—definitely worth it. ⸻

review_title: Hard to Beat for the Price
body_en: I purchased these for a business trip to Italy and wore them daily for the two weeks that I was there, during which I walked extensively. For me, there was a break-in period of a few days; before it loosens up, it will bite your heel, so I recommend wearing bandages or heel pads initially. Following the break-in, it's a very comfortable shoe and has served me well. I purchased a wide, and for this shoe, I found the width agreeable; in my experience, Cole Haan wide widths tend to be hit or miss (i.e., a wide is sometimes not all that wide). In terms of durability, I would not expect these to remain in good condition for more than a year if you wear them daily. The leather is not of high quality, but it's acceptable for the price. Expect them to crease very quickly if not using shoe trees. That doesn't bother me, but I know some find it objectionable. All in all, I like them and would buy them again. It's a comfortable alternative to traditional dress shoes for the office and works equally well for casual wear. Most higher quality options cost at least two or three times as much, and many are unavailable in a wide.

To start things off: these appeared as Women’s when I added them to my cart (I think it’s a bug with having W for wide sizes) but I can confirm they showed up as Men’s which is what I ordered. Good: These shoes are really nice and much lighter than I expected, a good budget alternative to Common Projects and substantially more comfortable (what I was looking for). If you’re looking for a classic white leather sneaker without any real branding these are a great option. Bonus points for being available in Wide widths, although the toe box seems to be the only part with any notable width added (midfoot is still a little narrower than I’d like). The leather is extremely soft so they’ll break in and crease quickly, but that’s pretty standard for white leather sneakers. Bad: Mine had DEFINITELY been walked around in before and had a few marks on them (see pics). I don’t mean just little creases from being tried on in a store, these had small scuffs/scratches - even one where somebody tried to fill a pinprick with white out - and some phantom purple stain on the end of a lace (honestly looks like grape jelly). On a positive note the sole and insole themselves are spotless, so either somebody wiped them down very well or just clumsily wore them around indoors before returning them. The heel piece is stiff like others have mentioned and I can see that being uncomfortable during break in. There’s also a slight color variation between the leather and sole, I’d call the leather more ivory and the sole/laces straight white (fine for me but might be a deal breaker if you were looking for perfect white). Ultimately I need these ASAP and I’m not seeing any more left in my size, so I’ll keep them despite showing minor signs of wear. I figure since they’re white sneakers I’ll probably scuff them up after 1-2 wears anyways so it’s not the end of the world. UPDATE: 90 days in, these are great shoes. They’re way more comfortable than my Vans/Converse and have held up pretty well. The sole is soft so it does show wear quickly (although cleanly) but the upper itself feels almost like calfskin once it’s broken in. I’ve also gotten a number of compliments on them which is rare. These have become my go to sneaker and I’ll buy another pair once these wear out - albeit probably not on Amazon because these were clearly worn a number of times before they showed up.

review_title: Support properly, and perform their duty day after day
body_en: I wear only New Balance Extra Wide shoes. The explanation is neither mysterious nor flattering: I carry more weight than I ought to, and my feet insist on reminding me. These provide the width I need along with an arch that actually supports rather than merely decorates the insole. In a marketplace increasingly devoted to fashion masquerading as function, that is no small achievement. I generally buy the 608 V5 cross trainers because they consistently have the best availability in Extra Wide. That alone earns them a place near the top of my shopping list. They also come in enough colors to satisfy whatever mood strikes you. I've accumulated black, white, brown, blue, and now gunmetal. Evidently, when I find something that works, I become a predictable voter. The shoes are comfortable from the first day, supportive during long walks, and forgiving during those moments when the bathroom scale reminds me that arithmetic is undefeated. They have become my everyday footwear, accompanying me through errands, appointments, and the ordinary business of retirement. No product is without its legislative amendments. Occasionally the shoelaces seem unnecessarily thick or comically long, as though drafted by a committee unable to agree when to stop. It's hardly a constitutional crisis, but every so often I find myself wondering whether someone at New Balance has a side business selling extra lace. Because these are my primary shoes—and because I place a bit more stress on them than their designers probably envisioned—they're generally ready for retirement after about six months. I don't regard that as a defect so much as the inevitable consequence of constant use and a user who could stand to lose a few pounds. Institutions endure because they reliably perform their intended function. The same may be said of these shoes. They are not flashy, they make no extravagant promises, and they will not transform your life. They simply fit well, support properly, and perform their duty day after day. In an era of exaggerated marketing claims, there is something refreshingly conservative about a product that succeeds by quietly doing exactly what it was designed to do. Five stars.

I am extremely happy with these New Balance 608 V5 shoes. They are very comfortable right out of the box and provide excellent support for walking and standing all day. The fit is true to size, the quality is outstanding, and they look great with almost any outfit. The cushioning helps reduce foot fatigue, making them perfect for work, daily activities, or casual wear. I would definitely buy them again and highly recommend them to anyone looking for comfortable and durable sneakers.

I got these for power walking and compared to walking in slippers ( My usual) they’ve really upped My game, enabling me to do a 10 min 34 sec. Split time on a 2 mile walk yesterday. Not bad at nearly 64 yrs old. I also ordered a couple pair of Sketchers. Here’s how they compare. The NB is way more substantial, with a harder, no doubt more durable rubber sole, while the Sketchers have a much more soft, almost a foam sole. NB has much more support and stabilization, but is not quite as comfortable out of the box as the NB. Some of the new balance shoes have an awkward slip on/lacing system. That is very difficult to get snug.. The NB is lighter due to the flimsier foam soles. Don’t skimp on the width. These tend to run narrow even the extra wide isn’t quite wide enough on one of the models I got. Verdict: if you’re simply doing casual walking, perhaps the new balance might fit your needs, but if you’re going to be putting in the miles, like I do at break next speed, you’d probably do better to stick with the new balance.

review_title: Cute, Comfortable, and Supportive Shoe That Holds Up During 12-Hour Shift
body_en: I absolutely love these shoes and find them so cute and comfortable. I bought these shoes for work 3 weeks ago and have worn them every shift since. Of course my feet do get tired since I worked 12 hour shifts, but they have never once hurt like they have with other shoes I have worn in the past. The sole of the shoe is cushioned and has not compressed after use. I have never once slipped while wearing them on polished and tiled flooring, so they provide traction. The mesh on the side is breathable. They are a little harder to keep clean because of the fabric near the lace toe and heel. After three weeks of use, I have not noticed any loose stitching and they have held up very well. Additionally, there isn’t any noticeable wear to the outsole. These shoes are good for casual wear, work, travel, and light exercise.

body_en: First off, these New Balance Arishi V4, running shoes are very comfortable, do not drag when walking. They put a spring in my step. One might say I have too many shoes. Maybe. But I like having variety and I'm always looking for comfort as well I wear a size 12, I am 6 ft 1 250 lb and I frequent the gym 4+ plus days a week. I am lean but do like to do cardio. The feeling, sweating it out. I was looking for a pair of comfortable shoes to walk around in. Just randomly browsing. I was looking for specific shoes to help with my arches, which I barely have. I have flat feet and my left ankle pronates. It's an injury from my skateboarding and boxing probably more than 20 years ago. I am not sure as one day I noticed my ankle was off. Maybe I am just made this way LOL. I wear a special insoles made custom. I have many other decent insoles, full and 3/4 length. It's not as bad as it seems, at least I say that lol. They are meant and can't work for longer distances. That isn't to say the Arishi V4 isn't great in their own right. They do it 90% just as well for a fraction of the price. So if you're looking for a running shoe or walking shoe, generally a decent shoe and you have flat or pronated feet, look no further. These are the shoes for you. I noticed they don't have many reviews, so trust me definitely worth trying. For the price I paid, < $30ish, I think they are better than other running shoes I've owned. review_title: Actual comfy shoes with support, but definitely not good on wet concrete :p

(avid 25+ year Converse All Star wearer here). they seem to have excellent traction, i've only worn them out once (after i received my exchanged pair) and it was a comfy walk on dry sidewalk. the shoe quality seems to be good, i have noticed a few frayed threads sticking out, but honestly, i do not care. i dislike wearing shoes inside my home, especially on a top floor apartment (noise to neighbors, yes im nice and do everything to prevent heavy walking), but recently have an issue with tendonitis in one foot. OBVIOUSLY from my chucks and getting older and how i walk around at home lol, but listen, I wore these inside for a hour and hardly any noise, i felt floaty... normally I just slide around in socks. OVERALL: the wearability seems on point, I don't have any complaints yet. they are for work where I will be on concrete all day. I already know these will help. I can't really say HOW to choose your size, just do the research and buy a pair with the idea- you may have to exchange for a different size, and with that said- DO NOT LOSE THE TAGS (i removed mine from shoes but kept in great condition inside box for the return), DO NOT WALK OUTSIDE, KEEP EVERYTHING IN GOOD CONDITION- IN CASE- you have to do an exchange. They're worth the money, I honestly believe so and I don't like any shoe but converse all-stars. oh, and they send you an extra set of longer laces which i prefer. hope this helps anyone :) **Update- I wore these to work in a bakery/coffee/cafe, where there is concrete flooring. And by the dish area and after mopping it is too wet for these. These have 0 protection on slip-resistant. They aren't stated to have it, but who knows, some say there is good traction on wet sidewalks, so thats a plus. I can no longer wear them at work, did it for 1 day and can't risk it. The other downside for me, they have memory foam which traps heat, living in Texas, this is a huge nono. I'm learning so much about shoes in the last week I could be a sales person. If you're looking for slip-resistant, breathable. No. I did size up to a Wide which I thought would help, but these shoes are too tight for my preference. For years I used to buy $10 velcro shoes at Walmart. Granted, they received pretty rough treatment from me, since they doubled as work shoes in the yard and garden, so I would get another pair that I wore in "public" when the first pair started cracking. However, the last three years or so, the thin rubber soles, that were just glued to a sort of stiff foam rubber backing, began to become unglued and flap around after only a few days or weeks of use. Determined to get a year's worth of use, duct tape, done in a certain way, accomplished that. Sort of. After a while it just got to be ridiculous. Thus my search at Amazon to find some velcro shoes of better quality. And these are it. Three months and they haven't even shown signs of cracking. Plus they clean up well. The cheapos at Walmart were made of a sort of imitation brushed leather that showed stains and scuffs easily. With the smooth surface on these, a damp cloth works wonders on heavily dusty shoes. I only have three complaints that keep this product from getting five stars: 1. As others have noted, the straps are a little short. Not really a complaint from me, just a very mild annoyance. The velcro holds much better than the cheapos, so there's that. But that is what makes it annoying since you can't easily get your finger under the strap in order to get the shoes off quickly. 2. I love that there is much more sole to this shoe, it's just that compared to the cheapos, it's like wearing high heels. (And, yes, I did have some platform shoes in the seventies.) Plus they make more noise, especially on laminate flooring. They also aren't the most comfortable shoe in the world, but, hey, I would rather go barefoot anyway. 3. The price. Not a real biggie, but I would rather have paid about $10 less for this pair of shoes. But if they continue to hold up as well as they have so far, I will definitely buy these again.

The top part of the shoe is a mesh like fabric cloth, and allows for some breathability on a hot day. The overall quality of the shoe is pretty decent, and I detect no flaws in the craftsmanship. I am pleased with the shoe upon my initial experiences. Time will tell how the shoe holds up. But in the meantime, I am happy with it. For what I paid ($42), this is a pretty decent pair of athletic shoes. I can't speak to its performance for running, but for my intended use in the gym, this shoe fits the bill quite well without breaking the bank.

review_title: 318 Days. One Pair. Every Single Day. Here's How They Held Up.
body_en: 5 out of 5 stars: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 318 Days Later: Daily Worn as My ONLY Pair of Shoes I wanted to wait before reviewing these because I wanted to see how they'd hold up over time instead of writing a review after only a week. These Skechers became my only pair of shoes. I wore them every single day from September 14, 2025 until July 29, 2026 and beyond. That's: 318 consecutive days, my primary (and only) shoes, everyday walking, no rotation with another pair. I paid just under $50 after tax when I bought them. That works out to roughly 15.7 cents per day (about 16 cents/day) over their lifespan. I've attached a photo collage showing exactly what they look like after those 318 days so people can judge the durability for themselves. Comfort: The Air-Cooled Memory Foam was easily my favorite feature. They were comfortable right out of the box and stayed comfortable for most of their life. The Hands Free Slip-Ins also worked exactly as advertised. Being able to step into them without bending over never got old. Durability: Considering these were my only shoes, I'm impressed. After 318 days, The uppers are still intact: Check No holes in the toe mesh: Check Stitching has held together: Check Soles are still attached: Check They still have usable traction: Check The main wear is exactly where I'd expect it: Heel lining has worn through. The insole covering has rubbed away in the heel area. The cushioning isn't as fresh as when they were new. The outsole has gradually worn from everyday walking. Nothing unexpected happened. They simply aged from daily use. Would I buy them again? Yes. In fact, I'm planning on buying the exact same pair again today. Not because these completely failed, but because I got almost 11 months of everyday use from them for about 16 cents per day, which I think is excellent value. I'll will keep this pair as backup shoes for rainy days, yard work, or quick errands. If you're looking for an everyday walking shoe that's comfortable, convenient, and can hold up to nearly a year of constant use, I think these are a solid choice. Would I recommend them? Absolutely!

For many years I faithfully wore the Nike Air Walk and then, low and behold, they stopped making them! They were one of very few "wide" shoes that Nike made -- plus they were all leather, very light, provided great support and were super comfortable. So, once they were discontinued, I was on the search for a replacement.... I didn't think of Skechers much as a "serious" brand, mostly because I didn't know much about them, but it turns out they do sell some wide fitment shoes, and these, for me, are an absolute great fit! I tried a pair, a few years back, and have faithfully replaced them every time, having once again found a pair of shoes I really love. They are very similar to the Air Walks, in comfort and durability, although, sadly, they don't last as long as the Nike's did. Then again, they are about half the price! So, I don't feel too bad having to replace these more often. I'd say a pair lasts six to eight months, where the Nike's used to last more than a year, but, as I say, these are a lot more affordable to replace, so I guess it kind of works out, cost wise. For me, the most important thing is having a pair of shoes that are comfortable, versatile and look good enough to wear to work with good Levi's and a sport shirt, yet can also be used for walks or even light hikes. Since they are all white I have the same problem I had with the white Air Walks, which is that they tend to get dirty kind of quickly, but, like the Air Walks, they also clean up beautifully with some shoe cleaner and a bit of Sneaker whitener, so they tend to look great until they simply wear out -- in my case it is usually the side that eventually blows out -- which was the same on the Air Walks, but just didn't happen as quickly. Even so, six to eight months of life is pretty good to get out of them, considering I wear these pretty often throughout the average week. So, I'm a fan now, and in fact will be getting a second pair of these to have around, since they also come in blue and white, and that way I don't have to clean these up as often, and that's actually an improvement over the Air Walks, since they only came in the white or solid black. With these, I can now have an all white pair, and now can also have a more "casual" sneaker for other looks or outfits or uses, and, since two pairs is not much more than one pair of what the Air Walks use to cost, I'm actually a bit ahead of the game. I'm very happy with these, and I'd certainly recommend them highly!

review_title: Superb quality, but not for my feet
body_en: I have been a huge fan of Sketchers for awhile now; their quality and craftsmanship are superb and their shoes are built to last! I am pretty tough on my shoes, and demand a lot from them. I need a shoe that offers sturdy support, as my back is pretty much a wuss, and will freak out about the littlest things, including lack of shoe support. Sketchers has always delivered everything I need in a shoe. I was excited to try this design, because I am on my feet a lot at work (I work 12-hour shifts on concrete floors at a manufacturing plant). From what I've read online, these shoes were ideal for my needs, because they offered the support I need for both my back and my feet. I also like the fact that these shoes have a very aggressive tread, as I do a lot of outdoor activities including hiking and camping, and I expect my everyday shoe to hold up for the task (even though I have dedicated hiking boots, sometimes you want a lighter-weight option, especially when you're carrying 60-80 pounds on your back). When these shoes arrived, I was impressed with the amount of tread and grip they provided. It wasn't like the dinky little tread you see on most shoes, it looked like they took a tire, cut it to shape, and put it on the bottom of the shoe - Sketchers meant business when they designed this shoe! The material is warm, but lets your feet breathe, so your feet stay nice and warm in the winter. I can't say how they are in the summer, as I didn't own them in the summer months. Inside, there is a lot of padding all around, especially in the tongue of the shoe, which is nice - it gives a real nice snug fit to keep the shoe in place without having to really strap down the lacing tight. There is a huge amount of padding in back on the bottom for your heels, which, for me, is where the problem comes in. For most people, this would be a very nice feature, but for some reason, it ended up hurting my heels pretty badly, almost to the point where I didn't want to walk from one end of the house to the other. After wearing them for just one 12-hour shift, my feet were screaming, and all I wanted to do was either sit back in a chair with my feet up or lay in bed, just so I wouldn't be on my feet. I understand that every pair of shoes needs to be broken in, and during that time the shoes can be a bit uncomfortable, but not this much. While I absolutely like these shoes and have absolutely nothing against them (other than the heel issue mentioned above), I am forced to return them to Amazon. Please remember that this is not the case for most people - my feet are extremely picky to begin with, and simply put, these shoes just aren't for me. I really like the quality and materials that Sketchers used to design this shoe, and I can honestly say that I believe they are a shoe that will hold up to use and abuse for quite a long time. Despite them not being the right shoe for my feet, I would still highly recommend them, but be aware that there is a large amount of padding in the heel area, and will lift the heel area of your foot upwards somewhat. I don't hold anything against Sketchers or these shoes. In fact, once my return is processed, I plan on buying a new pair of my go-to shoes, which are the Sketchers Men's Stamina Nuovo sneakers. All around, great shoe, just not for me (unfortunately).

review_title: Level of fragrance really depends on the type of candle you choose!
body_en: Have ordered 2 of these candles - the Peace + Tranquility (white) and the Reflection + Clarity (light blue). Both were excellent, but the Peace + Tranquility definitely had a lighter aroma / more subtle than the Reflection + Clarity. Saw several reviews stating they couldn't smell the candle. There are 2 likely reasons - 1: if you have a large room/house that you want to smell the candle in, I highly recommend the coffee table jar, which has 3 wicks and smells much stronger than the single wick candles. However, since it has three wicks, it does burn through faster. I light mine every night for a couple of hours after dinner while I clean the kitchen and they each lasted about 2-3 weeks with nightly use. Secondly, it definitely seems to vary with the the fragrance type you use. The Peace + Tranquility is very light and fresh smelling, but not at all strong. The Reflection + Clarity is very strong and pleasant, it kind of smells like laundry detergent though (this can be a good or bad thing depending on how you feel about your laundry detergent!). I have a large house with high ceilings and you can smell the Reflection + Clarity everywhere after being lit 30 minutes or so. I like to use the R+C type of I make a very strong-smelling dinner (with lots of garlic or onions) where I want to refresh the house. I use the P+T when I just want a nice calm scent. I will definitely order again, but will probably try another couple of types since they seem to vary quite a bit...

review_title: Wenn Bruce Wayne eine Kerze wäre…
body_en: When my wife handed me this candle and told me to stop smelling like a mix of bicycle storage and a granola bar, I didn't know that I was about to enter a different fragrance league. I lit it, leaned back - and the room changed. Our street mutt mix with German Shepherd eyes and the libido of a battering ram suddenly rolled up at my feet, sighing. Even the cat briefly stopped haunting the living room like a furry Gollum. The scent? Absolutely manly, but without coming with a mallet. More like someone walking into a room with a tailored suit and secrets rather than armpit hair and chainsaws. The blend of sandalwood and oud fills the room in an elegant way - warm, spicy, almost meditative. I caught myself taking a deep breath, even though I'm usually a team "window open, smell out" team. The design of the candle is pure style. Black, noble, with a gold label that doesn't scream but whispers: "I'm here because I'm worth it." The burning behavior is also great – clean, quiet, no buzzing or soot. It's sitting on my desk now as I write this review and I feel a little bit like an author writing the novel of his life in a Victorian gentlemen's club. The only thing missing is a fireplace - but as long as that candle is burning, that doesn't matter. She doesn't smell like Christmas, or like cotton candy, but like a man who knows who he is. Or at least wants to act like he knows. Note: I received this product for free for review purposes through the Amazon Vine program. My review is based on my honest and independent experience.

review_title: A Stunning, High-Tech Twist on a Classic Scented Candle
body_en: This is an exceptionally unique and high-quality scented candle that delivers a true "wow" factor the moment it is lit. It comes securely presented in branded, factory-sealed manufacturer packaging with molded foam insert protection, making it an ideal option for easy gift wrapping. Design & Build Quality Jar & Aesthetics: The heavy glass vessel features a vibrant, glossy finish reminiscent of a shiny candy apple red—making it an absolute showstopper for holiday decor or ambient home accents. Dimensions: It stands roughly 3.85 inches tall with a 3.25-inch diameter. Wax & Fragrance: Made with a smooth, creamy soy wax blend and a central cotton wick that provides a steady, clean burn. Upon removing the top protective label, it emits a soothing, well-balanced aroma of soft lavender blended with fresh eucalyptus that subtly fills the room. Functionality & Heat-Activated LED Display What sets this candle apart is its clever heat-activated lighting mechanism: How It Works: A subtle metal sensor prong sits near the wick, connected to a battery-powered circuit in the base. Once the wick is lit, heat travels down the sensor and immediately triggers micro-LED lights embedded within a liquid-gel ring inside the double-walled glass. The Effect: The entire red jar glows with a gorgeous, warm ambient light while burning and turns off automatically when extinguished. Longevity: The internal power source is permanently sealed in the base for safety. While non-replaceable, it is designed to last through the full burn life of the 12oz soy wax. (Note: If you decide to clean out the jar to repurpose or refill it later, just take care around the sensor prong so a new wick can sit adjacent to it!) Durability & Value From the solid weight of the glass to the flawless execution of the LED sensor, this candle offers fantastic build quality, functionality, and charm. It elevates a standard scented candle into a captivating centerpiece. It makes a marvelous, memorable gift or personal indulgence, and offers incredible value for such a creative concept.

review_title: Nice, Cute Candle but Scent Doesn’t Match Description
body_en: The Viyffo 18 oz anniversary candle arrived nicely packaged in a cute box with a small red ribbon on top, which made it feel gift-ready. Inside, the candle was well-protected in thick foam, so there were no issues with damage during shipping—definitely a plus. The candle itself comes in a sturdy glass jar and is visually appealing, with white soy wax decorated with colorful candy sprinkles around the outside. The gold screw-on lid adds a nice touch, and overall it has a fun, festive look. However, there were a couple of downsides. The label had some noticeable glue or grease marks, which took away from the otherwise polished look. Also, while the scent is advertised as vanilla and candy, it came across more citrusy to me. It’s not an unpleasant smell, just not what I expected. The scent is fairly light, so it works best in smaller spaces if you want to actually notice the fragrance. On the bright side, the candle burns slowly, which helps it last longer. For $9, it’s a decent-sized candle and a good value, but the mismatch in scent is a bit off-putting.

Mushrooming create more carbon in the air which builds up on paint, walls, and in air filters. I know this because I burn a LOT of candles and try to keep carbon to a minimum. In this recent batch, the wicks are too long for size of the candle which can lead to mushrooming. I’ve started to trim the wick before burning, hoping this well help. Still a great product, but this is definitely a change from previous orders. Fyi only.

review_title: Perfect quality non-drip candles for the value
body_en: I have lit these candles at dinner on multiple occasions and every morning when I enjoy my espresso ritual 🥰 The result has been consistently as I expect. The color of the candles are spot on as described. They fit perfectly with the standard holders. There has been no dripping wax through out the whole burning time until I blew them all out. As you can see in the attached pictures, I set these candles super straight on the holders. We talked, laughed when dining at the table and also moved around in the kitchen. The burning wicks were not completely straight up, and yet, didn’t make the hot wax streak down at all. In fact there was very minimum hot wax where the flame was. There was no direct breeze in the kitchen area. There was no opened windows either. The furnace was also not on and I do not use space heater or AC, or electric fan. About the promised burning time, please understand that the “up-to-8-hour” suggestion is just an “estimate” of the maximum burning time. That time varies depending on certain conditions such as how high the flame is, how long the burning wick is…If I constantly trim the wick down to minimum and keep the flame very short, the candles can burn up to that promised hours for sure. This is a legal and lawful way that all vendors use to market their product’s details and descriptions. It has been applied to so many different products out there in the market (not just these items) such as meds/drugs (they all mention that results may vary), or gasoline usage per mile can also vary,…I am just a regular consumer/shopper. I do not write reviews in exchange for free products or incentive from vendors/sellers. I am very pleased with the performance of these candles. I do not mind if they do not burn the full 8 hours. Like I said, that detail is not important to me. The burning time can fluctuate and does not affect the quality of these candles which is the non-dripping part that is far more important to me. I do not want to keep removing layers of wax from the holders after burning candles, or having hot wax on my table or furniture, or ruining my table cloths.

review_title: Great candles, all arrived whole during transport
body_en: Pleasant smell. Lasts a long time, due to size and to slow burn rate. They burn well, and the fire doesn't go out by itself, or get too strong or weak. Not too much smoke. Eventually, as the candle burns down, the top of the glass container gets covered in black soot, affecting esthetics for some. Still, there's no risk of wax dripping, so they're clean. No tunneling, but you do have to let it burn until all the wax is melted (no hard walls on the sides). The glass feels strong and substantial. I haven't had issues with glass breaking during use or during transport. They're shipped to you in sturdy, thick, well-insulated packaging. Since my area is prone to blackouts, I keep a lot of candles at hand. I also like them for smell and ambiance. I bought about 10 of these when they were on sale, and none arrived broken! If you lay one on its side in warm weather (which happened to one of mine during transport), then the wax softens and pools sideways, and can make the wick inaccessible. What I did was set the candle upright in a pot of hot water (in such a way that the hot water touched the walls of the jar and would soften the wax, but without there being so much water that it poured inside the jar). That reset the wax and revealed the wick. Problem solved. Amusingly enough, Amazon wants me to review this candle's "taste"! I can't speak to that!

review_title: Warm, Cozy, and Perfect for Fall!
body_en: I bought this spiced pumpkin candle to get into the fall mood, and it has quickly become my favorite seasonal scent. The fragrance is strong enough to fill the room within minutes but not overpowering—it’s the perfect balance of pumpkin, cinnamon, and a hint of vanilla. It makes the whole house feel warm and cozy, almost like fresh pumpkin bread just came out of the oven. The burn time has been impressive. I’ve been lighting it in the evenings for about two weeks now, and it’s still going strong with an even melt (no tunneling, which is a big plus). The wax burns cleanly, and the wick is easy to trim, so maintenance is minimal. I also appreciate the design of the jar—it’s simple and seasonal without being overly flashy, so it looks nice on my coffee table and blends well with my other fall décor. If I had to mention one small drawback, it’s that the scent is so good that I find myself burning it every day—I may run out sooner than planned! My tip: grab two if you want it to last the whole season. Overall, this candle is a must-have for anyone who loves fall scents. It’s cozy, long-lasting, and makes your home instantly feel festive.

This is by far and away my favorite candle. The smell is both comforting and arousing. When you open the candle for the first time the aroma alone, without burning the candle is enough to fill a room. Commonly that is what I will do. Just open the candle, not light it, and let the fragrance fill the room for a few hours. Eventually it is time to light it. Both wicks need to be burning for it to evenly burn down. I hate candles that leave wax in the jar as they burn. This one does not do that. All of the wax burns off as it is used up. At the bitter end all that is left is a jar with two burnt up wicks and a very small amount of the wax residue. This also burns for a very long time. I’d say, end to end, if you light it and just let it burn it would keep burning for about a week total. Maybe 10 days. I have bought many of these and burning it about an hour or two per night I’d say I get roughly 4 to 5 weeks of use out of it. Maybe a little less than that with weekend burning a bit longer sometimes. It normally comes in a very sturdy package. I like to order it with other goods so as to give it extra protection in shipping. But I have had them deliver it in the original shipping container no problem. That being said I have also gotten one broken like some other reviewers mentioned. What I did was take a small ball peen hammer and carefully broke away the glass outside. Piece by piece. Cut myself doing this but not bad, so follow these instructions with caution. Nevertheless, once I got all of the glass away and carefully removed the bottom glass (which is glued to the candle wicks so use a knife [again carefully] to separate the wick bottoms from the glass) so I could put the candle into a container and light it. It worked. But again that happened once and I have bought MANY of these over the years with no issues. Let me also say that pumpkin spice is my favorite. And the ladies like it too. Good for getting in the mood if you know what I mean. But I have burned other flavors and they all seem to be top quality. Very fragrant and delicious smelling. Everybody loves the smell of my house when I burn these. I don’t write reviews unless I truly hate or believe in a product. So just know that I think this product is worth the cost, definitely. Hope you enjoy one as much as I do.

review_title: One of the most satisfying and best scented candles out there!
body_en: Hello everyone, my name is John and this is my honest opinion on this product. You can buy candles almost anywhere. With so many retailers and brands, it is hard to choose which ones to buy. Maybe you like how one smells but it is too small. Maybe you like how one smells but it is too expensive. Well my fellow candle buyers, look no further than the Vanilla Bean Woodwick Jar Candle by Virginia Candle Company. Now I have to say this was a gift for a friend but I have owned many different Virginia Candle Company Candles in the past and I have loved them all. They are a conversation piece around the holidays and whenever family is over I always hear, "What is that smell? It smells great!" or "What is that crackling sound, is that the candle?" Now, for someone who has never bought one of these candles before, you may not know that these candles actually do make a nice crackling noise as they burn. Nothing dramatic enough to make the in-laws think there is a raging, crackling fire in the other room at thanksgiving, but not quiet enough that you have to tell everyone to quite down so you can admire that satisfying crackling and popping coming from the candle. It is honestly probably my favorite attribute to these candles. I just love that little crackle so much because of how satisfying it is .Anyway, you are probably tired of reading me talking about my obsession of crackling candles so here is what I can tell you about the smell. They have many great scents that are a pure delight to your nostrils. These candles give off a scent that is noticeable, but not too faint. The scent is strong, but not overpowering. Each of these candles smell just perfect. Now the reason I choose to review this specific scent of candle is because it is my favorite. It truly smells like vanilla bean, one of my favorite smells. Another notable attribute to these candles is the duration of burn time you have. Unlike your traditional wick, these candles burn longer and better. Plus they give a pretty little flame which looks a bit different from your generic candle. Anyway, thats all I really have to say. In conclusion, I would highly recommend this candle or any other candle by Virginia Candle Company. If you ask me how high these candles raise the bar, I would tell you that they are the bar. Nothing can beat them. But in all seriousness, I really do enjoy these candles and have given quite a few of them to my friends and family as gifts after they had asked me about them. These candles really are unique from any other because of the wick they use. If you are considering these candles, I really would encourage you to purchase one because you will not be disappointed with it. I will admit they are a bit pricey compared to your generic candle, (I mean seriously, 18 dollars for a candle) but these truly are a higher quality of candle compared to other brands. Anyway I hope this review was helpful, thanks for reading! ;) (Disclamer: I was not payed or sponsored in anyway to review this product. This is my honest and unbiased opinion on this product. Once again, I hope this review was helpful.)

review_title: A Luxurious Scent That Turns Any Room Into A Cozy Retreat

It’s the perfect combination of floral and woody without being overpowering. The candle is hand-poured with a soy wax blend for a clean, even burn, and its fragrance lingers long after it’s been extinguished, filling the room with a cozy, spa-like ambiance. Whether you’re unwinding after a long day, reading a book, or simply creating a relaxing atmosphere, this candle instantly elevates the space. It also burns evenly and lasts much longer than many candles I’ve tried, making it well worth it. If you enjoy luxurious, warm fragrances with a touch of floral elegance, I highly recommend giving this one a try—it feels like bringing a high-end boutique hotel right into your home. ✨

review_title: Un set aromático, decorativo y muy agradable para regalar 🕯️🍂
body_en: This set of 6 AOOVOO autumn scented candles is designed for those who enjoy creating warm and cozy environments at home. The selection of scents revolves around typical fall fragrances, such as apple pie, cinnamon, spiced apple, pumpkin pecan pie, pumpkin spice and baking spice. It is a proposal very oriented towards those looking for a homely, sweet and comfortable feeling. 🍎🎃 Each candle comes presented in a carefully designed glass jar, so it not only works as a scented candle, but also as a small decorative element. In addition, the set arrives in a gift box, something practical if purchased for birthdays, seasonal details, Christmas or simply to surprise someone without having to add too much packaging. 🎁 Aspects to highlight ⭐ 🍂 Variety of very autumnal aromas. The set includes six different fragrances, all with a warm and sweet aromatic line. It is a good option for those who enjoy pastry, cinnamon, apple or pumpkin type smells, especially in living rooms, bedrooms or reading corners. 🕯️ Soy wax. The candles are made with soy wax, a fairly common alternative in better quality candles. It tends to offer a cleaner, more uniform burn than other conventional waxes, as long as they are used correctly. ⏳ Good total duration. The set adds up to 1197 g of wax, with an announced duration of up to 300 hours in total. This allows them to be used for a long time if the fragrances are alternated or turned on in moderate sessions. 🎁 Careful presentation for a gift. The box and glass jars with gold labels make the set look nice without preparing additional packaging. It's a simple detail, but it adds up a lot if bought as a gift. 🏡 They provide an uncomplicated environment. They are candles designed to create a cozy feeling at home: a quiet dinner, an afternoon of reading, a family gathering or an autumn night. They do not require installation or special accessories, beyond the usual precautions when using candles. Aspects that can be improved ⚠️ 🍰 Sweet aromas that won't be for everyone. The selection is very focused on warm, spicy and baking fragrances. Those who prefer fresh, floral or more neutral aromas may find them somewhat intense or sweet. 🏠 Best for medium or small stays. Although the set is complete, the actual intensity of the aroma may vary depending on the size of the room. In very large spaces it may be less noticeable, especially if there is ventilation. 🔥 They require the usual precautions. Like any candle, they should be used with caution, away from fabrics, drafts, children or pets. It is something obvious, but important in a product of this type. Final rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4.5 out of 5) 🕯️🍂 This AOOVOO candle set offers a very pleasant combination of autumnal aromas, good presentation and generous duration. It stands out especially as a gift or as a decorative accessory for those who enjoy warm environments and sweet aromas. I don't give it five stars because the aromatic selection is quite specific and may be too sweet for some tastes. Even so, it is a highly recommended set for those looking for cozy, beautiful and easy-to-give candles.
A really great range with wonderful scents. Both safe and attractively packaged. You wish for the cold days to come so that you can light the candles and enjoy their pleasant smell.

I bought this set mainly to scent the house during the fall and winter, and I find it very successful. In the sense that the olfactory signature really gives a warm atmosphere in the house. The different gourmet scents, like apple cake or cinnamon, create a warm and comforting atmosphere without being too cloying. Despite everything, we remain on the same family of scents, with almost the presence of cinnamon in all of them. The candles are well presented and the glass jars look neat.
