The combustion is regular and the soy wax melts evenly when good usage practices are followed (let the entire surface melt during the first uses). The scents diffuse gradually and create a pleasant atmosphere without being too intrusive. Obviously I'm not a fan of soy wax...we would prefer beeswax for candles that last longer. I also like that I have six different candles. It is a box that is suitable both for yourself and as a gift, especially as the holidays approach. It's a good gift idea that people will like! As with most scented candles, the intensity varies depending on the size of the room. In a large living room, the scent will naturally be more discreet than in a bedroom or office. Despite everything, be careful, these are very present fragrances! They will take over any other smell in the house! You have to want your interior to smell like a candle, and not just a candle that smells discreetly. In the end, it's a pleasant box set that perfectly sets the mood for fall. The scents are varied, the presentation is neat and the candles offer good value for money for those who like to create a warm atmosphere at home.

review_title: Great Polarized Sunglasses for the Price
body_en: I picked up a pair of the FEIDUSUN Polarized Sunglasses a few months back, and they've honestly become one of my go-to accessories whenever I head out. I was on the hunt for a good pair of polarized sunglasses that were both stylish and effective at protecting my eyes, and I think I've definitely found that with these. The black retro design is really classic and versatile. They go with pretty much any outfit I wear, whether I'm dressed casually or a bit more put-together. I like the clean and simple look of them, and more importantly, they feel really comfortable on my face. They're not too heavy, and they don't pinch my nose or the sides of my head, even after wearing them for several hours, which is a big plus for me. I've had sunglasses in the past that become uncomfortable after a while, but these have been great. But beyond the looks, what really stands out about these sunglasses is their performance. The polarized lenses make a significant difference in reducing glare. I notice it most when I'm driving on a sunny day or when I'm around water. The clarity of vision is so much better, and my eyes feel less strained. I've even worn them while fishing, and the difference in being able to see below the surface of the water was noticeable. It really cuts down on that harsh reflected light. UV protection is, of course, crucial, and I feel confident that my eyes are well-protected with these sunglasses. That gives me peace of mind, especially during those really bright sunny days we get here. Knowing that I'm shielding my eyes from harmful rays is a big factor in why I choose to wear them. After using them pretty regularly for the past few months, I can also say that they seem to be quite durable. They've been tossed into my bag countless times, and they still look and function perfectly. The hinges feel sturdy, and the lenses haven't scratched easily, which is always a concern with sunglasses. I'm not exactly the most careful person with my accessories, so the fact that these have held up well is a testament to their build quality. One thing I appreciate is that they don't feel flimsy or cheap. For the price point, I was pleasantly surprised by the overall quality. They feel like a more expensive pair of sunglasses than they actually are. Whether I'm driving, walking around town, or just relaxing outdoors, these FEIDUSUN sunglasses have become my constant companion. They provide the right amount of shade without making everything look too dark, and the polarization really enhances visual clarity. In short, the FEIDUSUN Polarized Sunglasses are an excellent buy for anyone looking for a stylish, comfortable, and effective pair of polarized sunglasses. They do a fantastic job of reducing glare and protecting against UV rays, and they seem to be built to last. I'm really happy with my purchase and would definitely recommend them to others.

I’m a nocturnal creature, always have been. Naturally I am up until dawn, and only rouse at dusk. Being that I do 12 hour night shifts, I really don’t have a need “flip” my schedule, and can exclusively live the vampire life. I don’t know if it is cause or effect, but I’ve always been photosensitive as well. As a child, I didn’t realize that it wasn’t normal to squint constantly on a sunny day. I ruin every photo from the flash. I even get light-triggered debilitating migraines. I NEED my sunglasses. So after losing my second pair of Ray-Bans, I couldn’t stomach the cost knowing that I have a tendency to set things down and walk away absent mindedly. Most likely I had dropped them in a parking lot from my purse or hoodie pocket, as I had done in numerous occasions, documented by the scrapes and scuffs on the lenses. It’s just not practical for me to splurge on the item I never prioritized when juggling keys, phone, and bag. My first lost ones were black and silver Clubmasters which I’ve had a hell of a time replacing in those classic colors, much less the polarized ones. I really missed how stylish they were. Then my classic Wayfarers disappeared. In scoping out to actually buy new Clubmasters, did I come across this package deal with both styles and super affordable. I wouldn’t feel shame about my treatment of sunglasses at this price point. When I received them I was super impressed. They were a little lighter weight, but overall seemingly sturdy and nice quality. Superb style, I wouldn’t be ashamed of not wearing designer. So I threw them in my bag to leave for work in the evening, to keep one in the car and save one for my purse. The next morning leaving work, it was nice and bright outside, and after a long shift, it is just the worst to be tired and blinded on a congested commute home. As soon as I hit the exit, I whip out my new glasses, and noticed I still had some eye strain, chalking it up to physical fatigue. Drive home, same thing. The next day I used the other glasses, and it again felt too bright. It only then occurred to me that these are not as dark as I was used to with my Ray Bans. I gave it a few more days, and realized these just don’t seem to make a difference for me. Feels like I’m wearing nothing at all. (Nothing at all, nothing at all…) Taking them on and off, I feel as if there is barely a difference, like they’re a placebo. I had focused so much on getting polarized, I forgot how the most crucial part of sunglasses is the darkening effect. They appear to be dark when you look at them, so it’s kind of an odd thing, and why it took me a day or so for it even to click with me with what was wrong. These are so weak, I feel like the polarized effect didn’t even do much for glare. I can even see clearly LCD displays that I couldn’t see previously even with other discount brands, so I’d say even this feature isn’t as good as it could be. Perhaps these may be useful in other sporting uses that people wear these glasses for, or could even be tinted enough for some, but absolutely not for me. If you’re truly dependent on eye protection and can’t leave the house without them like me, just keep looking.

review_title: Finally, She Found Glasses That Do Both
body_en: My wife usually buys glasses based on how they look, not necessarily how they function. God forbid you get a pair of glasses that actually protect your eyes. No, they have to match the purse, sandals, dress, watch, and underwear all at the same time. I kind of like it that she matches the underwear, but the rest isn't that big of a deal to me. So imagine my surprise when she finally found a pair that "look cute" AND actually do something useful. We're making progress! She pulled them out of the box and was immediately happy with them. They look good, they fit well, and they're polarized. Then I noticed something. Here's What I Found... One of the lenses wasn't sitting quite right in the frame. I was able to pop it back into place, but unfortunately, it looks like it had been sitting that way in the packaging for long enough to leave a slight warp along the top of the lens. See the pictures for what I'm talking about. That's probably a quality-control issue that should have been caught before they left the factory. Other than that, though, they're actually pretty nice glasses. And the polarization is a big deal for us. My wife and I spend a lot of time outside, especially at the beach, and polarized lenses make a noticeable difference in bright sunlight. My wife can get headaches from the sun, so having properly polarized sunglasses is much more useful than simply having really dark lenses (or trendy cute ones). There's a difference between dark and actually cutting the glare, and these do the latter. Well, I'll Be... Maybe next time we see dolphins at the beach, she'll actually be able to see them. My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens. So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed. Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses: - they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing. - For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available: --- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized' --- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others --- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available --- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT: ----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm ----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length ----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length --- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass: ----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140 ----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135 ----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145 ----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140 ----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160 ----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135 ----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135 ----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135 - once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs: - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get. I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly. Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

review_title: Yeah, this ain't it. Real review right here.
body_en: I wear Maui Jim's, Smiths, and Suncloud (also by Smith). I want a new style so... Ordered them. The fit: great. The wright: great. They feel durable. They feel comfortable. The style is great. The lenses: useless and I would honestly say no chance I'd wear these sunglasses. Literally zero chance. Why? 1. Put these on and look at a regular light bulb. Any light bulb at home. You'll see three images of that light bulb, one to the left which is faint, one to the right which is faint, and the bulb itself in the middle. Not joking. It's as if there is a "glare". This is because the lenses are not perfect thickness and magnification, and the lens coating are layered poorly (I am guessing here). Put on a pair of Maui Jim's (or other high end brand) and you'll see just one light bulb. I'm not making this up. Try it. This will affect everything you look at, brighter objects more. 2. Look at these glasses while wearing high end glasses. You'll see the polarization film -- especially around the bridge and arms. Now, look at the high end glasses through these. You wont see the polarization film (it's there, you just can't see it). High end lenses have much better and even polarization. The lenses on these glasses are simply too cheap, the flaws are really noticeable. I wish they were better, really do. I love this rimless style.

I’m a nocturnal creature, always have been. Naturally I am up until dawn, and only rouse at dusk. Being that I do 12 hour night shifts, I really don’t have a need “flip” my schedule, and can exclusively live the vampire life. I don’t know if it is cause or effect, but I’ve always been photosensitive as well. As a child, I didn’t realize that it wasn’t normal to squint constantly on a sunny day. I ruin every photo from the flash. I even get light-triggered debilitating migraines. I NEED my sunglasses. So after losing my second pair of Ray-Bans, I couldn’t stomach the cost knowing that I have a tendency to set things down and walk away absent mindedly. Most likely I had dropped them in a parking lot from my purse or hoodie pocket, as I had done in numerous occasions, documented by the scrapes and scuffs on the lenses. It’s just not practical for me to splurge on the item I never prioritized when juggling keys, phone, and bag. My first lost ones were black and silver Clubmasters which I’ve had a hell of a time replacing in those classic colors, much less the polarized ones. I really missed how stylish they were. Then my classic Wayfarers disappeared. In scoping out to actually buy new Clubmasters, did I come across this package deal with both styles and super affordable. I wouldn’t feel shame about my treatment of sunglasses at this price point. When I received them I was super impressed. They were a little lighter weight, but overall seemingly sturdy and nice quality. Superb style, I wouldn’t be ashamed of not wearing designer. So I threw them in my bag to leave for work in the evening, to keep one in the car and save one for my purse. The next morning leaving work, it was nice and bright outside, and after a long shift, it is just the worst to be tired and blinded on a congested commute home. As soon as I hit the exit, I whip out my new glasses, and noticed I still had some eye strain, chalking it up to physical fatigue. Drive home, same thing. The next day I used the other glasses, and it again felt too bright. It only then occurred to me that these are not as dark as I was used to with my Ray Bans. I gave it a few more days, and realized these just don’t seem to make a difference for me. Feels like I’m wearing nothing at all. (Nothing at all, nothing at all…) Taking them on and off, I feel as if there is barely a difference, like they’re a placebo. I had focused so much on getting polarized, I forgot how the most crucial part of sunglasses is the darkening effect. They appear to be dark when you look at them, so it’s kind of an odd thing, and why it took me a day or so for it even to click with me with what was wrong. These are so weak, I feel like the polarized effect didn’t even do much for glare. I can even see clearly LCD displays that I couldn’t see previously even with other discount brands, so I’d say even this feature isn’t as good as it could be. Perhaps these may be useful in other sporting uses that people wear these glasses for, or could even be tinted enough for some, but absolutely not for me. If you’re truly dependent on eye protection and can’t leave the house without them like me, just keep looking.

My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens. So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed. Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses: - they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing. - For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available: --- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized' --- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others --- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available --- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT: ----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm ----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length ----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length --- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass: ----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140 ----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135 ----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145 ----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140 ----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160 ----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135 ----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135 ----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135 - once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs: - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get. I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly. Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

review_title: Order somehow switched and still 10% doubt to the authenticity

Nearly every detail is copied. So, after looking at different sellers, watching videos of real and fake glasses I searched for SunglassHut on Amazon. They are the brick and morter authorized sellers. I saved my order to my shopping cart from the Sunglasshut page on Amazon and they were $199.95. When I checked out I noticed it said "sold by and fullfilled by Amazon for $118. This made me a little worried. I wanted to pay the extra money to be sure they were authentic.Why the seller changed I have no idea. Now my review. I am still not 100 percent they are authentic but about 90 percent sure. All the research I have done and the fakes I have seen have all the same markings on the glasses and the case. The only thing the real ones have that the fake ones do not are that the ends of the plastic ear pieces curve a little bit. all the pictures and videos I have seen show the fakes with straight ear pieces at the very ends. The lenses are indeed polarized as you can tell from looking at different peoples rear windows of their cars in the sun. The glass has an invisable checkerboard pattern with the glasses on and it goes away with them off. The blue mirroring is nice and you cant see your eyes from other peoples perspective unless sunlight is coming in from the sides. The fit is good and I will go to my local Sunglasshut store to have them adjusted. Overall 4 stars because of placing in my cart from the sunglasshut page and then it being changed to sold and fullfilled through Amazon, and the fact I still have that 10% doubt they could be fakes.

I purchased these in July of 2014. I paid $189 for the black frame/netural gray Glass lenses. They have held up very well. No scratches, and the temple springs are as good as they were when new. I take good care of them, keeping them in their case when not in use, and clean them regularly using a bit of dish soap. I love the clarity and weight of the glass lenses, as they are superior to any of the composite lenses I've had a chance to compare them to, including their own brand's plastic lenses. (I spent some time in a Bass Pro Shop comparing these to Costas, Smiths, and Oakleys) These are my everyday casual and business wear glasses. These are great for driving; the polarization on these lenses is superior to Oakley in my opinion, and I love how well the polarizing lenses cut glare. These also work fantastic for cutting glare on watery surfaces like lakes and rivers, but honestly I am too fearful of losing these in the water to wear them near it! I would not wear these for any activity requiring a lot of movement, such as playing sports, since they are heavy, and because most of the weight is in the lenses, they are likely to fall off. During every day use though, these are secure enough that them falling off your head is a non-issue (unless you try to "store" them on the top of your head when not in use - DON'T do that!). My only grip with these is that after wearing them continuously for more than an hour, they do become a bit uncomfortable on the bridge of my nose.. taking them off for a brief period helps with any discomfort, but this is the sacrifice I'm willing to make to wear glass lenses. I will admit I keep a pair of Oakley flak jackets around for outdoor activities, and for times when I worry about scratching the lens (such as bumming on the beach). However, the quality of these are fantastic and I am glad I purchased them... I will buy another when the time comes. Couple of tips: - In my opinion, I would NOT suggest purchasing these glasses in a composite lens... the glass lenses are so much clearer. In my opinion, these frames are designed to hold a heavy glass lens in place. I would prefer to purchase a composite lens in a "frameless" or "semi-frameless" option to take advantage of the lighter weight of the composite lenses, and the ability to swap lenses on some brands of frames. - The shiny black frame, on the inside of the frame actually reflects light at some angles, and can be distracting. Wearing a hat eliminates this completely, but if you're looking for a frame that completely blocks the sun due to the way it wraps and fits your face, this probably isn't going to be sufficient.

After a visit to the eye doc it was presumed that my "fave" sunglasses may not be up to the protection job they might have had when new. I was told that many brands of glasses only lightly "coat" the lenses for UV protection especially the "plastic" lenses. Cheap glasses may not have any UV protection at all despite the claims...who tests them?? Nobody?? What apparently isn't told is that these coatings may/do deteriorate over time AND using alcohol lens cleaners and dish soaps may also remove coatings. My research indicated that the more expensive brands have higher quality and more durable UV coatings (impregnated or baked into the glass) that are important to protect your eyes from sun damage -- not just shading. Although my "Faves" were not inexpensive, they were 4 or 5 years old and apparently had inferior to perhaps zero UV blocking abilities today! Long story short, I researched the MJs and found that these glass lenses have superior harmful UV blocking. my Polycarbonate "faves" lenses...less so and were (only effective when new) likely "coated". I did a side by side comparison between these and my old "faves" and I was blowen away by the superior clarity and color crispness of these Maui Jim glasses. You only have one set of eyes...treat them with respect and invest in quality eye ware...not for fashion but, so you don't lose you vision acuity in later years when it's too late to undo damage. Suffice it to say....these are GREAT sunglasses and even look good...a bonus!!! My eyes deserve the investment. Yours do too!!

If you’re outdoors a lot or need high-quality sunglasses for everyday use, I’d highly recommend the Maui Jim Stingray.

I grabbed this Liphisy 64″ Tripod with the remote and phone holder, and suddenly my clips looked way more polished — like I actually intended them to look that good. 📸 Story: From Shaky Hands to Steady Shots The first time I set it up, I clumsily bumped it while trying to angle the phone for a timelapse. Instead of toppling over like my old mini tripod usually did, this one stayed planted, and I just laughed — because that little bit of stability made such a difference in every shot I took after. 📏 Sturdy & Adjustable The height range up to 64 inches is genuinely useful — whether I’m standing tall for overhead shots or crouching down for detail work, the tripod adjusts smoothly. The legs feel solid and stable, even when fully extended, and it holds heavier phones or small cameras without wobbling. 📐 Multi-Angle Flexibility It’s easy to tilt and rotate the phone mount to whatever angle I need. I’ve used it for vertical videos, landscape framing, and even side-angled product shots — all without feeling like I was fighting the setup. 📱 Remote & Phone Holder The included remote control is a small but actually handy addition. I can start/stop recording or take photos without rushing back to tap the screen. The phone holder grips the device securely — no slipping or awkward readjustments in the middle of a shot. 🛠 Build & Ease of Use Assembly was intuitive — nothing confusing about the knobs or height settings. It feels durable yet lightweight, so I don’t mind moving it from room to room or bringing it outside for midday shots. 🎥 Everyday & Creative Use Whether I’m filming lessons, timelapses of tanks, cooking clips, or just group photos with friends, this tripod adapts well. It makes videos look way more intentional than anything I’ve done handheld. 💰 Value for Money For a tripod that reaches a full 64″, includes a remote, and works with both phones and lightweight cameras, this feels like good value. You’re not just paying for functionality — you’re upgrading the quality of what you create.

I just opened the box and unfolded it and set my phone in it and it was ready to go. I love the rose color and there is no way my phone is going to fall out and I expect it to work for many years. It is durable and the perfect height. My phone is very protected. I would like to buy another one to keep beside my chair while I'm watching TV. I highly recommend this wonderful phone holder. I just fold it up and it fits into my pocketbook and is very portable.

My first reaction to the stand was "I wish I thought of this design first." It is an excellent design for versatility, and its construction is superb. The metal is thick stock with a durable finish (perhaps it's even a powder coat). The hinges are sturdy and their adjustment has a smooth resistance that keeps the phone securely in position. The base has non-slip silicone pads that do a good job of preventing the stand from moving on a desk surface when using the touch screen of the phone. Similarly, the upper part of the phone bracket has two silicon pads to stabilize the phone. When using my phone while charging, the cord can be passed through the back of the stand to keep it out of the way. The bracket piece that holds the phone is the proper height for placing the phone in either the vertical or horizontal position. Finally, the stand folds flat for storage in a backpack or a small bag. In summary, this product is a winner.

review_title: This is a great product and works well.

Having a desk accessory that requires zero assembly and holds my iPhone steady without constant readjustment is a major win for hands-free productivity. The folding design so convenient, and this high-quality accessories has optimized my workspace as well as this is travel-friendly.

Omg!! I love it. It’s perfect for zoom meetings, watching videos, talking on the phone, or just scrolling through Amazon! It’s very light yet durable. Small enough to fit in my purse. There is no assembly, the piece comes folded. A plus if you are charging your phone. I highly recommend this for your cellphone.

Does what it needs to do. I got it to hold my iPhone 15 by my computer for calls while working. Little smaller than I anticipated, but I should have read the specs more closely. Would not be good with larger phone. Am happy with the product.
I love this phone stand. It works great and it's pretty to look at. Hold my phone firm, can be adjusted, and the charging cords fits while it's on the stand.

Having used the Adjustable Cell Phone Stand for several months now, I am excited to share my experience with a product that has not only met but exceeded my expectations in every way. **Design and Build Quality**: Right out of the box, the first thing you notice is the sleek design of the stand. It's modern and minimalistic, blending seamlessly with any desk or table setup. The build quality is exceptional – it's sturdy and stable, made from high-grade materials that feel durable and reliable. **Adjustability and Flexibility**: The standout feature of this stand is its adjustability. It offers a wide range of motion with vertical and horizontal rotation, allowing me to position my phone at the perfect angle, whether I’m on a video call, watching a video, or simply glancing at notifications. The height adjustment is smooth and holds the phone securely at any level. **Compatibility**: This stand impresses with its universal compatibility. It easily accommodates phones of various sizes, from smaller models to larger smartphones. The grip is firm yet gentle, thanks to its rubberized holders that protect the phone from scratches. **Portability**: Despite its sturdy build, the stand is surprisingly lightweight and compact, making it easy to carry around. I’ve found it convenient for both home and office use, and it even fits into my bag for when I’m on the go. **Stability and Non-Slip Base**: The stability of this stand is remarkable. Even when tapping the screen vigorously, it stays put, thanks to its weighted base and non-slip pads. This stability gives me confidence that my phone is safe and won’t topple over. **Ease of Use**: The stand is incredibly user-friendly. Adjusting the angle and height requires minimal effort, and it maintains the chosen position without any slippage. The design also allows for easy charging, as there’s ample space to plug in a charger without having to remove the phone from the stand. **Aesthetic Appeal**: The aesthetic appeal of this stand cannot be overstated. It looks premium and sophisticated, adding a touch of elegance to my workspace. The choice of colors and finishes is an added bonus, allowing for personalization. **Value for Money**: Considering its versatility, build quality, and the level of convenience it offers, this cell phone stand is excellent value for money. It’s a practical investment for anyone who uses their phone extensively throughout the day. **Final Thoughts**: The Adjustable Cell Phone Stand is a product that goes beyond the basics, offering unparalleled flexibility, stability, and quality. Whether for professional or personal use, it enhances the overall experience with your mobile device. Its combination of functionality, durability, and stylish design makes it a standout choice in its category.

review_title: Works for my Galaxy S25 phone
body_en: I used to have trouble remembering where my cell phone was in the house because I'd lay it down flat and then papers or other things would get laid on top of it and I couldn't find it again. Also, it can be difficult to see the screen when it's laying flat on a table and there's light from above you. This stand solved both of those problems. I liked it so much I bought two more of them so I can have one in the bedroom, one next to my computer and one on our dining table. It's adjustable so I use it with the holder part of it more vertical than the photo on Amazon, so it holds my phone at a better angle for viewing and is not as easy to tip backward. There is a hole in the back of the stand part of it for a charger cord but I don't use that. Even with the holder part having an open area for the cord to attach to the phone, the cord has to make a tight bend to get plugged in and it would eventually ruin the cord. I charge it with the cord coming from the front or side of the holder.

I use this stand on my desk because I get dual factor authorization requests texted to my phone. This stand holds the phone at a perfect angle so I don't have to pick up the phone to get face recognition. I have a case and a ring grip on it, and the phone still sits securely on the stand. Happy with this purchase
This is sleek and great for holding my cell phone on the desk.

body_en: I have been really happy with this tripod. The 1.8 m height is very convenient because it gives me more options for taking photos and recording videos from different angles. For the price, it is a useful and convenient accessory to have. I would recommend it to anyone looking for an affordable tripod with a good height and remote control.

review_title: A Stylish and Versatile Cell Phone Stand
body_en: I recently purchased the Doboli Cell Phone Stand for Desk in the adorable Pink color, and I'm absolutely delighted with it! This stand is not only functional, but it also adds a touch of elegance to my desk setup. First and foremost, this phone stand is incredibly sturdy and well-built. Made from premium quality materials, it securely holds my iPhone and even accommodates my tablet without any wobbling or slipping. The silicone pads on the base and backrest provide excellent grip, ensuring that my devices stay in place. The adjustable viewing angle is a fantastic feature. Whether I'm working, watching videos, or video calling, I can effortlessly adjust the stand to a comfortable position that suits my needs. It provides a perfect viewing angle, reducing neck strain and allowing me to multitask efficiently. Furthermore, the Doboli Cell Phone Stand is incredibly versatile. It is compatible with various smartphones, including iPhones and Android devices. I appreciate that it can also accommodate my tablet, making it a versatile accessory for all my mobile devices. The wide space at the bottom allows easy charging while the phone is resting on the stand. The design of this stand is simply delightful. The Pink color adds a touch of femininity to my workspace and complements my decor beautifully. It is compact and lightweight, making it easy to carry around or pack for travel. Overall, I highly recommend the Doboli Cell Phone Stand for Desk to anyone in need of a reliable and stylish phone holder. Its sturdy construction, adjustable viewing angles, and compatibility with various devices make it a must-have accessory. Say goodbye to cluttered desks and strained necks – this stand has got you covered!

review_title: Great for the price, not super stable
body_en: Super easy to put together, well constructed, and cute! The rose gold/pink color is a light pastel pink. The rubber grips on the base and on the actual holder help the stand to stay in place, and keep devices from sliding. For less than $10, it’s definitely worth the purchase. I also like that I can use it for my phone and my iPad, and works as a backup to hold/display my switch while not in use. Very versatile! I can also see myself using it to prop up notes for school, maybe a light textbook. CONS: If you have the stand extended all the way up (or at all) and are tapping on your device, the device and the whole stand shakes, which is annoying. So if you plan on using it to stream it’s not a big deal, but it makes it difficult if you’re planning to touch the device for any reason (like to press pause), and in this sense isn’t very study. I will not be using my iPad on it while it’s extended, as the stand falls this way, but if it’s not extended it’s more sturdy. If you don’t have it extended, it will still shake when tapped but not too bad. If you’re using a phone on it to FaceTime, the rubber holder blocks the mic and you’ll need to adjust it every now and then (which is kind of disappointing because I mainly purchased this to make it easier to FaceTime a loved one who’s far away). If you use a pop socket, you’ll need to remove it before using this stand or the phone slides off. Overall though, for less than $10, it’s an excellent stand. This is also a great gift idea.

I purchased the Doboli Cell Phone Stand in hopes of no longer having to lean my iPad against other items throughout the kitchen, bedroom or bathroom even. The assembly instructions are on the back of the products box, they are very clear & easy to read/follow. Although the holder can be pulled upward or lifted, i’m more comfortable with the holder being only upward. The product does feel a bit wiggly when it’s lifted with the iPad (I have the 10th generation for reference). The weight added to the holder appears to be appropriate if used for a smaller device (in my opinion), although, if you’re leaving your iPad in just one place, so far, it appears to do what it’s intended to. The box does mention it’s good to hold an iPad up to 9.7in in length. I’ll provide any updates if any damage occurs or accidents. So far i’m happy with the product, in regards to price and quality. 💗

review_title: Overall great but will not last for a long period of time
body_en: I bought two of these and have had them for about two years. I keep one of them on the desk permanently (the pink version). It's perfect for just chilling there, easy access to the charging port, and is adjustable. I love how you can adjust the height, tilt it forward/back, and turn it side-to-side. It comes in two pieces : the phone holder and the actual stand. It's a simple assembly- just click it into place. After two years of wear and tear, I can say that my pink stand is starting to crack at the point where the phone holder clicks into/on the stand and also upwards and downwards from that point. The two separate pieces have become a place of stress for the stand from general wear and tear. If you try to tilt the phone too flat (straight) and you have a larger phone (iPhone max pro here) it WILL fall out. Imagine being on zoom/FaceTime and tilting it to show something directly in front of you (->) and bam! out it falls. It has happened dozens of time to me. Overall great phone stand but I might try a new stand for my phone next time. The Good: Portable Adjustable Easy set up Looks great access to charging point The Bad: Not adjustable enough Will drop heavier/larger phones if tilted too far Limited durability - point of weakness

review_title: An In-Depth Look at the Nearly Flawless LISEN Cell Phone Stand: Versatility Meets Minor Shortcomings
body_en: I’ve had the pleasure of incorporating the LISEN Cell Phone Stand into my daily routine for the last two weeks, and overall, I am very impressed with its diverse functionality, elegant design, and the durability it brings to the table. The stand has made multitasking a breeze and quickly became an indispensable part of my office setup. Given the extensive period over which I’ve tested it, under various conditions and for different devices, I feel quite comfortable bestowing upon it a well-deserved 4-star rating. review_title: Detailed review: So far so good!
body_en: This is only the second tripod I've ever owned, and so far it's going really well! I was iffy about buying a $20 tripod, as there are so many cheaper options out there, but it's totally worth it! This tripod has a little bit of weight to it, which makes it feel sturdier. I will say it is a bit tall, even in it's compact form, so it's not very "portable". For instance, I put it in my backpack and it sticks out since it doesn't fit all the way into the bag. If you're going to be using this as a portable selfie stick while traveling etc, I think something lighter and more compact would be better for you; however, this works great if you're setting up the tripod for more stationary reasons. Moving on to the things I love about it: The legs on a tripod are arguably one of the most import features, at least for me. It's what's going to be holding the weight up and providing a sturdy base support. I love that the legs on this tripod are very much controllable/customizable. If you look at the main picture of this listing, the legs are not in the down-most open position yet. You can control how much you want the legs to open and "flare" out at the bottom. If you want super sturdy support, you can open them further out to provide a wider base. The locking mechanism is also very helpful as you can control how wide your base goes. I love this level of personalization because sometimes I want my tripod to take the least amount of space as possible. It's also very important for me that the legs open with ease. I broke my first cheap tripod because the legs were hard to control and I was trying to force them shut/open. The legs on this tripod open and close with ease, but a little push needs to be applied. The legs also have rubber bottoms to prevent slipping. I have not used this outdoors, so I cannot speak on its performance while it's windy out. I use this tripod to hold my iPhone 14 Pro and I've never had instability issues where it's tipping over. The phone mount is great as it stretches open on both sides as opposed to just one sliding mechanism- This makes it very easy to insert and remove my phone. Its got 4 flip locks to control the height. I don't typically use it at the tallest height. I'd say I use 2 flip lock's worth of height and that's already tall enough for me. There is no installation required, which is a huge plus. You only have to screw the phone mount, or the other mount if you're using it for another device. Takes seconds to screw in. The only criticism I have (which isn't even a big deal) would be that I wish I could immediately move a phone up or down while it's in the phone mount. For instance, if I have my phone set up in the phone mount, it points directly ahead in a straight line, however, sometimes let's say I want to capture more floor, so I wish I could immediately point the phone a little downwards to see more floor. In order to do this, I have to unscrew the little knob to control the range of the phone mount, move the phone facing more towards the floor, and then screw it back in place again. It doesn't take that much time or anything, but sometimes I want it to be a super quick and easy fix, specially if I just want the view to be a couple Millimeters more towards the floor. I do not use the Bluetooth remote, though it already came with batteries and ready to use. If you're an inexperienced tripod user like me and you plan to be using it in a public space, I recommend you get familiar with the set up at home; that way you can set it up and compact it back down fast and with ease. It only took me one minute to figure out how to use it at home and I could quickly set it up when I was on the go. All in all, I think this tripod is sturdy, easy to use, and it seems like it will last me a long time.

review_title: Best. Purchase. EVER. My tripod goes everywhere with me now!
body_en: This thang. Fabulous, fabulous, fabulous. Did I mention it's fabulous? This is probably the purchase i will enjoy using the most, second only to my Samsung Note 10 Plus. This tripod is to use with said phone. Hence my excitement. If we ever get paroled from Covid Quarantine, I will be able to take pictures of EVERYONE using this bundle of joy. I do, however, LOVE taking pics. Amateur photography is my thing, and this little toy has already brought me so much joy. It's super easy to flip up to whichever height you want it at to quickly set up for the perfect shot. I should mention that my phone is very well protected in a nifty little case which I also got on Amazon. It's therefore even bigger than the phone would be by itself. In it's case, my phone measures 6.75" by almost 3.4". The retractable phone holder opens adequately wide to accommodate and then securely hold my phone in whatever way I set it. I've got an alarming number of friends who drank iKoolaid and are in love with their iPhones. My Samsung though, with it's screen size and resolution, takes far superior pictures. They can snap inferior pictures with their iWatches, BUT I HAVE... THIS! The added beauty that an iWatch can't cover is being able to use the far better rear camera, instead of being confined to selfie mode, as seen on an iWatch. So this wins, every time, hands down. The knobs to adjust the height of the tripod are straightforward. You get increments of height added on for every know you unlock, as shown on the product description pictures. You can also stop it at any interim point you like. So if you need your camera at a very specific height, that is easy to accomplish. It is also super easy to switch your phone back and forth between portrait mode and landscape mode: it's a snap to do. I must confess that I have not bothered to link the remote control that came with this tripod with my phone to use it to take pictures. I can do that with a simple voice command or with my nifty phone stylus. So I may NEVER get around to sampling that aspect of this product. Either way, this has been the best gift to myself ever. Assembly, from pulling it out of its handy carrying case to full set-up with your phone clipped and ready to say cheese could be done in about 10 seconds easily. I can also use this for birdwatching, nature shots, and anything else I want to do. Really easy to carry around and flip out whenever you see a shot you want to line up. I love going out on nature trails to snap pics, so this will be used heavily by me. If I had any suggestion for improvement, it wouldn't actually have anything to do with the tripod: it would be that they probably could have put a light shoulder strap on the carrying case, a bit longer than the cord that is currently on it. So i may run a different cord through the loops, but I'm absolutely thrilled with this baby. Happy happy happy customer!

review_title: Sturdy, but there are some fine details that deserve consideration
body_en: The magnetic Tripod/Selfie stick arrived in the color and as described in the Amazon listing. The package included the selfie stick, a magnetic fill light, a USB charging cord, and a fabric case big enough to carry the stick and the accessories. The selfie-stick felt solid in my hand and appeared to be of premium quality.There is also a traditional tripod mount for a 360 camera or action Camera. The tripod was easy to set up, and extend to its full height. The tripod legs appeared sturdy. The magnetic fill-light easily attached to the back of the magnetic selfie stick. It had a dial that allowed for dimming and variable brightness. The magnet for the selfie stick seemed strong enough… but I did find myself accidently knocking my phone off of the selfie-stick when attempting to remove the magnetic light. Fortunately my phone landed on a plush carpet, but I did wonder about how well the magnetic mount might work in real world conditions, where I am often setting up the selfie stick on concrete, or perhaps in crowded areas. It seems like I will need to be careful to assure I don’t accidently dislodge my camera. I also found that the magnetic tripod mount was not as compact as the phone clamp mount that I have on another similar style selfie stick. The tripod mount is nice… but it doesn’t have a dial on it like other similar tripod mount, that helps fine tune the direction the phone/camera is mounted. At time of review this tripod/selfie stick has a price that is higher than comparable products. Although in theory, I like the idea of a magnetic phone mount, in practice I will likely use a more secure mounting method like a clamp mount, and this tripod/selfie stick will likely not replace a cheaper but similar product already in my camera bag.

review_title: Throw away your other selfie sticks and phone tripods, this is IT

No fancy locks, no twisting, just pull and leave. Its way too easy. Out of all the selfie sticks ive owned, this here, is BY FAR, the most innovative, convenient and well thought of piece that I simply have no reason to leave it behind with any trips I go to. It simply works as you want it to. Easiest 5 stars ive ever give. I highly highly recommend this supervision version of selfie stick+tripod combo.

review_title: Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!
body_en: I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings. The finish is very satin and may not be pleasing for those that enjoy glossy guitars though i think it's OK and seems tough enough. My GL1 came with a small blemish in the wood on the back which is an imperfection in the wood itself and not the finish. I would take 1/2 a star for the blemish but quality control is overall pretty good and the fret ends aren't noticeably sharp. I would not recommend this instrument for beginners due to the short fret spacing and slightly more difficult fingering for some chords. A 1/2 or 3/4 scale classical or steel string guitar will be a better choice for learning the fundamentals and will have more volume for performances later on when the player gains confidence. Who is this instrument for? number one, it's for me. I have been playing guitar for decades and have a soft spot for small bodied instruments and recently started playing my wife's ukulele due to my guitar being down for the count. Ukulele players might enjoy this instrument as a way to cross over to six string though the string spacing will take some getting used to. Guitar players who want a sturdy travel guitar will be well served by this instrument but will have to make peace with transposing everything up a fourth. Some players have used high tension strings to allow for standard guitar tuning. I'm not sure I will do so as I like the sound as it is and also play ukulele music. Overall I think the Yamaha GL-1 is a reasonable value for the money and I'm very happy with it so far.

69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes. This thing came quicky to me in Hawaii, and it is in perfect condition! Since it had nylon/classical type strings, it is going to take much longer for the strings to settle down and stop sretching. Way longer than my steel stringers. So, don't write a review after a few days complaining about this. All classical style nylon string guitars do this! Pick it up,tune it, play it, and keep tuning it. The tuners on mine seem just fine. It is a total blast for me to play. It sounds great, especially for the small body size. It has very good volume and sustain too. A bit stingy on the fret markers, both on the fingerboard and side of the neck. If you have big fingers, some chording might be a bit crowded. It doesn't have a truss rod. But, many classical guitars and many other guitaleles don't have them either. I have yet to read a review, or watch a video review, where the owner had a neck warp. In short, I should have bought one of these long ago. Update after more than a year now. I still love this little 6 stringer! I have been selling some of my amps and ukes etc. I had considered selling my Yamaha, but cannot do it! It is just such a great insrument. Mine is still perfect. Drawbacks? Few. The 17" scale is a bit tight for me. One string started unravelling after not too much playing. I was able to buy the one string and replaced it. I read a review somewhere where the writer returned his due to various flaws. Looking at mine it's hard to believe. I think Yamaha should make an option of the GL-1 that would come with an under saddle pickup with tuner and volume/tone controls. Great price, great instrument, great FUN!! 2/28/2025 update: Just wanted to say my estimation of this instrument has gone up if anything. I am taking super good care of it. It us holding up great. I had one of the wound strings start to unravel early and replaced it. Zero problems. After break in it holds tune as good or better than my other string instruments. That alone is saying a lot. The climate here in the Puna District on the big island plays he'll with stringed instruments. Most go sharp sitting overnight, and flat sitting during the day. This little guy is built very well. I wish it had come with an active pickup with tuned and equalizer, but it's still a keeper!

review_title: Perfect little guitar for fun and travel
body_en: This little thing is one of my dearest possessions!! I've played guitar as a hobby off and on for about 18 years and have a couple of full-sized acoustics. About a year ago I started researching smaller instruments because I wanted something easy to travel with. I looked into 1/4 size student guitars and I looked into the Little Martin and its Taylor equivalent. While the Little Martin has great reviews and a great sound, it costs 3-4 times more than this little guy does. It's definitely worth that price, but I didn't have that kind of money to spend. For about $100, the Yamaha Guitalele is excellent. It has a beautiful sound and it's very easy to pick up and take it with you on trips! (To keep it safer for long trips I bought a hard shell tenor uke case which works really well for it. I also bought one of those little Snark clip-on tuners and have been very satisfied with that as well.) Two things which take some adjusting to if you are used to playing a full-size guitar: 1) The strings are a lot closer together and your fingers may feel fat and clumsy at first. I got used to this pretty fast though. 2) The guitalele is tuned to A instead of the standard E tuning of a full-sized guitar. Basically this means anything you play on the guitalele is like playing your reg. guitar with a capo on the 5th fret. So when you play a C-shape chord on this guy, you are actually playing a G chord. I was used to playing a lot of songs on my regular guitar and had to figure out how to translate them to continue playing them in the same key. (It's possible to lower the tuning to E if you want, but the strings have a slack, kind of rubbery sound and they don't stay in tune as long.) I'd recommend checking out the YouTube video reviews for this instrument before you buy it if you have any more questions. You can hear what it sounds like and get some expert input! It really is great. I love mine to the moon and back and have had a blast playing it!

review_title: Fun instrument for the price, but don't expect perfection.
body_en: This guitalele has opened up a bit since I got it. I started playing ukulele 2 years ago, and started learning guitar almost a year ago. After having Amazon cancel an order I placed on an acoustic guitar from the Amazon Warehouse. (Grr! Btw on that! I feel really cheated considering the same guitar turned up with a seller who refabs and resells damaged instruments, and I was extremely excited about it, until I got the message "they couldn't find it," last minute on delivery day!!! 😠 That's so wrong imo.) I chose this guitalele in it's stead however. It has issues with frets not being cut long enough in spots but nothing that makes it unplayable. It's cosmetic for the most part. There's a few other purely cosmetic issues. Mine has a couple spots the factory missed applying the wood filler to, on the body to make it smooth. Theres a small spot on the bottom of the neck where the wood chipped before assembly and it wasn't filled with filler or even glue to fill the gap. It's a mass produced instrument at an affordable price. I was expecting small imperfections. The sloppy fret cutting job is the only kind-of annoying one to me. The one I have is actually a replacement for one I exchanged which had a mfg. defect which made it unplayable. The first one wasn't inspected properly and shouldn't have left the factory in the dangerous condition it was in. Amazon took care of me immediately and the exchange was smooth and painless. Hopefully yamaha corrects the quality control issues in their factory. For my own play style I had the nut filed down so my hand could glide over the nut. The stock nut height stopped my hand down there like a brick wall, and having the nut done cost as much as the guitalele. This probably won't bother most people. I'm just throwing it out there, that the nut sticks up above the string height, and if you like to slide in or out by the nut, it might be something to consider for someone. The piece of wood that was used on the back of the one I received is unexpectedly pretty. I got lucky. The top has nice strait grain. The neck is ugly. It's constructed in a few pieces and mine doesn't remotely match. One side appears to have had a patch of tear out or something, and Yamaha filled it really nicely with filler, but the filler is darker than the neck wood and adds to the kind of sloppy franken-neck look. Again, not a deal breaker. I can't feel a difference, and they have to keep costs down. When I got it, it sounded a little "stuffy." After playing it daily since I got it, the wood seems to have opened up a bit on all tones except the low A, which still sounds the same. If it does open up, this instrument is pretty impressive sounding for the money in my opinion. Someone said in another review the thing is built like a tank. I agree. It's not a delicate feeling instrument. It seems pretty well constructed until the fret wire though. Overall it's been fun to play. It's the perfect size. I left sheerness blank in the star rating. Not sure how that applies to a guitalele or any stringed instrument? Thickness doesn't really apply either, but I rated it 4 because the wood is thick. I might update this review in the future if anything changes, but I'd probably get another one if something happens to mine.

review_title: decent, doesn't need to be tuned up a full 4th to sound OK
body_en: Mahalo used to make a similar product for less than half the price, so this guy seems a little overpriced to me – but since the Mahalo seems to be discontinued, there's no real competitor, and this hardly breaks the bank. It has entirely acceptable playability, sound, intontation, etc. I especially like to play it like a mandolin, flat-picking single lines, but of course it can play full-chord accompaniments, sounding just like a ukulele but lower. Travels fine, though one thing to note about the classic camp-singalong use is that the nylon strings are suuuuuper sensitive to temperature changes, so it's a bit frustrating playing it outdoors in chilly air next to a hot campfire – you might need to invest in a steel-string alternative if you can't abide that. You *can* tune it to standard guitar tuning (E2, A2, D3, ...), which is useful if you want to use it for, say, composing on the go and not get confused about which key you're in – but down there the strings sound like garbage and don't stay in tune. The recommended tuning is up a 4th, which I find a bit high, since you can't even play G2 (de facto a lot of things you play on guitars tend to be in keys like G, D, C ...). One solution is to use the recommended tuning but with "drop G" (lowest string = G2), which sounds fine. But you also can just tune the whole thing a major 3rd higher than a guitar (major 2nd lower than the recommended tuning), rather than a 4th (so: G2, C3, F3 ....) which IMHO sounds just as good and stays in tune just as well. (I just personally keep getting confused by the mental arithmetic that requires – what you expect to be a G major chord is actually Bb major ... etc.)

I love this thing. I tied a strap to it with some shoe strings, I slap it on my back, get on my bike. I take it with me when I go hiking, to school, to the beach, or anywhere really. The tuning on it is ADGCEA which would be equal to as if you had a capo on a regular guitar's 5th fret, which means that you can play the same chord shapes as a regular guitar, the notes will just be higher. As far as quality goes, I'm pretty happy with it. Some people said the strings that they got were no good, but I've had mine for about 3 months now and I have no complaints. The strings are very sensitive though. They bend very easily, so sometimes the chords played sound good and other times they might sound a little off. I see as a very delicate instrument.. when I press down my fingers for chords I press them straight down and make sure I'm not bending them. A;so, because they bend easily, it can go out of tune pretty easily too. I tune mine often, to make sure they are good to go. I have always tuned my normal guitars by ear, however I find that it is harder to do with the guitarlele, so I use a tuner usually. Visually I have no complaints, the wood and finish are nice, the neck has good action and feel, although a small part of me wishes that they had some artwork around the soundhole. As for sound quality, I love it.. the higher strings/notes do stand out more in a way, and definitely have the ukulele sound, but if you play gently enough it creates a nice balance. The resonance is beautiful. It has a very warm, mellow sound. It's pretty loud for it's size too. And it is so versatile, you can play Spanish style chords like Em and Am which sounds awesome (Onda Vaga uses a uke, perfect example, youtube them), .. you can emulate a mandolin to an extent.. I'm not saying it sounds exactly like a mandolin since it obviously can't replicate the resonant-sound of the double layered strings, but it does have the high notes from the strings that at least sound somewhat similar to a mandolin, if you want to cover a song with one. Or you can just play regular songs, normal chord shapes, even powerchords sound good. It's just like guitar. Just tuned to much higher notes. If you know music theory, you can do a lot with this little guitar. I even have used a capo on mine and it sounds good, although when I put it too high up the fret spaces are so small it's hard to make the chord shapes ;-) Before I saw the guitarlele I was looking at rogue instruments because they sell cheap mandolins and ukuleles. I checked out reviews of their instruments on youtube and they had some mixed reviews.. they didn't seem like very good quality. I saw someone mention the guitarlele on the comments, and when I looked it up I knew it was the 'travel' instrument I wanted. 100 bucks, for a completely unique Yamaha brand instrument? You can't go wrong. Yamaha aren't the super-high end guitars, but my bigger acoustic is a yamaha and I don't have any complaints about that one either (a friend gave it to me to replace my epiphone acoustic which I need to get a new saddle for). I hope this review was helpful. If you get one, enjoy it. I know I enjoy mine. I've even started buying other travel instruments like a melodica and a Buffalo Drum.. so yeah. Enjoy!!

review_title: Here is the "real deal" review on this Guitalele
body_en: I've been playing, and writing music since 1984. I play a myriad of instruments and currently, I write and record commercially licensed music under BMI, Inc. My Wife bought this instrument for me for a holiday gift, but I wanted to check it out before it gets wrapped.. just in case of damage. I am glad that I did. I also know how to setup and do maintenance on both electronic and acoustic instruments. The good things about this instrument: This instrument sounds really good, as it seems to be structurally sound. I do not see any cracks in the body or missing glue around the neck joint. The strings are nice wrapped around to tuning pags. The open faced tuners and gears seem to be of a higher quality than others that I have seen. The bad things about this instrument: The bridge saddle is WAY too high. I have no issues in regards to setting up a bridge saddle, but I expected Yamaha to be a "bit more" on the quality control side of things and at least have the saddle to a more "normal" height. The fretboard and body of this instrument was "very" dry. I used some Music Nomad f-one oil on the fretboard and some of the body as it needed it "badly". The thing that was VERY surprising to me, is there were run-offs / rough spots in the back and sides of the instrument. For a more inexpensive instrument from a no-name company.. I could see that. .but for the price and the Yamaha name.. again.. VERY SURPRISING. I'm also having some issues in regards to getting a partial from Amazon for some reason, but I have amplified that further up the chain on the Amazon side. Other things to think about: I was able to tune this to a standard guitar tuning, that is very possible. The neck is "wide" just like a classical guitar. A lot of people think this is a hybrid instrument of an acoustic guitar and a baritone ukulele. It's really a cross between an Classical Guitar and a baritone ukulele. Conclusion: I am sure that I will have a really awesome time opening this on Christmas day and setting up the saddle on the bridge. And I can probably buff out the rough spots in the finish.. but buying this really changed my mind in regards to Yamaha quality control. UPDATE: I was able to take off a lot of material from the saddle, and lowered the strings, so the playability is better, but I still am a bit suprised in regards to the rough spots in the finish. The instrument should be priced in the $50.00 USD mark. Other than that, it does make a nice portable instrument in regards to classical guitar or baritone ukulele. - Tom

review_title: A Delightful Addition to the Collection!
body_en: This little guy is so much fun! I love playing the ukulele, but sometimes it can be a little frustrating. With only four strings, uke chords often end up in awkward inversions, having a chord tone other than the tonic as the lowest note. By adding two strings to the bass side, you can always have the inversion you want. For uke players the chords will be a little more complex with two additional strings to deal with. Also, in strumming the "uke sound" you'll need to get the hang of not hitting the bottom two strings. But it's all worth the effort and makes for a more "musically complete" sound. For uke players aspiring to play guitar, this is a great bridge. I think guitarists will find it fun as well. The chords are all familiar but will sound a fourth up. Guitarists who are familiar with using a capo won't have any problem with this. Videos online show how to restring the instrument so it can play down in guitar range, but I think it's more fun as a "super uke!" I like the sunburst style and mahogany back and sides. It has a nice, warm uke-y tone. I'm glad I got it!
I am very satisfied!

review_title: A nice little guitar for the price
body_en: At this price level I had low expectations, but having respect for the Yamaha brand I took a chance and ordered the guitar, half expecting to send it back it it proved a disappointment. It didn’t disappoint at all. As an experienced player of various full size acoustic guitars I must admit this little guitar is surprisingly well made and pleasant to play for such an economy price. TBH I didn’t buy it for myself, it was supposed to be an alternative instrument for my Ukelele playing partner to progress to. She didn’t like it, because two extra strings aid a step to far for her. Ah we’ll never mind I tried. Also I hope to use it to teach guitar to my 8 year old grandchild but haven’t introduced it to him yet. The body size is ideal for him, and the classical type nylon strings should be easier for him. However the neck width is about the same as a full size guitar and flat rather than radiused, which is not ideal for small hands. Also due to the necessarily short neck the tuning cannot be standard EADGBE like a full size so that’s an obstacle to learning the fretboard for later progression to a full size guitar when he’s older.

review_title: Mucho mejor de lo que me esperaba
body_en: The truth is that I had read a lot about this product before purchasing it and, once I received it, I was pleasantly surprised. The qualities of the wood are very very good, the action of the strings is correct and the sound corresponds to the size of the instrument's case. I've been playing the guitar for years and I wanted this one to be at home quiet on the couch. A tuning is not a problem. You can tune it with a click tuner in chromatic mode. It maintains the tuning very well from the beginning and the strings came new, not rusty at all and they are not damaged by the frets as some said. The case is much better than I expected with a slight thickness and a handle. The problem that people say about the tuning being different is not a problem at all. You can play the same songs but they sound a little higher, but no problem. Before buying the guitalele, try your guitar with a capo on the fifth fret so you can get an idea of ​​what the guitalele sounds like. So very very satisfied with the purchase.

review_title: Great first real guitar for a kid
body_en: Incredible first guitar for a child that loves music. A little big for my five year old but he’s still able to mess around with it and get a feel for a real guitar. The sound is beautiful and the tuning retains well for how rough it’s handled.

One other thing I’ll add before I start is unlike other reviewers, I haven’t had all the best brand Guitars. I’ve had electric and acoustic guitars, Bass guitars, and Ukuleles of various sizes - all at the $250 or less range. So with that… I love this instrument. This is the closest thing I’ve ever had to a “deluxe guitar”. I’ve purchased boxes in this range before and thought “yeah, okay, this’ll do.” This is the first time I’ve thought “okay this is what I’m talking about!” First off, this box keeps in tune. Not only thought but the tuning pegs are tight and seem to snap into tune pretty easily. I walk around the house and sit it up against all kinds of surfaces and don’t have to worry about knocking it out of tune. Next and just as important, it seems this guitar has raised frets and low action. I saw a few reviews and YouTube comments that made me think this was going to be hard to play and have high action, but this is perfect! I’m not worried about going to get a setup any time soon. The neck shape does seem to make fretting easier as well. This box was built with a lot of thought and a lot of love. I most recently played baritone ukulele, and even at 6’0 with relatively big hands, a dreadnought style guitar is too cumbersome for me. This thing could be great for a smaller person or kid, but it’s also very comfortable for me. Lastly but not least, the sound! I will say that when played with a pick or my nails it doesn’t produce a bad sound, but I wouldn’t say that’s the guitars strong suit. It’s kind of high and thin. BUT if you either strum this with your thumb and fingers or (even better) finger style pluck, this thing sounds gorgeous. It’s warm and resonant with lots of emotion. I’ve tried hammer ons, pull offs. Slides, bends, slides into bends, it all sounds clean, full, and resonant. I’m a beginner player, but I can see how I’m really going to be expressing myself with this box soon. If I had to gripe about anything at all, the bridge is just a little rough and grainy. Like not enough to give me a splinter, but not totally smooth. The rest of the body and guitar feels so nice and high quality to me. So yeah besides maybe not being the best guitar for pick-exclusive playing, and it might not have any electronics or bells and whistles, I feel like a wizard who found his wand with this guitar. Happy playing y’all! Ps, the little treats added in the box were a cute touch. 🙂
