But this amp is heads and shoulders above every other competitive solution in this same market space. Here is what differentiates this one from the competitors in this space, as the tone with the others is good as well but… with the Yamaha, the tone is fantastic because they’ve done component level modeling to build out their amps, which means you get incredibly accurate modeling. The effects just sweeten the tone that much more. The cabinet models are also very good and broaden the tone options. Then, when you add the wireless capability for both streaming via Bluetooth and then using the Line 6 G10t for wireless guitar with it, just leaves all the others in the dust! The new app! The Yamaha app looks just like the knobs on the top of the amp for the interface. It allows you to adjust it in real time to tweak, then if you want to save it - you can save it to one of the three banks of five patches. Very simple and straightforward to use. Bluetooth! This allows you to stream from your mobile device for either playing along, or just streaming music in stereo. This works amazingly well so you can adjust the volume’s and sound like you’re part of the mix. Wireless guitar! I also bought the Line 6 G10t (optional $99) I can leave the transmitter plugged in to the quarter inch jack as it charges the transmitter while it’s plugged in so it’s always ready to go, and gives me eight hours of playtime. Rechargeable, built in batteries! I can just pick up my guitar, the amp and walk out onto my deck - stream music from my iPad and start jamming. Bass or guitar! I use it for both bass and for guitar and the bass modeling sounds amazing. The bass models sound particularly well, over the previous version of the THR (no bass specific modeling on the old version as it was for guitar). These models are super well-balanced and have a deep rich bass tone. I have saved patches for both bass guitar and for regular six string guitar that I use frequently, actually daily. I use this amp daily for practice and for writing recording, it is second to none and a crucial part of my gear.

review_title: Impressive Desktop Guitar Amp! It is NOT the Acoustic model as stated.
body_en: Note: Amazon is listing this version of the Yamaha THR30II Wireless as an Acoustic Amp. It is NOT. The black model is the Electric guitar version. Amazon / Yamaha should correct this. The Acoustic version is a brown colored model. Fact: Yamaha has annihilated the competition with the THR30II Wireless Desktop Amp. The guitar sound this thing produces is remarkable and has far surpassed my expectations of what an amp this size is capable of producing. If you don’t require a larger amp for concert performance, Yamaha’s latest desktop may be all you need. But even if you wanted to use it on stage, simply connect the THR30II Wireless to a house system or another amp using the 1/4 inch stereo outs on the back of the unit. As a longtime pro guitar player I admit I’m getting tired of heavy amps and a suitcase of cords and pedals. Perhaps that’s just one of the reasons I find the 30 watt desktop THR30II Wireless so refreshing. Yamaha has produced a powerful desktop system with a realistic tube tone that sounds so good, it makes me want to play longer, and even at my age, that continues to make me a better player. There are 8 variations.. clean, crunch, lead, hi gain, special, bass, acoustic and flat. Each with 3 variations.. modern, boutique and classic. The acoustic and flat settings are perfect for acoustics and the bass, middle and treble controls actually work, providing excellent EQ control. Whether playing or recording at home, in a studio, or busking on the corner, the THR30II Wireless is incredible. With the built in rechargeable battery you’ll be able to play for 4-5 hours. The craftsmanship is impressive. Built like a tank and impeccably manufactured. Even the headphone amp, where most manufacturers tend to cheap out, is one of the best I’ve heard. It’s as good as the THR30’s custom twin speakers. The THR30II has an aux-in as well. Though with Bluetooth providing the capability of playing along with music from your smart device, you may never use the aux-in function. Of course the THR30II Wireless Desktop Amp can also be used as an everyday Bluetooth speaker. Yamaha has been making a version of this desktop amp for well over a decade, but only now with wireless and Bluetooth (and slightly larger speakers on the THR30II), has it really come of age. I’m glad I waited too, as the stunning new black model wasn’t available until recently. Then there’s that warm tube-like orange glow behind the amp grill. Nice! (Especially noticeable on the black model.) The built in effects include all the pro processing Yamaha is known for, and if you connect your smart device and use the free downloadable Yamaha THR Remote app, you’ll have a dozen additional settings like multiple cabs, reverbs, delays, a noise gate and adjustable compression. All THR30II settings, including a separate Bluetooth audio channel, are controllable via the THR Remote app. But you ask, how does it sound? To me, the true test of any amp is how it sounds at lower to mid volume. With stage amps you need to drive the wattage to obtain the sound you may be looking for. With the THR30II, Yamaha’s engineers and sound techs obviously spent major time coming up with a way to deliver that warm tube sound at living room level. It’s one of the THR30II’s top features. Dial in a setting and save it to one of 5 available presets. ( I saved 4 for electric and 1 for acoustic.) Plug in a Line 6 Relay G10 and play wirelessly from 50’ away. The guitar jack automatically charges the Relay G10 when plugged in. Or use any $50 set of wireless TX and RX plugs. Of all the equipment I’ve purchased over the last 30 years, the THR30II Wireless desktop amp (Black) is one of the most amazing pieces of gear I’ve owned. It’s built like a Rolls Royce, is stunning in appearance, is 100% portable, and the quality of sound it produces defies its diminutive size. There is also a Tap Tempo feature and built in tuner. I can’t stop playing my guitar through it, finding the sound it produces extremely addictive. So there you have it. Now go and get one. ** A special thanks to Musique Gagné in Quebec City for their professional and friendly assistance in getting the THR30II to me. They were quick to respond to emails, highly informative on the product, enabled my specific delivery request and were always courteous. I look forward to dealing with them many times. **

This is the best amp I have owned. It sounds glorious and looks beautiful. I don't use the app much but it allows a lot of tone tweaking. Downloading a large number of tones is a big plus. I have an old VOX DA5 which has no app and sounds anemic in large spaces but sounds very good in small spaces. I also have a Spark 2 which is very good and has many decent tones, especially with AI engine, but doesn't come even close to THR30ii. While this one is almost twice the price of Spark 2, I would recommend it over spark 2 any day. What THR cannot easily do that Spark 2 can is to create tones by just telling it - "give me a Ken Burrell tone from Midnight blue" gives something that is close enough. And despite not having an AI capability like Spark 2 has, I prefer this amp for its tone and sound. The feature I have used is to download tones (I think there are 40 or so tones) and save them on the amp. Those tones are all better sounding than Spark 2 tones. Also, the bluetooth audio capability in this is far superior to Spark 2 which sometimes distorts sound. I suspect that as I use Spark 2 in a big city where airwaves might be saturated with wifi and bluetooth signals I have experienced some connection issues on Spark 2. I use THR30ii in a place where there is zero bluetooth and wifi density and that is why I have never experienced any connection problems. Overall, I would highly recommend this amp.

Have kids? Do they want to play guitar? Do they *really* want to play guitar? Maybe it's you? Do you think you want to play guitar? Let's face it, kids say a lot of things. You really want to encourage your kids' love of music, at the same time, you don't know what instrument they are going to stick with, and what's going to gather dust. This makes for a great starting point. You get the guitar (of course), but it has a ton of extras -- a strap, picks, tuner, extra strings, a "learn guitar" book, and more. I can't really think of anything else you'd need to buy when starting out. What I like: * A decent guitar (look at the price, you aren't getting a fancy guitar; you are getting a good serviceable guitar.) * A bunch of extras like mentioned before. As I told my daughter, as with any "kit" you get stuff you'll use and won't use, but it teaches you what you need and don't need. * A bag to take it to a friend's house or store when not in use (there is also an included wall hook) * Interesting paint -- my daughter really likes the purple/black finish. What could use improvement: * Construction is fair. There are many inclusions in the finish and glue drips under the paint. Most you can't see if a couple feet away. Again, to me, something like this is a start. It's good enough to allow the child to learn (and my daughter played her first song within 30 minutes from the book), but it's not so good it will break the bank. It's beyond a toy. As the person learns, you can decided which parts to upgrade and what to abandon. If my daughter enjoys playing and wants to continue, then I know the more expensive guitar is worth the investment. If she doesn't, then this is a nice guitar for her to strum on the weekends. Music is a great investment, and this is a great starting point for my daughter.

review_title: Very Good, But Small 3/4 Accoustic Guitar
body_en: I am basically an advanced beginner, having started out about a year and a half ago on the Yamaha 3/4 Size Classcal Guitar (with nylon strings.) Also taking lessons. I recently purchased this Yamaha FG 3/4 Size Accoustic Guitar. In my opinion, it has good intonation, has a more than decent rich sound to it. It is definitely not a "toy" guitar. After about five tunings at the beginning, it has held its tune well--only very few tweaks. The action is low without buzzing, which is good for tender finger tips, and just plain, overall fretting. I have to agree with some of the reviewers who believe this to be smaller than a 3/4 size guitar. This one is pretty small. I don't think it's 3/4 size--more of a half-size. I am only 5 feet tall, female, with small frame and fingers, and I find the distance between the strings to be a bit of a tight squeeze. Distance in frets is okay for my stature. I was worried that going to a steel string accoustic guitar would be painful on the tips of my fretting fingers since I have nerve damage in my fingers--one of the reasons I started off on the Yamaha 3/4 size classical with nylon strings (which is a great nylon string guitar for beginners), but I don't realize any difficulty or pain with this steel string guitar. I have calluses by now, but even so, for one just starting out on a steel string, I don't think it's any more painful than starting out on nylon strings. A setup by a luthier, I don't think it is at all necessary unless you are at least an intermediate, at which point you probably own a $500+ guitar that has a louder sound (I think this one has more than average projection, and aginn, intonation). Besides a bit of a problem with the string-to-string closeness, the only other thing I can think of is the fretboard, compared to the overall size of the guitar, and the body, is more than average heavy--not a real biggie, but I thought I'd mention it. Because of its small size, if you are taller than five feet, or have average or large hands, I can't give it five stars. If you know enough about guitars and think you can handle a guitar this size, I would give it five stars, especially for a small child. All in all, if you are looking for a beginner steel string accoustic guitar, especially for a child just starting out, I don't think you could go wrong with this guitar. You get a real guitar at a very good price, that's pretty vibrant, while keeping in mind that it is on a small scale. Here, I would give it five stars. If I had a child who wanted to start playing a steel string accoustic guitar, I would not hesitate to purchase this guitar. If you are taller than five feet, or have large fingers, I do feel this good guitar would be a bit of a tight squeeze, and also possibly not as comfortable to hold. If, on the other hand, you want to purchase a very nice quality guitar without shelling out big bucks, especially for a beginner, I would highly recommend this guitar.

Editing...changing the strings on this guitar made a huge difference. I struggled for nearly four months with the strings that came on it. Note that description says a Junior 3/4 size. It is smaller than a 3/4 size guitar. I was really struggling learning to play on a regular sized guitar because I have small hands and fingers along with some arthritis and short arms. I was disappointed with the purchase at first and was going to return it but over the course of the month, changed my mind. It does have a good sound when I can play the cords correctly and isn't as bulky to take to lessons. I do recommend it for someone like me that has small hands and fingers and has the desire to learn to play a guitar. There is a bag included in the purchase. The bag has extra material on one side of the zipper which is probably there to protect the guitar but it will catch and jam the zipper if you are not careful. I did finally cut that material off and no longer have an issue.

We bought this for my then 13 year old daughter to start learning to play guitar. This guitar has served its purpose well. She uses it daily and it sounds fine. It is smaller, which is good for her to learn on.
Magnificent guitar with exquisite sound!

review_title: Definitely recommend this for a beginner!
body_en: This was recommended by our music teacher and it turned out to be the best investment. Easy to play and great quality. My beginner player found it comfortable and love the way it looks. Definitely recommend this.

I bought this "used - like new" to save a few bucks, but I am sure it is brand new, not a single flaw. The only problem was that the shipping box was a little damaged, but the guitar was packed safely inside, the internal packing was like new. It plays well and really rings compared to my full size Yamaha classical. It is a little small for my fingers on some chords but I really enjoy playing it. It would be perfect for a children's beginner instrument. I tuned it a couple of times and then it holds tune well. The steel strings don't stretch compared to nylon strings. I was worried that the tuners would be too cheap but they work well. Decent sound for such a small instrument. I will keep it.

review_title: Won't hod tune on E-string.... can't play
body_en: Was so excited to give my grandson this for christmas. Figuring it to be a Yamaha guitar it would be as a fine tuned instrument. Unfortunately the E string will not tune. The pieve that adjust the tension of the Estring just slips won't hold tension or tune... VERY DISAPPOINTED in the craftmanship bc I have played Yamaha guitars all my life 60 yrs & am a big fan of Yamaha guitars.... needless to say this untunable guitar just sits there unplayed what a shame... I am going to contact seller & see if they will replace or repair this guitar. I will re- update after contacting seller. Other than the E-string not tuning this would be a good guitar worth the money but as of now it's just for looks. UPDATE... BUYER BEWARE SELLER DOES NOT BACK PRODUCT SOLD!!! I PAID OVER $150 FOR THIS GUITAR ONLINE..BIG MISTAKE THEY DO NOT CHECK THEIR GUITARS CRAFTSMANSHIP B4 THEY SHIP. BUYER BEWARE....
Very good; pleasant to touch due to its size and easy to transport. Advisable

First impression was, it’s tiny! Here’s a pic beside a Martin D18 for scale. But it’s got a nice little top. Great vintage toner colour, put some oil on the fretboard as it was dry as a bone. Rosewood though, and nice! Sounds a little boxy but I’ve been playing it hard and it actually opened up a lot. Tuners work, frets are all level, doesn’t buzz, action at the nut is absolutely perfect btw. It comes filed right down to just clearing the first fret, not sure how they did that. It’s Indonesia made, not Japan. Fret ends a little sharp, I’ll give em a polish when I restring, not terrible though. Intonation isn’t perfect as I recall, but breaking it in. Not a compensated saddle. I’m keeping this in my work truck and I’m gonna love it. I’m sure it’ll open up more and I’m really impressed with the quality from the indonesian guitar makers and Yamaha, for this price. Very glad I bought this.
Bad quality tuning, this products has bad quality I purchased this for a gift but later I figured it out my niece didn’t use it because of bad quality sounds even though properly tuned.

This is a really great, small, good-sounding travel guitar that hardly goes out of tune, is also easy to play and doesn't cost hundreds of euros in the event of a loss (campfire incident:-). Yamaha quality.

The guitar is really great, my 6 year old son loved it! I was afraid it would be too big because he's not very big but not at all! The finishes are very beautiful, the quality wood and the storage pouch is very correct. It is very difficult to find folk guitars of this size.
The most pretty sounding beautiful guitar I have ever played.

review_title: Pretty nice Guitar for the money
body_en: So far I like it please pretty well right out of the box. It was cold. I had to let it warm up. It had some fret buzz when it first got here after it warmed up it went away. I’m gonna put new strings on it. The strings that comes with it are kind of crappy. Other than that. It’s a good guitar. I gave it four stars because of crappy strings lol

This guitar is exactly as the manufacturer describes it. If you are looking for something different and with good sound based on this price category, it could be a good option. It will sound as good as the amplifier it is connected to, although it transmits good sound unplugged.

review_title: Worse shipping box ever! This poor guitar had no chance from Ohio to Maryland.
body_en: Worst shipping box ever ! This guitar was cracked at the jack input, the head was chipped and strap pin was sticking thru the box. The quilty of the unit was poor. Glue spears ar the bridge and the neck/body. Bad polising the whole body. Sorry to say, I like Washburn .

review_title: awesome deal on an awesome guitar
body_en: Came exactly on time,beautiful guitar,an sounds amazing.This is a good quality guitar,sounds just as good as the higher end ones
Best acoustic I've ever played!

While I love this guitar as an acoustic, the electric features leave much to be desired. I purchased this for play in live settings, but learned soon after the purchase that the amplification would stop for no reason right in the middle of a song. It only requires that the cable be unplugged and reinserted, but this is very inconvenient when it happens mid song. Acoustically I would give this guitar 5 stars. Electrically I give it 2 stars.
Hello, I already received it, it is very pretty and sounds good, the only bad thing I can say is that it did not arrive in the same color that I ordered it, although it is still very pretty.
Love the look and feel great sound

absolutely love this guitar, it sound fantastic and it looks stunning, the electronics were not working when I unboxed it so had to unscrew the unit and jiggle the attachment wire for the electronics as it was not connected right but was easy fix so not a big deal. totally love this Washburn and would recommend if you are looking for a decent sounding and great looking guitar that won't break the bank.

review_title: Its not completely perfect but close enough and it is a very interesting guitar
body_en: There is the most minor flaw in the finish in one spot most people wouldn't even see other then that I love the guitar great neck now string rattles very pleased

Easy to put together. You have to detune it pretty good to loosen the strings up enough to click it into place. But if you’re comfortable tuning your guitar pretty often like a guitar player needs to be anyway, it’s totally fine. I was surprised at the build quality of this. Very nice weight to it. Solid made. Mini head stock to cut down on length. Smooth, routered edges. Tight and strong tuners. Solid nut. Very nice sounding especially with these elixirs on here that it comes with. It sounded a little dull when I had it a few steps down but most acoustics do. Tuned up to standard or a half step down, it’s sounds really nice and clear and full. It does come with a nice case, but I have a decent size LL Bean “locker” backpack that this fits completely into so I can still throw more clothes and whatnot into for plane ride carry on. This thing is legit and I’m pretty picky.

review_title: For a traveling guitar player, a must have.
body_en: Surprisingly good sounding a easy to play. However, no place for a clip-on tuner. Action level is great, it feels durable and is good value for money. Only a slight string buzz when you don't tighten the screw. All in all, great thing and had no problems whatsoever taking it in the airplane!

I was honestly not expecting much. I did some quick searching for a travel guitar and found this one. I needed something quick as I travel in two more days. The guitar arrived on time packed in its little backpack. I was supriseed at how small a package it was that it came in. I followed the assembly instructions and made sure that the neck was seated properly. The string action is very nice. Its small size is comfortable. It was already damn near in tune on the first strum and through the tuning pegs are a little tight it tuned easily and stayed in tune as I played it for the next hour and a half. It is loud for its size. It plays very nicely and I am very happy with this guitar. The tone is the only negative aspect of this great little guitar but this is for me not an issue as I intend to use this to stay in practice during some long TDYs. It will definitely not replace my Zager as my main guitar but it will serve very nicely on my trips.

Don’t expect the sound or feel of a full size guitar. That said, it sounds pretty good for what it is. I purchased the puddle jumper with no electronics, but solid spruce top. Decent action after a small truss rod adjustment, works well at the beach or around a campfire. Easy to assemble/de-assemble and fit into backpack that fits under an airplane seat. A bit or room in pack for other carry on items. You can also put stuff inside the body while dis-assembled. Use caution as the nut can fall out while dis-assembled. Also seems to be hard on the strings so carry spares. The set screw on the locking wing nut also got loose and fell out - easy to put back in but don’t loose screw/wingnut/washer. They include an extra nut, allen key, and peg with the guitar which is nice.

I have a Martin travel guitar, that is the one like a strumstick. This guitar has the full body, it is only 12 frets/octave/ to the body, it is the size of a parlor guitar. This one has a better sound than the Martin Strumstick style guitar. No bass on that guitar, too small a body. This sounds great and holds a tune as long as temperature and humidity are constant. If it varies much, the guitar will need tuning, but so what. It is easy to take down and set back up. The travel bag is nice. Small bag for a guitar! Amazing. No need to loosen strings, etc. The large wing nut on the back gets tightened up after initial set of neck. To remove, loosen wing nut, THEN the button will loosen the neck. Very secure, solid neck set. You get two bridges, one taller. The taller one is fine, the shorter one was too short and would buzz strings.

I LOVE this guitar. It really does fit under the seat on an airplane, but just barely, so double check the specifics for your plane before you travel. After you attach the neck to the body and tune it, gently tug the strings and retune. You probably have to tug and retune two or three times, then it will stay in tune while you play.

Action needs to improve & intonation (strings height is far away from fret making it hard to press. I do like the sound when strumming but again, my wrist is working harder to press on chords. I love the concept as I travel quite a bit and bring my guitar everyone I go. I have 4 guitars and have looked at travel options and was happy to find on Amazon. I wish the design was better, it will help to those guitar players who use fingers instead of strumming. Specially if perform your wrist will not hold. The sound is nice. I am returning.

Just received my Puddle Jumper guitar. Since it's winter time here, I let it warm up a bit before putting it together. So far so good. I'm just a little past being a beginner, but I've been wanting a guitar I can travel with. I think this is going to work great! Just make sure to follow the instructions and tighten it as best you can to get a good action on it. Be patient as you tune it up as well :) I also contacted the manufacturer via their website. They got back to me within a day and were very helpful.
I am surprised on the quality and ease to put the guitar together. It was nice to have another bridge so to lower the action. Sound is nice, for the price. Nice to have to take to jams.

I love this little guitar. It looks and feels like a well made instrument. Is competitively priced. It has a good tone and is very LOUD. (Compares well to my 00028 Martin or Gibson acoustic). Action is a little high but adjustable, and otherwise very playable. The bag does (just) fit under the seat in front so this works as hand luggage on BA. Most importantly it stays in tune once constructed and is easy to assemble and dis-assemble. Just a super bit of kit for a travelling guitarist. Mine has just accompanied me to Greece and will be heading to the US shortly.

This was a gift for my husband who missed his Taylor when vacationing. He was so impressed with how much he enjoyed this travel guitar. Assembly is quick and easy! 2 months away and he played every day like he was at home.

Have been playing for a few days now and I must say I'm very impressed both by the guitar itself and the support received locally here in the UK. On first assembly I felt the action was a little high for my preference, however after a couple of email exchanges and a short call this was completely resolved by utilising parts shipped as standard with the instrument. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this guitar. Thank you guys!

I bought the Puddle Jumper and right off the bag it was good but I felt like the touch was a little bit too high. They do provide a lower saddle in the kit which, for me, made a huge difference. People complaining about the touch height don't realise it's not your regular guitar and some adjustments can be done easily. Quality wise I can easily compare this to a Mahogany Baby Taylor. The sound is just as good ( a little bit more full than the Baby Taylor) but takes a little bit more tuning when you install the neck. I took the Jumper over the Overhead because I wanted the smallest model. That being said I would like to try the overhead because I'm already impressed with the sound quality of the little Puddle Jumper. You can't compare it with a quality full size guitar ( Martin, Yamaha, Taylor , etc) , but for a travelling guitar with that kind of feature ( collapsible) it's hard to beat!

review_title: Nice Child's Guitar. Sounds Nice When Tuned to A-D-G-C-E-A
body_en: This is a child's guitar, so I didn't have very high expectations. The reviews capture the good and bad. This isn't going to win any significant praise for craftsmanship. But it works and sounds pretty good. The strings are going to stretch for a long time. Nylon strings will always stretch and slip a bit. Nature of the beast. Buy better strings that can handle the tighter tune this will need to sound good. You will want to tune it to A-D-G-C-E-A to play it with standard guitar notes/chords. It will take at while for the guitar to hold this tune, but it will. Better strings will help, but they aren't needed right away. The workmanship is pretty basic. There are obvious flaws in the finish, but not horrible. Nothing that impacts play. But it isn't going to win awards. The frets and fingerboard are smooth and feel good. What matters is here. My 3.5 year old son is over the moon with this. He just loves that he can bang away and daddy doesn't get upset with the bumps and drops - which shows this items true value. It's made well enough to be used by kids and it takes abuse well. 4.5 Stars when you factor the low price and durability. UPDATE: ** 2/26/15 ** We continue to enjoy playing this guitar. My son has learned a bit and can play a few notes and chords -- he just really enjoys the ability to "jam" when I'm playing mine. I love the quality of this cheap guitar. It now stays in tune for as long as we don't bump the turning pegs or the weather changes drastically. Otherwise, it stays in tune rather well - with the original strings. The tone is rich for the size. Action is still easy on the hands, but maybe a tad high. Not horrible mind you. In the nearly 2 years we've owned this, it has held up very well and looks pretty darn good considering what it has been through as my 3.5 year old is now 5, and lugs this around the house with him nearly daily. He even left it out in the play house out back and had to run and get it when he remembered at bed time. He loves it enough to want to care for it, so it goes back onto the stand each day. I enjoy playing it from time to time. I'm no guitarist - I really stink - but it is fun to play classical music on this and it sounds the part. So very happy and have now pushed this to 5 stars based on the durability and quality over time. While the finish isn't anything special and the hardware is cheap - so it the price and you are getting a lot more than you are paying for in this item. Winner. Highly recommend.

This isn't some cheap, throw away toy guitar. Sure, it's no Martin but it is a very real, wood guitar that sounds pretty good and is the right size for a small child. Actually, I enjoyed playing it myself. The strings are nylon and so are easy to play. Yes, they need to be tuned more often than steel but that is the nature of nylon. If you are looking for first rate beginner guitar for a 5 to 8 year old, this is it.

review_title: Nice first guitar for 5-8 year olds
body_en: 1/2 size guitars (34"), tend do be more expensive than beginner full size guitars. Considering a growing child who maintains interest in the instrument, will need a larger guitar in a relative short time. So...we don't want to spend too much money, but want a good enough instrument to get a good start. This Hohner is a good choice for little hands. I'm a retired teacher and musician. First inspection: good finish, no flaws. The neck is perfect. Holding down a string at top and bottom of the neck shows a very slight bend in the middle. (perfect) It was suggested to re-string with better quality which I did. https://www.amazon.com/DAddario-EJ27N-Student-Fractional-Classical/dp/B003B0W7O8 (Get help if you've never done this.) The action at the first frets is very easy. (Most lesson book start here.) There is plenty of room to file notches in the plastic bridge to improve action in the upper neck, but truthfully, a good student will be on to a bigger guitar by the time that's needed. The tuning pegs grind a bit. They did loosen after installing new strings. Be prepared to do lots of tuning in the beginning. (every day for a while while strings stretch) Can't wait for Christmas to give this to my grandson! You might check out the bundle with string set and tuner. You can download a good tuner on your Iphone. (Hint: look for green pick) Hope this helps you.

I'm a intermediate guitarist and I wanted something that would travel well and be fun to noodle around on. I saw this on WOOT! and picked it up for $30 thinking if it didn't work out there was no big loss. This little guitar is awesome! YES, you have to play the heck out of it and tune it frequently in the beginning. NO, my strings haven't snapped. I can't find any flaws in the build or finish on BOTH of mine... I say both because I loved the first one so much I came back here to Amazon and bought a second one so I could leave one up at my cabin. The second one is exactly the same quality as the first. I spent some time gently stretching the strings by pulling gently on them above the sound hole before tuning each time I played it for the first week or so. I play some songs with a capo and it's no problem. Barre chords sound great. I have bigger hands and sometimes it gets a little crowded on the fretboard, but overall I don't have any problems. This is a real instrument and has pretty decent sound for its size. I have four full-sized guitars, a Martin backpacker, and two of these Hohners and I find myself picking up the Hohner because it's so darn fun and easy to play. I would highly recommend this as a travel guitar to anyone. I see it is now $67 but I got mine here on Amazon for $29.99, so just keep watching the item. Also, Fleabay has them listed often for around $30 new.

review_title: Best Small Beginner Guitar at this Price Point
body_en: Update: After trying several 1/2 and 1/4 size small children’s guitars around this price point, this one is clearly the best. It’s the only guitar that has good intonation and a set up that is playable out of the box. That’s a lot to expect from a tiny, inexpensive guitar, but this one delivers. Original: This is a playable guitar that is most appropriate for a child who is just starting out. Watch my video to hear finger picking and strumming! Comfortable Playability: The low action makes it easy on the fingertips, which is great for beginners or children just starting out. Tuning: The included strings can hold standard tuning after stretching the strings bit, which can be accelerated by gently pulling on them and playing for several days in a row. Tuning Stability: During continuous play, after about 15 minutes, the G, B, and high E strings tend to go about 5-10 cents flat (roughly a tenth of a half step on the piano). The guitar will certainly need to be tuned every time it is played, but that's best practice with any guitar. Size: Although I'm used to playing a Taylor GS Mini (3/4 scale), I found the smaller size of this guitar a bit tricky to adjust to as an adult. It’s likely perfect for a child aged 5-8 years old and those with smaller hands/frames. String Issues: The low E string tends to slip off the fretboard occasionally, which can be frustrating during play. The low E can also be buzzy if your fingers are positioned perfectly. Capo and Barre Chords: It handles barre chords and capos well, though it tends to go slightly sharp when using a capo.

Just got the Hohner guitar today, but here are my first impressions: Tuning was brutal; Tried tuning to typical E-A-D-G-B-E but the strings seemed very tight and sure enough I snapped the 1st string (luckily had an extra). I then double checked the packaging material to see if there was any info about how to tune but there wasn't, so I did a quick Google search to learn that 1/2 sized guitars should be tuned to A-D-G-C-E-A. This worked much better, but the guitar still goes out of tune every 5 minutes. Hopefully it will hold it's tune better one the strings settle in. The sounds quality is pretty poor - better than a toy - but hardly like a real guitar. Guitar seems cheaply made in terms of finish, but appears to be reasonably sturdy. Given the price the guitar is an okay deal, but in retrospect I'd rather spend a bit more money to get a higher-quality instrument. *Update after several months of use*: The guitar holds it tune just fine now. Still annoyed that the directions didn't specify the A-D-G-C-E-A tuning but it ended up being an okay purchase. Would increase to 3.5 stars if that was an option.

review_title: Don't buy this guitar, cheap toy, far from a musical instrument
body_en: I'm a guitar player, and purchased this for my 5 year old niece to see if there is any interest in learning. So my goal was to get something that was good enough to hold tune and 'play' while sounding like a real guitar for the next year or so until an upgrade. And reasonably priced so if she used it as a baseball bat it wouldn't be the end of the world. So I read the reviews, and quickly decided on this Hohner as a majority of the reviewers said it held its tune (nothing more important really). This guitar could barely be tuned when new, but I attributed this to the guitar as well as the strings being new. So we kept tuning. Pretty much have to tune this guitar every time you pick it up, and even more than once while you're playing it. Just simply cannot hold a tune (sorry to be repetitive). So I wrote the seller a couple months after purchasing explaininng this. Also told them that we still hadn't tried new strings, and it was quite possible that it's just the strings so that was my next step. They replied that they were very sorry to hear that, and to go ahead and try the new strings, if no improvement we could send it back for a replacement. So we changed the strings, gave it another couple months in case the strings were still 'stretching', and the same issue, the guitar just won't stay tuned. Wrote Musician's Friend again to which they replied: 'I apologize for the inconvenience this may have caused you, unfortunately we cant do any kind of return or exchange for the guitar at this time. If you have any questions please feel free to contact us. Please feel free to contact us if you have any other questions or concerns, or if you are not completely satisfied with the service you have received from us today. We appreciate your feedback.' Not exactly what we were expecting. To keep this in context, it's a very cheap guitar, looks nice, I guess you get what you pay for. But the point being we did our homework and reviewed various in this category. Would have gladly paid more for a guitar that would stay tuned. Very surprised that Musician's Friend took this stance. If this is indicative of their service, heads up. If zero stars were an option, zero stars would be the rating,

We are the parents of 2-year old twins, and sought to find a guitar which would be a good 'starter' for them. With over 30 years of guitar playing myself - both acoustic and electric, my first concern after reading numerous reviews was the question of whether the instrument would stay in tune. I can say that after two months, I can very highly recommend this guitar. After receiving the instrument, the first thing I did was rewind the strings using the standard through-the-hole (tuner hole), reverse direction (and go underneath the previous wind) and bring up to pitch so that the strings would stay 'locked' rather than slip every time you tune it. I also shortened the amount of string used on the E,A and D (heavier) strings by about three inches to reduce slack and slippage. The guitars are one of their favorite toys, sounds good, and they began to 'sing' within a few weeks. Yes they have brutally treated the instruments, including sitting on, stepping on and generally abused them. Nevertheless except for the expected dings and slight chips, they have held up well. A quick tune once a week with an analog tuner, and the occasional tweak, and we enjoy lots of time with Old MacDonald and Johnny Cash ha ha. And most importantly of course, I don't have to spend time tuning it constantly! Best of luck to all with your musical efforts!

review_title: Exactly what we were looking for!
body_en: We bought this for my sons 2nd birthday so he could play his guitar with and like Daddy. It met all our expectations and then some. We knew a "toy" guitar wouldn't cut it, and this is just a smaller version of the real thing; real looking, feeling and sounding. And so far has stood up to a very active 2 year old! Couldn't have asked for anything better. We're so thrilled.
Good size, resistant material The children really liked it and the adults too It arrived in an excellent time
This ended up being a children's guitar and not the pictured "folk guitar"
This is a great little acoustic guitar amp with an additional mic channel. It has a built in looper and some nice modeling effects.
Anytime you can get a $450 guitar amp for $290, you need to consider it. The amp arrived and looked brand new. It has excellent sound and love all the newer features.

review_title: Quality name and everything I need in one amp...
body_en: Excellent
The product arrived in an excellent manner, it met my expectations. I recommend to anyone looking for an acoustic amplifier with exceptional sound!..

review_title: Gran opción para tocar y cantar al mismo tiempo con un sólo amplificador
body_en: This amp is a great option for playing and singing on a single device, but you have to take into account some aspects: it is very small, it is actually ideal for rehearsal, but it has audio outputs to connect to a PA. On the other hand, it is important to take into account that both channels of this amp have 16V phantom power, so if you want to connect a 48V condenser microphone (there are many on the market) it will not work, you must have an external power supply for the microphone. The quality of the effects is very good and with the footsitch (not included) you can take advantage of the looper that this amp has.

This is a great amp. The tone, volume and effects are exactly what I was looking for in a small acoustic amp. My star rating is based off the shipping damage. I have kept the amp because I needed it for a show but hopefully the shipping company will ensure proper care and packaging in the future. Note: The company did offer to take it back but I wouldn’t have been able to get another soon enough.
It is an excellent amplifier with clear and real sound.

review_title: Does Not Work with any external vocal effects
body_en: I use a TC Helicon Vocalizer and the Fender Junior volume was barely audible when connecting the TC. Going direct with a mic was fine using same cables so that was not the problem. The only other comment was the bass response was not great and the cabinet vibrated when bass was turned up.

I was hoping this set would be a decent guitar, but didn't really expect it to be decently made (for what it is... a youth guitar). But... the neck is perfectly straight. There's not a blemish on it. There were picks, gig bag, a pipe tuner and-- some surprise here-- an unadvertised extra set of strings. I would rate this 5 stars for "what it is"... a very low cost starter guitar. But I rate it 4 stars for a couple of general flaws: 1) The frets are not metal. They are molded into the guitar neck and PAINTED gold. That's a real shame, but for a starter guitar at this price not a deal-killer. It's for this reason along I give it 4 rather than 5 stars. 2) The gig bag is minimal of course. But the zipper broke the first time I used it. No padding, zero quality. It's meant to carry the guitar, nothing else. Had the zipper not broken it would have been fine and what is expected, but a gig bag with a broken zipper isn't of much use. I guess one can always resort to safety pins or velcro patches. Specs: * The guitar measures 31 inches from tail to tip of head, plus the strap peg on the end (yes, it has a strap peg!). Lower body is 11.5 inches wide x 2.75 inches deep. Nut is 1.5 inches wide. Nut to 18th fret is 12.25 inches. Basically-- a mid-size travel guitar similar in size to the Yamaha 6-string "Guitalele". Sound however, is quite "guitar". * The top is good-quality laminate with a resonant tone-- no dead spots (which is far more than I expected). It's not a spruce top, but the laminate is plenty resonant (far more so than many travel guitars) and has excellent sound-- amazingly so for an instrument of this class. * Tuning pegs are standard 3-to-a-set sidewinders, expected on this type of guitar. * The strap attaches to an end peg and is tie-on at the neck. STRING NOTE: I've noticed several of the negative reviews here refer to the guitar "not tuning", strings breaking, action too high, etc. While the action was pretty decent on mine, it's very common for even a quality guitar to arrive with less than desirable action (ask any guitar store). Action is fairly easy to correct by filing the bridge piece down (which is why it's detachable). When one tunes a steel-string guitar, it is imperative to tune it slowly, in steps, and allow the strings time to stretch over a period of 3-4 days. If one tries to tune it quickly strings will undoubtedly break, even on top-of-the-line guitars. Expecting a guitar to "hold a tune" when initially strung is unreasonable. All strings stretch out of tune until they hit their proper tension. Any experienced guitar player is aware of these things-- with all guitars and all brands of strings. SWITCH TO NYLON. Although this guitar comes with steel strings (even an extra set) I think it would be a shame to put that kind of tension on a neck that will most likely warp under such pressure. Despite the low cost I like an instrument to last-- and I think this will last for some time if one uses nylon strings. Because of the resonance you will still get an excellent tone. For protection, putting this in the gig bag and then retaining the triangular box for car trips can offer considerable protection (after all, the box survived shipping, yup?). There's no need to buy an expensive padded gig bag or hard shell case for a guitar that costs less than a tank of gas. Were it not for the wooden frets I'd give this guitar 5 stars. But that is a corner-cut that I don't find acceptable in anything but a plastic instrument found in the toy aisle. At the very least they could have used glued-on metal frets. Other than that, it's a decent guitar and once nylon strings are added, should work fine for a first-year student or child. It's well-worth the purchase and at least is a functional, nice-sounding guitar with decent action. I disagree with the concept of "buy a cheap guitar to see if a child will stick with it". Cheap guitars usually don't play well and so naturally the child won't like it (fortunately, this one plays pretty well). But my credo: pay more and buy a good guitar to start with (there are plenty for under $200) and then as with all things, require the child to "stick with it". No one ever regrets having learned to play an instrument, even though they may-- as kids do-- resist practice. That's where parents come in and gently guide and encourage. Go with quality. But if you can't afford or don't want to buy a quality instrument, this one will certainly suffice. It's decent.

review_title: A Very Nice Guitar for this Price Range
body_en: The guitar arrived in perfect condition (7-16-2024) packed in its gig bag and cardboard box. I chose the Cedar top. My first impression was that the finish is beautiful. I could not find a blemish or defect anywhere. The neck is arrow straight and the set up is ok; action is just a little high (about 5 mm) at the 12th fret. The fretboard top and edges are very smooth. I only found one sharp fret wire end-- on the 14th fret. The strings are ok, not the greatest. The tone is good. The gig bag has a some padding to protect the guitar if you carry it around in your car. I think it would cost close to $30 to buy it separately. The tuner is very good; I keep it clipped on the headstock since nylon strings need frequent tuning in the first couple weeks of use. The capo is "so-so", really not that great. If you use a capo a lot you might need a better one. I would say the same for the foot rest; its a little unstable but useable.. All in all, the accessory package is a really good deal! My only other complaint is that they used a black stain on the Bridge which rubbed off on the included cleaning cloth. I really had to rub it a lot to get all the stain out. I think they also used a black stain on the fretboard but it doesn't seem to rub off. I won't hesitate to give it 5 stars because it is really beautiful, sounds good, and is a great value at $169.

review_title: Staying in tune for almost a year
body_en: It will be a year next month, since I got this guitar. I average 30 minutes a day fingerstyle play. I was really pleased with the construction. The frets were well done. Only one was a little high. I did have to adjust the truss rod to eliminate some buzz on the 6th string at the 3rd fret. 3 strings required rewinding. I am really surprised how well it stays in tune. After the first week, the strings settled and has only required tuning after humidity changes in my area. The body of the guitar is well made and all the fit and finish is really quite beautiful. I work with wood as part of my trade, and an ill fitting piece stands out. This guitar is lovely and the tones are clear and strong. The sound comes out true and each open string pluck is it's own musical piece. I highly recommend this guitar!

Very pleased with this guitar. Tone is nice. Action is low (a consistent height of strings above frets) which makes the pressing of nylon strings comfortable. The action is adjustable since it has a truss rod and included allen wrench but I don't need to adjust it. Also included is a guitar case, clip-on tuner, capo, picks, extra strings, strap, cleaning cloth, and a footstool. I was surprised to see how accurate the tuner is and how easily I could tune the guitar. More surprisingly, I'm pleased with how long the guitar stays in tune. The tuner was not just for guitars. It is for chromatic, guitar, bass, violin, and Ukulele tuning. I’ve used it to tune my B-flat trumpet. Pitch range is listed at 440Hz. If you plan to hang the guitar on a wall, the width of the headstock above the nut is slightly over 2 in, so the first wall hanger I got did not fit. I ended up purchasing the Onmiwod black walnut wall hanger. It has a hook opening of 2.13 in. It works great and was easy to install.

I went ahead and ordered a set of diadario ej45s but honestly the strings that came with it sound pretty darn good so I'm not in a hurry to change them out. It also came with the bag tuner, footrest etc. normally I don't care about stuff like that but the accessories seem like decent quality and I will use them. Upon changing the strings to my go to, Elixir Nano PB lights, I noticed that the guitar lost a lot of what I liked about its initial sound. There is NOTHING about this stand that I dislike. I already plan to buy another one next month to put in my home studio. This one sits out by the amp and pedal board. So, obviously, the pictures show that I do not have a guitar on this particular guitar stand. That is the Korg RK100-S2 keytar. And it is a pain in the butt to place on a stand. It's odd shape makes it unstable, and the power on/off switch is right there between the two forks. Along with audio in jacks, the MIDI out, the USB port and a gain switch for a microphone. I have never heard of the CAHAYA music company before, and I wasn't sure if I wanted to get the stand for that reason alone. But, for the price, I figured that I could just leave it on the curb if it didn't work out. My main concern was needing the neck forks to be offset so much (as can be seen in the picture). I've had other stands (much more expensive) that had a kind of tongue in groove system that didn't let the neck rotate at all. That was my main concern. As you can see, no matter how screwy a position you need that neck fork to be, it can accommodate. I did have to make a slight alteration to the base forks. Again, see the picture. I used a couple of zip ties to pinch the ends of the base forks together approximately 1/2 inch. The pictures and dimensions provided by the company were at the top of the page were correct. What I didn't take into account was that my strap lock takes up about 1 inch of the bottom of the keytar. The instrument still rested easily on the base, but just barely. So I did this just to be safe. The rubber on the forks seems to be the standard stuff you will find on a lot of lower to mid-range stands. I definitely like the padding that you can find on the higher tier stands from Gator and On Stage better, but those stands come at a premium, and wouldn't have held this instrument well anyway. My concern is that this type of rubber gets tacky when it's hot, and that MIGHT damage the finish of a really nice instrument. Time will tell if it damages the finish of THIS really nice instrument, but it doesn't feel tacky at the moment, and the keytar is super stable when resting on it. Assembly was a breeze. I didn't even look at the instructions. Although, I did notice that there were both words and illustrations for anybody that needs a little help. The neck hinge is secured with a nut and bolt. And that is nice, because even some of the $80+ stands just have a squeeze kind of grip that is tight and stable, but also can be easily collapsed if hit at the right (or completely wrong) time! As for the base forks, they also secure with a nut and bolt, but there are also (2) two washers provided that allow you to tighten the base on really well, but still allows the forks to rotate into a self-leveling position when you place your instrument on it. Honestly, with the exception that I wish it had a better quality foam rubber padding, this might just be the most well engineered guitar stand that I have ever owned. It is certainly the most versatile.

review_title: Decent quality at a great price.
body_en: This review covers two CAHAYA products: - 5 in 1 Dual Use Sheet Music Stand - Guitar Stand Floor Universal I bought them together, use them together, and have similar feedback on them, so am cross-posting this review for both products. I am an amateur, non-gigging player and have no need of (and cannot afford!) professional quality stands. However, I am tired of purchasing lower-end products that are poorly-designed and poorly manufactured using inferior materials. CAHAYA has hit the sweet spot offering decent quality stands at affordable prices. This music stand came as part of a kit including a desktop adaptor, travel bag, music clip, and sheet music folder. Personally I have little use for the folder, but it's a nice touch to include it. The desktop adaptor and clip work well when you need them. The bag is great and I use it whenever I need to quickly vacate the family room for visitors. It even accommodates my CAHAYA guitar stand. Everything (except the sheet music folder) breaks down quickly and goes into the bag in about a minute. The most important piece--the music stand itself--is well-designed and well-manufactured. Most important for me is that it easily accommodates thick three-ring binders full of music. It adjusts to any height I need, whether sitting or standing. For daily, same-location amateur use, this music stand kit is a bargain. If you expect to break it down, pack it up, throw it in a vehicle and reassemble it several times a week, you should probably go more high-end. (But if you just don't have the budget to do so, this kit can probably survive some length of pro service as long as you don't abuse it ) The CAHAYA Universal Floor Guitar Stand is similar to the music stand in terms of materials, reliability, and value: an absolute bargain for a single-location amateur. If you expect to set it up in different venues every week where it might get knocked over by a drummer stumbling toward his or her kit or by a drunk audience member, you should probably go more high-end. But this stand is light years better than some of the products that are just $10 cheaper. Some people complain that it holds the guitar too high, making it too unsteady. I was a little concerned about this at first, but I use it for a relatively heavy bass, and have never had a problem. In fact, the cradle appears to be high to accommodate the adjustable tripod legs, so it was designed this way for a reason. My only minor complaint is that you need to completely remove bolts, knobs, nuts, and washers when fully collapsing the stand. If you expect to be doing this a lot, there's a good chance you're going to drop and lose a piece at some point. Otherwise, this stand is a great solution for anybody on a budget that won't be abusing their equipment.

review_title: No reason NOT to get this guitar!
body_en: I received this guitar just 2 days ago. I can honestly say it's the best guitar I've ever played, although I 've never played a Martin or any other high-priced name. I wanted a guitar that has a full sound but isn't heavy like my electric Firefly. Let me break down what I like. Playability: The fingerboard is very smooth, no high frets, and ample space to play chords I hadn't played before. Happy I can play Classical Gas for the first time in about 15 years. The neck setting is perfect for me. RESONANCE: I have the Washburn hanging on my wall. I've been randomly checking the tuning as I walk by. Pleasantly discovered that the notes will "ring" for a few seconds as I leave the room. When I play the guitar, I hear strings that had always seemed muffled before.Great to hear full chords! ELECTRONICS: The tuner works easily. Just be sure to remove the plastic around the battery. The equalizer is something I'm playing with. Right now, everything is set at halfway on the dials. TUNING: Easy, smooth and holds the tuning fairly well for a new guitar. FINISH: This is a beautiful guitar that is both colorful and well finished. I only found one small clear coat blemish near the strap peg. It's nothing to get excited about. Overall, I am glad I selected this guitar. It will be great for gigs and open mics.

review_title: Excellent guitar and kit for a beginner, I highly recommend!
body_en: This is an excellent guitar, and the kit accessories round it out to a full set proper for the ideal beginner experience. I am so impressed! I am an experienced classical guitarist and I chose this for my 7 year old daughter's birthday. I felt pretty confident that the item description hit all the important points. It was well packed and arrived safe and sound. Once she opened it and we checked it all out, I was VERY happy (and so was she! this was a WOW gift). The quality of the guitar itself is excellent for a beginner. Nylon strings mean that the fingers won't be in pain, which can make a new player not want to continue practicing. This is so user friendly. It was easy to accurately tune the strings with the included tuner. (You will find that you need to tune it frequently, especially at first, which is normal). The chord chart is great, the strap, capo, picks, additional strings and gig bag are all fantastic. Getting a full kit like this is great because even a beginner needs to see the full picture of what's possible with their new instrument, and of course the gig bag means that the guitar is protected. MAJOR gift value, excellent all the way around. Another fun little part to this gift: the box that it comes in was literally taller than her, which made for some really hysterical pictures and honestly just added to the birthday fun. Most importantly, she loves the guitar. As a musician, I can say there's really nothing like getting your first proper instrument and this certainly delivered that moment for her. THANK YOU!!

review_title: A perfect birthday surprise — she's obsessed!
body_en: I bought this as a birthday gift for my daughter and she absolutely loves it! She already plays ukulele, so she had a musical foundation going in — but the moment she picked this guitar up, she was hooked. The jump in sound quality compared to what she was used to is genuinely impressive for this price range. The tone is warm, full, and resonant in a way that really surprised us all in the family, especially Mom. The 38" size is ideal — not too big, not too small, and easy for a younger player to handle comfortably. The starter kit that comes with it is a great bonus: the gig bag is sturdy enough for travel, the tuner works great right out of the box, and having a pick included means she could start playing immediately without any extra shopping. Recommend!

body_en: I bought this guitar for my son who is just starting learn how to play the guitar and I’m really happy with it. It looks great, feels comfortable to hold, and has a nice sound for the price. I also liked that it came with useful accessories, so I had everything I needed to get started right away. Overall, it’s a great value and a good choice for anyone learning to play or looking for an affordable acoustic guitar.

I got this little guitar kit for a young beginner my granddaughter, and it's a great starter set! The guitar itself is the perfect size small enough for little hands but still feels like a real instrument, not a toy. The brown finish looks classic and clean, and the sound is actually better than I expected for something in this price range. What I really like was how complete the kit is. It comes with everything: a tuner (super handy!), extra strings, a capo, picks, a winder, a strap, and even a gig bag. The tuner is simple to use, even for a beginner, and the capo fits snugly. The gig bag isn’t super thick, but it's good enough for carrying around and keeping the dust off. Setup was easy and everything was ready to go right out of the box, just needed a little tuning, which is normal for new guitars. This would make an awesome birthday or holiday gift for any kid interested in music. Overall, I’m happy with this purchase and think it’s a great value for what you get. Definitely recommend for a first guitar!
